title: SAEMAPE lance l'identification des mineurs artisanaux après l'évacuation du site radioactif
excerpt: Kolwezi, le 7 avril 2026 - Le Service d'Assistance et d'Appui aux Mines Artisanales et à Petite Echelle (SAEMAPE) a lancé une opération d'identification des mineurs artisanaux dans la province du Lualaba, suite à l'évacuation du site de résidus T17 en raison d'inquiétudes liées aux matières radioactives.
title_en: SAEMAPE Launches Artisanal Miner Identification After Evacuation of Radioactive Site
excerpt_en: Kolwezi, April 7, 2026 - The Service for Assistance and Support of Artisanal and Small-Scale Mining (SAEMAPE) has launched an operation to identify artisanal miners in Lualaba province, following the evacuation of the T17 tailings site over concerns related to radioactive materia
body_en:
Kolwezi, April 7, 2026 - The Service for Assistance and Support of Artisanal and Small-Scale Mining (SAEMAPE) has launched an operation to identify artisanal miners in Lualaba province, following the evacuation of the T17 tailings site over concerns related to radioactive materials.
The T17 site, located within the Kamoto Copper Company concession, was declared a radiological emergency zone, prompting the removal of artisanal miners and triggering a broader reorganization of informal mining activities in the area.
As part of this transition, SAEMAPE began its identification campaign on April 4 at the Kasulo site in Kolwezi. The initiative follows an earlier phase focused on registering mining cooperatives, with the aim of establishing a reliable database of actors operating in the artisanal mining sector.
Officials say the operation is intended to formalize artisanal mining, improve oversight, and enhance safety conditions for miners working in often unregulated and hazardous environments.
SAEMAPE leadership described the process as a key step toward structuring the sector and reducing disorder at mining sites. Provincial authorities emphasized that better identification would also help enforce safety standards and improve governance in mining areas.
On the ground, the process began with the symbolic issuance of identification cards to representatives of several mining cooperatives operating at Kasulo, alongside individual artisanal miners.
Stakeholders involved in the sector have largely welcomed the initiative, viewing it as a move toward greater organization and recognition of their activities. Many miners expressed hope that formal identification would improve working conditions and provide greater legitimacy for their work.
According to SAEMAPE, the initial phase targets miners relocated from the T17 site and plans to redistribute them to designated artisanal zones, including Kasulo, UCK, and Menuiserie.
Authorities indicate that the program will be gradually extended across Lualaba province as part of broader efforts to regulate artisanal mining and strengthen control over mineral extraction activities.
body_fr:
Kolwezi, le 7 avril 2026 – Le Service d'Assistance et d'Appui aux Mines Artisanales et à Petite Echelle (SAEMAPE) a lancé une opération d'identification des mineurs artisanaux dans la province du Lualaba, suite à l'évacuation du site de résidus T17 en raison d'inquiétudes liées aux matières radioactives.
Le site T17, situé dans la concession de Kamoto Copper Company, a été déclaré zone d’urgence radiologique, entraînant le retrait des mineurs artisanaux et déclenchant une réorganisation plus large des activités minières informelles dans la région.
Dans le cadre de cette transition, la SAEMAPE a débuté sa campagne d'identification le 4 avril sur le site de Kasulo à Kolwezi. L'initiative fait suite à une phase antérieure axée sur l'enregistrement des coopératives minières, dans le but d'établir une base de données fiable des acteurs opérant dans le secteur minier artisanal.
Les responsables affirment que l'opération vise à formaliser l'exploitation minière artisanale, à améliorer la surveillance et à renforcer les conditions de sécurité des mineurs travaillant dans des environnements souvent non réglementés et dangereux.
Les dirigeants de la SAEMAPE ont décrit le processus comme une étape clé vers la structuration du secteur et la réduction du désordre sur les sites miniers. Les autorités provinciales ont souligné qu'une meilleure identification contribuerait également à faire respecter les normes de sécurité et à améliorer la gouvernance dans les zones minières.
Sur le terrain, le processus a commencé par la délivrance symbolique de cartes d'identité aux représentants de plusieurs coopératives minières opérant à Kasulo, aux côtés de mineurs artisanaux individuels.
Les acteurs du secteur ont largement accueilli favorablement cette initiative, y voyant une démarche vers une plus grande organisation et reconnaissance de leurs activités. De nombreux mineurs ont exprimé l’espoir qu’une identification formelle améliorerait les conditions de travail et donnerait une plus grande légitimité à leur travail.
Selon la SAEMAPE, la phase initiale cible les mineurs relocalisés du site T17 et prévoit de les redistribuer vers des zones artisanales désignées, notamment Kasulo, UCK et Menuiserie.
Les autorités indiquent que le programme sera progressivement étendu à toute la province de Lualaba dans le cadre d'efforts plus larges visant à réglementer l'exploitation minière artisanale et à renforcer le contrôle sur les activités d'extraction minière.

title: Japan Funds Major Electricity Upgrade Project in Kinshasa’s Mont-Amba District
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 20, 2026 - Work has officially begun on a large-scale electricity infrastructure project in the Mont-Amba district of Kinshasa, supported by a Japanese grant of approximately USD 27 million aimed at improving power supply reliability and access. The funding, equiv
title_en: Japan Funds Major Electricity Upgrade Project in Kinshasa’s Mont-Amba District
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 20, 2026 - Work has officially begun on a large-scale electricity infrastructure project in the Mont-Amba district of Kinshasa, supported by a Japanese grant of approximately USD 27 million aimed at improving power supply reliability and access. The funding, equiv
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 20, 2026 - Work has officially begun on a large-scale electricity infrastructure project in the Mont-Amba district of Kinshasa, supported by a Japanese grant of approximately USD 27 million aimed at improving power supply reliability and access.
The funding, equivalent to 3.898 billion Japanese yen, has been provided to the National Electricity Company SNEL SA under a cooperation framework supported by the Japan International Cooperation Agency Japan International Cooperation Agency (JICA).
The project targets the stabilization of electricity distribution across several communes in Mont-Amba, including Limete, Lemba, Matete, Ngaba, and Kisenso. It involves the installation of new 220 kV high-voltage transformers and the construction of control rooms at the Funa and Liminga substations.
Authorities say the infrastructure upgrade is expected to improve electricity reliability, support local economic activity, and enhance living conditions in one of Kinshasa’s most densely populated districts.
The works, initially planned for 2025 following the signing of the grant agreement between Japan and the DRC, officially began two weeks ago and are scheduled to run for 24 months.
Implementation is being carried out by international engineering firms selected through a competitive procurement process, including Trust Engineering Partners and Yachiyo Engineering.
According to project stakeholders, the grant does not involve direct cash transfers to the national utility. Instead, funds are managed jointly within the cooperation framework between both governments, with contractors selected through tender procedures after technical feasibility studies.
Officials involved in the project emphasize that the initiative reflects a model of infrastructure cooperation focused on transparency, technical oversight, and results-based implementation, in line with public procurement standards.
The project is part of broader efforts to strengthen urban energy infrastructure in Kinshasa, where demand for electricity continues to outpace supply due to rapid population growth and expanding economic activity.

body_en:
Masisi, April 10, 2026 - Heavy fighting erupted early Friday between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters in the localities of Mahanga and Kilongo, in Masisi territory, heightening tensions in a region already affected by recurrent violence.
According to local sources, the clashes began around 5:00 a.m., with sustained exchanges of heavy and light weapons fire reported for several hours. The violence triggered panic among civilians in nearby villages.
The fighting took place in the Osso Banyungu sector, a strategic area near Buhimba on the border between Masisi and Walikale territories. The zone is frequently the scene of armed confrontations due to its importance for territorial control.
Sources indicate that Wazalendo fighters launched an offensive aimed at retaking positions held by AFC/M23 elements in Mahanga and Kilongo.
The situation remains volatile, with ongoing insecurity prompting some residents to flee toward safer areas as fears of further escalation persist.

title: Authorities Warn of Alleged Rwandan Military Camp in Kabare
excerpt: Kabare, April 20, 2026 - The provincial government of South Kivu has raised concerns over reports of a Rwandan military presence in Kabare territory, warning of what it describes as a serious violation of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s sovereignty. In a statement, provincial
title_en: Authorities Warn of Alleged Rwandan Military Camp in Kabare
excerpt_en: Kabare, April 20, 2026 - The provincial government of South Kivu has raised concerns over reports of a Rwandan military presence in Kabare territory, warning of what it describes as a serious violation of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s sovereignty. In a statement, provincial
body_en:
Kabare, April 20, 2026 - The provincial government of South Kivu has raised concerns over reports of a Rwandan military presence in Kabare territory, warning of what it describes as a serious violation of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s sovereignty.
In a statement, provincial authorities said local residents had reported the establishment of a military camp in the village of Mumosho, an area currently under the control of AFC/M23 rebels. Officials allege that Rwandan soldiers recently entered the area and began setting up a base.
The provincial government described the development as a “grave attack” on the country’s territorial integrity and a violation of ongoing peace efforts aimed at stabilizing eastern DRC.
Authorities also warned of the risks posed to civilian populations, citing concerns over the militarization of inhabited areas and the potential consolidation of a foreign presence on Congolese soil.
The South Kivu administration called for the immediate halt to any construction linked to the reported camp and demanded the withdrawal of all foreign forces from the territory. It also urged the central government to take urgent measures to restore state authority in the affected areas.
Officials said they would continue to document alleged violations while working with national institutions to support efforts aimed at protecting civilians and preserving territorial integrity.
The province remains one of the main theaters of conflict in eastern DRC, where AFC/M23 rebels continue to operate across several territories despite previous withdrawals from key urban centers.

title: Le premier groupe de migrants expulsés par les États-Unis arrive à Kinshasa dans le cadre d’un arrangement temporaire
excerpt: Kinshasa, le 17 avril 2026 - Le gouvernement de la République démocratique du Congo a confirmé l'arrivée du premier groupe de migrants expulsés des États-Unis, suite à un arrangement temporaire convenu entre Kinshasa et Washington. Selon un communiqué du Mini
title_en: First Group of US-Deported Migrants Arrives in Kinshasa Under Temporary Arrangement
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 17, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has confirmed the arrival of the first group of migrants deported from the United States, following a temporary arrangement agreed between Kinshasa and Washington. According to a statement from the Mini
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 17, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has confirmed the arrival of the first group of migrants deported from the United States, following a temporary arrangement agreed between Kinshasa and Washington.
According to a statement from the Ministry of Communication and Media, 15 individuals were received in the capital on Friday, April 17, under a schedule coordinated by the competent authorities.
The government clarified that the arrivals are being admitted under short-stay permits in line with national immigration law and the country’s international commitments. Officials stressed that the arrangement does not constitute a permanent relocation or settlement program.
Authorities further indicated that the reception, accommodation, and logistical support for the individuals are being financed by the United States, under conditions that comply with security protocols and administrative procedures governing the movement of persons.
Kinshasa described the arrangement as strictly temporary, limited in duration, and managed under controlled conditions, while reaffirming its commitment to humanitarian principles, national sovereignty, and public interest.
The agreement forms part of broader diplomatic understandings between the DRC and the United States, which have recently expanded cooperation in areas including migration management and strategic partnerships.
However, the development has triggered strong reactions from opposition groups, civil society actors, and human rights organizations. Critics argue that the arrangement raises security and humanitarian concerns and have called for greater transparency regarding its implementation.
Some opposition voices have linked their concerns to historical precedents in the Great Lakes region, warning against potential security risks in sensitive border areas, particularly in eastern Congo, where displacement crises have previously had cross-border consequences.
The government, for its part, maintains that the arrangement is tightly regulated and will be implemented in full compliance with national law and international obligations.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, le 17 avril 2026 - Le gouvernement de la République démocratique du Congo a confirmé l'arrivée du premier groupe de migrants expulsés des États-Unis, suite à un arrangement temporaire convenu entre Kinshasa et Washington.
Selon un communiqué du ministère de la Communication et des Médias, 15 personnes ont été reçues dans la capitale, vendredi 17 avril, selon un calendrier coordonné par les autorités compétentes.
Le gouvernement a précisé que les arrivées sont admises avec des permis de court séjour, conformément à la loi nationale sur l’immigration et aux engagements internationaux du pays. Les responsables ont souligné que cet arrangement ne constitue pas un programme permanent de réinstallation ou d'installation.
Les autorités ont en outre indiqué que l'accueil, l'hébergement et le soutien logistique des personnes étaient financés par les États-Unis, dans des conditions conformes aux protocoles de sécurité et aux procédures administratives régissant la circulation des personnes.
Kinshasa a décrit l'accord comme étant strictement temporaire, limité dans le temps et géré dans des conditions contrôlées, tout en réaffirmant son engagement envers les principes humanitaires, la souveraineté nationale et l'intérêt public.
L'accord fait partie d'accords diplomatiques plus larges entre la RDC et les États-Unis, qui ont récemment élargi leur coopération dans des domaines tels que la gestion des migrations et les partenariats stratégiques.
Cependant, cette évolution a suscité de vives réactions de la part des groupes d’opposition, des acteurs de la société civile et des organisations de défense des droits humains. Les critiques affirment que l’accord soulève des problèmes de sécurité et humanitaires et ont appelé à une plus grande transparence quant à sa mise en œuvre.
Certaines voix de l’opposition ont lié leurs inquiétudes aux précédents historiques dans la région des Grands Lacs, mettant en garde contre des risques potentiels pour la sécurité dans les zones frontalières sensibles, en particulier dans l’est du Congo, où les crises de déplacement ont déjà eu des conséquences transfrontalières.
Le gouvernement, pour sa part, maintient que cet accord est étroitement réglementé et sera mis en œuvre dans le plein respect de la législation nationale et des obligations internationales.

title_en: Mining Sector Under Scrutiny as Government Flags Link to Insecurity
excerpt_en: Bunia, April 20, 2026 - The Minister of Mines, Louis Watum Kabamba, has arrived in Bunia for an official visit aimed at assessing the mining sector amid growing concerns over its role in financing armed groups and sustaining insecurity in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The
body_en:
Bunia, April 20, 2026 - The Minister of Mines, Louis Watum Kabamba, has arrived in Bunia for an official visit aimed at assessing the mining sector amid growing concerns over its role in financing armed groups and sustaining insecurity in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The visit, part of a broader tour covering Ituri, Bas-Uélé, and Maniema provinces from April 19 to 23, focuses on strengthening oversight of both artisanal and industrial mining activities in resource-rich areas, particularly those linked to gold production.
Authorities say the mission seeks to improve governance of the sector, enhance state control over extraction and trade chains, and address informal mining networks that largely operate outside regulatory frameworks.
However, the government acknowledges that mining remains closely tied to insecurity in several territories of Ituri. In areas such as Djugu and Mambasa, mineral exploitation has repeatedly been associated with the financing of armed groups and the expansion of illicit trade networks.
Speaking during the visit, the minister stressed the need for stronger mineral traceability systems and reforms aimed at cutting off illegal flows that deprive the state of revenue while fueling instability.
Local observers and stakeholders have long raised concerns over unregulated extraction, warning that competition for control of mining sites has become a key driver of violence in the region.
In Ituri, minerals are increasingly viewed not only as an economic asset but also as a strategic resource that shapes armed group activity and territorial control. Despite ongoing military operations, weak regulation of extraction and trade continues to sustain a parallel economy linked to conflict dynamics.
The minister’s mission is expected to feed into broader reform efforts, though analysts note that lasting impact will depend on coordinated action between security forces, mining authorities, and governance institutions to disrupt illicit supply chains and restore state oversight.
body_fr:
Bunia, le 20 avril 2026 - Le ministre des Mines, Louis Watum Kabamba, est arrivé à Bunia pour une visite officielle visant à évaluer le secteur minier dans un contexte d'inquiétudes croissantes quant à son rôle dans le financement des groupes armés et le maintien de l'insécurité dans l'est de la République démocratique du Congo.
La visite, qui fait partie d'une tournée plus large couvrant les provinces de l'Ituri, du Bas-Uélé et du Maniema du 19 au 23 avril, se concentre sur le renforcement de la surveillance des activités minières artisanales et industrielles dans les zones riches en ressources, en particulier celles liées à la production d'or.
Les autorités affirment que la mission vise à améliorer la gouvernance du secteur, à renforcer le contrôle de l’État sur les chaînes d’extraction et de commerce, et à s’attaquer aux réseaux miniers informels qui opèrent en grande partie en dehors des cadres réglementaires.
Le gouvernement reconnaît cependant que l’exploitation minière reste étroitement liée à l’insécurité dans plusieurs territoires de l’Ituri. Dans des régions telles que Djugu et Mambasa, l’exploitation minière a été associée à plusieurs reprises au financement de groupes armés et à l’expansion de réseaux commerciaux illicites.
S'exprimant lors de la visite, le ministre a souligné la nécessité de systèmes de traçabilité des minéraux plus solides et de réformes visant à mettre fin aux flux illégaux qui privent l'État de revenus tout en alimentant l'instabilité.
Les observateurs locaux et les parties prenantes expriment depuis longtemps leurs inquiétudes concernant l’extraction non réglementée, avertissant que la concurrence pour le contrôle des sites miniers est devenue un moteur clé de la violence dans la région.
En Ituri, les minerais sont de plus en plus considérés non seulement comme un atout économique, mais aussi comme une ressource stratégique qui façonne l’activité des groupes armés et leur contrôle territorial. Malgré les opérations militaires en cours, la faible réglementation de l’extraction et du commerce continue de soutenir une économie parallèle liée à la dynamique du conflit.
La mission du ministre devrait alimenter des efforts de réforme plus larges, même si les analystes notent que l’impact durable dépendra d’une action coordonnée entre les forces de sécurité, les autorités minières et les institutions de gouvernance pour perturber les chaînes d’approvisionnement illicites et rétablir la surveillance de l’État.

title: IRDH Calls for Creation of Mining Royalties Observatory Amid Rising Scrutiny of Extractive Sector
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 21, 2026 - As the Democratic Republic of Congo expands its role in global critical minerals supply chains, a leading civil society organization is urging stronger oversight of mining revenues and corporate accountability through the creation of a Mining Royalties
title_en: IRDH Calls for Creation of Mining Royalties Observatory Amid Rising Scrutiny of Extractive Sector
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 21, 2026 - As the Democratic Republic of Congo expands its role in global critical minerals supply chains, a leading civil society organization is urging stronger oversight of mining revenues and corporate accountability through the creation of a Mining Royalties
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 21, 2026 - As the Democratic Republic of Congo expands its role in global critical minerals supply chains, a leading civil society organization is urging stronger oversight of mining revenues and corporate accountability through the creation of a Mining Royalties Observatory.
The Institute for Human Rights Research (IRDH) says the initiative is necessary to address persistent inequalities in the extractive sector and ensure that revenues from mining activities translate into tangible benefits for local communities.
The proposal comes as the country strengthens copper export partnerships with the United States, targeting annual shipments of around 500,000 tons. The operations involve state-owned interests through Gécamines, trading and logistics arrangements with Mercuria Energy Group, and financial backing from the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation.
According to IRDH, the expansion of mining cooperation is reshaping governance expectations in the sector, particularly through emerging initiatives that emphasize traceability and supply chain transparency, including what stakeholders refer to as the “Vault” framework.
The organization argues that while new investors such as KoBold Metals and Virtus Minerals Inc. are generating optimism, human rights compliance must become a binding condition rather than a voluntary commitment.
IRDH notes that the Congolese mining landscape remains dominated by major international groups, including Glencore and other global operators active in copper and cobalt production. It warns that the concentration of mining rights among a limited number of actors makes independent oversight increasingly necessary.
The sector continues to attract substantial financing from international institutions such as the World Bank Group, the African Development Bank, and the Africa Finance Corporation. However, IRDH says these investments have not yet translated into proportionate improvements in living conditions in mining-affected communities.
The proposed Mining Royalties Observatory would aim to shift civil society engagement from advocacy to legal enforcement. It would be tasked with consolidating documentation on mining revenues and contractual obligations into legally actionable evidence for Congolese courts, particularly in cases involving fraud, embezzlement, or environmental non-compliance.
Beyond the national level, the initiative also envisions cooperation with international regulatory bodies, including securities market authorities in major jurisdictions, to increase corporate accountability.
IRDH argues that linking compliance with environmental and social standards to access to international finance could significantly alter incentives for multinational companies operating in the country.
As global competition intensifies over critical minerals, the proposal reflects broader debates over resource governance, revenue transparency, and the balance of power between states, corporations, and affected communities.

title: AFC/M23 Takes Control of Tushunguti, Biriko Under Threat

excerpt_en: South Kivu, April 8, 2026 - AFC/M23 rebels have taken control of the town of Tushunguti in Kalehe territory after intense clashes with local Wazalendo fighters, marking a further deterioration of the security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The fighting, which
body_en:
South Kivu, April 8, 2026 - AFC/M23 rebels have taken control of the town of Tushunguti in Kalehe territory after intense clashes with local Wazalendo fighters, marking a further deterioration of the security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The fighting, which occurred on April 7 in the Ziralo area of South Kivu, forced self-defense groups to retreat, allowing the rebels to seize the town, considered a strategic location near the border with North Kivu.
Local sources report that the fall of Tushunguti now places the town of Biriko, in Walikale territory, under direct threat. The area is regarded as particularly sensitive due to its proximity to recent conflict zones.
The escalation has triggered new waves of displacement, with hundreds of households fleeing toward safer areas. This movement adds to an already severe humanitarian crisis affecting the region.
No official casualty figures have been released at this stage. However, sources on the ground describe a rapidly worsening situation, with urgent needs for both security intervention and humanitarian assistance.
Residents, already affected by years of conflict, remain in a state of heightened fear as uncertainty persists over further advances and the broader trajectory of the violence.

title: Armed Attack on National Route 4 Leaves Seven Injured
excerpt: Kisangani, April 18, 2026 - Seven people were injured in an armed attack on a passenger bus along National Route 4, about 54 kilometers from Kisangani, in the Bakumu-Mandombe sector. The incident occurred on Friday afternoon when a vehicle belonging to a transport agency en route
title_en: Armed Attack on National Route 4 Leaves Seven Injured
excerpt_en: Kisangani, April 18, 2026 - Seven people were injured in an armed attack on a passenger bus along National Route 4, about 54 kilometers from Kisangani, in the Bakumu-Mandombe sector. The incident occurred on Friday afternoon when a vehicle belonging to a transport agency en route
body_en:
Kisangani, April 18, 2026 - Seven people were injured in an armed attack on a passenger bus along National Route 4, about 54 kilometers from Kisangani, in the Bakumu-Mandombe sector.
The incident occurred on Friday afternoon when a vehicle belonging to a transport agency en route to Butembo was ambushed by armed men reportedly wearing military uniforms. According to eyewitnesses, the assailants opened fire, wounding several passengers.
Five of the injured were transported back to Kisangani for medical treatment due to the severity of their condition, while two others continued their journey toward Bafwasende.
Passengers reported that a soldier aboard the bus responded to the attack, leading to an exchange of gunfire that lasted several minutes. During the incident, the driver was forced off the road and taken toward a nearby forest before later managing to return, reportedly after the attackers withdrew.
Despite the violence, no property was reported stolen. Witnesses also noted that military reinforcements arrived at the scene after the attack had ended.
In a separate development, three young men were arrested at a checkpoint on the Ituri road several hours after the incident. Authorities said the suspects raised suspicion due to their appearance and were found in possession of a mobile phone they were unable to unlock. They were taken into custody in Kisangani as investigations continue.

title: Le Parlement de la RDC avance sur l’accord de paix au Rwanda et l’accord stratégique américain
excerpt: Kinshasa, le 14 avril 2026 - L'Assemblée nationale de la République démocratique du Congo a déclaré recevables deux projets de loi ratifiant les accords signés avec le Rwanda et les États-Unis, marquant une étape importante dans le processus législatif des deux initiatives diplomatiques. Le texte
title_en: DRC Parliament Moves Forward on Rwanda Peace Deal and US Strategic Agreement
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 14, 2026 - The National Assembly of the Democratic Republic of Congo has declared admissible two draft laws ratifying agreements signed with Rwanda and the United States, marking an important step in the legislative process for both diplomatic initiatives. The tex
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 14, 2026 - The National Assembly of the Democratic Republic of Congo has declared admissible two draft laws ratifying agreements signed with Rwanda and the United States, marking an important step in the legislative process for both diplomatic initiatives.
The texts, presented on April 13, have been referred to the Foreign Affairs Committee for detailed examination before a possible plenary vote.
The agreements include a peace framework between Kinshasa and Kigali, as well as a strategic partnership between the DRC and the United States covering key sectors such as security, critical minerals, infrastructure, and economic cooperation.
Among the lawmakers reacting to the development, MP Hermès Itina Mayamba welcomed the parliamentary decision, describing both agreements as a potential turning point for peace and development in the country.
He stated that the peace accord with Rwanda and the strategic partnership with the United States could contribute to stabilizing the security situation in eastern Congo while also supporting long-term economic growth.
The legislator emphasized that the National Assembly was acting within its constitutional mandate by authorizing the ratification process of international treaties, which he said provides legal backing for government commitments.
He further noted that the initiatives come at a critical moment, as the country continues to face prolonged insecurity in its eastern provinces, and stressed the importance of institutional action to support peacebuilding efforts.
MP Itina also praised the diplomatic efforts of President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo, highlighting his role in advancing negotiations that led to the agreements. He similarly acknowledged the contribution of the government led by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka and Foreign Affairs Minister Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner.
According to parliamentary procedure, the Foreign Affairs Committee will now conduct an in-depth review of both agreements before submitting its report to the plenary for further debate and potential ratification.
If approved, the agreements would enter into force as binding international commitments, shaping both the DRC’s regional security framework and its strategic economic partnerships.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, le 14 avril 2026 - L'Assemblée nationale de la République démocratique du Congo a déclaré recevables deux projets de loi ratifiant les accords signés avec le Rwanda et les États-Unis, marquant une étape importante dans le processus législatif des deux initiatives diplomatiques.
Les textes, présentés le 13 avril, ont été renvoyés en commission des Affaires étrangères pour un examen approfondi avant un éventuel vote en plénière.
Les accords comprennent un cadre de paix entre Kinshasa et Kigali, ainsi qu'un partenariat stratégique entre la RDC et les États-Unis couvrant des secteurs clés tels que la sécurité, les minéraux critiques, les infrastructures et la coopération économique.
Parmi les législateurs réagissant à cette évolution, le député Hermès Itina Mayamba a salué la décision parlementaire, décrivant les deux accords comme un tournant potentiel pour la paix et le développement du pays.
Il a déclaré que l'accord de paix avec le Rwanda et le partenariat stratégique avec les États-Unis pourraient contribuer à stabiliser la situation sécuritaire dans l'est du Congo tout en soutenant la croissance économique à long terme.
Le législateur a souligné que l'Assemblée nationale agissait dans le cadre de son mandat constitutionnel en autorisant le processus de ratification des traités internationaux, qui, selon lui, fournit un soutien juridique aux engagements du gouvernement.
Il a en outre noté que ces initiatives intervenaient à un moment critique, alors que le pays continue de faire face à une insécurité prolongée dans ses provinces orientales, et a souligné l'importance d'une action institutionnelle pour soutenir les efforts de consolidation de la paix.
Le député Itina a également salué les efforts diplomatiques du président Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo, soulignant son rôle dans l'avancement des négociations qui ont abouti aux accords. Il a également reconnu la contribution du gouvernement dirigé par la Première ministre Judith Suminwa Tuluka et la ministre des Affaires étrangères Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner.
Conformément à la procédure parlementaire, la commission des affaires étrangères procédera désormais à un examen approfondi des deux accords avant de soumettre son rapport à la plénière pour un débat plus approfondi et une éventuelle ratification.
S’ils sont approuvés, les accords entreraient en vigueur en tant qu’engagements internationaux contraignants, façonnant à la fois le cadre de sécurité régionale de la RDC et ses partenariats économiques stratégiques.

title: L’OIM clarifie son rôle dans l’accord sur les migrants entre la RDC et les États-Unis alors que le débat s’intensifie à Kinshasa
excerpt: Kinshasa, 21 avril 2026 - L'Organisation internationale pour les migrations (OIM) a précisé qu'elle ne participe pas aux accords bilatéraux comme l'arrangement entre la République démocratique du Congo et les États-Unis concernant l'accueil temporaire des migrants expulsés.
title_en: IOM Clarifies Role in DRC-US Migrant Arrangement as Debate Grows in Kinshasa
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 21, 2026 - The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has clarified that it does not participate in bilateral agreements such as the arrangement between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United States concerning the temporary reception of deported m
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 21, 2026 - The International Organization for Migration (IOM) has clarified that it does not participate in bilateral agreements such as the arrangement between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United States concerning the temporary reception of deported migrants.
The clarification comes after the Congolese government requested humanitarian support for the first group of 15 migrants who arrived in Kinshasa under the agreement between Washington and Kinshasa.
In a statement, the UN migration agency stressed that it is not involved in the negotiation or implementation of bilateral migration deals and reserves the right to limit or suspend its involvement if minimum protection standards cannot be guaranteed. It added that any questions regarding the scope or terms of such agreements should be directed to national authorities.
The IOM also reiterated that its assistance is strictly humanitarian and includes voluntary return programs only when migrants provide free, prior, and informed consent.
The clarification comes amid growing debate over the agreement, which has already seen its first operational phase implemented with the arrival of an initial group of migrants in Kinshasa on April 17.
Government authorities maintain that the arrangement is temporary, regulated under national law, and part of a broader diplomatic cooperation framework with the United States. Officials have described the program as a short-term hosting mechanism rather than a permanent resettlement policy.
However, the initiative continues to generate political and civil society reactions within the country. Critics, including opposition figures and human rights organizations, have raised concerns about transparency, security implications, and the lack of clarity over the migrants’ nationalities and final destinations.
Some voices have also drawn historical parallels with past regional displacement crises in the Great Lakes region, warning about potential risks associated with cross-border population movements in fragile security contexts.
Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka has previously described the arrangement as a cooperative service provided by the DRC to the United States, while emphasizing its temporary nature and the fact that the costs of accommodation and support are covered by the U.S. side.
As discussions continue, the government maintains that the framework remains strictly transitional and subject to international humanitarian standards and national immigration law.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, 21 avril 2026 - L'Organisation internationale pour les migrations (OIM) a précisé qu'elle ne participe pas aux accords bilatéraux comme l'arrangement entre la République démocratique du Congo et les États-Unis concernant l'accueil temporaire des migrants expulsés.
Cette clarification intervient après que le gouvernement congolais a demandé une aide humanitaire pour le premier groupe de 15 migrants arrivés à Kinshasa dans le cadre de l'accord entre Washington et Kinshasa.
Dans un communiqué, l'agence des migrations des Nations Unies a souligné qu'elle n'est pas impliquée dans la négociation ou la mise en œuvre d'accords migratoires bilatéraux et se réserve le droit de limiter ou de suspendre son implication si des normes minimales de protection ne peuvent être garanties. Il a ajouté que toute question concernant la portée ou les conditions de ces accords devrait être adressée aux autorités nationales.
L'OIM a également réitéré que son aide est strictement humanitaire et comprend des programmes de retour volontaire uniquement lorsque les migrants donnent leur consentement libre, préalable et éclairé.
Cette clarification intervient dans un contexte de débat croissant autour de l'accord, dont la première phase opérationnelle a déjà été mise en œuvre avec l'arrivée d'un premier groupe de migrants à Kinshasa le 17 avril.
Les autorités gouvernementales soutiennent que l’accord est temporaire, réglementé par le droit national et s’inscrit dans un cadre de coopération diplomatique plus large avec les États-Unis. Les responsables ont décrit le programme comme un mécanisme d'accueil à court terme plutôt que comme une politique de réinstallation permanente.
Cependant, l’initiative continue de susciter des réactions politiques et de la société civile dans le pays. Les critiques, notamment des personnalités de l’opposition et des organisations de défense des droits de l’homme, ont exprimé leurs inquiétudes concernant la transparence, les implications en matière de sécurité et le manque de clarté sur les nationalités et les destinations finales des migrants.
Certaines voix ont également établi des parallèles historiques avec les crises régionales de déplacement passées dans la région des Grands Lacs, mettant en garde contre les risques potentiels associés aux mouvements transfrontaliers de population dans des contextes de sécurité fragiles.
La Première ministre Judith Suminwa Tuluka a précédemment décrit cet accord comme un service coopératif fourni par la RDC aux États-Unis, tout en soulignant son caractère temporaire et le fait que les frais d'hébergement et de soutien sont pris en charge par la partie américaine.
Alors que les discussions se poursuivent, le gouvernement maintient que le cadre reste strictement transitoire et soumis aux normes humanitaires internationales et au droit national de l’immigration.

title: DRC Approves Recovery Plan for $300 Million in Outstanding Industrial Promotion Fund Debts
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 13, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has approved a recovery and audit strategy to address an estimated $300 million in outstanding debts owed to the Industrial Promotion Fund (FPI), in a move aimed at unlocking blocked resources for indus
title_en: DRC Approves Recovery Plan for $300 Million in Outstanding Industrial Promotion Fund Debts
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 13, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has approved a recovery and audit strategy to address an estimated $300 million in outstanding debts owed to the Industrial Promotion Fund (FPI), in a move aimed at unlocking blocked resources for indus
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 13, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has approved a recovery and audit strategy to address an estimated $300 million in outstanding debts owed to the Industrial Promotion Fund (FPI), in a move aimed at unlocking blocked resources for industrial development.
The issue was presented at the 86th meeting of the Council of Ministers held on April 10 in Kinshasa, under the chairmanship of President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo. The briefing was delivered by the Minister of State, acting Minister of Industry, during discussions focused on improving the efficiency and financial sustainability of state development institutions.
According to the government, the unpaid debts-owed by various insolvent or non-compliant borrowers-represent a significant financial constraint on the Industrial Promotion Fund, which is intended to finance structuring projects for national economic development.
Officials stressed that recovering these funds is considered essential to support ongoing efforts to stimulate industrial growth and strengthen domestic production capacity.
The Minister of Industry also proposed the creation of a special government commission to oversee the recovery process. The body would be responsible for classifying debtors based on good or bad faith, negotiating settlement agreements, initiating legal recovery actions where necessary, and recommending measures to safeguard assets belonging to insolvent borrowers.
The proposal also includes the identification of internal operational weaknesses within the FPI, including governance gaps, limited technical capacity, and informal practices in project financing, which may have contributed to the accumulation of unpaid debts.
However, authorities cautioned that delays in recovery could further weaken both the institution and the broader industrial sector, which continues to require significant financial support.
The Industrial Promotion Fund (FPI), established under Ordinance-Law No. 89/031 of 1989 and later restructured into a public administrative and financial institution, is mandated to finance industrial development, support local production, and contribute to infrastructure linked to productive investment. It also manages resources derived from the industrial promotion tax and supports projects aimed at reducing import dependence.
The government says the recovery initiative is part of broader reforms to improve public financial management and ensure that development funds are effectively mobilized for industrial transformation and economic diversification.

excerpt_en: Walikale, April 8, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by Wazalendo fighters, repelled an offensive by AFC/M23 rebels in Walikale territory, following several hours of intense fighting on April 7. Clashes broke out around 11:00 a.m. in t
body_en:
Walikale, April 8, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by Wazalendo fighters, repelled an offensive by AFC/M23 rebels in Walikale territory, following several hours of intense fighting on April 7.
Clashes broke out around 11:00 a.m. in the villages of Minjenje and at the Nkingwe bridge, located in the Banakindi area within the Kisimba group. According to local and security sources, the rebels launched the हमला from Malemo in neighboring Masisi territory, targeting FARDC positions.
Heavy and light weapons were used during the exchanges, which lasted until approximately 5:00 p.m., triggering panic among residents in surrounding villages.
Security sources reported that FARDC and allied Wazalendo forces managed to contain and push back the attackers toward their positions in Malemo. A preliminary toll indicates that at least seven rebel fighters were killed during the clashes.

title_en: DRC-AFC/M23 Talks: Parties Agree on Urgent Humanitarian Measures
excerpt_en: Montreux, April 17, 2026 - Delegates from the Democratic Republic of Congo and the AFC/M23 rebellion have agreed on the urgent need to facilitate humanitarian aid and protect essential civilian infrastructure, following a new round of talks held in Switzerland. The negotiations,
body_en:
Montreux, April 17, 2026 - Delegates from the Democratic Republic of Congo and the AFC/M23 rebellion have agreed on the urgent need to facilitate humanitarian aid and protect essential civilian infrastructure, following a new round of talks held in Switzerland.
The negotiations, mediated by Qatar and conducted from April 13 to 17 in Montreux, resulted in what both sides described as “substantial progress” toward a protocol on humanitarian access and legal protection, according to a joint communiqué issued at the close of the discussions.
Both parties reaffirmed their commitment to respecting international humanitarian law, human rights law, and refugee law, while also adhering to the constitutional principles of the DRC.
The communiqué further highlights a pledge to refrain from targeting or damaging infrastructure critical to civilian survival. This includes food supplies, agricultural land, livestock, water installations, irrigation systems, as well as telecommunications, energy services, hospitals, and schools.
The renewed engagement marks a shift after months of stalled negotiations and comes against the backdrop of a deteriorating security situation in eastern DRC, where ongoing clashes have continued to impact civilian populations.
Observers say the outcome could represent a step toward easing humanitarian conditions, though its implementation will depend on sustained commitment from both sides on the ground.

title: L'AFDC-A retire son soutien à la motion de censure contre le ministre de l'Intérieur Jacquemain Shabani
excerpt: Kinshasa, le 14 avril 2026 - Une motion de censure visant le vice-Premier ministre chargé de l'Intérieur et de la Sécurité, Jacquemain Shabani, a perdu de son ampleur après que la formation politique AFDC-A a annoncé le retrait du soutien de ses élus signataires de l'accord.
title_en: AFDC-A Withdraws Support for Motion of No Confidence Against Interior Minister Jacquemain Shabani
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 14, 2026 - A motion of no confidence targeting Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the Interior and Security, Jacquemain Shabani, has lost momentum after the political grouping AFDC-A announced the withdrawal of support from its elected officials who had signed the
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 14, 2026 - A motion of no confidence targeting Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the Interior and Security, Jacquemain Shabani, has lost momentum after the political grouping AFDC-A announced the withdrawal of support from its elected officials who had signed the initiative.
The announcement was made by AFDC-A leader Senator Modeste Bahati Lukwebo, who distanced his political platform from what he described as an “isolated” move by two of its National Assembly members. According to the statement, the MPs acted without prior consultation and in violation of internal party rules.
The two deputies, Cizungu Ntaboba Landry and Placide Wemba Mukagwa, had signed the motion alongside other legislators, triggering the parliamentary procedure that could have led to the resignation or dismissal of the Interior Minister if sufficient signatures were secured and a plenary vote held.
Bahati Lukwebo called on the lawmakers to withdraw their signatures, reaffirming that AFDC-A, which is part of the ruling Sacred Union coalition supporting President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo, had not endorsed the initiative.
One of the MPs involved, Cizungu Ntaboba, later indicated his withdrawal from the parliamentary process linked to the motion. He had previously accused the Interior Ministry of serious governance failures, including interference in provincial administration, obstruction of parliamentary oversight, violations of institutional balance, and abuse of authority.
The motion itself had cited broader concerns over national security and alleged responsibility for persistent insecurity in parts of the country.
With AFDC-A’s withdrawal, the initiative appears to have been significantly weakened, raising uncertainty over whether it will gather enough parliamentary support to proceed to a vote in the National Assembly.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, le 14 avril 2026 - Une motion de censure visant le Vice-Premier ministre chargé de l'Intérieur et de la Sécurité, Jacquemain Shabani, a perdu de son ampleur après que la formation politique AFDC-A a annoncé le retrait du soutien de ses élus signataires de l'initiative.
L'annonce a été faite par le sénateur Modeste Bahati Lukwebo, leader de l'AFDC-A, qui a éloigné son programme politique de ce qu'il a décrit comme une démarche « isolée » de deux de ses membres de l'Assemblée nationale. Selon le communiqué, les députés ont agi sans consultation préalable et en violation des règles internes du parti.
Les deux députés, Cizungu Ntaboba Landry et Placide Wemba Mukagwa, avaient signé la motion aux côtés d'autres législateurs, déclenchant la procédure parlementaire qui aurait pu conduire à la démission ou à la destitution du ministre de l'Intérieur si un nombre suffisant de signatures avait été obtenu et si un vote en plénière avait eu lieu.
Bahati Lukwebo a appelé les législateurs à retirer leurs signatures, réaffirmant que l'AFDC-A, qui fait partie de la coalition au pouvoir de l'Union sacrée soutenant le président Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo, n'avait pas soutenu l'initiative.
L'un des députés impliqués, Cizungu Ntaboba, a par la suite indiqué son retrait du processus parlementaire lié à la motion. Il avait auparavant accusé le ministère de l'Intérieur de graves défaillances en matière de gouvernance, notamment d'ingérence dans l'administration provinciale, d'obstruction au contrôle parlementaire, de violations de l'équilibre institutionnel et d'abus d'autorité.
La motion elle-même faisait état de préoccupations plus larges concernant la sécurité nationale et d’une responsabilité présumée dans l’insécurité persistante dans certaines parties du pays.
Avec le retrait de l’AFDC-A, l’initiative semble avoir été considérablement affaiblie, ce qui soulève des incertitudes quant à savoir si elle rassemblera suffisamment de soutien parlementaire pour procéder à un vote à l’Assemblée nationale.

title_en: DRC Turns to Turkey to Boost Military Capabilities Amid Security Challenges in the East
excerpt_en: Ankara, April 20, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo is seeking to deepen defense cooperation with Turkey as part of efforts to modernize and strengthen the operational capacity of its armed forces, the government has announced. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National
body_en:
Ankara, April 20, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo is seeking to deepen defense cooperation with Turkey as part of efforts to modernize and strengthen the operational capacity of its armed forces, the government has announced.
Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense and Veterans Affairs Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita is on an official mission in Ankara, where he visited several Turkish defense industry facilities focused on advanced military technologies.
The visit follows a series of diplomatic and security engagements, including participation in a maritime security forum in Paris and bilateral discussions with French defense officials, as Kinshasa continues to diversify its international defense partnerships.
According to the Ministry of National Defense, the Ankara visit is a technical and exploratory mission aimed at gaining a detailed understanding of Turkey’s defense industrial capacity and identifying potential areas of cooperation in military modernization.
Turkey, a NATO member with a rapidly expanding defense sector, has become a reference point for countries seeking to develop domestic capabilities in areas such as drones, cybersecurity, and command-and-control systems.
During the visit, Congolese officials examined facilities linked to Turkish defense industry actors, including HAVELSAN, a company specializing in software systems, simulation technologies, autonomous systems, and cybersecurity solutions for military and civilian applications.
Authorities in Kinshasa say the objective is to support broader reforms aimed at building a more modern, self-reliant, and operationally effective defense structure capable of responding to evolving security threats.
The mission takes place against the backdrop of ongoing conflict in eastern DRC, where government forces continue to face armed groups, including the AFC/M23 rebellion, as well as broader regional security tensions.
Officials also referenced previous engagements with Turkish defense institutions, including participation in international defense exhibitions and bilateral agreements aimed at strengthening cooperation in military training, equipment, and industrial development.
At the end of his visit, the defense minister expressed satisfaction with the expertise observed and reaffirmed Kinshasa’s intention to strengthen military cooperation with Ankara, particularly in areas related to defense technology transfer and operational capacity building.
The government says such partnerships are part of a broader strategy to modernize the armed forces and enhance national sovereignty in defense capabilities.
body_fr:
Ankara, le 20 avril 2026 - La République démocratique du Congo cherche à approfondir sa coopération en matière de défense avec la Turquie dans le cadre des efforts visant à moderniser et à renforcer la capacité opérationnelle de ses forces armées, a annoncé le gouvernement.
Le vice-Premier ministre et ministre de la Défense nationale et des Anciens Combattants Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita est en mission officielle à Ankara, où il a visité plusieurs installations de l'industrie de défense turque axées sur les technologies militaires avancées.
Cette visite fait suite à une série d'engagements diplomatiques et sécuritaires, notamment la participation à un forum sur la sécurité maritime à Paris et des discussions bilatérales avec des responsables français de la défense, alors que Kinshasa continue de diversifier ses partenariats internationaux de défense.
Selon le ministère de la Défense nationale, la visite à Ankara est une mission technique et exploratoire visant à acquérir une compréhension détaillée de la capacité industrielle de défense de la Turquie et à identifier les domaines potentiels de coopération en matière de modernisation militaire.
La Turquie, membre de l’OTAN dont le secteur de la défense est en rapide expansion, est devenue une référence pour les pays cherchant à développer leurs capacités nationales dans des domaines tels que les drones, la cybersécurité et les systèmes de commandement et de contrôle.
Lors de la visite, des responsables congolais ont examiné des installations liées aux acteurs turcs de l'industrie de défense, notamment HAVELSAN, une société spécialisée dans les systèmes logiciels, les technologies de simulation, les systèmes autonomes et les solutions de cybersécurité pour applications militaires et civiles.
Les autorités de Kinshasa affirment que l’objectif est de soutenir des réformes plus larges visant à construire une structure de défense plus moderne, plus autonome et plus efficace sur le plan opérationnel, capable de répondre à l’évolution des menaces sécuritaires.
La mission se déroule dans le contexte du conflit en cours dans l’est de la RDC, où les forces gouvernementales continuent de faire face à des groupes armés, notamment la rébellion AFC/M23, ainsi qu’à des tensions sécuritaires régionales plus larges.
Les responsables ont également évoqué des engagements antérieurs avec les institutions de défense turques, notamment la participation à des expositions internationales de défense et des accords bilatéraux visant à renforcer la coopération en matière de formation militaire, d'équipement et de développement industriel.
Au terme de sa visite, le ministre de la Défense s’est félicité de l’expertise constatée et a réaffirmé l’intention de Kinshasa de renforcer la coopération militaire avec Ankara, notamment dans les domaines liés au transfert de technologies de défense et au renforcement des capacités opérationnelles.
Le gouvernement affirme que de tels partenariats font partie d’une stratégie plus large visant à moderniser les forces armées et à renforcer la souveraineté nationale en matière de capacités de défense.

title: DRC Adopts Strategic Mineral Reserve Framework to Strengthen State Control Over Key Resources
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 12, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has approved a draft decree establishing a strategic reserve for critical mineral substances, a decision aimed at stabilizing markets and reinforcing national control over strategic mining resources. Th
title_en: DRC Adopts Strategic Mineral Reserve Framework to Strengthen State Control Over Key Resources
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 12, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has approved a draft decree establishing a strategic reserve for critical mineral substances, a decision aimed at stabilizing markets and reinforcing national control over strategic mining resources. Th
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 12, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has approved a draft decree establishing a strategic reserve for critical mineral substances, a decision aimed at stabilizing markets and reinforcing national control over strategic mining resources.
The measure was adopted during the 86th meeting of the Council of Ministers held on April 10 in Kinshasa, under the chairmanship of President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo. The text was presented by the Minister of Mines, Louis Watum Kabamba, and concerns mineral substances deemed essential both to the Congolese economy and to international markets.
According to the government, the creation of this strategic reserve is intended to help stabilize prices of key mineral resources, support the structured development of the sector, and reinforce the country’s economic sovereignty over its natural wealth.
In the same session, the government also approved amendments to the decree governing the Regulatory and Control Authority for Markets of Strategic Mineral Substances, known as ARECOMS. The revised framework strengthens the institution’s mandate, which includes the regulation, supervision, and stabilization of strategic mineral markets across the country.
ARECOMS, a public administrative and technical body with legal, administrative, and financial autonomy, operates under the supervision of the Ministry of Mines. It is responsible for overseeing production and export activities in the strategic minerals sector, improving the business climate, and ensuring compliance with national regulations, including provisions related to anti-money laundering and the financing of terrorism.
Authorities also confirmed that ARECOMS will be responsible for managing the newly created strategic reserve and will have the capacity to establish operational offices and branches throughout the national territory to ensure effective implementation of its mandate.
Officials say the reform reflects a broader effort by the government to strengthen governance in the mining sector, enhance market stability, and improve the country’s economic and industrial positioning in global strategic mineral supply chains.

title: MONUSCO Reconnaissance Mission in Mambasa Blocked by Protesters
excerpt: Bunia, April 7, 2026 - A reconnaissance mission by United Nations peacekeepers in Mambasa territory, Ituri province, was disrupted by local protests on Monday, amid rising insecurity linked to repeated attacks by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF). The deployment, carried out by
title_en: MONUSCO Reconnaissance Mission in Mambasa Blocked by Protesters
excerpt_en: Bunia, April 7, 2026 - A reconnaissance mission by United Nations peacekeepers in Mambasa territory, Ituri province, was disrupted by local protests on Monday, amid rising insecurity linked to repeated attacks by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF). The deployment, carried out by
body_en:
Bunia, April 7, 2026 - A reconnaissance mission by United Nations peacekeepers in Mambasa territory, Ituri province, was disrupted by local protests on Monday, amid rising insecurity linked to repeated attacks by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF).
The deployment, carried out by the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO), aimed to assess the security situation and support efforts to protect civilians in the area.
According to MONUSCO officials, the mission was conducted in coordination with the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) as part of its civilian protection mandate. The initiative follows a series of deadly ADF attacks that have left dozens of civilians dead in recent weeks.
Local sources confirmed the arrival of peacekeepers on the outskirts of Mambasa. However, the convoy was blocked by groups of young protesters who erected barricades and burned tires to prevent MONUSCO forces from entering the area.
Residents cited growing frustration and mistrust toward the UN mission, which some accuse of failing to respond effectively to recurring violence by armed groups. Local authorities also reported a tense climate marked by skepticism among sections of the population.
Facing the resistance, MONUSCO personnel were forced to withdraw, according to multiple accounts. The incident underscores ongoing tensions between the peacekeeping mission and local communities, particularly in areas heavily affected by armed group activity.
Mambasa territory has experienced a resurgence of ADF attacks in recent months, with civilians frequently targeted in rural and mining zones. These attacks, often involving killings, abductions, and the destruction of property, have led to significant population displacement.
Despite joint military operations conducted by the FARDC and Ugandan forces, the ADF continues to operate across parts of Ituri as well as neighboring territories such as Irumu and Beni, maintaining a persistent threat to civilian populations.

Ihula, April 17, 2026 - A tense calm has settled in Ihula, in Walikale territory, a day after heavy fighting between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters forced residents to flee.
Clashes erupted on April 16 in the locality, located in the Balindu area of the Kisimba group, when Wazalendo elements launched an offensive on positions held by AFC/M23. The fighting triggered widespread panic, with civilians fleeing toward nearby Kalembe or seeking refuge in surrounding bush areas.
The human toll remains unclear, though local sources report that a rebel position was set on fire during the brief incursion by Wazalendo fighters.
Following the clashes, Wazalendo forces withdrew from the area, allowing AFC/M23 elements to reassert control over the locality.
Despite the lull in fighting, the situation remains volatile. Many residents have yet to return to their homes, opting to remain in safer areas amid fears of renewed violence.

title_en: “Save the DRC” Opposition Movement Holds Second Conclave, Denounces Political and Security Crisis
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 13, 2026 - The opposition movement “Save the DRC,” led by former President Joseph Kabila, has concluded its second conclave held from April 6 to 8, 2026, focusing on the country’s political, security, economic, and social situation. In a statement issued after the
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 13, 2026 - The opposition movement “Save the DRC,” led by former President Joseph Kabila, has concluded its second conclave held from April 6 to 8, 2026, focusing on the country’s political, security, economic, and social situation.
In a statement issued after the meeting, the movement said participants reviewed ongoing national crises and various domestic and international initiatives aimed at resolving them. The group, which operates from outside the Democratic Republic of Congo, was established in October 2025 in Nairobi and brings together exiled political figures and banned political actors.
The movement strongly criticized what it described as a “deliberate slide toward dictatorship” under the current administration, led by President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo, accusing it of political repression, restrictions on dissent, and refusal to engage in what it considers a credible national dialogue.
It further denounced alleged violations of fundamental rights, including attacks on political freedoms, targeted violence against dissenting voices, and the abandonment of civilian populations in parts of eastern Congo, particularly in Ituri and North Kivu, where armed groups continue to operate.
According to the movement’s communiqué, these situations constitute serious breaches of constitutional provisions and international humanitarian law, and reflect what it calls a broader crisis of governance.
“Save the DRC” also accused the government of ignoring the root causes of the ongoing crisis, including contested political legitimacy, governance failures, manipulation of judicial institutions, and the use of identity-based divisions for political control.
The group further criticized recent diplomatic agreements between Kinshasa and international partners, including arrangements with the United States concerning migration and other bilateral cooperation frameworks, arguing that such initiatives do not address underlying domestic instability.
Reaffirming its political position, the movement declared its opposition to any constitutional revision process, invoking Article 64 of the Constitution as justification for what it describes as a “defense of constitutional order.”
The conclave also reportedly examined regional and international mediation efforts, including past agreements such as the Sun City framework, arguing that current peace initiatives have failed to adequately address structural causes of conflict.
While operating in exile, the movement says it intends to continue mobilizing political support internationally, positioning itself as part of a broader opposition front challenging the current political order in Kinshasa.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, le 13 avril 2026 – Le mouvement d’opposition « Sauvons la RDC », dirigé par l’ancien président Joseph Kabila, a conclu son deuxième conclave tenu du 6 au 8 avril 2026, axé sur la situation politique, sécuritaire, économique et sociale du pays.
Dans un communiqué publié après la réunion, le mouvement a déclaré que les participants ont passé en revue les crises nationales en cours et diverses initiatives nationales et internationales visant à les résoudre. Le groupe, qui opère depuis l'extérieur de la République démocratique du Congo, a été créé en octobre 2025 à Nairobi et rassemble des personnalités politiques exilées et des acteurs politiques interdits.
Le mouvement a vivement critiqué ce qu’il a décrit comme un « glissement délibéré vers la dictature » sous l’administration actuelle, dirigée par le président Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo, l’accusant de répression politique, de restrictions à la dissidence et de refus de s’engager dans ce qu’il considère comme un dialogue national crédible.
Il a en outre dénoncé des violations présumées des droits fondamentaux, notamment des atteintes aux libertés politiques, des violences ciblées contre les voix dissidentes et l'abandon des populations civiles dans certaines parties de l'est du Congo, notamment en Ituri et au Nord-Kivu, où des groupes armés continuent d'opérer.
Selon le communiqué du mouvement, ces situations constituent de graves violations des dispositions constitutionnelles et du droit international humanitaire et reflètent ce qu’il appelle une crise de gouvernance plus large.
« Sauvons la RDC » accuse également le gouvernement d’ignorer les causes profondes de la crise actuelle, notamment la légitimité politique contestée, les échecs de gouvernance, la manipulation des institutions judiciaires et le recours aux divisions identitaires pour le contrôle politique.
Le groupe a en outre critiqué les récents accords diplomatiques entre Kinshasa et des partenaires internationaux, y compris les accords avec les États-Unis concernant la migration et d'autres cadres de coopération bilatérale, arguant que de telles initiatives ne s'attaquent pas à l'instabilité intérieure sous-jacente.
Réaffirmant sa position politique, le mouvement a déclaré son opposition à tout processus de révision constitutionnelle, invoquant l'article 64 de la Constitution pour justifier ce qu'il qualifie de « défense de l'ordre constitutionnel ».
Le conclave aurait également examiné les efforts de médiation régionaux et internationaux, y compris les accords passés tels que celui de Sun City, arguant que les initiatives de paix actuelles n'ont pas réussi à s'attaquer de manière adéquate aux causes structurelles du conflit.
Tout en opérant en exil, le mouvement affirme avoir l'intention de continuer à mobiliser un soutien politique au niveau international, en se positionnant comme faisant partie d'un front d'opposition plus large remettant en question l'ordre politique actuel à Kinshasa.

title: La RDC décrit l’accueil temporaire des migrants américains comme un « service » dans le cadre d’un accord bilatéral
excerpt: Kinshasa, le 20 avril 2026 - Le Premier ministre de la République démocratique du Congo a déclaré que l'accueil temporaire par le pays des migrants expulsés des États-Unis s'effectue dans le cadre d'un « service » coopératif dans le cadre d'un accord bilatéral entre Kinshasa et Washington.
title_en: DRC Describes Temporary US Migrant Reception as a “Service” Under Bilateral Arrangement
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 20, 2026 - The Prime Minister of the Democratic Republic of Congo has said that the country’s temporary reception of migrants deported from the United States is being carried out as a cooperative “service” under a bilateral arrangement between Kinshasa and Washing
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 20, 2026 - The Prime Minister of the Democratic Republic of Congo has said that the country’s temporary reception of migrants deported from the United States is being carried out as a cooperative “service” under a bilateral arrangement between Kinshasa and Washington.
Speaking in a media interview, Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka confirmed that the program involves the temporary hosting of third-country nationals transferred from the United States, describing the initiative as strictly transitional and time-limited.
She indicated that the individuals concerned are asylum seekers and suggested they originate from several Latin American countries, while noting that their presence in the DRC is part of an agreement involving U.S. immigration authorities and international partners, including the International Organization for Migration.
According to the Prime Minister, the arrangement is not intended as a long-term settlement mechanism, but rather a short-term humanitarian and logistical solution while alternative destinations are identified for the individuals concerned.
She emphasized that the United States is covering all associated costs, including accommodation and basic needs, and described the agreement as a form of cooperation in which the DRC is providing logistical support to a partner country.
Authorities in Kinshasa have reiterated that the program is temporary in nature and will be implemented in compliance with international humanitarian law and national legislation governing the entry and residence of foreigners.
The initiative has already begun with the arrival of an initial group of 15 individuals in Kinshasa on April 17, marking the start of the operational phase of the arrangement.
The program has, however, drawn political attention domestically, with parliamentary questions submitted to the National Assembly seeking clarification on its legal and operational framework. The initiatives have yet to be scheduled for plenary debate.
Government officials maintain that the arrangement is strictly controlled, temporary, and part of broader diplomatic cooperation between the DRC and the United States.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, le 20 avril 2026 - Le Premier ministre de la République démocratique du Congo a déclaré que l'accueil temporaire par le pays des migrants expulsés des États-Unis s'effectue dans le cadre d'un « service » coopératif dans le cadre d'un accord bilatéral entre Kinshasa et Washington.
S'exprimant dans une interview avec les médias, la Première ministre Judith Suminwa Tuluka a confirmé que le programme implique l'hébergement temporaire de ressortissants de pays tiers transférés des États-Unis, qualifiant l'initiative de strictement transitoire et limitée dans le temps.
Elle a indiqué que les individus concernés sont des demandeurs d'asile et a suggéré qu'ils soient originaires de plusieurs pays d'Amérique latine, tout en soulignant que leur présence en RDC s'inscrit dans le cadre d'un accord impliquant les autorités américaines de l'immigration et les partenaires internationaux, dont l'Organisation internationale pour les migrations.
Selon le Premier ministre, cet arrangement ne constitue pas un mécanisme de règlement à long terme, mais plutôt une solution humanitaire et logistique à court terme, le temps d'identifier des destinations alternatives pour les personnes concernées.
Elle a souligné que les États-Unis couvrent tous les coûts associés, y compris l'hébergement et les besoins de base, et a décrit l'accord comme une forme de coopération dans laquelle la RDC fournit un soutien logistique à un pays partenaire.
Les autorités de Kinshasa ont réitéré que le programme est de nature temporaire et qu'il sera mis en œuvre conformément au droit international humanitaire et à la législation nationale régissant l'entrée et le séjour des étrangers.
L'initiative a déjà commencé avec l'arrivée d'un premier groupe de 15 personnes à Kinshasa le 17 avril, marquant le début de la phase opérationnelle du dispositif.
Le programme a cependant attiré l'attention politique au niveau national, avec des questions parlementaires soumises à l'Assemblée nationale demandant des éclaircissements sur son cadre juridique et opérationnel. Les initiatives n’ont pas encore été programmées pour un débat en plénière.
Les responsables gouvernementaux soutiennent que cet accord est strictement contrôlé, temporaire et s’inscrit dans le cadre d’une coopération diplomatique plus large entre la RDC et les États-Unis.

title: DRC Central Bank Cuts Key Rate and Tightens Foreign Currency Controls
excerpt: Kinshasa, April 10, 2026 - The Central Bank of Congo (BCC) has lowered its key interest rate from 15.0% to 13.5% and introduced stricter regulations on the physical importation and use of foreign currency banknotes, following a Monetary Policy Committee meeting held on April 9 in
title_en: DRC Central Bank Cuts Key Rate and Tightens Foreign Currency Controls
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 10, 2026 - The Central Bank of Congo (BCC) has lowered its key interest rate from 15.0% to 13.5% and introduced stricter regulations on the physical importation and use of foreign currency banknotes, following a Monetary Policy Committee meeting held on April 9 in
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 10, 2026 - The Central Bank of Congo (BCC) has lowered its key interest rate from 15.0% to 13.5% and introduced stricter regulations on the physical importation and use of foreign currency banknotes, following a Monetary Policy Committee meeting held on April 9 in Kinshasa.
Chaired by Governor André Wameso, the committee said the decision aims to preserve macroeconomic stability amid ongoing global economic uncertainty, including energy market disruptions and rising international pressures on inflation and trade.
The BCC also reduced the marginal lending facility rate from 19% to 17.5%, while maintaining reserve requirement ratios unchanged for deposits in both local and foreign currency.
According to the central bank, the Congolese economy continues to show resilience, with growth projected at 6.2% in 2026, up from 5.8% the previous year, driven by strong performance in both mining and non-mining sectors. Inflation, meanwhile, has declined significantly, standing at 2.2% at the end of March 2026 compared to 10.1% a year earlier.
A key structural decision announced by the bank concerns foreign currency management. The BCC will establish exclusive authority over the physical importation of foreign currency banknotes within 12 months. Starting April 9, 2027, commercial banks will no longer be allowed to import physical foreign currency, and cash transactions in foreign currency are expected to be fully replaced by electronic payments.
Authorities say the measure is intended to strengthen financial system security, improve oversight, and combat money laundering and illicit financial flows.
The central bank also plans to introduce six-month maturity instruments for BCC bonds to improve liquidity management.
Officials noted that the Congolese franc has shown mixed performance, with slight appreciation on the parallel market but depreciation on the official market since the beginning of the year, reflecting cyclical demand for foreign exchange and seasonal pressures.
The monetary authorities stressed that the policy adjustments are part of broader efforts to maintain stability in a challenging global environment marked by volatile energy prices, geopolitical tensions, and tightening international financial conditions.
