title: L'envoyé de l'ONU rencontre le leader de RSF à Nairobi pour discuter de la désescalade au Soudan
excerpt: Nairobi, 6 avril 2026 ; L'Envoyé personnel des Nations Unies pour le Soudan, Pekka Haavisto, s'est entretenu lundi à Nairobi avec le commandant des Forces de soutien rapide Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, connu sous le nom de « Hemetti », dans le cadre des efforts en cours visant à explorer les voies menant à une désescalade dans le conflit au Soudan.
title_en: UN Envoy Meets RSF Leader in Nairobi to Discuss De-escalation in Sudan
excerpt_en: Nairobi April 6, 2026; The United Nations Personal Envoy for Sudan, Pekka Haavisto, held talks on Monday in Nairobi with Rapid Support Forces commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as “Hemetti,” as part of ongoing efforts to explore pathways toward de-escalation in Sudan’s confli
body_en:
Nairobi April 6, 2026; The United Nations Personal Envoy for Sudan, Pekka Haavisto, held talks on Monday in Nairobi with Rapid Support Forces commander Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as “Hemetti,” as part of ongoing efforts to explore pathways toward de-escalation in Sudan’s conflict.
The meeting in the Kenyan capital forms part of Haavisto’s first regional diplomatic tour aimed at advancing dialogue between Sudan’s warring parties. It follows earlier discussions in Khartoum with the head of Sudan’s Transitional Sovereign Council, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan.
According to the United Nations, the talks focused on practical steps to reduce violence and improve the protection of civilians. UN spokesperson Stéphane Dujarric described the engagement as a “constructive opportunity” to exchange views, adding that all parties consulted have expressed willingness to cooperate with the UN process.
He stressed that such commitments must quickly translate into tangible progress toward ending civilian suffering.
Prior to arriving in Kenya, Haavisto held consultations in Cairo with Egyptian officials, the Arab League, and representatives of the Sudanese diaspora. The mission comes amid a broader expansion of UN humanitarian operations in Sudan, including the return of Resident and Humanitarian Coordinator Denise Brown to Khartoum with a core UN team, marking a partial re-establishment of UN presence in the city.
The United Nations estimates that more than 1.6 million people have returned to Khartoum in recent months, despite ongoing risks from unexploded ordnance and damaged infrastructure.
Meanwhile, the humanitarian situation remains critical. A recent drone strike on Al Jabalayn Teaching Hospital in White Nile State killed 10 health workers and injured 22 others, according to UN reporting.
The UN’s 2026 Humanitarian Needs and Response Plan for Sudan seeks $2.9 billion to assist 20 million people but remains severely underfunded, with only 16% of required funding received to date.
body_fr:
Nairobi, 6 avril 2026 ; L'Envoyé personnel des Nations Unies pour le Soudan, Pekka Haavisto, s'est entretenu lundi à Nairobi avec le commandant des Forces de soutien rapide Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, connu sous le nom de « Hemetti », dans le cadre des efforts en cours visant à explorer les voies menant à une désescalade du conflit au Soudan.
La réunion dans la capitale kenyane fait partie de la première tournée diplomatique régionale de Haavisto visant à faire progresser le dialogue entre les parties belligérantes au Soudan. Cela fait suite à des discussions antérieures à Khartoum avec le chef du Conseil souverain de transition du Soudan, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan.
Selon les Nations Unies, les discussions se sont concentrées sur des mesures pratiques visant à réduire la violence et à améliorer la protection des civils. Le porte-parole de l'ONU, Stéphane Dujarric, a décrit cet engagement comme une « opportunité constructive » d'échanger des points de vue, ajoutant que toutes les parties consultées ont exprimé leur volonté de coopérer avec le processus de l'ONU.
Il a souligné que de tels engagements doivent rapidement se traduire par des progrès tangibles vers la fin des souffrances des civils.
Avant d'arriver au Kenya, Haavisto a tenu des consultations au Caire avec des responsables égyptiens, la Ligue arabe et des représentants de la diaspora soudanaise. La mission intervient dans le cadre d'une expansion plus large des opérations humanitaires de l'ONU au Soudan, y compris le retour de Denise Brown, coordinatrice humanitaire résidente, à Khartoum avec une équipe de base de l'ONU, marquant un rétablissement partiel de la présence de l'ONU dans la ville.
Les Nations Unies estiment que plus de 1,6 million de personnes sont retournées à Khartoum ces derniers mois, malgré les risques persistants liés aux munitions non explosées et aux infrastructures endommagées.
Pendant ce temps, la situation humanitaire reste critique. Une récente frappe de drone sur l'hôpital universitaire Al Jabalayn, dans l'État du Nil Blanc, a tué 10 agents de santé et en a blessé 22 autres, selon un rapport de l'ONU.
Le Plan de réponse et de besoins humanitaires de l’ONU pour le Soudan à l’horizon 2026 prévoit 2,9 milliards de dollars pour aider 20 millions de personnes, mais reste gravement sous-financé, avec seulement 16 % du financement requis reçu à ce jour.

title_en: Detained Sudanese Students in Egypt Risk Missing National Exams
excerpt_en: Egypt April 5, 2026 ; Sudanese families in Egypt are voicing growing concern as several secondary school students remain in detention just days before national exams are set to begin on April 13, raising fears they could miss a critical academic milestone. The detentions come ami
body_en:
Egypt April 5, 2026 ; Sudanese families in Egypt are voicing growing concern as several secondary school students remain in detention just days before national exams are set to begin on April 13, raising fears they could miss a critical academic milestone.
The detentions come amid a broader crackdown by Egyptian authorities on foreign nationals, a campaign that has affected thousands of Sudanese residents, including some with valid documentation.
Families say the situation threatens to prevent the students from sitting for the Sudan School Certificate examinations, potentially jeopardizing their academic futures.
One parent said her son has been held for several weeks, prompting the family to consider sending him back to Sudan to ensure he does not lose the school year, despite ongoing insecurity there. Another parent described the prospect of returning as both difficult and psychologically taxing, particularly given the uncertainties surrounding travel and safety.
Officials at the Sudanese Embassy in Cairo said the number of detained students remains limited, adding that efforts are underway to secure their release or facilitate their return to Sudan in time for the exams. Authorities are also exploring alternative arrangements to allow affected students to sit for exams individually or in small groups if necessary.
Coordination between Sudanese and Egyptian officials is ongoing, with a focus on ensuring that students can access examination centers under stable conditions.
In a joint statement, rights organizations called on Egyptian authorities to expedite legal procedures for detained students and consider temporary documentation measures to allow them to move freely during the examination period.
They also urged all parties to safeguard the education sector from the impact of conflict. Since the outbreak of war in April 2023, Sudan’s national examination system has faced significant disruptions, including delays, damage to educational infrastructure, and widespread displacement of students and teachers.
body_fr:
Égypte, 5 avril 2026 ; Les familles soudanaises en Égypte expriment leur inquiétude croissante alors que plusieurs élèves du secondaire restent en détention quelques jours seulement avant le début des examens nationaux, le 13 avril, faisant craindre qu'ils ne ratent une étape scolaire cruciale.
Ces détentions surviennent dans le cadre d'une répression plus large menée par les autorités égyptiennes contre les ressortissants étrangers, une campagne qui a touché des milliers de résidents soudanais, dont certains possédant des documents valides.
Les familles affirment que la situation menace d’empêcher les élèves de se présenter aux examens du Soudan School Certificate, ce qui pourrait compromettre leur avenir scolaire.
Un parent a déclaré que son fils était détenu depuis plusieurs semaines, ce qui a incité la famille à envisager de le renvoyer au Soudan pour s'assurer qu'il ne perde pas l'année scolaire, malgré l'insécurité qui y règne. Un autre parent a décrit la perspective du retour comme étant à la fois difficile et éprouvante sur le plan psychologique, en particulier compte tenu des incertitudes entourant le voyage et la sécurité.
Les responsables de l'ambassade du Soudan au Caire ont déclaré que le nombre d'étudiants détenus restait limité, ajoutant que des efforts étaient en cours pour obtenir leur libération ou faciliter leur retour au Soudan à temps pour les examens. Les autorités étudient également des dispositions alternatives pour permettre aux étudiants concernés de passer les examens individuellement ou en petits groupes si nécessaire.
La coordination entre les responsables soudanais et égyptiens est en cours, l'objectif étant de garantir que les étudiants puissent accéder aux centres d'examen dans des conditions stables.
Dans une déclaration commune, les organisations de défense des droits ont appelé les autorités égyptiennes à accélérer les procédures judiciaires pour les étudiants détenus et à envisager des mesures de délivrance de documents temporaires pour leur permettre de se déplacer librement pendant la période d'examen.
Ils ont également exhorté toutes les parties à protéger le secteur de l'éducation des conséquences du conflit. Depuis le déclenchement de la guerre en avril 2023, le système national d’examens soudanais a été confronté à d’importantes perturbations, notamment des retards, des dommages aux infrastructures éducatives et des déplacements massifs d’étudiants et d’enseignants.

title: Legal Group Warns of Systematic Attacks on Aid Convoys and Drone Strikes in Sudan
excerpt: Sudan April 7, 2026 ; A Sudanese legal monitoring organization has raised alarm over what it describes as a sustained and systematic pattern of attacks targeting humanitarian operations amid the ongoing conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF)
title_en: Legal Group Warns of Systematic Attacks on Aid Convoys and Drone Strikes in Sudan
excerpt_en: Sudan April 7, 2026 ; A Sudanese legal monitoring organization has raised alarm over what it describes as a sustained and systematic pattern of attacks targeting humanitarian operations amid the ongoing conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF)
body_en:
Sudan April 7, 2026 ; A Sudanese legal monitoring organization has raised alarm over what it describes as a sustained and systematic pattern of attacks targeting humanitarian operations amid the ongoing conflict between the Sudanese Armed Forces and the Rapid Support Forces (RSF).
In a report released Tuesday, the group Emergency Lawyers said incidents involving aid convoys, warehouses, and relief workers have sharply increased since the war began in April 2023, severely undermining humanitarian access across Darfur and Kordofan.
The report documents more than 15 attacks on humanitarian convoys as of February 2026, alongside repeated cases of looting and destruction of logistics facilities. It describes the pattern as coordinated rather than isolated, pointing to a broader collapse in protections for humanitarian operations.
At least 10 aid workers have been killed and 11 others injured, according to the findings. In addition, around 20 aid trucks have been destroyed or burned, while some convoys were completely looted. The group also reported that more than 50 World Food Programme warehouses and 87 humanitarian offices have been seized, looted, or destroyed, resulting in significant losses of food and medical supplies.
The report further highlights what it calls a qualitative escalation in attacks, including the reported use of drones against aid convoys during 2025 and 2026.
The organization said these actions constitute serious violations of international humanitarian law and may amount to war crimes, particularly where humanitarian assistance is deliberately obstructed or starvation is used as a method of warfare.
It also outlined additional methods used to restrict aid delivery, including administrative obstruction, criminalization of humanitarian work, and politicization of relief efforts by warring parties.
Emergency Lawyers called for urgent international intervention to strengthen accountability mechanisms and ensure protection for humanitarian workers, warning that continued attacks risk deepening the country’s humanitarian crisis.

title: Le Président Guelleh félicite les électeurs suite à l'élection présidentielle à Djibouti
excerpt: Djibouti, le 11 avril 2026 - Le Président de la République, Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, a félicité le peuple djiboutien pour sa participation à ce qu'il a qualifié d'élection présidentielle transparente et apaisée, tenue le 10 avril.
title_en: President Guelleh Praises Voters Following Djibouti Presidential Election
excerpt_en: Djibouti, April 11, 2026 - The President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, has commended the Djiboutian people for their participation in what he described as a transparent and peaceful presidential election, held on April 10.
body_en:
Djibouti, April 11, 2026 - The President of the Republic, Ismail Omar Guelleh, has commended the Djiboutian people for their participation in what he described as a transparent and peaceful presidential election, held on April 10.

In a statement to the press following the announcement of the results, President Guelleh paid tribute to voters, emphasizing their role in the country’s democratic process. “It is our entire people who have triumphed today, embarking on a new chapter in their legitimate pursuit of sustainable development,” he said.

The head of state also expressed hope for strengthened national unity. “I hope for greater cohesion, unity, and fraternity for our nation,” he added.

According to the official results, President Guelleh, who was seeking re-election, secured a decisive victory with 97.81% of the vote. His main challenger, Mohamed Farah Samatar, president of the Unified Democratic Centre (CDU), received 2.19% of the votes cast.
body_fr:
Djibouti, le 11 avril 2026 - Le Président de la République, Ismaïl Omar Guelleh, a félicité le peuple djiboutien pour sa participation à ce qu'il a qualifié d'élection présidentielle transparente et apaisée, tenue le 10 avril.

Dans une déclaration à la presse suite à l’annonce des résultats, le Président Guelleh a rendu hommage aux électeurs, soulignant leur rôle dans le processus démocratique du pays. « C'est notre peuple tout entier qui a triomphé aujourd'hui, ouvrant un nouveau chapitre dans sa quête légitime du développement durable », a-t-il déclaré.

Le chef de l'Etat a également exprimé l'espoir d'un renforcement de l'unité nationale. "J'espère une plus grande cohésion, unité et fraternité pour notre nation", a-t-il ajouté.

Selon les résultats officiels, le Président Guelleh, qui briguait sa réélection, a remporté une victoire décisive avec 97,81% des voix. Son principal challenger, Mohamed Farah Samatar, président du Centre démocratique unifié (CDU), a obtenu 2,19% des suffrages exprimés.

body_en:
Sudan April 7, 2026; The leader of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, known as “Hemetti,” has called on the United Nations to establish humanitarian offices in areas controlled by his forces to facilitate aid delivery amid Sudan’s ongoing conflict.
Speaking following a meeting in Nairobi with the UN Secretary-General’s Personal Envoy for Sudan, Pekka Haavisto, Hemetti said he had formally requested expanded UN presence in RSF-held territories to improve humanitarian coordination.
The United Nations has previously rejected the RSF’s attempt to establish a parallel government under its “Founding Alliance,” but continues to engage with the group’s leadership in a limited capacity for humanitarian access and civilian protection discussions.
The meeting between Hemetti and Haavisto took place on Monday in the Kenyan capital, following the envoy’s broader regional consultations that included visits to Sudan and Egypt.
According to statements from the alliance aligned with the RSF, Hemetti urged the UN to accelerate the establishment of offices in areas under its control, arguing that such a step would improve aid distribution to affected civilians.
He also called for an independent international investigation into the origins of the conflict, including allegations of chemical weapons use, and insisted that accountability for the outbreak of war is essential for any political settlement.
Hemetti blamed elements linked to Sudan’s Islamist movement and allied army factions for triggering the conflict, while also criticizing what he described as oversimplified international narratives that fail to account for Sudan’s long-standing political crises.
During his regional mission, Haavisto also met with Abdel Fattah al-Burhan in Port Sudan, as well as Egyptian officials, Arab League representatives, and various Sudanese political actors in Cairo.
The UN envoy reiterated the organization’s commitment to ending the conflict and said consultations are ongoing with all parties to identify pathways toward a political and humanitarian resolution.
body_fr:
Soudan, 7 avril 2026 ; Le chef des Forces de soutien rapide (RSF), Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, connu sous le nom de « Hemetti », a appelé les Nations Unies à établir des bureaux humanitaires dans les zones contrôlées par ses forces afin de faciliter l’acheminement de l’aide dans le contexte du conflit en cours au Soudan.
S'exprimant à l'issue d'une réunion à Nairobi avec l'envoyé personnel du secrétaire général de l'ONU pour le Soudan, Pekka Haavisto, Hemetti a déclaré qu'il avait officiellement demandé une présence élargie de l'ONU dans les territoires contrôlés par RSF afin d'améliorer la coordination humanitaire.
Les Nations Unies ont précédemment rejeté la tentative des RSF d’établir un gouvernement parallèle sous son « Alliance fondatrice », mais continuent de dialoguer avec les dirigeants du groupe dans le cadre d’une capacité limitée pour l’accès humanitaire et les discussions sur la protection des civils.
La rencontre entre Hemetti et Haavisto a eu lieu lundi dans la capitale kenyane, à la suite des consultations régionales plus larges de l’envoyé qui comprenaient des visites au Soudan et en Égypte.
Selon les déclarations de l'alliance alignée sur RSF, Hemetti a exhorté l'ONU à accélérer la mise en place de bureaux dans les zones sous son contrôle, arguant qu'une telle mesure améliorerait la distribution de l'aide aux civils touchés.
Il a également appelé à une enquête internationale indépendante sur les origines du conflit, y compris les allégations d'utilisation d'armes chimiques, et a insisté sur le fait que la responsabilisation dans le déclenchement de la guerre est essentielle à tout règlement politique.
Hemetti a imputé le déclenchement du conflit à des éléments liés au mouvement islamiste soudanais et aux factions militaires alliées, tout en critiquant ce qu’il a décrit comme des récits internationaux trop simplistes qui ne tiennent pas compte des crises politiques de longue date au Soudan.
Au cours de sa mission régionale, Haavisto a également rencontré Abdel Fattah al-Burhan à Port-Soudan, ainsi que des responsables égyptiens, des représentants de la Ligue arabe et divers acteurs politiques soudanais au Caire.
L’envoyé de l’ONU a réitéré l’engagement de l’organisation à mettre fin au conflit et a déclaré que des consultations étaient en cours avec toutes les parties pour identifier les voies menant à une résolution politique et humanitaire.

title_en: Sudan Suspends Private Broadcaster Sudania 24 Over Alleged Hate Speech
excerpt_en: Sudan April 8, 2026 ; Sudan’s Ministry of Information has suspended the private television channel Sudania 24 and revoked its operating licenses, accusing it of professional misconduct and incitement of tribal tensions. The broadcaster, owned by businessman Wajdi Mirghani, has be
body_en:
Sudan April 8, 2026 ; Sudan’s Ministry of Information has suspended the private television channel Sudania 24 and revoked its operating licenses, accusing it of professional misconduct and incitement of tribal tensions.
The broadcaster, owned by businessman Wajdi Mirghani, has been operating from outside Sudan since the outbreak of war in April 2023 forced the closure of its Khartoum headquarters. It has primarily continued its reporting through digital platforms and social media.
According to a ministry statement, the suspension followed recent coverage of a protest in the Dalgo locality of Northern State. The channel had aired footage showing local residents opposing the presence of displaced people from Darfur, which authorities said contributed to the spread of hate speech and regional division.
The ministry further ordered the suspension of work permits for the channel’s correspondents until all licenses are renewed and editorial compliance commitments are made.
Sudania 24 has previously faced government restrictions. In December 2024, it was forced to cancel its “Circle of Events” program after hosting opposition figures accused of insulting the military.
Officials said they are working with the Ministry of Telecommunications to block the specific content cited in the violation. They also emphasized that the government does not hold ownership in the channel and is not responsible for its editorial output.
Authorities justified the decision as necessary to protect national unity and social stability, noting that the broadcaster currently operates without an authorized studio inside the country.
body_fr:
Soudan, 8 avril 2026 ; Le ministère soudanais de l’Information a suspendu la chaîne de télévision privée Soudania 24 et révoqué ses licences d’exploitation, l’accusant de faute professionnelle et d’incitation aux tensions tribales.
La chaîne, propriété de l'homme d'affaires Wajdi Mirghani, opère depuis l'extérieur du Soudan depuis que le déclenchement de la guerre en avril 2023 a forcé la fermeture de son siège à Khartoum. Il a principalement poursuivi ses reportages via les plateformes numériques et les réseaux sociaux.
Selon un communiqué du ministère, la suspension fait suite à la récente couverture d'une manifestation dans la localité de Dalgo, dans l'État du Nord. La chaîne avait diffusé des images montrant des résidents locaux s'opposant à la présence de personnes déplacées du Darfour, ce qui, selon les autorités, contribuait à la propagation des discours de haine et à la division régionale.
Le ministère a en outre ordonné la suspension des permis de travail des correspondants de la chaîne jusqu’à ce que toutes les licences soient renouvelées et que des engagements de conformité éditoriale soient pris.
Soudania 24 a déjà été confrontée à des restrictions gouvernementales. En décembre 2024, il a été contraint d’annuler son programme « Cercle des événements » après avoir accueilli des personnalités de l’opposition accusées d’insultes à l’armée.
Les responsables ont déclaré qu'ils travaillaient avec le ministère des Télécommunications pour bloquer le contenu spécifique cité dans la violation. Ils ont également souligné que le gouvernement n'est pas propriétaire de la chaîne et n'est pas responsable de sa production éditoriale.
Les autorités ont justifié cette décision comme étant nécessaire pour protéger l'unité nationale et la stabilité sociale, notant que la chaîne fonctionne actuellement sans studio autorisé à l'intérieur du pays.

title: Hundreds Killed as Drone Strikes Escalate Across Sudan, Targeting Civilian Infrastructure
excerpt: Sudan April 7, 2026 ; Intensifying drone warfare by Sudan’s warring parties has resulted in hundreds of civilian deaths and widespread destruction of critical infrastructure in the first quarter of 2026, according to conflict monitoring data and humanitarian sources. Analysis fro
title_en: Hundreds Killed as Drone Strikes Escalate Across Sudan, Targeting Civilian Infrastructure
excerpt_en: Sudan April 7, 2026 ; Intensifying drone warfare by Sudan’s warring parties has resulted in hundreds of civilian deaths and widespread destruction of critical infrastructure in the first quarter of 2026, according to conflict monitoring data and humanitarian sources. Analysis fro
body_en:
Sudan April 7, 2026 ; Intensifying drone warfare by Sudan’s warring parties has resulted in hundreds of civilian deaths and widespread destruction of critical infrastructure in the first quarter of 2026, according to conflict monitoring data and humanitarian sources.
Analysis from the Armed Conflict Location and Event Data Project and local emergency response networks indicates a sharp rise in the use of suicide and loitering munitions since the start of the year, turning several cities across Darfur and Kordofan into active combat zones.
Estimates compiled from local and international reporting suggest that between 480 and 500 civilians have been killed in direct drone strikes on civilian targets since January, with more than 1,200 others injured.
The United Nations reported in late March that a drone strike on the Ed Daein Teaching Hospital in East Darfur killed more than 70 people, including patients, children, women, and medical personnel. The UN further estimated that over 500 civilians have been killed in similar strikes nationwide since the beginning of the year.
Medical staff at the Ed Daein facility described narrowly surviving the attack, which occurred during the first day of Eid, when multiple missiles struck the hospital in quick succession, causing panic and heavy casualties among patients and staff.
East Darfur has recorded the highest number of drone strikes, with local authorities reporting more than 250 raids in the past six months. South and West Darfur have also been heavily affected, with strikes hitting hospitals, religious sites, and marketplaces.
In North Kordofan, the city of El Obeid has been repeatedly targeted in attacks attributed to the Rapid Support Forces (RSF). In South Kordofan, the cities of Dilling and Kadugli have also experienced sustained aerial bombardment.
Elsewhere, reciprocal strikes have expanded the geographic scope of the conflict. The RSF has carried out attacks in White Nile, Al Jazirah, River Nile, and Red Sea states, while government forces have targeted RSF positions in Blue Nile, Darfur, and Kordofan regions.
At least 18 health and essential service facilities were hit by drone strikes during the first quarter of the year, forcing four major hospitals out of operation. The World Health Organization documented at least five attacks on medical facilities within the first 50 days of 2026, resulting in 69 deaths.
In West Kordofan, drone strikes on residential areas in Lagawa killed five civilians and injured 15 others, triggering new waves of displacement as residents fled intensified bombardments.

title: Le Soudan approuve des mesures économiques pour stabiliser sa monnaie alors que la livre sterling atteint un niveau record
excerpt: Soudan, 2 avril 2026 ; Le Haut Comité économique du Soudan a approuvé une série de mesures d’urgence visant à stabiliser la monnaie nationale et à faire face à l’aggravation de l’instabilité économique.
title_en: Sudan Approves Economic Measures to Stabilize Currency as Pound Hits Record Low
excerpt_en: Sudan April 2, 2026 ; Sudan’s Higher Economic Committee has approved a set of emergency measures aimed at stabilizing the national currency and addressing worsening economic instability.
body_en:
Sudan April 2, 2026 ; Sudan’s Higher Economic Committee has approved a set of emergency measures aimed at stabilizing the national currency and addressing worsening economic instability.

The decisions were taken during a meeting chaired by Prime Minister Kamil Idris and attended by senior ministers responsible for economic planning, finance, and trade.

The Sudanese pound has continued its steep decline since the outbreak of war in April 2023, falling from around 600 per US dollar to approximately 3,665 per US dollar on the parallel market, reflecting severe macroeconomic pressures.

Authorities attribute the collapse to disrupted production, declining exports, and the prolonged impact of the conflict on national economic activity.

The newly approved measures include tighter regulation of luxury imports, policies to expand and diversify exports, and incentives aimed at encouraging Sudanese expatriates to channel remittances through formal banking systems.

Officials also reviewed the country’s foreign exchange reserves, the availability of essential commodities, and broader fiscal performance during the meeting.

The committee stressed the need to regulate export revenues more strictly, reduce government spending, and eliminate informal or illegal fees affecting economic activity.

In addition, state institutions have been instructed to adopt electronic revenue collection systems and complete foreign trade procedures through a centralized digital platform designed to improve transparency and reduce corruption.
body_fr:
Soudan, 2 avril 2026 ; Le Haut Comité économique du Soudan a approuvé une série de mesures d’urgence visant à stabiliser la monnaie nationale et à faire face à l’aggravation de l’instabilité économique.

Les décisions ont été prises lors d'une réunion présidée par le Premier ministre Kamil Idris et à laquelle ont participé les principaux ministres responsables de la planification économique, des finances et du commerce.

La livre soudanaise a poursuivi sa forte baisse depuis le déclenchement de la guerre en avril 2023, passant d'environ 600 pour un dollar américain à environ 3 665 pour un dollar américain sur le marché parallèle, reflétant de graves pressions macroéconomiques.

Les autorités attribuent cet effondrement à la perturbation de la production, à la baisse des exportations et à l'impact prolongé du conflit sur l'activité économique nationale.

Les mesures récemment approuvées comprennent une réglementation plus stricte des importations de produits de luxe, des politiques visant à développer et à diversifier les exportations et des incitations visant à encourager les expatriés soudanais à acheminer leurs fonds via les systèmes bancaires formels.

Les responsables ont également examiné les réserves de change du pays, la disponibilité des produits essentiels et les performances budgétaires plus larges au cours de la réunion.

Le comité a souligné la nécessité de réglementer plus strictement les revenus d'exportation, de réduire les dépenses publiques et d'éliminer les frais informels ou illégaux affectant l'activité économique.

En outre, les institutions publiques ont été chargées d'adopter des systèmes électroniques de collecte des recettes et d'effectuer les procédures de commerce extérieur via une plateforme numérique centralisée conçue pour améliorer la transparence et réduire la corruption.
author: jean-marc-okito

title: Le ministère de la Justice examine les rapports annuels de performance
excerpt: Bamako, le 30 mars 2026 – Par ailleurs, le ministère malien de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme a tenu la présentation symbolique de son rapport annuel d’activités 2025, réunissant de hauts responsables judiciaires et des représentants du gouvernement.
title_en: Justice Ministry Reviews Annual Performance Reports
excerpt_en: Bamako, March 30, 2026 - In a separate development, Mali’s Ministry of Justice and Human Rights held the symbolic presentation of its 2025 annual activity report, bringing together senior judicial officials and government representatives.
body_en:
Bamako, March 30, 2026 - In a separate development, Mali’s Ministry of Justice and Human Rights held the symbolic presentation of its 2025 annual activity report, bringing together senior judicial officials and government representatives.

The session, chaired by Justice Minister Mamoudou Kassogué, featured presentations from eleven central services and four courts, reviewing institutional performance and administrative reforms.

The Secretary General, Dr. Boubacar Sidiki Diarra, emphasized that the reporting process aims to improve transparency and accountability within the justice system, providing a clearer overview of institutional performance.

Minister Kassogué described the initiative as a key reform milestone, stating that the reports serve as a guiding tool for decision-making and institutional planning. He also underscored the importance of continued efforts to strengthen judicial capacity and improve service delivery.

Officials said the exercise represents an important step toward modernizing governance within the justice sector and enhancing overall institutional efficiency.
body_fr:
Bamako, le 30 mars 2026 – Par ailleurs, le ministère malien de la Justice et des Droits de l’Homme a tenu la présentation symbolique de son rapport annuel d’activités 2025, réunissant de hauts responsables judiciaires et des représentants du gouvernement.

La séance, présidée par le ministre de la Justice Mamoudou Kassogué, comprenait des présentations de onze services centraux et de quatre tribunaux, passant en revue les performances institutionnelles et les réformes administratives.

Le Secrétaire général, Dr Boubacar Sidiki Diarra, a souligné que le processus de reporting vise à améliorer la transparence et la responsabilité au sein du système judiciaire, en fournissant un aperçu plus clair de la performance institutionnelle.

Le ministre Kassogué a décrit l'initiative comme une étape clé de la réforme, déclarant que les rapports servent d'outil d'orientation pour la prise de décision et la planification institutionnelle. Il a également souligné l'importance de poursuivre les efforts visant à renforcer les capacités judiciaires et à améliorer la prestation de services.

Les responsables ont déclaré que cet exercice représentait une étape importante vers la modernisation de la gouvernance au sein du secteur de la justice et l'amélioration de l'efficacité institutionnelle globale.

title: Les forces soudanaises accusées de torture et de détention arbitraire, selon un groupe de défense des droits
excerpt: Soudan, 8 avril 2026 ; Les forces affiliées aux Forces armées soudanaises (SAF) ont été accusées d'avoir arbitrairement détenu et torturé des civils dans les zones sous leur contrôle, dans le cadre d'une campagne plus large ciblant des opposants présumés, selon un nouveau rapport de Human Rights Watch (HRW).
title_en: Sudanese Forces Accused of Torture and Arbitrary Detention, Rights Group Says
excerpt_en: Sudan April 8, 2026 ; Forces affiliated with the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have been accused of arbitrarily detaining and torturing civilians in areas under their control, as part of a broader campaign targeting perceived opponents, according to a new report by Human Rights Watch (HRW).
body_en:
Sudan April 8, 2026 ; Forces affiliated with the Sudanese Armed Forces (SAF) have been accused of arbitrarily detaining and torturing civilians in areas under their control, as part of a broader campaign targeting perceived opponents, according to a new report by Human Rights Watch (HRW).

The report alleges that the military and allied groups, including the General Intelligence Service and the al-Baraa Ibn Malik battalion militia, have targeted individuals based on ethnic identity, humanitarian work, and political affiliation.

Based on interviews with 28 individuals conducted between June 2025 and February 2026, the report documents alleged abuses in several regions, including Khartoum, Gezira, Gedaref, Red Sea, and Northern states. Detainees were reportedly held incommunicado in military bases or residential buildings converted into detention facilities.

HRW said testimonies from former detainees, their families, and legal representatives describe a pattern of arbitrary arrests, ill-treatment, and a climate of impunity.

In response, the Attorney General’s office rejected allegations of widespread arbitrary detention and deaths in custody. Authorities acknowledged only a single case currently under criminal investigation and maintained that all detainees are being held legally under police supervision and oversight.

The report also indicates that individuals from Darfur have been disproportionately targeted, with some accused of collaborating with the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), which has its origins in the region. Witnesses described cases in which detainees were beaten and accused of bringing the conflict to the capital.

Humanitarian workers have also reportedly been affected. Local volunteers providing aid services, including community kitchens, were subjected to interrogation and detention. In one case, an aid worker in East Khartoum was held for more than two weeks and questioned about funding sources following the army’s recapture of the area.

Despite a January 2026 directive by military leader Abdel Fattah al-Burhan ordering the release of hundreds of women from a prison in Omdurman, rights monitors indicated that many remain in detention without due process. The report further notes that at least 25 women have been sentenced to death on charges of collaboration.
body_fr:
Soudan, 8 avril 2026 ; Les forces affiliées aux Forces armées soudanaises (SAF) ont été accusées d'avoir arbitrairement détenu et torturé des civils dans les zones sous leur contrôle, dans le cadre d'une campagne plus large ciblant des opposants présumés, selon un nouveau rapport de Human Rights Watch (HRW).

Le rapport allègue que l’armée et les groupes alliés, notamment les services de renseignement généraux et la milice du bataillon al-Baraa Ibn Malik, ont ciblé des individus en fonction de leur identité ethnique, de leur travail humanitaire et de leur affiliation politique.

Basé sur des entretiens avec 28 personnes menés entre juin 2025 et février 2026, le rapport documente des abus présumés dans plusieurs régions, notamment Khartoum, Gezira, Gedaref, la Mer Rouge et les États du Nord. Les détenus auraient été détenus au secret dans des bases militaires ou des immeubles résidentiels transformés en centres de détention.

HRW a déclaré que les témoignages d'anciens détenus, de leurs familles et de leurs représentants légaux décrivent une tendance aux arrestations arbitraires, aux mauvais traitements et à un climat d'impunité.

En réponse, le bureau du procureur général a rejeté les allégations faisant état de détentions arbitraires généralisées et de décès en détention. Les autorités ont reconnu qu'un seul cas faisait actuellement l'objet d'une enquête pénale et ont affirmé que tous les détenus étaient détenus légalement sous la supervision et la surveillance de la police.

Le rapport indique également que les individus du Darfour ont été ciblés de manière disproportionnée, certains étant accusés de collaborer avec les Forces de soutien rapide (RSF), originaires de la région. Des témoins ont décrit des cas dans lesquels des détenus ont été battus et accusés d'avoir provoqué le conflit dans la capitale.

Les travailleurs humanitaires auraient également été touchés. Les volontaires locaux fournissant des services humanitaires, notamment des cuisines communautaires, ont été soumis à des interrogatoires et à des détentions. Dans un cas, un travailleur humanitaire à Khartoum Est a été détenu pendant plus de deux semaines et interrogé sur ses sources de financement après la reprise de la zone par l’armée.

Malgré une directive de janvier 2026 du chef militaire Abdel Fattah al-Burhan ordonnant la libération de centaines de femmes d'une prison d'Omdurman, les observateurs des droits ont indiqué que nombre d'entre elles restent en détention sans procédure régulière. Le rapport note en outre qu'au moins 25 femmes ont été condamnées à mort pour collaboration.

title: Le Groupe africain à l’ONU organise une retraite stratégique sous la direction du Mali
excerpt: New York, les 29 et 30 mars 2026 – Les ambassadeurs du Groupe africain auprès des Nations Unies se sont réunis à New York pour une retraite stratégique de haut niveau visant à renforcer la coordination et à faire progresser les priorités du continent au sein du système des Nations Unies.
title_en: African Group at the UN Holds Strategic Retreat under Mali’s Leadership
excerpt_en: New York, March 29-30, 2026 - Ambassadors of the African Group to the United Nations convened in New York for a high-level strategic retreat aimed at strengthening coordination and advancing the continent’s priorities within the UN system.
body_en:
New York, March 29-30, 2026 - Ambassadors of the African Group to the United Nations convened in New York for a high-level strategic retreat aimed at strengthening coordination and advancing the continent’s priorities within the UN system.

The meeting was chaired by Issa Konfourou, Ambassador and Permanent Representative of Mali to the United Nations, who held the presidency of the African Group for the month of March. The retreat was attended by the UN Secretary-General, António Guterres, as well as the Deputy Secretary-General, underscoring the significance of the gathering.

Held under the theme “Strengthening the Role of African Actors within the United Nations System: Challenges and Opportunities,” the discussions focused on enhancing Africa’s collective influence on key global issues and promoting a unified approach to the continent’s strategic interests.

In his opening remarks, Ambassador Konfourou stressed the importance of Africa’s active engagement in ongoing UN reform processes. He also highlighted the need to advance resolutions that secure adequate financing for African priorities, with the goal of fostering balanced and sustainable development across the continent.

title: Burhan s'engage en faveur de la transition démocratique à l'occasion de l'anniversaire du soulèvement de 2019
excerpt: Soudan, 6 avril 2026 ; Le chef de l’armée soudanaise et chef du Conseil souverain, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, a réaffirmé l’engagement de l’armée en faveur d’une transition démocratique et d’un éventuel transfert du pouvoir aux civils.
title_en: Burhan Pledges Commitment to Democratic Transition on Anniversary of 2019 Uprising
excerpt_en: Sudan April 6, 2026; Sudan’s army chief and head of the Sovereign Council, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, has reaffirmed the military’s commitment to a democratic transition and eventual transfer of power to civilians.
body_en:
Sudan April 6, 2026; Sudan’s army chief and head of the Sovereign Council, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, has reaffirmed the military’s commitment to a democratic transition and eventual transfer of power to civilians.

In a recorded speech marking the seventh anniversary of the 2019 mass sit-in outside the army headquarters in Khartoum, Burhan said the armed forces remain determined to complete the political transition process initiated after the ousting of former president Omar al-Bashir.

The address, filmed at multiple military locations, highlighted the army’s historical role in Sudan’s uprisings, referencing the 1985 revolution that removed Jaafar Nimeiri and the 2019 protests that ended Bashir’s three-decade rule.

Burhan described the military as a partner of the Sudanese people in what he termed the “battle of dignity,” referring to the ongoing conflict against the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), as well as the broader political transition process.

He reiterated that the armed forces are committed to enabling a democratic process in which Sudanese citizens can freely choose their system of governance.

“This is an occasion to renew our pledge to the Sudanese people that we are their sons and partners,” he said, adding that the military would continue working toward completing the transition begun in 2019.

Burhan stated that the Sudanese population has historically stood with the military during pivotal moments, including the 1985 and 2019 uprisings, and has again aligned with it during the ongoing war that began in April 2023.

He further said Sudanese citizens would ultimately prevail and reject humiliation or tyranny.
body_fr:
Soudan, 6 avril 2026 ; Le chef de l’armée soudanaise et chef du Conseil souverain, Abdel Fattah al-Burhan, a réaffirmé l’engagement de l’armée en faveur d’une transition démocratique et d’un éventuel transfert du pouvoir aux civils.

Dans un discours enregistré marquant le septième anniversaire du sit-in de masse de 2019 devant le quartier général de l'armée à Khartoum, Burhan a déclaré que les forces armées restaient déterminées à achever le processus de transition politique lancé après l'éviction de l'ancien président Omar al-Bashir.

Le discours, filmé dans plusieurs sites militaires, a souligné le rôle historique de l’armée dans les soulèvements au Soudan, faisant référence à la révolution de 1985 qui a renversé Jaafar Nimeiri et aux manifestations de 2019 qui ont mis fin aux trois décennies de règne de Bashir.

Burhan a décrit l'armée comme un partenaire du peuple soudanais dans ce qu'il a appelé la « bataille pour la dignité », faisant référence au conflit en cours contre les Forces de soutien rapide (RSF), ainsi qu'au processus de transition politique plus large.

Il a réitéré que les forces armées sont déterminées à permettre un processus démocratique dans lequel les citoyens soudanais peuvent choisir librement leur système de gouvernance.

"C'est l'occasion de renouveler notre engagement envers le peuple soudanais selon lequel nous sommes ses fils et partenaires", a-t-il déclaré, ajoutant que l'armée continuerait à œuvrer pour achever la transition commencée en 2019.

Burhan a déclaré que la population soudanaise s'est historiquement tenue aux côtés de l'armée pendant les moments charnières, notamment les soulèvements de 1985 et de 2019, et s'est à nouveau alignée sur elle pendant la guerre en cours qui a commencé en avril 2023.

Il a ajouté que les citoyens soudanais finiraient par l'emporter et rejeteraient l'humiliation ou la tyrannie.

title: L'ONU rouvre son siège à Khartoum pour la première fois depuis le début de la guerre
excerpt: Khartoum, 2 avril 2026 ; Les Nations Unies ont rouvert leur siège à Khartoum pour la première fois depuis le déclenchement de la guerre en avril 2023, marquant une étape importante vers la reprise de ses opérations dans la capitale soudanaise.
title_en: UN Reopens Headquarters in Khartoum for First Time Since War Began
excerpt_en: Khartoum April 2, 2026; The United Nations has reopened its headquarters in Khartoum for the first time since the outbreak of war in April 2023, marking a significant step toward restoring its operations in the Sudanese capital.
body_en:
Khartoum April 2, 2026; The United Nations has reopened its headquarters in Khartoum for the first time since the outbreak of war in April 2023, marking a significant step toward restoring its operations in the Sudanese capital.

The reopening follows nearly three years of relocation to Port Sudan, where UN activities had been based due to ongoing fighting in Khartoum.

The ceremony was attended by senior Sudanese officials, including Foreign Minister Mohieddin Salem and Khartoum Governor Ahmed Osman Hamza, alongside representatives from the United Nations and its affiliated agencies.

Government officials welcomed the move, describing it as an important signal of improving conditions and renewed cooperation between Sudan and international partners.

The foreign minister said the return of UN operations to Khartoum reflects a shared commitment to stabilizing the country and advancing peace efforts. He emphasized the government’s intention to work closely with UN agencies under national initiatives aimed at achieving long-term stability.

He also reiterated the government’s position on the conflict, stating that authorities remain committed to restoring order and rejecting external interference in Sudan’s internal affairs.

The minister called on regional organizations, including the African Union and IGAD, to take more active roles in supporting stability and reassessing Sudan’s standing within regional frameworks.

UN officials highlighted the gradual resumption of activities in the capital as part of broader efforts to expand humanitarian operations and coordination across the country.
body_fr:
Khartoum, 2 avril 2026 ; Les Nations Unies ont rouvert leur siège à Khartoum pour la première fois depuis le déclenchement de la guerre en avril 2023, marquant une étape importante vers la reprise de ses opérations dans la capitale soudanaise.

La réouverture fait suite à près de trois ans de réinstallation à Port-Soudan, où les activités de l'ONU étaient basées en raison des combats en cours à Khartoum.

La cérémonie s'est déroulée en présence de hauts responsables soudanais, dont le ministre des Affaires étrangères Mohieddin Salem et le gouverneur de Khartoum Ahmed Osman Hamza, ainsi que des représentants des Nations Unies et de leurs agences affiliées.

Les responsables gouvernementaux ont salué cette décision, la décrivant comme un signal important d'amélioration des conditions et de coopération renouvelée entre le Soudan et les partenaires internationaux.

Le ministre des Affaires étrangères a déclaré que le retour des opérations de l'ONU à Khartoum reflète un engagement commun à stabiliser le pays et à faire progresser les efforts de paix. Il a souligné l’intention du gouvernement de travailler en étroite collaboration avec les agences des Nations Unies dans le cadre d’initiatives nationales visant à parvenir à une stabilité à long terme.

Il a également réitéré la position du gouvernement sur le conflit, affirmant que les autorités restaient déterminées à rétablir l’ordre et à rejeter toute ingérence extérieure dans les affaires intérieures du Soudan.

Le ministre a appelé les organisations régionales, notamment l’Union africaine et l’IGAD, à jouer un rôle plus actif dans le soutien à la stabilité et à réévaluer la position du Soudan dans les cadres régionaux.

Les responsables de l'ONU ont souligné la reprise progressive des activités dans la capitale dans le cadre d'efforts plus larges visant à étendre les opérations humanitaires et la coordination à travers le pays.

excerpt_en: Walikale, March 24, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), backed by Wazalendo fighters, repelled an attempted incursion by AFC/M23 rebels near Mungazi in Walikale territory, North Kivu. According to local security and administrative sources, the reb
body_en:
Walikale, March 24, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), backed by Wazalendo fighters, repelled an attempted incursion by AFC/M23 rebels near Mungazi in Walikale territory, North Kivu.
According to local security and administrative sources, the rebels attempted to advance through the Usuka River corridor, using forest routes to bypass army positions and carry out a surprise attack on the town of Mungazi, located in the Luberike grouping and currently under government control.
The operation was intercepted by a joint FARDC-Wazalendo patrol in the surrounding forest, triggering intense exchanges of gunfire that caused panic among residents. Following a counteroffensive, government forces managed to push the attackers back toward their initial positions near Kibati.
By Tuesday, calm had largely returned to Mungazi and nearby areas, with daily activities gradually resuming. FARDC and allied fighters remain deployed in the area, maintaining a heightened state of alert as the broader security situation in Walikale continues to be volatile.

title: AFC/M23 Describes Troop Movements as “Strategic Rotation,” Kinshasa Questions Intentions
excerpt: Goma, DRC, March 29, 2026 - The AFC/M23 movement says recent withdrawals observed from several front-line positions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo are part of what it describes as a “normal strategic rotation,” amid ongoing uncertainty over the security situation in Nort
title_en: AFC/M23 Describes Troop Movements as “Strategic Rotation,” Kinshasa Questions Intentions
excerpt_en: Goma, DRC, March 29, 2026 - The AFC/M23 movement says recent withdrawals observed from several front-line positions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo are part of what it describes as a “normal strategic rotation,” amid ongoing uncertainty over the security situation in Nort
body_en:
Goma, DRC, March 29, 2026 - The AFC/M23 movement says recent withdrawals observed from several front-line positions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo are part of what it describes as a “normal strategic rotation,” amid ongoing uncertainty over the security situation in North and South Kivu.
In a statement issued Saturday, March 28, spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka said the troop movements recorded in multiple areas are routine redeployments within the group’s structure.
He described the activity as part of a “normal and strategic rotation of units of the Congolese Revolutionary Army (ARC),” adding that the movement remains committed to what it calls confidence-building measures under the ongoing peace framework.
The AFC/M23 also reaffirmed its stated commitment to civilian protection and said it remains prepared to respond to threats on the ground.
The explanation comes amid heightened attention to recent shifts in territorial presence reported in parts of Walikale, Rutshuru, and Lubero, where local sources have noted withdrawals or repositioning of armed elements in recent days.
However, the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has expressed skepticism about the group’s claims.
Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya said Kinshasa is closely monitoring the situation but remains focused on what it considers the core issue: the presence of foreign-linked armed forces on Congolese territory.
He said the government expects a “definitive withdrawal” rather than what it views as tactical or temporary movements, adding that similar redeployments have been observed in the past without leading to lasting de-escalation.
The exchanges take place against the backdrop of the stalled Doha peace process, which was intended to advance implementation of a broader framework agreement signed in late 2025.
Although initial progress had been recorded under the agreement, including early protocol signings, negotiations have since slowed, with no substantive new rounds reported in recent weeks.
Diplomatic sources have cited both regional tensions and logistical constraints affecting mediation efforts, while officials in Kinshasa maintain that they remain committed to the process but want clearer guarantees on implementation.
Despite the diplomatic track, fighting and local insecurity continue in several areas of eastern DRC, with residents frequently reporting shifting frontlines, temporary withdrawals, and renewed clashes between AFC/M23 elements, Wazalendo fighters, and other armed groups.

title: Internal Divisions and Rivalries Weaken Cohesion Within M23 Leadership, Report Warns
excerpt: April 4, 2026 - A new analysis highlights deep internal fractures within the M23 movement, warning that personal rivalries, strategic disagreements, and political-military tensions are weakening its overall cohesion at a critical moment in its evolution. The assessment indicates
title_en: Internal Divisions and Rivalries Weaken Cohesion Within M23 Leadership, Report Warns
excerpt_en: April 4, 2026 - A new analysis highlights deep internal fractures within the M23 movement, warning that personal rivalries, strategic disagreements, and political-military tensions are weakening its overall cohesion at a critical moment in its evolution. The assessment indicates
body_en:
April 4, 2026 - A new analysis highlights deep internal fractures within the M23 movement, warning that personal rivalries, strategic disagreements, and political-military tensions are weakening its overall cohesion at a critical moment in its evolution.
The assessment indicates that the movement is divided along three main fault lines: tensions between its leadership and its external backers, rivalries between senior military commanders, and growing friction between its armed wing and its political structure, the Congo River Alliance (AFC).
At the military level, long-standing mistrust between M23 Chief of Staff General Sultani Makenga and external supporters is described as a structural source of instability. While Makenga has historically maintained close ties with regional actors, relations have been repeatedly strained by past conflicts, shifting alliances, and concerns over discipline and reliability within the chain of command.
The report also points to escalating competition between senior commanders, particularly between Makenga and General Baudouin Ngaruye, whose rivalry dates back to earlier phases of rebellion in eastern Congo. Although the two leaders were temporarily reconciled after rejoining the movement in recent years, tensions have reportedly re-emerged over operational authority and control of strategic resources, including customs revenue streams in areas under their influence.
Beyond military leadership disputes, the study underscores growing friction between the armed wing of M23 and its political leadership under the AFC, led by Corneille Nangaa. The political structure was created to broaden the movement’s base beyond its traditional support base, but has increasingly been marked by competing visions over strategy and end goals.
While the military leadership is largely focused on consolidating territorial control in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, the political leadership is described as pursuing a broader national agenda, creating divergence in priorities and command structure.
The report warns that these internal divisions could significantly complicate any future peace process, recalling that similar fractures contributed to the collapse of the movement in previous years and remain a key vulnerability amid ongoing conflict dynamics in the region.

The dialogue brought together media professionals to reflect on the state of journalism following Rwanda’s participation in the UN Human Rights Council’s Universal Periodic Review (UPR), which issued 286 recommendations, including 29 related to media freedom and development.
Participants highlighted several major concerns, including the rise of unqualified individuals presenting themselves as journalists, which they say is undermining professional standards in the sector.
Media practitioners also cited financial constraints as a major issue, noting that limited advertising revenue and weak media markets make it difficult for institutions to properly pay journalists, leading some professionals to leave traditional media for independent platforms such as YouTube.
Outdated media policies and regulatory frameworks were also raised as a barrier to adapting journalism standards to the digital age, with calls for legal reforms to better align with modern media practices.
Gender-based violence and limited participation of women in media were also identified as ongoing concerns affecting inclusivity in the sector.
The Legal Aid Forum said it will continue supporting efforts to strengthen journalism capacity, improve working conditions, and promote professional standards across the industry.

title: AFC/M23 accuses FARDC of deadly drone strikes on civilians in Minembwe
excerpt: South Kivu, DR Congo, March 30, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition has accused the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and allied groups of carrying out drone strikes on civilian areas in the Minembwe highlands, resulting in at least seven deaths. According to M23

excerpt_en: South Kivu, DR Congo, March 30, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition has accused the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and allied groups of carrying out drone strikes on civilian areas in the Minembwe highlands, resulting in at least seven deaths. According to M23
body_en:
South Kivu, DR Congo, March 30, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition has accused the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and allied groups of carrying out drone strikes on civilian areas in the Minembwe highlands, resulting in at least seven deaths.
According to M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka, the attacks took place between late March 29 and early March 30, targeting densely populated areas including Mikenke and Gakenke.
He alleged that suicide drones were used in what he described as indiscriminate strikes against civilian populations, also reporting additional casualties in Shanji, Kalehe Territory, where at least seven civilians were killed and around 20 others injured.
The group claims the attacks violate international humanitarian standards and accuses the Congolese government of continuing military operations despite prior ceasefire understandings linked to postponed talks in Doha.
Kinshasa has not immediately responded to the allegations.

body_en:
Washington, April 4, 2026 - Former U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs Tibor Nagy has said that dismantling the FDLR armed group in the Democratic Republic of Congo is essential to ending long-standing insecurity in the country’s east.
In comments following a recent interview with Rwandan President Paul Kagame published in Jeune Afrique, Nagy argued that international actors should apply consistent expectations on all armed groups operating in the region.
He stated that if pressure is placed on Rwanda regarding its alleged links to armed actors, similar scrutiny should be applied to the DRC concerning groups it is accused of tolerating or failing to dismantle.
Nagy has previously questioned the Congolese government’s commitment to eliminating the FDLR, a group widely described by regional and international stakeholders as a destabilizing armed force in the Great Lakes region.
In the referenced interview, President Kagame reiterated Rwanda’s security concerns along its border and defended what he described as defensive measures aimed at preventing cross-border threats. He also argued that regional security dynamics require broader attention to multiple armed actors rather than focusing on a single party.
The remarks come amid continued diplomatic debate over security arrangements, armed group activity, and peace implementation efforts in eastern DRC.

title: Report alleges journalists detained in inhumane conditions by M23 in Goma
excerpt: Goma, March 24, 2026 - Armed group M23 has been accused of detaining civilians, including at least two journalists, in shipping containers under harsh and inhumane conditions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, according to a new investigation by the Reporters Without Border
title_en: Report alleges journalists detained in inhumane conditions by M23 in Goma
excerpt_en: Goma, March 24, 2026 - Armed group M23 has been accused of detaining civilians, including at least two journalists, in shipping containers under harsh and inhumane conditions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, according to a new investigation by the Reporters Without Border
body_en:
Goma, March 24, 2026 - Armed group M23 has been accused of detaining civilians, including at least two journalists, in shipping containers under harsh and inhumane conditions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, according to a new investigation by the Reporters Without Borders.
The report, based on testimonies and visual evidence, indicates that several of these containers are located within the compound of the Goma Provincial Assembly in the Himbi neighborhood, as well as near the premises of the national broadcaster in the city. These sites have reportedly been used as informal detention centers since M23 took control of Goma in early 2025.
Former detainees describe extremely harsh conditions, with dozens of people confined in metal containers lacking light and ventilation. According to testimonies, detainees were allowed outside only once per day and received minimal food. Some survivors also reported acts of violence, including beatings, and deaths occurring inside the containers.
Visual material analyzed as part of the investigation reportedly shows individuals held under armed supervision near the containers. Satellite imagery comparisons suggest that the structures appeared after M23 established control over the city.
The findings align with previous concerns raised by human rights groups over the use of unofficial detention sites in conflict zones, where abuses such as torture and summary executions are alleged to occur.
The AFC/M23 leadership has strongly denied the accusations. Spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka dismissed the report as unfounded, claiming it is part of a campaign aimed at discrediting the movement, and insisting that journalists are free to operate in areas under their control.
Meanwhile, the broader media environment in eastern DRC continues to deteriorate. Dozens of journalists have reportedly fled the region over the past year due to threats and insecurity, while others have faced violence, intimidation, or restrictions on their work.
The situation underscores growing concerns over press freedom and civilian protection in conflict-affected areas of the Great Lakes region, as insecurity and competing narratives continue to shape the information landscape.

body_en:
MASISI, North Kivu March 29, 2026 - Intense fighting broke out on Sunday in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi territory, eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, pitting AFC/M23 fighters against Wazalendo self-defense groups, according to local sources.
The clashes reportedly began around 7:00 a.m., when AFC/M23 elements launched coordinated assaults targeting Wazalendo positions near Kazinga and Ngululu. Both localities had been under Wazalendo control in recent weeks and are now at the center of renewed fighting as each side attempts to consolidate or reclaim territory.
Residents reported sustained exchanges of heavy and light weapons fire throughout the day, with gunfire audible across multiple surrounding villages. The violence also affected areas bordering Walikale territory, deepening panic among civilian populations.
The renewed hostilities come amid a volatile security landscape in North Kivu, where reported AFC/M23 withdrawals from parts of Walikale, Lubero, and Rutshuru contrast with continued fighting in Masisi, where no signs of de-escalation have been observed.
Civilians remain exposed to the violence, with many expressing fear of further escalation as armed groups continue to contest control of strategic rural areas in the province.

title: Two Dead and Several Injured in Nia-Nia During Anti-ADF Protests
excerpt: Nia-Nia, Ituri Province April 3, 2026 - At least two people were killed and several others injured on Friday, April 3, during violent unrest in Nia-Nia in Ituri Province, as public anger over repeated ADF attacks escalated into clashes between residents and security forces. The v

excerpt_en: Nia-Nia, Ituri Province April 3, 2026 - At least two people were killed and several others injured on Friday, April 3, during violent unrest in Nia-Nia in Ituri Province, as public anger over repeated ADF attacks escalated into clashes between residents and security forces. The v
body_en:
Nia-Nia, Ituri Province April 3, 2026 - At least two people were killed and several others injured on Friday, April 3, during violent unrest in Nia-Nia in Ituri Province, as public anger over repeated ADF attacks escalated into clashes between residents and security forces.
The violence erupted when a gold miner suspected of collaboration with armed groups was brought to the police station, sparking outrage among residents who gathered in large numbers and attempted to storm the facility.
Tensions quickly escalated into confrontations between protesters and police officers. In an effort to disperse the crowd, security forces opened fire, leaving one civilian dead and two others wounded.
During the unrest, another individual suspected by residents of involvement in recruitment activities for armed groups was also targeted by the crowd, highlighting the depth of mistrust and fear within the community.
The protests come amid growing anger over a series of deadly attacks attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), including recent killings in nearby localities that left dozens of civilians dead, homes burned, and significant destruction of property.
Authorities have not yet issued a detailed statement on the incident, while tensions remain high in the area as communities continue to demand stronger protection against repeated armed violence.

title: Over 31,000 cases resolved through plea bargains in Rwanda since 2022
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda, March 31, 2026 - The Ministry of Justice reports that more than 31,000 criminal and civil cases have been resolved through plea bargaining since 2022, as Rwanda continues efforts to reduce court congestion and prison overcrowding. According to official figures, 31
title_en: Over 31,000 cases resolved through plea bargains in Rwanda since 2022
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda, March 31, 2026 - The Ministry of Justice reports that more than 31,000 criminal and civil cases have been resolved through plea bargaining since 2022, as Rwanda continues efforts to reduce court congestion and prison overcrowding. According to official figures, 31
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda, March 31, 2026 - The Ministry of Justice reports that more than 31,000 criminal and civil cases have been resolved through plea bargaining since 2022, as Rwanda continues efforts to reduce court congestion and prison overcrowding.
According to official figures, 31,143 cases have been concluded through plea bargains over the period, including 8,532 cases between July 2025 and March 2026 alone.
Authorities say these reforms have contributed to a 24.4% decline in the prison population during the 2024/2025 fiscal year.
The justice system has also expanded the use of mediation, with 9,559 cases resolved through alternative dispute mechanisms since 2022.
Legal reforms, including Law No. 22/2018 on civil and administrative procedures, have strengthened the role of mediation at different stages of judicial proceedings, encouraging settlement before trial.
The Ministry of Justice has also promoted training programs for professional mediators and launched an Alternative Dispute Resolution (ADR) center to institutionalize out-of-court settlements.
Officials say these initiatives have helped reduce the court case backlog from 62% in 2022/2023 to 45% as of March 2026.
Judicial authorities and law educators continue to promote ADR clubs in universities and secondary schools to further embed mediation culture among young people and future legal professionals.

title: DRC and Burundi launch talks to repatriate Congolese refugees displaced by Uvira conflict
excerpt: Kalemie, April 4, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and Burundi have begun discussions aimed at facilitating the voluntary return of Congolese refugees displaced by last year’s fighting in Uvira, South Kivu Province. The talks, which also include the United Nations High Com
title_en: DRC and Burundi launch talks to repatriate Congolese refugees displaced by Uvira conflict
excerpt_en: Kalemie, April 4, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and Burundi have begun discussions aimed at facilitating the voluntary return of Congolese refugees displaced by last year’s fighting in Uvira, South Kivu Province. The talks, which also include the United Nations High Com
body_en:
Kalemie, April 4, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and Burundi have begun discussions aimed at facilitating the voluntary return of Congolese refugees displaced by last year’s fighting in Uvira, South Kivu Province.
The talks, which also include the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), are taking place in Kalemie, Tanganyika Province, according to South Kivu Governor Jean-Jacques Purusi.
Authorities estimate that the December 2025 clashes in and around Uvira and nearby areas displaced large populations internally, while hundreds of thousands sought refuge in Burundi and Tanzania.
The discussions are expected to define procedures and timelines for repatriation of refugees currently hosted in Burundi and Tanzania.
Officials in Kinshasa say the initiative is part of broader efforts to stabilize return areas and coordinate humanitarian assistance for displaced populations.
The situation in Uvira remains sensitive following months of conflict involving armed groups and government forces, which led to large-scale population movements across the region.

body_en:
Masisi, March 23, 2026 - Intense clashes broke out early Monday in Kazinga, a locality in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi territory, North Kivu, as AFC/M23 fighters launched a new offensive against Wazalendo positions.
According to local security and community sources, the fighting began around 5:00 a.m., with heavy and light weapons used on both sides. Loud explosions were reported across nearby villages, triggering panic among residents, many of whom sought shelter as violence escalated.
Kazinga, considered a strategic area, has in recent weeks been under the control of Wazalendo groups. The latest offensive is widely seen as an attempt by AFC/M23 to regain control of the locality amid shifting frontlines in the region.
The renewed fighting highlights the ongoing volatility in Masisi territory, where clashes between AFC/M23 and pro-government forces, often backed by Wazalendo militias, continue to intensify. Civilians remain at high risk, with repeated cycles of displacement and insecurity affecting already vulnerable communities.

body_en:
RUTSHURU, North Kivu March 29, 2026 - At least two people were killed and several others injured during an armed incursion in Kanyangohe/Masha, Bwito chiefdom, in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, according to local sources.
The attack occurred during the night of March 27-28, when unidentified armed men stormed the village located near Mwesso in neighboring Masisi territory.
Preliminary reports indicate that among the dead are a commander of a local self-defense group linked to AFC/M23 influence in the area and a civilian. Several wounded victims were treated at a nearby health facility, though the exact number of injured remains unclear.
The assault triggered panic in the area, forcing residents to flee toward Mwesso and surrounding localities in search of safety.
The incident comes amid heightened insecurity in Rutshuru territory, where armed violence continues to affect civilian populations. It also occurs against the backdrop of reported withdrawals by AFC/M23 elements from several localities in North Kivu, a development that appears to be accompanied by renewed instability and sporadic attacks in some areas.

title: DRC, UNHCR, and Burundi Prepare Tripartite Meeting on Refugee Returns as Authorities Report Progress in Uvira
excerpt: Kalemie/Kinshasa April 3-4, 2026 - A tripartite meeting between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), and Burundi is scheduled for April 4 in Kalemie to coordinate the voluntary return of Congolese refugees and establis
title_en: DRC, UNHCR, and Burundi Prepare Tripartite Meeting on Refugee Returns as Authorities Report Progress in Uvira
excerpt_en: Kalemie/Kinshasa April 3-4, 2026 - A tripartite meeting between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), and Burundi is scheduled for April 4 in Kalemie to coordinate the voluntary return of Congolese refugees and establis
body_en:
Kalemie/Kinshasa April 3-4, 2026 - A tripartite meeting between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), and Burundi is scheduled for April 4 in Kalemie to coordinate the voluntary return of Congolese refugees and establish a framework for repatriation in the coming months.
The discussions come as authorities in South Kivu report what they describe as an improving socio-political and security situation in several areas, including the city of Uvira, following the withdrawal of AFC/M23 forces and the gradual restoration of state authority.
Officials indicate that stabilization efforts are ongoing in areas previously affected by intense fighting, with government presence being progressively re-established in territories that had fallen under rebel control during recent escalations.
The South Kivu provincial leadership estimates that more than 1.2 million people remain internally displaced, while around 800,000 Congolese refugees are still hosted in neighboring countries, particularly in Burundi and Tanzania. These populations were displaced amid years of conflict marked by grave human rights violations, including killings, kidnappings, torture, and sexual violence across several localities in the east.
Preparatory measures for returns are already underway, including demining operations aimed at clearing explosives left behind in conflict-affected zones to allow for safe resettlement of civilians.
The upcoming Kalemie meeting is expected to define practical modalities, timelines, and coordination mechanisms for the phased return of refugees, in collaboration with host countries and international partners.
Authorities say the return process has already begun in limited cases, but stress that large-scale repatriation will depend on sustained security guarantees and continued stabilization in eastern Congo, where pockets of insecurity persist despite recent withdrawals of armed groups from certain areas.

title: President Kagame addresses rumors about his health and absence from public view
excerpt: Kigali, April 3, 2026 - President Paul Kagame has dismissed speculation about his health following a period in 2025 when he spent several weeks away from public engagements. In an interview with Jeune Afrique, President Kagame explained that his absence was due to personal time o
title_en: President Kagame addresses rumors about his health and absence from public view
excerpt_en: Kigali, April 3, 2026 - President Paul Kagame has dismissed speculation about his health following a period in 2025 when he spent several weeks away from public engagements. In an interview with Jeune Afrique, President Kagame explained that his absence was due to personal time o
body_en:
Kigali, April 3, 2026 - President Paul Kagame has dismissed speculation about his health following a period in 2025 when he spent several weeks away from public engagements.
In an interview with Jeune Afrique, President Kagame explained that his absence was due to personal time off, which he spent with his grandchildren, emphasizing that it should not be interpreted as a health concern.
He said he had taken around three weeks to a month of leave and noted that public reactions reflected unfamiliarity with leaders taking extended personal time.
Kagame added that his current health is strong, stating that he remains in good condition compared to many people of similar age, while acknowledging the natural uncertainties of aging.
The president’s remarks follow earlier public speculation during his 2025 absence, which prompted clarification from government officials at the time.
He also used the interview to reflect on privacy expectations for public officials and the need to normalize periods of rest away from official duties.
