body_en:
Nakuru County, Kenya, March 29, 2026 - Kenyan police have rescued 67 girls believed to be victims of a suspected human trafficking network in Njoro, Nakuru County.
According to local police commander Nelson Koech, the victims were found confined in a house where they had reportedly been lured with promises of employment opportunities.
Survivors told authorities they had been held for months in overcrowded and unsanitary conditions, alleging abuse and punishment for those who questioned their situation.
Police said the premises were being used by an agency that recruits individuals for work abroad, though its operating license had expired in December 2025. Authorities had previously ordered its closure.
The agency has denied allegations of abuse, with representatives indicating they may pursue legal action.
The Kenyan government has repeatedly warned citizens against using unverified recruitment channels, citing growing cases of fraud and trafficking linked to illegal job placement schemes.

title: Alleged 1994 letter denying the Genocide against the Tutsi linked to Rusesabagina case surfaces
excerpt: Kigali, April 3, 2026 - New claims have emerged regarding the contents of a letter reportedly found at the home of Paul Rusesabagina during the post-1994 period, which is alleged to contain narratives denying or distorting the Genocide against the Tutsi. According to author Mukag
title_en: Alleged 1994 letter denying the Genocide against the Tutsi linked to Rusesabagina case surfaces
excerpt_en: Kigali, April 3, 2026 - New claims have emerged regarding the contents of a letter reportedly found at the home of Paul Rusesabagina during the post-1994 period, which is alleged to contain narratives denying or distorting the Genocide against the Tutsi. According to author Mukag
body_en:
Kigali, April 3, 2026 - New claims have emerged regarding the contents of a letter reportedly found at the home of Paul Rusesabagina during the post-1994 period, which is alleged to contain narratives denying or distorting the Genocide against the Tutsi.
According to author Mukagasana Yolande, the letter-said to have been written in August 1994 by clergy who had fled to Goma and addressed to Pope John Paul II-contained statements attributing responsibility for the violence to political actors rather than acknowledging the genocide.
Mukagasana, who shared her account during a book presentation in Mageragere, said she discovered the document while visiting Rusesabagina’s home shortly after the end of the genocide. She later referenced the alleged contents in her published work, stating that it reflected harmful narratives about the 1994 events.
She also said the letter influenced her personal relationship with the household at the time.
The claims have not been independently verified.
Paul Rusesabagina, known internationally for his role during the 1994 genocide and later legal controversies in Rwanda, was convicted in 2021 on terrorism-related charges linked to the MRCD/FLN group. He was released in March 2023 after receiving a presidential pardon and later returned to the United States.
Rusesabagina has previously acknowledged writing a letter expressing remorse, but later disputed interpretations of its meaning in a 2024 interview.

title_en: Fighting for Bule intensifies amid suspicions of external support to armed groups
excerpt_en: Djugu, March 23, 2026 - Clashes continue in the locality of Bule, in Djugu territory of Ituri province, as fighting persists between the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and the Convention for the People’s Revolution (CRP), an armed group linked to Thomas
body_en:
Djugu, March 23, 2026 - Clashes continue in the locality of Bule, in Djugu territory of Ituri province, as fighting persists between the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and the Convention for the People’s Revolution (CRP), an armed group linked to Thomas Lubanga.
Since January, Bule has remained a strategic flashpoint, with control of the area shifting between the two sides. In early February, heavy fighting led to the CRP pushing FARDC forces to the outskirts of the town, despite a counter-offensive launched the same day by government troops. The situation has since remained contested, with both sides maintaining positions in and around the area.
The conflict has also taken a toll on civilians. Reports indicate that several non-combatants have been killed in the violence, including individuals accused of collaborating with opposing forces. In nearby localities, additional clashes have resulted in civilian casualties caused by stray bullets, further heightening fear among residents.
Tensions have been exacerbated by targeted violence against specific communities. In some cases, civilians have reportedly been killed or threatened for refusing to support armed groups, contributing to an atmosphere of intimidation and deepening ethnic divisions in the region.
The situation is further complicated by suspicions within the FARDC regarding possible external support to the CRP. Congolese military sources have expressed concern over alleged links between the armed group and elements of the Ugandan army, citing observed interactions and a perceived lack of intervention during certain attacks. These allegations have not been officially confirmed.
The broader security context in Djugu remains fragile, with ongoing clashes between armed groups and government forces continuing to drive displacement and humanitarian needs. The province of Ituri has been under a state of siege since 2021, with military authorities overseeing security operations. While officials argue that some progress has been made, the persistence of violence highlights the challenges facing efforts to restore lasting stability.
As fighting continues around Bule and surrounding areas, civilians remain the most vulnerable, caught between competing forces in a conflict that shows little sign of immediate resolution.

title_en: Wazalendo Reoccupy Mpety After AFC/M23 Withdrawal Amid Shifting Frontlines in North Kivu
excerpt_en: WALIKALE, North Kivu March 29, 2026 - Wazalendo self-defense fighters have re-entered and reoccupied the town of Mpety in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, two days after the withdrawal of AFC/M23 elements from the area, according to local sources. Mpety, located in the Banak
body_en:
WALIKALE, North Kivu March 29, 2026 - Wazalendo self-defense fighters have re-entered and reoccupied the town of Mpety in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, two days after the withdrawal of AFC/M23 elements from the area, according to local sources.
Mpety, located in the Banakindi area of the Kisimba group in Walikale territory, had been under the presence of AFC/M23 fighters before their reported pullout earlier in the week. Following their departure, Wazalendo units that had been positioned several kilometers away advanced rapidly to secure the locality.
Local accounts indicate that the groups moved in to establish control and prevent any potential return of AFC/M23 forces. Since March 27, Wazalendo fighters and local commanders have been visibly present in the town, marking a new phase in the shifting control of the area.
The reoccupation reflects a broader pattern of fluid frontlines in North Kivu, where armed groups frequently reposition in response to clashes, withdrawals, or tactical redeployments.
While some residents have welcomed the Wazalendo presence as a relative improvement in security conditions, others remain concerned that the situation could escalate again if AFC/M23 elements attempt to re-enter the area, potentially triggering renewed fighting.
The development comes amid continued instability across Walikale territory and wider parts of North Kivu, where civilian populations remain exposed to recurring insecurity, displacement risks, and unpredictable changes in territorial control.

body_en:
Kisimba, Walikale, North Kivu April 3, 2026 - Several villages in the Kisimba area, including Ndumbi, Buma, Iteya, Buhaya, Mpety, and Minjenje, have come under the control of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and allied Wazalendo fighters following the withdrawal of AFC/M23 rebels without reported clashes.
The shift in control marks a significant change in the security landscape of this part of Walikale Territory in North Kivu Province, where frontlines have remained fluid amid ongoing fighting between armed groups.
The rebel withdrawal reportedly occurred without resistance, allowing government forces and their local allies to quickly reoccupy the affected villages and reestablish positions on the ground.
Following the pullback, AFC/M23 fighters are believed to have repositioned toward Malemo, a locality near Kalembe in neighboring Masisi Territory, suggesting a tactical redeployment rather than a full retreat from the broader area.
The development has created mixed reactions among local communities. While some residents cautiously welcome the return of government control and hope for improved stability, others remain fearful that the situation could quickly reverse, given the region’s history of repeated changes in territorial control.
Military forces are currently consolidating their positions in the recaptured villages in an effort to secure the area and prevent any possible counteroffensive, as tensions remain high despite the absence of active clashes at present.

body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda, March 29, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of Gender and Family Promotion, Consolée Uwimana, has called on members of the Liberal Party (PL) to play an active role in addressing pressing social challenges affecting families.
Speaking at the party’s National Council meeting, Uwimana highlighted key issues including domestic violence, teenage pregnancy, child abuse, trafficking, and drug use, warning that these problems continue to undermine family stability.
She stressed that building a secure and capable society begins at the family level, urging parents, communities, and institutions to take responsibility for child upbringing and social cohesion.
Uwimana emphasized that resolving family conflicts and strengthening parental roles could significantly reduce many of the country’s social challenges.
Liberal Party President Donatille Mukabalisa reaffirmed the party’s commitment to supporting national efforts, calling on members at all levels to contribute to building a stable and resilient society.
Authorities say collective action will be key to improving social well-being and supporting Rwanda’s long-term development goals.

excerpt_en: North Kivu, DR Congo, March 29, 2026 - The AFC/M23 rebel group has denied reports that it is withdrawing fighters from areas under its control in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The claims, circulated in local media over the weekend, suggested that M23 forces were redeployi
body_en:
North Kivu, DR Congo, March 29, 2026 - The AFC/M23 rebel group has denied reports that it is withdrawing fighters from areas under its control in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The claims, circulated in local media over the weekend, suggested that M23 forces were redeploying from several locations in Lubero territory to other positions, allegedly under international pressure.
In a statement, North Kivu Governor Erasto Bahati dismissed the reports, describing ongoing movements as routine military rotations rather than a withdrawal.
Authorities said the information circulating on social media was intended to create confusion among the population, urging residents to remain calm and continue their daily activities.
The situation in eastern DRC remains tense, with ongoing military operations and competing narratives surrounding developments on the ground.

title: La RDC suspend le plafonnement des prix du transport de carburant pendant 45 jours dans un contexte de tensions sur le marché pétrolier mondial
excerpt: Kinshasa le 24 mars 2026 - Le gouvernement de la République Démocratique du Congo a suspendu temporairement le plafonnement des différentiels de prix de transport des produits pétroliers pour une durée de 45 jours, dans le cadre des mesures visant à stabiliser l'approvisionnement en carburant et à protéger les achats des consommateurs.
title_en: DRC suspends fuel transport price cap for 45 days amid global oil market tensions
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 24, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has temporarily suspended the cap on transport price differentials for petroleum products for a period of 45 days, as part of measures aimed at stabilizing fuel supply and protecting consumer purchasing
body_en:
Kinshasa March 24, 2026 - The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has temporarily suspended the cap on transport price differentials for petroleum products for a period of 45 days, as part of measures aimed at stabilizing fuel supply and protecting consumer purchasing power.
The decision was taken under instructions from Prime Minister Judith Suminwa Tuluka, who directed the ministries responsible for the economy, hydrocarbons, and finance to implement the suspension in response to rising geopolitical tensions affecting global energy markets.
Authorities say the measure is intended to anticipate the economic impact of disruptions in international oil supply routes, including key maritime corridors such as the Strait of Hormuz and the Suez Canal.
While the suspension could lead to higher logistics costs in the short term, the government has announced compensatory steps, including temporary reductions or suspensions of certain border taxes and royalties to limit pressure on fuel prices.
Officials also indicated that additional measures will be implemented to ensure the steady import and distribution of petroleum products via regional supply routes through Kenya and Tanzania, while monitoring freight and insurance costs used to calculate average border pricing.
Despite global market volatility, the government has reassured the public that national fuel reserves remain sufficient to meet demand until June, with additional shipments expected in the coming weeks to reinforce supply.
The policy follows discussions in a recent Council of Ministers meeting chaired by President Félix Tshisekedi, during which officials emphasized the need for coordinated action to maintain macroeconomic stability in the face of external shocks.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, le 24 mars 2026 - Le gouvernement de la République démocratique du Congo a suspendu temporairement le plafonnement des différentiels de prix de transport des produits pétroliers pour une durée de 45 jours, dans le cadre de mesures visant à stabiliser l'approvisionnement en carburant et à protéger le pouvoir d'achat des consommateurs.
La décision a été prise sur instructions du Premier ministre Judith Suminwa Tuluka, qui a demandé aux ministères en charge de l'économie, des hydrocarbures et des finances de mettre en œuvre la suspension en réponse aux tensions géopolitiques croissantes affectant les marchés mondiaux de l'énergie.
Les autorités affirment que cette mesure vise à anticiper l'impact économique des perturbations des routes internationales d'approvisionnement en pétrole, y compris les principaux corridors maritimes tels que le détroit d'Ormuz et le canal de Suez.
Même si la suspension pourrait entraîner une hausse des coûts logistiques à court terme, le gouvernement a annoncé des mesures compensatoires, notamment des réductions ou suspensions temporaires de certaines taxes et redevances aux frontières, afin de limiter la pression sur les prix des carburants.
Les responsables ont également indiqué que des mesures supplémentaires seront mises en œuvre pour garantir l'importation et la distribution régulières de produits pétroliers via les routes d'approvisionnement régionales à travers le Kenya et la Tanzanie, tout en surveillant les coûts de fret et d'assurance utilisés pour calculer les prix moyens à la frontière.
Malgré la volatilité des marchés mondiaux, le gouvernement a rassuré le public sur le fait que les réserves nationales de carburant restent suffisantes pour répondre à la demande jusqu'en juin, et que des expéditions supplémentaires sont attendues dans les semaines à venir pour renforcer l'offre.
Cette politique fait suite aux discussions lors d’une récente réunion du Conseil des ministres présidée par le président Félix Tshisekedi, au cours de laquelle les responsables ont souligné la nécessité d’une action coordonnée pour maintenir la stabilité macroéconomique face aux chocs extérieurs.

title: Les parties prenantes de la RDC font pression pour des réformes visant à améliorer les conditions des mineurs artisanaux face aux problèmes de gouvernance
excerpt: Kinshasa, le 5 avril 2026 - Un débat politique tenu à Kinshasa a mis en lumière les conditions précaires auxquelles sont confrontés les mineurs artisanaux en République démocratique du Congo, appelant à des réformes urgentes pour améliorer la gouvernance, la sécurité et la transparence dans le secteur. title_en: DRC stakeholders push for reforms to improve conditions for artisanal miners amid governance concerns
excerpt_en: Kinshasa April 5, 2026 - A political discussion held in Kinshasa has highlighted the precarious conditions faced by artisanal miners in the Democratic Republic of Congo, calling for urgent reforms to improve governance, safety, and transparency in the sector. Organized on April 2
body_en:
Kinshasa April 5, 2026 - A political discussion held in Kinshasa has highlighted the precarious conditions faced by artisanal miners in the Democratic Republic of Congo, calling for urgent reforms to improve governance, safety, and transparency in the sector.
Organized on April 2 by the DRC Political Scientists’ Network (Dypol) in partnership with the Friedrich Ebert Foundation (FES), the meeting brought together policymakers, civil society actors, and mining sector experts to examine challenges affecting artisanal mining communities.
Participants noted that despite its major contribution to the national economy and livelihoods of millions, the artisanal mining sector remains characterized by informal operations, weak regulation, unsafe working conditions, child labor risks, and gender inequality.
Speaking after the discussions, Dypol national coordinator Christian Moleka stressed the need for a revised mining code that clearly defines the role of artisanal mining and strengthens oversight mechanisms to improve safety and transparency across supply chains.
He emphasized that artisanal miners are often the most vulnerable actors in a value chain that generates significant revenues, yet they remain marginalized and exposed to frequent accidents and poor working conditions.
Representatives of the Friedrich Ebert Foundation highlighted the importance of promoting more inclusive and sustainable mining governance, where artisanal mining can contribute to long-term development rather than persistent precarity.
Journalist Flore Kayala, who specializes in mining issues, drew attention to the economic role of women in the sector, noting that they remain underrepresented and face limited access to financing and cooperative leadership structures dominated by men.
She called for inclusive policies and better financial support mechanisms to enable women to participate more actively in mining activities and benefit from sector revenues.
The meeting is expected to produce a roadmap aimed at improving coordination between government institutions, civil society, mining companies, and artisanal miners to promote safer, more transparent, and more equitable mining practices in the DRC.

body_fr:
Kinshasa, le 5 avril 2026 - Un débat politique tenu à Kinshasa a mis en lumière les conditions précaires auxquelles sont confrontés les mineurs artisanaux en République démocratique du Congo, appelant à des réformes urgentes pour améliorer la gouvernance, la sécurité et la transparence dans le secteur.
Organisée le 2 avril par le Réseau des politologues de la RDC (Dypol) en partenariat avec la Fondation Friedrich Ebert (FES), la réunion a réuni des décideurs politiques, des acteurs de la société civile et des experts du secteur minier pour examiner les défis affectant les communautés minières artisanales.
Les participants ont noté que malgré sa contribution majeure à l'économie nationale et aux moyens de subsistance de millions de personnes, le secteur minier artisanal reste caractérisé par des opérations informelles, une réglementation faible, des conditions de travail dangereuses, des risques de travail des enfants et des inégalités entre les sexes.
S'exprimant après les discussions, le coordinateur national de Dypol, Christian Moleka, a souligné la nécessité d'un code minier révisé qui définit clairement le rôle de l'exploitation minière artisanale et renforce les mécanismes de surveillance pour améliorer la sécurité et la transparence dans les chaînes d'approvisionnement.
Il a souligné que les mineurs artisanaux sont souvent les acteurs les plus vulnérables d'une chaîne de valeur qui génère des revenus importants, mais qu'ils restent marginalisés et exposés à des accidents fréquents et à de mauvaises conditions de travail.
Les représentants de la Fondation Friedrich Ebert ont souligné l'importance de promouvoir une gouvernance minière plus inclusive et durable, où l'exploitation minière artisanale peut contribuer au développement à long terme plutôt qu'à une précarité persistante.
La journaliste Flore Kayala, spécialisée dans les questions minières, a attiré l'attention sur le rôle économique des femmes dans le secteur, soulignant qu'elles restent sous-représentées et confrontées à un accès limité au financement et aux structures de leadership coopératif dominées par les hommes.
Elle a appelé à des politiques inclusives et à de meilleurs mécanismes de soutien financier pour permettre aux femmes de participer plus activement aux activités minières et de bénéficier des revenus du secteur.
La réunion devrait produire une feuille de route visant à améliorer la coordination entre les institutions gouvernementales, la société civile, les sociétés minières et les mineurs artisanaux afin de promouvoir des pratiques minières plus sûres, plus transparentes et plus équitables en RDC.

title_en: Fresh clashes erupt between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo in Kanune
excerpt_en: Walikale, March 22, 2026 - Heavy fighting broke out early Sunday in the village of Kanune, located in the Ikobo grouping of Walikale territory, North Kivu, as clashes opposed fighters of the AFC/M23 coalition to Wazalendo militias. According to local sources, the confrontation be
body_en:
Walikale, March 22, 2026 - Heavy fighting broke out early Sunday in the village of Kanune, located in the Ikobo grouping of Walikale territory, North Kivu, as clashes opposed fighters of the AFC/M23 coalition to Wazalendo militias.
According to local sources, the confrontation began around 5:00 a.m. when Wazalendo elements launched an offensive on positions held by AFC/M23 forces. Residents reported sustained gunfire involving both heavy and light weapons, forcing civilians to remain confined to their homes amid growing panic.
The area of Ikobo has been under AFC/M23 control for nearly a year, following earlier confrontations that saw Wazalendo fighters pushed out of the zone. Since then, the security situation has remained fragile, with recurring tensions and sporadic violence.
Recent movements of rebel reinforcements toward nearby areas, particularly Kisimba, are believed to have altered the balance on the ground. Observers suggest that this redeployment may have weakened certain AFC/M23 positions, especially in the western parts of Buleusa, prompting the latest attempt by Wazalendo forces to regain lost territory.
As fighting continues, the humanitarian situation remains a major concern. Civilians, already affected by prolonged instability, face increasing risks as clashes intensify in and around populated areas. Local authorities have yet to provide an official update on casualties or displacement, while the situation on the ground remains highly fluid.

excerpt_en: WALIKALE, North Kivu March 27, 2026 - The village of Kateku, in the Iremya area of the Ikobo group, was recaptured on March 26 by Wazalendo fighters following clashes with AFC/M23 elements, according to local administrative and community sources. The fighting reportedly broke out
body_en:
WALIKALE, North Kivu March 27, 2026 - The village of Kateku, in the Iremya area of the Ikobo group, was recaptured on March 26 by Wazalendo fighters following clashes with AFC/M23 elements, according to local administrative and community sources.
The fighting reportedly broke out after AFC/M23 fighters had occupied the area. The confrontation lasted around two hours before the armed group withdrew, allowing Wazalendo forces to regain control of the village.
Local sources indicate that at least one combatant from AFC/M23 was killed during the clashes. Following the setback, the group reportedly retreated toward Buleusa, a major locality in the Ikobo area.
The renewed fighting triggered fresh civilian displacement, with residents fleeing toward Buleusa and others moving further into neighboring Lubero territory in search of safety.
Traditional leaders in the area have confirmed the change of control, while warning that the security situation in this part of Walikale remains highly unstable, marked by recurring clashes and shifting control between armed groups.

title_en: ADF Attack on Mambasa-Kisangani Axis Leaves 43 Dead, Dozens of Homes Destroyed
excerpt_en: Bafwakoa, Mambasa Territory, Ituri Province April 2, 2026 - At least 43 civilians were killed and extensive material destruction recorded on Thursday, April 2, following a deadly attack attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in Bafwakoa, a village located about 148 kilo
body_en:
Bafwakoa, Mambasa Territory, Ituri Province April 2, 2026 - At least 43 civilians were killed and extensive material destruction recorded on Thursday, April 2, following a deadly attack attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in Bafwakoa, a village located about 148 kilometers from Mambasa along the Kisangani road in Ituri Province in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The attack occurred in the evening when armed assailants stormed the village, opening fire on civilians and setting fire to homes and vehicles. Local reports indicate that 44 houses were burned, along with several motorcycles and a truck, leaving significant material losses in the community.
The assault took place in a region currently under a state of siege, where military authorities are deployed to restore security amid persistent attacks by armed groups operating in the area.
Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya confirmed the toll, stating that 43 people were killed and multiple properties destroyed, describing the attack as a serious violation of human rights carried out by ADF elements against civilians. He added that security forces are intensifying operations aimed at dismantling ADF networks and restoring stability in the region.
Authorities have urged the population to cooperate with security services and report any suspicious activity, while reaffirming ongoing military efforts to neutralize armed groups responsible for repeated atrocities.
The attack has once again raised concerns over the effectiveness of security measures in eastern Democratic Republic of the Congo, where civilians continue to suffer repeated massacres despite ongoing joint operations by Congolese forces and regional partners.
The ADF, active mainly in forested areas across North Kivu and Ituri, continues to carry out deadly attacks along the Beni, Lubero, Irumu, and Mambasa axes, despite years of military operations aimed at ending its insurgency.

title: Rwanda banks finance major telecom infrastructure deal involving 1,400 towers
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda, March 28, 2026 - A consortium of six commercial banks in Rwanda has provided financing to support a large-scale telecommunications infrastructure transaction involving more than 1,400 mobile network towers. The deal, led by the Bank of Kigali alongside BPR Bank Rw
title_en: Rwanda banks finance major telecom infrastructure deal involving 1,400 towers
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda, March 28, 2026 - A consortium of six commercial banks in Rwanda has provided financing to support a large-scale telecommunications infrastructure transaction involving more than 1,400 mobile network towers. The deal, led by the Bank of Kigali alongside BPR Bank Rw
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda, March 28, 2026 - A consortium of six commercial banks in Rwanda has provided financing to support a large-scale telecommunications infrastructure transaction involving more than 1,400 mobile network towers.
The deal, led by the Bank of Kigali alongside BPR Bank Rwanda, the Development Bank of Rwanda (BRD), I&M Bank Rwanda, Ecobank Rwanda, and Access Bank Rwanda, is part of a syndicated loan arrangement backing the acquisition and management of critical telecom assets.
The towers, originally owned by IHS Holdings Rwanda, were sold in October 2025 to Paradigm Tower Ventures for an estimated $274.5 million and later transferred to its local subsidiary, Ishara Towers Rwanda, which will oversee operations in the country.
Bank of Kigali CEO Diane Karusisi said the transaction demonstrates the growing capacity of Rwanda’s financial sector to support large-scale infrastructure investments essential for digital connectivity and economic growth.
Paradigm Tower Ventures CEO Gordon Porter welcomed the agreement, describing it as a strong example of partnership between international investors and Rwandan financial institutions.
The telecom towers are considered critical infrastructure, supporting mobile communications, internet access, and digital financial services across the country.

body_en:
Musanze, Rwanda, March 29, 2026 - A group of 28 postgraduate students from SOAS University of London has visited the Mutobo Demobilization and Reintegration Centre in northern Rwanda to study the country’s approach to rehabilitating former armed group members.
The visit focused on understanding how Rwanda receives and reintegrates former fighters from groups such as the FDLR, many of whom return from eastern Democratic Republic of Congo after years in armed movements.
The delegation was received by Jacques Nziza, Vice President of the Rwanda Demobilization and Reintegration Commission, who outlined ongoing efforts to support ex-combatants in transitioning back into civilian life.
Students also held discussions with former fighters, who shared testimonies about their experiences in the bush and their decision to return and reintegrate into Rwandan society.
Professor Phil Clark, speaking on behalf of the group, praised the initiative, highlighting its role in promoting peace, reconciliation, and long-term stability in the Great Lakes region.

title_en: Rwanda and DRC exchange accusations over Banyamulenge attacks amid ongoing tensions
excerpt_en: Kigali, April 3, 2026 - Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have traded accusations over recent violence in eastern DRC, particularly in areas inhabited by the Banyamulenge community. Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo criticized statements from the DRC
body_en:
Kigali, April 3, 2026 - Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have traded accusations over recent violence in eastern DRC, particularly in areas inhabited by the Banyamulenge community.
Rwandan government spokesperson Yolande Makolo criticized statements from the DRC government accusing AFC/M23 of responsibility for attacks in Minembwe, arguing instead that Congolese forces and their allies are the ones carrying out abuses.
Makolo accused Kinshasa of “distorting the truth” and attempting to shift blame for actions committed by government forces and allied groups, including Burundian troops and Wazalendo militias.
The allegations come amid continued instability in eastern DRC, where multiple armed actors remain active despite ongoing peace talks in Doha.
Rwanda maintains that lasting peace in the region depends on the dismantling of the FDLR, which Kigali accuses of spreading genocidal ideology and fueling insecurity in the area.
The DRC government has not publicly responded to the latest statements.

title: Course au poste de gouverneur de Sankuru : une contestation judiciaire menace le calendrier des élections du 15 avril
excerpt: Sankuru, 4 avril 2026 - Un différend juridique sur l'éligibilité des candidats a introduit une nouvelle incertitude dans le processus électoral pour le poste de gouverneur de la province de Sankuru, avec une audience clé au tribunal prévue le 10 avril. Le Conseil d'État est sur le point d'examiner une affaire déposée par la province de Sankuru.
title_en: Sankuru gubernatorial race: Legal challenge threatens April 15 election timetable
excerpt_en: Sankuru April 4, 2026 - A legal dispute over candidate eligibility has introduced fresh uncertainty into the electoral process for the governorship of Sankuru province, with a key court hearing scheduled for April 10. The Council of State is set to examine a case filed by guberna
body_en:
Sankuru April 4, 2026 - A legal dispute over candidate eligibility has introduced fresh uncertainty into the electoral process for the governorship of Sankuru province, with a key court hearing scheduled for April 10.
The Council of State is set to examine a case filed by gubernatorial candidate Justin Omokala Wemambolo, who is contesting the final list of candidates published by the Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI).
Omokala is challenging the inclusion of fellow candidate Jules Lodi Emongo, arguing that his candidacy as an independent violates constitutional and electoral provisions. According to him, Emongo-elected as a senator under the banner of the Union for Democracy and Social Progress-failed to formally resign from his party before declaring an independent bid, as required by law.
He also contests the eligibility of Emongo’s running mate for vice-governor, claiming the individual, a civil servant, did not submit a resignation or official leave of absence prior to entering the race, in breach of electoral regulations.
The dispute follows a decision by the Sankuru Court of Appeal, which rejected Omokala’s appeal on procedural grounds, ruling that he lacked standing despite appearing on the provisional list of candidates. Omokala has since escalated the matter to the Council of State, the country’s highest administrative jurisdiction.
He further criticized CENI for publishing the final list before the conclusion of ongoing legal proceedings, arguing that the electoral body should have awaited the outcome of the April 10 hearing.
The controversy comes as the gubernatorial election, initially delayed due to funding constraints, is now scheduled for April 15. The final list includes 10 candidates, down from 11 following the withdrawal of one contender.
With legal proceedings still underway, the outcome of the Council of State hearing could prove decisive in determining whether the electoral calendar in Sankuru can be maintained.
body_fr:
Sankuru, 4 avril 2026 - Un différend juridique sur l'éligibilité des candidats a introduit une nouvelle incertitude dans le processus électoral pour le poste de gouverneur de la province de Sankuru, avec une audience clé au tribunal prévue le 10 avril.
Le Conseil d'Etat va examiner le dossier déposé par le candidat au poste de gouverneur Justin Omokala Wemambolo, qui conteste la liste définitive des candidats publiée par la Commission électorale nationale indépendante (CENI).
Omokala conteste l'inclusion de son compatriote Jules Lodi Emongo, arguant que sa candidature en tant qu'indépendant viole les dispositions constitutionnelles et électorales. Selon lui, Emongo, élu sénateur sous la bannière de l'Union pour la démocratie et le progrès social, n'a pas formellement démissionné de son parti avant de déclarer une candidature indépendante, comme l'exige la loi.
Il conteste également l’éligibilité du colistier d’Emongo au poste de vice-gouverneur, affirmant que l’individu, un fonctionnaire, n’a pas présenté de démission ni de congé officiel avant de se lancer dans la course, en violation du règlement électoral.
Le litige fait suite à une décision de la Cour d’appel de Sankuru, qui a rejeté l’appel d’Omokala pour des raisons de procédure, estimant qu’il n’avait pas qualité pour agir bien qu’il apparaisse sur la liste provisoire des candidats. Omokala a depuis porté l’affaire devant le Conseil d’État, la plus haute juridiction administrative du pays.
Il a en outre critiqué la CENI pour avoir publié la liste définitive avant la conclusion des procédures judiciaires en cours, arguant que le corps électoral aurait dû attendre le résultat de l'audience du 10 avril.
La controverse survient alors que l'élection du gouverneur, initialement retardée en raison de contraintes financières, est désormais prévue pour le 15 avril. La liste définitive comprend 10 candidats, contre 11 suite au retrait d'un candidat.
Alors que les procédures judiciaires sont toujours en cours, l'issue de l'audience du Conseil d'Etat pourrait s'avérer décisive pour déterminer si le calendrier électoral du Sankuru peut être maintenu.

title: Le gouverneur du Sud-Kivu déclare que le contrôle de l'AFC/M23 réduit les revenus de la province de 84 % dans un contexte de conflit en cours
excerpt: Kinshasa le 3 avril 2026 - Le gouverneur du Sud-Kivu, Jean-Jacques Purusi, a prévenu que la province perd la grande majorité de ses revenus à cause des territoires contrôlés par le groupe armé AFC/M23, qui, selon lui, a établi une administration parallèle dans certaines parties de l'Est.
title_en: South Kivu governor says AFC/M23 control cuts provincial revenue by 84% amid ongoing conflict
excerpt_en: Kinshasa April 3, 2026 - The governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Purusi, has warned that the province is losing the vast majority of its revenues due to territories controlled by the AFC/M23 armed group, which he says has established a parallel administration in parts of eastern
body_en:
Kinshasa April 3, 2026 - The governor of South Kivu, Jean-Jacques Purusi, has warned that the province is losing the vast majority of its revenues due to territories controlled by the AFC/M23 armed group, which he says has established a parallel administration in parts of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
Speaking at a press briefing in Kinshasa on April 2, the governor stated that the occupation of key areas including Bukavu, Walungu, Kabare, and parts of Kalehe has resulted in an estimated 84% loss of provincial revenue.
He explained that South Kivu’s budget, which was projected at around USD 66 million, had effectively collapsed after government authorities relocated from Bukavu to Uvira, leaving major economic zones outside state control.
Purusi further alleged that the AFC/M23 administration generates between USD 17 million and USD 20 million per month through taxation in the occupied areas, claiming that these funds are transferred across the border into Rwanda.
According to him, the group has implemented a structured taxation system over local populations under difficult living conditions, while benefiting from the region’s economic activities.
In response to the fiscal collapse, the governor said he had obtained authorization from Kinshasa to reorganize revenue collection in remaining government-controlled areas, particularly at border points. He suggested that improved digitization, banking access, and streamlined customs systems could help restore up to USD 3-4 million in monthly revenue.
However, he acknowledged that the province’s economic base has been severely weakened due to looting, destruction of infrastructure, bank closures, and the broader disruption of local commerce.
Meanwhile, despite ongoing international diplomatic efforts-including the Washington process and talks mediated in Doha by Qatar-progress toward stabilizing the security situation in eastern Congo remains limited. Both Kinshasa and Kigali continue to trade accusations over violations of existing agreements, while negotiations aimed at restoring state authority and reintegrating armed groups have stalled.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, le 3 avril 2026 - Le gouverneur du Sud-Kivu, Jean-Jacques Purusi, a averti que la province perd la grande majorité de ses revenus à cause des territoires contrôlés par le groupe armé AFC/M23, qui, selon lui, a établi une administration parallèle dans certaines parties de l'est de la République démocratique du Congo.
S'exprimant lors d'une conférence de presse à Kinshasa le 2 avril, le gouverneur a déclaré que l'occupation de zones clés, notamment Bukavu, Walungu, Kabare et certaines parties de Kalehe, avait entraîné une perte estimée à 84 % des revenus provinciaux.
Il a expliqué que le budget du Sud-Kivu, qui était prévu à environ 66 millions de dollars, s’était effectivement effondré après le déménagement des autorités gouvernementales de Bukavu à Uvira, laissant les principales zones économiques hors du contrôle de l’État.
Purusi a en outre allégué que l'administration de l'AFC/M23 génère entre 17 et 20 millions de dollars par mois grâce aux impôts dans les zones occupées, affirmant que ces fonds sont transférés de l'autre côté de la frontière vers le Rwanda.
Selon lui, le groupe a mis en place une fiscalité structurée sur les populations locales vivant dans des conditions difficiles, tout en bénéficiant des activités économiques de la région.
En réponse à l'effondrement budgétaire, le gouverneur a déclaré qu'il avait obtenu de Kinshasa l'autorisation de réorganiser la collecte des recettes dans les zones encore contrôlées par le gouvernement, en particulier aux postes frontières. Il a suggéré qu'une numérisation améliorée, un accès bancaire et des systèmes douaniers rationalisés pourraient aider à restaurer jusqu'à 3 à 4 millions de dollars de revenus mensuels.
Cependant, il a reconnu que la base économique de la province a été gravement affaiblie en raison des pillages, de la destruction des infrastructures, des fermetures de banques et de la perturbation plus large du commerce local.
Pendant ce temps, malgré les efforts diplomatiques internationaux en cours – y compris le processus de Washington et les pourparlers négociés à Doha par le Qatar – les progrès vers la stabilisation de la situation sécuritaire dans l’est du Congo restent limités. Kinshasa et Kigali continuent de s'accuser mutuellement de violations des accords existants, tandis que les négociations visant à restaurer l'autorité de l'État et à réintégrer les groupes armés sont dans l'impasse.

title: Gims placed in police custody in money laundering investigation in France
excerpt: Paris March 25, 2026 - Congolese-French singer and rapper Gims has been taken into police custody for questioning in connection with an investigation into alleged organized money laundering activities. According to judicial sources, the 39-year-old artist is being questioned unde
title_en: Gims placed in police custody in money laundering investigation in France
excerpt_en: Paris March 25, 2026 - Congolese-French singer and rapper Gims has been taken into police custody for questioning in connection with an investigation into alleged organized money laundering activities. According to judicial sources, the 39-year-old artist is being questioned unde
body_en:
Paris March 25, 2026 - Congolese-French singer and rapper Gims has been taken into police custody for questioning in connection with an investigation into alleged organized money laundering activities.
According to judicial sources, the 39-year-old artist is being questioned under a rogatory commission issued by investigating magistrates and overseen by France’s National Anti-Organized Crime Prosecutor’s Office. He is reportedly being examined as part of inquiries into suspected complex financial operations involving significant monetary flows.
Gims, whose birth name is Gandhi Djuna, was apprehended on Wednesday upon his arrival at Paris-Charles de Gaulle Airport from Dubai. Investigators are seeking to clarify his possible role in financial transactions described as suspicious, although no formal charges have been publicly announced at this stage.
A prominent figure in Francophone music and a self-described ambassador of Congolese culture, Gims was appointed cultural ambassador for the Democratic Republic of Congo in January 2022 by President Félix Tshisekedi. He was also granted a diplomatic passport in recognition of his role in promoting Congolese culture abroad.
Alongside his international career, he has frequently highlighted Congolese musical heritage, collaborating with and drawing inspiration from major figures such as Koffi Olomide. His work often incorporates Congolese rhythms, helping broaden their reach across global Francophone audiences.
Beyond music, Gims has been involved in cultural and humanitarian initiatives linked to the Democratic Republic of Congo, including proposals for modern recording studios in Kinshasa and Lubumbashi and support for cultural events aimed at promoting Congolese music internationally. He has also used his platform to speak out on humanitarian crises in eastern Congo and to call for international attention to ongoing violence in the region.

title: RSF Report Warns of Mass Exodus of Journalists From Eastern DRC Amid Rising Insecurity
excerpt: KINSHASA / EASTERN DRC March 27, 2026 - A growing number of journalists are fleeing the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo due to escalating threats, violence, and deteriorating working conditions linked to ongoing armed conflict, according to a Reporters Without Borders (RSF)
title_en: RSF Report Warns of Mass Exodus of Journalists From Eastern DRC Amid Rising Insecurity
excerpt_en: KINSHASA / EASTERN DRC March 27, 2026 - A growing number of journalists are fleeing the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo due to escalating threats, violence, and deteriorating working conditions linked to ongoing armed conflict, according to a Reporters Without Borders (RSF)
body_en:
KINSHASA / EASTERN DRC March 27, 2026 - A growing number of journalists are fleeing the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo due to escalating threats, violence, and deteriorating working conditions linked to ongoing armed conflict, according to a Reporters Without Borders (RSF) report reviewed under embargo.
The report, drawing on testimony from the National Union of the Congolese Press (UNPC), indicates that dozens of media professionals have been displaced from conflict-affected provinces, particularly North Kivu and South Kivu. While some have relocated within the country, others have sought refuge in neighboring states including Burundi, Uganda, and Rwanda.
RSF describes a pattern of dangerous displacement journeys, with journalists crossing areas controlled by armed groups or security forces. Several report having faced threats, arrests, interrogations, or temporary detention linked to their professional activities.
Conditions in host countries remain precarious. Some Congolese journalists in exile reportedly face detention in transit centers or administrative uncertainty before release, while others struggle with limited resources and lack of legal status.
The report notes that relocation to Kinshasa is not always a viable alternative, citing high living costs, limited professional opportunities, and unstable income conditions that make continued journalism difficult for displaced reporters.
Multiple testimonies also highlight sustained pressure on media workers, including accusations of collaboration with armed groups and threats following the publication or broadcast of sensitive reporting. In some cases, journalists say they were compelled to relay information dictated by actors in the conflict.
Several journalists interviewed in the report say they have been forced to abandon the profession entirely due to insecurity. One testimony cited by RSF describes a journalist leaving Rutshuru after repeated threats and eventually giving up reporting work.
The report also raises concerns about cross-border risks, noting that exiled journalists may continue to face surveillance, detention, or legal harassment in host countries. It references cases in the region as examples of broader patterns affecting press freedom in conflict contexts.
RSF concludes that the ongoing displacement of journalists is severely undermining access to independent reporting from eastern Congo and calls for stronger protections for media workers both within the country and across borders.

title: Heavy Clashes Erupt Between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo in Shoa
excerpt: Shoa, Masisi, North Kivu April 1, 2026 - Violent fighting broke out early Wednesday, April 1, in Shoa, located in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi Territory in North Kivu Province, as AFC/M23 fighters engaged Wazalendo forces in a renewed confrontation over control of the area.
title_en: Heavy Clashes Erupt Between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo in Shoa
excerpt_en: Shoa, Masisi, North Kivu April 1, 2026 - Violent fighting broke out early Wednesday, April 1, in Shoa, located in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi Territory in North Kivu Province, as AFC/M23 fighters engaged Wazalendo forces in a renewed confrontation over control of the area.
body_en:
Shoa, Masisi, North Kivu April 1, 2026 - Violent fighting broke out early Wednesday, April 1, in Shoa, located in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi Territory in North Kivu Province, as AFC/M23 fighters engaged Wazalendo forces in a renewed confrontation over control of the area.
Local sources reported sustained exchanges of heavy and light weapons fire from the early hours of the morning, indicating intense and ongoing clashes that left the situation highly unstable and unclear throughout the day.

title: Rwanda reports sharp decline in dental disease cases following nationwide awareness campaigns
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda, March 28, 2026 - Health officials in Rwanda say cases of dental disease have significantly decreased following sustained public awareness campaigns, particularly in schools. According to the National Health Institute (RBC), reductions have been recorded in tooth d
title_en: Rwanda reports sharp decline in dental disease cases following nationwide awareness campaigns
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda, March 28, 2026 - Health officials in Rwanda say cases of dental disease have significantly decreased following sustained public awareness campaigns, particularly in schools. According to the National Health Institute (RBC), reductions have been recorded in tooth d
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda, March 28, 2026 - Health officials in Rwanda say cases of dental disease have significantly decreased following sustained public awareness campaigns, particularly in schools.
According to the National Health Institute (RBC), reductions have been recorded in tooth decay and hygiene-related oral conditions, following intensified education programs on oral health.
Bagahirwa Irène, a specialist in non-communicable diseases at RBC, said cases of tooth decay have dropped from 45% to 16%, while pain linked to poor oral hygiene has fallen from 44% to 7%.
She attributed the progress to school-based awareness campaigns aimed at encouraging children to adopt regular dental hygiene practices.
The head of the Association of Dentists and Oral Surgeons, Niyibizi Fabrice, said most patients treated are young children suffering from preventable dental conditions, but noted that awareness efforts are beginning to show results.
The Secretary of State in the Ministry of Education, Irere Claudette, stressed the importance of combining school feeding programs with hygiene education, urging students to adopt consistent oral care habits.
Despite the improvement, health data still indicates that dental care-seeking behavior remains largely reactive, with many patients only visiting clinics when pain becomes severe, highlighting ongoing gaps in preventive care awareness.

body_en:
Bimbo, Central African Republic, March 28, 2026 - Rwandan troops serving under the United Nations peacekeeping mission in the Central African Republic (MINUSCA) have carried out a humanitarian medical outreach at Bimbo Women’s Prison near Bangui.
The First Battalion of the Rwandan contingent conducted medical screenings and treatment for inmates, focusing on general health conditions as well as dental and eye care services, following a request from prison authorities through MINUSCA.
The team also distributed essential medicines and held psychosocial support sessions aimed at restoring hope and improving mental well-being among detainees.
Battalion Commander Lt Col Paul Gasasira said the initiative reflects MINUSCA’s commitment not only to peace and security, but also to the protection of human dignity for all, including prisoners.
Prison Director Djadde Clotilde expressed appreciation for the mission, praising the Rwandan contingent for its humanitarian support and cooperation.
Officials say the intervention provided both medical relief and emotional support, reinforcing trust between peacekeepers and local institutions.

title_en: Norbert Basengezi elected Second Vice-President, replacing Bahati Lukwebo
excerpt_en: Kinshasa April 3, 2026 - Senator Norbert Basengezi Katintima has been elected Second Vice-President of the Senate of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, securing a clear majority in Friday’s vote. According to results announced by Senate President Jean-Michel Sama Lukonde, Base
body_en:
Kinshasa April 3, 2026 - Senator Norbert Basengezi Katintima has been elected Second Vice-President of the Senate of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, securing a clear majority in Friday’s vote.
According to results announced by Senate President Jean-Michel Sama Lukonde, Basengezi received 87 votes in favor, against 5 votes opposed and 3 invalid ballots.
A former head of the Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI) and senator representing South Kivu, Basengezi was designated by the ruling coalition, the Sacred Union of the Nation, to succeed Modeste Bahati Lukwebo in the Senate bureau.
His election follows a process marked by the withdrawal of other contenders. Senator Françoise Bemba Ndokwa, initially in the race, saw her candidacy withdrawn by her party, the Movement for the Liberation of Congo. Another candidate, Mariane Bakiele, also stepped down on the eve of the vote, citing alignment with the majority coalition’s choice and respect for the Head of State, Félix Tshisekedi.
With no remaining challengers, Basengezi stood as the sole candidate, a position validated by a special commission set up to review applications.
The vacancy followed the resignation of Bahati Lukwebo, which the Senate formally acknowledged during a plenary session on March 21. His departure came amid a petition seeking his removal over alleged “incompetence.” A special parliamentary commission had been tasked with examining the case but closed its proceedings after his resignation.
Basengezi’s election consolidates the Sacred Union’s hold over key positions within the upper chamber, at a time of ongoing political realignments within the country’s institutions.
body_fr:
Kinshasa le 3 avril 2026 – Le sénateur Norbert Basengezi Katintima a été élu deuxième vice-président du Sénat de la République démocratique du Congo, obtenant une nette majorité lors du vote de vendredi.
Selon les résultats annoncés par le président du Sénat Jean-Michel Sama Lukonde, Basengezi a obtenu 87 voix pour, contre 5 voix contre et 3 bulletins nuls.
Ancien chef de la Commission électorale nationale indépendante (CENI) et sénateur représentant le Sud-Kivu, Basengezi a été désigné par la coalition au pouvoir, l'Union sacrée de la nation, pour succéder à Modeste Bahati Lukwebo au bureau du Sénat.
Son élection fait suite à un processus marqué par le retrait des autres prétendants. La sénatrice Françoise Bemba Ndokwa, initialement en lice, a vu sa candidature retirée par son parti, le Mouvement de libération du Congo. Une autre candidate, Mariane Bakiele, a également démissionné à la veille du scrutin, invoquant son alignement sur le choix de la coalition majoritaire et son respect pour le chef de l’État, Félix Tshisekedi.
Sans challenger restant, Basengezi s'est présenté comme seul candidat, une position validée par une commission spéciale chargée d'examiner les candidatures.
Cette vacance fait suite à la démission de Bahati Lukwebo, que le Sénat a officiellement reconnue lors d'une séance plénière le 21 mars. Son départ intervient au milieu d'une pétition demandant sa destitution pour prétendue « incompétence ». Une commission parlementaire spéciale avait été chargée d'examiner le cas mais a clôturé ses travaux après sa démission.
L’élection de Basengezi consolide l’emprise de l’Union sacrée sur des postes clés au sein de la chambre haute, à une époque de réalignements politiques en cours au sein des institutions du pays.

title_en: Diplomatic dispute erupts over AU process for UN Secretary-General nomination
excerpt_en: Addis Ababa, March 30, 2026 - A procedural dispute has emerged within the African Union (AU) after 20 member states objected to the handling of Senegal’s former president Macky Sall’s proposed candidacy for UN Secretary-General. The controversy centers on whether AU Chairperson É
body_en:
Addis Ababa, March 30, 2026 - A procedural dispute has emerged within the African Union (AU) after 20 member states objected to the handling of Senegal’s former president Macky Sall’s proposed candidacy for UN Secretary-General.
The controversy centers on whether AU Chairperson Évariste Ndayishimiye followed established rules when forwarding the nomination process.
Several countries reportedly argued that the procedure bypassed required AU mechanisms, including review by a ministerial committee responsible for vetting candidates for international positions.
Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Olivier Nduhungirehe, stated that AU rules require nominations to pass through structured approval stages before being transmitted to the United Nations.
He said any direct submission without full committee validation would constitute a breach of established AU procedures.
The AU framework, developed from earlier OAU resolutions and later revised in 2006, outlines a multi-step process involving member states, ministerial review, and approval by the Council of Ministers.
Diplomatic observers say the disagreement highlights broader tensions over decision-making authority within the AU and the interpretation of its internal governance rules.
No official response has yet been issued by the AU Commission regarding the procedural concerns.
body_fr:
Addis-Abeba, le 30 mars 2026 – Un différend procédural est apparu au sein de l’Union africaine (UA) après que 20 États membres se sont opposés à la gestion de la candidature proposée par l’ancien président sénégalais Macky Sall au poste de secrétaire général de l’ONU.
La controverse porte sur la question de savoir si le président de l'UA, Évariste Ndayishimiye, a suivi les règles établies lors de la transmission du processus de nomination.
Plusieurs pays auraient fait valoir que la procédure contournait les mécanismes requis par l’UA, notamment l’examen par un comité ministériel chargé de sélectionner les candidats aux postes internationaux.
Le ministre rwandais des Affaires étrangères, Olivier Nduhungirehe, a déclaré que les règles de l’UA exigent que les candidatures passent par des étapes d’approbation structurées avant d’être transmises aux Nations Unies.
Il a déclaré que toute soumission directe sans la validation complète du comité constituerait une violation des procédures établies de l'UA.
Le cadre de l'UA, élaboré à partir de résolutions antérieures de l'OUA puis révisé en 2006, décrit un processus en plusieurs étapes impliquant les États membres, un examen ministériel et une approbation par le Conseil des ministres.
Les observateurs diplomatiques affirment que ce désaccord met en évidence des tensions plus larges sur le pouvoir décisionnel au sein de l’UA et l’interprétation de ses règles de gouvernance interne.
Aucune réponse officielle n'a encore été publiée par la Commission de l'UA concernant les problèmes de procédure.

title: La RDC et l’Angola font pression pour une intégration économique plus approfondie au forum de Kinshasa
excerpt: Kinshasa, le 1er avril 2026 - La troisième édition du Forum économique République démocratique du Congo-Angola s'est ouverte à Kinshasa avec des appels à des engagements concrets pour accélérer le commerce transfrontalier et renforcer l'intégration économique régionale. Organisé sous le thème « Intégration sous-régionale
title_en: DRC and Angola push for deeper economic integration at Kinshasa forum
excerpt_en: Kinshasa April 1, 2026 - The third edition of the Democratic Republic of Congo-Angola Economic Forum opened in Kinshasa with calls for concrete commitments to accelerate cross-border trade and strengthen regional economic integration. Held under the theme “Sub-regional Integratio
body_en:
Kinshasa April 1, 2026 - The third edition of the Democratic Republic of Congo-Angola Economic Forum opened in Kinshasa with calls for concrete commitments to accelerate cross-border trade and strengthen regional economic integration.
Held under the theme “Sub-regional Integration and the Development of Cross-Border Trade,” the forum brought together government officials, private sector leaders, and economic experts from both countries to build on earlier editions held in Kinshasa and Luanda in 2023.
Opening the discussions, Deputy Prime Minister and Economy Minister Daniel Mukoko Samba stressed the importance of aligning bilateral cooperation with the broader objectives of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), which seeks to boost trade across the continent.
He outlined three key priorities for the discussions: reducing informal cross-border trade, improving payment systems between the two countries, and promoting joint infrastructure and industrial projects to support long-term economic cooperation.
Officials from both sides expressed expectations for tangible outcomes, including new investments, joint ventures, and sectoral agreements in strategic areas such as energy, hydrocarbons, fisheries, and cross-border electricity supply.
Government representatives emphasized that while states are responsible for creating a conducive regulatory environment, the private sector plays a central role in driving investment, innovation, and job creation.
The forum is expected to serve as a platform for strengthening economic ties between Kinshasa and Luanda, while advancing broader regional integration objectives across Central and Southern Africa.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, le 1er avril 2026 - La troisième édition du Forum économique République démocratique du Congo-Angola s'est ouverte à Kinshasa avec des appels à des engagements concrets pour accélérer le commerce transfrontalier et renforcer l'intégration économique régionale.
Organisé sous le thème « Intégration sous-régionale et développement du commerce transfrontalier », le forum a réuni des responsables gouvernementaux, des dirigeants du secteur privé et des experts économiques des deux pays pour s'appuyer sur les éditions précédentes tenues à Kinshasa et Luanda en 2023.
Ouvrant les discussions, le vice-Premier ministre et ministre de l'Économie Daniel Mukoko Samba a souligné l'importance d'aligner la coopération bilatérale sur les objectifs plus larges de la Zone de libre-échange continentale africaine (ZLECAf), qui vise à stimuler le commerce à travers le continent.
Il a souligné trois priorités clés pour les discussions : réduire le commerce transfrontalier informel, améliorer les systèmes de paiement entre les deux pays et promouvoir des projets d'infrastructures et industriels communs pour soutenir la coopération économique à long terme.
Les responsables des deux côtés ont exprimé leurs attentes de résultats tangibles, notamment de nouveaux investissements, des coentreprises et des accords sectoriels dans des domaines stratégiques tels que l'énergie, les hydrocarbures, la pêche et l'approvisionnement transfrontalier en électricité.
Les représentants gouvernementaux ont souligné que même si les États sont responsables de la création d’un environnement réglementaire favorable, le secteur privé joue un rôle central dans la stimulation des investissements, de l’innovation et de la création d’emplois.
Le forum devrait servir de plate-forme pour renforcer les liens économiques entre Kinshasa et Luanda, tout en faisant progresser les objectifs plus larges d'intégration régionale en Afrique centrale et australe.

title_en: Rwanda’s tech minister outlines five steps for East Africa to accelerate AI development
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda, March 30, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of ICT and Innovation, Paula Ingabire, has called on member states of the East African Community (EAC) to adopt a coordinated approach to advancing Artificial Intelligence (AI) across the region. Speaking at a regional conference
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda, March 30, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of ICT and Innovation, Paula Ingabire, has called on member states of the East African Community (EAC) to adopt a coordinated approach to advancing Artificial Intelligence (AI) across the region.
Speaking at a regional conference in Kigali, she outlined five key priorities: establishing AI governance laws, creating a regional research and innovation center, developing shared data infrastructure, harmonizing regulations, and investing in large-scale skills training.
Ingabire emphasized that AI could significantly boost economic growth, citing projections that the technology could contribute up to $1 trillion to Africa’s GDP by 2035.
She also highlighted the need to increase African language content online, noting that less than 3% of global internet content is currently available in African languages.
Officials say the initiative aims to position East Africa as a competitive player in the global digital economy while ensuring inclusive access to emerging technologies.
body_fr:
Kigali, Rwanda, 30 mars 2026 - La ministre rwandaise des TIC et de l'innovation, Paula Ingabire, a appelé les États membres de la Communauté d'Afrique de l'Est (EAC) à adopter une approche coordonnée pour faire progresser l'intelligence artificielle (IA) dans la région.
S'exprimant lors d'une conférence régionale à Kigali, elle a souligné cinq priorités clés : établir des lois sur la gouvernance de l'IA, créer un centre régional de recherche et d'innovation, développer une infrastructure de données partagée, harmoniser les réglementations et investir dans la formation professionnelle à grande échelle.
Ingabire a souligné que l’IA pourrait stimuler considérablement la croissance économique, citant des projections selon lesquelles cette technologie pourrait contribuer jusqu’à 1 000 milliards de dollars au PIB de l’Afrique d’ici 2035.
Elle a également souligné la nécessité d'augmenter le contenu en ligne en langues africaines, notant que moins de 3 % du contenu Internet mondial est actuellement disponible dans les langues africaines.
Les responsables affirment que l'initiative vise à positionner l'Afrique de l'Est en tant qu'acteur compétitif dans l'économie numérique mondiale tout en garantissant un accès inclusif aux technologies émergentes.

body_en:
Guadalajara April 1, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has qualified for the 2026 FIFA World Cup for the first time in 52 years, prompting the government to declare Wednesday, April 1, a paid public holiday nationwide.
The decision, announced by the Ministry of Employment and Labour, aims to allow citizens to celebrate what officials described as a moment of national unity and pride following a landmark sporting achievement.
According to the ministry, the measure applies across the entire national territory and gives workers a paid day off in recognition of the national team’s success.
The qualification was secured after the national team, known as the Leopards, defeated Jamaica’s Reggae Boyz 1-0 after extra time in the final of the intercontinental playoffs held in Guadalajara, Mexico.
The victory marks a return to football’s biggest stage for the DRC after more than five decades of absence, with the team becoming one of the African representatives at the 2026 World Cup.
Under coach Sébastien Desabre, the Leopards delivered a tightly contested performance, managing to break through in extra time after a disciplined defensive display and sustained pressure from their opponents.
The result has sparked nationwide celebrations, with authorities and supporters hailing the achievement as a historic milestone for Congolese football and a moment of collective national pride.

title: AFC/M23 Withdrawal Reported From Several Localities in North Kivu’s Walikale Territory
excerpt: WALIKALE, North Kivu March 27, 2026 - Movements attributed to AFC/M23 elements were observed on March 26 in several localities of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, including Minjenje and Mpety in the Kisimba group, as well as Kanune in the Ikobo group, according to local admi
title_en: AFC/M23 Withdrawal Reported From Several Localities in North Kivu’s Walikale Territory
excerpt_en: WALIKALE, North Kivu March 27, 2026 - Movements attributed to AFC/M23 elements were observed on March 26 in several localities of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, including Minjenje and Mpety in the Kisimba group, as well as Kanune in the Ikobo group, according to local admi
body_en:
WALIKALE, North Kivu March 27, 2026 - Movements attributed to AFC/M23 elements were observed on March 26 in several localities of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, including Minjenje and Mpety in the Kisimba group, as well as Kanune in the Ikobo group, according to local administrative and security sources.
Witnesses reported the departure of armed fighters from Minjenje and Mpety, with personnel and equipment seen moving through the Banakindi area. In Kalembe, a key transit point, residents observed convoys of fighters traveling both by vehicle and on foot, raising further confirmation of a coordinated pullback.
Security sources also indicated that similar movements took place in Kanune, where armed elements reportedly left the area in the early afternoon, heading toward Miriki in neighboring Lubero territory. Residual presence, however, was still reported in parts of the affected zones.
No official communication has been issued by AFC/M23 leadership regarding the reported withdrawals. The movements come days after a meeting of the group’s officers in Minjenje along the Kalembe-Mpety axis, according to local accounts.
On the ground, interpretations remain divided. Some observers describe the movements as a tactical repositioning, while others among the civilian population suspect a maneuver aimed at avoiding security pressure or reshaping frontlines.
The developments occur against a fragile security backdrop in Walikale, where recent clashes between AFC/M23 elements and Wazalendo fighters have triggered population displacement toward safer areas, including Miriki. Many residents remain cautious, awaiting clearer signs of stability and the possibility of safe returns for displaced communities.

title_en: A Nurse and Red Cross Volunteer Arrested and Injured in Kalembe by Armed Fighters
excerpt_en: Kalembe, Masisi, North Kivu March 31, 2026 - A nurse and a Red Cross volunteer were arrested and injured on Monday, March 30, in Kalembe, in the Mweso health zone of Masisi Territory in North Kivu Province, after being targeted by armed AFC/M23 fighters. The incident occurred at
body_en:
Kalembe, Masisi, North Kivu March 31, 2026 - A nurse and a Red Cross volunteer were arrested and injured on Monday, March 30, in Kalembe, in the Mweso health zone of Masisi Territory in North Kivu Province, after being targeted by armed AFC/M23 fighters.
The incident occurred at the Kalembe health center, where the head nurse, identified as Kapita Lucien, was reportedly beaten and shot in the hand during the attack. The local Red Cross coordinator, Byamungu Mauwa Samson, was also physically assaulted before both men were taken away on motorcycles to an unknown destination.
The two humanitarian workers are alleged to have been accused-without evidence-of having links to AFC/M23.
Their abduction has raised alarm among local residents, who fear for their safety and are calling for urgent intervention by humanitarian organizations, including the International Committee of the Red Cross and Médecins Sans Frontières, to secure their release.
The incident has heightened concerns over the protection of medical and humanitarian personnel operating in conflict-affected areas of Masisi Territory, where insecurity remains widespread and access to health services is already severely constrained.
No official response has yet been issued by AFC/M23 regarding the incident.

title: Djibouti, Ethiopia and Somalia reinforce cooperation on maritime security and migration
excerpt: Djibouti City, Djibouti, end of March 2026 — Djibouti, Ethiopia, and Somalia have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening regional cooperation on maritime security and the management of migration flows. The announcement follows recent tripartite discussions focused on improv
title_en: Djibouti, Ethiopia and Somalia reinforce cooperation on maritime security and migration
excerpt_en: Djibouti City, Djibouti, end of March 2026 — Djibouti, Ethiopia, and Somalia have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening regional cooperation on maritime security and the management of migration flows. The announcement follows recent tripartite discussions focused on improv
body_en:
Djibouti City, Djibouti, end of March 2026 — Djibouti, Ethiopia, and Somalia have reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening regional cooperation on maritime security and the management of migration flows.
The announcement follows recent tripartite discussions focused on improving coordination in the Red Sea and Gulf of Aden, particularly in response to rising migration risks and maritime safety concerns.
Officials from the three countries emphasized their shared interest in promoting regional stability and addressing irregular migration challenges through joint efforts.
Conclusion
Djibouti enters April 2026 at a decisive moment, shaped mainly by the April 10 presidential election, where final preparations are complete and voter participation is expected to be strong.
At the same time, the country is pursuing economic diversification, with major investments in infrastructure, housing, mining, and new partnerships with international financial institutions.
However, humanitarian and security challenges remain, especially migration risks in the Red Sea, recurring shipwrecks off Obock, and ongoing regional tensions that require continued vigilance.
Overall, Djibouti is balancing electoral stability, economic reform, and regional pressures, with the coming election seen as a key moment for its political and economic trajectory in 2026.
By Kader K.
Jeff Buleli

title: Rwanda’s Education Ministry moves to strengthen counseling support after student suicide cases
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda, March 27, 2026 - The Ministry of Education (MINEDUC) says it is working on introducing enhanced psychological counseling services in schools following recent cases of student deaths suspected to be linked to suicide. The announcement comes after the death of a stu
title_en: Rwanda’s Education Ministry moves to strengthen counseling support after student suicide cases
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda, March 27, 2026 - The Ministry of Education (MINEDUC) says it is working on introducing enhanced psychological counseling services in schools following recent cases of student deaths suspected to be linked to suicide. The announcement comes after the death of a stu
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda, March 27, 2026 - The Ministry of Education (MINEDUC) says it is working on introducing enhanced psychological counseling services in schools following recent cases of student deaths suspected to be linked to suicide.
The announcement comes after the death of a student at RP Tumba College of Vocational Education in Rulindo District on March 24, 2026. Authorities are investigating circumstances surrounding the incident, which also involved the death of a visiting student.
Education Minister Joseph Nsengimana said the government is considering new measures to strengthen mental health and psychosocial support systems within schools and higher learning institutions.
He noted that the initiative aims to complement existing student support programs, particularly for learners in secondary schools and public higher education institutions, where government assistance is already provided.
The minister emphasized that early identification of psychological distress among students is a key priority, adding that counseling services could play a critical role in prevention efforts.
He also urged parents and guardians to remain actively involved in the lives of their children, stressing that education is a shared responsibility between schools and families.
Authorities continue to investigate the recent incident, with findings expected to clarify the circumstances surrounding the deaths.
According to national health data, hundreds of suicide attempts are recorded annually in Rwanda, with young people aged 19 to 35 representing the largest proportion of cases. Officials say the figures highlight the need for stronger mental health awareness and intervention strategies in schools and communities.

Rusizi District, Rwanda, March 26, 2026 - Rwanda has received 222 citizens who were previously held in areas of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo under the control of the FDLR armed group.
The returnees, including 149 children, 58 women, and 15 men, crossed into Rwanda through the La Corniche border post, which connects Rwanda and the DRC.
Upon arrival, they were transported to the Nyarushishi transit camp in Rusizi District, where they will undergo temporary reception and support procedures before reintegration into their communities.
Officials said the group had been living in a temporary camp in Goma after leaving various locations in eastern DRC where they had reportedly been under the influence or control of the FDLR.
Local authorities welcomed the returnees, urging them to actively participate in rebuilding their lives and contributing to national development.
The Deputy Mayor of Rubavu District in charge of economic development Nzabonimpa Déogratias encouraged them to reunite with their families, resume education for children, and access available social and health services.
He emphasized that reintegration support includes financial assistance and basic supplies intended to help returnees restart their lives, with adults receiving 188 USD, minors receiving 113 USD, and each individual provided with food assistance valued at 45,000 Rwandan francs.
Authorities stated that the return process is part of ongoing efforts to assist nationals coming back from conflict-affected areas and to facilitate their reintegration into normal civilian life.
