title: Over 130 Rwandans return home from DRC after years held by armed group
excerpt: Rusizi, Rwanda, April 2, 2026 - A total of 133 Rwandans have returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo after years of displacement and alleged captivity under the FDLR armed group. The group crossed into Rwanda through the Grande Barrière border post and was received by auth
title_en: Over 130 Rwandans return home from DRC after years held by armed group
excerpt_en: Rusizi, Rwanda, April 2, 2026 - A total of 133 Rwandans have returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo after years of displacement and alleged captivity under the FDLR armed group. The group crossed into Rwanda through the Grande Barrière border post and was received by auth
body_en:
Rusizi, Rwanda, April 2, 2026 - A total of 133 Rwandans have returned from the Democratic Republic of Congo after years of displacement and alleged captivity under the FDLR armed group.
The group crossed into Rwanda through the Grande Barrière border post and was received by authorities before being transferred to the Nyarushishi transit center in Rusizi District for reintegration support.
Among the returnees were women, men, and children, many of whom say they had been influenced by fear-based messages warning them not to return to Rwanda.
One returnee, Nyirakaromba, said they were told they would be killed if they went back to Rwanda, but later learned from others who had returned that conditions were safe and peaceful.
Others described difficult living conditions in eastern DRC, including forced labor, insecurity, and exploitation by armed groups.
The return operation was coordinated under agreements involving Rwanda, the Democratic Republic of Congo, and the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), reached during a meeting in Addis Ababa in 2025.
Local authorities in Rubavu District welcomed the returnees and encouraged them to reintegrate into their communities, resume normal life, and ensure children return to school.
The government also provided reintegration assistance, including cash support and basic supplies to help families restart their lives.

title_en: DRC and Brazil sign agreement on employment for dependents of diplomatic staff
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 31, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and Brazil have signed a bilateral agreement allowing dependents of diplomatic mission staff to engage in paid employment, marking a new step in strengthening ties between the two countries. The agreement was concluded du
body_en:
Kinshasa March 31, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo and Brazil have signed a bilateral agreement allowing dependents of diplomatic mission staff to engage in paid employment, marking a new step in strengthening ties between the two countries.
The agreement was concluded during the official visit to Kinshasa by Brazilian Foreign Minister Mauro Vieira from March 29 to 30, as part of broader efforts to deepen cooperation and reinforce longstanding diplomatic relations.
According to Congolese authorities, the deal applies to dependents of staff serving in diplomatic missions, consular posts, and permanent representations, facilitating their access to local labor markets under defined legal frameworks.
Officials from both countries described the agreement as progress in legal and social cooperation, while reaffirming their shared commitment to expanding collaboration across multiple sectors.
Discussions between the two sides identified key areas of priority, including agriculture, infrastructure, defense, education, mining, culture, research, and economic development. Both governments also expressed their intention to boost trade and encourage investment flows.
The visit builds on previous engagements, notably multisectoral consultations held in Brasília and a Congolese diplomatic mission in August 2025.
As part of this ongoing partnership, the second session of the DRC-Brazil multisectoral consultations is scheduled to take place in Kinshasa in 2027.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, le 31 mars 2026 - La République démocratique du Congo et le Brésil ont signé un accord bilatéral permettant aux personnes à la charge du personnel des missions diplomatiques d'exercer un emploi rémunéré, marquant une nouvelle étape dans le renforcement des liens entre les deux pays.
L'accord a été conclu lors de la visite officielle à Kinshasa du ministre brésilien des Affaires étrangères Mauro Vieira les 29 et 30 mars, dans le cadre d'efforts plus larges visant à approfondir la coopération et à renforcer les relations diplomatiques de longue date.
Selon les autorités congolaises, l'accord s'applique aux personnes à charge du personnel des missions diplomatiques, des postes consulaires et des représentations permanentes, facilitant ainsi leur accès aux marchés du travail locaux dans des cadres juridiques définis.
Les responsables des deux pays ont décrit l'accord comme un progrès dans la coopération juridique et sociale, tout en réaffirmant leur engagement commun à élargir la collaboration dans de multiples secteurs.
Les discussions entre les deux parties ont identifié des domaines prioritaires clés, notamment l'agriculture, les infrastructures, la défense, l'éducation, l'exploitation minière, la culture, la recherche et le développement économique. Les deux gouvernements ont également exprimé leur intention de stimuler les échanges commerciaux et d'encourager les flux d'investissement.
La visite s'appuie sur des engagements antérieurs, notamment des consultations multisectorielles tenues à Brasilia et une mission diplomatique congolaise en août 2025.
Dans le cadre de ce partenariat en cours, la deuxième session des consultations multisectorielles RDC-Brésil devrait avoir lieu à Kinshasa en 2027.

title_en: Rwandan minister warns of inherited genocide ideology among youth
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda, March 29, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of National Unity and Civic Engagement, Jean Damascène Bizimana, has raised concerns over the persistence of genocide ideology among some youth, attributing it in part to narratives passed down by parents. Speaking at a public ev
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda, March 29, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of National Unity and Civic Engagement, Jean Damascène Bizimana, has raised concerns over the persistence of genocide ideology among some youth, attributing it in part to narratives passed down by parents.
Speaking at a public event in Kigali, the minister said some young people expressing hostility toward the country and its leadership are influenced by misinformation within their families, particularly from individuals linked to the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi.
He warned that false accounts and denial narratives are being transmitted across generations, sometimes amplified through social media, undermining national unity and reconciliation efforts.
Bizimana emphasized that individuals who have served sentences for genocide-related crimes have a responsibility to tell the truth to their children and contribute positively to rebuilding society.
Recent studies cited by officials indicate that a portion of the population believes some former convicts continue to hold divisive views, while social media platforms abroad are also seen as contributing to the spread of harmful narratives.
Authorities say continued civic education and awareness efforts remain essential to strengthening unity and preventing the transmission of extremist ideologies.
body_fr:
Kigali, Rwanda, 29 mars 2026 - Le Ministre rwandais de l'Unité nationale et de l'Engagement civique, Jean Damascène Bizimana, a fait part de ses inquiétudes quant à la persistance de l'idéologie du génocide chez certains jeunes, l'attribuant en partie aux récits transmis par les parents.
S'exprimant lors d'un événement public à Kigali, le ministre a déclaré que certains jeunes exprimant leur hostilité envers le pays et ses dirigeants sont influencés par la désinformation au sein de leurs familles, en particulier de la part d'individus liés au génocide perpétré contre les Tutsi en 1994.
Il a averti que les fausses informations et les récits de déni se transmettent d’une génération à l’autre, parfois amplifiés par les médias sociaux, sapant ainsi l’unité nationale et les efforts de réconciliation.
Bizimana a souligné que les personnes qui ont purgé des peines pour des crimes liés au génocide ont la responsabilité de dire la vérité à leurs enfants et de contribuer positivement à la reconstruction de la société.
Des études récentes citées par les responsables indiquent qu'une partie de la population pense que certains anciens détenus continuent d'avoir des opinions controversées, tandis que les plateformes de médias sociaux à l'étranger sont également considérées comme contribuant à la propagation de discours préjudiciables.
Les autorités affirment que la poursuite des efforts d’éducation civique et de sensibilisation reste essentielle pour renforcer l’unité et prévenir la transmission des idéologies extrémistes.

title_en: DRC signs $100 million telecom infrastructure deal with Helios Towers to expand national connectivity
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 31, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has signed an investment agreement worth more than 100 million US dollars aimed at expanding telecommunications infrastructure across several provinces. The agreement was concluded between the National Agency for Investme
body_en:
Kinshasa March 31, 2026 - The Democratic Republic of Congo has signed an investment agreement worth more than 100 million US dollars aimed at expanding telecommunications infrastructure across several provinces.
The agreement was concluded between the National Agency for Investment Promotion (ANAPI) and Helios Towers DRC, a company specializing in the construction and management of shared telecommunications infrastructure.
The project is intended to support the government’s broader digital transformation agenda, aligned with the National Digital and Inclusion Plan 2025 and the “DRC Digital 2030” strategy, which seeks to position the country as a regional digital hub in Central Africa.
According to Helios Towers DRC management, the investment will focus on the expansion of mobile network infrastructure, including the installation of telecommunications towers in both urban and rural areas to improve coverage and service quality.
The company reported that more than 4,000 jobs have already been created through its operations in the country, with expectations of additional employment opportunities as infrastructure deployment expands.
Officials from ANAPI described the agreement as a signal of growing investor confidence in the Democratic Republic of Congo, attributing it to ongoing reforms aimed at improving the business environment and strengthening economic governance.
The initiative is expected to contribute to national development priorities, particularly in improving digital access, fostering economic inclusion, and supporting the structural transformation of the economy through expanded connectivity.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, le 31 mars 2026 - La République démocratique du Congo a signé un accord d'investissement d'une valeur de plus de 100 millions de dollars américains visant à développer les infrastructures de télécommunications dans plusieurs provinces.
L'accord a été conclu entre l'Agence nationale de promotion des investissements (ANAPI) et Helios Towers DRC, une entreprise spécialisée dans la construction et la gestion d'infrastructures de télécommunications partagées.
Le projet vise à soutenir le programme plus large de transformation numérique du gouvernement, aligné sur le Plan National Numérique et Inclusion 2025 et la stratégie « RDC Numérique 2030 », qui vise à positionner le pays comme un hub numérique régional en Afrique Centrale.
Selon la direction d'Helios Towers RDC, l'investissement se concentrera sur l'expansion de l'infrastructure du réseau mobile, y compris l'installation de tours de télécommunications dans les zones urbaines et rurales pour améliorer la couverture et la qualité du service.
L'entreprise a indiqué que plus de 4 000 emplois ont déjà été créés grâce à ses opérations dans le pays, et qu'elle s'attend à des opportunités d'emploi supplémentaires à mesure que le déploiement des infrastructures se développe.
Les responsables de l'ANAPI ont décrit l'accord comme un signal de la confiance croissante des investisseurs dans la République démocratique du Congo, l'attribuant aux réformes en cours visant à améliorer l'environnement des affaires et à renforcer la gouvernance économique.
L'initiative devrait contribuer aux priorités de développement nationales, notamment en améliorant l'accès numérique, en favorisant l'inclusion économique et en soutenant la transformation structurelle de l'économie grâce à une connectivité élargie.

La plateforme Numida permet aux utilisateurs de postuler pour un bus
title_en: Digital lending platform Numida launches in Rwanda to expand access to business loans
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda, March 25, 2026 - A technology-driven lending company has officially launched operations in Rwanda, offering quick, collateral-free loans to small business owners in a move aimed at improving financial inclusion. The platform, Numida, enables users to apply for bus
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda, March 25, 2026 - A technology-driven lending company has officially launched operations in Rwanda, offering quick, collateral-free loans to small business owners in a move aimed at improving financial inclusion.
The platform, Numida, enables users to apply for business loans via a mobile application, with approvals and disbursements made within 24 hours. Loan amounts range from 800,000 Rwandan francs to 12 million francs, with repayment periods of up to 30 days.
The launch event took place in Kigali on March 24, 2026, and marks the company’s formal entry into the Rwandan financial market.
To access the service, applicants are required to have a smartphone, a national ID, a passport photo, and a legally registered business operating in Rwanda for at least six months, along with documentation from the Rwanda Development Board.
Numida Chief Executive Officer Mina Shahid said the platform is designed to support small businesses and aligns with Rwanda’s long-term development goals under Vision 2050, which aims to broaden access to financial services and drive economic growth.
Officials from the Central Bank of Rwanda (BNR) confirmed that the company has received the necessary authorization to operate as a non-deposit-taking lending institution, emphasizing that it meets regulatory requirements.
A representative from the BNR noted that expanding access to credit is part of the country’s strategy to support entrepreneurship and business development.
Early beneficiaries have already reported positive experiences, with small business owners stating that the platform provides faster and easier access to funding compared to traditional financial institutions.
Since beginning operations in Rwanda, Numida has reportedly disbursed around 120 million Rwandan francs in loans to approximately 150 entrepreneurs.
The company already operates in Uganda and Kenya and has facilitated over 150 million dollars in loans across the region, supporting thousands of small businesses. It aims to expand its reach further in Rwanda throughout 2026.
body_fr:
Kigali, Rwanda, le 25 mars 2026 - Une société de prêt axée sur la technologie a officiellement lancé ses opérations au Rwanda, offrant des prêts rapides et sans garantie aux propriétaires de petites entreprises dans le but d'améliorer l'inclusion financière.
La plateforme, Numida, permet aux utilisateurs de demander des prêts commerciaux via une application mobile, avec des approbations et des décaissements effectués dans les 24 heures. Les montants des prêts varient de 800 000 francs rwandais à 12 millions de francs, avec des délais de remboursement allant jusqu'à 30 jours.
L’événement de lancement a eu lieu à Kigali le 24 mars 2026 et marque l’entrée officielle de la société sur le marché financier rwandais.
Pour accéder au service, les candidats doivent disposer d'un smartphone, d'une pièce d'identité nationale, d'une photo d'identité et d'une entreprise légalement enregistrée opérant au Rwanda depuis au moins six mois, ainsi que de la documentation du Rwanda Development Board.
Mina Shahid, directrice générale de Numida, a déclaré que la plateforme est conçue pour soutenir les petites entreprises et s'aligne sur les objectifs de développement à long terme du Rwanda dans le cadre de la Vision 2050, qui vise à élargir l'accès aux services financiers et à stimuler la croissance économique.
Les responsables de la Banque centrale du Rwanda (BNR) ont confirmé que la société a reçu l'autorisation nécessaire pour fonctionner en tant qu'institution de prêt sans dépôt, soulignant qu'elle répond aux exigences réglementaires.
Un représentant de la BNR a souligné que l’élargissement de l’accès au crédit fait partie de la stratégie du pays visant à soutenir l’entrepreneuriat et le développement des entreprises.
Les premiers bénéficiaires ont déjà fait état d'expériences positives, les propriétaires de petites entreprises affirmant que la plateforme offre un accès plus rapide et plus facile au financement par rapport aux institutions financières traditionnelles.
Depuis le début de ses opérations au Rwanda, Numida aurait accordé environ 120 millions de francs rwandais sous forme de prêts à environ 150 entrepreneurs.
La société opère déjà en Ouganda et au Kenya et a facilité plus de 150 millions de dollars de prêts dans toute la région, soutenant ainsi des milliers de petites entreprises. Il vise à étendre davantage sa portée au Rwanda tout au long de 2026.

title: DRC NGO highlights rural women’s role in forest conservation during closing of Women’s Month
excerpt: Kinshasa March 31, 2026 - The NGO National Alliance for Support and Promotion of Indigenous and Community Heritage Areas and Territories in the Democratic Republic of Congo (ANAPAC DRC) has emphasized the central role of rural women in forest conservation and local development as
title_en: DRC NGO highlights rural women’s role in forest conservation during closing of Women’s Month
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 31, 2026 - The NGO National Alliance for Support and Promotion of Indigenous and Community Heritage Areas and Territories in the Democratic Republic of Congo (ANAPAC DRC) has emphasized the central role of rural women in forest conservation and local development as
body_en:
Kinshasa March 31, 2026 - The NGO National Alliance for Support and Promotion of Indigenous and Community Heritage Areas and Territories in the Democratic Republic of Congo (ANAPAC DRC) has emphasized the central role of rural women in forest conservation and local development as part of activities marking the closing of Women’s Month.
The event, held in Kinshasa alongside celebrations linked to the International Day of Forests, highlighted women’s contribution to agriculture, forest product processing, and the supply of urban markets in a country where forests remain a key pillar of economic and social life.
According to ANAPAC DRC, its Inclusive Conservation Initiative (ICI) project has supported Indigenous and local women across several provinces through income-generating activities and financial assistance aimed at strengthening both livelihoods and environmental stewardship.
Project representatives reported that women’s committees established under the initiative have received grants ranging between 5,000 and 10,000 US dollars, alongside agricultural tools and processing equipment designed to reduce workload and improve productivity in rural communities.
Officials involved in the program said the initiative has contributed not only to income growth but also to social empowerment, citing increased participation of women in public meetings and community decision-making processes. Participation levels were reported to have risen significantly, with women now taking a more active role in local development discussions.
The project, implemented across multiple biocultural landscapes, supports activities such as cassava, maize, rice, peanut, bean cultivation, livestock farming, and fish farming, with the goal of strengthening economic autonomy while promoting sustainable resource management.
Speaking during the event, representatives of ANAPAC DRC stressed that conservation efforts cannot succeed without integrating local communities, particularly women, who play a major role in managing forest-based livelihoods.
They also called on public authorities to take greater ownership of such initiatives to ensure long-term sustainability beyond external funding cycles, especially in areas where rural women face limited access to processing infrastructure and markets.
The organization further underscored the importance of continued support for Indigenous and local women, noting that strengthening their economic resilience is closely linked to environmental protection and biodiversity conservation in the country.

title: Washington Calls for Immediate Withdrawal of Rwandan Forces From Eastern DRC, Imposes Sanctions
excerpt: NEW YORK / WASHINGTON, March 26, 2026 - The United States has called for the immediate withdrawal of Rwandan troops from eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, while announcing targeted sanctions against senior Rwandan military officials, during a briefing to the United Nations Se
title_en: Washington Calls for Immediate Withdrawal of Rwandan Forces From Eastern DRC, Imposes Sanctions
excerpt_en: NEW YORK / WASHINGTON, March 26, 2026 - The United States has called for the immediate withdrawal of Rwandan troops from eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, while announcing targeted sanctions against senior Rwandan military officials, during a briefing to the United Nations Se
body_en:
NEW YORK / WASHINGTON, March 26, 2026 - The United States has called for the immediate withdrawal of Rwandan troops from eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, while announcing targeted sanctions against senior Rwandan military officials, during a briefing to the United Nations Security Council on March 26.
Speaking on behalf of the U.S. administration, Senior Advisor for African Affairs Massad Boulos expressed “deep disappointment” over what Washington described as a recent escalation by Rwanda in eastern DRC, calling it a “direct violation” of commitments made under the Washington peace framework.
The U.S. referred to the implementation of the Washington agreements (December 4, 2025), noting that while some progress had been achieved, recent developments threatened to undermine the fragile process.
According to the U.S. statement, sanctions have been imposed on members of the Rwandan Defence Forces (RDF), including four senior generals, in response to their alleged role in destabilizing activities in eastern Congo.
Washington reiterated its demand for the “immediate withdrawal of Rwandan forces from Congolese territory,” alongside renewed calls for respect of DRC sovereignty and intensified efforts by Kinshasa to neutralize the FDLR armed group.
The U.S. envoy also stressed the importance of restoring state authority in the Kivu provinces and addressing the ongoing illegal exploitation of natural resources, which he said continues to fuel the conflict.
While acknowledging the roles of regional and international mediation efforts - including MONUSCO and Qatari and African-led initiatives - Washington emphasized that lasting peace would require strict adherence to ceasefire commitments and genuine political will from all parties.
The statement also referenced the killing of a French humanitarian worker during a March 11 attack in Goma, extending condolences and underscoring concerns over civilian safety in the conflict zone.

title: AFC/M23 Seizes Control of Humura and Mukohwa After Heavy Fighting
excerpt: Masisi, North Kivu March 30, 2026 - The towns of Humura and Mukohwa, located in the Nyamaboko 1 group in Masisi Territory in North Kivu Province, came under the control of AFC/M23 fighters on Sunday, March 29, following intense clashes with the Armed Forces of the Democratic Repu
title_en: AFC/M23 Seizes Control of Humura and Mukohwa After Heavy Fighting
excerpt_en: Masisi, North Kivu March 30, 2026 - The towns of Humura and Mukohwa, located in the Nyamaboko 1 group in Masisi Territory in North Kivu Province, came under the control of AFC/M23 fighters on Sunday, March 29, following intense clashes with the Armed Forces of the Democratic Repu
body_en:
Masisi, North Kivu March 30, 2026 - The towns of Humura and Mukohwa, located in the Nyamaboko 1 group in Masisi Territory in North Kivu Province, came under the control of AFC/M23 fighters on Sunday, March 29, following intense clashes with the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and allied Wazalendo groups.
Fighting reportedly lasted throughout the day, with heavy exchanges forcing pro-government forces to withdraw and leave the two localities in rebel hands.
The advance is seen as part of a broader shift in control across parts of Masisi, increasing concerns over the security of surrounding areas and key positions.
Local sources indicate that the fall of nearby positions has also put the strategic area of Rutoboko under pressure, particularly due to its role as a logistical hub for government forces. The site is known for its use in military supply operations, including helicopter landings supporting frontline deployments.
A fragile calm was reported on Monday in Humura and Mukohwa, although the situation remains tense, with fears of renewed fighting.
The latest developments come amid ongoing instability in Masisi Territory, where control frequently shifts between FARDC, Wazalendo allies, and AFC/M23 forces. Civilians continue to bear the brunt of repeated clashes, facing displacement and worsening humanitarian conditions.

title: Minister Habimana says revised electoral law should not raise concerns
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda, March 26, 2026 - The Minister of Local Government Dominique Habimana has stated that the ongoing revision of the electoral law should not cause public concern, describing it instead as a reform aimed at improving the country’s local electoral system. He made the r
title_en: Minister Habimana says revised electoral law should not raise concerns
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda, March 26, 2026 - The Minister of Local Government Dominique Habimana has stated that the ongoing revision of the electoral law should not cause public concern, describing it instead as a reform aimed at improving the country’s local electoral system. He made the r
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda, March 26, 2026 - The Minister of Local Government Dominique Habimana has stated that the ongoing revision of the electoral law should not cause public concern, describing it instead as a reform aimed at improving the country’s local electoral system.
He made the remarks while appearing before the Chamber of Deputies, where lawmakers were examining the draft Organic Law on elections article by article.
The proposed changes include a shift in how district councilors are elected. Under the new framework, the eight general councilors at district level would be chosen indirectly by an electoral college composed of representatives elected from the cell level and representatives of different social categories at district level.
Officials explained that the reform is intended to streamline representation following the reduction of district council seats to eight, requiring an adjusted selection process.
Minister Habimana assured lawmakers that the changes remain within international legal standards and are consistent with Rwanda’s existing electoral practices.
The Chairperson of the National Electoral Commission Oda Gasinzigwa said the reforms are part of efforts to improve electoral processes and strengthen democratic participation.
She noted that the revised law is urgent, as it will be applied in local elections scheduled between October and November 2026, and urged Parliament to expedite its approval to allow adequate time for voter education.
The Executive Secretary of the National Electoral Commission Jean Claude Musabyimana added that the changes aim to broaden participation in the electoral college, ensuring stronger representation of citizens in decision-making structures.
Parliament’s Committee on Governance and Gender Equality confirmed that it will carefully review the draft law before forwarding it to the full Chamber of Deputies and subsequently to the Senate for further consideration.

title: Gen Muhoozi signals possible Uganda troop withdrawal from eastern DRC amid political conditions
excerpt: Kampala, Uganda, March 25, 2026 - Uganda’s Chief of Defence Forces Muhoozi Kainerugaba has announced that Ugandan troops deployed in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo could be withdrawn from several positions, depending on political developments in Ituri Province. Ugandan forc
title_en: Gen Muhoozi signals possible Uganda troop withdrawal from eastern DRC amid political conditions
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, March 25, 2026 - Uganda’s Chief of Defence Forces Muhoozi Kainerugaba has announced that Ugandan troops deployed in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo could be withdrawn from several positions, depending on political developments in Ituri Province. Ugandan forc
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, March 25, 2026 - Uganda’s Chief of Defence Forces Muhoozi Kainerugaba has announced that Ugandan troops deployed in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo could be withdrawn from several positions, depending on political developments in Ituri Province.
Ugandan forces are currently deployed in joint operations with the Armed Forces of the DRC to combat armed groups, including the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), which are linked to the Islamic State network.
Gen. Muhoozi said Uganda is prepared to withdraw troops from areas stretching from Lubero to Mahagi in coordination with the Congolese government, emphasizing the goal of achieving lasting stability in eastern DRC.
However, he stated that the withdrawal from Lubero would depend on whether changes are made to the leadership of Ituri Province, indicating that all Ugandan troops could leave the area if the current governor remains in office.
Eastern DRC continues to face complex insecurity, with more than 250 armed groups operating in the region, many of which are involved in violence against civilians, according to regional security assessments.
The announcement comes amid ongoing military cooperation between Uganda and the DRC, which has focused on joint operations against insurgent groups and improving security along shared border regions.

body_en:
Bujumbura, April 1, 2026 - Burundi’s President Évariste Ndayishimiye has confirmed that fatalities occurred following a weapons explosion at a military base in the Musaga area of Bujumbura.
In a statement shared on social media, President Ndayishimiye expressed condolences to families of those killed and wished a swift recovery to the injured.
He said the government remains confident in its capacity to defend national sovereignty despite the incident.
The explosion, which occurred on the night of March 31, reportedly affected an arms depot inside a military facility in the Musaga zone. Authorities have attributed the fire to an electrical fault.
However, security sources cited by AFP indicated that the incident may have resulted in more than 10 deaths, although official figures have not been fully confirmed.
The Burundian military and Ministry of Internal Security have launched further assessments to determine the exact cause and full extent of the damage.

title: Youssouf Ezangi extradé vers le Royaume-Uni pour purger une peine à perpétuité suite à la tentative de coup d'État de 2024 en RDC
excerpt: Kinshasa, le 2 avril 2026 - Le ressortissant britannique Youssouf Ezangi, ancien plombier originaire de la République démocratique du Congo, a été extradé vers le Royaume-Uni pour purger une peine d'emprisonnement à perpétuité pour son rôle dans la tentative de coup d'État de mai 2024 à Kinshasa.
title_en: Youssouf Ezangi extradited to the United Kingdom to serve life sentence over 2024 DRC coup attempt
excerpt_en: Kinshasa April 2, 2026 - British national Youssouf Ezangi, a former plumber originally from the Democratic Republic of Congo, has been extradited to the United Kingdom to serve a life sentence for his role in the May 2024 attempted coup in Kinshasa.
body_en:
Kinshasa April 2, 2026 - British national Youssouf Ezangi, a former plumber originally from the Democratic Republic of Congo, has been extradited to the United Kingdom to serve a life sentence for his role in the May 2024 attempted coup in Kinshasa.

Ezangi, 53 at the time of the events, was transferred from Ndolo Military Prison on March 31, 2026, under a judicial cooperation arrangement between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United Kingdom. His handover was carried out in the presence of diplomatic and military officials, including representatives of the British Embassy in Kinshasa.

He had been convicted by military courts for armed violence and terrorism-related offences linked to the failed coup attempt led by Christian Malanga on May 19, 2024. Initially sentenced to death, his punishment was later commuted to life imprisonment following a presidential pardon.

According to judicial proceedings, Ezangi was part of a group that entered key state locations in Kinshasa, including the residence of senior officials and the Palais de la Nation, during the short-lived assault on state institutions.

The extradition was formally approved as part of bilateral legal cooperation between Kinshasa and London, with authorities describing the transfer as a continuation of judicial enforcement rather than a release from accountability.

During the trial, Ezangi reportedly stated he first met Malanga in London in 2016 and later reconnected with him in several African countries before the 2024 operation. He claimed he was not fully aware of the objectives of the mission, though prosecutors linked him to the armed group that attempted to seize strategic sites in the capital.

The 2024 coup attempt, which briefly shook Kinshasa, resulted in multiple convictions of both Congolese and foreign nationals. Among those previously transferred abroad were American citizens, including Marcel Malanga, and Belgian-Congolese academic Jean-Jacques Wondo, who were also handed life sentences after being extradited to serve their terms in their home countries.

Authorities say Ezangi’s transfer leaves only a small number of foreign-linked detainees still held in the DRC in connection with the failed coup.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, le 2 avril 2026 - Le ressortissant britannique Youssouf Ezangi, ancien plombier originaire de la République démocratique du Congo, a été extradé vers le Royaume-Uni pour purger une peine d'emprisonnement à perpétuité pour son rôle dans la tentative de coup d'État de mai 2024 à Kinshasa.

Ezangi, 53 ans au moment des faits, a été transféré de la prison militaire de Ndolo le 31 mars 2026, dans le cadre d'un accord de coopération judiciaire entre la République démocratique du Congo et le Royaume-Uni. Sa remise s'est effectuée en présence de responsables diplomatiques et militaires, dont des représentants de l'ambassade britannique à Kinshasa.

Il avait été reconnu coupable par des tribunaux militaires de violences armées et d'infractions liées au terrorisme liées à la tentative de coup d'État manquée menée par Christian Malanga le 19 mai 2024. Initialement condamné à mort, sa peine a ensuite été commuée en réclusion à perpétuité suite à une grâce présidentielle.

Selon la procédure judiciaire, Ezangi faisait partie d'un groupe qui est entré dans des lieux clés de l'État à Kinshasa, notamment la résidence de hauts fonctionnaires et le Palais de la Nation, au cours de l'assaut de courte durée contre les institutions de l'État.

L'extradition a été formellement approuvée dans le cadre de la coopération juridique bilatérale entre Kinshasa et Londres, les autorités décrivant le transfert comme une continuation de l'exécution judiciaire plutôt que comme une dispense de responsabilité.

Au cours du procès, Ezangi aurait déclaré avoir rencontré Malanga pour la première fois à Londres en 2016, puis avoir repris contact avec lui dans plusieurs pays africains avant l'opération de 2024. Il a affirmé qu'il n'était pas pleinement conscient des objectifs de la mission, même si les procureurs l'ont lié au groupe armé qui avait tenté de s'emparer de sites stratégiques dans la capitale.

La tentative de coup d’État de 2024, qui a brièvement ébranlé Kinshasa, a donné lieu à de multiples condamnations de ressortissants congolais et étrangers. Parmi les personnes précédemment transférées à l'étranger figuraient des citoyens américains, dont Marcel Malanga, et l'universitaire belgo-congolais Jean-Jacques Wondo, qui ont également été condamnés à la prison à vie après avoir été extradés pour purger leur peine dans leur pays d'origine.

Les autorités affirment que le transfert d’Ezangi ne laisse qu’un petit nombre de détenus liés à l’étranger toujours détenus en RDC en relation avec l’échec du coup d’État.
author: amina-kabasele

title: La RDC organise un atelier sur la diplomatie minière pour renforcer la gouvernance et le positionnement mondial du secteur minier
excerpt: 30 mars 2026 - Les parties prenantes du secteur minier de la République démocratique du Congo se sont réunies à Kinshasa pour un atelier de haut niveau axé sur le renforcement de la diplomatie minière, l'amélioration de la gouvernance et l'amélioration de la position du pays dans les chaînes de valeur mondiales des minéraux critiques. title_en: DRC holds workshop on mining diplomacy to strengthen governance and global positioning of mineral sector
excerpt_en: March 30, 2026 - Stakeholders in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s mining sector gathered in Kinshasa for a high-level workshop focused on strengthening mining diplomacy, improving governance, and enhancing the country’s position in global critical mineral value chains. Organize
body_en:
March 30, 2026 - Stakeholders in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s mining sector gathered in Kinshasa for a high-level workshop focused on strengthening mining diplomacy, improving governance, and enhancing the country’s position in global critical mineral value chains.
Organized by the Bon Regard Association (BREG) in collaboration with government institutions, technical services, development partners, diplomatic missions, and civil society organizations, the two-day forum (March 30-31) aims to produce policy recommendations for national decision-makers.
Officials emphasized that the DRC’s vast mineral wealth-particularly in critical minerals essential to the global energy transition-places the country in a strategic position within the international economy, but that structural challenges continue to limit its full potential.
Speaking on behalf of the Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Nzengu Mishinga Jules highlighted transparency, accountability, and coordinated diplomacy as key pillars for strengthening the country’s mining governance and international credibility.
He stressed the need for closer synergy between the Ministries of Mines, Planning, and Finance, along with diplomatic services, to ensure a coherent strategy that moves the country beyond the perception of being merely a raw materials exporter.
International partners also expressed support for reform efforts. The United Kingdom reaffirmed its commitment to supporting governance and transparency initiatives in the sector, including additional contributions through programs implemented by the Natural Resource Governance Institute (NRGI).
British officials underscored the DRC’s “crucial role” in the global energy transition and encouraged reforms that could attract responsible investment and strengthen institutional stability.
NRGI representatives emphasized that improved governance, reduced illicit resource flows, and better environmental and human rights standards are essential for transforming mining wealth into sustainable national development.
Participants also highlighted persistent challenges in the sector, including conflict-linked resource extraction, weak governance structures, environmental degradation, and limited local value addition.
Organizers said the workshop is intended to move beyond discussion toward actionable recommendations that will help the government strengthen mining diplomacy and position the DRC as a strategic, rules-based actor in global mineral supply chains.
body_fr:
30 mars 2026 - Les parties prenantes du secteur minier de la République démocratique du Congo se sont réunies à Kinshasa pour un atelier de haut niveau axé sur le renforcement de la diplomatie minière, l'amélioration de la gouvernance et l'amélioration de la position du pays dans les chaînes de valeur mondiales des minéraux critiques.
Organisé par l'Association Bon Regard (BREG) en collaboration avec des institutions gouvernementales, des services techniques, des partenaires au développement, des missions diplomatiques et des organisations de la société civile, le forum de deux jours (30 et 31 mars) vise à produire des recommandations politiques à l'intention des décideurs nationaux.
Les responsables ont souligné que les vastes richesses minérales de la RDC, en particulier celles essentielles à la transition énergétique mondiale, placent le pays dans une position stratégique au sein de l’économie internationale, mais que des défis structurels continuent de limiter son plein potentiel.
S'exprimant au nom du ministère des Affaires étrangères, Nzengu Mishinga Jules a souligné que la transparence, la responsabilité et la diplomatie coordonnée sont des piliers clés pour renforcer la gouvernance minière du pays et sa crédibilité internationale.
Il a souligné la nécessité d'une synergie plus étroite entre les ministères des Mines, de la Planification et des Finances, ainsi que les services diplomatiques, pour garantir une stratégie cohérente qui fasse passer le pays au-delà de la perception d'un simple exportateur de matières premières.
Les partenaires internationaux ont également exprimé leur soutien aux efforts de réforme. Le Royaume-Uni a réaffirmé son engagement à soutenir les initiatives de gouvernance et de transparence dans le secteur, y compris des contributions supplémentaires par le biais de programmes mis en œuvre par le Natural Resource Governance Institute (NRGI).
Les responsables britanniques ont souligné le « rôle crucial » de la RDC dans la transition énergétique mondiale et ont encouragé des réformes susceptibles d’attirer des investissements responsables et de renforcer la stabilité institutionnelle.
Les représentants du NRGI ont souligné qu'une meilleure gouvernance, une réduction des flux de ressources illicites et de meilleures normes environnementales et en matière de droits de l'homme sont essentielles pour transformer la richesse minière en un développement national durable.
Les participants ont également souligné les défis persistants du secteur, notamment l’extraction des ressources liée aux conflits, la faiblesse des structures de gouvernance, la dégradation de l’environnement et la valeur ajoutée locale limitée.
Les organisateurs ont déclaré que l'atelier vise à aller au-delà de la discussion vers des recommandations concrètes qui aideront le gouvernement à renforcer la diplomatie minière et à positionner la RDC en tant qu'acteur stratégique et fondé sur des règles dans les chaînes mondiales d'approvisionnement en minéraux.
author: amina-kabasele

title_en: Gen. Muhoozi expresses support for Israel amid ongoing Israel-Iran conflict
excerpt_en: Kampala, Uganda, March 26, 2026 - Uganda’s Chief of Defence Forces Muhoozi Kainerugaba has publicly stated his support for Israel in the ongoing conflict involving Israel and Iran, according to remarks shared through his public communications. He indicated that his position is ba
body_en:
Kampala, Uganda, March 26, 2026 - Uganda’s Chief of Defence Forces Muhoozi Kainerugaba has publicly stated his support for Israel in the ongoing conflict involving Israel and Iran, according to remarks shared through his public communications.
He indicated that his position is based on geopolitical and religious considerations, stating that Uganda would side with Israel if the conflict escalates in a way that threatens its defeat.
In his comments, Gen. Muhoozi said any outcome leading to what he described as the destruction or defeat of Israel would prompt alignment with Israel’s position, adding that he believes the world is growing weary of the ongoing hostilities in the Middle East.
He further referenced historical and religious ties in explaining his stance.
The conflict, referred to as the Israel-Iran war, reportedly began on February 28, 2026, and has continued for several weeks, with various international actors closely monitoring its escalation.
Gen. Muhoozi also made remarks suggesting strong political alignment with Israel, noting previous expressions of support, including plans to honor historical Israeli figures. Among them is Col. Yonatan Netanyahu, who led the 1976 Entebbe rescue operation in Uganda and was later killed during the same period.
The broader conflict involves Israel and Iran, with Iran’s Supreme Leader Ali Khamenei remaining a central figure in Iran’s leadership during the ongoing tensions.
The situation remains highly volatile, with international calls for de-escalation continuing as the conflict develops.
body_fr:
Kampala, Ouganda, 26 mars 2026 - Le chef des forces de défense ougandaises, Muhoozi Kainerugaba, a publiquement déclaré son soutien à Israël dans le conflit en cours impliquant Israël et l'Iran, selon des propos partagés dans ses communications publiques.
Il a indiqué que sa position était fondée sur des considérations géopolitiques et religieuses, affirmant que l'Ouganda se rangerait du côté d'Israël si le conflit s'aggravait au point de menacer sa défaite.
Dans ses commentaires, le général Muhoozi a déclaré que tout résultat conduisant à ce qu’il a décrit comme la destruction ou la défaite d’Israël inciterait à un alignement sur la position israélienne, ajoutant qu’il pensait que le monde était de plus en plus las des hostilités en cours au Moyen-Orient.
Il a en outre fait référence aux liens historiques et religieux pour expliquer sa position.
Le conflit, appelé guerre Israël-Iran, aurait commencé le 28 février 2026 et se poursuivrait depuis plusieurs semaines, divers acteurs internationaux surveillant de près son escalade.
Le général Muhoozi a également fait des remarques suggérant un fort alignement politique avec Israël, notant les expressions de soutien antérieures, y compris les projets visant à honorer des personnalités historiques israéliennes. Parmi eux se trouve le colonel Yonatan Netanyahu, qui a dirigé l’opération de sauvetage d’Entebbe en Ouganda en 1976 et a ensuite été tué au cours de la même période.
Le conflit plus large implique Israël et l’Iran, le guide suprême iranien Ali Khamenei restant une figure centrale du leadership iranien pendant les tensions actuelles.
La situation reste très volatile, et les appels internationaux à la désescalade se poursuivent à mesure que le conflit se développe.

title: Mercuria et EGC signent un protocole d'accord pour développer une chaîne d'approvisionnement responsable en cobalt en RDC
excerpt: Shanghai/Kinshasa 28 mars 2026 - L'Entreprise Générale du Cobalt (EGC) et Mercuria Energy Trading ont signé un protocole d'accord visant à structurer et formaliser une chaîne d'approvisionnement artisanale en cobalt en République Démocratique du Congo, avec un focus sur le Kasulo m
title_en: Mercuria and EGC sign MOU to develop responsible cobalt supply chain in DRC
excerpt_en: Shanghai/Kinshasa March 28, 2026 - The Entreprise Générale du Cobalt (EGC) and Mercuria Energy Trading have signed a memorandum of understanding aimed at structuring and formalizing an artisanal cobalt supply chain in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with a focus on the Kasulo m
body_en:
Shanghai/Kinshasa March 28, 2026 - The Entreprise Générale du Cobalt (EGC) and Mercuria Energy Trading have signed a memorandum of understanding aimed at structuring and formalizing an artisanal cobalt supply chain in the Democratic Republic of Congo, with a focus on the Kasulo mining site in Kolwezi.
Announced in Shanghai, the agreement seeks to establish what both parties describe as a “gold standard” model for artisanal and small-scale mining, emphasizing transparency, sustainability, and responsible sourcing in cobalt production.
The initiative will involve cooperation with artisanal miners, local cooperatives, the state mining company Gécamines, as well as national and provincial authorities to address key challenges in the sector, including health and safety standards, human rights compliance, environmental protection, and end-to-end traceability.
The framework is expected to align with international guidelines such as the OECD Due Diligence Guidance for Responsible Supply Chains and the United Nations Guiding Principles on Business and Human Rights, alongside national regulatory standards.
EGC, which oversees artisanal cobalt production in the DRC, and Mercuria, a global commodities trading firm, say the partnership aims to professionalize artisanal mining by improving regulation and ensuring safer working conditions while maintaining supply chain reliability.
The Kasulo project is intended to serve as a pilot model for structured artisanal mining, with ambitions of becoming an international reference point for responsible cobalt sourcing.
Company representatives stated that the collaboration reflects growing global demand for ethically sourced critical minerals used in batteries and energy technologies, and underscores efforts to integrate artisanal mining into formal supply systems.
body_fr:
Shanghai/Kinshasa 28 mars 2026 - L'Entreprise Générale du Cobalt (EGC) et Mercuria Energy Trading ont signé un protocole d'accord visant à structurer et formaliser une chaîne d'approvisionnement artisanale en cobalt en République démocratique du Congo, avec un focus sur le site minier de Kasulo à Kolwezi.
Annoncé à Shanghai, l’accord vise à établir ce que les deux parties décrivent comme un modèle « de référence » pour l’exploitation minière artisanale et à petite échelle, mettant l’accent sur la transparence, la durabilité et l’approvisionnement responsable dans la production de cobalt.
L'initiative impliquera une coopération avec les mineurs artisanaux, les coopératives locales, la société minière d'État Gécamines, ainsi que les autorités nationales et provinciales pour relever les principaux défis du secteur, notamment les normes de santé et de sécurité, le respect des droits de l'homme, la protection de l'environnement et la traçabilité de bout en bout.
Le cadre devrait s'aligner sur les lignes directrices internationales telles que le Guide de l'OCDE sur le devoir de diligence pour des chaînes d'approvisionnement responsables et les Principes directeurs des Nations Unies relatifs aux entreprises et aux droits de l'homme, ainsi qu'aux normes réglementaires nationales.
EGC, qui supervise la production artisanale de cobalt en RDC, et Mercuria, une société mondiale de négoce de matières premières, affirment que le partenariat vise à professionnaliser l'exploitation minière artisanale en améliorant la réglementation et en garantissant des conditions de travail plus sûres tout en maintenant la fiabilité de la chaîne d'approvisionnement.
Le projet Kasulo est destiné à servir de modèle pilote pour une exploitation minière artisanale structurée, avec l'ambition de devenir une référence internationale pour un approvisionnement responsable en cobalt.
Les représentants de l'entreprise ont déclaré que la collaboration reflète la demande mondiale croissante de minéraux essentiels d'origine éthique utilisés dans les batteries et les technologies énergétiques, et souligne les efforts visant à intégrer l'exploitation minière artisanale dans les systèmes d'approvisionnement formels.

body_en:
Djibouti City, Djibouti, March 2026 — The government has announced plans to mobilize more than $50 million for the development of its mining sector as part of the Djibouti Vision 2035 strategy.
Officials say the initiative aims to reduce the country’s reliance on ports and military-related revenues by expanding into natural resource development and broader economic diversification.
The plan is expected to attract investment into exploration and extraction projects, positioning mining as a new pillar of long-term national growth.
body_fr:

Les responsables affirment que l’initiative vise à réduire la dépendance du pays à l’égard des ports et des revenus militaires en s’étendant au développement des ressources naturelles et à une diversification économique plus large.
Le plan devrait attirer des investissements dans des projets d'exploration et d'extraction, positionnant ainsi l'exploitation minière comme un nouveau pilier de la croissance nationale à long terme.

title_en: Chinese to build three factories including transformer plant in Nyagatare
excerpt_en: Nyagatare, Rwanda, March 25, 2026 - Chinese investors are set to establish three factories in Nyagatare District, including a transformer manufacturing plant, in a move expected to boost industrial capacity and agricultural production in the region. District authorities said the
body_en:
Nyagatare, Rwanda, March 25, 2026 - Chinese investors are set to establish three factories in Nyagatare District, including a transformer manufacturing plant, in a move expected to boost industrial capacity and agricultural production in the region.
District authorities said the projects will include two factories producing electrical equipment and one facility dedicated to manufacturing fertilizer from cow dung mixed with other substances.
The development follows a March 11 meeting between Eastern Province Governor Pudence Rubingisa and a delegation of Chinese investors who visited the province to assess investment opportunities and explore potential partnerships.
After the meeting, the investors traveled to Nyagatare District, where local officials presented a range of opportunities. Several proposals attracted immediate interest, with investors agreeing to move forward without delay.
Acting Mayor Kakooza Henry said key areas of interest included the construction of electrical equipment factories and a fertilizer plant.

title: Over 200 suspects arrested in large security sweep at Lubumbashi military camp in Haut-Katanga
excerpt: Lubumbashi March 30, 2026 - Security forces in southeastern Democratic Republic of Congo arrested more than 200 suspected criminals during a large-scale cordon-and-search operation at Major Vangu Camp in Lubumbashi, Haut-Katanga province. The joint operation was conducted under t
title_en: Over 200 suspects arrested in large security sweep at Lubumbashi military camp in Haut-Katanga
excerpt_en: Lubumbashi March 30, 2026 - Security forces in southeastern Democratic Republic of Congo arrested more than 200 suspected criminals during a large-scale cordon-and-search operation at Major Vangu Camp in Lubumbashi, Haut-Katanga province. The joint operation was conducted under t
body_en:
Lubumbashi March 30, 2026 - Security forces in southeastern Democratic Republic of Congo arrested more than 200 suspected criminals during a large-scale cordon-and-search operation at Major Vangu Camp in Lubumbashi, Haut-Katanga province.
The joint operation was conducted under the supervision of provincial Interior Minister Jean-Jacques Kashiba and the provincial police commissioner, Blaise Kilimbalimba. It involved units of the National Police, supported by elements of the 22nd Military Region and other security services.
Authorities reported the seizure of 19 AK-47 rifles, along with ammunition, military uniforms, and various bladed weapons including machetes, crowbars, hammers, and shears. Security forces also recovered items such as alcoholic beverages and narcotics during the searches.
Police spokesperson Major Charles Bin Lwamba stated that those arrested included civilians, soldiers, and women, describing the group as suspected of involvement in criminal activity within and around the camp area.
The operation involved systematic searches of residential homes, shops, informal markets, and other structures inside and outside the camp perimeter, according to security officials.
The sweep followed a recent military gathering at Major Vangu Camp where the Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Lt. Gen. Jules Banza Mwilambwe, called for stronger unity and discipline within the ranks to reinforce national security and territorial integrity.

title: Kinshasa Accuses Kabila After ‘Sudanization’ Remarks Amid Rising Political Tensions
excerpt: KINSHASA, March 26, 2026 - Authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo have strongly reacted to recent statements by former president Joseph Kabila, interpreting them as an implicit assumption of responsibility for the activities of armed groups operating in the country’s eas
title_en: Kinshasa Accuses Kabila After ‘Sudanization’ Remarks Amid Rising Political Tensions
excerpt_en: KINSHASA, March 26, 2026 - Authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo have strongly reacted to recent statements by former president Joseph Kabila, interpreting them as an implicit assumption of responsibility for the activities of armed groups operating in the country’s eas
body_en:
KINSHASA, March 26, 2026 - Authorities in the Democratic Republic of Congo have strongly reacted to recent statements by former president Joseph Kabila, interpreting them as an implicit assumption of responsibility for the activities of armed groups operating in the country’s east.
The controversy follows a renewed public intervention by Kabila after consultations with socio-political actors in North and South Kivu and a Nairobi-based declaration by the “Save the Democratic Republic of Congo” political initiative. The former head of state used the opportunity to criticize the governance of President Félix Tshisekedi, marking one of his most direct political interventions in recent months.
In a recent interview with a Belgian media outlet, Kabila rejected the commonly used term “balkanization” to describe the security crisis in eastern Congo, instead referring to a process of “Sudanization.” He drew parallels with the historical fragmentation of Sudan, which led to the independence of South Sudan in 2011 after years of civil conflict.
Government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya condemned the remarks during a briefing in Kinshasa, describing them as a “form of claim of responsibility” linked to the actions of the AFC/M23 rebellion active in eastern DRC, an armed group Kinshasa alleges is supported by Rwanda.
Muyaya further argued that the timing and framing of Kabila’s statement were politically significant, suggesting they reflected an underlying agenda. He also dismissed the former president’s criticism of current governance, insisting that the present administration has prioritized infrastructure development and institutional reform, while accusing previous leadership of failing to address long-standing national challenges.
The remarks come in the context of continued political mobilization linked to a conclave held in Nairobi in October 2025, where allies and political figures close to Kabila announced the formation of the “Save the DRC Movement.” The platform describes its mission as restoring democratic governance, addressing systemic crisis, and promoting national reconciliation.
The initiative has accused the current government of democratic backsliding and institutional abuse, and has called for an inclusive national dialogue facilitated by religious institutions. It also rejects unilateral political processes led by the presidency.
The movement, also referred to in several local languages as Tobikisa Ekolo, Tuokowe Taifa, and Tupandishayi Ditunga, has indicated plans to coordinate opposition forces and engage regional and international stakeholders regarding the situation in the Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: Two Wazalendo Killed, Eight Arrested in Clashes with Army in Shabunda
excerpt: Shabunda Centre, Shabunda March 30, 2026 - At least two Wazalendo fighters were killed and eight others arrested on Sunday, March 29, during clashes in Shabunda Centre in Shabunda Territory in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, after an attempted disarmament operation by the a
title_en: Two Wazalendo Killed, Eight Arrested in Clashes with Army in Shabunda
excerpt_en: Shabunda Centre, Shabunda March 30, 2026 - At least two Wazalendo fighters were killed and eight others arrested on Sunday, March 29, during clashes in Shabunda Centre in Shabunda Territory in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, after an attempted disarmament operation by the a
body_en:
Shabunda Centre, Shabunda March 30, 2026 - At least two Wazalendo fighters were killed and eight others arrested on Sunday, March 29, during clashes in Shabunda Centre in Shabunda Territory in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, after an attempted disarmament operation by the armed forces.
The confrontation broke out in the morning when government troops intervened against an armed group linked to the Sisawa faction, accused of extorting and intimidating civilians in the area. An exchange of fire followed during the operation.
The group targeted was associated with the network led by Amisi Sisawa, also known as “Muswahili,” who had been accused of maintaining an unauthorized armed structure operating under the Wazalendo label.
Local civil society figures reported that the intervention resulted in the deaths of two armed men on the spot, while their commander and eight other members were captured.
Military authorities stated that the operation was conducted against a criminal group presenting itself as part of the Wazalendo movement and accused of multiple abuses against civilians, including looting, extortion, and forced labor in mining zones.
It was further reported that the same group had previously attacked a provincial delegation led by the South Kivu justice authorities during an earlier incident in Shabunda, aimed at obstructing judicial proceedings.
The arrested individuals are expected to face legal proceedings as investigations continue into the activities of the armed group operating in the region.

title: Uganda’s Discreet Role in M23 Resurgence and Recruitment Exposed, Report Says
excerpt: April 5, 2026 - Uganda played a discreet but significant role in the resurgence of the M23 movement, facilitating the return of its military leadership to eastern Democratic Republic of Congo and serving as a recruitment hub for the group’s reconstitution, according to a new anal
title_en: Uganda’s Discreet Role in M23 Resurgence and Recruitment Exposed, Report Says
excerpt_en: April 5, 2026 - Uganda played a discreet but significant role in the resurgence of the M23 movement, facilitating the return of its military leadership to eastern Democratic Republic of Congo and serving as a recruitment hub for the group’s reconstitution, according to a new anal
body_en:
April 5, 2026 - Uganda played a discreet but significant role in the resurgence of the M23 movement, facilitating the return of its military leadership to eastern Democratic Republic of Congo and serving as a recruitment hub for the group’s reconstitution, according to a new analysis.
The report outlines how, after the movement’s military defeat in 2013, most M23 fighters were relocated to Ugandan military facilities in southwestern Uganda, where they remained for several years under army supervision.
In 2017, M23 military leader Sultani Makenga reportedly left a Ugandan military camp and moved toward the border area around Mount Sabyinyo, near the tri-border zone between Uganda, Rwanda, and the DRC. His departure is described as having been quietly facilitated by elements within Uganda’s military structure, allowing a gradual return of leadership figures into Congolese territory.
The analysis further indicates that Uganda later became a key recruitment base during the M23’s remobilization phase beginning in 2021, with former encampment sites serving as a pool for new fighters joining the movement. This recruitment dynamic is presented as part of a broader and informal network involving military environments and cross-border mobility.
Tensions between regional states are also cited as a contributing factor to shifting alliances, particularly between Uganda and Rwanda, as competing security interests and military deployments in eastern Congo intensified.
The report also notes allegations of coordination between elements of the Ugandan armed forces and M23 recruits during training activities conducted in border regions of eastern Congo, alongside other regional military actors.
However, it emphasizes that the exact nature of Uganda’s involvement remains complex and not fully defined, and does not clearly distinguish between official state policy and the actions of individual military actors operating within broader regional security dynamics.
Conclusion
The period from late March to early April 2026 reflects a Democratic Republic of Congo navigating between meaningful institutional progress and enduring structural fragility. While authorities in Kinshasa advanced key reforms and strengthened international partnerships, the eastern regions remain gripped by insecurity and humanitarian strain.
Institutional and Economic Foundations
The launch of the second General Population and Housing Census marks a historic step toward modern governance, supported by an $80 million commitment from the African Development Bank. This initiative aims to close a decades-long data gap, laying the groundwork for better public policy and equitable development. At the same time, renewed mining diplomacy-through agreements with China and strategic discussions on lithium and cobalt-highlights the country’s ambition to move up the global value chain and assert greater economic sovereignty.
Political Tensions and Constitutional Debate
However, political dynamics remain fragile. The debate over constitutional revision continues to polarize national actors. The National Episcopal Conference of Congo has warned against initiating reforms without broad consensus, citing the current security climate. Meanwhile, opposition figure Moïse Katumbi has firmly rejected any attempt to amend the constitution, framing it as a potential threat to democratic stability. In parallel, President Félix Tshisekedi has called for improved cooperation between provincial institutions, underscoring persistent governance challenges linked to decentralization.

title: WFP food coupon program improves nutrition outcomes in southern Djibouti

title_en: WFP food coupon program improves nutrition outcomes in southern Djibouti
excerpt_en: Ali Sabieh / Tadjourah, Djibouti, March 2026 — A new assessment shows significant improvements in household food security among beneficiaries of a food assistance program implemented by the World Food Programme. According to program data, more than 80% of participating households
body_en:
Ali Sabieh / Tadjourah, Djibouti, March 2026 — A new assessment shows significant improvements in household food security among beneficiaries of a food assistance program implemented by the World Food Programme.
According to program data, more than 80% of participating households report improved food consumption and a reduced reliance on negative coping strategies.
The initiative, which provides fresh produce coupons to vulnerable families, is part of ongoing efforts to strengthen food security and resilience in southern regions of Djibouti.

title: Rwanda to host international blood transfusion experts conference in 2026

title_en: Rwanda to host international blood transfusion experts conference in 2026
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda, March 26, 2026 - Rwanda is set to host an international conference bringing together global experts in blood transfusion and blood-based medicine, marking a return of the high-level meeting after 12 years. The conference is organized in partnership with the Africa
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda, March 26, 2026 - Rwanda is set to host an international conference bringing together global experts in blood transfusion and blood-based medicine, marking a return of the high-level meeting after 12 years.
The conference is organized in partnership with the Africa Society for Blood Transfusion (AfSBT) and is expected to gather specialists, blood bank professionals, and healthcare experts from across Africa and beyond.
The announcement was made during the 12th AfSBT conference held in Namibia from March 21-26, 2026, where Rwanda presented its advancements in blood transfusion systems, including the use of drones for rapid blood delivery to remote areas.
Rwanda was represented by Dr. Thomas Muyombo, who highlighted the country’s progress in ensuring efficient and timely access to blood supplies.
The country last hosted the AfSBT conference in 2016, and the upcoming edition is expected to further strengthen Rwanda’s role in regional and global blood safety initiatives.
AfSBT, founded in 1997 in Abidjan, Côte d’Ivoire, works to promote safe and effective blood transfusion practices across African countries.
Rwanda has recorded significant improvements in its national blood program, with more than 84,000 units of blood collected in 2024 and a reported 99.72% supply fulfillment rate in hospitals.
Health data shows that O positive remains the most donated blood type, while AB negative is the least common. A total of over 58,000 people donated blood during the year, with men representing the majority of donors.
The upcoming conference is expected to reinforce collaboration among African health systems and advance innovations in blood transfusion services.

title: Mass grave containing 32 bodies, mostly children, discovered in Kericho
excerpt: Kericho, Kenya, March 25, 2026 - Authorities in Kenya have launched an investigation after 32 bodies, mostly children, were discovered in a mass grave in the Kericho area. Police said the exhumation began following a court order directing them to recover 14 bodies suspected to ha
title_en: Mass grave containing 32 bodies, mostly children, discovered in Kericho
excerpt_en: Kericho, Kenya, March 25, 2026 - Authorities in Kenya have launched an investigation after 32 bodies, mostly children, were discovered in a mass grave in the Kericho area. Police said the exhumation began following a court order directing them to recover 14 bodies suspected to ha
body_en:
Kericho, Kenya, March 25, 2026 - Authorities in Kenya have launched an investigation after 32 bodies, mostly children, were discovered in a mass grave in the Kericho area.
Police said the exhumation began following a court order directing them to recover 14 bodies suspected to have been buried in the area. The operation later uncovered additional remains, bringing the total to 32 bodies.
According to officials, the victims include seven adults and 25 children. A Kenyan medical officer said post-mortem examinations are underway to establish the identities of the deceased and determine the exact causes of death.
Preliminary findings suggest that some of the bodies were transferred from a hospital in Nyamira to Kericho for burial without proper authorization, raising questions over procedural and legal compliance.
Authorities stated that some remains appeared to have been removed from a hospital before burial, but emphasized that forensic analysis is ongoing to clarify circumstances surrounding the deaths.
The discovery has prompted widespread concern, with investigators continuing efforts to determine whether the burials were conducted in violation of legal procedures or involve additional criminal elements.

title: AFC/M23 claims FARDC seen fighting alongside FDLR despite disarmament pledge
excerpt: Eastern DRC, April 1, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition has accused the Congolese army (FARDC) of operating alongside FDLR fighters just days after government announcements that operations had begun to dismantle the armed group. The allegations come shortly after the DRC military decl
title_en: AFC/M23 claims FARDC seen fighting alongside FDLR despite disarmament pledge
excerpt_en: Eastern DRC, April 1, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition has accused the Congolese army (FARDC) of operating alongside FDLR fighters just days after government announcements that operations had begun to dismantle the armed group. The allegations come shortly after the DRC military decl
body_en:
Eastern DRC, April 1, 2026 - The AFC/M23 coalition has accused the Congolese army (FARDC) of operating alongside FDLR fighters just days after government announcements that operations had begun to dismantle the armed group.
The allegations come shortly after the DRC military declared on March 29, 2026, that it had launched efforts to disarm the FDLR and compel its fighters to surrender voluntarily or by force.
Deputy Chief of Staff of the FARDC, Lt. Gen. Nduru Jacques Ychaligonza, had stated that troops deployed in eastern regions would prioritize disarmament operations while aiming to avoid bloodshed.
However, AFC/M23 later alleged that government forces were seen collaborating with FDLR units on active front lines, calling it a violation of ceasefire commitments and recent peace understandings.
The group further claimed that joint FARDC-FDLR activity has contributed to civilian casualties in ongoing clashes, and accused Kinshasa of failing to implement agreed security measures.
The Congolese government has not independently confirmed these allegations.
The dispute highlights ongoing tensions surrounding implementation of the Washington D.C. peace agreement, which includes provisions requiring the dismantling of the FDLR as part of broader regional security commitments.

title: La BAD promet 80 millions de dollars pour soutenir le recensement national longtemps retardé en RDC
excerpt: Kinshasa, 25 mars 2026 - La Banque africaine de développement (BAD) a engagé 80 millions de dollars pour soutenir le deuxième Recensement général de la population et de l'habitat (RGPH-2) de la République démocratique du Congo, un exercice statistique majeur visant à mettre à jour les données démographiques nationales près de quatre décennies après le dernier siècle.
title_en: AfDB pledges $80 million to support long-delayed national census in the DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 25, 2026 - The African Development Bank (AfDB) has committed $80 million to support the Democratic Republic of Congo’s second General Population and Housing Census (RGPH-2), a major statistical exercise aimed at updating national demographic data nearly four decades after the last cen
body_en:
Kinshasa March 25, 2026 - The African Development Bank (AfDB) has committed $80 million to support the Democratic Republic of Congo’s second General Population and Housing Census (RGPH-2), a major statistical exercise aimed at updating national demographic data nearly four decades after the last census.

The announcement was made during a donor roundtable focused on mobilizing financing for the nationwide operation, which the government estimates will cost around $192 million in total.

According to AfDB officials, the pledged funding will be split into two components: $50 million dedicated to field operations and $30 million to strengthen national statistical institutions, including the National Institute of Statistics (INS) and other agencies involved in planning, budgeting, and monitoring.

The AfDB described the initiative as a “historic” step for the country, noting its experience in supporting large-scale statistical operations across Africa. The institution also indicated that additional funding could be considered pending internal approval.

The Congolese government is seeking to establish a “basket fund” mechanism to pool contributions from multiple development partners in order to ensure coordinated and transparent financing of the census process.

Authorities say the census is critical for improving development planning, reducing inequalities, and supporting progress toward the Sustainable Development Goals (SDGs), which are approaching the 2030 deadline.

The last full population census in the DRC dates back to 1984, leaving major gaps in demographic and socio-economic data used for national policy design.

Officials argue that the absence of reliable population data has hindered effective governance and resource allocation, making the upcoming census a key national priority and a long-standing political commitment.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, 25 mars 2026 - La Banque africaine de développement (BAD) a engagé 80 millions de dollars pour soutenir le deuxième Recensement général de la population et de l'habitat (RGPH-2) de la République démocratique du Congo, un exercice statistique majeur visant à mettre à jour les données démographiques nationales près de quatre décennies après le dernier recensement.

L'annonce a été faite lors d'une table ronde des donateurs axée sur la mobilisation de financements pour l'opération à l'échelle nationale, dont le coût total, selon les estimations du gouvernement, est d'environ 192 millions de dollars.

Selon les responsables de la BAD, le financement promis sera divisé en deux composantes : 50 millions de dollars consacrés aux opérations sur le terrain et 30 millions de dollars pour renforcer les institutions statistiques nationales, notamment l'Institut national de la statistique (INS) et d'autres agences impliquées dans la planification, la budgétisation et le suivi.

La BAD a qualifié cette initiative d’étape « historique » pour le pays, soulignant son expérience dans le soutien d’opérations statistiques à grande échelle à travers l’Afrique. L'institution a également indiqué qu'un financement supplémentaire pourrait être envisagé en attendant l'approbation interne.

Le gouvernement congolais cherche à établir un mécanisme de « fonds commun » pour mettre en commun les contributions de plusieurs partenaires de développement afin d'assurer un financement coordonné et transparent du processus de recensement.

Les autorités affirment que le recensement est essentiel pour améliorer la planification du développement, réduire les inégalités et soutenir les progrès vers les objectifs de développement durable (ODD), qui approchent de l'échéance de 2030.

Le dernier recensement complet de la population en RDC remonte à 1984, laissant d'importantes lacunes dans les données démographiques et socio-économiques utilisées pour l'élaboration des politiques nationales.

Les responsables affirment que l’absence de données démographiques fiables a entravé une gouvernance efficace et une allocation des ressources, faisant du prochain recensement une priorité nationale clé et un engagement politique de longue date.
author: jean-marc-okito
