title_en: DRC government plans Kakobola 2 hydropower project to expand electricity supply in Kwilu province
excerpt_en: Kikwit March 28, 2026 - The Congolese government is considering the construction of a second hydroelectric facility, Kakobola 2, following the commissioning of the Kakobola Dam in Kikwit. The proposed project, announced on March 26 in Bandundu by Water Resources Minister Aimé Mol
body_en:
Kikwit March 28, 2026 - The Congolese government is considering the construction of a second hydroelectric facility, Kakobola 2, following the commissioning of the Kakobola Dam in Kikwit.
The proposed project, announced on March 26 in Bandundu by Water Resources Minister Aimé Molendo Sakombi, would be located about two kilometers from the existing site in Gungu territory. It is expected to generate 15 megawatts of electricity, increasing the overall production capacity of the Kakobola complex to approximately 25 megawatts.
Officials say technical studies for Kakobola 2 have already been completed, and construction could be finalized within two years. The project is estimated to cost around 55 million US dollars for the plant itself, with an additional 40 million dollars earmarked for transmission infrastructure.
The current Kakobola facility has already begun supplying electricity to nearly 20,000 households, with authorities presenting the expansion as part of a broader strategy to improve energy access across Kwilu province.
According to government projections, the new infrastructure is expected to support not only residential electrification but also public services and local economic activity, including schools, hospitals, and small and medium-sized enterprises.
Minister Sakombi described the project as a key step in transforming the province’s economic ecosystem, emphasizing plans to extend electricity access to productive sectors such as agro-processing and milling activities.
The initiative forms part of a wider national energy expansion agenda aimed at strengthening infrastructure in rural and semi-urban areas, following the official inauguration of the Kakobola dam by President Félix Tshisekedi.

excerpt: Mambasa, March 24, 2026 - A senior leader of the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), Difenda Kasibandi, has been killed during a joint military operation conducted by the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and the Ugandan army (UPDF) in the Asangwa area, near th

excerpt_en: Mambasa, March 24, 2026 - A senior leader of the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), Difenda Kasibandi, has been killed during a joint military operation conducted by the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and the Ugandan army (UPDF) in the Asangwa area, near th
body_en:
Mambasa, March 24, 2026 - A senior leader of the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF), Difenda Kasibandi, has been killed during a joint military operation conducted by the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and the Ugandan army (UPDF) in the Asangwa area, near the Lindi River.
According to the Congolese army, Kasibandi was killed alongside four other fighters in an operation targeting a key ADF stronghold located along the border between Lubero and Mambasa territories. The offensive also led to the rescue of three civilians who had been held hostage by the armed group.
Military sources indicate that the operation was part of broader efforts to dismantle ADF networks operating between North Kivu and Ituri provinces. The targeted group was reportedly linked to a faction led by a senior ADF figure known for directing attacks against civilians in the Bapere region.
Recent movements of ADF fighters between Lubero and Mambasa have reinforced concerns about the group’s mobility and its ability to regroup across territories despite ongoing military pressure.
Following the operation, army officials reiterated their warning to individuals suspected of collaborating with the ADF, stating that all those involved with the group would be tracked down and held accountable.

title: FARDC Launches Operation Against FDLR, Calls for Surrender and Repatriation to Rwanda
excerpt: KISANGANI, Tshopo March 29, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have officially launched a new operation targeting elements of the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR), a Rwandan armed group operating in eastern Congo. The announce
title_en: FARDC Launches Operation Against FDLR, Calls for Surrender and Repatriation to Rwanda
excerpt_en: KISANGANI, Tshopo March 29, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have officially launched a new operation targeting elements of the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR), a Rwandan armed group operating in eastern Congo. The announce
body_en:
KISANGANI, Tshopo March 29, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have officially launched a new operation targeting elements of the Democratic Forces for the Liberation of Rwanda (FDLR), a Rwandan armed group operating in eastern Congo.
The announcement was made on Sunday, March 29, at Camp General Bauma in Kisangani by General Jacques Ychaligonza, who oversaw a military parade marking the start of the campaign.
The operation aims to identify, disarm, and repatriate FDLR fighters still present on Congolese territory. Addressing troops, General Ychaligonza urged members of the group to surrender, stating that they should lay down their weapons “whether willingly or by force” and return to their country of origin, Rwanda.
He emphasized that the operation prioritizes avoiding bloodshed, calling for voluntary surrender and describing Kisangani as a designated reception point for those who give up arms. According to military authorities, a prepared site in the city will host surrendered fighters before their repatriation.
The launch follows what the army described as a completed awareness phase aimed at encouraging defections from the FDLR ranks. Military officials said three battalions have already been assigned to the operation and are expected to be deployed in the coming days.
General Ychaligonza said the campaign is being conducted within the framework of the Washington Agreement (DRC-Rwanda peace framework), and stressed that international actors are expected to monitor its implementation.
He also reassured that surrendered fighters would be treated under supervised conditions before eventual repatriation.
Beyond the launch of the operation, the senior FARDC commander held a series of meetings with military leadership in the 3rd Defense Zone and Kisangani garrison officers, focusing on broader security coordination and stabilization efforts in the region.
The announcement comes amid ongoing security challenges across eastern DRC, where multiple armed groups remain active despite parallel military and diplomatic initiatives aimed at restoring stability.

excerpt: Busendo, Rutshuru, North Kivu April 4, 2026 - At least two people were killed and several others abducted on Saturday, April 4, after armed assailants ambushed a civilian convoy in the Busendo area inside Virunga National Park in Rutshuru Territory in eastern Democratic Republic
title_en: Deadly Ambush in Virunga National Park Leaves Two Dead and Several Abducted
excerpt_en: Busendo, Rutshuru, North Kivu April 4, 2026 - At least two people were killed and several others abducted on Saturday, April 4, after armed assailants ambushed a civilian convoy in the Busendo area inside Virunga National Park in Rutshuru Territory in eastern Democratic Republic
body_en:
Busendo, Rutshuru, North Kivu April 4, 2026 - At least two people were killed and several others abducted on Saturday, April 4, after armed assailants ambushed a civilian convoy in the Busendo area inside Virunga National Park in Rutshuru Territory in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The attack targeted vehicles traveling along the Kiwanja-Butembo axis when unidentified armed men opened fire on passengers. Two victims died instantly, while another was seriously wounded, according to accounts from the scene.
Several passengers were also taken hostage by the attackers, whose identity and whereabouts remain unknown, raising fears of further violence and insecurity for travelers using the route.
The ambush occurred just weeks after transport services had resumed along the Kiwanja-Kanyabayonga road following a temporary suspension caused by persistent insecurity in the region.
The area, which lies along a strategic corridor frequently affected by armed group activity, has experienced repeated attacks in recent months, further complicating efforts to restore safe civilian movement and stabilize transport networks in North Kivu Province.

excerpt_en: Kinshasa, April 2, 2026 - A British citizen, Youssouf Ezangi, has been transferred from the Democratic Republic of Congo to the United Kingdom following his conviction in a high-profile coup plot case. Ezangi was among 37 individuals convicted for their alleged role in an attempt
body_en:
Kinshasa, April 2, 2026 - A British citizen, Youssouf Ezangi, has been transferred from the Democratic Republic of Congo to the United Kingdom following his conviction in a high-profile coup plot case.
Ezangi was among 37 individuals convicted for their alleged role in an attempted overthrow of President Félix Tshisekedi linked to events in May 2024 involving Christian Malanga.
Initially sentenced to death alongside several foreign nationals, including U.S. citizens Tyler Thomson and Benjamin Zalman-Polun, his sentence was later commuted to life imprisonment following international diplomatic pressure.
Authorities in Kinshasa confirmed that Ezangi was transferred on March 31, 2026, under a judicial cooperation agreement between the DRC and the United Kingdom, with the presence of British Embassy officials during the handover.
Officials say the arrangement allows him to serve the remainder of his sentence in the UK.
The move follows earlier decisions in which other foreign convicts were pardoned or repatriated to their home countries after diplomatic negotiations.

title: DRC announces plan to begin disarming FDLR under regional peace commitments
excerpt: Kinshasa, DR Congo, March 30, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have announced plans to begin disarming the FDLR armed group as part of ongoing regional peace and security arrangements. The group, composed of remnants of former FAR soldiers and I
title_en: DRC announces plan to begin disarming FDLR under regional peace commitments
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DR Congo, March 30, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have announced plans to begin disarming the FDLR armed group as part of ongoing regional peace and security arrangements. The group, composed of remnants of former FAR soldiers and I
body_en:
Kinshasa, DR Congo, March 30, 2026 - The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have announced plans to begin disarming the FDLR armed group as part of ongoing regional peace and security arrangements.
The group, composed of remnants of former FAR soldiers and Interahamwe militia linked to the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, has long been cited by Rwanda as a persistent security threat operating in eastern DRC.
Military officials say the disarmament operation will start with calls for voluntary surrender, followed by enforced disarmament if necessary, with designated reception sites reportedly being prepared in Kisangani.
Deputy Chief of Staff Jacques Ychaligonza Nduru said the army’s objective is to avoid bloodshed while ensuring all fighters lay down their weapons.
The move aligns with provisions of the Washington peace agreement signed in December 2025, which links security normalization steps to the dismantling of armed groups in the region.
Rwanda’s ambassador to the United Nations, Martin Ngoga, has previously reiterated that the FDLR remains a serious security concern due to its ideological roots and continued activity in eastern DRC.
Analysts warn that implementation may be complex, citing longstanding accusations of infiltration and integration of armed elements into local security structures.
Authorities in the region say successful disarmament could mark a significant step toward reducing tensions in the Great Lakes region, though challenges remain over verification and coordination.

title: DRC-AFC/M23 peace talks may be relocated from Doha to Switzerland
excerpt: April 4, 2026 - Ongoing peace talks between the Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo and the AFC/M23 rebel group, currently held in Doha, Qatar, could be moved to Switzerland, according to diplomatic and institutional sources. The negotiations, which began early last ye
title_en: DRC-AFC/M23 peace talks may be relocated from Doha to Switzerland
excerpt_en: April 4, 2026 - Ongoing peace talks between the Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo and the AFC/M23 rebel group, currently held in Doha, Qatar, could be moved to Switzerland, according to diplomatic and institutional sources. The negotiations, which began early last ye
body_en:
April 4, 2026 - Ongoing peace talks between the Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo and the AFC/M23 rebel group, currently held in Doha, Qatar, could be moved to Switzerland, according to diplomatic and institutional sources.
The negotiations, which began early last year under Qatari mediation, aim to address the root causes of the conflict in eastern DRC.
Reports indicate that renewed instability in the region, alongside broader international developments affecting Qatar, have contributed to discussions about relocating the talks.
The Center on International Cooperation at New York University has suggested that Switzerland could host the next phase of negotiations, with possible dates mentioned around mid-April 2026, though no formal agreement has been confirmed by either party.
Mediators continue to push for the resumption of dialogue, but both sides remain divided over allegations of ceasefire violations and ongoing security incidents in eastern DRC.
The AFC/M23 movement has accused the government in Kinshasa of continuing military operations in civilian-populated areas, while the government maintains its position on restoring state authority and security in conflict zones.
Conclusion
The period from March 23 to April 4, 2026 reflects a region shaped by a combination of persistent insecurity, active diplomacy, and ongoing modernization, with Rwanda playing a notable role in several developments across East Africa.
Eastern DR Congo remained highly unstable, marked by deadly ADF attacks and continued tensions between the DRC government and the AFC/M23 coalition. Although the DRC announced plans to disarm the FDLR, mistrust persists, as M23 continues to allege collaboration between the DRC forces and armed groups. Uganda’s military leadership has also suggested a possible conditional withdrawal from the region, adding further uncertainty to an already fragile security environment.
At the diplomatic and governance level, Rwanda expanded its international engagement through new ambassadorial appointments and strengthened cooperation with regional partners, including the export of digital tax systems to other African countries. Across the continent, broader political developments such as African Union procedural disputes and constitutional adjustments in Cameroon reflect ongoing institutional and governance transitions.
Economically, the region continues to attract investment, particularly in Rwanda’s industrial and infrastructure sectors, supported in part by international partners including China. The growth of digital financial services, including mobile lending platforms, highlights a wider regional shift toward financial inclusion, innovation, and modernization. Rwanda is also increasingly positioning itself in emerging discussions on digital governance and technologies such as artificial intelligence.
At the same time, Rwanda continues institutional reforms aimed at improving governance and efficiency, including updates to electoral frameworks and the expansion of plea bargaining within the justice system. Social policy efforts are also focused on issues such as student mental health and addressing long-standing challenges related to genocide memory and ideology.
Overall, while the region shows clear progress in economic development, governance reform, and digital transformation, long-term stability remains dependent on resolving armed conflicts in eastern DR Congo and strengthening trust and cooperation among regional actors.
By Jeff Buleli

title: Le tribunal de Kinshasa condamne un médecin à une peine avec sursis dans une affaire d'agression impliquant une vidéo d'un patient
excerpt: Kinshasa le 3 avril 2026 - La Haute Cour de Kinshasa/Kinkole a condamné le Dr David Balanganayi à deux mois de travaux forcés, avec sursis d'un an, dans une affaire découlant d'une vidéo largement diffusée le montrant agressant physiquement un patient.
title_en: Kinshasa court sentences doctor to suspended term in assault case involving patient video
excerpt_en: Kinshasa April 3, 2026 - The Kinshasa/Kinkole High Court has sentenced Dr. David Balanganayi to two months of penal servitude, suspended for one year, in a case stemming from a widely circulated video showing him physically assaulting a patient.
body_en:
Kinshasa April 3, 2026 - The Kinshasa/Kinkole High Court has sentenced Dr. David Balanganayi to two months of penal servitude, suspended for one year, in a case stemming from a widely circulated video showing him physically assaulting a patient.

The judgment, delivered on Friday, found the doctor guilty of simple assault and battery after reclassifying the initial charge of aggravated assault and battery. The court, however, dismissed accusations of torture and the publication of a criminal act, ruling that the evidence did not support those charges.

Under the suspended sentence, Dr. Balanganayi will avoid immediate imprisonment but will remain under probation for one year. Any further offense during this period would trigger enforcement of the custodial sentence.

In its civil ruling, the court ordered the state, held civilly liable, to pay compensation totaling 6 million Congolese francs to the plaintiffs, identified as Kidimba Kongolo Jean and Moya Dorcas.

The case, which has drawn significant public attention in recent days in Kinshasa, began after a video surfaced online showing a medical professional striking a patient, triggering widespread outrage on social media.

Public reaction intensified after First Lady Denise Nyakeru Tshisekedi publicly condemned the incident, calling for accountability.

During his defense, the doctor argued that his use of force was intended to compel the patient to accept treatment in a situation he described as critical, claiming it was aimed at saving her life.
body_fr:
Kinshasa le 3 avril 2026 - La Haute Cour de Kinshasa/Kinkole a condamné le Dr David Balanganayi à deux mois de travaux forcés, avec sursis d'un an, dans une affaire découlant d'une vidéo largement diffusée le montrant agressant physiquement un patient.

Le jugement, rendu vendredi, a déclaré le médecin coupable de coups et blessures simples après avoir requalifié l'accusation initiale de coups et blessures aggravés. Le tribunal a toutefois rejeté les accusations de torture et de publication d'un acte criminel, estimant que les preuves n'étayaient pas ces accusations.

En vertu de cette peine avec sursis, le Dr Balanganayi évitera une peine d'emprisonnement immédiate mais restera en probation pendant un an. Toute nouvelle infraction pendant cette période entraînerait l'exécution de la peine privative de liberté.

Dans son jugement civil, le tribunal a condamné l'Etat, tenu civilement responsable, à verser des indemnités d'un montant total de 6 millions de francs congolais aux plaignants, identifiés comme Kidimba Kongolo Jean et Moya Dorcas.

L’affaire, qui a attiré l’attention du public ces derniers jours à Kinshasa, a débuté après la diffusion en ligne d’une vidéo montrant un professionnel de la santé frappant un patient, déclenchant une indignation généralisée sur les réseaux sociaux.

La réaction du public s’est intensifiée après que la Première Dame Denise Nyakeru Tshisekedi a publiquement condamné l’incident, appelant à rendre des comptes.

Lors de sa défense, le médecin a fait valoir que son recours à la force visait à contraindre la patiente à accepter un traitement dans une situation qu'il qualifiait de critique, affirmant que cela visait à lui sauver la vie.

title: Le Rwanda délivre un message présidentiel au leader du Congo-Brazzaville, Sassou N'Guesso
excerpt: Brazzaville, République du Congo, le 26 mars 2026 - Le ministre rwandais de la Sécurité intérieure, Vincent Biruta, a été reçu par le président Denis Sassou Nguesso, à qui il a remis un message du président Paul Kagame lors d'une visite officielle.
title_en: Rwanda delivers presidential message to Congo-Brazzaville leader Sassou N’Guesso
excerpt_en: Brazzaville, Republic of the Congo, March 26, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of Internal Security Vincent Biruta has been received by President Denis Sassou Nguesso, to whom he delivered a message from President Paul Kagame during an official visit.
body_en:
Brazzaville, Republic of the Congo, March 26, 2026 - Rwanda’s Minister of Internal Security Vincent Biruta has been received by President Denis Sassou Nguesso, to whom he delivered a message from President Paul Kagame during an official visit.

The meeting took place on March 25 in Brazzaville, where discussions focused on bilateral relations and continued cooperation between the two countries.

According to officials, the message from President Kagame conveyed congratulations to Sassou N’Guesso following his recent electoral victory, in which he secured another presidential term after the March 15, 2026 elections.

The talks also touched on regional diplomatic developments, including Rwanda’s support for the candidacy of Louise Mushikiwabo for leadership of the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF), as Kigali continues to rally support ahead of upcoming internal voting processes.

Beyond diplomatic messaging, both sides reviewed the state of bilateral relations and explored ways to deepen cooperation across multiple sectors, including security, trade, and development.

Rwanda and Congo-Brazzaville maintain longstanding diplomatic ties, strengthened over the years through agreements covering aviation, tourism, energy, security, education, environmental protection, and trade.

Officials reaffirmed their commitment to further expanding cooperation as part of ongoing regional engagement efforts.
body_fr:
Brazzaville, République du Congo, le 26 mars 2026 - Le ministre rwandais de la Sécurité intérieure, Vincent Biruta, a été reçu par le président Denis Sassou Nguesso, à qui il a remis un message du président Paul Kagame lors d'une visite officielle.

La réunion a eu lieu le 25 mars à Brazzaville, où les discussions ont porté sur les relations bilatérales et la poursuite de la coopération entre les deux pays.

Selon les responsables, le message du président Kagame transmettait ses félicitations à Sassou N'Guesso suite à sa récente victoire électorale, au cours de laquelle il a obtenu un autre mandat présidentiel après les élections du 15 mars 2026.

Les discussions ont également porté sur les développements diplomatiques régionaux, notamment le soutien du Rwanda à la candidature de Louise Mushikiwabo à la direction de l’Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF), alors que Kigali continue de rassembler des soutiens avant les prochains processus de vote interne.

Au-delà des messages diplomatiques, les deux parties ont examiné l’état des relations bilatérales et exploré les moyens d’approfondir la coopération dans plusieurs secteurs, notamment la sécurité, le commerce et le développement.

Le Rwanda et le Congo-Brazzaville entretiennent des relations diplomatiques de longue date, renforcées au fil des années grâce à des accords couvrant l'aviation, le tourisme, l'énergie, la sécurité, l'éducation, la protection de l'environnement et le commerce.

Les responsables ont réaffirmé leur engagement à élargir davantage la coopération dans le cadre des efforts d'engagement régional en cours.

title: La CENCO prévient que la révision constitutionnelle est possible mais risquée dans le contexte de la crise sécuritaire en RDC
excerpt: Kinshasa, le 26 mars 2026 - La Conférence épiscopale nationale du Congo (CENCO) a déclaré que si la révision de la Constitution de la République démocratique du Congo est légalement possible, elle serait risquée dans les conditions sécuritaires et politiques actuelles du pays.
title_en: CENCO warns constitutional revision is possible but risky amid DRC’s security crisis
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 26, 2026 - The National Episcopal Conference of Congo (CENCO) has stated that while revising the Constitution of the Democratic Republic of Congo is legally possible, it would be risky under the country’s current security and political conditions.
body_en:
Kinshasa March 26, 2026 - The National Episcopal Conference of Congo (CENCO) has stated that while revising the Constitution of the Democratic Republic of Congo is legally possible, it would be risky under the country’s current security and political conditions.

Speaking during a press conference following its extraordinary plenary session held from March 23 to 25 in Kinshasa, CENCO leaders expressed concern over worsening insecurity, persistent instability, and a deepening humanitarian crisis affecting the population.

CENCO Secretary General Donatien Nshole reiterated the Church’s position that constitutional revision is allowed under existing legal procedures, but warned that opening such a process in the current climate could be dangerous due to lack of national consensus.

He stressed that the Constitution already outlines which provisions can or cannot be revised, and insisted that any reform process must be carefully managed to avoid further political tension.

The remarks come amid an ongoing national debate over possible constitutional changes, with supporters arguing that the 2006 Constitution no longer reflects current governance realities, while critics warn that reform efforts could be used for political advantage, including the removal of presidential term limits.

Opposition figures and civil society groups have raised concerns that such changes could extend the current president’s tenure beyond 2028, while the ruling camp maintains that reforms are needed to improve state efficiency.

CENCO called for caution and dialogue, emphasizing that any constitutional process must take place in a stable and consensual environment to avoid deepening existing national divisions.
body_fr:
Kinshasa, le 26 mars 2026 - La Conférence épiscopale nationale du Congo (CENCO) a déclaré que si la révision de la Constitution de la République démocratique du Congo est légalement possible, elle serait risquée dans les conditions sécuritaires et politiques actuelles du pays.

S'exprimant lors d'une conférence de presse à l'issue de sa session plénière extraordinaire tenue du 23 au 25 mars à Kinshasa, les dirigeants de la CENCO ont exprimé leur inquiétude face à l'aggravation de l'insécurité, à l'instabilité persistante et à l'aggravation de la crise humanitaire affectant la population.

Le secrétaire général de la CENCO, Donatien Nshole, a réitéré la position de l’Église selon laquelle la révision constitutionnelle est autorisée dans le cadre des procédures juridiques existantes, mais a averti que l’ouverture d’un tel processus dans le climat actuel pourrait être dangereuse en raison de l’absence de consensus national.

Il a souligné que la Constitution indique déjà quelles dispositions peuvent ou non être révisées, et a insisté sur le fait que tout processus de réforme doit être géré avec soin pour éviter de nouvelles tensions politiques.

Ces remarques interviennent au milieu d'un débat national en cours sur d'éventuels changements constitutionnels, les partisans affirmant que la Constitution de 2006 ne reflète plus les réalités actuelles de la gouvernance, tandis que les critiques avertissent que les efforts de réforme pourraient être utilisés à des fins politiques, y compris la suppression des limites du mandat présidentiel.

Des personnalités de l’opposition et des groupes de la société civile ont exprimé leurs inquiétudes quant au fait que de tels changements pourraient prolonger le mandat du président actuel au-delà de 2028, tandis que le camp au pouvoir maintient que des réformes sont nécessaires pour améliorer l’efficacité de l’État.

La CENCO a appelé à la prudence et au dialogue, soulignant que tout processus constitutionnel doit se dérouler dans un environnement stable et consensuel pour éviter d'approfondir les divisions nationales existantes.

title: Tshisekedi appelle à la coopération entre les institutions provinciales dans un contexte de tensions récurrentes en matière de gouvernance
excerpt: Bandundu, le 25 mars 2026 - Le président Félix Tshisekedi a appelé à une coopération et à une responsabilisation renforcées entre les gouvernements provinciaux et les assemblées provinciales de la République démocratique du Congo, mettant en garde contre la rivalité institutionnelle et l'instabilité politique qui continuent de perturber la gouvernance au niveau national.
title_en: Tshisekedi calls for cooperation between provincial institutions amid recurring governance tensions
excerpt_en: Bandundu March 25, 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi has urged stronger cooperation and accountability between provincial governments and provincial assemblies in the Democratic Republic of Congo, warning against institutional rivalry and political instability that continues to disrupt governance at
body_en:
Bandundu March 25, 2026 - President Félix Tshisekedi has urged stronger cooperation and accountability between provincial governments and provincial assemblies in the Democratic Republic of Congo, warning against institutional rivalry and political instability that continues to disrupt governance at the provincial level.

Speaking at the opening of the 13th Conference of Governors held on March 24 in Bandundu (Kwilu Province), the Head of State stressed that decentralization was intended to bring governance closer to citizens, not to create competing or paralyzed institutions.

He emphasized that provincial oversight by assemblies is legitimate and necessary in a democracy, but warned it should not be used for political pressure, personal interests, or actions that undermine public service delivery.

“The provinces need institutions that cooperate, respect each other, and hold each other accountable within the framework of the law,” President Tshisekedi said, adding that institutional balance is essential for effective governance and development.

He noted that persistent conflicts between provincial executives and assemblies have repeatedly undermined policy implementation, particularly in key sectors such as agriculture, livestock, fisheries, and rural development.

According to the President, no serious development agenda can succeed in an environment marked by political instability, institutional confrontation, or unclear division of responsibilities.

The speech comes against a backdrop of recurring tensions since the 2006 Constitution established decentralization, with provinces frequently experiencing disputes over governance, oversight, and leadership accountability.

Government officials have previously attempted to curb instability, including directives from the Interior Ministry aimed at temporarily suspending motions and petitions in provincial assemblies to restore order during periods of heightened political tension.
body_fr:
Bandundu, 25 mars 2026 - Le président Félix Tshisekedi a appelé à une coopération et à une responsabilisation renforcées entre les gouvernements provinciaux et les assemblées provinciales de la République démocratique du Congo, mettant en garde contre la rivalité institutionnelle et l'instabilité politique qui continuent de perturber la gouvernance au niveau provincial.

S'exprimant à l'ouverture de la 13ème Conférence des gouverneurs tenue le 24 mars à Bandundu (province du Kwilu), le Chef de l'Etat a souligné que la décentralisation avait pour objectif de rapprocher la gouvernance des citoyens et non de créer des institutions concurrentes ou paralysées.

Il a souligné que le contrôle provincial par les assemblées est légitime et nécessaire dans une démocratie, mais a averti qu'il ne devrait pas être utilisé à des fins de pression politique, d'intérêts personnels ou d'actions qui nuisent à la prestation des services publics.

« Les provinces ont besoin d'institutions qui coopèrent, se respectent et se tiennent mutuellement responsables dans le cadre de la loi », a déclaré le président Tshisekedi, ajoutant que l'équilibre institutionnel est essentiel pour une gouvernance et un développement efficaces.

Il a noté que les conflits persistants entre les exécutifs et les assemblées provinciales ont sapé à plusieurs reprises la mise en œuvre des politiques, en particulier dans des secteurs clés tels que l'agriculture, l'élevage, la pêche et le développement rural.

Selon le Président, aucun programme de développement sérieux ne peut réussir dans un environnement marqué par l'instabilité politique, la confrontation institutionnelle ou une répartition floue des responsabilités.

Ce discours intervient dans un contexte de tensions récurrentes depuis que la Constitution de 2006 a établi la décentralisation, les provinces étant fréquemment confrontées à des conflits sur la gouvernance, la surveillance et la responsabilité des dirigeants.

Les responsables gouvernementaux ont déjà tenté de freiner l'instabilité, notamment en donnant des directives du ministère de l'Intérieur visant à suspendre temporairement les motions et pétitions dans les assemblées provinciales afin de rétablir l'ordre pendant les périodes de tension politique accrue.

title: Madagascar adopte le système fiscal électronique du Rwanda dans le cadre d’un accord de modernisation des recettes
excerpt: Antananarivo / Kigali, 30 mars 2026 - Madagascar a signé un accord de coopération avec l'Autorité fiscale rwandaise (RRA) pour adopter le système de facturation électronique (EBM) du Rwanda, une plateforme numérique de collecte et de facturation des impôts conçue pour améliorer l'efficacité des recettes.
title_en: Madagascar adopts Rwanda’s electronic tax system in revenue modernization deal
excerpt_en: Antananarivo / Kigali, March 30, 2026 - Madagascar has signed a cooperation agreement with the Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) to adopt Rwanda’s Electronic Billing Machine (EBM) system, a digital tax collection and invoicing platform designed to improve revenue efficiency.
body_en:
Antananarivo / Kigali, March 30, 2026 - Madagascar has signed a cooperation agreement with the Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) to adopt Rwanda’s Electronic Billing Machine (EBM) system, a digital tax collection and invoicing platform designed to improve revenue efficiency.

The agreement was formalized during a visit by Malagasy tax officials to Kigali, where they also received technical training on the system’s implementation and operation.

RRA Commissioner General Ronald Niwenshuti said the EBM system has significantly improved tax compliance in Rwanda, particularly in value-added tax collection.

He noted that the technology has attracted interest from several African countries seeking to modernize their tax systems and strengthen public revenue management.

Madagascar’s tax authority chief, Edmond Rafaralahy, said the country aims to replicate Rwanda’s success, describing the system as a model of effective digital governance.

Officials say Madagascar will be supported by Rwandan firm QT Global in the rollout of the technology.

Rwanda introduced EBM in 2013 as part of broader tax reforms that have since expanded to near-universal adoption among VAT-registered businesses, with authorities crediting the system for improved compliance and increased revenue collection.

The partnership highlights growing regional cooperation in digital public finance systems across Africa.
body_fr:
Antananarivo / Kigali, 30 mars 2026 - Madagascar a signé un accord de coopération avec l'Autorité fiscale rwandaise (RRA) pour adopter le système de facturation électronique (EBM) du Rwanda, une plateforme numérique de collecte et de facturation des impôts conçue pour améliorer l'efficacité des recettes.

L’accord a été formalisé lors d’une visite des agents du fisc malgaches à Kigali, où ils ont également reçu une formation technique sur la mise en œuvre et le fonctionnement du système.

Le commissaire général de la RRA, Ronald Niwenshuti, a déclaré que le système EBM a considérablement amélioré la conformité fiscale au Rwanda, en particulier en matière de collecte de la taxe sur la valeur ajoutée.

Il a noté que cette technologie a suscité l'intérêt de plusieurs pays africains cherchant à moderniser leurs systèmes fiscaux et à renforcer la gestion des recettes publiques.

Le chef de l’administration fiscale malgache, Edmond Rafaralahy, a déclaré que le pays visait à reproduire le succès du Rwanda, décrivant le système comme un modèle de gouvernance numérique efficace.

Les responsables affirment que Madagascar sera soutenu par la société rwandaise QT Global dans le déploiement de cette technologie.

Le Rwanda a introduit l’EBM en 2013 dans le cadre de réformes fiscales plus larges qui se sont depuis étendues jusqu’à une adoption quasi universelle parmi les entreprises assujetties à la TVA, les autorités attribuant au système une meilleure conformité et une augmentation de la collecte des recettes.

Le partenariat met en évidence la coopération régionale croissante dans les systèmes de finances publiques numériques à travers l’Afrique.

title: CENI Suspends Sankuru Governor Election Due to Financial Constraints
excerpt: Kinshasa, March 21, 2026 – The Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI) announced on Friday, March 20, that it cannot continue operational activities for the election of the governor and vice-governor of Sankuru Province due to financial constraints. The election, initial
title_en: CENI Suspends Sankuru Governor Election Due to Financial Constraints
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, March 21, 2026 – The Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI) announced on Friday, March 20, that it cannot continue operational activities for the election of the governor and vice-governor of Sankuru Province due to financial constraints. The election, initial
body_en:
Kinshasa, March 21, 2026 – The Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI) announced on Friday, March 20, that it cannot continue operational activities for the election of the governor and vice-governor of Sankuru Province due to financial constraints.
The election, initially postponed and then rescheduled for Tuesday, April 7, 2026, is now on hold pending the availability of funds. In a statement signed by Deputy Rapporteur Paul Muhindo, CENI stressed that its legal obligation to hold the election within fifteen days after publishing the final candidate list (set for March 23) cannot be met without adequate resources.
CENI had earlier published a provisional list of 11 candidates on March 4, mostly men, sparking renewed debate over the low representation of women in provincial leadership. Following this, appeals against the list were scheduled from March 6-7, disputes from March 9-15, and publication of the final list on March 23. Campaign activities and accreditation of observers and journalists were planned from early to late April.
The postponement follows a formal request from Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior Jacquemain Shabani, who had urged CENI to organize elections quickly after the Constitutional Court upheld the removal of the previous governor on October 24, 2025. The ruling confirmed a vacancy at the head of the provincial executive and instructed that a new election be held in accordance with Article 198 of the Constitution.
CENI emphasized that the electoral process in Sankuru will resume once financial support is secured, underlining the critical role of resources in ensuring timely and lawful elections.

title: Five Killed, Two Injured in Landslide After Heavy Rains in Lushebere
excerpt: Masisi March 14, 2026 — At least five people were killed and two others injured following a landslide triggered by heavy rains in Lushebere, a village located about six kilometers from Masisi town in Masisi Territory. The disaster occurred overnight between Friday and Saturday af
title_en: Five Killed, Two Injured in Landslide After Heavy Rains in Lushebere
excerpt_en: Masisi March 14, 2026 — At least five people were killed and two others injured following a landslide triggered by heavy rains in Lushebere, a village located about six kilometers from Masisi town in Masisi Territory. The disaster occurred overnight between Friday and Saturday af
body_en:
Masisi March 14, 2026 — At least five people were killed and two others injured following a landslide triggered by heavy rains in Lushebere, a village located about six kilometers from Masisi town in Masisi Territory.
The disaster occurred overnight between Friday and Saturday after intense rainfall weakened the soil in this mountainous area, causing a sudden collapse that swept away several homes. Two houses were completely destroyed, burying their occupants under the mud.
Among the victims were twin children, while their father was seriously injured and rushed to the Masisi General Referral Hospital for treatment. In a related incident, a young man in his twenties was struck by lightning during the same storm and is also receiving medical care.
Residents described scenes of panic as the land gave way. “The rain fell all night. At dawn, we heard a loud noise before it collapsed onto the houses,” one witness said, recounting attempts to rescue those trapped beneath the debris.
Local inhabitants say the persistent heavy rains in recent days have destabilized the terrain, making landslides increasingly frequent in the area. “Our village is surrounded by hills. When the rains intensify, the soil becomes fragile and houses downhill are exposed,” another resident explained.
This tragedy comes just days after another deadly landslide at the Rubaya mining site, also in Masisi, highlighting the growing risks linked to extreme weather conditions in the region.
Faced with the recurrence of such disasters, residents are urging authorities to strengthen prevention measures and raise awareness among communities living in high-risk zones to prevent further loss of life.

title: DRC Launches Economic and Financial Criminal Court to Fight Corruption
excerpt: Kinshasa March 15, 2026 – The President of the Republic has officially established the Economic and Financial Criminal Court, a specialized judicial body tasked with tackling serious economic and financial crimes. The decree-law creating the court was promulgated on March 14, mar
title_en: DRC Launches Economic and Financial Criminal Court to Fight Corruption
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 15, 2026 – The President of the Republic has officially established the Economic and Financial Criminal Court, a specialized judicial body tasked with tackling serious economic and financial crimes. The decree-law creating the court was promulgated on March 14, mar
body_en:
Kinshasa March 15, 2026 – The President of the Republic has officially established the Economic and Financial Criminal Court, a specialized judicial body tasked with tackling serious economic and financial crimes. The decree-law creating the court was promulgated on March 14, marking a significant step in the Democratic Republic of Congo’s ongoing efforts to combat corruption, embezzlement, and other financial offenses.
Based in Kinshasa, the new court will include both a trial chamber and an appeals chamber, holding exclusive jurisdiction over cases involving public officials and serious financial misconduct. Its mandate covers corruption, bribery, embezzlement of public funds, counterfeiting, and forgery.
Officials note that the creation of this specialized court is the culmination of reforms initiated under former Justice Minister Constant Mutamba. The initiative aims to improve the speed, clarity, and efficiency of judicial proceedings while reinforcing public and international confidence in the rule of law.
The establishment of the Economic and Financial Criminal Court is seen as a critical step toward strengthening accountability in the DRC’s public sector and deterring economic crimes that have long hindered development.

title_en: Fifteen Hostages Freed from ADF Captivity
excerpt_en: FARDC-UPDF Operations March 13, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) has announced the release of 15 hostages held by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The civilians were freed during joint military operatio
body_en:
FARDC-UPDF Operations March 13, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) has announced the release of 15 hostages held by the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The civilians were freed during joint military operations conducted with the Uganda People's Defence Force (UPDF), part of an ongoing campaign launched in 2021 to dismantle ADF networks in North Kivu and Ituri provinces.
The former hostages were officially handed over on March 12 in Beni for social reintegration, marking another step in efforts to restore community stability in conflict-affected areas.

The clashes, involving heavy and light weapons fire, have heightened fear among residents in this border region with Burundi. title: Rwanda and DRC Agree to Advance Implementation of Washington Peace Accords
excerpt: Washington, 19 March 2026 – Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo have agreed to take concrete steps to implement the Washington Peace Accords, in a renewed effort to ease tensions and promote regional stability. The agreement, initially signed on 27 June 2025 with the
title_en: Rwanda and DRC Agree to Advance Implementation of Washington Peace Accords
excerpt_en: Washington, 19 March 2026 – Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo have agreed to take concrete steps to implement the Washington Peace Accords, in a renewed effort to ease tensions and promote regional stability. The agreement, initially signed on 27 June 2025 with the
body_en:
Washington, 19 March 2026 – Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo have agreed to take concrete steps to implement the Washington Peace Accords, in a renewed effort to ease tensions and promote regional stability.
The agreement, initially signed on 27 June 2025 with the support of the United States, focuses on addressing security concerns, including the dismantling of the FDLR armed group and the removal of Rwanda’s defensive measures along the border.
Although the accord was ratified by both countries in December 2025—along with provisions on economic cooperation in trade, mining, and infrastructure—implementation has remained limited.
Rwanda has maintained that it cannot lift its security measures while the FDLR and allied groups remain active near its borders. Kigali has also accused the Congolese government of continuing to support the group, including through integration into local armed forces and allied militias.
Against this backdrop, delegations from both countries met in Washington from 17 to 18 March 2026, where they committed to advancing implementation of the agreement.
According to U.S. officials, the parties agreed on measures aimed at de-escalation, including respect for each other’s sovereignty and territorial integrity.
Additional steps include the neutralization of the FDLR, a phased withdrawal of Rwanda’s security measures, and the protection of civilians affected by the conflict.
The renewed commitment signals a shared intention to achieve lasting peace and stability in eastern DRC and the wider Great Lakes region, though significant challenges to full implementation remain.

title: Rwanda Encourages Athletes to Invest Through Stock Exchange
excerpt: Kigali, 16 March 2026 – The Rwanda Stock Exchange (RSE), in partnership with the Ministry of Sports, has launched a campaign to encourage athletes to invest in financial markets and secure their long-term financial future. The initiative began with a training session bringing tog
title_en: Rwanda Encourages Athletes to Invest Through Stock Exchange
excerpt_en: Kigali, 16 March 2026 – The Rwanda Stock Exchange (RSE), in partnership with the Ministry of Sports, has launched a campaign to encourage athletes to invest in financial markets and secure their long-term financial future. The initiative began with a training session bringing tog
body_en:
Kigali, 16 March 2026 – The Rwanda Stock Exchange (RSE), in partnership with the Ministry of Sports, has launched a campaign to encourage athletes to invest in financial markets and secure their long-term financial future.
The initiative began with a training session bringing together sports stakeholders, focusing on how athletes can leverage the stock exchange for savings, investment, and financial stability beyond their careers.
The program emphasized the importance of financial literacy, highlighting how stocks and other financial products can offer sustainable income and long-term security, particularly for athletes whose earnings may fluctuate during and after their careers.
Rwego Ngarambe, Secretary of State in the Ministry of Sports, underscored the need for athletes to build strong financial foundations. “Athletes dedicate years to their careers. It is essential that they invest with the same commitment to secure their future and contribute to the country’s economic transformation,” he said.
The CEO of the Rwanda Stock Exchange, Pierre Célestin Rwabukumba, noted that the initiative aims to provide athletes with reliable and regulated investment opportunities. “Athletes can transform their future by investing gradually in approved financial products, gaining confidence while benefiting both during and after their careers,” he said.
Participants welcomed the campaign, saying it aligns with their need to plan for life after sports and achieve financial independence.
The initiative comes at a time when Rwanda’s sports sector is expanding, alongside growing attention to the financial well-being of athletes. Regulators and partners emphasized that improving access to investment opportunities and strengthening financial education will be key to helping athletes make informed financial decisions.

title: Rwandan Banking Executives Complete Advanced Leadership Training in Luxembourg
excerpt: Luxembourg March 9, 2026 — A group of 21 senior banking executives from Rwanda have graduated from a year-long leadership program designed to strengthen strategic capacity in the country’s financial sector. The initiative, known as the Advanced Banking Leadership Program (ABLP),
title_en: Rwandan Banking Executives Complete Advanced Leadership Training in Luxembourg
excerpt_en: Luxembourg March 9, 2026 — A group of 21 senior banking executives from Rwanda have graduated from a year-long leadership program designed to strengthen strategic capacity in the country’s financial sector. The initiative, known as the Advanced Banking Leadership Program (ABLP),
body_en:
Luxembourg March 9, 2026 — A group of 21 senior banking executives from Rwanda have graduated from a year-long leadership program designed to strengthen strategic capacity in the country’s financial sector.
The initiative, known as the Advanced Banking Leadership Program (ABLP), was delivered by the House of Training-ATTF in partnership with the Rwanda Bankers’ Association. The final phase of the program took place in Luxembourg, where participants were awarded certificates upon completion.
The ABLP is aimed at preparing high-potential banking professionals for senior leadership roles through specialized coursework, international case studies, and simulation-based training. It focuses on key areas shaping the modern financial industry, including financial technology, innovation, governance, and sustainable finance.
Participants represented several of Rwanda’s leading financial institutions, including BK, BRD, BPR Rwanda, Ecobank, NCBA, Bank of Africa, I&M Bank, Access Bank, and Equity Bank.
During the program’s final phase, participants engaged in the B@NKSIM simulation exercise, a computer-based platform that allows executives to model real-world banking scenarios. The exercise enables participants to make strategic decisions on financial management, risk, regulatory compliance, and operational performance.
Rwanda’s Ambassador to Luxembourg, Aurore Mimosa Munyangaju, congratulated the graduates, highlighting their role in advancing Rwanda’s banking sector.
She also expressed appreciation to the Government of Luxembourg, particularly the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and European Union, Defence, Development Cooperation and International Trade, for its support.
The program underscores growing cooperation between Rwanda and Luxembourg in financial sector development, as well as ongoing collaboration between the Rwanda Bankers’ Association and the House of Training-ATTF to build expertise and leadership capacity within Rwanda’s banking industry.

title: Agathon Rwasa Questions Burundi’s Military Role in Eastern DRC
excerpt: Bujumbura, 17 March 2026 – Burundian opposition figure Agathon Rwasa has criticized his country’s military involvement in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, arguing that it does not serve the interests of the Burundian people. Speaking in an interview with a lo
title_en: Agathon Rwasa Questions Burundi’s Military Role in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: Bujumbura, 17 March 2026 – Burundian opposition figure Agathon Rwasa has criticized his country’s military involvement in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, arguing that it does not serve the interests of the Burundian people. Speaking in an interview with a lo
body_en:
Bujumbura, 17 March 2026 – Burundian opposition figure Agathon Rwasa has criticized his country’s military involvement in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, arguing that it does not serve the interests of the Burundian people.
Speaking in an interview with a local media outlet, Rwasa said the deployment of Burundian troops is driven by the interests of the ruling CNDD-FDD party, rather than national priorities.
“I believe Burundi’s involvement in the Congo war serves the interests of the authorities, not the people,” he said.
Rwasa also questioned the manner in which Burundian troops are reportedly operating in the DRC, claiming that if their mission were legitimate, they would act openly under their own identity.
He further warned that the conflict risks escalating and spreading closer to Burundi’s borders, particularly given the instability in eastern DRC.
The Burundian government maintains that its troops were deployed to combat armed groups opposed to it, including RED Tabara, FOREBU, and FNL, which are said to operate in South Kivu.
However, Rwasa dismissed this justification, arguing that such operations do not explain the presence of Burundian forces in other areas, including North Kivu.
The remarks highlight ongoing debate within Burundi over its military engagement abroad, as the conflict in eastern DRC continues to draw in regional actors.

title: DRC Launches “Country Window” Project to Boost Geoscience and Mining Sector Modernization
excerpt: Kinshasa, March 20, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo officially launched the “Country Window DRC” project on Thursday, March 19, a major initiative under the PanAfGeo+ program, aimed at modernizing the mining sector and strengthening geoscience cooperation. The launch, pre
title_en: DRC Launches “Country Window” Project to Boost Geoscience and Mining Sector Modernization
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, March 20, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo officially launched the “Country Window DRC” project on Thursday, March 19, a major initiative under the PanAfGeo+ program, aimed at modernizing the mining sector and strengthening geoscience cooperation. The launch, pre
body_en:
Kinshasa, March 20, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo officially launched the “Country Window DRC” project on Thursday, March 19, a major initiative under the PanAfGeo+ program, aimed at modernizing the mining sector and strengthening geoscience cooperation.
The launch, presided over by Minister of Mines Louis Watum Kabamba, took place in Kinshasa and formalized collaboration with the European Union. The project is coordinated by the French Geological Survey (BRGM) and supports the National Geological Survey of Congo (SGN-C) in enhancing its technical and scientific capacities.
“The Country Window DRC project represents a significant opportunity to improve our understanding of the subsoil, strengthen the capacities of our institutions, and reduce the risks associated with mining investment. Geoscientific data is a strategic decision-making tool,” said Minister Kabamba.
The initiative aims to modernize the acquisition, management, and use of geological data, providing tools to guide investment decisions, improve mining governance, and promote responsible and transparent exploitation of natural resources. Kabamba emphasized that the project is part of the DRC’s broader strategy to transition from a raw materials export model to one focused on local value creation, sustainability, and transparency.
EU Support and Strategic Cooperation
Fabrice Basile, acting head of the EU delegation in the DRC, hailed the project as a concrete milestone in the 2023 strategic partnership roadmap between the EU and the DRC. He outlined the project’s four main areas of focus:
Modernizing geoscientific data management and consolidating the national database.
Mapping and assessing resources in priority areas, including artisanal mining sites.
Supporting artisanal mining with innovative technologies for decarbonization and waste recycling.
Strengthening human and technical capacities in public institutions, including ESG training.
“Our ambition is clear: to have a reliable national geoscience database, integrate artisanal mining communities into sustainable value chains, and train a new generation of Congolese geoscientists,” Basile said.
Reducing Investment Risks
The project is also designed to reduce risks for investors. Jean-Claude Guillaneau, PanAfGeo+ coordinator, explained that the program builds on the previous AfricaMaVal phases, which trained 1,773 experts across Africa. PanAfGeo+ Invest aims to expand the scope, focusing on critical minerals, water resources, and fostering a pan-African network of geoscience experts.
Project Scope and Objectives
Running from 2026 to 2029, the PanAfGeo+ Country Window DRC targets:
Geological and mining reconnaissance in Tanganyika, Kasai Central, and Kongo Central.
Feasibility studies for artisanal mining in Lualaba and Haut-Katanga.
Digitization of geological archives in the DRC and abroad.
Mapping artisanal mining nationwide and promoting sustainable, low-carbon practices.
Strengthening human capital through training programs and technical equipment provision.
The project involves multiple partners, including CTCPM, SAEMAPE, CAMI, and CRGM, and represents a significant step toward enhancing state sovereignty over geoscientific data while promoting sustainable investment and governance in the mining sector.
“Improving our knowledge of the geological potential is essential to ensure responsible, transparent, and sustainable exploitation of mineral resources, contributing to national economic and social development,” concluded Minister Kabamba.

title: IGF Confirms “Win-Win” Partnership and Increased Infrastructure Funding
excerpt: Kinshasa March 21, 2026 – Nearly two years after the renegotiation of the Sicomines mining and infrastructure project, the Inspector General of Finance, Jules Alingete, defended the fifth amendment as a successful step toward eliminating corruption and ensuring a balanced partner
title_en: IGF Confirms “Win-Win” Partnership and Increased Infrastructure Funding
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 21, 2026 – Nearly two years after the renegotiation of the Sicomines mining and infrastructure project, the Inspector General of Finance, Jules Alingete, defended the fifth amendment as a successful step toward eliminating corruption and ensuring a balanced partner
body_en:
Kinshasa March 21, 2026 – Nearly two years after the renegotiation of the Sicomines mining and infrastructure project, the Inspector General of Finance, Jules Alingete, defended the fifth amendment as a successful step toward eliminating corruption and ensuring a balanced partnership between the Democratic Republic of Congo and its Chinese partners.
Speaking during the China-DRC Media Forum in Kinshasa, Alingete emphasized that the renegotiation, validated by the President and his cabinet, created a “win-win” arrangement, with $324 million annually earmarked for infrastructure development, in addition to $150 million in dividends for Gécamines. Out of the project’s $900 million in annual profits, roughly $470 million benefits the DRC each year, while the Chinese consortium receives about $400 million.
Major Infrastructure Projects Underway
Alingete highlighted several projects funded under the Sicomines program, totaling over $650 million disbursed in just two years:
Kinshasa ring roads: $145 million disbursed of $383 million planned
Mbuji-Mayi – Mwene-Ditu – Kasese – Nguba road: $325 million financed
Kananga–Kalambambuji road: $88 million financed
Nkamba road (8 km): financed
Bukavu–Kamanyola road: $78 million disbursed, delayed due to regional conflict
He noted that prior to the review, over 15 years, only $800 million had been delivered for infrastructure, averaging $50 million per year, compared to $350 million per year since Amendment 5. Alingete stressed that nearly 70% of current infrastructure works in the country are funded through Sicomines.
Audit and Transparency Measures
The government also announced a technical and financial audit of the Sicomines project, covering 17 years from the Kabila administration to the current Tshisekedi government. The audit, to be conducted by international firms, aims to provide clarity on project implementation and pave the way for a potential sixth amendment. Officials assured that the process will not target former regime officials or collaborators but will focus on verifying figures and ensuring transparency.
A Response to Criticism
Alingete urged the public to ignore critics who question the renegotiation, emphasizing that the project now neutralizes past inconsistencies and corruption. He described the review as a model for balanced partnerships, with substantial infrastructure benefits already delivered and more expected over the next two decades.
Social and Health

excerpt: Kinshasa March 15, 2026 – Opposition leader Parole Kamizelo, also known as “Maîtrisable” (Controllable), has been sentenced to two years of penal servitude for insulting the Head of State. The ruling was issued by the Kinshasa/Ngaliema Magistrate's Court on March 9, 2026. Kamizel
title_en: Opposition Figure Parole Kamizelo Sentenced, Plans Appeal
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 15, 2026 – Opposition leader Parole Kamizelo, also known as “Maîtrisable” (Controllable), has been sentenced to two years of penal servitude for insulting the Head of State. The ruling was issued by the Kinshasa/Ngaliema Magistrate's Court on March 9, 2026. Kamizel
body_en:
Kinshasa March 15, 2026 – Opposition leader Parole Kamizelo, also known as “Maîtrisable” (Controllable), has been sentenced to two years of penal servitude for insulting the Head of State. The ruling was issued by the Kinshasa/Ngaliema Magistrate's Court on March 9, 2026.
Kamizelo’s legal team immediately announced plans to appeal the decision. Attorney Eloi Mubilansama described the verdict as “fundamentally unjust,” citing violations of fair trial guarantees and human rights protections under both the constitution and international law.
Known for his assertive presence on political programs, Kamizelo has gained notoriety since mid-2025 for his outspoken criticism of the Kinshasa government. During his trial, prosecutors accused him of questioning the official marriage of President Félix Tshisekedi, including repeatedly requesting photographic proof on television.
The PPRD party, to which Kamizelo belongs, has also called for his release and that of other officials reportedly held incommunicado, labeling their detention as arbitrary.

title: Mining Sites Attacked by Unidentified Armed Men
excerpt: Mambasa March 12, 2026 — Several mining sites in the Mambasa territory of Ituri Province were targeted by unidentified armed men late Wednesday evening, March 12. The assaults caused panic among residents and miners, forcing many to abandon their homes. Some spent the night outdo
title_en: Mining Sites Attacked by Unidentified Armed Men
excerpt_en: Mambasa March 12, 2026 — Several mining sites in the Mambasa territory of Ituri Province were targeted by unidentified armed men late Wednesday evening, March 12. The assaults caused panic among residents and miners, forcing many to abandon their homes. Some spent the night outdo
body_en:
Mambasa March 12, 2026 — Several mining sites in the Mambasa territory of Ituri Province were targeted by unidentified armed men late Wednesday evening, March 12. The assaults caused panic among residents and miners, forcing many to abandon their homes. Some spent the night outdoors, while others fled to Badengaido, the main town of the Bombo chiefdom.
According to local civil society sources, the attacks began around 8:00 p.m. in the Enjewa mining group, including the areas of Muchacha and Mavuvu, and continued into Thursday morning, creating a state of severe insecurity. Several houses were reportedly burned down, and many families were left displaced.
Jospin Paluku Mbowa, coordinator of the New Congolese Civil Society in Mambasa, said, “The residents and miners were taken by surprise. Many had to leave their homes, and several families spent the night outside. These assailants stormed various mining sites, causing widespread fear.”
Local authorities have not yet released an official assessment of the material damage or potential casualties.
The Mambasa territory, rich in mineral resources, remains vulnerable to armed incursions, putting the safety of civilians and mining operations at continual risk.

title_en: AFC/M23 Rebels Reoccupy Malemo Village in Masisi
excerpt_en: Masisi, North Kivu March 17, 2026 – The village of Malemo, located between Kalembe and Mpety in the Pinga area, has once again fallen under the control of AFC/M23 rebels, following the withdrawal of Wazalendo forces. The Wazalendo had retaken Malemo on March 14 after fierce clash
body_en:
Masisi, North Kivu March 17, 2026 – The village of Malemo, located between Kalembe and Mpety in the Pinga area, has once again fallen under the control of AFC/M23 rebels, following the withdrawal of Wazalendo forces.
The Wazalendo had retaken Malemo on March 14 after fierce clashes with the rebels, but their presence lasted only three days. On the morning of March 17, the Wazalendo voluntarily withdrew, allowing the AFC/M23 rebels to reoccupy the village without resistance.
The reasons for the withdrawal remain unclear, though sources indicate that the rebels, previously positioned in Mpety and Kalembe, took advantage of the situation to return to Malemo.
The security situation around Pinga remains highly volatile, with frequent clashes and shifting positions between AFC/M23 rebels and government forces supported by Wazalendo, leaving the civilian population exposed to continued insecurity.

title: Dr. Iyamuremye Criticizes Support for Sanctions Against Rwanda
excerpt: Kigali, 18 March 2026 – Former Senate President Augustin Iyamuremye has criticized Rwandans who express support for international sanctions against their own country, warning of the broader impact on ordinary citizens. Speaking on 18 March, Iyamuremye said he could not understand
title_en: Dr. Iyamuremye Criticizes Support for Sanctions Against Rwanda
excerpt_en: Kigali, 18 March 2026 – Former Senate President Augustin Iyamuremye has criticized Rwandans who express support for international sanctions against their own country, warning of the broader impact on ordinary citizens. Speaking on 18 March, Iyamuremye said he could not understand
body_en:
Kigali, 18 March 2026 – Former Senate President Augustin Iyamuremye has criticized Rwandans who express support for international sanctions against their own country, warning of the broader impact on ordinary citizens.
Speaking on 18 March, Iyamuremye said he could not understand why some Rwandans—particularly those living abroad—appear to welcome measures such as the suspension of foreign aid and other restrictions.
His remarks come amid strained relations between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo, which have prompted some international partners, including the United Kingdom and Canada, to suspend parts of their cooperation with Kigali.
Earlier in March 2026, the United States also imposed sanctions on members of the Rwandan Armed Forces, further intensifying the debate.
Iyamuremye argued that such measures primarily affect citizens rather than political leaders, citing potential disruptions to essential services and development projects.
“I cannot understand how a Rwandan could be happy that their country is being sanctioned,” he said. “These are services meant for citizens—roads, water, electricity and health facilities.”
He added that those who support such measures fail to distinguish between the government and the broader population, emphasizing the need for national cohesion during challenging times.
The comments highlight ongoing divisions among Rwandans regarding the impact and legitimacy of external pressure linked to regional security tensions.

title: Rwanda Targets Data-Driven Governance by 2030, Says Minister Ingabire
excerpt: Kigali, 15 March 2026 – Rwanda is aiming to become a fully data-driven government by 2030, with technology and innovation at the core of decision-making across all sectors, Minister of ICT and Innovation Paula Ingabire has said. Speaking in a recent media interview, Ingabire outl
title_en: Rwanda Targets Data-Driven Governance by 2030, Says Minister Ingabire
excerpt_en: Kigali, 15 March 2026 – Rwanda is aiming to become a fully data-driven government by 2030, with technology and innovation at the core of decision-making across all sectors, Minister of ICT and Innovation Paula Ingabire has said. Speaking in a recent media interview, Ingabire outl
body_en:
Kigali, 15 March 2026 – Rwanda is aiming to become a fully data-driven government by 2030, with technology and innovation at the core of decision-making across all sectors, Minister of ICT and Innovation Paula Ingabire has said.
Speaking in a recent media interview, Ingabire outlined the country’s ambition to ensure that every government action is based on real-time data and evidence, positioning Rwanda among global leaders in digital transformation.
“We want to be a government where every decision is based on information and evidence,” she said, emphasizing that technology is central to solving national challenges.
Empowering Youth as Innovators
The Minister stressed the importance of transforming Rwanda’s youth from technology users into creators, noting that young people must be given opportunities to develop solutions rather than simply consume digital tools.
To address barriers, the government has introduced reforms in public procurement, allowing tenders to be framed around problems rather than predefined solutions. This approach enables start-ups and young innovators to propose creative responses and compete alongside established companies.
“We have tested this approach and seen a wealth of ideas from young innovators,” Ingabire noted, adding that local entrepreneurs often have a deeper understanding of community challenges.
Expanding Opportunities in Public Markets
Public procurement remains a significant economic driver, with contracts valued at over 1,000 billion Rwandan francs annually in recent years. The reforms are expected to increase access for local businesses and youth-led enterprises, unlocking new opportunities in government projects.
Scaling Artificial Intelligence
Rwanda is also accelerating the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across key sectors such as healthcare, education, and agriculture. The AI Scaling Hub, hosted at the Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution (C4IR) in partnership with the Gates Foundation, is spearheading these efforts.
The initiative focuses on:
Raising public awareness about AI, including its benefits and risks
Building local expertise to develop homegrown AI solutions tailored to Rwanda’s needs
Bridging the Digital Access Gap
Despite 95% internet coverage, the Minister acknowledged that access alone is not enough. Many citizens still lack the devices needed to fully benefit from digital services.
To address this, the government, with support from the World Bank, is identifying vulnerable groups and developing financing solutions to help them acquire essential technology such as smartphones.
“These efforts will ensure that no one is left behind as Rwanda advances toward a digital and inclusive economy,” Ingabire said.
body_fr:
Kigali, 15 March 2026 – Rwanda is aiming to become a fully data-driven government by 2030, with technology and innovation at the core of decision-making across all sectors, Minister of ICT and Innovation Paula Ingabire has said.
Speaking in a recent media interview, Ingabire outlined the country’s ambition to ensure that every government action is based on real-time data and evidence, positioning Rwanda among global leaders in digital transformation.
“We want to be a government where every decision is based on information and evidence,” she said, emphasizing that technology is central to solving national challenges.
Empowering Youth as Innovators
The Minister stressed the importance of transforming Rwanda’s youth from technology users into creators, noting that young people must be given opportunities to develop solutions rather than simply consume digital tools.
To address barriers, the government has introduced reforms in public procurement, allowing tenders to be framed around problems rather than predefined solutions. This approach enables start-ups and young innovators to propose creative responses and compete alongside established companies.
“We have tested this approach and seen a wealth of ideas from young innovators,” Ingabire noted, adding that local entrepreneurs often have a deeper understanding of community challenges.
Expanding Opportunities in Public Markets
Public procurement remains a significant economic driver, with contracts valued at over 1,000 billion Rwandan francs annually in recent years. The reforms are expected to increase access for local businesses and youth-led enterprises, unlocking new opportunities in government projects.
Scaling Artificial Intelligence
Rwanda is also accelerating the adoption of Artificial Intelligence (AI) across key sectors such as healthcare, education, and agriculture. The AI Scaling Hub, hosted at the Centre for the Fourth Industrial Revolution (C4IR) in partnership with the Gates Foundation, is spearheading these efforts.
The initiative focuses on:
Raising public awareness about AI, including its benefits and risks
Building local expertise to develop homegrown AI solutions tailored to Rwanda’s needs
Bridging the Digital Access Gap
Despite 95% internet coverage, the Minister acknowledged that access alone is not enough. Many citizens still lack the devices needed to fully benefit from digital services.
To address this, the government, with support from the World Bank, is identifying vulnerable groups and developing financing solutions to help them acquire essential technology such as smartphones.
“These efforts will ensure that no one is left behind as Rwanda advances toward a digital and inclusive economy,” Ingabire said.

title: Rwanda Security Forces Launch Classroom Construction to Ease Overcrowding in Kamonyi
excerpt: Kamonyi, Rwanda March 9, 2026 — Authorities in Kamonyi District have launched the construction of new classroom facilities aimed at easing chronic overcrowding in local schools, as part of a broader civil-military initiative to support community development. The Rwanda National P
title_en: Rwanda Security Forces Launch Classroom Construction to Ease Overcrowding in Kamonyi
excerpt_en: Kamonyi, Rwanda March 9, 2026 — Authorities in Kamonyi District have launched the construction of new classroom facilities aimed at easing chronic overcrowding in local schools, as part of a broader civil-military initiative to support community development. The Rwanda National P
body_en:
Kamonyi, Rwanda March 9, 2026 — Authorities in Kamonyi District have launched the construction of new classroom facilities aimed at easing chronic overcrowding in local schools, as part of a broader civil-military initiative to support community development.
The Rwanda National Police and the Rwanda Defence Forces jointly laid the foundation stone for a 498 million Rwandan franc project at Kigese Technical Secondary School (TSS), located in Rugarika Sector. The project предусматривает the construction of 10 classrooms, along with a laboratory, administrative offices, sanitation facilities, and a dedicated space for girls.
Local officials say the expansion is expected to significantly reduce overcrowding at Kigese TSS and neighboring GS Masaka, where students have long faced congested and aging learning environments.
The Governor of the Southern Province, Alice Kayitesi, welcomed the initiative, describing it as a timely intervention to improve education conditions in the region.
“This school was overcrowded and had many old classrooms. These new facilities will address that challenge, and we are committed to supporting their completion,” she said.
Rwanda’s Minister of Defence, Juvenal Marizamunda, emphasized that the project reflects a broader strategy linking national security with socio-economic development.
“Security and development go hand in hand. Without security, there is no development, and it is difficult to sustain security in a country that does not address the welfare of its citizens,” he stated.
The construction effort is part of nationwide outreach activities launched by security institutions to strengthen ties with communities and contribute to social welfare programs.
Residents have also expressed optimism. A local parent, Uwimpayidufazizi, said the additional classrooms would create a better learning environment for children.
“This initiative will help our children study in better conditions and improve their chances of success,” she noted.
The development comes amid broader concerns over school infrastructure in Rwanda. In early 2025, the Ministry of Education Rwanda estimated that more than 26,000 additional classrooms are needed nationwide to adequately address overcrowding and improve learning conditions.
