title: Journalist Serge Sindani Released After Ten Days in Detention
excerpt: Kisangani March 13, 2026 — Journalist Serge Sindani, Director General of the media outlet kis24.info, was released on Friday after spending ten days in detention at the headquarters of the National Intelligence Agency (ANR) in Kisangani. Sindani had been abducted on March 3 in th
title_en: Journalist Serge Sindani Released After Ten Days in Detention
excerpt_en: Kisangani March 13, 2026 — Journalist Serge Sindani, Director General of the media outlet kis24.info, was released on Friday after spending ten days in detention at the headquarters of the National Intelligence Agency (ANR) in Kisangani. Sindani had been abducted on March 3 in th
body_en:
Kisangani March 13, 2026 — Journalist Serge Sindani, Director General of the media outlet kis24.info, was released on Friday after spending ten days in detention at the headquarters of the National Intelligence Agency (ANR) in Kisangani.
Sindani had been abducted on March 3 in the city center by ANR agents and was held incommunicado until March 9, without access to his family or colleagues. The reasons for his arrest only became clear after his lawyer was granted access to him earlier this week.
According to his attorney, Christian Kambi, the journalist was suspected of maintaining contacts with individuals linked to the M23 rebellion. However, relatives of Sindani stated that the allegations were based on his past membership in a WhatsApp group known as “Génération Naanga,” described as inactive since the departure of Corneille Nangaa to join the rebellion.
Following his release, Sindani has begun preventive medical treatment, according to his entourage.
This incident follows a previous arrest a few months earlier, during which he was detained for three days after allegedly publishing a photo showing military equipment near Kisangani International Airport.
The case has once again raised concerns about press freedom and the conditions of detention in the country, particularly regarding access to legal representation and communication with relatives.

title: February Sees Record Surge in Airstrikes Against M23 Positions
excerpt: DRC March 11, 2026 — The FARDC has intensified airstrikes and drone operations against M23 positions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, with February recording the highest number of air and drone strikes ever documented, according to ACLED. On February 24, a drone strike ki
title_en: February Sees Record Surge in Airstrikes Against M23 Positions
excerpt_en: DRC March 11, 2026 — The FARDC has intensified airstrikes and drone operations against M23 positions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, with February recording the highest number of air and drone strikes ever documented, according to ACLED. On February 24, a drone strike ki
body_en:
DRC March 11, 2026 — The FARDC has intensified airstrikes and drone operations against M23 positions in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, with February recording the highest number of air and drone strikes ever documented, according to ACLED.
On February 24, a drone strike killed Willy Ngoma, M23’s military spokesperson, along with several senior leaders near Rubaya, a strategic coltan mining hub producing around 15% of global supply and generating roughly $800,000 per month for the rebels.
The FARDC has deployed CH-4 and TAI Anka drones, fighter jets, and attack helicopters, alongside Wazalendo militia ground offensives in Mwenga, Masisi, and Fizi. Private military actors, including Vectus, associated with Erik Prince, also support operations linked to mining revenue control.
Despite the air campaign, M23 launched counter-offensives in late February, forcing temporary withdrawals of FARDC units. The rebels also conducted suicide drone attacks on the Kisangani military command center, a hub for FARDC air operations.

excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu March 16, 2026 – Residents of Walikale are being urged to exercise extreme caution following the discovery of several unexploded devices and munitions in and around the town. The devices were found on March 14, 2026, by local residents and handed over to the
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu March 16, 2026 – Residents of Walikale are being urged to exercise extreme caution following the discovery of several unexploded devices and munitions in and around the town.
The devices were found on March 14, 2026, by local residents and handed over to the CNC-ALPC (National Commission for the Control of Small Arms and Light Weapons). The discoveries have reignited security concerns, nearly ten months after the withdrawal of AFC/M23 rebels from Walikale town.
Officials reported the recovery of two 60mm mortar shells and a significant quantity of various munitions, thanks to the cooperation of the local population. One mortar shell was found in Mubanda, about four kilometers east of Walikale, by workers rehabilitating the Walikale-Kibua road, previously used by rebels. Another bomb was discovered on a residential property in Ndjingala, while additional munitions were recovered in the Nyalusukula neighborhood.
The head of the main CNC-ALPC post in Walikale, Clément Kubuya Ndoole, stressed the need for residents to avoid handling suspicious objects and to immediately alert authorities if explosives are found. He emphasized that community collaboration remains essential for long-term security and the gradual cleansing of Walikale from explosive remnants.
Since the start of its awareness campaign on unexploded ordnance, the CNC-ALPC has collected over 500 kilograms of munitions, which are awaiting destruction.

Masisi, North Kivu – March 23, 2026 – Violent clashes erupted early Monday in Kazinga, in the Osso Banyungu sector, as AFC/M23 rebels launched an offensive against Wazalendo positions in the area.
The fighting began around 5:00 AM, involving heavy and light weapons fire, with explosions reported in surrounding villages, triggering panic among civilians.
Local sources indicate that the attack is part of a renewed effort by the AFC/M23 to reclaim control of Kazinga, a strategic locality that has recently been under Wazalendo influence.
This latest escalation highlights the persistent instability in Masisi territory, where repeated clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and government-aligned forces continue to endanger the civilian population and worsen displacement and insecurity.

body_en:
Kampala, 14 March 2026 – Ugandan opposition leader Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu, widely known as Bobi Wine, has announced that he has emerged from nearly two months in hiding and will temporarily leave the country for engagements abroad.
Kyagulanyi said he went into hiding on January 15, 2026, shortly after the conclusion of presidential and parliamentary elections, citing security concerns and alleged targeting by government forces.
He accused authorities of conducting raids, setting up checkpoints, and targeting his associates, claiming that his supporters helped shield him during that period. “They did not find me because the people of Uganda protected me,” he said.
The opposition leader, who contested under the National Unity Platform (NUP), has rejected the election results, which saw incumbent President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni declared the winner. Official figures from the Electoral Commission showed Museveni securing 71.65% of the vote, while Kyagulanyi received 24.72%.
Bobi Wine stated that his trip abroad is temporary and work-related, aimed at engaging with international partners and allies. “I will be speaking with our friends around the world before returning to Uganda to continue the fight for freedom and democracy,” he said.
His announcement comes amid ongoing political tensions in Uganda, with the opposition continuing to contest the credibility of the electoral process and raising concerns over political freedoms and security.

title_en: Rwanda and Kenya Sign MoU to Boost Cross-Border Payments
excerpt_en: Kigali, 11 March 2026 – The Central Bank of Rwanda (BNR) and the Bank of Kenya have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to facilitate cross-border payments and strengthen regional financial integration. The agreement, inked on the sidelines of the Inclusive Fintech Forum i
body_en:
Kigali, 11 March 2026 – The Central Bank of Rwanda (BNR) and the Bank of Kenya have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to facilitate cross-border payments and strengthen regional financial integration.
The agreement, inked on the sidelines of the Inclusive Fintech Forum in Kigali, establishes a ‘License Passporting Framework for Payment Service Providers (PSPs)’, allowing licensed PSPs to operate seamlessly in either Rwanda or Kenya.
Officials said the MoU is expected to promote competition, encourage innovation, and accelerate technology-driven financial services across East Africa. It aligns with the East African Community (EAC) Cross-Border Payment System Masterplan, which seeks to create a common, efficient, and inclusive regional payment system.
A key objective of the agreement is to address regulatory fragmentation by ensuring that a license issued in one EAC country is recognized across member states, enabling broader access to cross-border financial services.
The BNR described the MoU as a significant step toward market growth, innovation, and digital financial integration, all under strict regulatory oversight. The Bank of Kenya reaffirmed its commitment to continued regional cooperation in the financial sector.

title: Rwandan Minister Warns Youth Against Drug Abuse, Links Responsibility to National Development
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda March 9, 2026 — Rwanda’s Minister of Youth and Arts Development, Jean Nepo Abdallah Utumatwishima, has urged young people to prioritize their health and avoid drug abuse, warning that substance addiction undermines both personal potential and national development.
title_en: Rwandan Minister Warns Youth Against Drug Abuse, Links Responsibility to National Development
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda March 9, 2026 — Rwanda’s Minister of Youth and Arts Development, Jean Nepo Abdallah Utumatwishima, has urged young people to prioritize their health and avoid drug abuse, warning that substance addiction undermines both personal potential and national development.
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda March 9, 2026 — Rwanda’s Minister of Youth and Arts Development, Jean Nepo Abdallah Utumatwishima, has urged young people to prioritize their health and avoid drug abuse, warning that substance addiction undermines both personal potential and national development.
Speaking at Lycée de Kigali during the launch of the third phase of the Ndi Umunyarwanda program, the minister stressed that Rwanda’s youth—who make up the majority of the population—are central to the country’s future and must act responsibly.
“The country needs you, and if you are found to be addicted to drugs at a young age, you have betrayed it,” he said, emphasizing the link between individual choices and national progress.
Utumatwishima warned that risky behaviors, including drug use and poor health decisions, could permanently limit young people’s ability to contribute to society.
He also highlighted unity as a core value of the Ndi Umunyarwanda program, urging students to reject divisive groups and instead promote solidarity.
“The first value is unity. We must avoid anything that separates us and instead build groups that bring us together,” he said.
As part of this effort, he noted that school-based clubs—such as those under AERG—have been merged with unity and solidarity groups to foster cohesion among students.
The Director General of the Rwanda Basic Education Board, Nelson Mbarushimana, said the program complements formal civic education by instilling values such as integrity, truth-telling, and responsibility among students.
“We want students who stand for truth, who can denounce wrongdoing, and who are committed to building the country,” he said.
Students attending the event said the program has helped deepen their understanding of Rwanda’s history and their role in addressing misinformation, particularly on social media.
Irakoze Cyusa Prince Louis, a final-year student, said the discussions equip them to challenge narratives that distort the country’s past.
“We are encouraged to confront those who rewrite history. With the knowledge we gain, we are able to respond and defend the truth,” he said.
Another student, Mugisha Falhat, noted that the program also enables young people to engage their families and peers in conversations about unity and the dangers of divisive ideologies.
Officials say Ndi Umunyarwanda remains a key platform for promoting national unity, civic responsibility, and resilience among Rwanda’s youth.

title: Equity Bank Rwanda Reassures Clients After Attempted Fraud Incident
excerpt: Kigali, 15 March 2026 – Equity Bank Rwanda Plc has reassured customers that their funds remain secure following an attempted fraud involving suspicious money transfer activities detected on 15 March 2026. In an official statement, the bank said its monitoring systems quickly iden
title_en: Equity Bank Rwanda Reassures Clients After Attempted Fraud Incident
excerpt_en: Kigali, 15 March 2026 – Equity Bank Rwanda Plc has reassured customers that their funds remain secure following an attempted fraud involving suspicious money transfer activities detected on 15 March 2026. In an official statement, the bank said its monitoring systems quickly iden
body_en:
Kigali, 15 March 2026 – Equity Bank Rwanda Plc has reassured customers that their funds remain secure following an attempted fraud involving suspicious money transfer activities detected on 15 March 2026.
In an official statement, the bank said its monitoring systems quickly identified unusual transactions, triggering immediate security protocols to contain the situation.
“Our systems continuously monitor irregular money transfers, and appropriate security measures were promptly activated,” the statement said.
The bank confirmed that swift intervention enabled the recovery of most of the targeted funds within 24 hours, while investigations continue in collaboration with relevant authorities, including the Central Bank of Rwanda and security agencies.
Equity Bank emphasized that no customer funds were lost, adding that all banking operations remain normal. “Customer accounts are fully protected, and services continue without disruption,” the bank stated.
Ongoing Investigation and Security Measures
The institution reiterated its zero-tolerance policy on financial crime, highlighting ongoing efforts to strengthen cybersecurity systems, enhance transaction monitoring, and reinforce internal controls.
Customers and stakeholders have also been encouraged to report any suspicious activities through the bank’s confidential whistleblowing channels, as part of broader efforts to maintain transparency and accountability.
Rising Cybersecurity Concerns
The incident comes amid growing concerns over cybercrime targeting financial institutions globally, prompting banks to invest heavily in advanced security technologies and closer cooperation with regulators.
Equity Bank Rwanda reaffirmed its commitment to protecting client assets and maintaining high standards of financial security as investigations into the attempted fraud continue.

According to a civil society organization operating in Ituri, 35 people were killed in Muchacha and 15 in Babesua between March 9 and 15. The attacks also involved the burning of multiple homes and widespread looting of property.
The violence has forced residents of several villages along the main RN4 road to flee to Mambasa and Niania centers, where they now live in precarious conditions, with agriculture and mining—the primary livelihoods in the region—disrupted.

“The DRC government should urgently address the security situation in Ituri, which undermines governance, and undertake extensive operations against the ADF while assisting the people of Mambasa who are in immediate danger,” a spokesperson said.
Reports, including those from the United Nations Office for the Coordination of Humanitarian Affairs (OCHA), confirm that the ADF remains the deadliest armed group in the country, responsible for the highest number of killings in the DRC.

title: DRC–Zambia–UNHCR: 9th Tripartite Commission Meeting on Refugee Repatriation
excerpt: Kolwezi, Lualaba – March 11, 2026 – The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), in coordination with the Congolese and Zambian authorities, convened the 9th meeting of the DRC–Zambia–UNHCR Tripartite Commission from March 10 to 12 in Kolwezi, the capital of Lualaba
title_en: DRC–Zambia–UNHCR: 9th Tripartite Commission Meeting on Refugee Repatriation
excerpt_en: Kolwezi, Lualaba – March 11, 2026 – The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), in coordination with the Congolese and Zambian authorities, convened the 9th meeting of the DRC–Zambia–UNHCR Tripartite Commission from March 10 to 12 in Kolwezi, the capital of Lualaba
body_en:
Kolwezi, Lualaba – March 11, 2026 – The United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), in coordination with the Congolese and Zambian authorities, convened the 9th meeting of the DRC–Zambia–UNHCR Tripartite Commission from March 10 to 12 in Kolwezi, the capital of Lualaba Province.
The meeting aims to promote voluntary repatriation of Congolese refugees in Zambia and Zambian refugees in the DRC, ensure security in return areas, and support the reintegration of returnees.
Governor Fifi Masuka emphasized that the discussions would strengthen cooperation and develop constructive guidelines for the benefit of the affected populations. Éric Mukandila, Permanent Secretary of the National Commission for Refugees (CNR), warned that ongoing armed conflicts, including the AFC-M23 rebellion, continue to displace populations both internally and across borders.
Pierre Atchom, UNHCR Representative in the DRC, highlighted that 11,523 Congolese refugees (3,150 households) were repatriated from Zambia between 2023 and 2025, reaffirming UNHCR’s commitment to supporting returns and reintegration.
The DRC is undertaking initiatives to monitor borders, strengthen community protection, rehabilitate schools and health centers, and promote economic empowerment through value chains, contributing to peace and food security.
The meeting will culminate in the adoption of a response plan to facilitate the large-scale return of refugees, in accordance with the 1951 Convention relating to the Status of Refugees and the principle of non-refoulement.

title: Landslide at Safi Mine in Lualaba Kills at Least 10 Artisanal Miners
excerpt: Kakanda, Lualaba March 13, 2026 – At least ten artisanal miners have died and one person injured following a landslide at the Safi mining site near Kakanda in Lualaba’s Lubudi territory. Rescue teams also recovered the body of a child, approximately 13 years old, from the debris.
title_en: Landslide at Safi Mine in Lualaba Kills at Least 10 Artisanal Miners
excerpt_en: Kakanda, Lualaba March 13, 2026 – At least ten artisanal miners have died and one person injured following a landslide at the Safi mining site near Kakanda in Lualaba’s Lubudi territory. Rescue teams also recovered the body of a child, approximately 13 years old, from the debris.
body_en:
Kakanda, Lualaba March 13, 2026 – At least ten artisanal miners have died and one person injured following a landslide at the Safi mining site near Kakanda in Lualaba’s Lubudi territory. Rescue teams also recovered the body of a child, approximately 13 years old, from the debris.
Authorities have recommended the immediate suspension of mining activities in the affected area and a technical assessment of the unstable quarry sections. The landslide occurred in a pit where miners were working early in the morning, exposing unsafe mining conditions.
A technical review identified several factors contributing to the disaster, including excessively high slabs of up to 37 meters (compared to the recommended five meters), fragile sandy-clay soil, dangerously steep slopes reaching 70–80 degrees, and the absence of proper drainage. These conditions indicate a lack of proper oversight in the artisanal operations.
The Safi site, part of the Boss Mining company’s permit, allows artisanal miners to operate in specific areas under strict agreements with local cooperatives. However, the cooperative involved had not received formal approval for technical operations, raising questions about the legality of the work conducted.
Officials have also called for the withdrawal of military personnel overseeing miners, suggesting that the Mines and Hydrocarbons Police take over supervision. The affected area remains closed while safety assessments and security measures are implemented.
The tragedy highlights ongoing safety challenges in unregulated artisanal mining and the urgent need for stronger oversight and compliance with mining standards.

title: HRW Documents Missing Opposition Members in CNC Detention Centers
excerpt: DRC March 11, 2026 — Human Rights Watch has documented 17 cases of disappeared individuals, mostly opposition figures, reportedly detained on questionable grounds or accused of supporting the AFC/M23 rebel group. The organization is calling on Kinshasa authorities to account for
title_en: HRW Documents Missing Opposition Members in CNC Detention Centers
excerpt_en: DRC March 11, 2026 — Human Rights Watch has documented 17 cases of disappeared individuals, mostly opposition figures, reportedly detained on questionable grounds or accused of supporting the AFC/M23 rebel group. The organization is calling on Kinshasa authorities to account for
body_en:
DRC March 11, 2026 — Human Rights Watch has documented 17 cases of disappeared individuals, mostly opposition figures, reportedly detained on questionable grounds or accused of supporting the AFC/M23 rebel group. The organization is calling on Kinshasa authorities to account for the missing or, preferably, bring them before a judge.
According to HRW, the National Cyber Defense Council (CNC)—a body attached to the Presidency of the Republic—has been used since March 2025 to arrest and detain political opponents arbitrarily through Congolese security forces.
“Over the past year, Congolese security forces have secretly arrested and detained people on trumped-up charges in the heart of the capital,” said Lewis Mudge, Central Africa director at HRW. “In most cases, the arrests appear to be politically motivated or involve individuals suspected of supporting armed groups in eastern DRC.”
HRW reached its conclusions after contacting 34 individuals, including nine former CNC detainees and 11 relatives. Accounts describe arrests conducted by uniformed Republican Guard and National Police officers, as well as plainclothes personnel, often at night. Several detainees reported being blindfolded during transport to or between CNC detention centers, without being shown any arrest warrants.
Detentions reportedly began at facilities within the Stade des Martyrs or CNC offices at the National Transport Office (ONATRA) in Kinshasa, before transferring detainees to other secret locations, including private rooms or hotels. Interrogations focused on alleged collusion with AFC/M23 rebels, rather than cyber-related offenses.
HRW also accuses the CNC of expanding its powers through arrests, interrogations, and secret detentions without judicial oversight.
Between December 2025 and January 2026, opposition members, including loyalists of former President Joseph Kabila, were arrested at night in their homes. Many went missing, while others were later found in CNC facilities before transfer to judicial authorities. Some high-profile figures, such as Emmanuel Ramazani Shadary and Aubin Minaku, both former leaders of the ruling PPRD party, were reportedly held in secret.
This report underscores growing concerns over political repression, arbitrary detention, and the lack of judicial oversight in Kinshasa, raising alarms about the treatment of opposition members amid the ongoing eastern DRC conflict.

title: FARDC Recaptures Mukole After Clashes with AFC/M23 Rebels
excerpt: Walikale March 10, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), backed by the Wazalendo militia, has regained control of the strategic position of Mukole, located in the Balindu area of Walikale Territory, following fierce fighting against AFC/M23 rebels.
title_en: FARDC Recaptures Mukole After Clashes with AFC/M23 Rebels
excerpt_en: Walikale March 10, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), backed by the Wazalendo militia, has regained control of the strategic position of Mukole, located in the Balindu area of Walikale Territory, following fierce fighting against AFC/M23 rebels.
body_en:
Walikale March 10, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), backed by the Wazalendo militia, has regained control of the strategic position of Mukole, located in the Balindu area of Walikale Territory, following fierce fighting against AFC/M23 rebels.
The clashes, which took place on Monday, March 9, were part of a targeted offensive by government-aligned forces to reclaim the area, which had been under rebel occupation for several days. The operation resulted in the recapture of Mukole, marking another shift in the evolving security dynamics in North Kivu.
Following the confrontation, AFC/M23 fighters reportedly withdrew toward Ihula, a locality situated along the border between Walikale and Rutshuru Territory.
The fighting left several casualties, including at least three reported deaths among the rebels, with injuries recorded on both sides.
The violence also triggered civilian displacement, as residents fled into nearby bush areas to escape the hostilities. As of Tuesday morning, a fragile calm had returned to Mukole, although many inhabitants remain in temporary refuge, uncertain about their safety.
The recapture of Mukole provides FARDC and allied forces with a key strategic advantage, enabling them to monitor surrounding areas, including Ihula and Kalonge in Walikale, as well as Kalembe in neighboring Masisi Territory—areas that remain under AFC/M23 control.

title_en: AFC/M23 Rebels Reinforce Positions in Kashebere and Kibati
excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu March 16, 2026 – The security situation in Walikale territory remains particularly worrying as AFC/M23 rebels have reinforced their positions in Kashebere and Kibati, both located in the Luberike group. Trucks carrying reinforcements of fighters and ammunitio
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu March 16, 2026 – The security situation in Walikale territory remains particularly worrying as AFC/M23 rebels have reinforced their positions in Kashebere and Kibati, both located in the Luberike group.
Trucks carrying reinforcements of fighters and ammunition arrived in Kashebere on the night of March 15. Following their arrival, these forces moved toward Kibati to consolidate control over this strategic part of the territory.
These movements come days after clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and the FARDC, supported by Wazalendo, in Mikumbi. Analysts warn that the reinforcements may signal preparations for new offensives, as tensions remain high in the region.
Recent fighting has also disrupted traffic on the Mungazi-Kashebere road, a vital route for population movement and transport of goods. Local residents continue to live in fear of imminent clashes, amid ongoing civilian displacement and persistent instability in parts of North Kivu.

title: Government Announces New Measures to Tackle Rising Insecurity in Kinshasa
excerpt: Kinshasa March 22, 2026 – The government has unveiled a series of measures to address the resurgence of insecurity, crime, and robberies in the capital, Kinshasa, amid growing public concern. The announcement was made by Deputy Prime Minister Jacquemain Shabani during the 83rd Co
title_en: Government Announces New Measures to Tackle Rising Insecurity in Kinshasa
excerpt_en: Kinshasa March 22, 2026 – The government has unveiled a series of measures to address the resurgence of insecurity, crime, and robberies in the capital, Kinshasa, amid growing public concern. The announcement was made by Deputy Prime Minister Jacquemain Shabani during the 83rd Co
body_en:
Kinshasa March 22, 2026 – The government has unveiled a series of measures to address the resurgence of insecurity, crime, and robberies in the capital, Kinshasa, amid growing public concern.
The announcement was made by Deputy Prime Minister Jacquemain Shabani during the 83rd Council of Ministers meeting. He confirmed that a high-level security meeting had been held on March 14, bringing together civilian, police, and military authorities to coordinate a response.
Key decisions include the intensification of arrests targeting criminal networks, particularly those involved in staged kidnappings, and the continuation of Operation “Ndobo”, which involves joint PNC-FARDC patrols to combat the Kuluna phenomenon.
Authorities also plan to convene inter-institutional meetings to address crimes involving men in uniform, as well as tighten oversight in the telecommunications sector, including a potential ban on pre-registered SIM cards and the re-identification of subscribers.
Despite ongoing operations, Kinshasa continues to face a rise in kidnappings and nighttime attacks, with many residents reporting little improvement in daily security.
President Félix Tshisekedi has acknowledged public concern, warning that these crimes are fueling a climate of fear, undermining state authority, and eroding public trust in security institutions. He has instructed security services to intensify operations to dismantle criminal networks responsible for kidnappings and armed robberies.

title: Rwanda Continues Efforts to Finalize Border Demarcation with Neighbors
excerpt: Kigali, 13 March 2026 – Rwanda is continuing a long-standing process to confirm its official borders with neighboring countries, more than two decades after the initiative was first launched, the Ministry of Environment has said. Speaking before Parliament, Minister of Environmen
title_en: Rwanda Continues Efforts to Finalize Border Demarcation with Neighbors
excerpt_en: Kigali, 13 March 2026 – Rwanda is continuing a long-standing process to confirm its official borders with neighboring countries, more than two decades after the initiative was first launched, the Ministry of Environment has said. Speaking before Parliament, Minister of Environmen
body_en:
Kigali, 13 March 2026 – Rwanda is continuing a long-standing process to confirm its official borders with neighboring countries, more than two decades after the initiative was first launched, the Ministry of Environment has said.
Speaking before Parliament, Minister of Environment Dr. Bernadette Arap explained that the process began in 2000, when the Cabinet approved the creation of a national commission to oversee border negotiations and demarcation with neighboring states. The commission officially started work in February 2001, supported by a technical team.
“Significant progress has been made, including demarcation work with the Democratic Republic of Congo and Uganda,” the Minister said. However, she noted that the process remains incomplete, as some borders have not yet been formally approved by all parties involved.
As a precaution, during the national land registration program (2009–2013), authorities instructed residents living within 200 meters of international borders not to register their land, in order to avoid potential disputes. As a result, some land in these areas remains unregistered to date.
Negotiations are ongoing. Recent engagements include meetings with Tanzania and a February 2025 session with Uganda, where both sides agreed to resume border demarcation efforts.
Land Boundary Disputes Persist
In addition to international borders, Rwanda is also addressing internal land boundary discrepancies identified during the nationwide land registration process.
Minister Arap revealed that 222,423 land plots have already been corrected, while efforts continue to resolve outstanding cases across 582 villages. Challenges included unclear boundaries due to terrain such as forests, pastures, and farmland, as well as instances where landowners were absent during the initial mapping.
To address this, authorities are now using modern mapping technologies to finalize corrections, with the goal of completing the process within the year.
The government is working with development partners to support boundary corrections in districts such as Kirehe, Nyagatare, and Kayonza, with plans to expand the effort to 10 additional districts.
Officials noted that while some residents can hire private land surveyors, others are being supported through local administrative structures to ensure fair representation and resolution.
The ongoing efforts reflect Rwanda’s commitment to clarifying territorial boundaries, strengthening land governance, and preventing future disputes both domestically and across its borders.

title: Rwanda Earns Over Rwf236.8 Billion from Tourism in Three Months
excerpt: Kigali, March 12, 2026 — Rwanda generated more than Rwf236.8 billion (approximately $161.5 million) in tourism revenue over a three-month period from November 2025 to January 2026, according to data from the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda. The figures highlight touris
title_en: Rwanda Earns Over Rwf236.8 Billion from Tourism in Three Months
excerpt_en: Kigali, March 12, 2026 — Rwanda generated more than Rwf236.8 billion (approximately $161.5 million) in tourism revenue over a three-month period from November 2025 to January 2026, according to data from the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda. The figures highlight touris
body_en:
Kigali, March 12, 2026 — Rwanda generated more than Rwf236.8 billion (approximately $161.5 million) in tourism revenue over a three-month period from November 2025 to January 2026, according to data from the National Institute of Statistics of Rwanda.
The figures highlight tourism as a key driver of the country’s economy, with significant contributions from both air and land arrivals. Visitors entering Rwanda by air accounted for the largest share of revenue, generating $136.7 million. Leisure travelers, including those visiting for holidays and tourism activities, contributed more than $65 million, with gorilla tourism alone accounting for at least 71.4% of that segment.
Regionally, visitors from North America were the top contributors, generating $40.8 million. This performance is partly attributed to Rwanda’s strategic international marketing efforts, including partnerships with major U.S. sports teams such as the Los Angeles Clippers and the Los Angeles Rams under the “Visit Rwanda” campaign. The initiative builds on earlier collaborations with European football clubs including Arsenal FC, Paris Saint-Germain, and FC Bayern Munich.
These partnerships aim to boost Rwanda’s global visibility and attract high-value tourists and investors, particularly from the United States, a major source market for international travel.
Land border entries also contributed to tourism earnings, generating $24.9 million, largely from visitors traveling for family and social purposes. Most land arrivals came through key border points linking Rwanda with neighboring countries including Uganda, Democratic Republic of the Congo, and Tanzania.
The report further indicates that Rwandans traveling abroad spent over $95.9 million during the same period, with air travelers accounting for the largest share of expenditures. Countries within the East African Community remained the primary destinations.
Education emerged as a leading reason for travel, both for visitors entering Rwanda and Rwandans traveling abroad, with students typically recording the longest stays.
Tourism remains a cornerstone of Rwanda’s economic strategy. In 2024, the country welcomed 1.36 million international visitors, generating $647 million in revenue. Authorities are now targeting $1 billion in annual tourism revenue by 2029, as part of broader efforts to expand the sector and strengthen its contribution to national growth.

title: Rwanda Aims to Place Primary Health Centers in Schools and Markets

title_en: Rwanda Aims to Place Primary Health Centers in Schools and Markets
excerpt_en: Kigali, 19 March 2026 – The Ministry of Health (MINISANTE) announced plans to establish primary health centers in schools and crowded public spaces, including markets, to provide timely medical care to students and residents. Minister of Health, Dr. Sabin Nsanzimana, emphasized t
body_en:
Kigali, 19 March 2026 – The Ministry of Health (MINISANTE) announced plans to establish primary health centers in schools and crowded public spaces, including markets, to provide timely medical care to students and residents.
Minister of Health, Dr. Sabin Nsanzimana, emphasized that while some schools have medical facilities, they often lack trained personnel. The new initiative will help address injuries, infectious diseases, and mental health needs directly at schools and busy public areas.
Dr. Nsanzimana also highlighted Rwanda’s ongoing program to train nurses in secondary schools, projecting that by 2028, over 3,000 secondary-school-trained nurses will graduate. This initiative aims to strengthen healthcare delivery across clinics, schools, and local communities.
“Having a large number of trained nurses will ensure sufficient staff where they are most needed,” said Dr. Nsanzimana, noting that the program is part of a broader effort to quadruple Rwanda’s healthcare workforce.
The Ministry continues to receive requests from educational institutions to offer nursing programs, reflecting growing demand for skilled healthcare professionals in the country.

excerpt: Goma, 14 March 2026 – The CNVDP-WAZ coalition, associated with the Wazalendo armed groups in the Democratic Republic of Congo, has expelled Member of Parliament Willy Mishiki Buhini after he publicly admitted involvement in a recent attack on Goma. Mishiki, who represented Walika
title_en: Wazalendo Expels MP Willy Mishiki After Goma Attack Admission
excerpt_en: Goma, 14 March 2026 – The CNVDP-WAZ coalition, associated with the Wazalendo armed groups in the Democratic Republic of Congo, has expelled Member of Parliament Willy Mishiki Buhini after he publicly admitted involvement in a recent attack on Goma. Mishiki, who represented Walika
body_en:
Goma, 14 March 2026 – The CNVDP-WAZ coalition, associated with the Wazalendo armed groups in the Democratic Republic of Congo, has expelled Member of Parliament Willy Mishiki Buhini after he publicly admitted involvement in a recent attack on Goma.
Mishiki, who represented Walikale territory in the DRC Parliament and served as President of the Council of Experts within the coalition, made the remarks during an interview with TV5 Monde on 11 March 2026.
In the interview, he stated that Wazalendo forces were fighting in Virunga National Park and had advanced to Nyiragongo, just a few kilometers from Goma, with the objective of retaking the city. He also acknowledged responsibility for the drone attack carried out in Goma in the early hours of 11 March, which killed three civilians, including French national Karine Buisset, an employee of UNICEF.
“We are fighting to retake Goma… that is the reason for this attack,” Mishiki said.
Following the statement, the CNVDP-WAZ leadership announced on 13 March that Mishiki had acted without consultation and had escalated tensions through his remarks. As a result, he was removed from his position and stripped of membership, with Katulanya Jacques appointed as his replacement.
Reacting to the development, Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, said that dismissing Mishiki does not negate his admission. “You cannot erase a confession, especially when it is supported by evidence,” he stated.
Meanwhile, the French government has announced an investigation into the attack that killed one of its nationals.
The AFC/M23 coalition has also weighed in, alleging that the attack was carried out by DRC government forces, claiming it targeted political and military figures including Joseph Kabila, Corneille Nangaa, Bertrand Bisimwa, Freddy Kaniki, and Gen. Maj. Sultani Makenga.
The incident underscores the complex and contested narratives surrounding the ongoing conflict in eastern DRC, particularly in and around Goma, where multiple armed groups and political actors remain active.

title: AFC/M23 Denies Rumors of Withdrawal from Bukavu
excerpt: Bukavu, South Kivu, March 21, 2026 — The rebel coalition AFC/M23 has dismissed circulating reports claiming it plans to leave the city of Bukavu, calling them fabricated and politically motivated. The rumors, widely shared on social media, cited a statement from Bertrand Bisimwa,
title_en: AFC/M23 Denies Rumors of Withdrawal from Bukavu
excerpt_en: Bukavu, South Kivu, March 21, 2026 — The rebel coalition AFC/M23 has dismissed circulating reports claiming it plans to leave the city of Bukavu, calling them fabricated and politically motivated. The rumors, widely shared on social media, cited a statement from Bertrand Bisimwa,
body_en:
Bukavu, South Kivu, March 21, 2026 — The rebel coalition AFC/M23 has dismissed circulating reports claiming it plans to leave the city of Bukavu, calling them fabricated and politically motivated.
The rumors, widely shared on social media, cited a statement from Bertrand Bisimwa, the coalition’s Deputy Director for Political Affairs, suggesting that the group intended to withdraw from Bukavu to pave the way for lasting peace.
Responding on March 21, AFC/M23 spokesman Lawrence Kanyuka described the statement as false, alleging it was circulated by the Democratic Republic of Congo government to divert attention from a recent attack in Goma.
Kanyuka emphasized that no false narrative could erase the memory of the March 11, 2026, attack in which French national Karine Buisset, employed by the United Nations Children’s Fund (UNICEF), was killed.
AFC/M23 seized control of Bukavu in February 2025. Speculation about a potential withdrawal has grown since the coalition pulled out of Uvira in January 2026, but the group insists its position in Bukavu remains unchanged.

excerpt_en: Washington, D.C. March 19, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda have agreed on concrete measures to de-escalate tensions in eastern DRC, following talks held on March 17–18 in the United States capital. The announcement was made in a joint statement with the United
body_en:
Washington, D.C. March 19, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo and Rwanda have agreed on concrete measures to de-escalate tensions in eastern DRC, following talks held on March 17–18 in the United States capital. The announcement was made in a joint statement with the United States.
The agreement outlines coordinated actions, including respect for sovereignty and territorial integrity, the planned withdrawal of Rwandan forces, and the lifting of certain defensive measures in eastern DRC. title: Middle East Conflict Paralyzes Gold Trade in North Kivu
excerpt: Butembo, North Kivu – March 12, 2026 – The war between the US-Israeli coalition and Iran is disrupting North Kivu’s gold market, leaving traders and miners struggling. Butembo, the main trading hub for artisanal gold from North Kivu and neighboring provinces, has seen a sharp slo
title_en: Middle East Conflict Paralyzes Gold Trade in North Kivu
excerpt_en: Butembo, North Kivu – March 12, 2026 – The war between the US-Israeli coalition and Iran is disrupting North Kivu’s gold market, leaving traders and miners struggling. Butembo, the main trading hub for artisanal gold from North Kivu and neighboring provinces, has seen a sharp slo
body_en:
Butembo, North Kivu – March 12, 2026 – The war between the US-Israeli coalition and Iran is disrupting North Kivu’s gold market, leaving traders and miners struggling. Butembo, the main trading hub for artisanal gold from North Kivu and neighboring provinces, has seen a sharp slowdown in operations as Dubai—the key destination for the region’s gold—reduces its purchases.
The crisis has left local gold buying offices short on cash and dependent on credit. Merchants who usually travel to Dubai to purchase goods have suspended their trips, further tightening the flow of funds in the region.
Artisanal miners are paying the heaviest price. In Manguredjipa, the price of gold per gram has fallen from $178 to between $90 and $100 since the outbreak of the conflict. The collapse in prices is severely affecting communities that rely almost entirely on artisanal mining for their livelihoods.
The disruption highlights the vulnerability of North Kivu’s gold trade, which depends heavily on international markets, and shows how geopolitical crises abroad can have immediate, devastating effects on local economies.

Mitsamiouli, Comoros March 20, 2026 – Sixteen Congolese nationals were among the victims of a shipwreck off the coast of Mitsamiouli, Comoros, on March 18, local authorities reported.
The official list released by Comorian authorities confirms 18 deaths in total, including two Burundians, while a separate statement from the Civil Security Directorate General indicated that the boat, carrying migrants from the East African coast, had capsized at sea.
The provisional report notes 12 confirmed dead, 12 missing, and 30 survivors, who are currently receiving treatment at Mitsamiouli hospital.
Rescue operations are ongoing, with Comorian authorities cautioning about the dangers of irregular sea crossings.

excerpt: Masisi March 10, 2026 — The strategic town of Kazinga, located in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi Territory, has returned to the control of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) following a military offensive conducted on Monday, March 9. According to lo
title_en: FARDC Recaptures Kazinga After Two Weeks of Rebel Occupation
excerpt_en: Masisi March 10, 2026 — The strategic town of Kazinga, located in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi Territory, has returned to the control of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) following a military offensive conducted on Monday, March 9. According to lo
body_en:
Masisi March 10, 2026 — The strategic town of Kazinga, located in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi Territory, has returned to the control of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) following a military offensive conducted on Monday, March 9.
According to local sources, the town had been under AFC/M23 rebel occupation for nearly two weeks before being retaken by government forces, supported by the Wazalendo militia, in a coordinated operation aimed at reasserting state authority in the area.
The offensive triggered intense fighting, with both heavy and light weapons used throughout the day. By evening, however, the situation had stabilized, and a relative calm returned to the town.
The clashes forced many civilians to flee into surrounding bush areas, where they are now facing dire humanitarian conditions, including lack of shelter, food, and access to basic services.
The recapture of Kazinga follows recent rebel withdrawals from nearby localities, including Buabo and Ndete, signaling a possible shift in territorial dynamics in parts of North Kivu.
Regarded as a strategic position within the Osso Banyungu sector, Kazinga’s return to government control strengthens the military foothold of loyalist forces and reinforces their presence in this volatile region of eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

title_en: Wazalendo Retake Malemo Village After Fierce Fighting Against AFC/M23
excerpt_en: Masisi, North Kivu March 16, 2026 – The village of Malemo, in the Bashali Mokoto group, was recaptured by the Wazalendo on Saturday, March 14, following fierce fighting against AFC/M23 rebels. Clashes began early in the morning and continued throughout the day along the Kalembe-M
body_en:
Masisi, North Kivu March 16, 2026 – The village of Malemo, in the Bashali Mokoto group, was recaptured by the Wazalendo on Saturday, March 14, following fierce fighting against AFC/M23 rebels.
Clashes began early in the morning and continued throughout the day along the Kalembe-Mpety axis, a strategic corridor linking Masisi to Walikale territory. By early evening, Wazalendo forces succeeded in dislodging the rebels from the village. Some AFC/M23 fighters retreated toward Kalembe, while others moved to Mindjendje and Mpety in Kisimba.
The recapture of Malemo is strategically significant, as it severs the link between Kalembe and Mpety, one of the main strongholds and logistical centers of the AFC/M23 in the Pinga region.
These clashes follow intense fighting reported 24 hours earlier in Kashuga, also in Bashali Mokoto, where the Wazalendo withdrew, leaving control to the AFC/M23 rebels.
The security situation remains highly volatile across several villages in Masisi and Walikale, with ongoing troop movements and clashes fueling civilian anxiety.

body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu – March 22, 2026 – Violent clashes broke out early Sunday in the village of Kanune, in the Ikobo area, between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters.
Hostilities began around 5:00 AM, when the Wazalendo launched an offensive on rebel positions. Since then, sustained heavy and light weapons fire has gripped the area, spreading fear among residents.
The civilian population remains confined indoors, fearing stray bullets and the intensity of the fighting. No official information has yet been released regarding casualties or damage.
The Ikobo area, under AFC/M23 control for nearly a year, has seen a volatile security situation, with recent reinforcements reported in nearby localities, particularly toward Kisimba. Analysts suggest these movements may have weakened some rebel positions, prompting the current Wazalendo attempt to retake the territory.
The situation remains fluid, raising serious concerns for the safety of civilians in a region already affected by prolonged conflict.

title: Investor Abdul Samad Rabiu Praises President Kagame’s Leadership
excerpt: Kigali, 13 March 2026 – Abdul Samad Rabiu, one of Africa’s wealthiest investors, has praised President Paul Kagame for his visionary leadership and commitment to Rwanda’s development, calling him an example for Africa and beyond. Rabiu made the remarks following talks with Presid
title_en: Investor Abdul Samad Rabiu Praises President Kagame’s Leadership
excerpt_en: Kigali, 13 March 2026 – Abdul Samad Rabiu, one of Africa’s wealthiest investors, has praised President Paul Kagame for his visionary leadership and commitment to Rwanda’s development, calling him an example for Africa and beyond. Rabiu made the remarks following talks with Presid
body_en:
Kigali, 13 March 2026 – Abdul Samad Rabiu, one of Africa’s wealthiest investors, has praised President Paul Kagame for his visionary leadership and commitment to Rwanda’s development, calling him an example for Africa and beyond.
Rabiu made the remarks following talks with President Kagame at an international conference on civilian nuclear energy, which brought together heads of state, government officials, and energy experts.
“His visionary leadership, commitment to development, and determination to advance Rwanda continue to serve as an example for Africa and beyond. President Kagame is a great example of leaders dedicated to Africa’s future and the continent’s opportunities,” Rabiu said.
President Kagame, who served as Head of Institutional Reforms of the African Union from 2016 to 2024, strengthened the organization’s functionality and economic stability, including the revival of the Peace Fund, which has raised $400 million.
Under Kagame’s leadership, Rwanda has become one of the fastest-growing economies in Africa, maintaining annual growth rates of over 8%. Poverty has significantly declined due to targeted programs, with the Seventh Rwandan Population and Housing Survey (EICV7) showing poverty falling from 39.8% in 2017 to 27.4% in 2024, and extreme poverty dropping from 11.3% to 5.4%.
Rabiu highlighted that these achievements reflect good governance that prioritizes the people and positions Rwanda as a model for sustainable development on the continent.

title: Rwanda Warns Against Repeating “Mistakes of 1994” Over Violence in Eastern DRC
excerpt: Kigali March 23, 2026 – Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Olivier Nduhungirehe, has called on the international community to act decisively to prevent atrocities in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, warning against a repeat of the failures that led to the
title_en: Rwanda Warns Against Repeating “Mistakes of 1994” Over Violence in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: Kigali March 23, 2026 – Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Olivier Nduhungirehe, has called on the international community to act decisively to prevent atrocities in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, warning against a repeat of the failures that led to the
body_en:
Kigali March 23, 2026 – Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Olivier Nduhungirehe, has called on the international community to act decisively to prevent atrocities in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, warning against a repeat of the failures that led to the Genocide against the Tutsi.
Speaking at an international conference focused on remembrance, reconciliation, and reconstruction, Nduhungirehe emphasized the need to draw lessons from past tragedies to address current risks. He pointed to ongoing violence in eastern DRC, alleging that communities, particularly Tutsi populations including the Banyamulenge, are being targeted.
“In the east of the Democratic Republic of Congo, those driven by an ideology targeting Tutsi communities continue to perpetrate violence, killings, and displacement,” he said.
The minister warned that silence in the face of such warning signs amounts to complicity, urging the international community to respond before the situation escalates further. “We must bring this to light. Remaining silent when such signs are visible is complicity,” he stated.
Nduhungirehe also referenced previous global commitments made after major atrocities, including the Holocaust, noting that despite the pledge of “never again,” similar tragedies have occurred.
He further linked the current situation in eastern DRC to the aftermath of the 1994 genocide, particularly the presence of armed groups such as the FDLR, which Rwanda accuses of perpetuating violence in the region.
According to Kigali, attacks against Kinyarwanda-speaking Congolese communities continue, with allegations that multiple armed actors are involved. Rwanda has repeatedly called on the international community to acknowledge and respond to these developments, arguing that early warning signs should not be ignored.
These remarks come amid ongoing tensions between Rwanda and the DRC, with Kinshasa accusing Kigali of supporting the AFC/M23 rebellion—an allegation Rwanda denies—further complicating efforts to stabilize the region.

“In the east of the Democratic Republic of Congo, those driven by an ideology targeting Tutsi communities continue to perpetrate violence, killings, and displacement,” he said.
The minister warned that silence in the face of such warning signs amounts to complicity, urging the international community to respond before the situation escalates further. “We must bring this to light. Remaining silent when such signs are visible is complicity,” he stated.
Nduhungirehe also referenced previous global commitments made after major atrocities, including the Holocaust, noting that despite the pledge of “never again,” similar tragedies have occurred.
He further linked the current situation in eastern DRC to the aftermath of the 1994 genocide, particularly the presence of armed groups such as the FDLR, which Rwanda accuses of perpetuating violence in the region.
According to Kigali, attacks against Kinyarwanda-speaking Congolese communities continue, with allegations that multiple armed actors are involved. Rwanda has repeatedly called on the international community to acknowledge and respond to these developments, arguing that early warning signs should not be ignored.
These remarks come amid ongoing tensions between Rwanda and the DRC, with Kinshasa accusing Kigali of supporting the AFC/M23 rebellion—an allegation Rwanda denies—further complicating efforts to stabilize the region.

title: Rwanda, United States Explore Expanded Healthcare Cooperation

title_en: Rwanda, United States Explore Expanded Healthcare Cooperation
excerpt_en: Kigali/Washington, March 12, 2026 — Rwanda’s Minister of Health, Sabin Nsanzimana, has held a series of high-level discussions in the United States aimed at strengthening collaboration between American and Rwandan healthcare institutions. During a visit to Ohio, the minister met
body_en:
Kigali/Washington, March 12, 2026 — Rwanda’s Minister of Health, Sabin Nsanzimana, has held a series of high-level discussions in the United States aimed at strengthening collaboration between American and Rwandan healthcare institutions.
During a visit to Ohio, the minister met with Tomislav Mihaljevic, Chief Executive Officer of the Cleveland Clinic, to explore potential partnerships that could enhance healthcare delivery and medical expertise in Rwanda. The talks focused on how leading U.S. medical institutions could support Rwanda’s health system through knowledge exchange and institutional collaboration.
In a separate meeting, Nsanzimana held discussions with Marcello Fantoni, Director of International Relations at Kent State University. The two sides examined opportunities for academic cooperation, particularly in research and the expansion of study opportunities for Rwandan students in the United States.
The minister also met with Jeff Graham at the United States Department of State in Washington, DC, where discussions centered on global health security and bilateral cooperation. Key areas included the implementation of the Rwanda–U.S. Health Partnership Agreement.
The agreement, valued at $228 million, is designed to support Rwanda’s healthcare sector, with a significant portion allocated to combating HIV/AIDS, malaria, and other communicable diseases, as well as strengthening disease surveillance and outbreak preparedness.
Under the partnership, the United States is expected to contribute $158 million over the next five years, while Rwanda plans to increase its own health investment by up to $70 million to further improve national healthcare systems.

title: Rwandan Troops Win Hearts in Jamaica After Post-Cyclone Reconstruction Effort

title_en: Rwandan Troops Win Hearts in Jamaica After Post-Cyclone Reconstruction Effort
excerpt_en: Montego Bay, Jamaica, 13 March 2026 – The Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) has concluded a 60-day humanitarian mission in Montego Bay, leaving a lasting impact on communities devastated by Cyclone Melissa. Deployed in collaboration with the Jamaican Defence Force (JDF), a contingent of
body_en:
Montego Bay, Jamaica, 13 March 2026 – The Rwanda Defence Force (RDF) has concluded a 60-day humanitarian mission in Montego Bay, leaving a lasting impact on communities devastated by Cyclone Melissa.
Deployed in collaboration with the Jamaican Defence Force (JDF), a contingent of 100 Rwandan soldiers worked to repair and rebuild damaged infrastructure in St James Province, following a disaster that claimed 45 lives and caused destruction equivalent to 45% of Jamaica’s GDP.
Many residents, encountering Rwanda for the first time, expressed deep gratitude for the support. “You came all the way from Africa to help us. I thank you from the bottom of my heart,” said one local resident. Another added, “I didn’t know how I would rebuild, but what you have done is incredible. God bless you.”
The Chief of the Jamaican Armed Forces, Vice Admiral Antonette Wemyss-Gorman, praised the RDF soldiers for their professionalism and discipline. “They are dedicated, efficient, and true professionals. In just two months, they have achieved a great deal and built strong ties with the community,” she said, noting the absence of any misconduct during their deployment.
She also emphasized the importance of strengthening bilateral relations between Rwanda and Jamaica, highlighting that the support provided would not be forgotten.
Colonel Moses Kayigamba, head of the RDF contingent, said Rwanda’s commitment to humanitarian action is rooted in its own history. “We take any suffering as our own,” he stated, referencing the country’s past and its determination to assist others in times of need.
The mission followed the devastating cyclone that struck Jamaica on October 28, 2025, with winds reaching 298 km/h, severely impacting St Elizabeth and Black River regions. According to humanitarian data, the disaster damaged 450 schools and over 120,000 homes, affecting 626,000 people, with hundreds left homeless.
The RDF’s intervention has been widely seen as a symbol of solidarity and international cooperation, reinforcing Rwanda’s growing role in global humanitarian and peace support operations.

title: Mob Killing in Kyankwanzi After Discovery of Human Remains Sparks Fear
excerpt: Kyankwanzi District Uganda, March 21, 2026 — Tensions are high in central Uganda’s Kyankwanzi District after two men suspected to be Rwandan nationals were killed by an angry mob following the discovery of human body parts in their home. The incident occurred on March 20 in Kirya
title_en: Mob Killing in Kyankwanzi After Discovery of Human Remains Sparks Fear
excerpt_en: Kyankwanzi District Uganda, March 21, 2026 — Tensions are high in central Uganda’s Kyankwanzi District after two men suspected to be Rwandan nationals were killed by an angry mob following the discovery of human body parts in their home. The incident occurred on March 20 in Kirya
body_en:
Kyankwanzi District Uganda, March 21, 2026 — Tensions are high in central Uganda’s Kyankwanzi District after two men suspected to be Rwandan nationals were killed by an angry mob following the discovery of human body parts in their home.
The incident occurred on March 20 in Kiryanongo village, Bananywa, where residents reportedly forced their way into the house of the two men, identified as Semasaka and Hakiza Damascene, after noticing a strong, foul odor coming from the premises.
According to local accounts, villagers conducted a search of the house and discovered dismembered body parts believed to belong to a woman from Nakabugo village who had been reported missing several days earlier. Some of the remains were allegedly found in a bag inside the residence.
The discovery triggered outrage among residents, who then turned on the two men, beating them to death before authorities could intervene.
Local leaders alerted police shortly after the killings. Officers from Bananywa Police Station, along with district-level investigators, were deployed to the scene to begin inquiries into both the suspected murder and the mob violence.
Luke Kigozi, the police spokesperson for Wamala Region, condemned the incident, stressing that the law must take its course.
He confirmed that investigations are underway into the circumstances surrounding the woman’s death, as well as the mob action that led to the killing of the two suspects.
The bodies of the two men and the deceased woman have been transported to Ntwetwe Health Center for post-mortem examinations as part of the ongoing investigation.
Authorities have urged residents to refrain from taking justice into their own hands, warning that such actions undermine the rule of law and complicate criminal investigations.

title: UN Security Council to Hold Closed-Door Meeting After Deadly Drone Attack in Goma
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC March 16, 2026 – The UN Security Council will hold closed-door consultations on Tuesday to discuss the escalating conflict in eastern DRC, following a deadly drone attack in Goma on March 11, which killed a UNICEF staff member. The meeting was requested by France. S
title_en: UN Security Council to Hold Closed-Door Meeting After Deadly Drone Attack in Goma
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC March 16, 2026 – The UN Security Council will hold closed-door consultations on Tuesday to discuss the escalating conflict in eastern DRC, following a deadly drone attack in Goma on March 11, which killed a UNICEF staff member. The meeting was requested by France. S
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC March 16, 2026 – The UN Security Council will hold closed-door consultations on Tuesday to discuss the escalating conflict in eastern DRC, following a deadly drone attack in Goma on March 11, which killed a UNICEF staff member. The meeting was requested by France.
Several Council members are expected to condemn the attack and stress the need to protect civilians and humanitarian workers. MONUSCO, the UN mission in the DRC, has warned that attacks on UN personnel may constitute war crimes under the Rome Statute.
The strike was also condemned by Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, Chairperson of the African Union Commission, and by the European Union, both calling for an impartial investigation. The Congolese government announced its own investigation on March 13.
The attack coincides with an escalation of drone use in the east, where the FARDC is conducting an offensive against the March 23 Movement (M23). Discussions at the Council are expected to focus on establishing a permanent ceasefire, in line with Security Council resolution 2808, adopted December 19, 2025, which renewed MONUSCO’s mandate.
The UN Secretary-General has recommended a “gradual, adaptable, and conditional” approach to supporting the ceasefire, including deploying light infantry battalions, a rapid deployment unit, and an advanced medical evacuation team, with 1,500–2,500 additional troops potentially needed in North and South Kivu.
Recent tensions were compounded by US sanctions on Rwandan military officials and the Rwandan Defence Forces (RDF) on March 2. Kinshasa welcomed the sanctions, while Kigali denounced them as unilateral.

title: Mukwege Warns Tshisekedi Against “Drummers,” Criticizes Purge of Dissenting Parliamentarians
excerpt: Kinshasa, March 23, 2026 – Nobel Peace Prize laureate Dr. Denis Mukwege called on President Félix Tshisekedi to resist pressure from what he described as the “drummers” surrounding him, warning that these advisors pursue personal interests and could betray the President as others
title_en: Mukwege Warns Tshisekedi Against “Drummers,” Criticizes Purge of Dissenting Parliamentarians
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, March 23, 2026 – Nobel Peace Prize laureate Dr. Denis Mukwege called on President Félix Tshisekedi to resist pressure from what he described as the “drummers” surrounding him, warning that these advisors pursue personal interests and could betray the President as others
body_en:
Kinshasa, March 23, 2026 – Nobel Peace Prize laureate Dr. Denis Mukwege called on President Félix Tshisekedi to resist pressure from what he described as the “drummers” surrounding him, warning that these advisors pursue personal interests and could betray the President as others did during previous regimes.
In a statement issued Monday, Mukwege urged the President to listen to his conscience and the voice of the people rather than the ambitions of loyalists promoting a third term, despite elections scheduled for 2028.
“Tomorrow, they will be the first to stab you in the back, as certain bigwigs and leading figures of the previous regime did,” Mukwege warned. “Listen instead to your conscience and the voice of the people. Our freedom depends on it.”
Political Consequences of Opposing Constitutional Change
The Nobel laureate also criticized the resignations of two senior lawmakers who opposed the proposed constitutional amendment: Vital Kamerhe, former Speaker of the National Assembly, and Modeste Bahati Lukwebo, Second Vice-President of the Senate. Both stepped down after petitions were filed by colleagues aligned with the ruling party and the Sacred Union coalition.
“By daring to oppose the proposed constitutional amendment while our country is at war, you had the courage to speak the truth, a sign of nobility for a representative of the people,” Mukwege said in an analysis published Monday. He lamented what he called a reversal of democratic principles, in which dissenting deputies and senators are sanctioned by the President for exercising oversight.
Mukwege condemned the “hypocrisy” of colleagues who privately share the dissenting view but publicly align with the establishment.
Third Term Debate and Political Tensions
The DRC political landscape has become increasingly polarized over proposals to amend the Constitution of February 18, 2006, to allow a potential third term for President Tshisekedi. Opposition figures, including Delly Sessanga, have pledged to mobilize citizens and organize street protests to block any constitutional change.
Meanwhile, supporters of the ruling UDPS party insist the amendment is necessary, describing Tshisekedi’s mandate not merely as a term in office but as a “mission” to complete. This debate has intensified political tensions and drawn international attention, with civil society leaders warning of threats to democratic governance and institutional integrity.

Kinshasa March 20, 2026 – The Electricity Regulatory Authority (ARE) of the Democratic Republic of Congo has signed a memorandum of understanding with the National School of Administration (ENA), establishing a strategic partnership to provide high-level certification training for its managers and staff.
The agreement, formalized during a ceremony at ENA on Friday, March 20, aims to strengthen ARE’s capacity in project management, public procurement, financial modeling, environmental safeguards, and risk management. Staff will benefit from internationally recognized certifications, including PMP for directors and CAPM for managers, enhancing the Authority’s project-oriented structure.
In her remarks, ARE Director General Soraya Aziz-Moto emphasized the strategic significance of the partnership. “ENA has established itself as the absolute benchmark for training administrative elites in our country,” she said. “This collaboration demonstrates that our administration can reinvent itself from within, combining institutional heritage with modern management methods.”
She added that certification programs will equip ARE staff with universal project management skills, ensuring precision, efficiency, and accountability in license processing and audits. “By certifying our teams, we are not simply seeking qualifications, but guaranteeing surgical precision and record-breaking efficiency in processing each license application and audit,” she stated.
Soraya Aziz-Moto also highlighted the broader goal of transforming the public administration sector. “Become the faces of this new era where every regulated kilowatt is managed with certified expertise, for the greater good of our nation,” she urged.
Speaking at the ceremony, ENA Director General Tombola Muke praised ARE’s initiative and confirmed that the collaboration, which includes PMI and ISO certifications, will commence promptly. He emphasized that this training will provide ARE with the skilled human capital needed to enhance governance and align with international standards while supporting sustainable development in the DRC.

title: ICRC Ready to Support Transfer of Over 5,000 Released FARDC Soldiers to Kinshasa
excerpt: Eastern DRC March 9, 2026 — The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has announced its readiness to facilitate the transfer of more than 5,000 Congolese soldiers released by the AFC/M23 rebellion in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The soldiers, members of the FAR
title_en: ICRC Ready to Support Transfer of Over 5,000 Released FARDC Soldiers to Kinshasa
excerpt_en: Eastern DRC March 9, 2026 — The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has announced its readiness to facilitate the transfer of more than 5,000 Congolese soldiers released by the AFC/M23 rebellion in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The soldiers, members of the FAR
body_en:
Eastern DRC March 9, 2026 — The International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC) has announced its readiness to facilitate the transfer of more than 5,000 Congolese soldiers released by the AFC/M23 rebellion in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The soldiers, members of the FARDC (Armed Forces of the DRC), were handed over on March 2 at the Rumangabo military camp in Rutshuru Territory, according to a statement issued by the AFC/M23. The group indicated that the troops, captured on various frontlines, would be transferred to Kinshasa under ICRC supervision.
“The AFC/M23 informs the public that it has handed over more than 5,000 FARDC members to the ICRC. They will be repatriated to Kinshasa under its supervision,” the statement said.
Responding to the announcement, François Moreillon, head of the ICRC delegation in Kinshasa, confirmed the organization’s position. “As a neutral intermediary, the ICRC stands ready to assist with such an operation, with the agreement of all parties,” he stated.
This large-scale prisoner transfer forms part of confidence-building measures agreed upon within the Doha mediation process, aimed at easing tensions between Kinshasa and the rebellion. The AFC/M23 says the release reflects its commitment to international humanitarian law and efforts to de-escalate the conflict.
The ICRC has previously played a similar role. In May 2025, it facilitated the transfer of more than 1,300 disarmed soldiers from Goma to Kinshasa.
However, despite this development, tensions remain high. The AFC/M23, often described as Rwandan-backed rebels, accuses the government of Kinshasa of refusing to release detained fighters, including individuals allegedly arrested “simply because of their appearance.”
The group further alleges ongoing ceasefire violations, claiming that government forces continue military operations targeting civilian populations and property, accusations that risk undermining fragile peace efforts in eastern DRC.
While the planned transfer could mark a significant step toward de-escalation, its success will depend on cooperation between all parties and sustained commitment to the broader peace process.

title_en: Militiamen Surrender in Kwamouth, Dozens of Weapons Turned Over
excerpt_en: Kwamouth, Kwango – March 15, 2026 – A new surrender of militiamen was reported on March 12 in Kinsele, where sixteen weapons of war were handed over to the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo). The cache included one PKM, ten AK-47s, five 12-gauge shotguns, an
body_en:
Kwamouth, Kwango – March 15, 2026 – A new surrender of militiamen was reported on March 12 in Kinsele, where sixteen weapons of war were handed over to the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo). The cache included one PKM, ten AK-47s, five 12-gauge shotguns, and ammunition, marking another step in the ongoing disarmament and demobilization process in the region.
The handover ceremony was attended by a delegation from the Minister Delegate for Defense, Eliezer Ntambwe, highlighting the government’s continued efforts to reintegrate former combatants.
The Eleventh Military Region confirmed that several Mobondo fighters participated in the surrender. According to Captain Antony Mualushayi, spokesperson for the FARDC, the fighters and recovered weapons were transferred to Kinshasa to continue the formal demobilization process.
During a broader peacekeeping mission in Kwamouth territory, Minister Eliezer Ntambwe announced the earlier surrender of over 600 Mobondo militiamen, many of whom were sent to Kaniama Kasese to join the National Service. Some of the former fighters expressed interest in military training, though placement at Kaniama Kasese was declared mandatory.
This latest surrender reflects ongoing progress in efforts to stabilize the region and reintegrate armed groups into national structures.

excerpt_en: Mitwaba, Haut-Katanga March 20, 2026 – The FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo) repelled a Mai-Mai Bakatanga incursion on March 19 in the village of Nkonga, about 35 kilometers from Mitwaba. Gunfire was reported between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m., as armed assailants b
body_en:
Mitwaba, Haut-Katanga March 20, 2026 – The FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo) repelled a Mai-Mai Bakatanga incursion on March 19 in the village of Nkonga, about 35 kilometers from Mitwaba.
Gunfire was reported between 3 p.m. and 5 p.m., as armed assailants briefly entered the area before being pushed back by the army. Local authorities described the attack as sudden and sporadic, with the situation now under control.
Officials confirmed that the FARDC regained full control of the village after routing the attackers, while provincial authorities reported a return to calm.
The incident highlights the persistent insecurity in Mitwaba territory, where Mai-Mai Bakatanga militias continue to carry out recurrent attacks against state forces. Recent violence has also targeted Upemba National Park, where at least five rangers were killed in similar incursions.
Despite military reinforcements, the security situation remains fragile, with key routes around Mitwaba becoming increasingly dangerous due to the presence of armed groups.
