title: Prime Minister Nsengiyumva Attends East African Community Heads of State Summit
excerpt: Prime Minister Justin Nsengiyumva arrived in Arusha on March 6, 2026, where he is representing President Paul Kagame at the 25th Ordinary Summit of Heads of State of the East African Community (EAC) scheduled for March 7, 2026. Upon arrival at Kilimanjaro International Airport, N
title_en: Prime Minister Nsengiyumva Attends East African Community Heads of State Summit
excerpt_en: Prime Minister Justin Nsengiyumva arrived in Arusha on March 6, 2026, where he is representing President Paul Kagame at the 25th Ordinary Summit of Heads of State of the East African Community (EAC) scheduled for March 7, 2026. Upon arrival at Kilimanjaro International Airport, N
body_en:
Prime Minister Justin Nsengiyumva arrived in Arusha on March 6, 2026, where he is representing President Paul Kagame at the 25th Ordinary Summit of Heads of State of the East African Community (EAC) scheduled for March 7, 2026.
Upon arrival at Kilimanjaro International Airport, Nsengiyumva was received by Dennis Londo and Rwanda’s Ambassador to Tanzania, Patrick Nyamvumba.
The summit brings together leaders from eight EAC member states: Tanzania, Rwanda, Kenya, Uganda, Democratic Republic of the Congo, Somalia, South Sudan, and Burundi.
During the meeting, leaders are expected to appoint a new Director General and Secretary General of the EAC, select judges for the East African Court of Justice, and extend the mandates of deputy secretaries general.
One of the key outcomes anticipated from the summit is the launch of a common customs document known as the “EAC Customs Bond.” The new document will replace separate customs documentation currently used by each country for cross-border trade. Officials say the initiative will allow traders to conduct business across EAC member states using a single document, reducing administrative barriers and facilitating coordination between customs authorities, insurers, and financial institutions.
The reform is expected to lower operational costs for traders and accelerate trade and investment within the region.
The summit will also launch the seventh EAC Development Plan, covering the period 2026/27 to 2030/31, which outlines the region’s strategic vision for regional integration and development aimed at boosting social progress and economic growth over the next five years.
Despite an existing legal framework designed to accelerate joint projects, the EAC has acknowledged that intra-regional trade remains relatively low. Trade among member states has stagnated at around 15% over the past decade, significantly below the regional target of 30% to 50%.
Currently, intra-EAC trade accounts for roughly one-eighth of total exports. Regional trade increased only slightly from 11.5% in 2016 to 12.2% in 2024, reflecting the bloc’s continued reliance on external markets.

title: Rwanda’s Prime Minister Calls for Public Support After Increase in Community Health Insurance Contributions
excerpt: On February 28, 2026, Prime Minister Dr. Justin Nsengiyumva called on citizens to better understand the recent increase in contributions to Rwanda’s Community Health Insurance scheme (Mutuelles de Santé), stressing that the measure aims to strengthen funding for the country’s hea
title_en: Rwanda’s Prime Minister Calls for Public Support After Increase in Community Health Insurance Contributions
excerpt_en: On February 28, 2026, Prime Minister Dr. Justin Nsengiyumva called on citizens to better understand the recent increase in contributions to Rwanda’s Community Health Insurance scheme (Mutuelles de Santé), stressing that the measure aims to strengthen funding for the country’s hea
body_en:
On February 28, 2026, Prime Minister Dr. Justin Nsengiyumva called on citizens to better understand the recent increase in contributions to Rwanda’s Community Health Insurance scheme (Mutuelles de Santé), stressing that the measure aims to strengthen funding for the country’s health sector.
The Prime Minister made the remarks while participating in a community work activity (Umuganda) in Kigali City, specifically in Kicukiro District, Gatenga Sector, Nyarurama Cell. Residents gathered to clean and repair clogged water pipes that had caused flooding and obstructed homes for several days.
During the event, Nsengiyumva explained that the government’s decision to raise Mutuelles de Santé contributions was not taken lightly but reflects the need to increase resources dedicated to healthcare services.
He acknowledged that the adjustment comes at a time when citizens are also facing rising costs of living, including higher electricity tariffs, but emphasized that such decisions are part of broader efforts to manage limited national resources effectively.
Using a household analogy, the Prime Minister explained that the government budget operates much like a family budget, where limited income must be distributed among many competing needs such as education, healthcare, and public services.
According to him, just as families must prioritize spending when income is limited, the government must also balance national priorities while ensuring that essential services—particularly healthcare—remain accessible to the population.
He noted that the last adjustment of community health insurance contributions was made in 2011, despite growing demands on the healthcare system over the past decade. As the population grows and healthcare needs expand, additional funding has become necessary to maintain and improve health services nationwide.
The Prime Minister therefore urged citizens to view the increased contributions as a collective investment aimed at sustaining universal access to healthcare in Rwanda.
Beyond the issue of healthcare financing, Nsengiyumva also addressed urban sanitation and environmental management. He encouraged residents and local authorities to adopt better waste management practices, particularly by separating garbage before collection.
He suggested that households use different bags for plastic bottles, paper, and biodegradable waste, which would make waste collection more efficient and reduce unpleasant odors caused by mixed waste.
Meanwhile, Kigali City Mayor Samuel Dusengiyumva warned residents that weather forecasts indicate heavier rainfall this year. He urged communities to avoid practices that could block drainage systems, such as dumping waste in water channels and erosion control infrastructure.
The mayor also called on residents to take preventive measures against flooding and erosion, emphasizing that proper waste disposal and maintenance of drainage systems are essential to mitigating the impact of heavy rains in the capital.

excerpt_en: Bugesera, February 26, 2026 – The Government of Rwanda received 164 refugees and migrants who had been stranded in Libya, as part of ongoing humanitarian efforts to assist vulnerable populations. The group includes 143 individuals from Sudan, affected by nearly three years of con
body_en:
Bugesera, February 26, 2026 – The Government of Rwanda received 164 refugees and migrants who had been stranded in Libya, as part of ongoing humanitarian efforts to assist vulnerable populations.
The group includes 143 individuals from Sudan, affected by nearly three years of conflict, 19 from Eritrea, one from Ethiopia, and one from South Sudan.
This initiative is part of the Emergency Transit Mechanism (ETM), established through an agreement between Rwanda, the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), and the African Union (AU). The program provides temporary accommodation for refugees and migrants in Libya while they await permanent resettlement in third countries.
The new arrivals were received at the Gashora temporary camp in Bugesera District, where they are processed before being relocated to countries that have agreed to host them.
Since the launch of the ETM in 2019, Rwanda has hosted 2,760 refugees and migrants from Libya, with over 2,500 successfully resettled in other countries.

body_en:
On March 5, 2026, the AFC/M23 coalition announced the deployment of specialized commando units near Bangoka International Airport in Kisangani, DRC, aimed at targeting drone operations used by the DRC army and its allies.
The coalition confirmed that it had carried out drone attacks on the airport on February 1 and March 1, 2026, intending to destroy facilities used to launch attacks on AFC/M23 bases and civilians in North Kivu and South Kivu provinces.
Deputy Spokesperson Dr. Oscar Balinda explained:
“The commando forces travel day and night, they go to do their work and then return. So they went and worked, and then returned. This is the terror we want to stop so that we can respect the ceasefire, return to the negotiating table, and achieve lasting peace.”
On March 2, 2026, AFC/M23 inducted 1,518 new fighters at the Rumangabo military base in Rutshuru Territory, defining them as specialized commando units trained to operate while mobile, rather than maintaining permanent bases.
Yannick Tshisola, Director of the Office of the AFC/M23 Commander-in-Chief, indicated that these commandos could play a decisive role in operations targeting Bangoka airport.
This deployment highlights AFC/M23’s focus on mobile, tactical operations to protect its controlled areas while signaling readiness for continued self-defense amidst the ongoing conflict in eastern DRC.

title: Presidents Macron and Tshisekedi to Meet in Paris, February 24, 2026

title_en: Presidents Macron and Tshisekedi to Meet in Paris, February 24, 2026
excerpt_en: PARIS February 24, 2026 — French President Emmanuel Macron is scheduled to meet with Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi in Paris on Wednesday, amid ongoing diplomatic efforts addressing the security and humanitarian crisis in eastern DRC. The two leaders last met on January 23,
body_en:
PARIS February 24, 2026 — French President Emmanuel Macron is scheduled to meet with Congolese President Félix Tshisekedi in Paris on Wednesday, amid ongoing diplomatic efforts addressing the security and humanitarian crisis in eastern DRC.
The two leaders last met on January 23, 2026, at the Élysée Palace, during which discussions centered on the humanitarian situation in eastern DRC and bilateral cooperation between France and the DRC.
On February 14, France welcomed Tshisekedi’s commitment to implement a ceasefire proposed by Angola for all warring parties in the Great Lakes region. French authorities also stressed the importance of implementing the Washington Agreement of December 4, 2025, calling on all stakeholders to respect their obligations.
French diplomacy reaffirmed its dedication to ensuring that peace momentum generated by the Washington Agreement, the Doha Framework Agreement of November 15, 2025, and African Union initiatives translates into tangible improvements in the lives of civilians in eastern DRC.
France also highlighted its role in monitoring the humanitarian response, citing the visit of Vivian van de Perre, Deputy Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General and Acting Head of MONUSCO, to Goma from February 12–14, 2026. This visit prepared UN support for ceasefire verification and monitoring in line with UN Security Council Resolution 2808 (2025).
“The first flight to Goma airport represents a critical step toward resuming small-scale, daytime humanitarian flights. France calls on all parties to collaborate to ensure continued humanitarian access for the benefit of the population,” the French Foreign Ministry stated.

title: Daniel Mukoko Highlights Local Industrialization and Value Chains
excerpt: KINSHASA March 2, 2026 — The first-ever DRC-Japan Business Forum officially launched on Monday at the Fleuve Congo Hotel in Kinshasa, bringing together Congolese and Japanese business leaders to explore investment opportunities and strengthen economic cooperation. The event was i
title_en: Daniel Mukoko Highlights Local Industrialization and Value Chains
excerpt_en: KINSHASA March 2, 2026 — The first-ever DRC-Japan Business Forum officially launched on Monday at the Fleuve Congo Hotel in Kinshasa, bringing together Congolese and Japanese business leaders to explore investment opportunities and strengthen economic cooperation. The event was i
body_en:
KINSHASA March 2, 2026 — The first-ever DRC-Japan Business Forum officially launched on Monday at the Fleuve Congo Hotel in Kinshasa, bringing together Congolese and Japanese business leaders to explore investment opportunities and strengthen economic cooperation. The event was initiated by the Embassy of Japan.
In his opening remarks, Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Economy Daniel Mukoko Samba emphasized the importance of transforming the Democratic Republic of Congo’s economy through industrialization and local processing of raw materials. He highlighted the DRC’s critical mineral resources, exceptional hydroelectric potential through the Inga complex, and geostrategic position in Africa as key assets for industrial partnerships.
“We need to move from extraction to processing,” Mukoko Samba stated, underscoring government ambitions to develop value chains in batteries, advanced metallurgy, recycling, special economic zones, and high-value-added technology partnerships.
He also stressed the potential for Japanese companies to contribute their expertise in electronics, automotive, advanced materials, and clean technology to the DRC’s industrialization efforts. Beyond mining, he pointed to the country’s agricultural potential, advocating for mechanization, smart irrigation, agri-food processing, and technical training as areas for Japanese investment. “Investing in Congolese agriculture is investing in regional stability and the continent’s food security,” he said.
The Deputy Prime Minister reassured investors regarding ongoing structural reforms, including digitalization of public administration, mining governance improvements, modernization of public-private partnerships, and enhanced business security. He also recalled President Félix Tshisekedi’s commitment, made during a February 5 meeting in Washington, to an investor-friendly environment.
This inaugural forum builds on previous DRC-Japan economic dialogues held in Tokyo (April 2025) and Osaka (June 2025), reflecting a shared commitment to deepen trade, investment, and industrial cooperation between the two nations.

body_en:
Kinshasa, February 27, 2026 – The Kinshasa/Matete High Court sentenced Josué Kaniki to death on Thursday, February 26, 2026, for the murder of his mother. In addition, he received three years of penal servitude for cannibalism, the offense of consuming human flesh. Under the rules governing concurrent sentencing, only the most severe penalty, the death sentence, was enforced.
The court also ordered the immediate arrest of Kaniki and mandated the payment of $50,000 USD in damages to the plaintiff for all harm suffered.
The verdict concludes a summary trial that has sparked outrage among the population of Kinshasa in recent days, highlighting the case’s shocking nature and the court’s firm stance on severe crimes.

title_en: AFC/M23 Rebels Driven Out of Mahanga Village Amid Renewed Fighting
excerpt_en: MASISI, North Kivu February 25, 2026 — Violent clashes erupted on Tuesday morning, February 24, between AFC/M23 rebels and the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by Wazalendo fighters, in Mahanga village, located in the Butsike area of the Nyamabo
body_en:
MASISI, North Kivu February 25, 2026 — Violent clashes erupted on Tuesday morning, February 24, between AFC/M23 rebels and the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by Wazalendo fighters, in Mahanga village, located in the Butsike area of the Nyamaboko I group, Masisi territory.
Government forces reportedly advanced from Buhimba in neighboring Walikale territory, targeting rebel positions in Mahanga. After a brief but intense exchange of gunfire, AFC/M23 fighters were driven out of the village, retreating into the surrounding bush in this part of the Osso Banyungu chiefdom.
The offensive triggered population movements, with several families fleeing Mahanga to seek refuge in the nearby bush, fearing renewed clashes.
Local observers noted that the situation remains highly volatile, as the different armed factions continue to reposition themselves in this part of Masisi territory, an area regularly affected by conflict and instability.
These developments underscore the persistent fragility of security in rural North Kivu, where civilians continue to bear the brunt of ongoing armed rivalries.

title: DRC Reaffirms Commitment to Human Rights, Rejects Allegations of Discrimination and Foreign Occupation
excerpt: GENEVA February 27, 2026 — The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) reaffirmed its firm commitment to protecting all its communities and respecting human rights during the high-level segment of the 61st session of the United Nations Human Rights Council (HRC) in Geneva, Switzerland
title_en: DRC Reaffirms Commitment to Human Rights, Rejects Allegations of Discrimination and Foreign Occupation
excerpt_en: GENEVA February 27, 2026 — The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) reaffirmed its firm commitment to protecting all its communities and respecting human rights during the high-level segment of the 61st session of the United Nations Human Rights Council (HRC) in Geneva, Switzerland
body_en:
GENEVA February 27, 2026 — The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) reaffirmed its firm commitment to protecting all its communities and respecting human rights during the high-level segment of the 61st session of the United Nations Human Rights Council (HRC) in Geneva, Switzerland.
Minister of State and Foreign Affairs, Thérèse Kayikwamba Wagner, addressed allegations that the DRC discriminates against Congolese of Tutsi origin, accusations often cited by the Rwandan government to justify interventions in eastern DRC. She emphasized that such claims do not reflect national policy and that transgressions by individuals are addressed under national law and international commitments.
“The alleged protection of a community cannot justify violations of international law or serve as a pretext for illegal occupation of DRC territory,” Minister Kayikwamba Wagner stated, stressing that the country relies on multilateral instruments rather than taking the law into its own hands.
The remarks also came amid controversy surrounding Major General Sylvain Ekenge, the FARDC spokesperson, who faced suspension after allegedly discriminatory comments toward Tutsi women. Lieutenant General Jules Banza, FARDC Chief of Staff, condemned the statements and reaffirmed the FARDC’s commitment to safeguard the sovereignty, territorial integrity, and security of all Congolese without discrimination.
Minister Kayikwamba Wagner underscored that the DRC continues judicial investigations into hate speech and conflict-related offenses, cooperating with the Commission of Inquiry to hold accountable those responsible. She called for national unity, condemning exploitation of isolated remarks by external actors, including the AFC/M23 rebellion and Rwandan authorities, in the context of ongoing tensions between Kinshasa and Kigali regarding the Washington process commitments.
The DRC’s statement highlights its determination to protect all communities, uphold international law, and maintain national cohesion amid persistent regional security and political challenges.

title: Buhimba Falls Back Under AFC/M23 Control, Triggering New Displacements
excerpt: WALIKALE March 2, 2026 — The village of Buhimba, located in the Waloa Yungu group of Walikale territory, North Kivu, returned to AFC/M23 rebel control on Sunday, March 1, after intense clashes with the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo) and allied Wazalendo
title_en: Buhimba Falls Back Under AFC/M23 Control, Triggering New Displacements
excerpt_en: WALIKALE March 2, 2026 — The village of Buhimba, located in the Waloa Yungu group of Walikale territory, North Kivu, returned to AFC/M23 rebel control on Sunday, March 1, after intense clashes with the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo) and allied Wazalendo
body_en:
WALIKALE March 2, 2026 — The village of Buhimba, located in the Waloa Yungu group of Walikale territory, North Kivu, returned to AFC/M23 rebel control on Sunday, March 1, after intense clashes with the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo) and allied Wazalendo fighters.
According to local sources, the rebels advanced from Kilongo in the Osso Banyungu sector of Masisi territory and launched an assault on government positions in Buhimba. Following several hours of fierce fighting, FARDC forces retreated to Ngenge, west of Buhimba, leaving the village in rebel hands.
The recapture has sparked a fresh wave of displacement. Residents from Ngenge and Kangati are fleeing for safety, with some taking refuge in the bush and others moving toward Kimua, according to the chief of Waloa Yungu.
This development intensifies the ongoing humanitarian crisis in the area, already strained by persistent insecurity. Local sources warn that the fighting could spread to surrounding villages, as clashes persist along the border between Walikale and Masisi territories.
The AFC/M23’s seizure of Buhimba comes amid a resurgence of hostilities in multiple strategic locations across eastern North Kivu, highlighting the volatility of the region.

title: James Swan Appointed Head of MONUSCO
excerpt: KINSHASA March 5, 2026 — United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres announced the appointment of American diplomat James Swan as the new Special Representative for the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO). He s
title_en: James Swan Appointed Head of MONUSCO
excerpt_en: KINSHASA March 5, 2026 — United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres announced the appointment of American diplomat James Swan as the new Special Representative for the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO). He s
body_en:
KINSHASA March 5, 2026 — United Nations Secretary-General António Guterres announced the appointment of American diplomat James Swan as the new Special Representative for the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (MONUSCO). He succeeds Bintou Keita of Guinea, whom Guterres thanked for her service to the mission.
James Swan is a seasoned diplomat with extensive experience in Africa, particularly in countries undergoing complex political and security transitions. He previously served as Special Representative of the Secretary-General for Somalia and headed the United Nations Transitional Assistance Mission in Somalia (UNTMIS) from March 2025, having also held the role on an interim basis since May 2024. He led the United Nations Mission in Somalia (UNSOM) from 2019 to 2022.
Before joining the UN, Swan completed a 32-year career in the U.S. government, with several assignments related to the DRC, including as U.S. Ambassador to the DRC (2013–2016), Deputy Chief of Staff at the U.S. Embassy (2001–2004), and Desk Officer (1996–1998). He also served as U.S. Ambassador to Djibouti (2008–2011), Special Representative for Somalia (2011–2013), and Assistant Secretary of State for African Affairs (2006–2008), with additional postings in Congo-Brazzaville, Somalia, Cameroon, Nicaragua, and Haiti.
Swan holds degrees from Georgetown University, Johns Hopkins University, and the National War College, and is fluent in French.

excerpt_en: On 23 February 2026, Sudan strongly criticized Uganda following a meeting between President Yoweri Museveni and Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, leader of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), intensifying diplomatic tensions between the two countries. Sudanese authorities described the visit of
body_en:
On 23 February 2026, Sudan strongly criticized Uganda following a meeting between President Yoweri Museveni and Mohamed Hamdan Dagalo, leader of the Rapid Support Forces (RSF), intensifying diplomatic tensions between the two countries.
Sudanese authorities described the visit of Dagalo, also known as “Hemedti,”, as an affront to human rights and to the Sudanese people, accusing the RSF leader of responsibility for widespread violence and civilian deaths during the ongoing Sudan conflict.
Officials in Khartoum argued that hosting the RSF leader constitutes a violation of international norms, which discourage support or engagement with armed groups opposing a recognized government.
During the meeting held on 20 February 2026, President Museveni emphasized the need for dialogue and political solutions as the only sustainable path toward peace in Sudan.
The visit comes as the Rapid Support Forces remain engaged in heavy fighting against Sudanese government forces, with the group facing serious accusations of war crimes and genocide.

body_en:
On March 5, 2026, before the United Nations Human Rights Council in Geneva, Rwanda condemned the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government for allegedly undermining peace in the Great Lakes region.
Edmond Tubanambazi, First Counselor at the Rwandan Embassy in Switzerland and at the UN offices in Geneva, emphasized that peace has been a cornerstone of Rwanda’s recovery over the past 32 years following the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi. He said the country continues to prioritize unity, reconciliation, and a culture of peace in its national reconstruction.
Tubanambazi accused the DRC of harboring and collaborating with the FDLR terrorist group, instead of dismantling it, and of integrating FDLR fighters into the FARDC and allied groups, posing a threat to regional security. He stressed that these actions have been repeatedly highlighted by the Office of the High Commissioner for Human Rights and the UN Security Council.
Rwanda, he added, is actively supporting regional security measures, including those under the African Union-led coalition and the Washington Peace Accords, and called for accountability and restraint to prevent armed groups from spreading hatred and committing crimes.

title: More Than 26,000 Refugee Children Integrated into the National Education System
excerpt: KIREHE, February 23, 2026 — More than 26,000 refugee children living in Mahama Camp in Kirehe District are currently enrolled in Rwanda’s education system, benefiting from access to primary, secondary and vocational education as part of the country’s broader refugee integration p
title_en: More Than 26,000 Refugee Children Integrated into the National Education System
excerpt_en: KIREHE, February 23, 2026 — More than 26,000 refugee children living in Mahama Camp in Kirehe District are currently enrolled in Rwanda’s education system, benefiting from access to primary, secondary and vocational education as part of the country’s broader refugee integration p
body_en:
KIREHE, February 23, 2026 — More than 26,000 refugee children living in Mahama Camp in Kirehe District are currently enrolled in Rwanda’s education system, benefiting from access to primary, secondary and vocational education as part of the country’s broader refugee integration policy.
Mahama Camp, the largest refugee settlement in Rwanda, hosts approximately 72,340 refugees from 14 countries, with the majority originating from the Democratic Republic of Congo and Burundi. Among them, over 26,000 students attend schools across different educational levels.
Refugee families in the camp benefit from improved living conditions, including basic infrastructure, cooking gas distribution, and access to public services, while children attend both nearby public schools and technical and vocational training institutions.
Investment in Vocational Education
Under the Jyambere Project, authorities have invested heavily in vocational training infrastructure to support refugee education in Kirehe District. Two major technical secondary schools were constructed to expand opportunities for young refugees.
Musaza Technical Secondary School (TSS) received more than 2 billion Rwandan francs in funding, including modern equipment, while Bukora TSS benefited from investments exceeding 3.5 billion Rwandan francs.
These institutions provide training in fields such as electrical engineering, tailoring, and other technical professions, preparing students for employment or further studies.
Refugee Students Embrace Opportunities
Many refugee students say access to education has allowed them to build skills and plan for a better future.
An 18-year-old student studying electrical engineering at Musaza TSS explained that growing up in Rwanda allowed him to pursue his education without interruption or discrimination. He expressed confidence that his technical skills would help him secure employment or continue to university studies after graduation.
Another student enrolled in tailoring training highlighted the equal treatment between refugee and local students, noting that she hopes to use her education to help her family overcome poverty.
Equal Access to Public Services
Local authorities emphasize that refugees in Mahama Camp benefit from equal access to education, healthcare, and economic services under national regulations.
Officials say integrating refugees into public services not only improves living standards but also contributes to local development, as refugees bring valuable skills and economic potential to host communities.
Infrastructure Development
Over the past seven years, the Jyambere Project has supported infrastructure development in six refugee-hosting districts, including Gisagara, Nyamagabe, Karongi, Gicumbi, Gatsibo, and Kirehe.
In Kirehe alone, the project has:
Built Musaza TSS and Bukora TSS
Constructed a two-story building at Kirehe Hospital
Begun renovation of Nyarubuye Health Center into a district hospital
Upgraded facilities serving both refugees and host communities
Rising Number of Refugee Students
Recent education data shows a steady increase in the number of refugee students enrolled in Rwandan schools.
During the 2023–2024 academic year, refugee enrollment rose by 10.9%, increasing from 39,728 students in 2022–2023 to 44,051 students.
Of these students:
51.3% were boys
48.7% were girls
The continued expansion of education access, particularly in technical and vocational training, is seen as a key factor in improving self-reliance and long-term prospects for refugee communities in Rwanda.

title: AFC/M23 Condemns International Silence as DRC Forces Escalate Attacks
excerpt: Eastern DRC, February 25, 2026 – The AFC/M23 coalition expressed deep disappointment at the international community’s silence amid escalating attacks by the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government forces, which have targeted both civilians and rebel positions using drones a
title_en: AFC/M23 Condemns International Silence as DRC Forces Escalate Attacks
excerpt_en: Eastern DRC, February 25, 2026 – The AFC/M23 coalition expressed deep disappointment at the international community’s silence amid escalating attacks by the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government forces, which have targeted both civilians and rebel positions using drones a
body_en:
Eastern DRC, February 25, 2026 – The AFC/M23 coalition expressed deep disappointment at the international community’s silence amid escalating attacks by the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government forces, which have targeted both civilians and rebel positions using drones and heavy weaponry.
AFC/M23 spokesman Lawrence Kanyuka reported that large-scale attacks occurred in Rutigita, Rugezi, and border areas of Minembwe and Kitazungura communes in Kalehe territory, causing deaths, mass displacement, and a worsening humanitarian crisis.
Bertrand Bisimwa, AFC/M23 Deputy Director for Political, Diplomatic, and Governance Affairs, criticized the DRC government for violating the ceasefire agreement, accusing it of choosing war over diplomacy. He highlighted the lack of concrete international measures to prevent continued fighting, contrasting the silence of global actors with the attention given when AFC/M23 defends itself.
The attacks on February 25 followed previous drone strikes by DRC forces in central Masisi and surrounding areas on February 24, illustrating a pattern of escalating military operations.
body_fr:
Eastern DRC, February 25, 2026 – The AFC/M23 coalition expressed deep disappointment at the international community’s silence amid escalating attacks by the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government forces, which have targeted both civilians and rebel positions using drones and heavy weaponry.

title_en: The Deadly February Attack on AFC/M23 Leadership in Masisi: What Really Happened
excerpt_en: Since late February 2026, the DRC army and allied Wazalendo groups have intensified attacks on AFC/M23 positions in Masisi territory, targeting the coltan-rich Rubaya area. These operations have involved heavy weapons and drones, as clashes continue in the region. On February 23,
body_en:
Since late February 2026, the DRC army and allied Wazalendo groups have intensified attacks on AFC/M23 positions in Masisi territory, targeting the coltan-rich Rubaya area. These operations have involved heavy weapons and drones, as clashes continue in the region.
On February 23, senior AFC/M23 officers, including Gen Maj Sultani Makenga, Brig Gen Gaceri Musanga, Col Japhet Gakufe, and Lt Col Willy Ngoma, visited Rubaya to boost the morale of their fighters. That day ended with the DRC coalition failing to capture Rubaya, though they continued attacks in Bahunde chiefdom, including Gatoyi, Gasenyi, and Kinigi.
According to AFC/M23 sources, the leaders decided to spend the night near Rubaya at barracks located in the pasture of Brig Gen Innocent Gahizi. Around 8:00 a.m. on February 24, Gen Maj Makenga rested at Mater Dei Catholic Church in Matanda, while other officers remained in the pasture barracks.
Lt Col Willy Ngoma, the military spokesman, was killed during a targeted attack on the barracks. The coalition’s deputy spokesman, Dr. Oscar Balinda, stated: “They came to shoot at our military spokesman, they shot him in the barracks where he was. It was a house, not on the road—a place where they were staying to stop attacks coming from Walikale.”
Rumors circulated that Gen Maj Makenga had been injured or killed, but AFC/M23 sources confirmed he was alive and on duty. Dr. Balinda emphasized, “He arrived at the battlefield, left, and went to other duties. He was not there when this happened. He is alive, he is on duty.”
On March 2, Gen Maj Makenga was seen at Rumangabo military base in Rutshuru, where he inducted 1,518 new fighters into AFC/M23. Addressing them, he stressed that their mission was to remove incompetent leaders in Kinshasa, restore stability, and support displaced Congolese. “Are you ready to remove Tshisekedi and these ignorant people working with him? Do you refuse to lead with bandits?” he asked, before affirming the group’s commitment to their cause.
Following the February attack, AFC/M23 vowed to continue targeting DRC government assets, including Bangoka airport in Kisangani, aiming to destroy drones used against its bases and hold the DRC government accountable for the deaths of its soldiers, including Lt Col Ngoma.
The clashes in North Kivu and South Kivu, particularly in Masisi, continue to highlight the intense conflict between AFC/M23 and DRC forces, with each side asserting its operational capabilities in self-defense and territorial control.

title: Ministerial Meeting Finalizes Year II Roadmap for AES Confederation
excerpt: Ouagadougou, February 26, 2026 – A ministerial delegation representing the AES Confederation convened in Ouagadougou on Thursday, February 26, 2026, to review and finalize the draft Year II Roadmap. The delegation was led by Lieutenant General Sadio Camara, Minister of State, Min
title_en: Ministerial Meeting Finalizes Year II Roadmap for AES Confederation
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, February 26, 2026 – A ministerial delegation representing the AES Confederation convened in Ouagadougou on Thursday, February 26, 2026, to review and finalize the draft Year II Roadmap. The delegation was led by Lieutenant General Sadio Camara, Minister of State, Min
body_en:
Ouagadougou, February 26, 2026 – A ministerial delegation representing the AES Confederation convened in Ouagadougou on Thursday, February 26, 2026, to review and finalize the draft Year II Roadmap.
The delegation was led by Lieutenant General Sadio Camara, Minister of State, Minister of Defense and Veterans Affairs, and included:
Madina Sissoko Dembélé, Minister of Transport and Infrastructure
Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation
Moussa Alassane Diallo, Minister of Industry and Trade
Focus of the Meeting
The meeting, attended by ministers responsible for the three strategic pillars of the AES Confederation, aimed to:
Consolidate institutional and operational achievements
Define future priorities for the Confederation
Align the roadmap with security, political, and economic objectives
Progress and Leadership
During the opening ceremony, Heads of Delegation from Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger highlighted the significant progress made since the Confederation’s establishment. They attributed these achievements to strengthened coordination and the shared vision of the member states, emphasizing the leadership of Presidents Ibrahim Traoré, Assimi Goïta, and Abdourahamane Tiani.
The Year II Roadmap, which will be submitted for adoption by the Heads of State, is designed to sustainably strengthen integration, sovereignty, and solidarity among AES member countries, building on the momentum initiated during Mali’s inaugural presidency under President Assimi Goïta.

body_en:

The association, organizer of the International Tuareg Craft Week (SIAT), has been recognized for its sustained commitment to Malian artisanal heritage and efforts to showcase the richness and diversity of traditional craftsmanship.

Gao, February 15, 2026 – The Islamic State – Sahel Province claimed responsibility for an attack on a Malian army checkpoint located at the eastern entrance of Ansongo on the Ansongo-Ménaka road, carried out Sunday morning, February 15, 2026.
According to reports, the assailants used automatic weapons, prompting the immediate withdrawal of Malian soldiers from the site upon the attackers’ arrival.
Damage and Seizures
In its statement, the group reported:
Setting fire to an armored vehicle and a motorcycle near the post
Seizing two rifles and a medium machine gun
Withdrawing without suffering any losses after the operation
The attack caused material damage to the military installation and underscores the continuing security threats posed by extremist groups in the Gao region.

title: Deliberate Destruction of Water Points and Worsening Humanitarian Crisis
excerpt: Kidal, February 27, 2026 – Reports from the Kidal region indicate a growing humanitarian crisis linked to the actions of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by Russian mercenaries. Local sources state that in addition to the recurring abductions of women in villages and nom
title_en: Deliberate Destruction of Water Points and Worsening Humanitarian Crisis
excerpt_en: Kidal, February 27, 2026 – Reports from the Kidal region indicate a growing humanitarian crisis linked to the actions of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by Russian mercenaries. Local sources state that in addition to the recurring abductions of women in villages and nom
body_en:
Kidal, February 27, 2026 – Reports from the Kidal region indicate a growing humanitarian crisis linked to the actions of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa), supported by Russian mercenaries.
Local sources state that in addition to the recurring abductions of women in villages and nomadic settlements, these forces are systematically destroying water sources used by civilian populations. Previously, poisoning water points with barrels of acid and other harmful substances was reported; now, reports indicate the outright destruction of the few remaining functional water infrastructure.
A new incident was recorded on Friday, February 27, 2026, in the Efali nomadic settlement, about 20 kilometers northeast of Tessalit, during Ramadan. Residents claim that the destruction of water points is intended to suffocate local communities, expose them to thirst, and force displacement, aggravating an already severe humanitarian situation in northern Mali.
Conclusion
The second half of February 2026 reflects a Mali navigating a dual reality: a government actively asserting its sovereignty and regional leadership, while simultaneously facing a volatile security environment and worsening humanitarian concerns.
Strategic Sovereignty and Diplomacy
Mali has reinforced its “Mali-first” approach through the formalization of the AES Confederation Year II Roadmap, which prioritizes defense, diplomacy, and development independent of traditional Western frameworks. While the government maintains engagement with the European Union and the United Kingdom, it is pivoting decisively toward strategic partnerships with Saudi Arabia, China, and Iran.
Domestically, this orientation is reflected in new economic directives favoring local products and national companies in public procurement, signaling a push for economic self-reliance and support for Malian enterprises. Initiatives like Operation Sunkalo Solidarity 2026 further underscore the government’s emphasis on social cohesion, national unity, and community support.
Persistent Security and Humanitarian Friction
Despite these political and diplomatic strides, security challenges remain severe. The Mopti and Kidal regions continue to be flashpoints for asymmetric warfare, with JNIM and Islamic State – Sahel Province conducting frequent ambushes, IED attacks, and targeted operations against Malian forces and Russian mercenaries.
Compounding this, reports of water point destruction, abductions, and other human rights violations in northern Mali signal a deepening humanitarian crisis. These developments threaten the impact of national initiatives like Sunkalo Solidarity and underscore the fragile state of civilian protection in conflict-affected regions.
Looking Ahead
The trajectory of Mali’s transitional government will depend on whether the institutional consolidation of the AES Confederation can translate into tangible stability and security for populations in the northern and central regions, while maintaining social cohesion and advancing economic self-reliance.
By Maïga Sidi Bonkana
(Boukari Zankey Sidi)
Jeff Buleli

Compounding this, reports of water point destruction, abductions, and other human rights violations in northern Mali signal a deepening humanitarian crisis. These developments threaten the impact of national initiatives like Sunkalo Solidarity and underscore the fragile state of civilian protection in conflict-affected regions.
Looking Ahead
The trajectory of Mali’s transitional government will depend on whether the institutional consolidation of the AES Confederation can translate into tangible stability and security for populations in the northern and central regions, while maintaining social cohesion and advancing economic self-reliance.
By Maïga Sidi Bonkana
(Boukari Zankey Sidi)
Jeff Buleli

body_en:
Bamako, February 24, 2026 – As part of Operation “Sunkalo Solidarity 2026”, initiated by President of the Transition General Assimi Goïta, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Abdoulaye Diop participated in a collective iftar held at the ASKO grounds in Korofina on Tuesday, February 24, 2026. The event was attended by administrative, municipal, and religious authorities.
A Symbolic Gathering
The gathering, imbued with spiritual, social, and symbolic significance, fostered reflection, fraternity, and communal solidarity, bringing together diverse segments of Malian society around values of sharing, divine invocation, and civic unity.
Minister Diop emphasized that the month of Ramadan, coinciding this year with Christian Lent, provides Malians a chance to draw closer to God and strengthen bonds of fraternity, tolerance, and mutual respect among citizens.
Commitment to National Unity
The minister highlighted the commitment of Mali’s highest authorities to:
Strengthen social and religious values of solidarity
Promote civic engagement
Consolidate national unity in the face of challenges
He concluded by calling on all Malians to join hands in renewed solidarity, brotherly love, fervent prayer, and patriotic action, to build a united, strong, and cohesive Mali, embracing all citizens regardless of religion, ethnicity, or social background.

excerpt_en: Bamako, February 20, 2026 – Prime Minister Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, on behalf of Transitional President General Assimi Goïta, launched Operation “Sunkalo Solidarity 2026” Friday, delivering 600 tons of rice to vulnerable populations across Bamako and the regions. The launch
body_en:
Bamako, February 20, 2026 – Prime Minister Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, on behalf of Transitional President General Assimi Goïta, launched Operation “Sunkalo Solidarity 2026” Friday, delivering 600 tons of rice to vulnerable populations across Bamako and the regions.
The launch took place at the ASKO football field in Korofina, Commune I of Bamako District, marking the start of a nationwide social assistance campaign coordinated by the government.
Distribution Across the Country
The initiative is set to operate at multiple locations:
19 sites in Bamako
4 sites in Kati
3 sites per region in other areas of the country
Of the total 600 tons of rice, 400 tons are allocated to the regions, while 200 tons will support three key ministerial departments, ensuring assistance reaches those most in need.
A Commitment to Solidarity
Government officials described the operation as a demonstration of national solidarity, aiming to support vulnerable populations, strengthen social cohesion, and promote a spirit of communal assistance during challenging times.

title_en: Mauritania–Mali Border – Stranded Mauritanian Trucks at Gogui Spark Tensions
excerpt_en: Gogui, February 20, 2026 – Dozens of Mauritanian truck owners stranded on the Malian side of the border at Gogui are calling on Mauritanian authorities to intervene urgently amid a growing logistical and regulatory dispute. According to transporters, their vehicles have been immo
body_en:
Gogui, February 20, 2026 – Dozens of Mauritanian truck owners stranded on the Malian side of the border at Gogui are calling on Mauritanian authorities to intervene urgently amid a growing logistical and regulatory dispute.
According to transporters, their vehicles have been immobilized for a week by Malian authorities, who are detaining trucks arriving from Burkina Faso and Ivory Coast over alleged overloading violations.
Dispute Over Unloading Requirements
The transporters stated they are willing to rectify the infraction and pay fines, but criticized the requirement to completely unload their cargo, which they argue is contrary to current regulations.
The standoff highlights ongoing cross-border transport challenges between Mali and Mauritania, raising concerns about trade disruptions and bilateral commercial tensions.

excerpt: Ouagadougou, February 24, 2026 – Senior officials responsible for the three pillars of the Confederation of Sahel States (CESA/ESA) began a two-day meeting in the Burkinabe capital on Tuesday, February 24, 2026, to review and finalize the draft roadmap for Year Two of the Confede
title_en: Senior Officials Review Draft Roadmap for Year Two of ESA Confederation
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, February 24, 2026 – Senior officials responsible for the three pillars of the Confederation of Sahel States (CESA/ESA) began a two-day meeting in the Burkinabe capital on Tuesday, February 24, 2026, to review and finalize the draft roadmap for Year Two of the Confede
body_en:
Ouagadougou, February 24, 2026 – Senior officials responsible for the three pillars of the Confederation of Sahel States (CESA/ESA) began a two-day meeting in the Burkinabe capital on Tuesday, February 24, 2026, to review and finalize the draft roadmap for Year Two of the Confederation.
The draft, proposed by Burkina Faso, which has held the rotating presidency of the ESA since December 23, 2025, aims to consolidate the achievements of Year One and continue building the confederation.
Leadership and Delegations
The opening session was chaired by Bassolma Bazie, President of the National Commission of the AES Confederation and head of the Burkinabe delegation, alongside Bayard Mariama Gamatie, head of the Nigerien delegation, and Ambassador Mahamane Hamadou Maiga, head of the Malian delegation.
Objectives and Vision
Officials emphasized that the roadmap must:
Serve as a consensus-based guide for priority actions
Promote peace, security, and the fight against terrorism
Ensure free movement of people and goods
Support endogenous economic development
Reflect the shared vision of the three Heads of State
The Malian delegation stressed that completing the roadmap successfully is essential for enhancing the well-being of populations across the Confederation.
The Burkinabe delegation underlined that the process requires sacrifice, unity, consultation, and solidarity, noting:
“It is essential to act in unity, coherence, and complementarity because this is a confederation roadmap, and from this perspective, the teams from the three sister countries should come together to determine the direction they are taking.”
Next Steps
The 48-hour preparatory meeting will conclude on February 26, with the results submitted for consideration by ministers responsible for the three pillars of the AES Confederation: Defence-Security, Development, and Diplomacy.
The exercise is expected to provide a clear, actionable compass to guide the future development and cohesion of the Confederation.

body_en:
Bamako, February 20, 2026 – Mali has announced a new policy for public procurement, emphasizing national products and local companies, according to a government directive issued this month.
The Ministry of Economy and Finance, led by Minister Alousseïni Sanou, issued a memo on February 13, 2026, instructing all officials handling public contracts to prioritize Malian companies and products manufactured within the country.
Supporting SMEs and National Production
The decision aligns with a national decree guiding public procurement towards small and medium-sized enterprises (SMEs) and supporting domestic production under Malian law.
Officials noted that the measure also follows recommendations from a government meeting held on February 11, 2026, aimed at promoting economic sovereignty, local industry, and the growth of national businesses.
This new approach signals Mali’s commitment to strengthening the domestic economy while ensuring that public spending benefits local enterprises.

title: Mali Celebrates 299th Anniversary of Saudi Arabia’s Founding
excerpt: Bamako, February 23, 2026 – Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Abdoulaye Diop participated on Monday in the celebration of the 299th anniversary of the Founding of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, at the invitation of Saudi Ambassador to Mali, Abdullah Saleh Sa
title_en: Mali Celebrates 299th Anniversary of Saudi Arabia’s Founding
excerpt_en: Bamako, February 23, 2026 – Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Abdoulaye Diop participated on Monday in the celebration of the 299th anniversary of the Founding of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, at the invitation of Saudi Ambassador to Mali, Abdullah Saleh Sa
body_en:
Bamako, February 23, 2026 – Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation Abdoulaye Diop participated on Monday in the celebration of the 299th anniversary of the Founding of the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia, at the invitation of Saudi Ambassador to Mali, Abdullah Saleh Saber.
At the solemn and convivial ceremony, Minister Diop, on behalf of Mali’s highest authorities, congratulated His Majesty King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, and the Saudi people, extending wishes for happiness, peace, and prosperity.
Highlighting Shared Heritage and Cooperation
The Minister also emphasized the civilizational and religious heritage of Mali, recalling Mansa Kankou Moussa’s historic pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324. He expressed satisfaction with the long-standing friendship and cooperation between Mali and Saudi Arabia, citing major projects such as the Grand Mosque of Bamako and the second Bamako Bridge.
Strengthening Bilateral Partnership
Minister Diop and the Saudi Ambassador underscored the need to enhance bilateral cooperation through:
Mutually beneficial productive investments
Implementation of structuring development projects
Promotion of economic and trade exchanges
Close collaboration in the fight against terrorism in Mali and within the AES Confederation
The ceremony reinforced Mali’s commitment to deepening diplomatic and economic ties with Saudi Arabia in a spirit of solidarity and partnership.

Mali, February 27, 2026 – The Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM) released footage on Friday marking the graduation of a new class of fighters from the camp of Commander Abou Yahya al-Mouhajir. The group reportedly operates several training camps across Mali and Burkina Faso, regularly preparing new recruits.
In a separate video released the same day, JNIM claimed responsibility for an attack using improvised explosive devices (IEDs) targeting Malian army forces and Russian military allies in Kidal, near the village of Tiskadween (Tissadwen) close to Aguelhok. The operation, conducted on February 18, 2026, reportedly killed six militia members allied with the Malian army, under the command of General Gamaou.

body_en:
Bamako, February 19, 2026 – Mali’s Minister for Malians Abroad and African Integration, Mossa Ag Attaher, received German Ambassador Dr. Corinna Fricke Thursday to discuss bilateral cooperation and migration issues, according to official sources.
The meeting, held in Bamako, highlighted the long-standing ties between Mali and Germany, which have been maintained since Mali’s independence in 1960. Both officials reaffirmed their commitment to strengthening cooperation across multiple sectors.
Focus on Migration and Development Cooperation
Ambassador Dr. Fricke expressed satisfaction with ongoing initiatives, noting the success of the recent ESA Summit held in Mali and other concrete programs supporting development and migration management.
Minister Mossa Ag Attaher welcomed the Ambassador, congratulating her on her appointment and wishing her success in her mission, while emphasizing Mali’s continued commitment to deepening partnerships with international allies.
The discussion reflected both countries’ shared interest in promoting development, migration governance, and sustainable cooperation.

According to the group, the assault also led to the seizure of two military vehicles, several automatic weapons, ammunition, and other military equipment.

Mauritania/Mali, February 26, 2026 – The family of Hamidou Olsan Diallo, a Mauritanian businessman, has issued an urgent appeal to Minister of Foreign Affairs Mohamed Salem Ould Merzoug to intervene regarding his detention in Mali.
Family sources report that Diallo, a resident of Lebheir (Barkéol district), was arrested by the Malian army in Héït three days ago and has had no contact since.

Bamako, February 19, 2026 – Mali’s Minister of National Education, Dr. Amadou Sy Savane, met Thursday with British Ambassador Angus McKee to discuss ways to strengthen bilateral cooperation in education, officials reported.
The meeting, held in Bamako, brought together the ministers’ respective teams to review ongoing and future collaborations between Mali and the United Kingdom in the educational sector.
UK Support for Malian Education
Officials highlighted the United Kingdom’s support, both bilaterally and through multilateral initiatives, particularly the Global Partnership for Education (GPE), which contributes to improving access, quality, and equity in Mali’s education system.
Year of Education and Culture 2026-2027
Minister Sy Savane also reminded the British delegation of Mali’s decision to declare 2026–2027 as the “Year of Education and Culture”, emphasizing the government’s commitment to strengthening educational programs and cultural initiatives nationwide.
The meeting underscored the desire of both countries to expand cooperation, promote knowledge exchange, and support sustainable development in education.

title_en: Ministry of Justice Clarifies Postponement of e-Justice Platform Launch
excerpt_en: Bamako, February 20, 2026 – The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, Keeper of the Seals, announced that the launch of Mali’s e-Justice platform has been postponed, following administrative requirements needed to ensure secure digital access for all citizens. The announcement co
body_en:
Bamako, February 20, 2026 – The Ministry of Justice and Human Rights, Keeper of the Seals, announced that the launch of Mali’s e-Justice platform has been postponed, following administrative requirements needed to ensure secure digital access for all citizens.
The announcement comes after the inaugural digital issuance of criminal records and nationality certificates, which was celebrated on February 10, 2026, as part of the 4th edition of Justice Week at the Ministry of Justice.
Reasons for the Delay
Officials explained that the delay is due to essential administrative formalities required to guarantee:
Secure digital access for Malians at home and abroad
Proper functionality and protection of sensitive legal documents
The official launch date and details on access and usage will be communicated in a future press release.
Public Advisory
The Minister of Justice urged the public to remain vigilant and cautious, warning against misinformation or unauthorized initiatives that could compromise the integrity of the digital services.
Authorities emphasized that the postponement is intended to ensure a safe, reliable, and fully operational e-Justice platform for the nation.

title_en: GSIM Landmine Attack Kills Six Militia Members Near Aguelhok
excerpt_en: Kidal, February 18, 2026 – The Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (GSIM) announced that it targeted a military vehicle carrying Malian army personnel and Russian mercenaries with a landmine near Tiskdouine, on the outskirts of Aguelhok, on Wednesday evening, February 18,
body_en:
Kidal, February 18, 2026 – The Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (GSIM) announced that it targeted a military vehicle carrying Malian army personnel and Russian mercenaries with a landmine near Tiskdouine, on the outskirts of Aguelhok, on Wednesday evening, February 18, 2026.
According to reports, the explosion killed six militia members affiliated with General El Hadj Ag Gamou, including the son of the sub-prefect of Tajamert, who was serving as acting prefect of Aguelhok.
Details of the Attack
The victims were escorting a convoy of Russian mercenaries tasked with securing logistical supplies. Local sources indicate that several of the deceased had previously been implicated in the deaths of dozens of civilians in the same area.
The incident underscores the persistent threats posed by armed groups in the Kidal region and highlights the risks faced by militias and foreign personnel operating in conflict zones.

body_en:
Bamako, February 17, 2026 – Mali’s Prime Minister Abdoulaye Maïga held talks Tuesday with European Union Special Representative for the Sahel João Gomes Cravinho, who presented the EU’s new strategy for engagement in the Sahel, officials said.
The meeting took place at the Prime Minister’s Office in Bamako, where the EU envoy was received in the presence of Foreign Affairs Minister Abdoulaye Diop, who formally introduced the visiting delegation.
EU Seeks Renewed Engagement
During the visit, João Gomes Cravinho, accompanied by the Head of the European Union Delegation to Mali, outlined the key pillars of what Brussels describes as a “New Approach” to the Sahel.
According to the EU representative, the strategy aims to:
Maintain the European Union’s commitment in the Sahel
Improve political dialogue
Strengthen cooperation with Sahel states
Rebuild mutual trust
He noted that the 27 member states of the European Union have agreed on the need to revitalize relations with countries in the Sahel region.
Focus on Political Dialogue
The discussions emphasized the importance of constructive dialogue between Mali and the European Union, at a time when regional security and development challenges remain significant.
The visit forms part of ongoing diplomatic consultations between Mali and its international partners, aimed at redefining cooperation frameworks and strengthening strategic partnerships in the Sahel.

title: AES Confederation – Prime Minister Chairs Strategic Meeting on Year II Roadmap
excerpt: Bamako, February 17, 2026 – Mali’s Prime Minister chaired a high-level meeting on Tuesday to review and advance the Year II roadmap of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), marking a new phase in the regional alliance’s development. The session, held at the Prime Minister’s Of
title_en: AES Confederation – Prime Minister Chairs Strategic Meeting on Year II Roadmap
excerpt_en: Bamako, February 17, 2026 – Mali’s Prime Minister chaired a high-level meeting on Tuesday to review and advance the Year II roadmap of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), marking a new phase in the regional alliance’s development. The session, held at the Prime Minister’s Of
body_en:
Bamako, February 17, 2026 – Mali’s Prime Minister chaired a high-level meeting on Tuesday to review and advance the Year II roadmap of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES), marking a new phase in the regional alliance’s development.
The session, held at the Prime Minister’s Office in Bamako, brought together members of the steering committee of the AES national committee to discuss the adoption of a consensus-based roadmap for the confederation’s second year of operations.
Irreversible Regional Alliance
Officials described the AES Confederation as an established and irreversible regional framework, strongly supported by the three member states:
Captain Ibrahim Traoré, President of Burkina Faso and current AES Chair
General Assimi Goïta, Transitional President of Mali
General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of Niger
The alliance was presented as a key instrument for strengthening regional sovereignty, security cooperation, and economic integration in the Sahel.
Building on Year I Achievements
Participants reviewed the concrete achievements of Year I, implemented under Mali’s presidency, and discussed priorities for the coming year.
According to officials, the Year II roadmap will incorporate lessons learned during the first phase and will be developed through consultation with all member states.
Three Strategic Pillars
The new roadmap is structured around three main pillars:
Defense and Security
Diplomacy
Development
Authorities said the plan aims to strengthen collective security, improve regional coordination, and promote sustainable development across AES member countries.
The meeting concluded with a commitment to finalize and implement the consensus roadmap, seen as a key step in consolidating the institutional framework of the AES Confederation.

The event, held at the ASKO grounds, brought together administrative officials, municipal authorities, and religious leaders in what participants described as a moment of spiritual reflection, community sharing, and social cohesion during the holy month of Ramadan.
Promoting Solidarity and National Unity
Officials said the initiative aims to reinforce social and religious values, encourage civic engagement, and strengthen national unity at a time when the country continues to face major political and security challenges.
Speaking at the gathering, Minister Diop emphasized the importance of faith, solidarity, and collective responsibility, noting that recent difficulties faced by Mali highlight the need for national cohesion and divine guidance.

The minister also pointed out that the coincidence of Ramadan with the Christian Lent offers a unique opportunity for Malians to deepen both spiritual devotion and social solidarity.
He called on citizens to strengthen brotherhood, mutual assistance, and patriotism, urging Malians to work together in a spirit of active solidarity and national commitment.
Minister Diop concluded by appealing for prayers, unity, and patriotic action, stressing that Mali remains a nation that brings together all its citizens regardless of religion or ethnicity.

title: Saudi Arabia Strengthen Ties During Saudi Founding Day Celebration
excerpt: Bamako, February 23, 2026 – Mali reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia during celebrations marking the 299th anniversary of Saudi Founding Day held Monday in Bamako. Foreign Affairs Minister Abdoulaye Diop attended the c
title_en: Saudi Arabia Strengthen Ties During Saudi Founding Day Celebration
excerpt_en: Bamako, February 23, 2026 – Mali reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia during celebrations marking the 299th anniversary of Saudi Founding Day held Monday in Bamako. Foreign Affairs Minister Abdoulaye Diop attended the c
body_en:
Bamako, February 23, 2026 – Mali reaffirmed its commitment to strengthening bilateral cooperation with the Kingdom of Saudi Arabia during celebrations marking the 299th anniversary of Saudi Founding Day held Monday in Bamako.
Foreign Affairs Minister Abdoulaye Diop attended the ceremony at the invitation of Saudi Ambassador Abdullah Saleh Saber, representing the Malian authorities at the official event.
Official Congratulations to Saudi Leadership
Speaking on behalf of Mali’s leadership, Minister Diop conveyed congratulations and best wishes to King Salman bin Abdulaziz Al Saud, Custodian of the Two Holy Mosques, as well as to Crown Prince Mohammed bin Salman, Prime Minister of Saudi Arabia, and to the Saudi people.
The Malian minister highlighted the historic religious and civilizational ties linking Mali and Saudi Arabia, recalling the famous pilgrimage to Mecca in 1324 by Mansa Kankou Moussa, one of the most renowned rulers of the Mali Empire.
Longstanding Cooperation
Minister Diop praised the longstanding friendship and cooperation between the two countries, noting several major achievements supported by Saudi Arabia, including:
The Grand Mosque of Bamako
The Second Bamako Bridge
Various development projects
These projects were presented as symbols of strong diplomatic relations and solidarity between the two nations.
Toward Stronger Economic Partnership
Both Malian and Saudi officials stressed the importance of expanding cooperation through productive investments and structuring development projects aimed at boosting economic and trade exchanges.
Discussions also highlighted the need for closer collaboration in the fight against terrorism in Mali and across the AES Confederation, reflecting shared security priorities in the Sahel region.
Officials from both sides expressed their commitment to building a mutually beneficial partnership based on solidarity, economic cooperation, and regional stability.

body_en:
Bamako, February 17, 2026 – The Government of Mali and the European Union (EU) held a high-level working session on Tuesday aimed at strengthening political dialogue and redefining cooperation in the Sahel, according to official sources.
The meeting brought together Foreign Affairs Minister Abdoulaye Diop and Minister for Malians Abroad Mossa Ag Attaher with a European delegation led by EU Special Representative for the Sahel João Gomes Cravinho, who was on an official visit to Bamako.
Focus on New Cooperation Framework
During what officials described as frank and interactive discussions, Malian authorities emphasized a strategic shift in governance, highlighting the country's determination to ensure national sovereignty, self-determination, and sustainable development.
Minister Diop presented Mali’s new governance vision, stressing the authorities’ commitment to taking control of the country’s political and security trajectory.
Talks focused on several key issues, including:
The EU’s new intervention approach in the Sahel
Ongoing security challenges linked to terrorism
The role of hybrid armed actors and state sponsors
The importance of a confederal dimension in Sahel interventions
Strengthening pragmatic and realistic cooperation
Priority Areas Identified
Both sides discussed cooperation in areas of common interest, including:
Peace and reconciliation under national ownership
Management of regular migration

title: ESA Foreign Ministers Engage Citizen Watchdogs to Combat Disinformation
excerpt: Ouagadougou, February 28, 2026 – The foreign ministers of the ESA Confederation participated on Friday, February 27, 2026, in a confederal forum of citizen watchdog organizations from Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso, organized by the National Coordination of Citizen Watchdog Associ
title_en: ESA Foreign Ministers Engage Citizen Watchdogs to Combat Disinformation
excerpt_en: Ouagadougou, February 28, 2026 – The foreign ministers of the ESA Confederation participated on Friday, February 27, 2026, in a confederal forum of citizen watchdog organizations from Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso, organized by the National Coordination of Citizen Watchdog Associ
body_en:
Ouagadougou, February 28, 2026 – The foreign ministers of the ESA Confederation participated on Friday, February 27, 2026, in a confederal forum of citizen watchdog organizations from Mali, Niger, and Burkina Faso, organized by the National Coordination of Citizen Watchdog Associations (CNAVC).
Theme and Objectives
The forum, held under the theme “The Strategic Role of Citizen Watchdogs in Defending the Sovereignty of the ESA Region in the Face of Disinformation and the War on Information”, aimed to:
Empower citizens to counter fake news and disinformation
Protect the image and sovereignty of the AES leadership
Harmonize responsible civic engagement across member states
According to Labidi Naba, general rapporteur of the forum, the event addresses the need to restructure, frame, and harmonize civic participation to support political action and defend the Confederation from external influence.
Participation and Key Messages
The meeting was chaired by H.E. Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré, Minister of Foreign Affairs of Burkina Faso, and attended by H.E. Bakary Yaou Sangare of Niger and H.E. Abdoulaye Diop of Mali.
The ministers emphasized:
Citizen mobilization as a key political asset to support ongoing AES actions and thwart destabilization efforts (Bakary Yaou Sangare)
The importance of information and communication technologies to promote cultural values and support governments (Abdoulaye Diop)
The need for a change in mindset and unity among citizens to highlight AES successes and counter disinformation (Karamoko Jean Marie Traoré)
Outcome and Next Steps
The forum concludes on Saturday, February 28, at the Thomas Sankara Memorial, with the drafting of:
The Citizen Vigilance Charter
A roadmap to guide future actions
The initiative reflects a growing focus on active citizen vigilance as a tool to protect sovereignty, strengthen regional unity, and counter information warfare across the ESA Confederation.

excerpt: Bamako, February 16, 2026 – Prime Minister and Head of Government Major General Abdoulaye Maïga conducted visits Thursday to key storage facilities for essential goods, as part of efforts to guarantee availability and accessibility of critical products for the Malian population.

Bamako, February 16, 2026 – Prime Minister and Head of Government Major General Abdoulaye Maïga conducted visits Thursday to key storage facilities for essential goods, as part of efforts to guarantee availability and accessibility of critical products for the Malian population.
The visits were carried out under directives from Transitional President and Head of State, Army General Assimi Goïta, aimed at strengthening food security and market stability.
Warehouses Stocked with Essential Goods
At the Mamadou Diarra S.A. warehouses, the Prime Minister observed stocks of:
15,000 tons of sugar
45,000 tons of rice
During his visit to Gaakoye et Frères establishments, he noted large quantities of rice, sugar, and cooking oil, confirming sufficient supplies for market distribution.
Government Commended for Efforts
Major General Maïga praised the Government’s coordination, particularly through the Ministry of Industry and Trade, for ensuring efficient supply chains and supporting the population’s access to essential goods during a critical period.

According to local sources, the attackers took control of the post, set fire to multiple vehicles and equipment, and then withdrew from the site.

title: Macron and Tshisekedi Discuss Eastern DRC Crisis and Francophonie Leadership
excerpt: Paris, February 25, 2026 – French President Emmanuel Macron held talks with DRC President Félix Tshisekedi at the Élysée Palace on Wednesday, focusing on the security and humanitarian situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo as well as strengthening bilateral cooperation
title_en: Macron and Tshisekedi Discuss Eastern DRC Crisis and Francophonie Leadership
excerpt_en: Paris, February 25, 2026 – French President Emmanuel Macron held talks with DRC President Félix Tshisekedi at the Élysée Palace on Wednesday, focusing on the security and humanitarian situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo as well as strengthening bilateral cooperation
body_en:
Paris, February 25, 2026 – French President Emmanuel Macron held talks with DRC President Félix Tshisekedi at the Élysée Palace on Wednesday, focusing on the security and humanitarian situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo as well as strengthening bilateral cooperation between Paris and Kinshasa.
The meeting comes amid ongoing diplomatic efforts to address the conflict in North and South Kivu, where fighting between armed groups and government forces continues to fuel a severe humanitarian crisis. According to officials from both countries, the two leaders discussed regional peace initiatives and the role of international partners in supporting stability in the Great Lakes region.
Macron and Tshisekedi last met on January 23, 2026, during a working visit by the Congolese president to Paris. That meeting also focused on the humanitarian situation in eastern DRC and ways to reinforce political, economic, and security cooperation between the two countries.
France recently welcomed Tshisekedi’s agreement to support a ceasefire proposal put forward by Angola, urging all parties involved in the conflict to respect the initiative. Paris has also stressed the need to fully implement the Washington Peace Agreement of December 4, 2025, calling on regional actors to honor their commitments and contribute to the de-escalation of tensions.
During their discussions, the two presidents also addressed the Democratic Republic of Congo’s candidacy for the leadership of the International Organisation of La Francophonie (OIF). Kinshasa has expressed interest in playing a greater role within the Francophonie, with the organization expected to elect its next Secretary-General at the Francophonie Summit scheduled for November 2026 in Cambodia.
Beyond the security situation, the meeting allowed Macron and Tshisekedi to review broader areas of cooperation, reflecting the longstanding partnership between France and the Democratic Republic of Congo, particularly in diplomacy, development, and multilateral engagement.
By Jeff Buleli

title: DRC Remains Among Most Corrupt Countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, Transparency International Reports
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 10, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) continues to rank among the worst-performing countries globally in terms of perceived corruption, according to the 2025 Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) published by Transparency International. With a score of
title_en: DRC Remains Among Most Corrupt Countries in Sub-Saharan Africa, Transparency International Reports
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 10, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) continues to rank among the worst-performing countries globally in terms of perceived corruption, according to the 2025 Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) published by Transparency International. With a score of
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 10, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) continues to rank among the worst-performing countries globally in terms of perceived corruption, according to the 2025 Corruption Perceptions Index (CPI) published by Transparency International.
With a score of 20 out of 100, the DRC remains at the bottom of the global ranking, reflecting persistent challenges in governance and public accountability. Sub-Saharan Africa, as a region, also performs poorly, with a regional average of 32 points. Only four of the 49 countries assessed scored above 50.
Transparency International notes that, since 2012, ten countries in the region have seen significant deterioration in corruption perception, while only seven improved, illustrating the ineffectiveness of anti-corruption efforts. The DRC remains stagnant, with no notable improvement in recent years.
The NGO highlights the human impact of corruption, stating that it hinders access to essential services and affects the most vulnerable populations the hardest. It calls on governments to implement strong measures to fight corruption and strengthen democratic governance.
Regional comparisons include:
Angola, score 32, improved 17 points since 2015 but still ranks low
Mozambique, lost 10 points over the past decade
Seychelles, top regional performer with 68 points, facing judicial delays in a money laundering case
Lowest scores: Sudan (14), Eritrea (13), Somalia (9), South Sudan (9)
“Corruption in the public sector always hits the most vulnerable people the hardest,” said Paul Banoba, Regional Advisor for Africa at Transparency International. He urged African governments to translate commitments into decisive action, including strengthening oversight institutions, enhancing transparency, and protecting civic space.

The incident occurred early on Saturday, January 31, in Mubi Centre, Walikale territory. Two judicial police officers were executing an arrest warrant for Kambale Muhindo Jean, a suspected member of an armed group accused of illegal possession of weapons.
According to the investigation, when the suspect attempted to evade arrest, Sergeant Maleso Buka Pierre fired his weapon without orders, fatally shooting the victim.
The military court not only sentenced him to death but also ordered payment of USD 10,000 in damages (equivalent in Congolese francs) to the victim’s family.
The prosecution described the verdict as “educational,” emphasizing that it sends a strong message against abuses by law enforcement officers.
Major Dieudonné Kasereka, head of communications for the 34th Military Region, highlighted that the ruling reinforces the obligation for security forces to respect rules of engagement and human rights, even during law enforcement operations.
