title: UN’s Jean-Pierre Lacroix Meets CENCO-ECC on Social Pact for Peace
excerpt: Kinshasa DRC, February 11, 2026 – During his ongoing working visit to the Democratic Republic of Congo, Jean-Pierre Lacroix, United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations, met with representatives of the Church of Christ in Congo (ECC) and the National Episcopal Con
title_en: UN’s Jean-Pierre Lacroix Meets CENCO-ECC on Social Pact for Peace
excerpt_en: Kinshasa DRC, February 11, 2026 – During his ongoing working visit to the Democratic Republic of Congo, Jean-Pierre Lacroix, United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations, met with representatives of the Church of Christ in Congo (ECC) and the National Episcopal Con
body_en:
Kinshasa DRC, February 11, 2026 – During his ongoing working visit to the Democratic Republic of Congo, Jean-Pierre Lacroix, United Nations Under-Secretary-General for Peace Operations, met with representatives of the Church of Christ in Congo (ECC) and the National Episcopal Conference of Congo (CENCO) to discuss the implementation of the Social Pact for Peace and the broader push for an inclusive national dialogue.
The ECC delegation was led by Pastor Maurice Mondengo, Deputy Chief of Staff to the National President of the ECC in charge of communication, media, and public relations, while CENCO was represented by Father Georges Kalenga, Deputy Secretary-General of the episcopate.
Speaking on the outcomes of the meeting, Pastor Mondengo highlighted discussions on operationalizing commitments from recent diplomatic negotiations in Washington and Doha, which aim to stabilize eastern DRC and promote lasting peace.
“UN Under-Secretary-General Jean-Pierre Lacroix, a man of peace, expressed his satisfaction and encouragement for our social pact initiative for peace and harmonious coexistence to continue its progress. He believes that through this initiative, we will achieve the long-awaited dialogue in Congo, and an inclusive dialogue,” Pastor Mondengo stated.
Although a joint roadmap for the national dialogue initiative has been validated with other religious denominations and the Presidency of the Republic, implementation by the government has been slow. Pastor Mondengo emphasized that rebuilding mutual trust remains crucial for progress.
“The well-being of Congo, the return of peace to Congo, is first and foremost a matter for the Congolese people. It does not necessarily depend on the support of the United Nations. It depends on you and me,” he added.
Following a meeting of African leaders in Luanda on February 9, Angola was tasked with initiating consultations with all relevant Congolese parties to create conditions for a national inter-Congolese dialogue. President Félix Tshisekedi has previously recognized the importance of national dialogue, although certain proposed conditions were rejected by opposition parties.
The opposition continues to demand an inclusive dialogue to foster national cohesion, at a time when M23/AFC rebels, reportedly supported by Rwanda, continue advancing in the east, seizing territories across North Kivu and South Kivu.
The discussions with CENCO and ECC underscore ongoing efforts by religious leaders and the UN to promote peaceful coexistence and create conditions for a comprehensive political dialogue in eastern DRC.

title: AFC/M23 Rebels Withdraw from Buhaya Near Pinga
excerpt: February 13, 2026 – AFC/M23 fighters withdrew overnight on Thursday, February 12, from the Buhaya position, a strategic hill overlooking Katobi in the Banakindi area, approximately 15 kilometers from Pinga in the Kisimba group, Walikale territory, North Kivu. The rebels had occup
title_en: AFC/M23 Rebels Withdraw from Buhaya Near Pinga
excerpt_en: February 13, 2026 – AFC/M23 fighters withdrew overnight on Thursday, February 12, from the Buhaya position, a strategic hill overlooking Katobi in the Banakindi area, approximately 15 kilometers from Pinga in the Kisimba group, Walikale territory, North Kivu. The rebels had occup
body_en:
February 13, 2026 – AFC/M23 fighters withdrew overnight on Thursday, February 12, from the Buhaya position, a strategic hill overlooking Katobi in the Banakindi area, approximately 15 kilometers from Pinga in the Kisimba group, Walikale territory, North Kivu.
The rebels had occupied Buhaya Hill since November 2025, after dislodging Wazalendo forces. The reason for the sudden withdrawal remains unknown, and no information is available about the fighters’ destination, according to the administrative secretary of Kisimba group, who confirmed the departure.
Residents of Katobi reported discovering on Friday morning that Buhaya Hill had been abandoned. Later in the day, Wazalendo forces regained control of the position, which they had lost three months earlier.
The withdrawal occurs amid a continuing unstable security situation in Walikale, where the movements of armed groups continue to fuel fear and uncertainty among the civilian population.

title_en: Eight Sentenced to Death, Including Mayor, Two Acquitted
excerpt_en: Panu February 16, 2026 – Idiofa, Kwilu Province – The Kikwit Garrison Military Court handed down eight death sentences, including that of Mayor Xénon Mufele of the semi-rural commune of Panu, following deadly clashes on February 3, 2026. Two other defendants were acquitted and re
body_en:
Panu February 16, 2026 – Idiofa, Kwilu Province – The Kikwit Garrison Military Court handed down eight death sentences, including that of Mayor Xénon Mufele of the semi-rural commune of Panu, following deadly clashes on February 3, 2026. Two other defendants were acquitted and released.
The court found the eight convicted individuals guilty of terrorism, rejecting any mitigating circumstances. In addition to the death penalty, each must pay US$25,000 to the eight civil parties, including General Angel Yanbgonga, Deputy Divisional Commissioner of Police for Kwilu, who will receive US$5,000 from each convicted person. A further 100,000 Congolese francs per person must be paid within eight days to cover court costs.
The clashes erupted early on February 3, after police arrested two suspected bandits, prompting gang members to seize them from custody. Four people, including two police officers, were killed during the violence.
The military prosecutor had requested the death penalty for all defendants, while also calling for the acquittal of Kibala Chadrac, a request partially upheld by the court.

title_en: New Clashes Between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo Disrupt Daily Life
excerpt_en: Kavumu, South Kivu, February 22, 2026 – The security situation in Kavumu, Kabare territory, remains chaotic after new clashes erupted on Sunday morning between AFC/M23 elements and the Wazalendo. The exchanges of fire, which began around 5:00 a.m., have paralyzed daily activities
body_en:
Kavumu, South Kivu, February 22, 2026 – The security situation in Kavumu, Kabare territory, remains chaotic after new clashes erupted on Sunday morning between AFC/M23 elements and the Wazalendo.
The exchanges of fire, which began around 5:00 a.m., have paralyzed daily activities in the town and surrounding areas. Residents have stayed indoors, churches remain empty, and public transportation has been disrupted.
Markets, shops, and businesses have been closed since the early hours, while local communities continue to live in fear amid the ongoing tensions.
These clashes follow days of violence in the Kabare territory, with confrontations between the warring parties first intensifying on Friday.

title: DRC-US Strategic Partnership Enters Implementation Phase
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 9, 2026 – The first meeting of the Joint Steering Committee between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United States, held on February 5, marks a major step in the operationalization of the strategic partnership between the two countries. Key Developments
title_en: DRC-US Strategic Partnership Enters Implementation Phase
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 9, 2026 – The first meeting of the Joint Steering Committee between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United States, held on February 5, marks a major step in the operationalization of the strategic partnership between the two countries. Key Developments
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 9, 2026 – The first meeting of the Joint Steering Committee between the Democratic Republic of Congo and the United States, held on February 5, marks a major step in the operationalization of the strategic partnership between the two countries.
Key Developments
The Committee reviewed the initial Strategic Asset Reserve submitted by the Congolese side, which will guide American private sector investments in the DRC. Projects supported by the U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) are prioritized, and American technical teams will be deployed on the ground to identify areas for specific financial and technical support.
The meeting formally activates the Joint Steering Committee as the central body for implementing the agreement, with a defined timetable and regular sessions.
Political Implications
The partnership is now moving from declarative commitments to a structured, institutional mechanism. The Committee serves as a permanent coordination forum, involving several Congolese ministries and U.S. agencies, reducing dependence on short-term political dynamics and creating a stable framework for collaboration.
Economic Implications
Economically, the focus has shifted from general promotion to presenting specific, bankable assets and projects. The inclusion of technical assistance on the ground and project review mechanisms ensures a move from a logic of intention to a logic of execution. Projects that fail to generate interest are re-evaluated after 18 months, reflecting a pragmatic, market-oriented approach.
Governance of Strategic Sectors
The partnership introduces regular dialogue mechanisms on sensitive economic issues, including cobalt export quotas. Congolese authorities are required to provide periodic briefings to the U.S. Embassy, strengthening transparency, accountability, and internal coordination.
A joint committee for the Grand Inga hydroelectric project highlights the strategic importance of this long-term infrastructure initiative and sets a framework for financial and institutional structuring.
Next Steps
The real impact of the partnership will depend on the ability of Congolese institutions to:
Speak with one voice
Propose bankable projects
Translate joint recommendations into actionable regulatory and fiscal decisions
While this initial meeting does not immediately transform the Congolese economic landscape, it establishes a technical, implementation-focused framework that underpins the future strategic collaboration between the DRC and the United States.

title: Grace Bilolo, Governor of Kongo Central, Released After First Hearing Over Alleged Embezzlement
excerpt: February 10, 2026 – Grace Kuanga Bilolo, Governor of Kongo Central, appeared before the prosecutor’s office near the Court of Cassation in Kinshasa on Tuesday following allegations of financial misconduct and embezzlement of public funds. He was released after the first hearing.
title_en: Grace Bilolo, Governor of Kongo Central, Released After First Hearing Over Alleged Embezzlement
excerpt_en: February 10, 2026 – Grace Kuanga Bilolo, Governor of Kongo Central, appeared before the prosecutor’s office near the Court of Cassation in Kinshasa on Tuesday following allegations of financial misconduct and embezzlement of public funds. He was released after the first hearing.
body_en:
February 10, 2026 – Grace Kuanga Bilolo, Governor of Kongo Central, appeared before the prosecutor’s office near the Court of Cassation in Kinshasa on Tuesday following allegations of financial misconduct and embezzlement of public funds. He was released after the first hearing.
The hearing focused on a report by the General Inspectorate of Finance (IGF), which audited Bilolo's administration in 2025. According to his defense lawyers, Bilolo presented his arguments and stated that no alarming irregularities had been found relative to prior media reports.
Espoir Siasi, legal advisor to the governor, said: “We remain at the disposal of the justice system, but everything has been done. The governor was released and has returned home. Any further charges will be communicated by the prosecutor if necessary.”
The IGF report revealed multiple alleged irregularities, including:
Non-payment of provincial tax and duty revenues amounting to 24,928,597 Congolese francs.
Misappropriation of USD 137,417.04 transferred improperly to the Provincial Assembly.
USD 440,889 used for vehicle acquisition for provincial deputies.
USD 35,183 not allocated to public works.
USD 423,720 owed to Decentralized Territorial Entities (ETD) of Muanda, which remained unpaid.
The Attorney General, Firmin Mvonde, classified these acts as embezzlement of public funds, punishable under Article 145 of the Penal Code (Book II). The governor was invited to present his version regarding the seriousness of these allegations.

Non-payment of provincial tax and duty revenues amounting to 24,928,597 Congolese francs.
Misappropriation of USD 137,417.04 transferred improperly to the Provincial Assembly.
USD 440,889 used for vehicle acquisition for provincial deputies.
USD 35,183 not allocated to public works.
USD 423,720 owed to Decentralized Territorial Entities (ETD) of Muanda, which remained unpaid.

excerpt_en: February 13, 2026 – The Batakirwa area of the Bafuna group (Wanianga sector) in Walikale territory, North Kivu, is facing a serious security crisis as two Wazalendo factions compete for control of the region. Since February 11, the Uhuru RDC armed group, led by Mashite Kashira, h
body_en:
February 13, 2026 – The Batakirwa area of the Bafuna group (Wanianga sector) in Walikale territory, North Kivu, is facing a serious security crisis as two Wazalendo factions compete for control of the region.
Since February 11, the Uhuru RDC armed group, led by Mashite Kashira, has deployed fighters in the villages of Kilambo, Buringa, and Iseya, threatening clashes with NDC-Rénové fighters under Muissa Shimiray Guidon if they attempt to enter the area. Local sources report that Uhuru RDC claims exclusive control over this mineral-rich territory, denying other armed groups any operational presence.
Civilians are caught in the crossfire. The local chief, who received threats, was forced to flee to Walikale town. He reported that residents are regularly intimidated by Uhuru RDC fighters, accused of supporting their rivals, NDC-Rénové.
“The population is in grave danger. These armed men openly threaten civilians and equate them with their enemies,” declared Chief Kabaki.
The chief has issued an urgent appeal to military and administrative authorities to intervene swiftly and defuse tensions before the situation escalates further, risking additional loss of life.

body_en:
February 16, 2026 – Kateku, Ikobo group, Walikale territory, North Kivu – The five civilians abducted during the armed incursion attributed to AFC/M23 rebels on Thursday, February 13, remain missing.
Local sources confirm that no information has emerged about the hostages’ whereabouts or the intentions of their captors. Traditional and administrative authorities report no sign of life from the victims.
"So far, we have no news of our compatriots. All efforts undertaken with community leaders and security services have been unsuccessful," stated a local official.
Families of the abducted civilians are in deep distress. “We spend our nights without sleep; we don’t even know if they’re still alive,” said a family member.
Civil society in Walikale is calling for the swift and unconditional release of the hostages and urges provincial and national authorities to strengthen civilian protection in this volatile area.

excerpt_en: South Kivu, February 21, 2026 – Residents of Kavumu and surrounding areas in the Kabare territory are living in fear following exchanges of fire between AFC/M23 rebels and the Wazalendo. The fighting began in the morning, briefly subsided, and then resumed in the evening. Locals
body_en:
South Kivu, February 21, 2026 – Residents of Kavumu and surrounding areas in the Kabare territory are living in fear following exchanges of fire between AFC/M23 rebels and the Wazalendo.
The fighting began in the morning, briefly subsided, and then resumed in the evening. Locals reported hearing gunfire from as far as Katana to Kavumu.
In the evening, clashes reportedly resumed around 6:30 p.m., coinciding with a noticeable reinforcement of Wazalendo forces near the shopping center.
The violence disrupted traffic along the main road linking Bukavu to Kavumu, forcing residents to stay indoors as combatants positioned weapons along key routes.
Authorities have yet to release official statements, but local communities remain on high alert amid the tensions.

title: IMF Reports DRC Structural Reforms Met but Remain Fragile
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 9, 2026 – The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has presented a generally positive assessment of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s structural reforms, following the second review of the program supported under the Extended Credit Facility (ECF). The report not
title_en: IMF Reports DRC Structural Reforms Met but Remain Fragile
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 9, 2026 – The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has presented a generally positive assessment of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s structural reforms, following the second review of the program supported under the Extended Credit Facility (ECF). The report not
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 9, 2026 – The International Monetary Fund (IMF) has presented a generally positive assessment of the Democratic Republic of Congo’s structural reforms, following the second review of the program supported under the Extended Credit Facility (ECF).
The report notes that the majority of structural benchmarks were met on schedule, with seven out of eight benchmarks achieved on time, and the remaining one completed with a slight delay. Additionally, three ongoing benchmarks were also fulfilled.
Key advances highlighted by the IMF include:
Strengthening the expenditure chain
Progressive decentralization of budget allocation
Implementation of instruments to improve monetary policy transmission
Enhanced revenue forecasting from the extractive sector
However, the IMF notes persistent institutional weaknesses and legislative delays, particularly regarding the standardized VAT invoicing system, which was not fully adopted by the planned date despite significant progress.
The report warns that while administrative and executive decisions have accelerated reform, this reliance creates institutional fragility in the absence of a stronger legislative framework. It emphasizes the need to:
Sustainably strengthen public financial management
Limit emergency procedures
Improve control and traceability of public expenditures
The IMF concludes that progress on structural reforms is real and significant, supporting the credibility of the program, but stresses that reforms must be consolidated institutionally to ensure long-term sustainability.

title: Mobile Phone Services Restored After Month-Long Outage in North and South Kivu
excerpt: February 17, 2026 – Mobile phone networks were restored overnight in several territories around Goma (North Kivu) and in Kalehe (South Kivu) after nearly one month of service disruption, according to local witnesses. Subscribers of Vodacom, Orange, and Airtel can now communicate
title_en: Mobile Phone Services Restored After Month-Long Outage in North and South Kivu
excerpt_en: February 17, 2026 – Mobile phone networks were restored overnight in several territories around Goma (North Kivu) and in Kalehe (South Kivu) after nearly one month of service disruption, according to local witnesses. Subscribers of Vodacom, Orange, and Airtel can now communicate
body_en:
February 17, 2026 – Mobile phone networks were restored overnight in several territories around Goma (North Kivu) and in Kalehe (South Kivu) after nearly one month of service disruption, according to local witnesses.
Subscribers of Vodacom, Orange, and Airtel can now communicate again in Nyiragongo, Rutshuru, Lubero, Masisi, and Walikale in North Kivu. The signal was restored around 11 p.m. on Monday.
Residents reported that during the outage, making calls, sending messages, and accessing the internet had been extremely difficult, forcing some to travel several kilometers to reach minimal coverage areas. “The restoration allows us to resume communication, improves information flow, and even facilitates mobile payments for teachers and healthcare workers in rural areas,” one resident explained.
The communications blackout also had broader consequences, including disrupted commercial activities, challenges for Virunga National Park conservation operations, and difficulties for humanitarian and health workers in monitoring and responding to emergencies.
While no official statement has confirmed the cause, a Vodacom technician in Walikale reported that the disruption originated in Kinshasa, where heavy rains damaged satellite link devices in Maluku, causing cascading outages in multiple provinces.

title: Death Toll from ADF Attack in Mambimbi-Isigo Rises to 21
excerpt: Lubero February 10, 2026 – The death toll from the recent attack attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in Mambimbi-Isigo, located in the Bapakombe groupement, Bapere sector, in Lubero territory (North Kivu), has risen from 15 to 21 civilians killed, with several people
title_en: Death Toll from ADF Attack in Mambimbi-Isigo Rises to 21
excerpt_en: Lubero February 10, 2026 – The death toll from the recent attack attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in Mambimbi-Isigo, located in the Bapakombe groupement, Bapere sector, in Lubero territory (North Kivu), has risen from 15 to 21 civilians killed, with several people
body_en:
Lubero February 10, 2026 – The death toll from the recent attack attributed to the Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) in Mambimbi-Isigo, located in the Bapakombe groupement, Bapere sector, in Lubero territory (North Kivu), has risen from 15 to 21 civilians killed, with several people still reported missing.
According to Kakule Kagheni Samuel, president of the local civil society in Bapere, six additional bodies were discovered on Monday, bringing the total number of victims to twenty-one. The attack occurred during the night of Friday, February 6, to Saturday, February 7, 2026. Assailants reportedly set fire to homes and destroyed property during the incursion.
Initial reports had confirmed at least fifteen deaths, including two women, along with the burning of several houses. Survivors described scenes of devastation, with one witness stating he was unable to count the number of bodies encountered while fleeing. Civil society had earlier reported a provisional toll of fifteen dead and seven houses burned.
The attack followed several days of reported ADF movements in the area. Residents had raised alerts about the presence of suspected rebels for more than four days prior to the assault. The security situation deteriorated rapidly, triggering mass displacement toward Njiapanda and other localities considered relatively safer.
Local sources indicate that the affected village remained inaccessible until Saturday evening, delaying the burial of victims, as several bodies were still lying at the scene.
The violence extends beyond Lubero. In neighboring Beni territory, six civilians were killed in an ambush on the evening of February 4, 2026, in Malibo, along the Oicha–Mamove road. The attack came just hours after another ambush on the same road that claimed four additional lives. In total, at least ten civilians were killed in one day, with several motorcycles burned during the assaults.
In a report released on February 3, the North Kivu provincial civil society coordination indicated that at least 63 civilians have been killed since the beginning of the year by suspected ADF rebels in Beni and Lubero territories. Of these, 52 deaths were recorded in Lubero and 10 in Beni, making Lubero the hardest-hit area.
Beyond the human toll, the attacks have caused extensive material damage, including the burning of a health post, 67 shops, and 10 houses, as well as the destruction of 23 motorcycles and a traditional “barza” used for community meetings.
The repeated violence has forced thousands of families into displacement, leaving them in precarious humanitarian conditions. Ongoing insecurity continues to prevent residents from returning to several localities now classified as high-risk zones, deepening the crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

The repeated violence has forced thousands of families into displacement, leaving them in precarious humanitarian conditions. Ongoing insecurity continues to prevent residents from returning to several localities now classified as high-risk zones, deepening the crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

February 13, 2026 – The village of Kateku, in the Ikobo group of Walikale territory, North Kivu, experienced systematic looting on the night of Thursday, February 13, local sources report. Armed men reportedly stormed the village while residents were asleep, surrounding the area before carrying out a methodical theft operation.
Witnesses stated that the looters went house to house, stealing livestock, cell phones, money, and other valuables. Residents blamed AFC/M23 rebels, who maintain control over parts of the region.
Following the attack, the assailants retreated to an unknown location, leaving behind a traumatized and impoverished population. By Friday morning, fear and despair dominated the village, according to local reports.
In response to the resurgence of violence, several residents are considering leaving Kateku to seek safety, fearing further attacks in the coming days.

excerpt_en: February 16, 2026 – Maasha, Ikobo group, Walikale territory, North Kivu – A convoy of traders traveling from Lubero to the Malimingi mining site was attacked by unidentified armed men on Saturday, February 15, in Maasha. According to administrative and security sources from the W
body_en:
February 16, 2026 – Maasha, Ikobo group, Walikale territory, North Kivu – A convoy of traders traveling from Lubero to the Malimingi mining site was attacked by unidentified armed men on Saturday, February 15, in Maasha.
According to administrative and security sources from the Wanianga sector, the assailants systematically looted the convoy, stealing money, cell phones, and merchandise. The victims, traumatized by the attack, were forced to return to Rusamambu. No fatalities were reported.
This incident highlights the ongoing insecurity in Walikale, where multiple armed groups operate and frequently target traders on strategic routes. A similar attack occurred in November 2025 along the same route.
Local traders and economic stakeholders are urging authorities to strengthen security measures to ensure safe passage to mining sites and protect the movement of people and goods.

title: Divergent Views on the Humanitarian Situation in Eastern DRC
excerpt: February 21, 2026 – Goma, North Kivu, DRC – The humanitarian crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo is being framed in starkly contrasting terms by two key actors. Hadja Lahbib, European Commissioner for Crisis Preparedness, Management, and Equality, described the situati
title_en: Divergent Views on the Humanitarian Situation in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: February 21, 2026 – Goma, North Kivu, DRC – The humanitarian crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo is being framed in starkly contrasting terms by two key actors. Hadja Lahbib, European Commissioner for Crisis Preparedness, Management, and Equality, described the situati
body_en:
February 21, 2026 – Goma, North Kivu, DRC – The humanitarian crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo is being framed in starkly contrasting terms by two key actors. Hadja Lahbib, European Commissioner for Crisis Preparedness, Management, and Equality, described the situation as “catastrophic” after her regional tour, while Corneille Nangaa, political coordinator of the AFC/M23, portrayed territories under his control as “the most secure area in the country.”
Hadja Lahbib’s Assessment
During her tour of the DRC, Burundi, and Rwanda, Commissioner Lahbib highlighted severe humanitarian challenges:
Over 21 million people in eastern DRC require emergency aid.
Nearly 28 million people face food insecurity.
Violence continues to cause repeated displacement, human rights violations, conflict-related sexual violence, and disease outbreaks.
Refugee flows into neighboring countries, particularly Burundi, strain limited resources.
Lahbib stressed the urgent need to improve humanitarian access, open safe corridors, and ensure the continuation of basic services.
Corneille Nangaa’s Perspective
In contrast, Nangaa claimed that areas controlled by the AFC/M23 constitute the most secure regions of eastern DRC. He cited:
Territories under his control cover 62,000 km², hosting around 20 million Congolese.
He rejects notions of foreign occupation, asserting, “We are not Rwandans, we are in Congo. A territory cannot be occupied by its own citizens.”
Nangaa pledged that humanitarian access will be guaranteed within M23-controlled zones.
He indicated that catastrophic situations are concentrated in Minembwe, Uvira, Beni, and Ituri, highlighting ongoing attacks and massacres outside his areas of influence.
Conflict Data Highlights
Despite Nangaa’s claims, available data shows continued violence across the region:
Uvira and Fizi plateaus: FARDC, supported by Burundi’s FDNB, launched offensives against M23 positions; Twirwaneho-M23-Red Tabara coalition engaged in multiple clashes.
North Kivu: 52 of 113 clashes documented in January occurred here; Rutshuru, Masisi, and Walikale saw heavy fighting.
Civilians targeted: Drone strikes, grenade attacks, and armed sweeps resulted in dozens of deaths, including in Mpombi, Kirumba, Sange, and other villages.
Uvira recapture: January 2026 operations by FARDC and Wazalendo led to at least 151 civilian deaths.
Refugee crisis: Tens of thousands of Congolese fled to Burundi, exacerbating humanitarian needs.
Analysis
The conflicting narratives underscore a diffuse conflict with no clearly demarcated front lines. While the European Commission emphasizes a dire humanitarian emergency, the AFC/M23 stresses relative security within its territories. Ground reports, however, indicate ongoing violence, civilian casualties, and displacement, casting doubt on claims of stability.
The situation highlights the complexity of eastern DRC: a multi-layered conflict involving government forces, local armed groups, and rebel coalitions, with civilians disproportionately affected.

title: President Félix Tshisekedi Appoints New Directors to RVA, ARE, SOKIMO, and Gécamines
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 23, 2026 – President Félix Tshisekedi appointed several directors to lead key public enterprises through a series of presidential decrees read on national television (RTNC). Kinkey Mulumba at RVA Blaise Londole and Vincent Futa were appointed Director General a
title_en: President Félix Tshisekedi Appoints New Directors to RVA, ARE, SOKIMO, and Gécamines
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 23, 2026 – President Félix Tshisekedi appointed several directors to lead key public enterprises through a series of presidential decrees read on national television (RTNC). Kinkey Mulumba at RVA Blaise Londole and Vincent Futa were appointed Director General a
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 23, 2026 – President Félix Tshisekedi appointed several directors to lead key public enterprises through a series of presidential decrees read on national television (RTNC).
Kinkey Mulumba at RVA
Blaise Londole and Vincent Futa were appointed Director General and Deputy Director General, respectively, of the Civil Aviation Authority (RVA). Tryphon Kinkey Mulumba was reappointed as Chairman of the Board of Directors. Londole succeeds Ngoma Mbaki, suspended by the Minister of State Enterprises following a malfunction at N’djili International Airport.
Jean-Marie Beya at ARE
At the Electricity Regulatory Authority (ARE), Jean-Marie Beya was named Chairman of the Board of Directors, while Soraya Aziz becomes Managing Director, assisted by Marco Nkuyu as Deputy Managing Director.
Deogratias Ngele Masudi at Gécamines
In the mining sector, Baraka Kabemba was appointed Managing Director of Gécamines, and Deogratias Ngele Masudi becomes Chairman of the Board of Directors of the state-owned mining company.
François Kakese at SOKIMO
A new Management Committee was also appointed to lead the Kilomoto Mining Company (SOKIMO SA). François Kakese Kimaza, formerly Quality and Performance Manager in the Office of the Head of State, becomes Chairman of the Board of Directors, while Yanick Nzonde Mulundu is named Managing Director, succeeding Pistis Bonongo, and Placide Nkala Basadilwa becomes Deputy General Manager (DGA).
These appointments signal a renewed leadership across critical transport, energy, and mining sectors in the DRC.

title: Eight Missing After Kalelu Ferry Accident Between Lomami and Kasai-Oriental
excerpt: February 13, 2026 – At least eight people are missing following an incident on the Kalelu ferry, which links the Bakua Mulumba chiefdom (Lomami province) to the Bakua Kalonji chiefdom (Kasai-Oriental province). The accident occurred Friday morning during the transport of a vehicl
title_en: Eight Missing After Kalelu Ferry Accident Between Lomami and Kasai-Oriental
excerpt_en: February 13, 2026 – At least eight people are missing following an incident on the Kalelu ferry, which links the Bakua Mulumba chiefdom (Lomami province) to the Bakua Kalonji chiefdom (Kasai-Oriental province). The accident occurred Friday morning during the transport of a vehicl
body_en:
February 13, 2026 – At least eight people are missing following an incident on the Kalelu ferry, which links the Bakua Mulumba chiefdom (Lomami province) to the Bakua Kalonji chiefdom (Kasai-Oriental province).
The accident occurred Friday morning during the transport of a vehicle on the ferry. According to eyewitnesses, around twelve people were in the vehicle.
As the ferry approached the shore and disembarkation began, the vehicle driver started the engine and suddenly put it in reverse, causing the vehicle to strike the ferry’s edge and plunge into the river.
Four passengers, including the driver, were rescued, while eight others remain missing. Search operations are ongoing to locate the victims.
Authorities are investigating the incident to determine the cause of the accident and assess safety measures on the ferry.

title: Armed Attack in Kavumu Leaves Couple and Child Dead
excerpt: Kabare February 10, 2026 – Three members of the same family, including a couple and their nearly five-year-old child, were killed in an armed attack carried out by unidentified assailants in Kavumu, within Kabare territory, in South Kivu. According to local sources, including rep
title_en: Armed Attack in Kavumu Leaves Couple and Child Dead
excerpt_en: Kabare February 10, 2026 – Three members of the same family, including a couple and their nearly five-year-old child, were killed in an armed attack carried out by unidentified assailants in Kavumu, within Kabare territory, in South Kivu. According to local sources, including rep
body_en:
Kabare February 10, 2026 – Three members of the same family, including a couple and their nearly five-year-old child, were killed in an armed attack carried out by unidentified assailants in Kavumu, within Kabare territory, in South Kivu.
According to local sources, including representatives of civil society in Kabare, the attack took place on the night of Sunday, February 8, at around 9:00 p.m. in the sub-village of Chirhodu, located in the Bugorhe groupement in Kavumu.
The victims were identified as Janvier Ombeni Bagula, his wife, and their young child. The circumstances surrounding the attack remain unclear, and no group has claimed responsibility.
Local civil society actors have strongly condemned the killings and are calling for reinforced security measures in the area. They are also urging residents to cooperate closely with security services to help prevent further violence.
The incident adds to growing concerns over persistent insecurity in parts of South Kivu, where armed attacks against civilians continue to be reported.

title: Rival Wazalendo Groups Clash Over Control of Katatwa-Karete Axis
excerpt: February 13, 2026 – Security remains precarious along the Katatwa–Otobora–Karete axis, in the Ibiro area of the Bakano group, Walikale territory, North Kivu, where two Wazalendo factions are fighting for control of this strategic stretch of National Route 3. The rival groups incl
title_en: Rival Wazalendo Groups Clash Over Control of Katatwa-Karete Axis
excerpt_en: February 13, 2026 – Security remains precarious along the Katatwa–Otobora–Karete axis, in the Ibiro area of the Bakano group, Walikale territory, North Kivu, where two Wazalendo factions are fighting for control of this strategic stretch of National Route 3. The rival groups incl
body_en:
February 13, 2026 – Security remains precarious along the Katatwa–Otobora–Karete axis, in the Ibiro area of the Bakano group, Walikale territory, North Kivu, where two Wazalendo factions are fighting for control of this strategic stretch of National Route 3.
The rival groups include the Mai-Mai Kifuafua, led by Shukuru Bulenda, and Raia Mutomboki, under the command of Kalumende. Local sources report that these rivalries have persisted for about two months, creating a constant threat of armed clashes as both sides assert ownership of the road.
A key consequence of this dispute is the proliferation of illegal roadblocks. Travelers along the route are forced to pay fixed sums at multiple checkpoints, often under threat of violence or reprisals.
“We are suffering because of the selfish interests of those in charge of these armed groups. You pay here, then a few meters further on, you pay again to the other side. It’s a real ordeal,” testified one traveler.
Reports also indicate cases of torture and ill-treatment for those unable to pay the imposed taxes. Residents are further burdened by the requirement to feed fighters daily, intensifying the hardship for a population already weakened by chronic insecurity.
Many families have begun fleeing their villages to escape this pressure, worsening the humanitarian crisis in the area.
“Several people are starting to leave the area. It’s better to live on the move than to remain in this form of slavery,” said a resident of Ibiro.
Civil society in Walikale has condemned the actions of these armed groups and called on military authorities to intervene urgently to protect civilians and prevent the situation from escalating into deadly clashes.
The Katatwa–Karete axis, part of National Route 3, is a crucial corridor for trade between Hombo and Walikale, making it a highly coveted area for armed groups seeking to finance their operations through illegal taxation. The ongoing struggle has effectively turned this key economic route into a lawless zone, severely impacting the local population.
body_fr:
February 13, 2026 – Security remains precarious along the Katatwa–Otobora–Karete axis, in the Ibiro area of the Bakano group, Walikale territory, North Kivu, where two Wazalendo factions are fighting for control of this strategic stretch of National Route 3.

“Several people are starting to leave the area. It’s better to live on the move than to remain in this form of slavery,” said a resident of Ibiro.

The Katatwa–Karete axis, part of National Route 3, is a crucial corridor for trade between Hombo and Walikale, making it a highly coveted area for armed groups seeking to finance their operations through illegal taxation. February 16, 2026 – Chanjikiro, Kisimba group, North Kivu – Nine fighters from the AFC/M23 rebellion voluntarily surrendered to the Wazalendo (Volunteers for the Defense of the Homeland) on Saturday, February 15, in Chanjikiro, Banamukema area. excerpt_en: February 20, 2026 – Rutshuru, North Kivu, DRC – An MSF (Médecins Sans Frontières) convoy carrying medical supplies was attacked on Wednesday, February 18, by armed men in Matin ya Moto, within Virunga National Park in the Rutshuru territory. The convoy was en route to the Kibiriz
body_en:
February 20, 2026 – Rutshuru, North Kivu, DRC – An MSF (Médecins Sans Frontières) convoy carrying medical supplies was attacked on Wednesday, February 18, by armed men in Matin ya Moto, within Virunga National Park in the Rutshuru territory. The convoy was en route to the Kibirizi health zone in the Bwito chiefdom.
During the attack, staff members were physically intimidated and had personal belongings seized; one team member sustained minor injuries. All MSF staff are reported safe and accounted for, and the medical supplies were successfully delivered.
The ambush also affected other travelers on the route, with civilians being robbed. MSF emphasized its continued commitment to supporting vulnerable populations despite the persistent insecurity and called for the protection of humanitarian operations in the region.
Local civil society notes that attacks on this strategic route are becoming increasingly frequent. Earlier, on February 1, another convoy traveling from Rutshuru to Butembo on the Rwindi–Kanyabayonga road was ambushed by unidentified armed men, in an area reportedly under AFC/M23 control at the time.
This incident highlights ongoing risks to humanitarian missions and civilians in North Kivu, where armed groups frequently target convoys along key transport routes.

title: DRC and Four African Countries Plan One-Stop Border Crossings to Boost Intra-African Trade
excerpt: Dubai, UAE, February 18, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo, Zambia, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, and Botswana have agreed to establish one-stop border crossings aimed at streamlining trade and reducing transport delays. The project was the focus of a technical meeting in Dubai, at
title_en: DRC and Four African Countries Plan One-Stop Border Crossings to Boost Intra-African Trade
excerpt_en: Dubai, UAE, February 18, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo, Zambia, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, and Botswana have agreed to establish one-stop border crossings aimed at streamlining trade and reducing transport delays. The project was the focus of a technical meeting in Dubai, at
body_en:
Dubai, UAE, February 18, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo, Zambia, Mozambique, Zimbabwe, and Botswana have agreed to establish one-stop border crossings aimed at streamlining trade and reducing transport delays.
The project was the focus of a technical meeting in Dubai, attended by the foreign trade ministers of the five countries, representatives from DP World, and the Secretary-General of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), Wamkele Mene.
According to Congolese Minister Julien Paluku Kahongya, the initiative, launched during the 39th African Union Summit in Addis Ababa, will lower transport costs and make products more competitive.
“Following the Addis Ababa meeting, we are continuing discussions here in Dubai with our counterparts from Mozambique, Zambia, Zimbabwe, and Botswana, along with AfCFTA and DP World, on the construction of one-stop border crossings to streamline trade and eliminate long vehicle queues at our borders,” said Minister Paluku.
AfCFTA Secretary-General Wamkele Mene highlighted that the initiative supports the effective implementation of the African Continental Free Trade Area, aiming to further promote intra-African trade. The meeting also addressed the financing model for these border infrastructures.

title: DRC Plans Stricter Regulation of Gambling Sector
excerpt: February 11, 2026 – National Deputy Willy Mishiki Buhini submitted a bill to the National Assembly aimed at regulating the gambling sector in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The proposed legislation seeks to establish procedures for collecting royalties and contributions from g
title_en: DRC Plans Stricter Regulation of Gambling Sector
excerpt_en: February 11, 2026 – National Deputy Willy Mishiki Buhini submitted a bill to the National Assembly aimed at regulating the gambling sector in the Democratic Republic of Congo. The proposed legislation seeks to establish procedures for collecting royalties and contributions from g
body_en:
February 11, 2026 – National Deputy Willy Mishiki Buhini submitted a bill to the National Assembly aimed at regulating the gambling sector in the Democratic Republic of Congo.
The proposed legislation seeks to establish procedures for collecting royalties and contributions from gambling activities, while strengthening state control over a sector that generates significant financial resources, much of which currently escapes the public treasury.
According to Deputy Mishiki, who represents Walikale (North Kivu), this initiative aligns with the DRC’s strategic partnership commitments with the United States, particularly regarding the fight against money laundering and financing of terrorism.
“Our legislation no longer allows the Congolese state to effectively control this sector,” he said. He also highlighted social concerns: gambling addiction is impacting impoverished communities, further deepening poverty.
The bill includes a 5% tax on gambling revenue and proposes reforms to the National Lottery Society, modeled after the Canadian Lottery, which finances over 60% of social housing. Deputy Mishiki claims that, if implemented, the law could allow the state to recover nearly two billion dollars and strengthen the financial system.

title: MONUSCO Plans Aerial Reconnaissance Over Uvira Ahead of Gradual Ground Deployment
excerpt: Uvira South Kivu February 10, 2026 – The United Nations peacekeeping mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo is preparing a gradual resumption of operations in the country’s east, beginning with aerial reconnaissance flights over Uvira, pending security guarantees. According
title_en: MONUSCO Plans Aerial Reconnaissance Over Uvira Ahead of Gradual Ground Deployment
excerpt_en: Uvira South Kivu February 10, 2026 – The United Nations peacekeeping mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo is preparing a gradual resumption of operations in the country’s east, beginning with aerial reconnaissance flights over Uvira, pending security guarantees. According
body_en:
Uvira South Kivu February 10, 2026 – The United Nations peacekeeping mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo is preparing a gradual resumption of operations in the country’s east, beginning with aerial reconnaissance flights over Uvira, pending security guarantees.
According to a UN source, the mission intends to launch reconnaissance flights as a first step, to be followed by a limited ground deployment, and eventually a progressive increase in troop presence, subject to recommendations expected before March. Officials stress that “nothing will be done without security guarantees,” a message reportedly conveyed to relevant parties and diplomatic representatives.
Securing Uvira, in South Kivu, is described as a key priority during this initial phase. The operational timeline foresees the reopening of the air route, followed by surveillance flights, and then a possible ground deployment if conditions permit. No official figures have been disclosed regarding the number of personnel to be deployed.
The stated objective of this phase is to support the implementation of the ceasefire, with MONUSCO expected to initiate its verification and observation mandate.
However, the United Nations underscores that it cannot single-handedly guarantee the success of peace efforts. The process also depends on the engagement of the agreement’s guarantors, notably the United States, Qatar, and the African Union.
This phased return would precede the approval of a full operational mandate expected in March, particularly concerning South Kivu. The UN aims to rapidly re-establish its footprint on the ground while preparing recommendations focused on operational efficiency and cost-effectiveness.

title: ADF Attack in Ilimba Kills Two Civilians
excerpt: February 13, 2026 – Violence continues to grip Beni territory, North Kivu, as Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters carried out an attack on Thursday, February 12, in Ilimba, a village along the Oicha–Mantumbi road, killing two civilians. Local sources report that the victims w
title_en: ADF Attack in Ilimba Kills Two Civilians
excerpt_en: February 13, 2026 – Violence continues to grip Beni territory, North Kivu, as Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters carried out an attack on Thursday, February 12, in Ilimba, a village along the Oicha–Mantumbi road, killing two civilians. Local sources report that the victims w
body_en:
February 13, 2026 – Violence continues to grip Beni territory, North Kivu, as Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) fighters carried out an attack on Thursday, February 12, in Ilimba, a village along the Oicha–Mantumbi road, killing two civilians.
Local sources report that the victims were the wife and son of the president of the Mantumbi civil society organization, both shot with firearms. In addition, two motorcycles were burned during the assault.
“In Miliese, where they were stopped by the Congolese army, the enemy set fire to a motorcycle near a military position. They also bypassed the area to kill civilians in Ilimba, where they shot and killed the wife of the president of the civil society organization and his son. Another motorcycle was also set ablaze,” said Kakule Katena, spokesperson for civil society in Mantumbi. He urged residents to remain vigilant and called on the Congolese government to intensify operations to track down the assailants.
This attack comes three days after a deadly assault in Mangadu, where five farmers were killed, and has further intensified the climate of fear that has gripped the Beni-Mbau area since the beginning of the week, following multiple ADF attacks on civilians.

title: Over 20 Schools Closed Amid Rising ADF Violence
excerpt: Beni, North Kivu DRC February 16, 2026 – At least 23 schools—15 primary and 8 secondary—have suspended operations in the Malio and Mwenye areas of the Bashu chiefdom due to escalating insecurity caused by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) attacks. The closures have affected schools
title_en: Over 20 Schools Closed Amid Rising ADF Violence
excerpt_en: Beni, North Kivu DRC February 16, 2026 – At least 23 schools—15 primary and 8 secondary—have suspended operations in the Malio and Mwenye areas of the Bashu chiefdom due to escalating insecurity caused by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) attacks. The closures have affected schools
body_en:
Beni, North Kivu DRC February 16, 2026 – At least 23 schools—15 primary and 8 secondary—have suspended operations in the Malio and Mwenye areas of the Bashu chiefdom due to escalating insecurity caused by Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) attacks.
The closures have affected schools in villages including Vurondo, Kisasa, Ndondi, Kiriva, Kisungu, Vulera, Kyondo, and Kitumbu, leaving students and teachers displaced to nearby towns such as Butuhe and Butembo. Classes have been suspended since Monday, January 26, disrupting the academic calendar, particularly the first semester exams for secondary students.
Civil society leaders are calling on the Congolese government and school authorities to:
Strengthen security measures in affected villages.
Protect school infrastructure from looting or occupation by armed groups.
Ensure displaced students can complete the school year.
The school closures coincide with continued ADF attacks in the region:
Upende/Mangadu (Feb 10): Four civilians, including a woman, were executed, most by beheading.
Mavete (Feb 14): Two civilians killed while traveling to their fields.
Since the start of 2026, at least 63 civilians have been killed by suspected ADF fighters in Beni and Lubero territories, with Lubero being the hardest hit (52 deaths) compared to Beni (10 deaths), according to the North Kivu provincial civil society coordination.
The growing threat has left parents and residents fearful for their safety, highlighting the urgent need for restored security and protection of civilian life and education in the region.

title: European Commissioner Hadja Lahbib Arrives in Goma Amid Humanitarian Briefings

title_en: European Commissioner Hadja Lahbib Arrives in Goma Amid Humanitarian Briefings
excerpt_en: February 20, 2026 – Goma, North Kivu, DRC – The European Commissioner for Equality, Preparedness and Crisis Management, Hadja Lahbib, arrived in Goma today as part of her tour of the Great Lakes region, focusing on humanitarian and protection issues. The morning began with a brie
body_en:
February 20, 2026 – Goma, North Kivu, DRC – The European Commissioner for Equality, Preparedness and Crisis Management, Hadja Lahbib, arrived in Goma today as part of her tour of the Great Lakes region, focusing on humanitarian and protection issues.
The morning began with a briefing on the humanitarian access situation with INSO and OCHA at the ECHO office, followed by meetings with national organizations addressing protection concerns in the city.
Commissioner Lahbib also visited Ndosho Hospital, supported by the International Committee of the Red Cross (ICRC), where she was briefed on the surgical response, trends in injuries treated, and toured critical care units, including a confidential discussion with two patients.
A working lunch was held with humanitarian partners, including international NGOs and UN representatives, to discuss coordination and operational challenges.
Later in the afternoon, the commissioner is scheduled to meet with AFC/M23 representatives to emphasize humanitarian access concerns and discuss the potential reopening of Goma airport. Lahbib visited Rwanda the previous day as part of her regional mission.
This visit underscores the urgent need for improved humanitarian access in eastern DRC, where ongoing conflict continues to affect civilians and disrupt essential services.

title: European Union Allocates €81 Million in Humanitarian Aid for Eastern DRC
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 17, 2026 – The European Union (EU) has announced the release of €81.2 million in emergency humanitarian aid to support vulnerable populations affected by the escalating conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The funding aims to assist displaced commu
title_en: European Union Allocates €81 Million in Humanitarian Aid for Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 17, 2026 – The European Union (EU) has announced the release of €81.2 million in emergency humanitarian aid to support vulnerable populations affected by the escalating conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The funding aims to assist displaced commu
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 17, 2026 – The European Union (EU) has announced the release of €81.2 million in emergency humanitarian aid to support vulnerable populations affected by the escalating conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The funding aims to assist displaced communities, address resource scarcity, and provide essential services to Congolese refugees in neighboring countries and fragile communities in Burundi.
The announcement coincides with a visit to the region by European Commissioner for Crisis Management, Hadja Lahbib, who is assessing urgent humanitarian needs on the ground.
“The objective is to secure the opening of safe corridors to provide relief to hundreds of thousands of people, including those in areas controlled by armed groups,” Lahbib said, emphasizing the need for safe humanitarian access.
The conflict in eastern DRC has resulted in severe shortages of food and water, inadequate shelter, and increased vulnerability of women and children to violence and exploitation.
Commissioner Lahbib’s visit itinerary includes:
Kinshasa, DRC – initial assessments and meetings with key stakeholders
Burundi (February 18–19) – including a planned visit to the Busuma refugee camp, where conditions are particularly dire, with insufficient water, food, and shelter
Kigali, Rwanda (February 20) – to conclude the regional mission
The EU’s intervention underscores the importance of coordinated humanitarian efforts in response to the ongoing crisis in the Great Lakes region.

title_en: DRC Investigates Alleged Biometric Passport Price Hikes in Beni
excerpt_en: February 12, 2026 – The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has dispatched a team to Beni, in North Kivu, to investigate reports of an illegal increase in the price of biometric passports. While the official fee is set at USD 75, some applicants claim to have paid up to USD 125 at the mo
body_en:
February 12, 2026 – The Ministry of Foreign Affairs has dispatched a team to Beni, in North Kivu, to investigate reports of an illegal increase in the price of biometric passports.
While the official fee is set at USD 75, some applicants claim to have paid up to USD 125 at the mobile data capture centers established in Beni and Butembo in October 2025.
Leading the mission, Teddy Kamembo Milambo, the Ministry’s Director of Legal Affairs and Litigation, urged citizens not to use intermediaries.
“If the allegations are true, it is up to the higher authorities to take the toughest possible action. The authorities' objective in setting the official price was to ease the difficulties faced by the population,” he said.
He emphasized that the official fee remains USD 75 and instructed citizens to submit applications directly, without intermediaries. “Those with old passports should continue to use them. No country rejects these documents,” he added.

title: Man Dies in Detention After Alleged Torture by Wazalendo Militiamen in Musimba
excerpt: Lubero February 10, 2026 – A man from Kirumba, in Lubero territory, died on Sunday, February 8, while detained in an underground cell allegedly run by Wazalendo militiamen in Musimba, on the southern outskirts of Butembo, in North Kivu. According to local civil society sources in
title_en: Man Dies in Detention After Alleged Torture by Wazalendo Militiamen in Musimba
excerpt_en: Lubero February 10, 2026 – A man from Kirumba, in Lubero territory, died on Sunday, February 8, while detained in an underground cell allegedly run by Wazalendo militiamen in Musimba, on the southern outskirts of Butembo, in North Kivu. According to local civil society sources in
body_en:
Lubero February 10, 2026 – A man from Kirumba, in Lubero territory, died on Sunday, February 8, while detained in an underground cell allegedly run by Wazalendo militiamen in Musimba, on the southern outskirts of Butembo, in North Kivu.
According to local civil society sources in Musimba, the victim is said to have died after being subjected to torture while held in what residents describe as a clandestine detention facility. The man had initially been accused of rape, arrested, and later granted provisional release by judicial authorities.
However, the decision reportedly triggered opposition from those who had arrested him, who allegedly organized his re-arrest before transferring him to the Wazalendo militia.
He was subsequently taken to an underground cell in Musimba, where he later died. The exact circumstances of his death remain disputed. Leaders of the Wazalendo militia deny allegations of torture, claiming instead that the detainee committed suicide by hanging.
The incident has reignited concerns over human rights abuses attributed to certain local armed groups operating in the region. Civil society actors accuse some militias of conducting arbitrary arrests, operating illegal detention centers, and assuming roles reserved for judicial institutions without legal mandate.
Civil society representatives in Musienene report that the victim’s body remains at the morgue of the Musienene General Referral Hospital, pending burial arrangements.
In the wider area, particularly in the Baswagha chiefdom and Musienene, Wazalendo-affiliated fighters have repeatedly faced accusations of looting, harassment, sexual violence, illegal taxation, the establishment of unauthorized roadblocks, and other abuses against civilians.
Human rights organizations have previously raised alarm over violations committed in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. In a report published on August 20, Amnesty International denounced serious abuses involving both the M23 rebellion and certain local armed groups, including elements associated with the Wazalendo militia.
The latest death is likely to intensify calls for greater oversight of armed groups operating alongside or in support of local security efforts, as concerns grow over accountability and the protection of civilians.

excerpt: Mulema Walikale February 12, 2026 – The security situation in northern Walikale territory, North Kivu, continues to deteriorate after fifteen civilians were abducted on Tuesday, February 10, in Muteresi, part of the Mulema area in the Kisimba groupement. Local traditional sources
title_en: Fifteen Civilians Abducted by Wazalendo Fighters in Mulema
excerpt_en: Mulema Walikale February 12, 2026 – The security situation in northern Walikale territory, North Kivu, continues to deteriorate after fifteen civilians were abducted on Tuesday, February 10, in Muteresi, part of the Mulema area in the Kisimba groupement. Local traditional sources
body_en:
Mulema Walikale February 12, 2026 – The security situation in northern Walikale territory, North Kivu, continues to deteriorate after fifteen civilians were abducted on Tuesday, February 10, in Muteresi, part of the Mulema area in the Kisimba groupement.
Local traditional sources report that the victims, all displaced farmers from Mulema, were traveling from Rusamambu in the Ikobo group, where they had sought refuge, to their fields in Minga to collect food for their families.
The civilians were reportedly ambushed by Wazalendo fighters from the CMC group of Bigabo before reaching their fields and have been held captive in Muteresi ever since. The motives for their detention remain unclear.
Families of the hostages, still in Rusamambu, expressed deep concern, having received no news of their loved ones. They are urgently appealing for their release so that they can return home and provide for their dependents.
Several villages in the Mulema area have remained largely deserted due to recurring clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters. Many displaced families have sought refuge in Rusamambu, Bukumbirwa, and Buleusa, living in precarious humanitarian conditions amid ongoing insecurity.

title: Traffic Resumes on Chivanga-Bulambika Road Despite Rebel Harassment

title_en: Traffic Resumes on Chivanga-Bulambika Road Despite Rebel Harassment
excerpt_en: February 15, 2026 – South Kivu – Road traffic resumed on Sunday, February 8, along the Chivanga–Kalonge–Bulambika–Hombo road in Kalehe territory, offering relief after months of paralysis caused by clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters. Motorcycle taxi drivers are
body_en:
February 15, 2026 – South Kivu – Road traffic resumed on Sunday, February 8, along the Chivanga–Kalonge–Bulambika–Hombo road in Kalehe territory, offering relief after months of paralysis caused by clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo fighters.
Motorcycle taxi drivers are now transporting goods from Bukavu to Hombo, enabling a tentative resumption of commerce. However, users report harassment at rebel checkpoints:
AFC/M23 rebels at Chivanga are reportedly demanding 50,000 FC per motorcycle.
Wazalendo fighters at the entrance to Kahuzi-Biega National Park are imposing 30,000 FC per motorcyclist.
Locals warn that these roadblocks may drive up transportation costs, affecting the price of basic necessities. Motorcycle taxi drivers have urged the armed groups to dismantle the checkpoints, warning that continued harassment threatens the region’s economic recovery.
The Miti–Bulambika–Hombo axis had been closed for several months, leading to serious economic and social consequences for the population. Traffic resumption marks a step toward normalcy, but security and fair passage remain major concerns.

title: Ten Young People Arrested by AFC/M23 Rebels in Kalembe and Kalonge
excerpt: February 20, 2026 – North Kivu, DRC – AFC/M23 rebels arrested a dozen young people overnight from February 19 to 20 in Kalembe and Kalonge, towns on the border between the Masisi and Walikale territories, according to local sources. The youths are accused of collaborating with th
title_en: Ten Young People Arrested by AFC/M23 Rebels in Kalembe and Kalonge
excerpt_en: February 20, 2026 – North Kivu, DRC – AFC/M23 rebels arrested a dozen young people overnight from February 19 to 20 in Kalembe and Kalonge, towns on the border between the Masisi and Walikale territories, according to local sources. The youths are accused of collaborating with th
body_en:
February 20, 2026 – North Kivu, DRC – AFC/M23 rebels arrested a dozen young people overnight from February 19 to 20 in Kalembe and Kalonge, towns on the border between the Masisi and Walikale territories, according to local sources.
The youths are accused of collaborating with the Wazalendo groups, which are active in several areas of North Kivu. Sources report that the arrests were carried out through a cordon and search operation, with the young people taken from their homes during the night and transported to an unknown location.
Families of the detainees have reported no news since the arrests, expressing deep concern over the youths’ fate. “We don’t know where they’ve been taken or the precise charges against them,” said a relative of one of the arrested individuals.
Local security and administrative authorities in Walikale confirmed the arrests but provided no details on the exact number of detainees, charges, or detention sites. AFC/M23 officials have yet to comment on the operation.
The arrests occur amid a tense security environment, marked by ongoing clashes between various armed groups in the region. Among residents, the operation has heightened fear, as accusations of collaboration are often difficult to verify and may be used to exert pressure on local youth.
Families and community leaders are calling for transparency and urgent information regarding the fate of those detained, as the region continues to grapple with persistent insecurity and instability.

Kinshasa, February 16, 2026 – Turkey has reiterated its commitment to supporting the Democratic Republic of Congo in its pursuit of lasting peace.

title: Washington Approves New DFC Investments in Africa to Secure Critical Minerals and Energy
excerpt: February 23, 2026 – The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) has approved strategic investments in Africa aimed at strengthening critical mineral supply chains, energy security, and the sovereignty and stability of key partner nations. According to DFC Managin
title_en: Washington Approves New DFC Investments in Africa to Secure Critical Minerals and Energy
excerpt_en: February 23, 2026 – The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) has approved strategic investments in Africa aimed at strengthening critical mineral supply chains, energy security, and the sovereignty and stability of key partner nations. According to DFC Managin
body_en:
February 23, 2026 – The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) has approved strategic investments in Africa aimed at strengthening critical mineral supply chains, energy security, and the sovereignty and stability of key partner nations.
According to DFC Managing Director Ben Black, these investments are designed to support economic development, enhance energy resilience, and consolidate supply chains essential to U.S. growth, security, and innovation.
While the specific transactions remain confidential, they are part of a broader U.S. effort to expand strategic influence in Africa. All projects will undergo further steps, including Congressional notification, prior to final commitment and closing.
The approval follows a recent expansion of the DFC’s authority by the U.S. Congress, which:
Removed geographic restrictions in strategic sectors.
Raised the agency’s investment ceiling to $205 billion.
Strengthened equity financing capabilities and created a new revolving investment fund.
In mid-February, the United States and the African Union Commission launched a strategic working group on infrastructure and investment, tasked with translating strategic priorities into fundable projects. A cross-border pilot project has been proposed as a proof of concept, with the Democratic Republic of Congo explicitly mentioned, potentially within a regional economic integration framework with Rwanda.
Targeted sectors include infrastructure and critical mineral supply chains, with an emphasis on commercial viability and alignment with Agenda 2063. The U.S. plans to leverage financial instruments such as the DFC, U.S. Export-Import Bank (EXIM), and multilateral banks, while supporting regulatory reforms and legal harmonization to mitigate risks.
The DFC board meeting included both public and private sector members, and a public hearing was held to gather stakeholder input on the agency’s activities.
Social and Health

title: New Wave of Mobondo Surrenders, Significant Cache of Weapons Recovered
excerpt: Kwango February 10, 2026 – The pacification efforts in areas affected by the Mobondo militia continue to gain momentum, with a new wave of surrenders reported in Kwango province. After earlier disarmament operations in Kwamouth and Maluku, authorities have now confirmed that seve
title_en: New Wave of Mobondo Surrenders, Significant Cache of Weapons Recovered
excerpt_en: Kwango February 10, 2026 – The pacification efforts in areas affected by the Mobondo militia continue to gain momentum, with a new wave of surrenders reported in Kwango province. After earlier disarmament operations in Kwamouth and Maluku, authorities have now confirmed that seve
body_en:
Kwango February 10, 2026 – The pacification efforts in areas affected by the Mobondo militia continue to gain momentum, with a new wave of surrenders reported in Kwango province.
After earlier disarmament operations in Kwamouth and Maluku, authorities have now confirmed that several Mobondo militiamen have laid down their arms in the villages of Ipongi and Mulosi, as well as near the Kwango Bridge.
Among those who surrendered are fighters affiliated with the group led by militia commander Mouton, described by officials as one of the most resistant factions within the movement. The militiamen reportedly handed themselves over to the defense and security forces, along with what authorities say is a significant quantity of weapons.
Deputy Minister of Defense Eliezer Ntambwe confirmed the development, noting that weapons are still being collected and that a precise inventory will be provided once the operation concludes in Kinshasa.
“Our brothers who were involved in this movement have agreed to lay down their arms. Many have done so. We are currently preparing to travel with them to Kinshasa so that those who choose to join the army can do so, and those who opt for vocational training can also access it. This also falls within our purview. I cannot give you a precise number of weapons, as we are still collecting them along the way. You will have more details once we arrive in Kinshasa,” stated Minister Ntambwe.
According to authorities, the surrendered fighters will be evacuated to Kinshasa, where some may undergo military integration, while others will benefit from vocational training programs as part of the broader disarmament and reintegration process.
Local militia leaders in Ipongi reportedly encouraged remaining fighters to abandon violence and join the peace process, signaling a possible shift within certain factions of the armed group.
Despite this progress, officials stress that the mission remains ongoing. Further security operations are expected in areas where the Mobondo threat persists, as the government seeks to restore stability across affected territories.

title: MONUSCO Acting Head to Visit Goma Ahead of Ceasefire Verification
excerpt: February 12, 2026 – Vivian van de Perre, Acting Head of the UN Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUSCO), is scheduled to visit Goma on Thursday to support preparations for monitoring and verifying a ceasefire, the mission announced. Ms. van de Perre, serving as the A
title_en: MONUSCO Acting Head to Visit Goma Ahead of Ceasefire Verification
excerpt_en: February 12, 2026 – Vivian van de Perre, Acting Head of the UN Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUSCO), is scheduled to visit Goma on Thursday to support preparations for monitoring and verifying a ceasefire, the mission announced. Ms. van de Perre, serving as the A
body_en:
February 12, 2026 – Vivian van de Perre, Acting Head of the UN Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUSCO), is scheduled to visit Goma on Thursday to support preparations for monitoring and verifying a ceasefire, the mission announced.
Ms. van de Perre, serving as the Acting Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General, will arrive by air, marking a significant operational step after a prolonged interruption of air access to Goma since January 2025. During the visit, she will engage with relevant stakeholders to advance practical arrangements for the ceasefire verification mechanism.
Under UN Security Council Resolution 2808 (2025), MONUSCO is authorized to assist in the implementation of a permanent ceasefire, including technical and logistical support to the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR) through the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus (EJVM+).
“I am going to Goma to support preparations for monitoring and verifying the ceasefire, in close coordination with the established ceasefire architecture, including the EJVM+,” Ms. van de Perre stated.
MONUSCO emphasized that its support will remain strictly within its mandate and in full respect of the sovereignty of the DRC.
A UN source indicated that the mission is also preparing a gradual resumption of operations in eastern DRC, beginning with aerial reconnaissance flights, followed by a limited ground deployment, and then a progressive increase in operational presence, contingent on security guarantees.
These measures aim to bolster the momentum of the ceasefire, though the UN stresses that successful peace efforts also rely on the engagement of the guarantors of the agreements, including the United States, Qatar, and the African Union.

title: Deadly Clashes in Panu: Nine Face Military Court over Terrorism Charges
excerpt: February 15, 2026 – Nine individuals are facing prosecution following clashes between police and bandits in Panu, which left four dead and eight wounded. The case is being heard by the Kikwit Garrison Military Court, covering Kwilu, Kwango, and Maï-Ndombe, during a special sessio
title_en: Deadly Clashes in Panu: Nine Face Military Court over Terrorism Charges
excerpt_en: February 15, 2026 – Nine individuals are facing prosecution following clashes between police and bandits in Panu, which left four dead and eight wounded. The case is being heard by the Kikwit Garrison Military Court, covering Kwilu, Kwango, and Maï-Ndombe, during a special sessio
body_en:
February 15, 2026 – Nine individuals are facing prosecution following clashes between police and bandits in Panu, which left four dead and eight wounded. The case is being heard by the Kikwit Garrison Military Court, covering Kwilu, Kwango, and Maï-Ndombe, during a special session held in Idiofa.
Eight civilians are charged with terrorism, while a police captain faces prosecution for failing to assist a person in danger, after allegedly filming his colleague’s beheading during the clashes. The eight injured police officers have filed civil suits, though no civilian victims have appeared in court.
“We expect the court to convict all these alleged perpetrators of terrorism. We expect reparations for the acts committed because they injured, robbed, and vandalized the property of the police officers they killed,” said Toto Nkonde, part of the victims’ legal team.
According to court proceedings, the confrontation erupted after police arrested three major gang leaders. In retaliation, young bandits mobilized, attacked police with stones, and attempted to expel them from the town. Despite warning shots, the clashes escalated before the bandits eventually surrendered.
The case underscores the persistent insecurity in the region and the military court’s role in addressing terrorism and violent unrest.
