title: Congolese Activists Call for Wider Awareness of the DRC’s Digital Law and Code
excerpt: Congolese human rights activists, influencers, and bloggers are urging the popularization of the DRC’s Digital Law and Code, following a conference on gendered disinformation and the fight against cyberbullying, which concluded on Wednesday, January 28, in Kinshasa. Speaking at t
title_en: Congolese Activists Call for Wider Awareness of the DRC’s Digital Law and Code
excerpt_en: Congolese human rights activists, influencers, and bloggers are urging the popularization of the DRC’s Digital Law and Code, following a conference on gendered disinformation and the fight against cyberbullying, which concluded on Wednesday, January 28, in Kinshasa. Speaking at t
body_en:
Congolese human rights activists, influencers, and bloggers are urging the popularization of the DRC’s Digital Law and Code, following a conference on gendered disinformation and the fight against cyberbullying, which concluded on Wednesday, January 28, in Kinshasa.
Speaking at the event, Ghislain Kabeya Mottomoke from the Ministry of Digital Economy stressed that the main goal is to strengthen public awareness of the Digital Code.
“We have the Digital Code, particularly Article 356, which defines everyone’s responsibilities. Anyone who spreads tribalist, racist, or xenophobic content faces penalties ranging from one month to two years in prison and fines of 500,000 to 10,000,000 Congolese francs,” he explained. “We then move to Article 359, which condemns harassment.”
He further noted that Article 360 explicitly prohibits the spread of rumors and false information:
“When such content is disseminated, it incurs criminal liability. Penalties range from one to six months in prison and a fine of 500,000 to 1,000,000 Congolese francs. These penalties may be combined or applied separately, at the discretion of the judge.”
For General Jean-Romain Kalemba Makengo, representing the Directorate of Telecommunications and New Technologies of the Congolese National Police, public collaboration remains essential in combating cybercrime.
“The Congolese National Police is working hand in hand with the public to stop cyberbullies in their harmful activities,” he said.
The conference was organized by the Political Affairs Division of MONUSCO, in partnership with the Ministry of Digital Economy.

title: The summary proceedings against three magistrates at the Haut-Katanga Court of Appeal continued on Monday, January 26, at the Haut-Katanga Court of Appeal in Lubumbashi. The trial pits the public prosecutor against three magistrates from the Tanganyika Court of Appeal, as well as a merchant, all charged with corruption in a case related to attempted rape with violence.

The trial pits the public prosecutor against three magistrates from the Tanganyika Court of Appeal, as well as a merchant, all charged with corruption in a case related to attempted rape with violence.
excerpt_en: The opening of the hearings on Friday, January 23, was already noteworthy due to the presence of the President of the Court of Cassation and the First Advocate General of the Republic, who traveled from Kinshasa specifically to attend the proceedings. The Court began its investig
body_en:
The opening of the hearings on Friday, January 23, was already noteworthy due to the presence of the President of the Court of Cassation and the First Advocate General of the Republic, who traveled from Kinshasa specifically to attend the proceedings.
The Court began its investigation by identifying the four defendants. Each was then called to the stand to give their account of the events. The defense team challenged the procedure, arguing a lack of evidence in a criminal case being tried under summary proceedings.
At the conclusion of the proceedings, the prosecution requested three years of imprisonment for the magistrates and two years for the merchant. The hearing was adjourned until Monday.
Background
In July 2025, in Kalemie, a woman filed a complaint against merchant Joseph Kafwimbi Kiwele for attempted rape. The Kalemie High Court acquitted the accused. Dissatisfied, the plaintiff appealed to the Tanganyika Court of Appeal.
On December 19, this court sentenced merchant Patrick Kafwimbi to six months of house arrest and a fine of $10,000. Some magistrates deemed this sentence insufficient given the seriousness of the alleged offenses.

excerpt: Goma, North Kivu – January 26, 2026 — Vodacom Congo (DRC) reported a disruption of its services in Goma after an intrusion at its technical center, resulting in a temporary loss of network monitoring and control. The incident affected voice calls, SMS, internet access, and M-Pesa
title_en: Vodacom Network Disrupted in Goma Following Technical Center Intrusion
excerpt_en: Goma, North Kivu – January 26, 2026 — Vodacom Congo (DRC) reported a disruption of its services in Goma after an intrusion at its technical center, resulting in a temporary loss of network monitoring and control. The incident affected voice calls, SMS, internet access, and M-Pesa
body_en:
Goma, North Kivu – January 26, 2026 — Vodacom Congo (DRC) reported a disruption of its services in Goma after an intrusion at its technical center, resulting in a temporary loss of network monitoring and control.
The incident affected voice calls, SMS, internet access, and M-Pesa mobile money services. The company apologized for the inconvenience, describing the situation as “beyond its control”, and stated that its teams worked to restore service. By the afternoon, connectivity had returned after several hours of outage.
Goma has been under the control of the AFC/M23, a Rwandan-backed rebel group, for the past year. While no direct link has been established between the intrusion and the security situation, telecommunications infrastructure is known to play a significant role in the ongoing conflict in eastern DRC, according to previous UN Group of Experts reports.
Vodacom remains the market leader in mobile telephony in the DRC, with 25.8 million active subscribers as of September 2025, representing a 35.2% market share. Over the same period, the company generated $198.1 million in revenue, or 31.9% of total market revenue, second only to Airtel. Vodacom also leads in mobile internet subscribers (12.78 million) and mobile money accounts (15.3 million active accounts).

title: Belgium Urges European Action and Humanitarian Air Access via Goma

title_en: Belgium Urges European Action and Humanitarian Air Access via Goma
excerpt_en: Brussels Belgium January 30, 2026 — Belgium has renewed its call for stronger European engagement in response to the worsening security and humanitarian crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), urging the European Union to treat the conflict as a priority rather than
body_en:
Brussels Belgium January 30, 2026 — Belgium has renewed its call for stronger European engagement in response to the worsening security and humanitarian crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), urging the European Union to treat the conflict as a priority rather than a forgotten crisis.
Speaking at an EU meeting on Thursday, January 29, Belgian Deputy Prime Minister and Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot emphasized that the situation on the ground continues to deteriorate, despite ongoing diplomatic efforts.
“Belgium is deeply sensitive to the tragedies unfolding in the Democratic Republic of Congo. While we welcome political mediation initiatives undertaken in Washington and Doha, the situation on the ground is worse than ever. This is extremely worrying from a humanitarian perspective,” Prévot said.
According to him, this persistent decline prompted Belgium, alongside other EU member states, to place the eastern DRC crisis on the meeting agenda. He expressed concern over how rarely the issue is discussed at the European level. “I am surprised that this is only the second time in a year that eastern Congo has been addressed. This cannot be a forgotten conflict. The European Union has a role to play,” he insisted.
While reaffirming Belgium’s support for ongoing mediation processes, Prévot called for tangible outcomes, including a ceasefire and a return to lasting peace. He also reiterated his country’s position on respecting Congolese sovereignty and territorial integrity.
“We hope these mediation efforts will lead to genuine ceasefire and peace solutions. We must advocate for the withdrawal of the M23 and Rwandan troops so that the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC are preserved,” he stated.
However, the Belgian minister stressed that the immediate priority remains humanitarian. He painted a stark picture of the suffering endured by civilians, particularly women and children, who are disproportionately affected by sexual violence.
“The urgent need at this moment is for European action to address the humanitarian situation, where a woman is raped every four minutes and a child every thirty minutes,” he said.
In this context, Prévot called for concrete measures to facilitate aid delivery, including the reopening of Goma International Airport for exclusively humanitarian purposes.
“It is urgent to activate Goma airport to deliver massive amounts of humanitarian aid. Let there be no doubt: there is no intention to use this airport for military purposes. Belgium’s objective is a broader European commitment to children who have long suffered the tragic horrors of this conflict,” he clarified.
The reopening of Goma airport remains a sensitive and central issue in political discussions. Kinshasa has announced an initiative to reopen the airport to facilitate humanitarian assistance, while the M23 and Rwanda insist that any decision should be made within the framework of the peace process and in respect of territorial control on the ground.

title_en: Calm Returns to Rusamambu, Kalonge, and Kasopo (Walikale) After Clashes Between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo
excerpt_en: Walikale February 3, 2026 — Calm was restored on Tuesday morning, February 3, in the villages of Rusamambu (Ikobo group), Kalonge, and Kasopo (Kisimba group) in Walikale territory, North Kivu, following a night of violent clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and the Wazalendo of the CM
body_en:
Walikale February 3, 2026 — Calm was restored on Tuesday morning, February 3, in the villages of Rusamambu (Ikobo group), Kalonge, and Kasopo (Kisimba group) in Walikale territory, North Kivu, following a night of violent clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and the Wazalendo of the CMC/APC group.
According to local sources, the fighting began around 1:00 a.m., when the Wazalendo launched attacks on rebel positions. Exchanges of fire, involving heavy and light weapons, continued until approximately 6:00 a.m.
Residents spent a restless night at home, fearing the spread of violence. No official information is available yet regarding casualties or material damage.
Sources indicate that the Wazalendo withdrew from Rusamambu, Kalonge, and Kasopo on Tuesday morning, leaving the villages under AFC/M23 control.

title_en: Burundian Presidency Announces Crisis Monitoring, Including the Situation in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: African Union February 5, 2026 — Burundi is preparing to assume the rotating presidency of the African Union (AU) on February 15, 2026, marking a first since the creation of the Organization of African Unity (OAU) in 1963, which later became the AU, Ambassador Edouard Bizimana an
body_en:
African Union February 5, 2026 — Burundi is preparing to assume the rotating presidency of the African Union (AU) on February 15, 2026, marking a first since the creation of the Organization of African Unity (OAU) in 1963, which later became the AU, Ambassador Edouard Bizimana announced in a public address.
According to the Burundian minister, this presidency represents both “a sign of political confidence”, a political, economic, and strategic opportunity, and a collective responsibility, requiring the involvement of all Burundian society, public and private institutions, the economic sector, youth, researchers, and the country’s partners.
The address emphasizes that the Burundian presidency is occurring in a complex regional and international context, marked by armed conflicts, natural disasters, economic challenges, and a deteriorating climate for international cooperation.
Among the announced priorities are:
Accelerating the implementation of the AU's 2026 theme, “Water and Sanitation for All by 2063”.
Continuing the continental youth dialogue on peace, security, research, and innovation.
Strengthening the participation of young people and women in peace processes, within the “Silencing the Guns by 2030” initiative.
Contributing to the operationalization of the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA), with a focus on e-commerce, including an international symposium in Bujumbura.
Burundi will also oversee ordinary AU activities, including annual summits, statutory meetings, and monitoring relations with strategic partners, notably the European Union, China, United States, Russia, India, Japan, and the United Nations.
Continental crises will remain a focus, particularly the situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, Libya, the Sahel, and Sudan, as well as natural disasters and humanitarian emergencies.
The minister called for general mobilization of the Burundian diplomatic corps and foreign missions, highlighting opportunities for international visibility and investment attraction, while acknowledging financial, logistical, and human capacity challenges.
Ambassador Edouard Bizimana concluded by commending the work of Burundi’s Permanent Mission to the AU and calling for unity to ensure the success of this continental mandate.

title: Denis Mukwege Emerges as Potential Challenger to Mushikiwabo for OIF Leadership
excerpt: February 2, 2026 — Congolese-born Nobel Peace Prize laureate Dr. Denis Mukwege is emerging as a leading contender to challenge Louise Mushikiwabo of Rwanda for the post of Secretary General of the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF). Following Rwanda’s announceme
title_en: Denis Mukwege Emerges as Potential Challenger to Mushikiwabo for OIF Leadership
excerpt_en: February 2, 2026 — Congolese-born Nobel Peace Prize laureate Dr. Denis Mukwege is emerging as a leading contender to challenge Louise Mushikiwabo of Rwanda for the post of Secretary General of the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF). Following Rwanda’s announceme
body_en:
February 2, 2026 — Congolese-born Nobel Peace Prize laureate Dr. Denis Mukwege is emerging as a leading contender to challenge Louise Mushikiwabo of Rwanda for the post of Secretary General of the Organisation internationale de la Francophonie (OIF).
Following Rwanda’s announcement last month that it would nominate Mushikiwabo for a third term, the government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) has intensified efforts to put forward a rival candidate.
Initially, the DRC considered Isidore Kwandja Ngembo, an OIF observer involved in election monitoring and the organization of the 2023 Francophonie Games in Kinshasa. However, after a final decision was taken on January 30, 2026, two additional names emerged as potential challengers.
Dr. Mukwege, founder of Panzi Hospital in Bukavu and internationally renowned for his work treating survivors of sexual violence, has become the most prominent figure under consideration. Although he opposed President Félix Tshisekedi during the 2023 presidential campaign, reports indicate the two have since entered into dialogue and are expected to meet in New York in September 2025.
Another candidate being considered is Freddy Matungulu, former Minister of Finance (2001–2003) and former official at both the International Monetary Fund (IMF) and the African Development Bank (AfDB).
The DRC government has repeatedly voiced dissatisfaction with Rwanda holding the OIF’s top post, arguing that it deserves the position as the country with the largest French-speaking population, estimated at around 50% of its citizens.
The next OIF Summit of Heads of State and Government, scheduled for November 15–16, 2026, in Phnom Penh, Cambodia, will elect the organization’s next Secretary General.

title: Rwanda and Jamaica Sign MoU to Strengthen Capital Markets
excerpt: Kingston, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Stock Exchange (RSE) and the Jamaica Stock Exchange (JSE) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to enhance investment opportunities and build capacity in both markets. The agreement was signed during the 21st Investment and Capita
title_en: Rwanda and Jamaica Sign MoU to Strengthen Capital Markets
excerpt_en: Kingston, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Stock Exchange (RSE) and the Jamaica Stock Exchange (JSE) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to enhance investment opportunities and build capacity in both markets. The agreement was signed during the 21st Investment and Capita
body_en:
Kingston, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Stock Exchange (RSE) and the Jamaica Stock Exchange (JSE) have signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) to enhance investment opportunities and build capacity in both markets. The agreement was signed during the 21st Investment and Capital Markets Conference held in Kingston, Jamaica.
Rwanda was represented by RSE CEO Rwabukumba Pierre Célestin, while Jamaica was represented by Prime Minister Andrew Holness and JSE Chairman Livingstone Morrison.
The MoU focuses on developing capital markets, building innovation, and increasing visibility for companies in both countries to attract investment opportunities.
Rwabukumba emphasized that the agreement goes beyond formalities: “This partnership is more than just a document. It will be an opportunity to share experiences, grow together, and open new business and investment opportunities for professionals in the capital markets of both countries.”
Rwanda and Jamaica have previously collaborated in politics, tourism, transport, and industrial park development, and recently sent Rwandan military engineers to assist in infrastructure restoration after a major disaster in Jamaica in October 2025.

title: RIB Arrests Three, Including Barafinda, Over Alleged Spread of Public Disorder Rumors
excerpt: Kigali — The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has arrested three individuals, including political figure Barafinda Sekikubo Fred, on allegations of spreading rumors likely to cause public unrest, the Criminal Investigation Department announced. The suspects — Barafinda Sekikubo
title_en: RIB Arrests Three, Including Barafinda, Over Alleged Spread of Public Disorder Rumors
excerpt_en: Kigali — The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has arrested three individuals, including political figure Barafinda Sekikubo Fred, on allegations of spreading rumors likely to cause public unrest, the Criminal Investigation Department announced. The suspects — Barafinda Sekikubo
body_en:
Kigali — The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has arrested three individuals, including political figure Barafinda Sekikubo Fred, on allegations of spreading rumors likely to cause public unrest, the Criminal Investigation Department announced.
The suspects — Barafinda Sekikubo Fred, Mazimpaka Patrick, and Nkeramihigo Japhet — were arrested on January 29, 2026, and are accused of disseminating misleading information through various YouTube channels.
They are currently being held at RIB stations in Kimironko, Kicukiro, and Kimihurura as investigations continue.
In a statement, RIB warned the public “to avoid using social media in a manner that is contrary to the law,” adding that it “will not tolerate anyone who uses it to commit crimes.”
Background on Barafinda
In February 2020, RIB summoned Barafinda, but he did not appear and was later arrested on February 11, 2020, before being referred to Caraes Ndera Psychiatric Hospital for medical evaluation.
In March 2020, authorities reported that examinations confirmed he was undergoing treatment for a mental illness and was not under criminal monitoring due to his condition. In July 2020, doctors confirmed his illness was chronic and urged the public and media to refrain from exploiting him for interviews.
Barafinda acknowledged in June 2017 that he had spent time at Ndera, a mental health facility, without providing further details.

title: Ibalanky Signals Willingness to Work with AFC/M23 After Years of Serving Tshisekedi
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 31, 2026 — Claude Ibalanky Ekolomba, a senior Congolese politician who previously worked closely with President Félix Tshisekedi, has announced his willingness to collaborate with the AFC/M23 alliance, marking a significant political shift. Ibalanky was appointe
title_en: Ibalanky Signals Willingness to Work with AFC/M23 After Years of Serving Tshisekedi
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 31, 2026 — Claude Ibalanky Ekolomba, a senior Congolese politician who previously worked closely with President Félix Tshisekedi, has announced his willingness to collaborate with the AFC/M23 alliance, marking a significant political shift. Ibalanky was appointe
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 31, 2026 — Claude Ibalanky Ekolomba, a senior Congolese politician who previously worked closely with President Félix Tshisekedi, has announced his willingness to collaborate with the AFC/M23 alliance, marking a significant political shift.
Ibalanky was appointed by Tshisekedi as coordinator of the body monitoring the implementation of the Addis Ababa Peace Agreement, a key framework for restoring stability in the Democratic Republic of Congo. In 2023, he was also named the country’s special ambassador.
After nearly a year outside the country, Ibalanky resurfaced in Goma on January 31, 2025, where he was seen alongside senior AFC/M23 leaders, including Corneille Nangaa and Bertrand Bisimwa.
He stated that he has not formally joined the AFC/M23 but traveled to Goma to hold consultations with its leadership on how dialogue could help restore peace. Ibalanky emphasized that he does not intend to oppose President Tshisekedi, but rather seeks to serve as an advisor to the alliance, pending approval from its leader, Corneille Nangaa.
“I came to consult. I have not betrayed anyone; I am only on one side, which is Congo,” Ibalanky said. “If they accept my help and show me how we can work together, I will consider it. What matters is not being in Goma or Kinshasa, but working for peace.”
In 2023, Ibalanky founded the REPOP political party, which initially supported Tshisekedi’s bid for a second term. However, in January 2024, the party announced it would not recognize the election results, signaling a break with the ruling camp.

excerpt: The city of Kinshasa officially launched its awareness campaign on Tuesday, January 27, to encourage residents to declare and pay property tax (IF) for the 2026 fiscal year, as well as rental income tax (IRL) for the 2025 fiscal year. The payment deadline is set for February 1, 2
title_en: Kinshasa Launches Property and Rental Income Tax Awareness Campaign for 2026
excerpt_en: The city of Kinshasa officially launched its awareness campaign on Tuesday, January 27, to encourage residents to declare and pay property tax (IF) for the 2026 fiscal year, as well as rental income tax (IRL) for the 2025 fiscal year. The payment deadline is set for February 1, 2
body_en:
The city of Kinshasa officially launched its awareness campaign on Tuesday, January 27, to encourage residents to declare and pay property tax (IF) for the 2026 fiscal year, as well as rental income tax (IRL) for the 2025 fiscal year. The payment deadline is set for February 1, 2026.
At a press conference, the provincial Minister of Finance, Magloire Kabemba, announced the start of the campaign. During the event, the Kinshasa Revenue Authority (DGRK) presented the tax clearance certificate, an official document certifying payment of property taxes, rental income, and, where applicable, vehicle taxes. Printed on secure paper, this certificate is valid from the date of issue and forms part of a strategy to increase local revenue ahead of the deadline.
Decentralization of Tax Collection Sites
Alongside the minister, Gérard Kaja Kambowa, special advisor at the DGRK, stressed the importance of decentralizing tax collection sites to avoid congestion and facilitate taxpayer access.
This initiative is part of a broader effort to strengthen tax compliance, according to Kinshasa City Hall.
Following a meeting held on January 21, provincial authorities announced several measures targeting property owners and landlords, including:
Public display of taxpayers in good standing,
The opening of additional counters,
Making certain civil status documents conditional upon the regular payment of municipal taxes.
These measures aim to consolidate the transparency and efficiency of Kinshasa’s tax system while strengthening the culture of tax citizenship, City Hall stated.

body_en:
February 3, 2026 — The Observatory for Press Freedom in Africa (OLPA) confirms the release of Samson Fabrice Nyandabaga, journalist and director of Flash FM, a community radio station in Kamanyola (47 km from Bukavu, South Kivu, DRC).
The journalist was released on January 31, 2026, after 72 hours of detention in the intelligence cell of the AFC-M23 rebel movement.
He had been arrested on January 28, 2026, while covering the living conditions of displaced people in Uvira, following the withdrawal of AFC/M23 rebels. During his detention, he faced intense interrogation about alleged ties to international media and Congolese journalists reporting on issues deemed hostile by the rebels.
OLPA condemns this unjustified imprisonment, highlighting it as a clear violation of press freedom, which is guaranteed by Congolese law and international human rights instruments.
This incident underscores the ongoing risks faced by journalists operating in conflict-affected regions of eastern DRC.

title: Kinshasa Rejects Human Rights Watch’s Assessment of Uvira, Citing Rebel Responsibility
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 26, 2026 — The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has strongly contested a recent report by Human Rights Watch on the security situation in Uvira, South Kivu, following the withdrawal of the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion. The government warn
title_en: Kinshasa Rejects Human Rights Watch’s Assessment of Uvira, Citing Rebel Responsibility
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 26, 2026 — The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has strongly contested a recent report by Human Rights Watch on the security situation in Uvira, South Kivu, following the withdrawal of the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion. The government warn
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 26, 2026 — The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has strongly contested a recent report by Human Rights Watch on the security situation in Uvira, South Kivu, following the withdrawal of the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion. The government warned that separating current risks from the actions and strategies of the occupying forces is both legally inaccurate and politically dangerous.
In a statement released on Thursday, January 22, the Ministry of Communication emphasized that the Human Rights Watch report, titled “DR Congo: Civilians in South Kivu at Serious Risk”, primarily focuses on post-withdrawal risks without adequately situating them within the broader context of an illegal armed occupation characterized by systematic abuses against civilians and a deliberate strategy to destabilize the city.
“The withdrawal of the AFC/M23 from Uvira, which occurred on January 17, 2026, followed a period marked by looting, large-scale theft, threats, intimidation, and community stigmatization, all of which severely affected civilian security and social cohesion. This withdrawal was accompanied by premeditated disorder, deliberately orchestrated to prolong insecurity and create residual effects after the occupying forces departed,” the statement read.
According to the government, the primary responsibility for endangering civilians lies with the rebels, due to the illegal occupation, the manipulation of fear among residents, forced transfers and displacement of members of the Banyamulenge community, and the deliberate chaos left behind.
The government stressed that downplaying or reversing this responsibility is inconsistent with established facts and warned against any equivalence between the aggressed state and the occupying forces. “It is legally inaccurate and politically dangerous to dissociate the current risks in Uvira from the acts and strategies implemented by the occupying forces before and during their withdrawal. The DRC reaffirms its commitment to international human rights mechanisms, which must respect the full factual truth, the hierarchy of responsibilities, and the principle of non-equivalence,” the statement said.
The government also reiterated its willingness to cooperate with international mechanisms, provided their analyses and recommendations adhere to rigorous interpretations of international law and do not dilute responsibilities or reverse facts.
Since the rebel withdrawal, the redeployment of FARDC troops, the Congolese National Police, and other security services has facilitated the gradual restoration of state authority, the protection of civilians and their property, and the containment of risks, contributing to the preservation of public order.
Uvira, a strategic city in South Kivu, had previously fallen under the control of AFC/M23, strengthening the rebels’ influence in North and South Kivu. The city is seen as a key stronghold, potentially facilitating a rebel advance toward the Greater Katanga region, the economic heartland of the DRC.

title: Identification Operation Launched for Military and Police Personnel in Kisenso
excerpt: An operation to identify military and police personnel officially began on Friday, January 30, in the Kisenso district of Kinshasa, aimed at tightening control over law enforcement officers and armed forces members residing in the area. The initiative, launched by Kisenso Mayor G
title_en: Identification Operation Launched for Military and Police Personnel in Kisenso
excerpt_en: An operation to identify military and police personnel officially began on Friday, January 30, in the Kisenso district of Kinshasa, aimed at tightening control over law enforcement officers and armed forces members residing in the area. The initiative, launched by Kisenso Mayor G
body_en:
An operation to identify military and police personnel officially began on Friday, January 30, in the Kisenso district of Kinshasa, aimed at tightening control over law enforcement officers and armed forces members residing in the area.
The initiative, launched by Kisenso Mayor Godé Athswel, follows a surge in insecurity linked to unidentified men in uniform in several neighborhoods of the capital. These individuals are accused of extortion, home invasions, and other acts of violence.
Mayor Athswel said the operation is intended to protect residents and neutralize criminals who have infiltrated the security services.
“We took the precaution of identifying all soldiers in the Kisenso district, whether armed or not, and recording their weapon serial numbers for rigorous verification, in order to guarantee the safety of our population,” he stated.
Objective: Restoring Public Trust
Although the security situation in Kisenso is described as relatively calm, authorities acknowledge that in other parts of Kinshasa, deserters from military training are reportedly involved in looting and violence. The identification campaign is therefore seen as a key step toward restoring trust between the population and the security forces.

excerpt_en: February 3, 2026 — The Osso Banyungu sector (Masisi territory, North Kivu) has experienced a lull for nearly a month, with no clashes reported between government forces (FARDC) and AFC/M23 rebels. Local sources report that both sides are holding their positions. The rebels have n
body_en:
February 3, 2026 — The Osso Banyungu sector (Masisi territory, North Kivu) has experienced a lull for nearly a month, with no clashes reported between government forces (FARDC) and AFC/M23 rebels.
Local sources report that both sides are holding their positions. The rebels have not advanced along any new axes, while the FARDC, supported by the Wazalendo, remain entrenched in their initial lines.
This relative stability has enabled the spontaneous return of people to several villages. Displaced families who fled hostilities are gradually returning, despite a fragile security situation.
A tentative resumption of socio-economic activity is observed, particularly in local markets and small businesses, though progress is limited due to persistent insecurity on certain roads.
From a humanitarian perspective, the situation remains worrying. Needs are immense, while humanitarian access is severely restricted, limiting assistance to affected populations.

title: US Senators Discuss M23 Occupation of Eastern DRC, Backed by Rwanda
excerpt: February 5, 2026 — US Senators Jim Risch and Jeanne Shaheen met in Washington with President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to discuss bilateral relations, the Washington Peace and Prosperity Accords, and the security situation in eastern DRC, accordin
title_en: US Senators Discuss M23 Occupation of Eastern DRC, Backed by Rwanda
excerpt_en: February 5, 2026 — US Senators Jim Risch and Jeanne Shaheen met in Washington with President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to discuss bilateral relations, the Washington Peace and Prosperity Accords, and the security situation in eastern DRC, accordin
body_en:
February 5, 2026 — US Senators Jim Risch and Jeanne Shaheen met in Washington with President Félix Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) to discuss bilateral relations, the Washington Peace and Prosperity Accords, and the security situation in eastern DRC, according to a US Senate statement.
The senators, chairman and vice-chair of the Senate Foreign Relations Committee, emphasized that the United States is ready to become a stronger partner of the DRC, noting that bipartisan support must be matched by serious efforts by all parties to honor their commitments under the agreements.
Discussions included partnerships around critical minerals and investments to revitalize the Lobito Corridor, presented as a lever for mutual economic growth, regional trade, and long-term cooperation between the US and Africa.
The senators also voiced concern over “the continued occupation of parts of eastern Congo by the Rwandan-backed M23 group”, calling for a complete withdrawal of Rwandan forces to allow for “a real chance at lasting peace.”
The statement highlighted a humanitarian catastrophe in eastern DRC, where 26 million people face acute food insecurity, stressing that women, children, and minority communities cannot remain collateral damage.
Finally, the senators stressed that long-term stability requires the DRC to take decisive action against the FDLR and the violent Wazalendo militias, and called on Kinshasa to engage in credible national dialogue or political solutions to strengthen national cohesion and the future of the bilateral partnership.

title_en: Rwanda and Egypt Hold Talks to Strengthen Water Sector Cooperation
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 30, 2026 — Egypt’s Minister of Water Resources and Irrigation, Prof. Hani Sewilam, is in Rwanda for high-level talks aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation in the water sector and the management of natural water resources. Prof. Sewilam arrived in Kigali on
body_en:
Kigali, January 30, 2026 — Egypt’s Minister of Water Resources and Irrigation, Prof. Hani Sewilam, is in Rwanda for high-level talks aimed at strengthening bilateral cooperation in the water sector and the management of natural water resources.
Prof. Sewilam arrived in Kigali on Thursday, January 29, 2026, and is scheduled to meet with Rwanda’s Minister of Environment, Dr. Bernadette Arapu, and the Minister of Agriculture and Livestock, Dr. Ndabamenye Telesphore, according to the Egyptian Ministry of Water Resources.
The Egyptian official and his Rwandan counterparts are also expected to attend the closing ceremony of the Rwanda–Egypt Joint Steering Group meeting and visit various sites earmarked for the implementation of joint projects.
Officials said the discussions aim to provide practical solutions through knowledge-sharing, capacity building, and support for the execution of bilateral initiatives.
In September 2025, Rwanda and Egypt signed a Memorandum of Understanding (MoU) during President Paul Kagame’s visit to Egypt, covering areas such as water management, investment promotion, land exchange, and urban and housing development.
The two countries maintain strong ties across several sectors, including trade and investment, health, defense, infrastructure, and education.

title: NAEB Pushes to Reach $1.5 Billion in Exports by 2029
excerpt: Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The National Agricultural Export Promotion Board (NAEB) continues its efforts to expand Rwanda’s agricultural exports, aiming to achieve $1.5 billion in export earnings by 2029, as part of the country’s Second National Strategy for Accelerated Developme
title_en: NAEB Pushes to Reach $1.5 Billion in Exports by 2029
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The National Agricultural Export Promotion Board (NAEB) continues its efforts to expand Rwanda’s agricultural exports, aiming to achieve $1.5 billion in export earnings by 2029, as part of the country’s Second National Strategy for Accelerated Developme
body_en:
Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The National Agricultural Export Promotion Board (NAEB) continues its efforts to expand Rwanda’s agricultural exports, aiming to achieve $1.5 billion in export earnings by 2029, as part of the country’s Second National Strategy for Accelerated Development (NST2) and Vision 2050, according to NAEB Director General Bizimana Claude.
NAEB is working to facilitate timely export of agricultural and livestock products, focusing on market expansion, particularly in West and Central Africa. In December 2025, Rwanda signed a cooperation agreement with its Embassy in the Republic of Congo to export fruits and vegetables, following Bizimana’s working visit. The partnership also involves RwandAir, which helps address logistical challenges, including limited cargo space, ensuring products reach markets efficiently.
On January 21, 2026, 17 tons of Rwandan fruits and vegetables were shipped directly to Congo-Brazzaville, demonstrating improved coordination between government institutions and embassies to reduce transit delays, prevent losses, and increase foreign exchange earnings.
Bizimana emphasized the role of cold storage in processing, preserving, and consolidating goods to maintain quality until they reach international markets. He also highlighted that export initiatives respond to the needs of Rwandans living abroad, ensuring they have access to local products.
Rwanda’s exports continue to grow across Africa and beyond. Between December 22–26, 2025, the country earned $15,647,992 from exports to countries including the United Kingdom, Netherlands, UAE, Germany, and France, while vegetables alone totaled 241 tons, with the UAE, UK, and Spain as top destinations.
Agricultural exports remain a major source of income, with $893.1 million earned in 2025. Between January 12–16, 2026, exports generated more than $15.2 million (22.2 billion Rwf), and from January 19–23, 2026, they earned $13,947,661 (over 20 billion Rwf).
NAEB and the Ministry of Agriculture and Livestock aim to surpass $1 billion in agricultural export revenue for the 2025/26 fiscal year, as part of ongoing efforts to expand Rwanda’s presence in regional and international markets.

title: Trial of Gen Philémon Yav Irung Accused of Collaborating with Rwanda
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 29, 2026 – The Military High Court of the DRC is hearing the case against Gen Philémon Yav Irung, former commander of the 3rd military region covering North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri, Maniema, and Tshopo, accused of collaborating with the Rwandan government. The p
title_en: Trial of Gen Philémon Yav Irung Accused of Collaborating with Rwanda
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 29, 2026 – The Military High Court of the DRC is hearing the case against Gen Philémon Yav Irung, former commander of the 3rd military region covering North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri, Maniema, and Tshopo, accused of collaborating with the Rwandan government. The p
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 29, 2026 – The Military High Court of the DRC is hearing the case against Gen Philémon Yav Irung, former commander of the 3rd military region covering North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri, Maniema, and Tshopo, accused of collaborating with the Rwandan government.
The prosecution, represented by Lt Gen Lucien-René Likulia, claimed that Gen Yav received a message from Rwandan officials advising him not to advance military operations, including a meeting with Brig Gen Mwehu Lumbu Evariste at the Serena Hotel in Goma.
The court confronted the prosecution over a lack of evidence, as Lt Gen Likulia could not produce the alleged message, citing inability to access Gen Yav’s phone. Gen Yav’s lawyer, Me Charles Ngwapitshi, dismissed the claims as rumors, highlighting contradictions in witness testimony and questioning the prosecution’s decision to involve Gen (Rtd) James Kabarebe, a prominent Rwandan military figure, to lend weight to their case.
Key witnesses, including Lt Gen Constant Ndima and Gen Maj Sylvain Ekenge, provided conflicting accounts regarding the origin of the message, with some attributing it to Kabarebe’s advisor, and others unable to confirm.
Gen Yav, who was arrested in September 2022 amid ongoing AFC/M23 advances, stated in court on January 21, 2026, that the only message he received accused him and his colleagues of working with the FDLR terrorist group, with the sender still unknown.
The trial, which began on December 19, 2025, continues amid questions over the validity of the prosecution’s evidence and the role of regional political actors in the case.

title: Burundi Maintains Closed Borders with DRC, Refuses Return of Congolese Refugees
excerpt: Bujumbura, January 30, 2026 — Burundi has announced that it will not reopen its land border with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) or allow the return of Congolese refugees, citing ongoing security concerns, according to Foreign Affairs Minister Dr. Edouard Bizimana. The Gat
title_en: Burundi Maintains Closed Borders with DRC, Refuses Return of Congolese Refugees
excerpt_en: Bujumbura, January 30, 2026 — Burundi has announced that it will not reopen its land border with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) or allow the return of Congolese refugees, citing ongoing security concerns, according to Foreign Affairs Minister Dr. Edouard Bizimana. The Gat
body_en:
Bujumbura, January 30, 2026 — Burundi has announced that it will not reopen its land border with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) or allow the return of Congolese refugees, citing ongoing security concerns, according to Foreign Affairs Minister Dr. Edouard Bizimana.
The Gatumba and Vugizo border posts were closed on December 9, 2025, following the entry of AFC/M23 fighters into Uvira. Although the group withdrew on January 17, 2026, and DRC and Wazalendo forces, alongside the Burundian army, regained control the next day, the border remains closed due to continued security risks, including attempted crossings of the Ruzizi River.
Minister Bizimana explained at a press conference on January 29 that reopening the border requires ensuring that all security conditions are met. “Opening them today, and then closing them tomorrow because you are not well prepared, without making sure that the requirements are met, no one will do anything,” he said.
Since early December 2025, Burundi has hosted over 100,000 Congolese refugees fleeing fighting in the Ruzizi Valley. Many have expressed the desire to return home but have been turned away. Minister Bizimana acknowledged the difficult living conditions in refugee camps but assured that refugees continue to receive support, including financial assistance from the DRC government.
“We want those Congolese to return home, to their properties, but there are still issues that prevent the borders from being safely opened,” he stated, adding that the situation will be communicated when it is resolved.
Mercenaries Fuel Insecurity in South Kivu, Threatening Regional Stability
Kinshasa, 31 January 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC)’s eastern province of South Kivu is facing a new wave of instability as reports indicate a growing reliance on foreign mercenaries, raising alarm across the Great Lakes region.
Sources from international and regional media suggest that mercenaries from Eastern Europe and Colombia—countries known for deploying former soldiers abroad—are actively operating alongside both the DRC army and armed groups such as the FDLR, a terrorist organization formed by perpetrators of the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi. Rwanda has repeatedly warned that such alliances pose a serious threat to its own security and that of the broader region.
Observers note that President Félix Tshisekedi appears to have prioritized a military strategy over ongoing peace initiatives, sidelining regional and international efforts aimed at dialogue and reconciliation. The deployment of foreign fighters violates previous agreements reached in Luanda, Nairobi, Washington, and Doha, as well as other regional mechanisms designed to dismantle armed groups and restore peace.
Reports also suggest that mercenaries have obstructed the operations of the East African Community Regional Force (EACRF), even intimidating regional soldiers deployed to stabilize South Kivu—a move seen as Kinshasa’s reluctance to implement regional resolutions.
Analysts warn that the use of mercenaries often exacerbates conflict rather than resolving it. “History shows that foreign fighters rarely restore peace,” said one expert. “Their presence tends to fuel human rights violations, resource plundering, and further instability.” The DRC’s increasing reliance on Colombian mercenaries highlights persistent weaknesses within its national army.
The consequences extend beyond Congo’s borders. Regional security across Rwanda, Burundi, and Uganda is threatened, and ethnic tensions are exacerbated, placing civilians—particularly Tutsi communities—at risk outside zones controlled by the AFC/M23.
The international community has faced criticism for its muted response to mercenary activity and collaboration with armed groups. Experts argue that continued inaction could prolong the conflict, rather than promote resolution.
Observers are calling for urgent condemnation of mercenary use, renewed diplomatic pressure on Kinshasa to return to negotiations, and a commitment to dismantling terrorist organizations. Without decisive action, South Kivu—and the wider Great Lakes region—risks remaining trapped in a cycle of violence.

title: Julien Paluku Accuses Rwanda of Targeting Congolese Minerals Behind the M23 Conflict
excerpt: Julien Paluku: “The real FDLR that Kigali is after are Congolese minerals.” During the memorial day organized on Tuesday, January 27, at the Academy of Fine Arts in Kinshasa, the former governor of North Kivu and current Minister of Foreign Trade, Julien Paluku Kahongya, reiterat
title_en: Julien Paluku Accuses Rwanda of Targeting Congolese Minerals Behind the M23 Conflict
excerpt_en: Julien Paluku: “The real FDLR that Kigali is after are Congolese minerals.” During the memorial day organized on Tuesday, January 27, at the Academy of Fine Arts in Kinshasa, the former governor of North Kivu and current Minister of Foreign Trade, Julien Paluku Kahongya, reiterat
body_en:
Julien Paluku: “The real FDLR that Kigali is after are Congolese minerals.” During the memorial day organized on Tuesday, January 27, at the Academy of Fine Arts in Kinshasa, the former governor of North Kivu and current Minister of Foreign Trade, Julien Paluku Kahongya, reiterated a strong position of the Congolese government: “The occupation of certain urban areas by the AFC/M23 rebels, supported by Rwanda, has not only a military dimension, but above all an economic one.”
A Strategy of Destruction and Seizure
Julien Paluku denounced what he calls Rwanda’s strategy of destroying the human capital and economic fabric of the DRC. According to him, behind the military offensives lies a logic of systematically plundering Congolese natural resources.
“The volume of mineral exports to Rwanda has increased from $70 million to $2 billion in one year, even though Rwanda does not possess any mineral deposits. The real FDLR he is pursuing in the DRC is Congolese minerals,” he stated.
This declaration highlights one of the central issues of the conflict: the transformation of Congolese minerals into foreign wealth, fueling a parallel economy that weakens the Congolese state and deprives local populations of the benefits of their own resources.
At both the UN and the African Union, President Félix Tshisekedi and the government repeatedly emphasize that the war waged in eastern DRC by “Rwanda via the AFC/M23” has economic aims through the plundering of mineral resources.
On February 18, 2025, during a press conference, the Minister of Mines, Kizito Pakabomba, accused Rwanda of costing the DRC more than $1 billion annually. He also warned of Rwanda’s goal of reaching over $2 billion by 2026 through the illegal exploitation of Congolese mines.
One Year After the Fall of Goma
Paluku's remarks were made during the commemoration of the first anniversary of the M23's capture of Goma. The Suminwa government sought to mark this date by paying tribute to the resilience and unity of the Congolese people in the face of occupation.
The Minister of Communication and Media, Patrick Muyaya, emphasized the refusal to forget or trivialize the war in the East, recalling that remembrance is "an act of governmental responsibility."
The Themes of the Commemoration
The day of remembrance was structured around four themes:
The humanitarian crisis: thousands of displaced persons and victims of violence.
The economic stakes: the plundering of minerals and the weakening of the productive sector.

title: Trial of General Philémon Yav: Informant Confirms Alleged Demoralizing Remarks in Goma
excerpt: Goma, January 28, 2026 — The trial of Lieutenant General Philémon Yav Irung continued on Tuesday, January 27, with the hearing of four senior military officers as witnesses in the case brought by the Auditor General of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC).
title_en: Trial of General Philémon Yav: Informant Confirms Alleged Demoralizing Remarks in Goma
excerpt_en: Goma, January 28, 2026 — The trial of Lieutenant General Philémon Yav Irung continued on Tuesday, January 27, with the hearing of four senior military officers as witnesses in the case brought by the Auditor General of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC).
body_en:
Goma, January 28, 2026 — The trial of Lieutenant General Philémon Yav Irung continued on Tuesday, January 27, with the hearing of four senior military officers as witnesses in the case brought by the Auditor General of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC).
Those heard by the court were Lieutenant General Ndima Kongba Constant, former military governor of North Kivu; Major General Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa Efomi, former communications adviser to the same governor; Brigadier General Yangba Tene Dany, former operations adviser; and Brigadier General Mwehu Lumbu Evariste, former commander of the Sukola 2 South operational sector in South Kivu.
The judges questioned the witnesses about two messages that, according to the prosecution, form the basis of the charges and the arrest of General Yav. General Mwehu was specifically asked about a conversation with the defendant during a meeting in Goma, during which General Yav allegedly told him: “You, General Mwehu, are always at the front. The victory will benefit these Bangala. We won’t see you.” The prosecution argues that this statement was likely to demoralize the troops.
In his testimony, General Mwehu confirmed the exchange, stating that such remarks, coming from a superior officer, could indeed discourage soldiers. According to the prosecution, this constitutes the offense of inciting military personnel to act contrary to duty or discipline, while another message reportedly attributed to the late General Peter Cirimwami is being treated as treason, comparable to participation in an insurrection.
“Your Honor, it’s true,” General Mwehu told the court. “The Commander of the Third Defense Zone did not have an office in Goma; his office was in Kisangani. He often came for hearings or operational meetings and usually stayed at the Serena Hotel. I was returning to the field when I learned he was in Goma. I went to see him to give operational reports. As we were leaving the hotel courtyard, he made that statement. I did not react, and we moved on to another topic.”
General Yav Irung is suspected of having links to the inner circle of James Kabarebe. Reassigned to eastern DRC in 2020, he was appointed commander of the Third Defense Zone, a strategic military area covering North Kivu, South Kivu, Ituri, Maniema, and Tshopo. His trial comes nearly three years after his arrest in September 2022.
Nicknamed “The Tiger,” General Yav is among officers from the Greater Katanga region whose arrests have been cited by some political figures, including former President Joseph Kabila, as evidence of marginalization under President Félix Tshisekedi. The Congolese army has consistently rejected these claims, insisting that military justice operates strictly within the framework of the law and without ethnic considerations.

title: Five Health Facilities Shut Down in Mwenye After ADF Attacks
excerpt: Lubero, North Kivu – January 26, 2026 — Five health centers and several health posts have closed in the Mwenye area following renewed insecurity marked by the killing of civilians attributed to suspected Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) rebels. Facilities in Mausa, Pombi, Mandelya,
title_en: Five Health Facilities Shut Down in Mwenye After ADF Attacks
excerpt_en: Lubero, North Kivu – January 26, 2026 — Five health centers and several health posts have closed in the Mwenye area following renewed insecurity marked by the killing of civilians attributed to suspected Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) rebels. Facilities in Mausa, Pombi, Mandelya,
body_en:
Lubero, North Kivu – January 26, 2026 — Five health centers and several health posts have closed in the Mwenye area following renewed insecurity marked by the killing of civilians attributed to suspected Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) rebels.
Facilities in Mausa, Pombi, Mandelya, Musenge, and the Masoy referral health center have ceased operations. The Masoy center, located in the main town of Mwenye, has reportedly been closed for about a week.
This development has worsened the humanitarian crisis in an area already heavily affected by persistent violence.
Civil society leaders have condemned the silence of the authorities, saying the insecurity has paralyzed socio-economic activities across the Mwenye group in the Baswagha chiefdom, deepening a sense of abandonment among residents.
“Given the situation we are experiencing, nurses have been a great help to the population. Even members of armed groups and their families were receiving care free of charge. But the pressure on the Biambwe health center forced our nurses to close the facility,” said Kambale Muthano Jérémie Mutumwa, president of the New Congolese Civil Society. “This complicates life for the entire population, because all facilities in Mandelya, Pombi, Mausa, Masoya, and Musenge have now closed. We are not against healthcare workers. We only ask the government to ensure the safety of the population, including health facilities, so that professionals can work in decent conditions.”
Faced with this situation, healthcare workers are urgently calling on military authorities to intervene and fully implement Operation Shujaa, a joint operation between the FARDC (Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo) and the UPDF (Ugandan People’s Defence Force).
Since 2024, the Mwenye area has remained in a state of chronic instability, marked by massacres of civilians, mass displacement, the closure of schools, and now the shutdown of health facilities.
The latest violence occurred on the night of Tuesday, January 21, when suspected ADF fighters killed five civilians and burned about ten houses in the village of Mavwe-Mavwe, in the Mandelya district. Four women were among the victims.

title: AU Facilitators Meet Tshisekedi to Relaunch Regional Mediation Ahead of Visits to Kigali and Bujumbura
excerpt: Kinshasa — January 29, 2026 — President Félix Tshisekedi on Thursday received a delegation from the African Union (AU) Panel of Facilitators at the African Union City complex, as part of renewed diplomatic efforts to promote peace in the Democratic Republic of Congo and the wider
title_en: AU Facilitators Meet Tshisekedi to Relaunch Regional Mediation Ahead of Visits to Kigali and Bujumbura
excerpt_en: Kinshasa — January 29, 2026 — President Félix Tshisekedi on Thursday received a delegation from the African Union (AU) Panel of Facilitators at the African Union City complex, as part of renewed diplomatic efforts to promote peace in the Democratic Republic of Congo and the wider
body_en:
Kinshasa — January 29, 2026 — President Félix Tshisekedi on Thursday received a delegation from the African Union (AU) Panel of Facilitators at the African Union City complex, as part of renewed diplomatic efforts to promote peace in the Democratic Republic of Congo and the wider Great Lakes region.
Discussions focused on mediation initiatives aimed at ending the violence, particularly in the eastern provinces. “We are on a tour. We will listen to everyone and see what can be done for the well-being of this population that has suffered greatly for decades. Behind all this, there is human suffering that must be stopped,” said Sahle-Work Zewde, former President of Ethiopia.
According to the Congolese presidency, President Tshisekedi welcomed the facilitators’ efforts and reaffirmed his commitment to achieving a lasting and verifiable peace in eastern DRC, as well as to strengthening regional stability, in line with commitments made by all parties.
The delegation included Olusegun Obasanjo, former President of Nigeria; Sahle-Work Zewde, former President of Ethiopia; Mokgweetsi Eric Keabetswe Masisi, former President of Botswana; Catherine Samba-Panza, former President of the Central African Republic; Yackoly Kokou Johnson, Togolese Minister Delegate representing mediator Faure Gnassingbé; and Ambassador Akok Manyuat Madut, representing the African Union Commission. The facilitators are also scheduled to visit Kigali, Bujumbura, and Kampala.
The African Union has recently outlined the structure of its mediation for the peace process in eastern DRC following a high-level meeting held in Lomé on January 16 and 17. The mediation is led by Togolese President Faure Gnassingbé, appointed as AU mediator, and supported by a Togolese team drawn from the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and the Presidency.
Five co-facilitators, all former African heads of state, have been assigned specific thematic areas: Olusegun Obasanjo for military and security issues; Sahle-Work Zewde for humanitarian affairs; Uhuru Kenyatta for dialogue with local armed groups; Mokgweetsi Masisi for regional economic cooperation; and Catherine Samba-Panza for civil society, reconciliation, and women’s issues.
The mediation mechanism also includes an independent joint secretariat bringing together Togo, the African Union, the East African Community, the Southern African Development Community, and the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region. The African Union Commission coordinates with international partners, including the United Nations, Qatar, the European Union, and the five permanent members of the UN Security Council.

body_en:
Doha QATAR, February 2, 2026 — The government of the DRC and the Congo River Alliance/March 23 Movement (AFC/M23) signed the mandate of the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR) in Doha on Monday.
The signing followed a meeting of the ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism, organized by Qatar as part of its mediation efforts to resolve the conflict in eastern DRC.
Both parties reaffirmed their commitment to the ceasefire and the Doha Peace Framework, signed on November 15, 2025, and expressed their determination to implement all provisions in good faith to support the peace process.
The meeting included members of the mechanism, with the United States and the African Union as observers, as well as Togo, the AU-appointed mediator, MONUSCO, and the ICGLR.
Discussions focused on the evolving situation and current challenges, emphasizing the need to implement concrete measures to strengthen monitoring, verification, and information sharing in support of the peace process.
Plans for implementing the mechanism by MONUSCO and the ICGLR were reviewed, and both parties reaffirmed their commitment to supporting these efforts. MONUSCO will deploy an initial mission to Uvira in the coming days to monitor the ceasefire, with communication channels established to facilitate operations.
Members also agreed on next steps to strengthen the effectiveness of the mechanism and ensure regular meetings within its framework.

excerpt: Tshopo February 5, 2026 — Following the AFC/M23 drone attacks last weekend at Bangboka Airport in Kisangani, the Governor of Tshopo, Paulin Lendongolia, issued a circular urging close collaboration with security services. The attacks were publicly claimed by the AFC/M23 rebellion
title_en: Governor Announces Strengthened Security Measures Following AFC/M23 Drone Attacks at Kisangani Airport
excerpt_en: Tshopo February 5, 2026 — Following the AFC/M23 drone attacks last weekend at Bangboka Airport in Kisangani, the Governor of Tshopo, Paulin Lendongolia, issued a circular urging close collaboration with security services. The attacks were publicly claimed by the AFC/M23 rebellion
body_en:
Tshopo February 5, 2026 — Following the AFC/M23 drone attacks last weekend at Bangboka Airport in Kisangani, the Governor of Tshopo, Paulin Lendongolia, issued a circular urging close collaboration with security services. The attacks were publicly claimed by the AFC/M23 rebellion.
Recipients of the circular — including village chiefs, street chiefs, block leaders, concession holders, and owners of hotels and guesthouses — are instructed to report any unknown or suspicious person within their jurisdictions.
The governor emphasized the active involvement of local officials in security operations codenamed "Yeba Voisin" and "Filimbi" (Know thy neighbor; whistle), aiming to strengthen community surveillance and prevent suspicious infiltration.
“No tolerance will be shown for any failure to comply with these instructions. Any official who fails, neglects, or refuses to transmit the required information will be held personally responsible and could be considered an accomplice, with all the consequences provided by law.” — Governor Paulin Lendongolia
Regarding the airport, the provincial governor visited Bangboka Airport, noting that operations are proceeding normally.
The AFC/M23 claimed that it targeted the drone command center at Kisangani Airport, which they assert is used to launch attacks in Walikale, Rutshuru, Lubero, Kalehe, Mwenga, Masisi, and Minembwe. The rebellion also claims to be monitoring Kisangani Airport. Authorities in Kisangani are calling on the population to remain calm.

excerpt_en: Kampala, January 30, 2026 — Uganda’s Chief of Defence Forces, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, has issued an apology to the United States following remarks he made targeting the U.S. Embassy in Kampala, which he later said were based on false information. Gen Muhoozi, who is also the son
body_en:
Kampala, January 30, 2026 — Uganda’s Chief of Defence Forces, Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, has issued an apology to the United States following remarks he made targeting the U.S. Embassy in Kampala, which he later said were based on false information.
Gen Muhoozi, who is also the son of President Yoweri Kaguta Museveni, had earlier posted on social media accusing the U.S. Embassy of helping opposition leader Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu, popularly known as Bobi Wine, to flee the country. He also announced a suspension of military cooperation with the United States, including joint operations in Somalia.
Bobi Wine was last seen at his home on the night of January 15–16, 2026, shortly after the presidential election, when security forces reportedly attempted to arrest him but he escaped. On January 29, he said publicly that no soldier knew his whereabouts and challenged Gen Muhoozi, saying, “Catch me if you can.”
Later the same day, Gen Muhoozi retracted his earlier statements, acknowledging that the claims were incorrect.
“I would like to apologize to our great friends, the United States of America, for the earlier message I deleted. I was misinformed. I spoke to the U.S. Ambassador to our country and everything is fine. We will continue our military cooperation as usual,” he said.
Gen Muhoozi further explained that Uganda’s Ambassador to the United Nations, Adonia Ayebare, played a key role in resolving the misunderstanding and praised him for his swift diplomatic intervention, suggesting he be appointed Minister of Foreign Affairs.

title: RRA Gives Vehicle Owners One Month to Complete ‘Mutation’ or Face Penalties
excerpt: Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) announced that vehicle owners who have not yet completed the transfer (‘mutation’) of their vehicles have been given one month to do so, warning that failure to comply may result in penalties, including the confiscatio
title_en: RRA Gives Vehicle Owners One Month to Complete ‘Mutation’ or Face Penalties
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) announced that vehicle owners who have not yet completed the transfer (‘mutation’) of their vehicles have been given one month to do so, warning that failure to comply may result in penalties, including the confiscatio
body_en:
Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) announced that vehicle owners who have not yet completed the transfer (‘mutation’) of their vehicles have been given one month to do so, warning that failure to comply may result in penalties, including the confiscation of vehicles. The announcement was made during a joint press conference with the Rwanda National Police, which is responsible for road safety.
The campaign runs from January 26 to February 28, 2026, and aims to assist owners who acquired vehicles through purchase, inheritance, or gifts but have not transferred them to their names, as required by law within eight days of ownership change.
Improved Services for Vehicle Transfers
Deputy Commissioner for Taxation and Communications at RRA, Uwitonze Jean Paulin, said the agency has expanded services to facilitate transfers:
In Kigali, transfers are now available in Gikondo, Canal Olympia in Rebero, and Kigali Pelé Stadium in Nyamirambo, in addition to the Masaka office.
Working days have been increased from Tuesdays and Thursdays to every day except Sundays, and staff handling transfers have been increased tenfold.
Provincial offices will also provide services daily except Sundays.
So far, more than 16,000 people have applied for vehicle transfers: 3,000 with no obstacles will receive services immediately, while 10,000 must first resolve specific issues. Uwitonze emphasized that all applications will be processed and no applicant will be denied service.
Common obstacles include: the previous owner being deceased or abroad, or unresolved tax arrears, which must be cleared before the transfer. Fees for transfers are 30,000 Rwf for motorcycles and 60,000 Rwf for cars, payable by one or both parties involved.
Safety and Enforcement Concerns
National Police Spokesperson ACP Rutikanga noted that untransferred vehicles complicate traffic enforcement. Vehicles may be driven by someone other than the registered owner, making it difficult to assign responsibility for violations or fines.
He added that some drivers intentionally use unregistered vehicles, which may contribute to accidents and hinder police investigations, as drivers often flee the scene.
The RRA and National Police urged all vehicle owners to complete the mutation process promptly to avoid penalties and improve road safety.

title: Rwanda Takes UK to International Court Over £50 Million Dispute
excerpt: Kigali, January 28, 2026 — Rwanda has filed a case against the United Kingdom at the International Court of Arbitration in the Netherlands, claiming £50 million over alleged breaches of a bilateral agreement on undocumented migrants and economic cooperation. The Rwandan governmen
title_en: Rwanda Takes UK to International Court Over £50 Million Dispute
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 28, 2026 — Rwanda has filed a case against the United Kingdom at the International Court of Arbitration in the Netherlands, claiming £50 million over alleged breaches of a bilateral agreement on undocumented migrants and economic cooperation. The Rwandan governmen
body_en:
Kigali, January 28, 2026 — Rwanda has filed a case against the United Kingdom at the International Court of Arbitration in the Netherlands, claiming £50 million over alleged breaches of a bilateral agreement on undocumented migrants and economic cooperation.
The Rwandan government says the UK terminated the agreement unilaterally without prior consultation. The case, initially filed on November 24, 2025, invokes Article 22 of the agreement, which outlined provisions for sending undocumented migrants to Kigali and supporting economic development initiatives under the partnership.
The agreement, originally signed in April 2022 and implemented on April 25, 2024, was part of a joint effort to manage illegal migration and provide support for migrants living in precarious conditions. Rwanda emphasized that the agreement also addressed economic inequalities that push migrants into informal economies.
Following the election of UK Prime Minister Sir Keir Starmer in July 2024, the UK suspended the agreement, claiming it could not prevent undocumented migrants from entering the country by boat. Rwanda condemned the decision, saying it was made without consultation and contravened the terms of the agreement.
Rwanda also stated that in December 2024, the UK requested that £50 million payments due in April 2025 and April 2026 be delayed, citing plans to terminate the agreement. Negotiations to revise the terms did not occur, leaving Rwanda to insist that the funds must be paid as stipulated.
Rwanda’s complaint highlights multiple alleged breaches, including:
Failure to honor the agreed payment terms,
Non-compliance with Article 18 regarding financial obligations,
Violation of Article 19 concerning support for migrants facing hardship.
The Rwandan government emphasized that the dispute arose after repeated efforts to resolve issues amicably, which the UK refused, leaving Rwanda with no alternative but to seek legal recourse.
Rwanda underlined its ongoing commitment to protecting migrants, providing safe living conditions, and offering opportunities to support their survival and integration, despite the UK’s alleged refusal to fulfill its obligations.

Rwanda condemned the decision, saying it was made without consultation and contravened the terms of the agreement.
Rwanda also stated that in December 2024, the UK requested that £50 million payments due in April 2025 and April 2026 be delayed, citing plans to terminate the agreement. Negotiations to revise the terms did not occur, leaving Rwanda to insist that the funds must be paid as stipulated.
Rwanda’s complaint highlights multiple alleged breaches, including:
Failure to honor the agreed payment terms,
Non-compliance with Article 18 regarding financial obligations,
Violation of Article 19 concerning support for migrants facing hardship.
The Rwandan government emphasized that the dispute arose after repeated efforts to resolve issues amicably, which the UK refused, leaving Rwanda with no alternative but to seek legal recourse.
Rwanda underlined its ongoing commitment to protecting migrants, providing safe living conditions, and offering opportunities to support their survival and integration, despite the UK’s alleged refusal to fulfill its obligations.

title_en: FBI Investigates 2024 Coup Attempt in Kinshasa
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC – February 7, 2026 – The United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is investigating a failed coup attempt that occurred in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) in 2024. On the morning of 19 May 2024, armed men led by Congolese-American Christian Malanga
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC – February 7, 2026 – The United States Federal Bureau of Investigation (FBI) is investigating a failed coup attempt that occurred in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) in 2024.
On the morning of 19 May 2024, armed men led by Congolese-American Christian Malanga stormed the presidential palace, claiming to have overthrown President Félix Tshisekedi. They also attacked the homes of senior officials, including former Economy Minister Vital Kamerhe, killing several of his bodyguards, and former Defense Minister Jean-Pierre Bemba.
Tshisekedi’s security forces engaged the assailants in a violent battle at the palace, killing Malanga and arresting several individuals, including his son Marcel and other Americans: Tyler Thomson, Benjamin Zalman-Polun, and Joseph Peter.
Those arrested at the presidential palace were sentenced to death, but American nationals were extradited to the U.S. in April 2025 for trial in their country of origin.
The U.S. Department of Justice announced charges including conspiracy to support terrorist acts, use of weapons of mass destruction, attacks on state infrastructure, and conspiracy to commit murder or kidnapping.
According to Radio France Internationale (RFI), prior to their trial in Utah in March 2026, two FBI agents traveled to Kinshasa to investigate the crimes and assess the damage caused by the coup attempt.
Officials expected to be questioned include investigators, prosecutors, defense attorneys, and judges involved at all levels in the case.
Conclusion
In summary, the report highlights a period of significant diplomatic tension and internal reform in Rwanda and the broader Great Lakes region from late January to early February 2026. Domestically, Rwanda is advancing its digital governance and export goals while addressing social security and tax compliance. Regionally, however, the situation remains fragile, characterized by escalating friction with Burundi and the DRC, ongoing conflict in eastern Congo, and the controversial use of foreign mercenaries. These developments underscore a complex landscape where Rwanda continues to strive for economic progress and international recognition while navigating deep-rooted regional security challenges.
By Jeff Buleli

title: Washington Hardens Stance: Direct Sanctions Loom Over Kigali Amid DRC Strategic Realignment
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 6, 2026 – Diplomatic and economic tensions are rising as Washington signals a tougher approach toward Rwanda, while strengthening its partnership with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). This comes amid ongoing efforts by President Félix Tshisekedi to secur
title_en: Washington Hardens Stance: Direct Sanctions Loom Over Kigali Amid DRC Strategic Realignment
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 6, 2026 – Diplomatic and economic tensions are rising as Washington signals a tougher approach toward Rwanda, while strengthening its partnership with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). This comes amid ongoing efforts by President Félix Tshisekedi to secur
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 6, 2026 – Diplomatic and economic tensions are rising as Washington signals a tougher approach toward Rwanda, while strengthening its partnership with the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). This comes amid ongoing efforts by President Félix Tshisekedi to secure geostrategic and economic support during his international tour.
Targeted Sanctions on Kigali The U.S. is reportedly considering direct sanctions against high-level Rwandan officials for their involvement in the M23 rebellion, despite previously signed agreements. These measures form part of a broader strategy to pressure Kigali and safeguard stability in eastern DRC.
DRC Secures Strategic Support The DRC is increasingly positioned as a strategic partner in critical minerals, with Washington reinforcing its willingness to support Kinshasa in both security and economic initiatives. A framework is being established to back high-impact development projects, translating political commitments into concrete actions for economic growth and supply chain security.
High-Level Engagements President Tshisekedi has held cordial discussions with prominent U.S. leaders, emphasizing strategic cooperation. These talks highlight the deepening bilateral ties and personal support for Tshisekedi, framing him as a key actor in regional stabilization and development.
Kigali Faces Growing Isolation Rwanda is reportedly confronting increasing international pressure, with historic allies shifting their positions. The country’s leadership has rejected accusations regarding interference in the DRC and defied calls for compliance, intensifying its diplomatic isolation. Analysts view this shift as a direct consequence of Rwanda’s admission of involvement in destabilizing eastern Congo, leaving Kigali with fewer international allies.
Implications for the Region The evolving dynamics signal a geostrategic realignment in Central Africa, strengthening the DRC’s role as a security and economic pivot while placing Rwanda under heightened scrutiny. Observers suggest these developments could reshape regional alliances and influence the future of critical mineral access and security cooperation.

title: Religious Leaders Call for Stronger Civil-Military Ties to Promote Peace in North Kivu
excerpt: Beni, North Kivu, February 7, 2026 – On Saturday, religious leaders urged the army’s civic and patriotic education service and the FARDC Grand North operational sector command to strengthen civil-military relations, seen as a guarantee of lasting peace, in Beni, North Kivu. The a
