title: AFC/M23 Drone Attack on Kisangani Airport: Investigations Continue and Measures Taken in Response to New Threats (Government)
excerpt: February 8, 2026 – The drone attack carried out by the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion against Kisangani International Airport and other military installations in the capital of Tshopo Province was discussed during the Council of Ministers meeting held on Friday, February 6, at
title_en: AFC/M23 Drone Attack on Kisangani Airport: Investigations Continue and Measures Taken in Response to New Threats (Government)
excerpt_en: February 8, 2026 – The drone attack carried out by the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion against Kisangani International Airport and other military installations in the capital of Tshopo Province was discussed during the Council of Ministers meeting held on Friday, February 6, at
body_en:
February 8, 2026 – The drone attack carried out by the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion against Kisangani International Airport and other military installations in the capital of Tshopo Province was discussed during the Council of Ministers meeting held on Friday, February 6, at the African Union City complex, chaired by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa.
In his security briefing, the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense and Veterans Affairs, Guy Kabombo, stated that the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) are maintaining their positions and ensuring the protection of civilians and property against attacks by the RDF–M23–AFC coalition, which have been systematically thwarted.
“This is particularly true of the aerial attacks using kamikaze drones, primarily targeting Bangoka International Airport and other military installations in Kisangani. All the drones launched were destroyed before reaching their targets. Initial findings from the investigation, based on the analysis of recovered debris, indicate the likely country of manufacture, the type of drones used, and the explosive payload carried by each device. However, the investigation is ongoing and appropriate measures are being taken to address any new threats,” the meeting report states.
Regarding South Kivu, the Deputy Prime Minister reported that loyalist forces repelled attacks by the RDF–M23–AFC coalition, regaining control of several villages. According to Guy Kabombo, the FARDC are continuing operations to defend national territory in the mid- and high-altitude plateaus of Fizi, Uvira, and Mwenga.
The drone attack on Kisangani airport, claimed by the AFC/M23, also prompted a strong response from the African Union. Through the Chairperson of the African Union Commission, Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, the organization firmly condemned the attack on airport infrastructure in a major urban center.
In a statement released on Friday, February 6, the African Union Commission emphasized that such an act, which seriously endangers civilians, constitutes a flagrant violation of international humanitarian law, particularly the principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution, and warned against the spread of hostilities to cities far from the front lines.
These incidents come months after the ratification of the Washington Accords between Kinshasa and Kigali, yet the situation on the ground remains alarming, marked by ongoing fighting between government forces and the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 in North Kivu and South Kivu. Both sides continue to accuse each other of violating these agreements.
The same applies to the Doha talks, held under the auspices of the Emir of Qatar, which have struggled to produce tangible results. These negotiations, aimed at addressing the root causes of the conflict, including the restoration of state authority and the reintegration of armed groups, recently resumed after a prolonged deadlock and resulted in the signing of the terms of reference for the ceasefire verification mechanism between the two parties.
Conclusion
In summary, the period from January 24 to February 8, 2026, reflects a Democratic Republic of Congo at a critical crossroads, defined by a complex interplay of diplomatic hope, persistent conflict, and strategic economic repositioning.
While the government has made significant strides in securing international support—notably through a strategic realignment with Washington regarding critical minerals and the renewal of AGOA trade benefits—the security situation in the East remains dire. The humanitarian crisis continues to escalate, highlighted by the staggering rates of sexual violence and the displacement of thousands due to ongoing clashes with the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 and ADF rebels.
Moving forward, the restoration of peace and territorial integrity will depend on:
Effective implementation of peace accords, such as the Washington and Doha agreements, which currently face significant stagnation.
Strengthening national cohesion through inclusive dialogue and the consolidation of state authority in volatile regions like North Kivu, South Kivu, and Ituri.
Securing economic sovereignty by ending the illegal plundering of mineral resources and finalizing key infrastructure like the Lobito Corridor and the Banana port.
Ultimately, while the DRC is positioning itself as a central player in the global energy transition, the success of this vision remains tethered to its ability to resolve the persistent cycle of violence and exploitation in its eastern provinces.
By Glad Musema
Jeff Buleli
body_fr:
February 8, 2026 – The drone attack carried out by the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion against Kisangani International Airport and other military installations in the capital of Tshopo Province was discussed during the Council of Ministers meeting held on Friday, February 6, at the African Union City complex, chaired by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa.
In his security briefing, the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense and Veterans Affairs, Guy Kabombo, stated that the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) are maintaining their positions and ensuring the protection of civilians and property against attacks by the RDF–M23–AFC coalition, which have been systematically thwarted.
“This is particularly true of the aerial attacks using kamikaze drones, primarily targeting Bangoka International Airport and other military installations in Kisangani. All the drones launched were destroyed before reaching their targets. Initial findings from the investigation, based on the analysis of recovered debris, indicate the likely country of manufacture, the type of drones used, and the explosive payload carried by each device. However, the investigation is ongoing and appropriate measures are being taken to address any new threats,” the meeting report states.
Regarding South Kivu, the Deputy Prime Minister reported that loyalist forces repelled attacks by the RDF–M23–AFC coalition, regaining control of several villages. According to Guy Kabombo, the FARDC are continuing operations to defend national territory in the mid- and high-altitude plateaus of Fizi, Uvira, and Mwenga.
The drone attack on Kisangani airport, claimed by the AFC/M23, also prompted a strong response from the African Union. Through the Chairperson of the African Union Commission, Mahmoud Ali Youssouf, the organization firmly condemned the attack on airport infrastructure in a major urban center.
In a statement released on Friday, February 6, the African Union Commission emphasized that such an act, which seriously endangers civilians, constitutes a flagrant violation of international humanitarian law, particularly the principles of distinction, proportionality, and precaution, and warned against the spread of hostilities to cities far from the front lines.
These incidents come months after the ratification of the Washington Accords between Kinshasa and Kigali, yet the situation on the ground remains alarming, marked by ongoing fighting between government forces and the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 in North Kivu and South Kivu. Both sides continue to accuse each other of violating these agreements.
The same applies to the Doha talks, held under the auspices of the Emir of Qatar, which have struggled to produce tangible results. These negotiations, aimed at addressing the root causes of the conflict, including the restoration of state authority and the reintegration of armed groups, recently resumed after a prolonged deadlock and resulted in the signing of the terms of reference for the ceasefire verification mechanism between the two parties.
Conclusion
In summary, the period from January 24 to February 8, 2026, reflects a Democratic Republic of Congo at a critical crossroads, defined by a complex interplay of diplomatic hope, persistent conflict, and strategic economic repositioning.
While the government has made significant strides in securing international support—notably through a strategic realignment with Washington regarding critical minerals and the renewal of AGOA trade benefits—the security situation in the East remains dire. The humanitarian crisis continues to escalate, highlighted by the staggering rates of sexual violence and the displacement of thousands due to ongoing clashes with the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 and ADF rebels.
Moving forward, the restoration of peace and territorial integrity will depend on:
Effective implementation of peace accords, such as the Washington and Doha agreements, which currently face significant stagnation.
Strengthening national cohesion through inclusive dialogue and the consolidation of state authority in volatile regions like North Kivu, South Kivu, and Ituri.
Securing economic sovereignty by ending the illegal plundering of mineral resources and finalizing key infrastructure like the Lobito Corridor and the Banana port.
Ultimately, while the DRC is positioning itself as a central player in the global energy transition, the success of this vision remains tethered to its ability to resolve the persistent cycle of violence and exploitation in its eastern provinces.
By Glad Musema
Jeff Buleli

title: Rwanda Rejects EU Parliament Interference, Says It Has No Jurisdiction
excerpt: Kigali, January 29, 2026 — Foreign Affairs Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe reminded the European Parliament that it has no jurisdiction over Rwanda, stressing that the country will not accept external directives or interference in its judicial affairs. He stated that Rwanda will no
title_en: Rwanda Rejects EU Parliament Interference, Says It Has No Jurisdiction
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 29, 2026 — Foreign Affairs Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe reminded the European Parliament that it has no jurisdiction over Rwanda, stressing that the country will not accept external directives or interference in its judicial affairs. He stated that Rwanda will no
body_en:
Kigali, January 29, 2026 — Foreign Affairs Minister Olivier Nduhungirehe reminded the European Parliament that it has no jurisdiction over Rwanda, stressing that the country will not accept external directives or interference in its judicial affairs.
He stated that Rwanda will not tolerate the arrogance and interference of EU lawmakers, particularly regarding cases before Rwandese courts. His remarks followed an EU Parliament statement issued on January 28, after members received Rémy Amahirwa, son of opposition figure Victoire Ingabire, who is currently detained and on trial in Rwanda.
The minister emphasized that Rwanda is not an EU member and has been independent from European colonialism for over 60 years. Meanwhile, Justice Minister Emmanuel Ugirashebuja told the UN Human Rights Council in Geneva on January 21 that Rwanda continues to make progress in human rights, adding that the justice system is functioning transparently.
Rwandan authorities also recalled that the Rwandan Parliament previously condemned EU calls for the release of Ingabire and others, reaffirming the country’s sovereignty and judicial independence.

title: Congolese Lawyers Move to Halt DRC-US Mineral Deal
excerpt: February 5, 2026 – Congolese lawyers and human rights groups have filed a lawsuit with the Constitutional Court of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) seeking to halt the country’s mining deal with the United States. The deal, signed on December 4, 2025, allows American in
title_en: Congolese Lawyers Move to Halt DRC-US Mineral Deal
excerpt_en: February 5, 2026 – Congolese lawyers and human rights groups have filed a lawsuit with the Constitutional Court of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) seeking to halt the country’s mining deal with the United States. The deal, signed on December 4, 2025, allows American in
body_en:
February 5, 2026 – Congolese lawyers and human rights groups have filed a lawsuit with the Constitutional Court of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) seeking to halt the country’s mining deal with the United States.
The deal, signed on December 4, 2025, allows American investors to control several mineral mines in the DRC in exchange for US support in building the country’s security forces.
Earlier, on December 24, 2025, Catholic Bishop Fulgence Muteba criticized the agreement, calling it a mortgage of the country’s natural resources. Speaking to Catholics in Lubumbashi, he said:"Did you know that we signed a 99-year agreement to exploit natural resources? Precious minerals will not last forever. How can someone mortgage a country's resources for 99 years?"
Following President Donald Trump’s announcement that the US would support peace in the DRC and invest in mining, the DRC government sent a list of mines to Washington D.C. in mid-January 2026 for American inspection.
In the January 2026 lawsuit, the lawyers argued that the agreement:
Violates the Constitution, as it required Parliamentary approval or a popular vote before signing.
Undermines the country’s sovereignty over natural resources.
Contravenes the principle of equality before the law.
Lawyer Jean-Marie Kalonji, one of the plaintiffs, said: "By filing this lawsuit with the Constitutional Court, we are fulfilling our obligations as Congolese to protect the sovereignty of our country and preserve our resources for future generations."
The Oakland Institute, a US-based organization advocating for property rights, expressed support for the lawsuit, calling it well-founded and pledging to continue assisting the plaintiffs.
This legal challenge marks a significant escalation in debates over the DRC’s mineral wealth, foreign investment, and national sovereignty, placing Tshisekedi’s government under intense scrutiny.

title: AI to Diagnose Patients and Prescribe Medication – Pilot Program Underway
excerpt: Kigali 3 February 2026 – Rwanda is testing an AI-powered healthcare application designed to assist doctors in diagnosing patients and making quick decisions about medication prescriptions. The pilot is part of a government-backed project, Horizon 1000, developed in collaboration
title_en: AI to Diagnose Patients and Prescribe Medication – Pilot Program Underway
excerpt_en: Kigali 3 February 2026 – Rwanda is testing an AI-powered healthcare application designed to assist doctors in diagnosing patients and making quick decisions about medication prescriptions. The pilot is part of a government-backed project, Horizon 1000, developed in collaboration
body_en:
Kigali 3 February 2026 – Rwanda is testing an AI-powered healthcare application designed to assist doctors in diagnosing patients and making quick decisions about medication prescriptions. The pilot is part of a government-backed project, Horizon 1000, developed in collaboration with the Bill Foundation and OpenAI.
The project, currently tested in about 50 hospitals over the past two years, aims to accelerate medical services and improve care without replacing doctors. Muhire Andrew, Director of Information Technology at the Ministry of Health, emphasized that the technology supports clinical decisions but does not substitute human judgment.
The application listens to patients describe their symptoms, records them, and helps medical staff determine the appropriate treatment, including urgent cases requiring advanced care. It is designed to function offline, addressing challenges in rural areas with limited internet access.
If successful, Horizon 1000 could expand to 1,000 hospitals across Africa by 2028. The technology seeks to address Rwanda’s healthcare workforce shortage, where currently one doctor serves 1,000 patients, compared to the WHO recommendation of four doctors per 1,000 patients.
Challenges remain, including language barriers, as the system currently operates in English, while 75% of Rwandans speak Kinyarwanda. Solutions are being explored to ensure accurate patient understanding and effective AI support.
Following the Cabinet’s 2023 approval of the five-year National Policy to Accelerate AI Technology, an estimated $76.5 million investment is projected to mainstream AI across sectors, boosting economic development and innovation in Rwanda.

title_en: RED Tabara Denies Ties to Rwanda, AFC/M23, and 2015 Burundi Coup Plot
excerpt_en: January 29, 2026 — The armed group RED Tabara has rejected accusations of collaborating with Rwanda, the AFC/M23 alliance, and the attempted coup in Burundi in May 2015. The denial follows statements by Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye, who said in a January 17 interview
body_en:
January 29, 2026 — The armed group RED Tabara has rejected accusations of collaborating with Rwanda, the AFC/M23 alliance, and the attempted coup in Burundi in May 2015.
The denial follows statements by Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye, who said in a January 17 interview that RED Tabara was being used by Rwanda to destabilize Burundi and reinforce AFC/M23 in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
In response, RED Tabara spokesperson Patrick Nahimana said the group has never cooperated with Rwanda, citing the 2021 handover of 19 RED Tabara fighters by Rwandan authorities to Burundi as evidence. He also dismissed any link to the 2015 coup attempt, stating that those responsible were Burundian soldiers and not RED Tabara, which he said was already active prior to the events.
The group further denied any collaboration with AFC/M23, past or present, and accused the Burundian government of attempting to divert attention from the root causes of its opposition, particularly the dismantling of the Arusha Peace Accords.
RED Tabara reaffirmed that its struggle is aimed at promoting democratic governance in Burundi.

excerpt: Kampala Uganda, 4 February 2026 – Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, Chief of Staff of the Ugandan Armed Forces and son of President Yoweri Museveni, announced he will sack immigration officials obstructing Rwandans in Uganda from obtaining official documents. In a statement on 3 February
title_en: Gen Muhoozi Orders Sacking of Officials Blocking Rwandans’ Documents
excerpt_en: Kampala Uganda, 4 February 2026 – Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, Chief of Staff of the Ugandan Armed Forces and son of President Yoweri Museveni, announced he will sack immigration officials obstructing Rwandans in Uganda from obtaining official documents. In a statement on 3 February
body_en:
Kampala Uganda, 4 February 2026 – Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, Chief of Staff of the Ugandan Armed Forces and son of President Yoweri Museveni, announced he will sack immigration officials obstructing Rwandans in Uganda from obtaining official documents.
In a statement on 3 February 2026, Gen Muhoozi declared:
“I have decided to immediately sack all immigration officials who are making it difficult for our Rwandans in Uganda to obtain documents. Others will be deployed soon.”
Rwandans in Uganda are recognized under the 1995 Constitution as a legal ethnic group, tracing their presence in the country to before February 1926. Some have long complained that officials withheld passports and identity papers over doubts about ancestry.
Previously, President Museveni emphasized that citizenship applies to those born in Uganda, those of Ugandan descent, and eligible foreigners, calling for grassroots reviews to ensure proper documentation. Despite this, some Rwandans are still waiting for their papers.

title: Washington Hosts Inaugural Ministerial Meeting on Critical Minerals, Spotlight on DRC
excerpt: Washington, D.C., February 4, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is at the center of global attention as the inaugural Ministerial Meeting on Critical Minerals convenes this Wednesday under the chairmanship of U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The high-level gatheri
title_en: Washington Hosts Inaugural Ministerial Meeting on Critical Minerals, Spotlight on DRC
excerpt_en: Washington, D.C., February 4, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is at the center of global attention as the inaugural Ministerial Meeting on Critical Minerals convenes this Wednesday under the chairmanship of U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The high-level gatheri
body_en:
Washington, D.C., February 4, 2026 – The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is at the center of global attention as the inaugural Ministerial Meeting on Critical Minerals convenes this Wednesday under the chairmanship of U.S. Secretary of State Marco Rubio. The high-level gathering aims to strengthen and diversify global supply chains to reduce China's dominance in this strategically vital sector.
The meeting forms part of “Project Vault,” an initiative launched under the Trump administration to establish a strategic U.S. reserve of critical minerals including rare earth elements, cobalt, and lithium, backed by $12 billion in funding.
Global Participation Organizers expect delegations from over 50 countries, spanning Europe, Asia, and Africa. The DRC will be represented at the highest level, with President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi officially attending.
A Central Player The Democratic Republic of Congo, with its vast reserves of cobalt and coltan, is considered a key actor in the global energy transition. Analysts say the Washington meeting could redefine the geopolitical balance around critical minerals, positioning Kinshasa as a strategic partner of the United States.

body_en:
Lubero, North Kivu – 07/02/2026 – Facing a humanitarian emergency in the Lubero territory, the Integrated Federation for Reconstruction and Development (FIRD) has launched a $70,000 fundraising campaign to assist survivors of ADF attacks. The solidarity initiative, named “Save the Survivors of the ADF Massacres,” seeks to provide medical and social care to dozens of victims affected by recent attacks in the Bapere sector and Baswagha chiefdom.
According to FIRD, the wounded are in critical condition, with many forced to interrupt treatment due to lack of financial resources. The campaign targets the immediate needs of more than 80 people, including:
Over 30 seriously injured individuals hospitalized in various healthcare facilities.
More than 40 orphaned children who lost their parents in the massacres.
Exorbitant medical costs, which some patients cannot cover.
Zaidel Ngolo, coordinator of FIRD, highlighted the scale of the financial needs, noting that some patients require transfers to specialized centers or even treatment abroad.
“The need is immense. Some of the injured face medical bills of $2,000 to $3,000. This campaign aims to raise approximately $70,000 to address urgent healthcare needs,” Ngolo explained.
The NGO is appealing to individuals, businesses, and all people of goodwill for compassion and generosity to save the lives of those affected by the violence.

title: After Meeting Denis Sassou Nguesso, Félix Tshisekedi Condemns “Unjust” and “Barbaric” War in Eastern DRC

title_en: After Meeting Denis Sassou Nguesso, Félix Tshisekedi Condemns “Unjust” and “Barbaric” War in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: Oyo, January 25, 2026 — President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) met on Saturday, January 24, with his Congolese counterpart, Denis Sassou Nguesso, in the city of Oyo, where the two leaders discussed the strengthening of bilateral cooperation a
body_en:
Oyo, January 25, 2026 — President Félix Antoine Tshisekedi of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) met on Saturday, January 24, with his Congolese counterpart, Denis Sassou Nguesso, in the city of Oyo, where the two leaders discussed the strengthening of bilateral cooperation and good neighborly relations between their countries.
The talks focused heavily on the deteriorating security situation in the Great Lakes region, particularly the ongoing conflict in eastern DRC, and efforts to achieve lasting peace. President Tshisekedi said that despite the existence of the Washington and Doha peace processes, some parties continue to fail to honor their commitments.
“He is an elder statesman of the region, a Head of State who is very influential,” Tshisekedi told the press after the meeting. “It was only natural to brief him on what is happening in the Democratic Republic of Congo. In the East, there is a war — an unjust and barbaric war imposed upon us. There are peace processes that have been initiated, to which the protagonists have committed, but which are not being respected by some.”
The meeting comes amid persistent tensions between Kinshasa and Kigali, despite the involvement of U.S. President Donald Trump and what authorities describe as renewed momentum in the Washington process, marked by the ratification of agreements by Presidents Félix Tshisekedi and Paul Kagame. However, the situation on the ground remains fragile, with both sides exchanging accusations of non-compliance.
A similar impasse is affecting the Doha talks, held under the auspices of the Emir of Qatar, between Kinshasa and the AFC/M23 rebellion, which the Congolese government says is supported by Rwanda. These negotiations, intended to address the root causes of the conflict — including the restoration of state authority and the reintegration of armed groups — have yet to yield tangible results. Several agreed measures, including those outlined in the joint communiqué, the ceasefire mechanism, the declaration of principles, and the framework agreement, remain unimplemented.
This diplomatic inertia has coincided with the continuation of violent clashes between the AFC/M23 and government forces. Meanwhile, calls from socio-political actors to convene a national dialogue have yet to be heeded.
After announcing its withdrawal from mediation efforts in March 2025, Angola has begun a gradual and discreet return to the peace process, relaunching consultations and increasing contacts with key stakeholders. In parallel, Togo hosted a high-level meeting on Saturday, January 17, 2026, aimed at strengthening the coherence and consolidation of peace initiatives in the DRC and the wider Great Lakes region.

title: Tanganyika Traffic Resumes Between Kalemie and Uvira After Weeks of Disruption
excerpt: Kalemie/Uvira, January 27, 2026 — After several weeks of suspension, lake traffic on Lake Tanganyika between the cities of Kalemie and Uvira officially resumed on Tuesday, January 27, 2026, authorities announced. The decision was confirmed by Christian Kitungwa Muteba, Governor o
title_en: Tanganyika Traffic Resumes Between Kalemie and Uvira After Weeks of Disruption
excerpt_en: Kalemie/Uvira, January 27, 2026 — After several weeks of suspension, lake traffic on Lake Tanganyika between the cities of Kalemie and Uvira officially resumed on Tuesday, January 27, 2026, authorities announced. The decision was confirmed by Christian Kitungwa Muteba, Governor o
body_en:
Kalemie/Uvira, January 27, 2026 — After several weeks of suspension, lake traffic on Lake Tanganyika between the cities of Kalemie and Uvira officially resumed on Tuesday, January 27, 2026, authorities announced.
The decision was confirmed by Christian Kitungwa Muteba, Governor of Tanganyika Province, in an official statement. The suspension had followed the deterioration of the security situation in Uvira, the second-largest city in South Kivu, which had been under the threat and control of the AFC/M23 rebellion. The instability posed serious risks to neighboring Tanganyika Province, particularly the danger of infiltration by lake.
As a result, all lake movements — including trade, passenger transport, and migration — had been strictly prohibited by provincial authorities. With the withdrawal of the rebellion from Uvira and improvements in security, the government has now lifted these restrictions as part of broader efforts to restore state authority.
“As part of the progressive restoration of state authority, ordered by the Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo, and the resumption of all economic activities and migratory movements previously interrupted for security reasons, lake traffic between the cities of Uvira and Kalemie will resume as of January 27, 2026,” Governor Kitungwa Muteba stated.
The reopening has been welcomed with relief by economic operators, travelers, and lakeside communities, for whom this route represents a vital corridor for commercial, social, and humanitarian exchanges between eastern and southeastern Democratic Republic of Congo.

excerpt: Kisangani, February 2, 2026 — Bangboka Airport, located 17 kilometers from downtown Kisangani, was targeted in an armed attack using kamikaze drones between 5:00 a.m. on Saturday, January 31 and 2:00 a.m. on Sunday, February 1, according to the Tshopo provincial government. Autho
title_en: FARDC Shoots Down 8 Drones Targeting Bangboka Airport, Authorities Blame AFC/M23
excerpt_en: Kisangani, February 2, 2026 — Bangboka Airport, located 17 kilometers from downtown Kisangani, was targeted in an armed attack using kamikaze drones between 5:00 a.m. on Saturday, January 31 and 2:00 a.m. on Sunday, February 1, according to the Tshopo provincial government. Autho
body_en:
Kisangani, February 2, 2026 — Bangboka Airport, located 17 kilometers from downtown Kisangani, was targeted in an armed attack using kamikaze drones between 5:00 a.m. on Saturday, January 31 and 2:00 a.m. on Sunday, February 1, according to the Tshopo provincial government.
Authorities reported that the drones carried unconventional munitions composed of submunitions, and attributed the attack to Rwanda and its allies in the AFC/M23, describing it as a "barbaric, unjust, and persistent aggression" against the Democratic Republic of Congo.
Thanks to the vigilance and professionalism of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and their security partners, eight drones were neutralized before reaching the airport. No casualties or major damage were reported.
Provincial authorities stated:
“This attack demonstrates once again Rwanda’s intention to undermine the Washington peace agreement.”
They also called on the international community “to move beyond mere condemnations and take concrete, deterrent measures to end an aggression lasting more than three decades, and to ensure the withdrawal of foreign forces and their proxies from occupied areas of the DRC.”
Residents near Bangboka Airport, who had begun to flee in fear, were urged to return home, as no evacuation is currently necessary.

excerpt_en: Rutshuru February 3, 2026 — Fighting erupted early Tuesday morning, February 3, between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo forces in Kivuma and Kanyangohe, two locations in the Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru territory) of North Kivu. The rebels, coming from the town of Mweso in neighboring M
body_en:
Rutshuru February 3, 2026 — Fighting erupted early Tuesday morning, February 3, between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo forces in Kivuma and Kanyangohe, two locations in the Bwito chiefdom (Rutshuru territory) of North Kivu.
The rebels, coming from the town of Mweso in neighboring Masisi territory, targeted these areas, located about five kilometers from this strategic town.
Reports indicate the AFC/M23 launched simultaneous attacks against Wazalendo positions on the hills overlooking Kivuma and Kanyangohe, aiming to dislodge them, but their offensive was unsuccessful.
After several hours of intense fighting, the rebels retreated to Mweso, their point of origin.
These clashes have caused massive civilian displacements, worsening the already dire humanitarian situation in the region. Many families fled their villages, seeking refuge in Mweso, Muhongozi, and other locations.
Local humanitarian sources report that the number of displaced people is increasing daily, with many families living in classrooms under precarious conditions, lacking adequate food, healthcare, and protection.

excerpt_en: February 8, 2026 – The European Union’s Special Representative for the Great Lakes region, Johan Borgstam, has completed his third mission to Angola, where he met with the country’s highest authorities to discuss the security situation in eastern DRC and regional efforts toward a
body_en:
February 8, 2026 – The European Union’s Special Representative for the Great Lakes region, Johan Borgstam, has completed his third mission to Angola, where he met with the country’s highest authorities to discuss the security situation in eastern DRC and regional efforts toward a political solution to the conflict.
According to a statement from the EU delegation in Luanda, Mr. Borgstam held talks with Angolan President João Lourenço, as well as the Ministers of Foreign Affairs, Defense, and Transport. Discussions focused on Angola’s role in advancing lasting peace in the Great Lakes region and its commitment to an inclusive political dialogue in the DRC.
The European Union reiterated its call for immediate de-escalation in eastern DRC, an effective and lasting ceasefire, and an end to all support for armed groups. title: Rwanda Urges UN to Enforce International Law Equally for All Countries
excerpt: New York, January 28, 2026 — Rwanda’s Ambassador to the United Nations, Martin Ngoga, has called on the UN Security Council not to selectively target developing countries while ignoring violations committed by powerful nations. The remarks were made during a debate organized by S
title_en: Rwanda Urges UN to Enforce International Law Equally for All Countries
excerpt_en: New York, January 28, 2026 — Rwanda’s Ambassador to the United Nations, Martin Ngoga, has called on the UN Security Council not to selectively target developing countries while ignoring violations committed by powerful nations. The remarks were made during a debate organized by S
body_en:
New York, January 28, 2026 — Rwanda’s Ambassador to the United Nations, Martin Ngoga, has called on the UN Security Council not to selectively target developing countries while ignoring violations committed by powerful nations. The remarks were made during a debate organized by Somalia on international law enforcement.
Ambassador Ngoga stressed that international law exists, but its enforcement is inconsistent. “The collapse of respect for the law did not start yesterday… principles were respected only when necessary,” he said, highlighting that serious violations are often ignored when committed by influential states, while developing nations are punished disproportionately.
He criticized the council for delaying action even when civilians are dying and for failing to prevent ethnic persecution, stating, “Violations of international humanitarian law are discussed rather than condemned. Silence and discrimination destroy trust faster than any weapon.”
Ngoga emphasized that security concerns of all states must be taken seriously, regardless of size or power. “Selective enforcement… undermines the credibility of this institution. The question is not whether the rule of law is necessary, but whether we want to enforce it equally for all countries, large and small,” he said.
UN Secretary-General Antonio Guterres acknowledged that powerful countries often dictate what is considered acceptable, particularly during conflicts and divisions, creating a “wall” that influences international law selectively.
Ambassador Ngoga concluded that for international law to be effective, regional and international organizations must cooperate, and UN agencies need stronger coordination to ensure equal enforcement across all countries.

title: DRC Minister Urges Banyamulenge to Visit Government-Controlled Areas Amid Tensions
excerpt: 5 February 2026 – Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Rwanda, has called on the Banyamulenge community to visit areas controlled by the DRC government to witness the situation firsthand, asserting that their relatives are not being kill
title_en: DRC Minister Urges Banyamulenge to Visit Government-Controlled Areas Amid Tensions
excerpt_en: 5 February 2026 – Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Rwanda, has called on the Banyamulenge community to visit areas controlled by the DRC government to witness the situation firsthand, asserting that their relatives are not being kill
body_en:
5 February 2026 – Ambassador Olivier Nduhungirehe, Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation of Rwanda, has called on the Banyamulenge community to visit areas controlled by the DRC government to witness the situation firsthand, asserting that their relatives are not being killed.
The announcement follows a meeting on 4 February 2025 in Washington D.C., United States, where DRC Government Spokesperson Patrick Muyaya met with Congolese Tutsi, predominantly Banyamulenge. The meeting, widely publicized, aimed to deny reports of atrocities committed in Minembwe since 2017.
According to Muyaya, representatives including Me Emile Muhizi stated that the AFC/M23 opposes the DRC government, and that Rwanda allegedly seeks to unite them with other Congolese. They pledged to continue denouncing AFC/M23 actions.
Minister Nduhungirehe emphasized that media campaigns alone are insufficient, stating:"The meeting in nice rooms in Washington that was advertised in the media is good, but these people visiting areas controlled by the FARDC, FDLR, Wazalendo and FDNB, unaccompanied, would be better."
The Mahoro Peace Association (MPA), representing Banyamulenge in the United States, criticized the meeting, asserting that Muhizi and his colleagues are not elected representatives. The MPA, led by President Douglas G. Kabunda, stated:"These individuals who were selected, not elected, met with Minister Muyaya on their own. What they said has nothing to do with the position of the Banyamulenge Community living in the United States and has nothing to do with our elected institutions."
Muhizi and colleagues claimed that allegations of mistreatment of the Banyamulenge are false. However, tensions with Wazalendo groups, led by Gen. William Amuri Yakutumba and John Makanaki, continue, as they regard the Banyamulenge as Rwandans who should leave the DRC.
Hatred toward the Banyamulenge has escalated in South Kivu and North Kivu. In September 2025, Wazalendo fighters expelled Brig Gen Olivier Gasita from Uvira, labeling him a Tutsi, Rwandan, and enemy, giving the community 10 days to leave. In January 2026, Habyarimana Mbitse (alias Jules Mulumba), speaking for Wazalendo, attacked Lt Gen Pacifique Masunzu, calling him a traitor despite his service to the DRC government after separating from forces supporting the Banyamulenge.
The situation underscores ongoing tensions between the Banyamulenge, Wazalendo, and the DRC government, highlighting deep-rooted mistrust and security concerns in the eastern provinces.

title: TI-Rwanda Report Flags Persistent Gender-Based Corruption in Education and Health Sectors
excerpt: Kigali, January 29, 2026 — A new report by Transparency International Rwanda (TI-Rwanda) has revealed that despite Rwanda’s progress in improving service delivery, corruption, particularly gender-based corruption, remains prevalent in the education and health sectors. The finding
title_en: TI-Rwanda Report Flags Persistent Gender-Based Corruption in Education and Health Sectors
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 29, 2026 — A new report by Transparency International Rwanda (TI-Rwanda) has revealed that despite Rwanda’s progress in improving service delivery, corruption, particularly gender-based corruption, remains prevalent in the education and health sectors. The finding
body_en:
Kigali, January 29, 2026 — A new report by Transparency International Rwanda (TI-Rwanda) has revealed that despite Rwanda’s progress in improving service delivery, corruption, particularly gender-based corruption, remains prevalent in the education and health sectors.
The findings were presented at a consultative meeting bringing together TI-Rwanda and key stakeholders to jointly assess the state of corruption in service provision.
Education Sector
The report highlights that one of the major challenges in education is the widespread demand for gender-based bribes, especially in higher education institutions and universities. Some teachers reportedly abuse their authority by soliciting sexual favors from female students in exchange for good grades, academic promotion, or access to internships.
Survey results from 1,350 respondents show that:
8% were asked to bribe to secure a school place,
5% were asked to bribe to obtain good grades,
5% were asked to bribe to win a school food supply contract,
5% were asked to bribe to change their major.
The report further notes that both sexual and financial bribery continue to undermine the education system, disproportionately affecting vulnerable groups, including 7.8% of girls, 8.6% from poor families, 9.2% of persons with disabilities, 46.1% with mental disabilities, and 10.2% facing other challenges.
Health Sector
In the health sector, a separate survey of 1,400 residents found persistent risks of corruption in the delivery of health services, including the payment of bribes to receive care more quickly.
Gender-based corruption was particularly reported in maternal and reproductive health services, where some women said they were asked to provide sexual favors in exchange for services they are legally entitled to receive.
Overall, 26% of respondents reported encountering bribery in health facilities. Corruption rates were estimated at 5% in primary health care facilities, 4.4% in district health facilities, and 3.6% in central hospitals.
Official Reaction
TI-Rwanda’s Director of Programs and Research, Albert Rwego Kavatiri, said many victims are unaware they are being bribed or are afraid to report such acts, noting that bribery is punishable under the law.
“The numbers are low, but even though they are low, we don’t want them to disappear completely, we want the few people who still exist to be tracked and punished,” he said.

excerpt: Doha, January 28, 2026 — Peace talks between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government and the AFC/M23 coalition could resume this weekend, following a suspension since early December 2025 when AFC/M23 captured Uvira after a week of fighting in the Ruzizi Valley, South Ki
title_en: Doha Peace Talks Between DRC and AFC/M23 Could Resume This Weekend
excerpt_en: Doha, January 28, 2026 — Peace talks between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government and the AFC/M23 coalition could resume this weekend, following a suspension since early December 2025 when AFC/M23 captured Uvira after a week of fighting in the Ruzizi Valley, South Ki
body_en:
Doha, January 28, 2026 — Peace talks between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government and the AFC/M23 coalition could resume this weekend, following a suspension since early December 2025 when AFC/M23 captured Uvira after a week of fighting in the Ruzizi Valley, South Kivu Province.
The Qatari government, which is facilitating the talks, has invited both parties to a meeting to review the implementation of ceasefire agreements. While AFC/M23 has confirmed it will send a delegation, the DRC government initially did not.
After AFC/M23 withdrew all its fighters from Uvira on January 17, 2026, Qatar has renewed efforts to bring the sides together. The rescheduled talks are planned for January 31 to February 1, 2026.
The discussions are expected to focus on activating the body responsible for monitoring the ceasefire and identifying ways to rebuild trust between the DRC government and AFC/M23.

excerpt_en: Kisangani DRC 4 February 2026 – The AFC/M23 coalition confirmed it carried out a drone attack on Bangoka Airport in Kisangani, Tshopo Province, during the night of 31 January–1 February 2026. Spokesman Lawrence Kanyuka said the operation targeted drone launch sites used in North
body_en:
Kisangani DRC 4 February 2026 – The AFC/M23 coalition confirmed it carried out a drone attack on Bangoka Airport in Kisangani, Tshopo Province, during the night of 31 January–1 February 2026.
Spokesman Lawrence Kanyuka said the operation targeted drone launch sites used in North Kivu and South Kivu, accusing DRC government forces of using them to attack civilians.
“AFC/M23 will not remain passive while civilians are targeted. Wherever crimes are committed, we will strike evil at its source,” Kanyuka said.
The group called on the Kinshasa government to choose between peace and war, urging respect for the ceasefire. It also rejected any blame directed at third parties, claiming the equipment used had been seized at Goma and Kavumu airports, and warned that the government is not the only actor capable of using drones.
body_fr:
Kisangani DRC 4 February 2026 – The AFC/M23 coalition confirmed it carried out a drone attack on Bangoka Airport in Kisangani, Tshopo Province, during the night of 31 January–1 February 2026.
Spokesman Lawrence Kanyuka said the operation targeted drone launch sites used in North Kivu and South Kivu, accusing DRC government forces of using them to attack civilians.
“AFC/M23 will not remain passive while civilians are targeted. Wherever crimes are committed, we will strike evil at its source,” Kanyuka said.
The group called on the Kinshasa government to choose between peace and war, urging respect for the ceasefire. It also rejected any blame directed at third parties, claiming the equipment used had been seized at Goma and Kavumu airports, and warned that the government is not the only actor capable of using drones.

title: President Félix Tshisekedi Reaffirms Commitment to Inclusive and Peaceful Dialogue
excerpt: On Saturday, January 31, President Félix Tshisekedi reaffirmed his openness to dialogue among Congolese citizens, during a New Year’s greetings ceremony with ambassadors and diplomats accredited to the DRC in Kinshasa. “In this context, national unity is more essential than ever.
title_en: President Félix Tshisekedi Reaffirms Commitment to Inclusive and Peaceful Dialogue
excerpt_en: On Saturday, January 31, President Félix Tshisekedi reaffirmed his openness to dialogue among Congolese citizens, during a New Year’s greetings ceremony with ambassadors and diplomats accredited to the DRC in Kinshasa. “In this context, national unity is more essential than ever.
body_en:
On Saturday, January 31, President Félix Tshisekedi reaffirmed his openness to dialogue among Congolese citizens, during a New Year’s greetings ceremony with ambassadors and diplomats accredited to the DRC in Kinshasa.
“In this context, national unity is more essential than ever. That is why we reaffirm our openness to a peaceful and inclusive dialogue, resolutely aimed at consolidating national cohesion, without ever calling into question the institutions established through universal suffrage,” he declared.
The Head of State emphasized that any such dialogue would take place on national soil and be organized by the institutions of the Republic, in accordance with the Constitution, the laws of the Republic, and democratic principles.
He stressed that this process cannot serve to downplay aggression or dilute responsibilities.
“Justice will take its normal course, rigorously, to the very end, and without leniency, in order to honor the memory of those unjustly killed,” he said.
On this occasion, the President called on the international community to take concrete action to protect the country’s sovereignty and support peace efforts. He reiterated his refusal to negotiate with the perpetrators of crimes committed against the Congolese people.
He also pointed to recent remarks by a Rwandan diplomat before the U.S. Congress, officially acknowledging security cooperation between Rwanda and the AFC/M23 rebellion, saying this confirms the DRC’s position and must be taken seriously by the international community.
“This recognition is not a mere communication ploy, nor a political strategy. It sheds a harsh light on what numerous reports and multiple partners have long been pointing out: the existence of decisive support for an armed insurgent movement operating on the sovereign territory of the Democratic Republic of Congo,” he added.
He concluded by stating that no cause, narrative, or security justification can legitimize occupation, parallel administrations, forced displacement, or the plundering of resources to the detriment of a United Nations member state.

title: Five Dead in SNCC Train Derailment Near Kabanda Bridge
excerpt: On Saturday, January 31, a train operated by the National Railway Company of Congo (SNCC) derailed in Tanganyika province, resulting in five deaths and multiple injuries. Two of the victims were burned beyond recognition. The Bana-Katanga train left the tracks and plunged into a
title_en: Five Dead in SNCC Train Derailment Near Kabanda Bridge
excerpt_en: On Saturday, January 31, a train operated by the National Railway Company of Congo (SNCC) derailed in Tanganyika province, resulting in five deaths and multiple injuries. Two of the victims were burned beyond recognition. The Bana-Katanga train left the tracks and plunged into a
body_en:
On Saturday, January 31, a train operated by the National Railway Company of Congo (SNCC) derailed in Tanganyika province, resulting in five deaths and multiple injuries. Two of the victims were burned beyond recognition.
The Bana-Katanga train left the tracks and plunged into a ravine near the Kabanda bridge, between the villages of Kiluba and Makala, causing a fire and significant material damage.
According to Norris Mulongoy, provincial Minister of Transport for Tanganyika, the accident was caused by the poor condition of the tracks. Several injured passengers were transferred to Kalemie for medical care.
“The locomotive left the tracks before plunging into the ravine, causing a fire. Five people—three men, a woman, and a baby—were burned beyond recognition. This morning, the provincial government dispatched a team that provided details of the tragedy,” Mulongoy said.
Authorities continue to search for any additional bodies in the wreckage. Some local sources suggest the death toll may be higher, reporting eight dead and five injured.

title: Kinshasa Pays Final Tribute to Brigadier General Muaku Mbuluku Daniel
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 24, 2026 — Final tributes were paid on Friday, January 23, to Brigadier General Muaku Mbuluku Daniel, former commander of the 33rd Military Region of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), nearly four months after his death. The late gener
title_en: Kinshasa Pays Final Tribute to Brigadier General Muaku Mbuluku Daniel
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 24, 2026 — Final tributes were paid on Friday, January 23, to Brigadier General Muaku Mbuluku Daniel, former commander of the 33rd Military Region of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), nearly four months after his death. The late gener
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 24, 2026 — Final tributes were paid on Friday, January 23, to Brigadier General Muaku Mbuluku Daniel, former commander of the 33rd Military Region of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), nearly four months after his death.
The late general, who died on Friday, September 12, 2025, following a sudden illness while on duty, was laid to rest at the “Le Repos du Soldat” military cemetery in Kinshasa. He passed away at the Uvira General Hospital, where he had been serving in South Kivu province.
His burial was preceded by a state-level funeral ceremony held at the Ave Maria venue in the Kasa-Vubu district, attended by the Second Vice-President of the National Assembly, Christophe Mboso N’kodia, and the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, who represented the President of the Republic and Supreme Commander of the FARDC, Félix Antoine Tshisekedi Tshilombo. Also present were general and senior officers, civil authorities, and members of the bereaved family.
On behalf of the Supreme Commander of the FARDC, the Minister of National Defense laid a wreath, honoring the late officer’s loyal service to the nation and his death in the line of duty.
Speaking for the family, a representative described the general as “a beloved man whose life was built on rigor, sacrifice, and selflessness.” He added that Brigadier General Muaku Mbuluku Daniel “embodied the fundamental values of the army: honor, discipline, loyalty, and a sense of duty,” noting that he “wore the uniform with dignity, exercised command with justice, and fulfilled his responsibilities with exemplary integrity.”
A graduate of the 23rd class of the Kananga Officer Training School, the late general had served the nation since 1974. “Almost his entire adult life was dedicated to serving his country, often far from his family, with the sole motivation of defending the people and honoring the national flag,” the family representative said.
A well-known figure in the military hierarchy of South Kivu, General Muaku had recently visited those wounded in deadly demonstrations attributed to the Wazalendo. He had arrived in Uvira on August 4, shortly after his appointment, to succeed General Dunia Kashindi as commander of the 33rd Military Region.
He was assisted by two deputies: General Olivier Gasita Mukunda, in charge of operations and intelligence, and Jean-Ladis Mabosso, in charge of administration.
The announcement of his death came amid a tense security context in Uvira, where demonstrations had erupted over the appointment of General Olivier Gasita Mukunda. Sections of the local population had demanded his removal, prompting a government delegation to travel to the city on Thursday, September 11, 2025.

title: Lake Tanganyika Traffic Resumes Between Kalemie and Uvira After Weeks of Disruption
excerpt: Kalemie/Uvira, January 27, 2026 – 17:38 — After several weeks of suspension due to insecurity in Uvira, traffic on Lake Tanganyika between the cities of Kalemie (Tanganyika Province) and Uvira (South Kivu) officially resumed on Tuesday, January 27, 2026. The decision was announce
title_en: Lake Tanganyika Traffic Resumes Between Kalemie and Uvira After Weeks of Disruption
excerpt_en: Kalemie/Uvira, January 27, 2026 – 17:38 — After several weeks of suspension due to insecurity in Uvira, traffic on Lake Tanganyika between the cities of Kalemie (Tanganyika Province) and Uvira (South Kivu) officially resumed on Tuesday, January 27, 2026. The decision was announce
body_en:
Kalemie/Uvira, January 27, 2026 – 17:38 — After several weeks of suspension due to insecurity in Uvira, traffic on Lake Tanganyika between the cities of Kalemie (Tanganyika Province) and Uvira (South Kivu) officially resumed on Tuesday, January 27, 2026.
The decision was announced by Governor Christian Kitungwa Muteba of Tanganyika Province. The suspension had been implemented in response to the threat posed by the AFC/M23 rebellion, which had temporarily seized control over parts of Uvira, creating risks of infiltration and disruption across the lake.
“With the progressive restoration of state authority, ordered by the Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo, and the resumption of economic and migratory activities previously interrupted for security reasons, lake traffic between Uvira and Kalemie will resume as of January 27, 2026,” the governor’s statement read.
The reopening of this vital transport route is expected to boost trade, migration, and humanitarian activities, providing relief to local populations and economic operators who rely on the lake for daily commerce and travel.
This development comes after the withdrawal of the AFC/M23 rebellion from Uvira and reflects the ongoing efforts of the central government and provincial authorities to restore security and normalcy in eastern DRC.
Residents and businesses have welcomed the resumption, highlighting the lake’s importance as a key commercial and social link connecting the East and Southeast regions of the Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: Tshisekedi Highlights Rwanda-AFC/M23 Collaboration, Calls for UN Action
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 31, 2026 — President Félix Tshisekedi addressed ambassadors and diplomats at the New Year's greetings ceremony at the Palais de la Nation, reacting to Rwanda’s official admission of collaboration with the AFC/M23 rebel group in eastern DRC. This acknowledgment w
title_en: Tshisekedi Highlights Rwanda-AFC/M23 Collaboration, Calls for UN Action
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 31, 2026 — President Félix Tshisekedi addressed ambassadors and diplomats at the New Year's greetings ceremony at the Palais de la Nation, reacting to Rwanda’s official admission of collaboration with the AFC/M23 rebel group in eastern DRC. This acknowledgment w
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 31, 2026 — President Félix Tshisekedi addressed ambassadors and diplomats at the New Year's greetings ceremony at the Palais de la Nation, reacting to Rwanda’s official admission of collaboration with the AFC/M23 rebel group in eastern DRC. This acknowledgment was made by Mathilde Mukantabana, Rwanda’s Ambassador to the United States, before the US House of Representatives.
According to Tshisekedi, the admission reduces the scope for denial, clarifies responsibilities, and obliges the international community, particularly the United Nations, to implement Security Council resolutions.
“For years, we have denounced, with evidence, the external support fueling armed violence on our soil. Now, a high-ranking Rwandan official has officially confirmed security coordination with the AFC/M23 rebels. This is not a PR exercise or a political strategy. It exposes the decisive support provided to an armed insurgent movement operating on Congolese sovereign territory,” declared Félix Tshisekedi.
He emphasized:
“This admission constitutes a major turning point: it reduces denial, clarifies responsibilities, and compels action through international law, UN resolutions, and political commitments. No narrative, cause, or security justification can legitimize de facto occupation, parallel administrations, forced displacements, or plundering of resources against a UN member state.”
For the first time, Rwanda officially acknowledged its coordination with AFC/M23 in eastern DRC. Kigali claims this is a defensive measure aimed at protecting the Tutsi population and preventing a resurgence of genocidal violence.
In her statement to the US Congress on January 22, Mathilde Mukantabana explained that this coordination allowed the AFC/M23 to withdraw from Uvira, signaling commitment to de-escalation.
She further stated:
“Rwanda is engaging in security coordination with the AFC/M23 to build trust through transparency. The AFC/M23 has legitimate grievances against Kinshasa. Rwanda and the AFC/M23 share a common interest in protecting Tutsis from the FDLR and other extremist militias. Rwanda’s interest is also to prevent a cross-border genocidal insurgency threatening its existence.”
Kigali stresses that the coordination is strictly defensive, conditional, time-limited, linked to disarmament and neutralization of the FDLR, and does not seek to influence internal DRC politics.

excerpt: Uvira February 3, 2026 — The Congolese National Police (PNC) officially returned to the city of Uvira on Tuesday, February 3, after nearly two months of absence. This coastal town on Lake Tanganyika had been under the control of the AFC/M23 rebels. The police officers had previou

excerpt_en: Uvira February 3, 2026 — The Congolese National Police (PNC) officially returned to the city of Uvira on Tuesday, February 3, after nearly two months of absence. This coastal town on Lake Tanganyika had been under the control of the AFC/M23 rebels. The police officers had previou
body_en:
Uvira February 3, 2026 — The Congolese National Police (PNC) officially returned to the city of Uvira on Tuesday, February 3, after nearly two months of absence. This coastal town on Lake Tanganyika had been under the control of the AFC/M23 rebels.
The police officers had previously crossed into Burundi as the rebels advanced. Representing a company of approximately 100 officers, they entered through the Kavimvira border post, between the Burundian town of Gatuma and Uvira, in the presence of numerous onlookers.
A parade was held, attended by the interim mayor of Uvira and his deputy, symbolizing the restoration of state authority following the rebel withdrawal under U.S. pressure.
“This is the return of the State. It was the army that came before; now the police, who ensure public order, are here. This confirms that state authority is returning and being reasserted,” declared Kyky Kifara, the interim mayor of Uvira.
He also urged residents to reflect on past behavior: “What we were before the aggression must not be what we will become. Uvira has suffered greatly; it is being watched. We must be role models,” he added.
Following the AFC/M23 withdrawal, the army immediately began redeploying in Uvira and surrounding areas.
Uvira is the second-largest city in South Kivu after Bukavu, and during the rebel occupation, it had temporarily assumed the role of provincial capital, with provincial institutions transferred to the city.

title: South Africa to Withdraw Troops from MONUSCO
excerpt: February 8, 2026 – 09:38 – South Africa has decided to withdraw its military contribution from the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUSCO). According to the South African Presidency, President Cyril Ramaphosa informed UN Sec
title_en: South Africa to Withdraw Troops from MONUSCO
excerpt_en: February 8, 2026 – 09:38 – South Africa has decided to withdraw its military contribution from the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUSCO). According to the South African Presidency, President Cyril Ramaphosa informed UN Sec
body_en:
February 8, 2026 – 09:38 – South Africa has decided to withdraw its military contribution from the United Nations Organization Stabilization Mission in the Democratic Republic of Congo (MONUSCO). According to the South African Presidency, President Cyril Ramaphosa informed UN Secretary-General António Guterres of this decision.
South Africa is among the top ten troop-contributing countries to MONUSCO, with more than 700 soldiers deployed in the DRC under the UN peacekeeping mandate.
In a statement, the Presidency said that during a telephone conversation on January 12, 2026, President Ramaphosa explained that the unilateral withdrawal decision was motivated by the need to consolidate and reorient resources of the South African National Defence Force, after 27 years of supporting UN peacekeeping operations in the DRC.
The Presidency further indicated that South Africa will work with the United Nations to finalize the timeline and modalities of the withdrawal, which is expected to be completed before the end of 2026. President Ramaphosa also welcomed the UN Secretary-General’s appreciation of the decision.
The statement added that the South African government will continue to maintain close bilateral relations with the DRC government and support multilateral peace efforts led by the Southern African Development Community (SADC), the African Union (AU), and the United Nations to achieve lasting peace in the DRC.
In December 2025, the UN Security Council unanimously adopted Resolution 2808 (2025), extending MONUSCO’s mandate until December 20, 2026, including, on an exceptional basis, its Force Intervention Brigade.
Under this resolution, MONUSCO is authorized to maintain a maximum strength of 11,500 military personnel, 600 military observers and staff officers, 443 police officers, and 1,270 formed police unit members. Its strategic priorities remain:
Protection of civilians in its areas of deployment,
Implementation of the objectives set out in Resolution 2773 (2025), and
Stabilization and strengthening of state institutions in the DRC.
The Council also authorized MONUSCO to support the implementation of a permanent ceasefire in line with Resolution 2773 (2025). France, the penholder of the resolution, said it aims to place MONUSCO “on the front line of support for peace efforts,” including those of the African Union, Togo’s mediation, sub-regional organizations, as well as the United States and Qatar.

title_en: Burundi Ombudsman Says She Is Being Threatened for Exposing Illegal Activities
excerpt_en: Bujumbura, January 28, 2026 — Burundi’s Ombudsman, Aimée-Laurentine Kanyana, has told the National Assembly that powerful individuals are threatening her in an effort to obstruct her work and silence her for exposing illegal activities. Addressing lawmakers, Kanyana said those be
body_en:
Bujumbura, January 28, 2026 — Burundi’s Ombudsman, Aimée-Laurentine Kanyana, has told the National Assembly that powerful individuals are threatening her in an effort to obstruct her work and silence her for exposing illegal activities.
Addressing lawmakers, Kanyana said those behind the pressure would have arrested her if they could. “The problem is that they do not arrest the Ombudsman, otherwise there would be people who would have arrested her,” she stated.
In response, National Assembly Speaker Daniel Gélase Ndabirabe urged parliamentarians to support Kanyana so she can continue her duties without intimidation.
Her remarks come amid broader concerns over pressure on public officials. On December 28, 2025, Finance Minister Alain Ndikumana told the Senate that the management of the fertilizer company FOMI was intimidating him after the government refused to grant more than 50 billion Burundian francs not предусмотр in its contract.
Ndikumana said he would continue his work despite the pressure, stressing the need for responsible public spending. Senate President Gervais Ndirakobuca pledged legislative support, saying lawmakers would help confront corruption and defend those who speak the truth.

title: Rwanda Recognized Globally for Excellence in Government Services
excerpt: Dubai UAE, 4 February 2026 – Rwanda has been awarded global recognition as the country achieving the best improvements in government services, announced by the Rwandan Embassy in the UAE. The award was presented at the GovTech Prize 2026 during the World Government Summit (WGS) i
title_en: Rwanda Recognized Globally for Excellence in Government Services
excerpt_en: Dubai UAE, 4 February 2026 – Rwanda has been awarded global recognition as the country achieving the best improvements in government services, announced by the Rwandan Embassy in the UAE. The award was presented at the GovTech Prize 2026 during the World Government Summit (WGS) i
body_en:
Dubai UAE, 4 February 2026 – Rwanda has been awarded global recognition as the country achieving the best improvements in government services, announced by the Rwandan Embassy in the UAE. The award was presented at the GovTech Prize 2026 during the World Government Summit (WGS) in Dubai, UAE.
The award-winning initiative is the IremboGov platform, developed by the Irembo company, which has significantly enhanced citizens’ access to government services through digital technology.
The Rwandan Ambassador to the UAE, John Mirenge, accepted the award on behalf of the government, alongside Estelle Kayitesi, Director General for Policy and Partnerships at Irembo.
The WGS, established in 2013, convenes government leaders, sector experts, and the private sector to address governance challenges and explore emerging technologies for effective service delivery. The 2026 summit brought together participants from 150 countries.
The GovTech Prize honors government agencies that innovatively improve service delivery through technology. Over the past decade, thousands of applications from 126 countries have competed for this recognition.
Since its launch in 2015, IremboGov now offers over 240 services, enabling citizens to access government services remotely, without physically visiting offices. Monthly, the platform processes over 500,000 requests, with 80% of services paid electronically.
Rwanda’s digital government expansion is supported by growing internet and mobile access. According to the National Institute of Statistics (NISR), over 12 million Rwandans own and use phones, and nine million access the internet, while in 2024, approximately 680 government services were available digitally.
This recognition underscores Rwanda’s leadership in leveraging technology for citizen-centric governance.

title: RRA Urges Timely Payment of Property and Rental Income Taxes
excerpt: Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) has reminded taxpayers to pay their property tax and rental income tax for 2026 before the January 31 deadline. The notice affects business owners and rental property owners, who must declare and pay taxes for the prev
title_en: RRA Urges Timely Payment of Property and Rental Income Taxes
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) has reminded taxpayers to pay their property tax and rental income tax for 2026 before the January 31 deadline. The notice affects business owners and rental property owners, who must declare and pay taxes for the prev
body_en:
Kigali, January 27, 2026 — The Rwanda Revenue Authority (RRA) has reminded taxpayers to pay their property tax and rental income tax for 2026 before the January 31 deadline. The notice affects business owners and rental property owners, who must declare and pay taxes for the previous year.
Deputy Commissioner for Provinces and Local Government Taxes, Karasira Ernest, urged taxpayers to act early to avoid system delays and other obstacles, stating:
“We encourage those concerned to hurry up and declare and pay early. You can declare and pay later, but do not wait until the last day because it creates various obstacles.”
Property Tax (Patent Tax)
Applies to anyone starting a business, already in business, or operating a small or medium enterprise after a two-year exemption.
Taxpayers can pay annually or in installments. Annual payments are due by January 31, 2026. Installments are due:
1st installment: January 31
2nd installment: April 30
3rd installment: July 31
4th installment: October 31
Declarations can be completed via the RRA website or by dialling 800# on a mobile phone.
Rental Income Tax
Applies to individuals and companies owning rental properties in Rwanda.
Income includes rents from fully or partially rented houses, related activities, and interest from rental properties.
Deductions include 50% of maintenance costs and interest on bank loans.
Tax rates:
0% for annual rental income Rwf 1–180,000
20% for Rwf 180,001–1,000,000
30% for above Rwf 1,000,000
Karasira reminded all affected taxpayers to register rental properties with RRA and complete payments early to comply with the law.
Social and Health

title: Nangaa Warns DRC Forces Against Violence in Uvira
excerpt: Uvira, January 28, 2026 — AFC/M23 leader Corneille Nangaa has warned the DRC government-backed military alliance that if violence continues in Uvira, his fighters will take responsibility for protecting civilians. Nangaa said that AFC/M23 voluntarily withdrew from Uvira at the re
title_en: Nangaa Warns DRC Forces Against Violence in Uvira
excerpt_en: Uvira, January 28, 2026 — AFC/M23 leader Corneille Nangaa has warned the DRC government-backed military alliance that if violence continues in Uvira, his fighters will take responsibility for protecting civilians. Nangaa said that AFC/M23 voluntarily withdrew from Uvira at the re
body_en:
Uvira, January 28, 2026 — AFC/M23 leader Corneille Nangaa has warned the DRC government-backed military alliance that if violence continues in Uvira, his fighters will take responsibility for protecting civilians.
Nangaa said that AFC/M23 voluntarily withdrew from Uvira at the request of the United States to allow peace talks to continue. He noted that similar withdrawals had previously occurred in Bunagana, Masisi, and Walikale.
“This is not the first time we have done this… In Walikale, we left so that the Doha talks could take place. Now, too, we have been asked to leave Uvira,” he said.
Before leaving the city, Nangaa warned the international community that civilians could be killed, accused of collaborating with AFC/M23, and that Banyamulenge communities in South Kivu Province could be targeted. He said that requests for neutral forces to protect civilians were not respected.
He added that following their withdrawal, there were lootings, extrajudicial killings, arbitrary arrests, and targeted attacks, particularly against the Banyamulenge, with about 900 families displaced to areas such as Luvungi, Sange, and especially Kamanyola.
Nangaa stated that AFC/M23 had learned it could reclaim territory quickly if necessary. He accused DRC soldiers of criminal behavior and warned: “If they continue, we will take responsibility for rescuing the population.”
This warning comes amid discussions in Kinshasa about launching a rapid campaign to retake areas controlled by AFC/M23, after government forces cleared the group from Uvira on January 17, 2026.

Nangaa stated that AFC/M23 had learned it could reclaim territory quickly if necessary. He accused DRC soldiers of criminal behavior and warned: “If they continue, we will take responsibility for rescuing the population.”
This warning comes amid discussions in Kinshasa about launching a rapid campaign to retake areas controlled by AFC/M23, after government forces cleared the group from Uvira on January 17, 2026.

title: MONUSCO Requested to Deploy Troops to Uvira After Qatar Talks

title_en: MONUSCO Requested to Deploy Troops to Uvira After Qatar Talks
excerpt_en: Uvira DRC February 3, 2026 — At a meeting held in Qatar, participants requested that MONUSCO (UN peacekeeping mission in the DRC) deploy troops to the city of Uvira, the Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced. The request was made at the conclusion of a meeting monitoring t
body_en:
Uvira DRC February 3, 2026 — At a meeting held in Qatar, participants requested that MONUSCO (UN peacekeeping mission in the DRC) deploy troops to the city of Uvira, the Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs announced.
The request was made at the conclusion of a meeting monitoring the implementation of the ceasefire between the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) and the AFC/M23 alliance, under the Ceasefire Oversight and Verification Mechanism facilitated by Qatar.
The meeting brought together both parties as part of ongoing efforts to resolve the conflict in eastern DRC.
It was also announced that the DRC government and AFC/M23 signed a document outlining broad guidelines on the issues to be discussed and the modalities for negotiations, approved by the International Conference on the Great Lakes Region (ICGLR).
In a statement issued on the night of February 2, 2026, Qatar’s Foreign Ministry said both sides renewed their commitment to the ceasefire and the principles signed on November 15, 2025, in Doha.
“Both sides confirmed their commitment to implementing all agreed conditions in support of the peace agreement,” the ministry stated.
The meeting was attended by representatives of the United States, the African Union (AU) as observers, and Togo as the AU-appointed mediator, alongside officials from MONUSCO and the ICGLR.
Participants reviewed the security situation in the DRC and the ongoing challenges to peace, stressing the need for concrete measures to improve monitoring and information-sharing.
MONUSCO and ICGLR strategies for ceasefire monitoring were also examined, with participants reaffirming their support for both institutions.
MONUSCO was specifically asked to deploy troops to Uvira to monitor compliance with the ceasefire and to establish communication channels to ensure the effectiveness of monitoring operations.
On December 10, AFC/M23 announced it had captured Uvira in South Kivu. However, the group’s last fighters were reportedly killed in the city on January 17, 2026.
AFC/M23 stated that it withdrew from Uvira at the request of the international community, emphasizing that its priority is peace, unlike what it describes as the DRC government’s preference for renewed conflict.

title: CENI Releases Electoral Calendar for Governor and Vice-Governor Elections in Sankuru
excerpt: The Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI) has published the electoral calendar for the election of the governor and vice-governor of Sankuru province, on Thursday, January 29. The schedule outlines all stages of the process, from technical preparations to the announcem
title_en: CENI Releases Electoral Calendar for Governor and Vice-Governor Elections in Sankuru
excerpt_en: The Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI) has published the electoral calendar for the election of the governor and vice-governor of Sankuru province, on Thursday, January 29. The schedule outlines all stages of the process, from technical preparations to the announcem
body_en:
The Independent National Electoral Commission (CENI) has published the electoral calendar for the election of the governor and vice-governor of Sankuru province, on Thursday, January 29.
The schedule outlines all stages of the process, from technical preparations to the announcement of provisional results.
Key Stages of the Electoral Process
The timeline runs from January 28 to March 24:
January 28 – February 3: Technical preparations, staff training, and establishment of the Candidate Reception and Processing Office (BRTC)
February 4 – 10: Submission of candidacies to the Provincial Executive Secretariat in Lusambo
February 19: Publication of the provisional list of candidates
March 2 – 6: Filing of appeals with the Sankuru Court of Appeal
March 9: Publication of the final list
March 20 – 22: Election campaign
March 24: Voting by provincial deputies
March 24: Proclamation of provisional results by the Plenary Assembly
This election is being held in a sensitive political context. The outgoing governor, Victor Kitenge, was removed from office on May 26 by the Provincial Assembly, which accused him of mismanagement, particularly regarding security, and of refusing to respond to parliamentary summons.
