title: The Beni Health Zone Receives Medication for Malnutrition and Malaria
excerpt: The Beni health zone in North Kivu received a significant donation of medication for malnutrition and malaria on Saturday, January 24, provided by the central government through the Ministry of Public Health. This donation aims to strengthen healthcare services in a region severe
title_en: The Beni Health Zone Receives Medication for Malnutrition and Malaria
excerpt_en: The Beni health zone in North Kivu received a significant donation of medication for malnutrition and malaria on Saturday, January 24, provided by the central government through the Ministry of Public Health. This donation aims to strengthen healthcare services in a region severe
body_en:
The Beni health zone in North Kivu received a significant donation of medication for malnutrition and malaria on Saturday, January 24, provided by the central government through the Ministry of Public Health. This donation aims to strengthen healthcare services in a region severely affected by these endemic diseases, worsened by armed conflict, according to regional authorities.
Local health officials welcomed this aid as the result of repeated advocacy efforts, following a rise in cases and deaths linked to malaria and malnutrition.
The zone’s chief medical officer, Dr. Kasereka Tosalisana Michel, thanked the national and provincial authorities for their swift response to a scourge devastating the population.
“We thank the central and provincial governments for this crucial step in the fight against malaria, in addition to the horrors of war,” said Dr. Kasereka.
Prisca Kamala Luanda, the provincial health coordinator, added:
“This endemic area has recorded numerous cases and deaths; the government has heard the population’s cries for help.”
The handover ceremony took place at the Beni health zone office, in the presence of provincial authorities and health partners, signaling hope for a significant decrease in cases in the coming weeks.

title: FARDC Denounces Alleged Stratagems of Rwandan Army and AFC/M23 After Withdrawal from Uvira
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 24, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have accused the Rwandan army and its allies in the AFC/M23 coalition of employing “stratagems” aimed at perpetuating insecurity and chaos in eastern DRC, following their recent withdrawal f
title_en: FARDC Denounces Alleged Stratagems of Rwandan Army and AFC/M23 After Withdrawal from Uvira
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 24, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have accused the Rwandan army and its allies in the AFC/M23 coalition of employing “stratagems” aimed at perpetuating insecurity and chaos in eastern DRC, following their recent withdrawal f
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 24, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have accused the Rwandan army and its allies in the AFC/M23 coalition of employing “stratagems” aimed at perpetuating insecurity and chaos in eastern DRC, following their recent withdrawal from Uvira, in South Kivu province.
In a statement released on Friday, January 23, the FARDC said these maneuvers were observed immediately after the armed groups pulled out of the city. According to the army, on the eve of their departure, the Rwandan forces and AFC/M23 rebels allegedly systematically looted Uvira, leaving the city “at the mercy of well-organized gangs of looters.”
The FARDC reported that the destruction and theft targeted key state and private infrastructure, including road rehabilitation equipment and state-owned vehicles.
The statement further claims that these operations were planned during a meeting on January 17, 2026, in Uvira, involving representatives of the Rwandan army, AFC/M23, and their allies Twiraného and Red Tabara.
The Congolese army also rejected allegations of abuses committed by its forces against certain communities, describing them as “a blatant lie fabricated within the Rwandan army.” The FARDC said it had deployed security and protection measures for all communities, including the Banyamulenge, whom it said had “refused to be manipulated” by armed groups.
This stance echoes remarks by the mayor of Uvira, who acknowledged the complexity of the security situation in the city. The mayor said that “there were imposters posing as FARDC and imposters posing as Wazalendo who harassed the population,” adding that these individuals, after returning from the city, “learned their lesson and will certainly change.”
The mayor further stressed that “not all the incidents that occurred can be attributed to the regular forces, who act in accordance with human rights and the protection of civilians.”
In its statement, the FARDC reaffirmed that it would “not tolerate any act of genocide planned or carried out on Congolese soil” and reiterated its “firm determination to defend the integrity of the national territory and to protect all communities and their property, even unto the ultimate sacrifice.”
Following the withdrawal of the rebels, local authorities returned to Uvira and pledged to prepare for the return of Congolese refugees who had fled to Burundi during the fighting.

title: Mobondo Militiamen Surrender Weapons as Government Urges Return of Displaced Persons
excerpt: Kwamouth, January 27, 2026 — In a significant step toward peace in the Kwamouth territory, several Mobondo militiamen have surrendered their weapons in villages such as Etumba na Ngwaka, following a government-led peacekeeping mission. The weapons were handed over to the Armed Fo
title_en: Mobondo Militiamen Surrender Weapons as Government Urges Return of Displaced Persons
excerpt_en: Kwamouth, January 27, 2026 — In a significant step toward peace in the Kwamouth territory, several Mobondo militiamen have surrendered their weapons in villages such as Etumba na Ngwaka, following a government-led peacekeeping mission. The weapons were handed over to the Armed Fo
body_en:
Kwamouth, January 27, 2026 — In a significant step toward peace in the Kwamouth territory, several Mobondo militiamen have surrendered their weapons in villages such as Etumba na Ngwaka, following a government-led peacekeeping mission.
The weapons were handed over to the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) in the presence of Minister Delegate for Defense in charge of Veterans, Eliezer Ntambwe, who has been leading the mission for a week. While local reports suggest about 100 weapons have been surrendered, the minister indicated that the final tally will be submitted to Kinshasa at the conclusion of the mission.
Some leaders of the Mobondo militia, along with their traditional healers, have also joined the peace process, signaling a broader willingness among the movement’s members to reintegrate into civilian life.
Minister Ntambwe highlighted that the Mobondo phenomenon has evolved beyond its original ethnic conflict roots between the Teke and Yaka communities, becoming increasingly associated with livestock raiding and other criminal activities. “Those who started this Mobondo story are already with us, including their traditional healers. This proves there is a will to leave this movement,” Ntambwe stated.
The minister conveyed a message from the President of the Republic, encouraging former combatants to resume normal lives and leave the movement, which had drawn in many participants, including some innocent civilians seeking protection.
Ntambwe also urged displaced populations to return to their villages, assuring them that security measures have been deployed by the 11th and 14th Military Regions and the Republican Guard to protect civilians and their property.
“This peacekeeping mission primarily aims to facilitate the surrender of Mobondo militiamen in this part of the country,” the minister explained. He emphasized that insecurity in the region has hindered the implementation of several government programs, underscoring the broader importance of stabilizing Kwamouth.
The surrender of weapons and the ongoing reintegration efforts mark a critical step toward restoring security and normalcy in the affected communities, while allowing the government to implement development and social programs more effectively.

title: Faure Gnassingbé Travels to Kigali to Meet with Paul Kagame
excerpt: Kigali Rwanda, January 30, 2026 — Rwandan President Paul Kagame received Togolese Prime Minister Faure Gnassingbé, the African Union (AU) chief mediator for the peace process in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in Urugwiro Village, as part of ongoing diplomatic consult
title_en: Faure Gnassingbé Travels to Kigali to Meet with Paul Kagame
excerpt_en: Kigali Rwanda, January 30, 2026 — Rwandan President Paul Kagame received Togolese Prime Minister Faure Gnassingbé, the African Union (AU) chief mediator for the peace process in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in Urugwiro Village, as part of ongoing diplomatic consult
body_en:
Kigali Rwanda, January 30, 2026 — Rwandan President Paul Kagame received Togolese Prime Minister Faure Gnassingbé, the African Union (AU) chief mediator for the peace process in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), in Urugwiro Village, as part of ongoing diplomatic consultations on the Great Lakes crisis.
The two heads of state held a private meeting before a broader session with the AU Panel of Facilitators, which includes former African heads of state: Olusegun Obasanjo (Nigeria), Sahle-Work Zewde (Ethiopia), Mokgweetsi Masisi (Botswana), and Catherine Samba-Panza (Central African Republic).
The discussions focused on the security situation in eastern DRC, the progress of ongoing diplomatic initiatives, and ways to strengthen coordination between regional and continental mediation efforts to promote peace, security, and stability in the Great Lakes region.
“I thank President Paul Kagame for the quality of the discussions held today in Kigali. Our discussions focused primarily on the challenges of peace and stability in the Great Lakes region, particularly in eastern DRC, as well as on strengthening bilateral cooperation,” said Faure Gnassingbé.

title: FARDC Repels AFC/M23 Rebel Attack in Kalinga
excerpt: Walikale February 3, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by the Wazalendo, successfully repelled an attack by AFC/M23 rebels in Kalinga, Banamulema (Kisimba group), Walikale territory, North Kivu, on the morning of Tuesday, February 3. A
title_en: FARDC Repels AFC/M23 Rebel Attack in Kalinga
excerpt_en: Walikale February 3, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by the Wazalendo, successfully repelled an attack by AFC/M23 rebels in Kalinga, Banamulema (Kisimba group), Walikale territory, North Kivu, on the morning of Tuesday, February 3. A
body_en:
Walikale February 3, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), supported by the Wazalendo, successfully repelled an attack by AFC/M23 rebels in Kalinga, Banamulema (Kisimba group), Walikale territory, North Kivu, on the morning of Tuesday, February 3.
According to the administrative secretary of the Kisimba group, the attackers came from Mpety, considered one of the rebels’ main strongholds, aiming to expand their influence by seizing new positions.
The FARDC, aided by Wazalendo groups, resisted the assault, forcing the rebels to retreat towards Mpombi, in the Balinda area.
In retaliation, the rebels launched bombings in Kalinga, causing panic among civilians and prompting many residents to flee for safety.
Security sources confirm that Kalinga remains under the control of the FARDC and Wazalendo, though the situation remains tense in the combat zone.

excerpt_en: Ituri February 7, 2026 – Irumu Territory, Ituri – The security situation in Walese Vonkutu chiefdom remains dire as six civilians were killed in recent attacks attributed to Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) rebels in the village of Pakanza, south of Irumu territory. Local youth fro
body_en:
Ituri February 7, 2026 – Irumu Territory, Ituri – The security situation in Walese Vonkutu chiefdom remains dire as six civilians were killed in recent attacks attributed to Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) rebels in the village of Pakanza, south of Irumu territory.
Local youth from the Bandavilemba group mobilized on Friday to search for missing civilians and discovered the bodies in an advanced state of decomposition.
According to Piscasse Vahingania, first vice-president of the Bwanasura local youth council:
Two of the bodies were recovered and transported to Eringeti for proper burial.
Four bodies were buried on site where they were found.
Mr. Vahingania urged young people to continue cooperating with security forces to help prevent further attacks. He also called on local authorities to strengthen civilian protection and safeguard property, while encouraging the community to maintain hope despite ongoing fear and uncertainty.
The Walese Vonkutu chiefdom continues to be heavily affected by ADF activity, with local communities demanding stronger government action to restore state authority and protect civilians in this part of Ituri.

title_en: Rwanda Announces 20th National Dialogue Conference for February 2026
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 28, 2026 — The Government of Rwanda has announced that the 20th National Dialogue Conference will be held on February 5–6, 2026, according to decisions from a Cabinet meeting chaired by President Paul Kagame on January 28. The Cabinet confirmed it had been briefed
body_en:
Kigali, January 28, 2026 — The Government of Rwanda has announced that the 20th National Dialogue Conference will be held on February 5–6, 2026, according to decisions from a Cabinet meeting chaired by President Paul Kagame on January 28.
The Cabinet confirmed it had been briefed on preparations for the event, which serves as a national platform bringing together Rwandans at home and abroad to discuss the country’s development, assess progress in improving citizens’ well-being, and hold leaders accountable for their actions.
The conference focuses on evaluating national performance, identifying challenges across key sectors, and shaping policies aimed at sustainable development.
The last National Dialogue Conference was held on January 23–24, 2024, and was inaugurated by President Kagame. It drew participants from across the country and the diaspora, with gatherings in locations such as Kigali, Gatsibo, Rutsiro, Burera, Nyanza, and Poland.
At that time, President Kagame reaffirmed that Rwanda was secure and called on citizens—especially the youth—to take the lead in advancing national development. He emphasized that Rwanda’s future must be shaped first and foremost by Rwandans themselves, urging unity, responsibility, and self-reflection as the foundation of national progress.

title_en: New Economic Partnership Signed
excerpt_en: Rwanda-Brazil, 4 February 2026 – Rwanda and Brazil have formalized a strategic partnership to boost trade, investment, and sectoral cooperation. The agreement was signed during the ‘Rwanda-Brazil Economic Cooperation Forum’. Rwanda was represented by Jean-Guy Afrika, Director Gen
body_en:
Rwanda-Brazil, 4 February 2026 – Rwanda and Brazil have formalized a strategic partnership to boost trade, investment, and sectoral cooperation. The agreement was signed during the ‘Rwanda-Brazil Economic Cooperation Forum’.
Rwanda was represented by Jean-Guy Afrika, Director General of the National Development Board (RDB), while Brazil was represented by Jorge Viana of its Export Promotion Agency (APEX-Brazil).
The deal sets a clear framework for trade promotion, investment facilitation, trade-related travel, and sectoral collaboration. Additionally, APEX-Brazil signed a cooperation agreement with the Rwanda Private Sector Federation, led by Stephen Ruzibiza, to further strengthen private sector engagement.
Jean-Guy Afrika highlighted the complementary strengths of the two nations: Brazil with its leadership in agriculture, industry, and energy, and Rwanda offering a safe investment environment and strategic access to East and Central African markets.
Brazilian Ambassador Irene Vida Gala encouraged Brazilian investors to explore opportunities in Rwanda, calling the agreement a major step in bilateral cooperation.
Rwanda-Brazil relations date back to 1981, with agreements on air services (2019) and food security (2011). Since 2022, Rwanda has imported wheat and sugar from Brazil, replacing some imports from Ukraine.
The partnership aims to expand trade and investment while reinforcing the private sector and sustainable economic growth in both countries.

title: Morocco Moves to Ratify Air Transport Agreement with Rwanda
excerpt: Rabat, January 30, 2026 — Morocco has taken a key step toward ratifying the air transport agreement it signed with Rwanda on September 25, 2025, following a review by the Moroccan Cabinet on January 29, 2026. The agreement was originally signed during the International Civil Avia
title_en: Morocco Moves to Ratify Air Transport Agreement with Rwanda
excerpt_en: Rabat, January 30, 2026 — Morocco has taken a key step toward ratifying the air transport agreement it signed with Rwanda on September 25, 2025, following a review by the Moroccan Cabinet on January 29, 2026. The agreement was originally signed during the International Civil Avia
body_en:
Rabat, January 30, 2026 — Morocco has taken a key step toward ratifying the air transport agreement it signed with Rwanda on September 25, 2025, following a review by the Moroccan Cabinet on January 29, 2026. The agreement was originally signed during the International Civil Aviation Organization (ICAO) session in Montreal, Canada, with Rwandan Ambassador Higiro Prosper representing Rwanda and Moroccan Transport Minister Abdessamad Kayouh signing on behalf of Morocco.
The cabinet review is part of the administrative process preceding final approval, which will be followed by implementation. Minister Kayouh presented draft law No. 67.25, aimed at securing parliamentary approval for the agreement.
The accord seeks to strengthen cooperation in civil aviation between the two countries. Minister Kayouh emphasized that Morocco aims to double passenger traffic from 40 million to 80 million by 2030.
Ambassador Higiro Prosper described the agreement as a significant milestone, highlighting its potential to expand RwandAir operations and accelerate the development of Kigali International Airport in Bugesera District, which will have a capacity of over 14 million passengers annually.
Currently, RwandAir operates flights to 30 destinations across 22 countries in Africa, Europe, the Middle East, and Asia, and the agreement is expected to further enhance the airline’s connectivity and growth prospects.

title: Ugandan Troops May End 19-Year Peacekeeping Mission in Somalia
excerpt: Kampala, January 27, 2026 — Uganda’s military is considering ending its 19-year peacekeeping mission in Somalia, according to Maj Gen Felix Kulayigye, spokesperson for the Ugandan Armed Forces. The announcement follows remarks by Chief of Staff Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who said:
title_en: Ugandan Troops May End 19-Year Peacekeeping Mission in Somalia
excerpt_en: Kampala, January 27, 2026 — Uganda’s military is considering ending its 19-year peacekeeping mission in Somalia, according to Maj Gen Felix Kulayigye, spokesperson for the Ugandan Armed Forces. The announcement follows remarks by Chief of Staff Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who said:
body_en:
Kampala, January 27, 2026 — Uganda’s military is considering ending its 19-year peacekeeping mission in Somalia, according to Maj Gen Felix Kulayigye, spokesperson for the Ugandan Armed Forces.
The announcement follows remarks by Chief of Staff Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba, who said:
"After 19 years in Somalia, very soon we plan to leave the country completely."
Maj Gen Kulayigye highlighted Uganda’s contributions since its deployment in 2007, emphasizing efforts to facilitate dialogue among Somali factions and reduce ongoing fighting. He explained that peace talks previously held abroad in countries such as Kenya, Ethiopia, and Egypt had failed, but Uganda helped organize successful talks on Somali soil, fostering local ownership of the peace process.
He also noted Uganda’s role in supporting Somali elections, ensuring leadership transitions were conducted peacefully rather than through violence. Since 2006, Somalia has held four elections under Uganda’s facilitation.
Despite Uganda’s efforts, Al-Shabaab continues to carry out terrorist attacks, indicating that the security situation remains fragile even as Uganda evaluates the conclusion of its long-term mission.
This potential withdrawal marks a significant shift in the Horn of Africa’s security landscape, as Ugandan forces have been a central component of stabilizing Somalia for nearly two decades.

excerpt_en: Minembwe, DRC — February 2, 2026 — The armed group MRDP-Twirwaneho has accused the Congolese army (FARDC) of conducting intensive drone operations over Minembwe, claiming that more than 18 military drones were deployed in the area over a three-day period. According to Colonel Kam
body_en:
Minembwe, DRC — February 2, 2026 — The armed group MRDP-Twirwaneho has accused the Congolese army (FARDC) of conducting intensive drone operations over Minembwe, claiming that more than 18 military drones were deployed in the area over a three-day period.
According to Colonel Kamasa Ndakize Welcome, spokesperson for Twirwaneho, the drone flights occurred between January 30 and February 1, 2026, and allegedly resulted in the deaths of numerous civilians, as well as the destruction of civilian infrastructure, including homes, hospitals, and churches.
“These attacks were carried out in densely populated areas, particularly in the Minembwe center, where many people had sought refuge after fleeing earlier violence involving a coalition of forces including the DRC army, Burundi, Wazalendo militias, and the FDLR,” Kamasa said.
He further claimed that the air operations intensified in January 2026, following the withdrawal of AFC forces from Uvira, and alleged that the campaign forms part of a broader strategy by the Kinshasa government to target the Banyamulenge community.
MRDP-Twirwaneho stated that it remains ready to resist what it described as actions aimed at the extermination of civilians by government forces.

title: Maxime Prévot Sounds the Alarm: “A Woman Is Raped Every 4 Minutes, a Child Every 30 Minutes in Eastern DRC”
excerpt: The Belgian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Maxime Prévot, raised alarm on Friday, January 31, following the European Union Foreign Affairs Council meeting, over the security and humanitarian crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Describing the si
title_en: Maxime Prévot Sounds the Alarm: “A Woman Is Raped Every 4 Minutes, a Child Every 30 Minutes in Eastern DRC”
excerpt_en: The Belgian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Maxime Prévot, raised alarm on Friday, January 31, following the European Union Foreign Affairs Council meeting, over the security and humanitarian crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. Describing the si
body_en:
The Belgian Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of Foreign Affairs, Maxime Prévot, raised alarm on Friday, January 31, following the European Union Foreign Affairs Council meeting, over the security and humanitarian crisis in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
Describing the situation as a “forgotten conflict,” the Belgian minister highlighted the scale of sexual violence, stating that “a woman is raped every four minutes and a child every 30 minutes in eastern DRC.”
Faced with this emergency, Maxime Prévot called for stronger and more immediate EU action.
“On the ground, the situation is worse than ever, extremely worrying from a humanitarian perspective. This is one of the reasons why, along with other colleagues, we insisted that this issue be placed on the agenda. I am also surprised that this is only the second time in a year that the situation in eastern Congo has been examined. This cannot be a forgotten conflict: the European Union has a role to play,” he said.
He stressed the need to continue political mediation toward a genuine ceasefire and lasting peace, while calling for the withdrawal of M23 and Rwandan troops and respect for the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the DRC.
However, he emphasized that the humanitarian emergency remains the top priority.
“A woman is raped every four minutes, a child every thirty minutes.” He therefore urged a rapid and effective European response, particularly through the reactivation of Goma airport to enable the large-scale delivery of humanitarian aid, insisting that “there is absolutely no question of military use of this airport.”

title_en: Manono Lithium Employees Demand Government-Set Minimum Wage
excerpt_en: Manono – February 8, 2026 – Employees of COLINGO, a subcontractor of Manono Lithium, staged a demonstration on Friday, February 6, demanding the implementation of the government-mandated minimum wage of 21,500 FC per day, instead of the 13,500 FC they currently receive. A COLINGO
body_en:
Manono – February 8, 2026 – Employees of COLINGO, a subcontractor of Manono Lithium, staged a demonstration on Friday, February 6, demanding the implementation of the government-mandated minimum wage of 21,500 FC per day, instead of the 13,500 FC they currently receive.
A COLINGO supervisor explained the background of the dispute:
“We had agreed with our supervisor that he would start paying us 13,500 FC per day. There was also the issue of work uniforms that needed to be resolved: we had to buy the uniforms and vests for 48,000 FC, and that was done.”
The supervisor, who has been working with the company for six months, highlighted the challenges faced by employees in securing fair wages and proper work conditions.

title: FARDC Repels AFC/M23 Attack on Strategic Nkobe Hill Near Pinga
excerpt: Walikale, North Kivu – January 24, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have successfully repelled a renewed AFC/M23 rebel attack on Nkobe Hill, a strategic position overlooking the town of Pinga in Walikale territory. According to the administrativ
title_en: FARDC Repels AFC/M23 Attack on Strategic Nkobe Hill Near Pinga
excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu – January 24, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have successfully repelled a renewed AFC/M23 rebel attack on Nkobe Hill, a strategic position overlooking the town of Pinga in Walikale territory. According to the administrativ
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu – January 24, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have successfully repelled a renewed AFC/M23 rebel attack on Nkobe Hill, a strategic position overlooking the town of Pinga in Walikale territory.
According to the administrative secretary of the Kisimba group, the rebels have launched repeated attempts in recent days to breach security defenses and penetrate Pinga, but without success. On Friday, January 23, AFC/M23 fighters reportedly tried to outflank positions held by the FARDC and the Volunteers for the Defense of the Homeland (VDP) at Nkobe Hill, which overlooks the village of Munsanga.
The assault was met with a strong response from loyalist forces, forcing the attackers to retreat toward Buhaya, near Mpety, in the Banakindi area, considered the rebels’ main stronghold in the Pinga region.
A fragile calm was observed on Saturday, with Nkobe Hill remaining firmly under the control of the FARDC.
The human and material toll of the clashes was not immediately available at the time of publication.

title: Great Lakes Crisis Returns to EU Foreign Ministers’ Agenda
excerpt: Brussels, January 27, 2026 — The ongoing crisis in the Great Lakes region is back at the center of attention for the European Union (EU), as a meeting of EU foreign ministers is scheduled for Thursday, January 29, 2026, in Brussels with the security and humanitarian situation in
title_en: Great Lakes Crisis Returns to EU Foreign Ministers’ Agenda
excerpt_en: Brussels, January 27, 2026 — The ongoing crisis in the Great Lakes region is back at the center of attention for the European Union (EU), as a meeting of EU foreign ministers is scheduled for Thursday, January 29, 2026, in Brussels with the security and humanitarian situation in
body_en:
Brussels, January 27, 2026 — The ongoing crisis in the Great Lakes region is back at the center of attention for the European Union (EU), as a meeting of EU foreign ministers is scheduled for Thursday, January 29, 2026, in Brussels with the security and humanitarian situation in the region as the main agenda item.
The announcement comes amid the first anniversary of Goma’s occupation by the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 rebellion and follows recent interventions by the United States and Qatar to mediate the crisis between Kinshasa and Kigali and between the Congolese government and the AFC/M23.
The EU Special Representative for the Great Lakes Region, Johan Borgstam, met with Prime Minister Judith Suminwa in Kinshasa on Monday, January 26, 2026, to discuss priorities ahead of the Brussels meeting. Borgstam emphasized the EU’s commitment to the DRC and stressed the importance of understanding the humanitarian and security needs on the ground.
“This visit allows the Prime Minister to convey relevant messages to the European ministers on January 29. It’s about demonstrating the EU as a supportive, reliable, and predictable partner for the DRC,” Borgstam said.
The EU is currently the largest humanitarian partner in the Great Lakes region, financing programs for agencies such as UNHCR and WFP, and supporting refugee camps, including the Busuma camp in Burundi, which hosts 68,000 Congolese refugees. Borgstam highlighted recent deliveries of 73 tons of humanitarian supplies, reflecting the EU’s concrete support for displaced populations.
In addition to humanitarian assistance, the EU has played a significant role in sanctions against individuals linked to the Rwandan Defence Force (RDF) and the M23 rebellion, following the occupation of Goma and Bukavu. Among those sanctioned are:
Ruki Karusisi, commander of the RDF special forces in eastern DRC
Eugène Nkubito, commander of RDF’s 3rd Division deployed in North Kivu
Brigadier General Pascal Muhizi, commander of RDF’s 2nd Division
Bertrand Bisimwa, president of M23
Désiré Rukomera, responsible for recruitment and propaganda
John Imani Nzenze, M23 colonel
Jean-Bosco Nzabonimpa Mupenzi, deputy finance chief of M23
Jean Bahati Musanga, former finance head and current governor of the rebellion’s administration in Goma
Borgstam warned that, despite diplomatic processes such as the US-led Washington process and Qatar’s Doha talks, the situation on the ground remains tense. Violence continues to escalate, and mutual accusations of non-compliance with agreements persist between the DRC, Rwanda, and the AFC/M23.
The upcoming EU foreign ministers’ meeting will serve as an opportunity to reassess the Great Lakes crisis, reaffirm support for humanitarian operations, and maintain international pressure on parties involved to respect commitments and restore peace and stability in the region.

Uvira Territory — January 30, 2026 — An explosion killed three people and injured around ten others on Thursday, January 29, at a market in Sange, located in the Ruzizi Plain of South Kivu.
The blast occurred in the early evening, according to local and humanitarian sources. The injured were evacuated to Sange General Hospital for treatment, while the bodies of the deceased were recovered by their families.
The cause of the explosion has not yet been officially established.
Sange is considered a fallback area for AFC/M23 fighters following their withdrawal from the lakeside city of Uvira, adding to ongoing security concerns in the Ruzizi Plain.

title_en: New Clashes Between AFC/M23 and Wazalendo in Bukumbirwa (Walikale)
excerpt_en: Bukumbirwa February 3, 2026 — Violent clashes erupted early Tuesday morning, February 3, between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo from the NDC-Rénové group in Bukumbirwa, located in the Ikobo area of Walikale territory, North Kivu. The Wazalendo launched an attack on AFC/M23 position
body_en:
Bukumbirwa February 3, 2026 — Violent clashes erupted early Tuesday morning, February 3, between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo from the NDC-Rénové group in Bukumbirwa, located in the Ikobo area of Walikale territory, North Kivu.
The Wazalendo launched an attack on AFC/M23 positions around 4:00 a.m., causing widespread panic among residents.
The sounds of heavy and light weapons fire continued for several hours, forcing locals to remain indoors.
After approximately three hours of fighting, the Wazalendo retreated into the bush, leaving Bukumbirwa under rebel control. The toll from these clashes is not yet known.
Socio-economic activities have tentatively resumed, according to local sources. Several witnesses report a strengthening of AFC/M23 positions in Bukumbirwa and Rusamambu, with reinforcements from Buleusa reportedly arriving in these towns on Tuesday morning.

title_en: Woman Raped and Killed by FARDC Soldier, Perpetrator Arrested
excerpt_en: Lubero February 6, 2026 – North Kivu – A tragic and violent incident occurred in Tembe village, near Bamulumba in the Bapere sector, Lubero territory, where a woman was raped and killed on Thursday, February 4, by a soldier of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo
body_en:
Lubero February 6, 2026 – North Kivu – A tragic and violent incident occurred in Tembe village, near Bamulumba in the Bapere sector, Lubero territory, where a woman was raped and killed on Thursday, February 4, by a soldier of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC).
According to Samuel Kakule Kagheni, president of the Bapere sector civil society, the soldier raped the victim and then decapitated her with a machete while she was locked inside a hut. Shockingly, the act occurred in the presence of the victim’s children.
The administrator of Lubero territory, Colonel Kiwewa Mitela Alain, confirmed the events and stated that the soldier has been arrested and is currently held at the military prosecutor's office in Mangurejipa, pending trial by the competent military courts.
This incident is part of a series of abuses involving FARDC soldiers in the region since 2025. Previous cases include:
September 8, 2025: A soldier shot and killed his own wife in Kanyatsi.
September 10, 2025: Another FARDC soldier killed a civilian at point-blank range in the village of Lima, approximately six kilometers from Njiapanda, also in Lubero territory.
Authorities and local civil society actors continue to call for accountability and justice to prevent further abuses and restore confidence in security forces.

title: MPs Call for Pensioner Representation on RSSB Board
excerpt: Kigali, January 28, 2026 — Members of Parliament on the Social Affairs Committee have requested that pensioners be represented on the board of directors of the Rwanda National Social Security Board (RSSB). The request was reiterated on January 27, 2026, during discussions with Mi
title_en: MPs Call for Pensioner Representation on RSSB Board
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 28, 2026 — Members of Parliament on the Social Affairs Committee have requested that pensioners be represented on the board of directors of the Rwanda National Social Security Board (RSSB). The request was reiterated on January 27, 2026, during discussions with Mi
body_en:
Kigali, January 28, 2026 — Members of Parliament on the Social Affairs Committee have requested that pensioners be represented on the board of directors of the Rwanda National Social Security Board (RSSB). The request was reiterated on January 27, 2026, during discussions with Minister of Finance and Economic Planning, Yusuf Murangwa, on a report by the Auditor General reviewing RSSB’s performance over the past 10 years.
MP Yvonne Mujawabega emphasized that the board of directors of insurance institutions should include representatives for all stakeholders, including employees, employers, and the government, to ensure that the interests of members are reflected in investment and policy decisions. She raised concerns about past pension contribution increases, noting that some employees and employers were surprised by the changes and questioned how members’ voices are represented.
MP Mukabunani Christine noted that while RSSB invests to generate profits, there are times when projects may not be profitable. She questioned whether increased contributions translate into higher benefits for members, including medical care coverage and pension payouts, and whether these benefits keep pace with rising living costs.
Minister Yusuf Murangwa explained that the increase in contributions was necessary and had been delayed due to Covid-19 and rising prices. The decision had been under study for nearly eight years, and consultations were held prior to approval. He stressed that RSSB’s primary role is to manage members’ contributions efficiently and generate profits, with oversight from MINECOFIN.
On governance, Minister Murangwa acknowledged a gap and stated that the RSSB board should be reformed to include capable representatives of all members, including pensioners. “It is time to reform the RSSB Board of Directors… we hope that as the years go by, it will improve,” he said.
Murangwa also noted that RSSB is financially stable, contrary to some beliefs, and contributes significantly to the national economy, even supporting key development projects in the country.

title: Obasanjo Urges Root-Level Solutions to Congo Crisis
excerpt: Kinshasa DRC, 4 February 2026 – Olusegun Obasanjo, former Nigerian President and African Union mediator, has called for the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s (DRC) problems to be resolved from the roots up. Speaking after a meeting with Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni on 3 Feb
title_en: Obasanjo Urges Root-Level Solutions to Congo Crisis
excerpt_en: Kinshasa DRC, 4 February 2026 – Olusegun Obasanjo, former Nigerian President and African Union mediator, has called for the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s (DRC) problems to be resolved from the roots up. Speaking after a meeting with Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni on 3 Feb
body_en:
Kinshasa DRC, 4 February 2026 – Olusegun Obasanjo, former Nigerian President and African Union mediator, has called for the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s (DRC) problems to be resolved from the roots up.
Speaking after a meeting with Ugandan President Yoweri Museveni on 3 February 2026, Obasanjo emphasized that the ongoing crisis in the DRC stems from mismanagement of internal conflicts and tensions with neighboring countries.
Reflecting on his first visit to the Congo in 1960, during the Katanga independence struggle led by Moïse Tshombe, Obasanjo said, “The problem that led to the UN peacekeeping mission in Leopoldville in 1960 is still here today. Understanding the problem properly is the first step toward solving it.”
He stressed that previous attempts, particularly those led from Washington, failed because the root causes were not addressed, and that a comprehensive African-led approach is necessary. Obasanjo added that while international partners like Washington, Qatar, and France can contribute, the solution must be driven by Africans.
President Museveni noted that the current situation in the DRC is less severe than during Tshombe’s era, as there is no desire among Congolese provinces for independence. He called for leveraging the support of AU mediators to achieve lasting peace.

title: Rwanda and Pakistan Strengthen Trade Ties via Gwadar Port

title_en: Rwanda and Pakistan Strengthen Trade Ties via Gwadar Port
excerpt_en: Islamabad, January 30, 2026 — Rwanda and Pakistan have agreed to expand trade cooperation by using Gwadar Port as a gateway to export goods to African markets through maritime routes, following a bilateral meeting between Pakistan’s Minister for Shipping, Muhammad Junaid Anwar Ch
body_en:
Islamabad, January 30, 2026 — Rwanda and Pakistan have agreed to expand trade cooperation by using Gwadar Port as a gateway to export goods to African markets through maritime routes, following a bilateral meeting between Pakistan’s Minister for Shipping, Muhammad Junaid Anwar Chaudhry, and Rwanda’s Minister of Commerce and Industry, Prudence Sebahizi.
Officials said that Gwadar Port will enable Pakistan to export goods efficiently to East African countries, which collectively represent a market of approximately 500 million people. New maritime routes connecting Karachi to major African ports, including Djibouti and Mombasa, are expected to reduce trade costs by 30% and shorten delivery times.
The Karachi–Djibouti route is set to play a central role in operations, while the Karachi–Mombasa route will further integrate regional trade networks.
Under the agreement, Pakistan plans to use Gwadar Port to export goods to East Africa and import Rwandan products such as tea, coffee, avocados, and other agricultural and livestock products. Rwanda, in turn, imports medical supplies, rice, clothing materials, and agricultural technology from Pakistan.
Rwanda highlighted that expanding water transport routes will help overcome existing logistics bottlenecks by combining port access with regional land transport networks. The initiative is also expected to help Rwanda access South and Central Asian markets.
The agreement aligns with Pakistan’s economic and maritime development strategy, which positions Gwadar Port as a key hub to boost trade between South Asia and East Africa.

title: Rwanda Receives 15 FDLR Fighters and Their Families from DRC
excerpt: Rubavu, January 27, 2026 — The Government of Rwanda has received 15 FDLR fighters along with 19 family members from eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The fighters were initially temporarily housed by MONUSCO, the United Nations Mission in the DRC, which oversees the reh
title_en: Rwanda Receives 15 FDLR Fighters and Their Families from DRC
excerpt_en: Rubavu, January 27, 2026 — The Government of Rwanda has received 15 FDLR fighters along with 19 family members from eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The fighters were initially temporarily housed by MONUSCO, the United Nations Mission in the DRC, which oversees the reh
body_en:
Rubavu, January 27, 2026 — The Government of Rwanda has received 15 FDLR fighters along with 19 family members from eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). The fighters were initially temporarily housed by MONUSCO, the United Nations Mission in the DRC, which oversees the rehabilitation of former combatants.
The group crossed into Rwanda through Rubavu District on January 27, 2026. The fighters are scheduled to be transferred to the Rwandan Reintegration Commission (RDRC) facility in Mutobo, Musanze District, for reintegration programs.
Earlier in January, Rwanda received 13 FDLR fighters and six family members on January 20, followed by another 14 individuals, including eight fighters from the group’s special forces unit (CRAP), three days later.
MONUSCO reports that since the AFC/M23 coalition took control of Goma in January 2025, the number of FDLR fighters returning to Rwanda has increased, with nearly 300 having returned so far. The fighters are returning in small groups as Rwanda awaits the DRC army to launch operations to dismantle the terrorist group, as outlined in the peace agreement signed in Washington D.C. on June 27, 2025.
As of June 2025, the FDLR had an estimated 7,000–10,000 fighters, with most, including senior leaders, based in Walikale and Masisi Territories in North Kivu Province.

title: AFC/M23 Accuses DRC Government of Politicizing Rubaya Mining Tragedy
excerpt: February 2, 2026 — The AFC/M23 coalition has condemned the DRC government, accusing it of exploiting the deaths of more than 200 people in the Rubaya mining area for political purposes. The coalition said the tragedy, which occurred on January 28, 2026, was caused by landslides t
title_en: AFC/M23 Accuses DRC Government of Politicizing Rubaya Mining Tragedy
excerpt_en: February 2, 2026 — The AFC/M23 coalition has condemned the DRC government, accusing it of exploiting the deaths of more than 200 people in the Rubaya mining area for political purposes. The coalition said the tragedy, which occurred on January 28, 2026, was caused by landslides t
body_en:
February 2, 2026 — The AFC/M23 coalition has condemned the DRC government, accusing it of exploiting the deaths of more than 200 people in the Rubaya mining area for political purposes.
The coalition said the tragedy, which occurred on January 28, 2026, was caused by landslides triggered by heavy rains and unstable soil, not by issues related to territorial control. The victims reportedly included numerous miners.
On January 31, the DRC Ministry of Mineral Resources stated that most of the victims were engaged in illegal mining under AFC/M23 control. This claim was strongly rejected by the group.
AFC/M23 spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka criticized the government’s response, saying:“Instead of acknowledging the long-standing failure of the government to regulate the mining sector, it is trying to exploit the disaster caused by heavy rains in the Rubaya mines for political gain.”
The coalition emphasized that mining accidents have occurred repeatedly in areas under government control, citing more than 800 deaths across multiple sites over the years.
Among the examples cited were Nyamukubi and Bushushu in South Kivu, where more than 500 people died on May 4, 2023. AFC/M23 also recalled previous disasters, including:
37 deaths in Fizi in October 2018,
43 deaths at the KOV mine in Lualaba in June 2019, and
50 deaths near Kamituga, South Kivu, in September 2020 — all in areas under state control.
AFC/M23 concluded that the Rubaya tragedy reflects systemic failures in mining regulation, rather than the actions of any single group.

title_en: Félix Tshisekedi and AU Facilitators Discuss Peace Initiatives in the Great Lakes Region
excerpt_en: The President of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Félix Tshisekedi, met on Thursday, January 29, with the African Union’s panel of facilitators to discuss peace initiatives in the DRC and the wider Great Lakes region. According to the Presidency of the Republic, the Head of Stat
body_en:
The President of the Democratic Republic of Congo, Félix Tshisekedi, met on Thursday, January 29, with the African Union’s panel of facilitators to discuss peace initiatives in the DRC and the wider Great Lakes region.
According to the Presidency of the Republic, the Head of State commended the facilitators’ efforts and reaffirmed his commitment to a lasting and verifiable peace in eastern DRC.
He also reiterated his support for regional stability, in line with the commitments made by all parties.
For her part, Ms. Sahle-Work Zewde, former President of Ethiopia, stressed the urgency of action to end civilian suffering:
“We are on a tour. We will listen to everyone and see what can be done for the well-being of this population, which has suffered greatly for decades. We forget that behind all this, there is human suffering that must be stopped.”

body_en:
Lubumbashi, February 4, 2026 – The Ministry of Environment took decisive action against the CDM mining company on Wednesday, February 4, following a catastrophic acid water spill in November 2025. Environment Minister Marie Nyange ordered the suspension of operations, making any resumption contingent on a comprehensive environmental risk assessment.
Incident Spurs Expert Investigation The November 4th incident involved the overflow of an acid water discharge basin, severely polluting Lubumbashi’s environment. In response, the minister established a commission of national and international experts tasked with:
Analyzing technical and structural causes of the spill
Identifying shortcomings in toxic waste management
Proposing sustainable solutions to prevent recurrence and safeguard ecosystems
Compliance With Environmental Standards During a meeting with mining operators in Haut-Katanga, Minister Nyange underscored the government’s stance: industrial development must not compromise environmental standards.
“Our approach aims to establish mining operations that respect environmental standards and comply with the country’s international commitments. Pollution will no longer be tolerated,” Nyange emphasized.
Rising Pressure on Mining Sector This action reflects increasing pressure on the mining industry in Haut-Katanga province to assume its social and environmental responsibilities, especially in a region characterized by heavy industrial activity.

title: DRC Validates 2026 Roadmap for Recognition of Genocides
excerpt: Kinshasa, February 5, 2026 – The Congolese government officially validated on Thursday the 2026 Strategy Roadmap aimed at securing recognition of genocides committed on Congolese soil. The adoption of the roadmap followed a harmonization meeting between officials from the Nationa
title_en: DRC Validates 2026 Roadmap for Recognition of Genocides
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 5, 2026 – The Congolese government officially validated on Thursday the 2026 Strategy Roadmap aimed at securing recognition of genocides committed on Congolese soil. The adoption of the roadmap followed a harmonization meeting between officials from the Nationa
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 5, 2026 – The Congolese government officially validated on Thursday the 2026 Strategy Roadmap aimed at securing recognition of genocides committed on Congolese soil.
The adoption of the roadmap followed a harmonization meeting between officials from the National Fund for Victim Reparations (FONAREV) and the Inter-institutional Commission for Victim Assistance and Support for Reforms (CIA-VAR), chaired by Minister of Human Rights Samuel Mbemba.
During the session, Minister Mbemba and his counterparts outlined planned actions at both national and international levels, including the drafting of a preliminary bill for the preservation and protection of memorial heritage linked to international crimes in the DRC and the suppression of genocide denial.
The discussions also touched on the upcoming dialogue involving members of the Government, the National Assembly, the Senate, parliamentary committees, and the diplomatic corps accredited to the DRC.
Minister Mbemba emphasized that the initiative seeks effective recognition by states and international organizations of genocides committed in the DRC by Rwanda, noting that such recognition has already been acknowledged by the African Commission on Human and Peoples' Rights.

title: Kinshasa Urges UN to Fully Enforce Resolution 2773 Amid Persistent Rebel Occupations
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 27, 2026 — Nearly a year after the adoption of United Nations Security Council Resolution 2773, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is calling on the UN to fully assume its responsibilities in addressing the deteriorating security situation in the eastern pro
title_en: Kinshasa Urges UN to Fully Enforce Resolution 2773 Amid Persistent Rebel Occupations
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 27, 2026 — Nearly a year after the adoption of United Nations Security Council Resolution 2773, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is calling on the UN to fully assume its responsibilities in addressing the deteriorating security situation in the eastern pro
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 27, 2026 — Nearly a year after the adoption of United Nations Security Council Resolution 2773, the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is calling on the UN to fully assume its responsibilities in addressing the deteriorating security situation in the eastern provinces of the country.
The resolution, unanimously adopted in February 2025, condemned Rwanda for supporting the AFC/M23 rebellion and demanded the immediate withdrawal of its troops from Congolese territory. It also called on the AFC/M23 to cease hostilities in the DRC. Despite these mandates, the implementation of Resolution 2773 remains largely ineffective, and the eastern DRC continues to face intense insecurity, nearly a year after the occupation of Goma by the rebel movement.
During the 10096th session of the UN Security Council on Monday, January 26, 2026, Ambassador Jocelyne Kabengele Lukundula, Deputy Permanent Representative of the DRC to the UN, urged the Council to rigorously implement all resolutions and prioritize the promotion and strengthening of the rule of law. She stressed that this requires:
Full enforcement of adopted resolutions,
Increased support for fragile states,
Ensuring humanitarian operators have unimpeded access to provide assistance to civilians, and
Better coordination among UN bodies to strengthen collective peace efforts.
“Regional organizations, particularly African ones, play a critical role in peaceful dispute resolution and in reinforcing states’ legal and institutional capacities,” Ambassador Kabengele Lukundula said. “The DRC remains committed to multilateralism, law, and justice as guarantees of lasting and inclusive peace.”
On the ground, the security situation in North and South Kivu has worsened since the resolution’s adoption. The AFC/M23 rebellion, supported by Rwanda, continued its territorial expansion, establishing its own parallel administration beyond Kinshasa’s control. While the movement temporarily withdrew from Uvira under US pressure, it retains control over other eastern areas, maintaining security and public services under its authority.
Diplomatic processes, including the Washington process between Kinshasa and Kigali and the Doha talks with the AFC/M23, have produced limited progress. Parties continue to accuse each other of failing to honor commitments, fueling ongoing tensions.
Despite prior denials, Rwanda has now acknowledged security cooperation with the AFC/M23, further complicating efforts to stabilize the region. Humanitarian and security conditions remain critical, with civilian populations facing displacement, attacks, and limited access to essential services, highlighting the urgent need for UN action and the effective enforcement of Resolution 2773.
The DRC continues to call on the UN Security Council to act decisively, ensuring that the resolution translates into tangible security improvements for populations affected by decades of conflict in the eastern DRC.

title: FARDC Airstrikes Hit AFC/M23 Positions in Mindjendje, Walikale
excerpt: Walikale North Kivu, January 30, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have continued their military operations against AFC/M23 rebels in Walikale territory, aiming to dismantle rebel positions and reduce their operational capacity in this part of No
title_en: FARDC Airstrikes Hit AFC/M23 Positions in Mindjendje, Walikale
excerpt_en: Walikale North Kivu, January 30, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have continued their military operations against AFC/M23 rebels in Walikale territory, aiming to dismantle rebel positions and reduce their operational capacity in this part of No
body_en:
Walikale North Kivu, January 30, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have continued their military operations against AFC/M23 rebels in Walikale territory, aiming to dismantle rebel positions and reduce their operational capacity in this part of North Kivu.
Following the repulsion of a rebel attack in Chanjikiro, the Congolese army, through its air force, carried out airstrikes on Thursday, January 29, 2026, targeting AFC/M23 positions in Mindjendje, near Mpety, within the Kisimba group.
Local administrative authorities reported that the strikes occurred in the early evening, around 4:00 p.m. local time, shortly after the clashes in Chanjikiro.
A FARDC drone was deployed during the operation to strike what security sources identified as a key rebel logistics base in the Pinga area. Significant material damage was reported at the targeted site.
These airstrikes follow similar operations in recent days against positions in Mindjendje and Mpety, reflecting an intensification of FARDC military efforts in Walikale territory.

title_en: Mediator and Wife Beheaded by Rogue Militiamen
excerpt_en: Peace Process in Jeopardy in Kwamouth, February 3, 2026 — Deaths continue in Kwamouth, despite ongoing efforts to encourage militiamen to surrender. Between January 26 and 27, a mediator and his wife were killed at the Brazza farm, deep in the territory. The man had been sent to
body_en:
Peace Process in Jeopardy in Kwamouth, February 3, 2026 — Deaths continue in Kwamouth, despite ongoing efforts to encourage militiamen to surrender. Between January 26 and 27, a mediator and his wife were killed at the Brazza farm, deep in the territory.
The man had been sent to raise awareness among militiamen as part of the peace process recently launched on the Bateke Plateau by Minister Delegate for Defense, in charge of veterans, Eliezer Ntambwe. He was killed by rogue militiamen, who subsequently dismembered his body. His wife, accompanying him, was also murdered by the same armed men.
Chief Stany Libie of Kimomo village supports government efforts to encourage militiamen to surrender, stating that force must be used against those resisting the peace initiative.
“Some militiamen have rejected the message of peace, including the Cobra and American warlords, in Diangele, who have boycotted government actions. For all enemies of peace, measures must be taken to neutralize them. This is yet another sabotage of the peace process by these militiamen,” said Stany Libie.
Several Mobondo militiamen have voluntarily surrendered as part of the awareness campaign led by Minister Eliezer Ntambwe. In Kwamouth and the Maluku commune, some militiamen have joined the defense and security forces.
The Deputy Minister of Defense, responsible for veterans, reported encountering several victims attempting to protect themselves. However, the implementation of government programs has been delayed due to persistent insecurity in this region of Maï-Ndombe.

title: Call for Investigations After Assassination of Civil Society Leader in Ituri
excerpt: Ituri DRC, February 6, 2026 – The Ituri Civil Society Coordination has confirmed the assassination of Désiré Malo Dra, president of the Bahema Badjere civil society, and called on justice and security authorities to conduct independent and urgent investigations to clarify the cir
title_en: Call for Investigations After Assassination of Civil Society Leader in Ituri
excerpt_en: Ituri DRC, February 6, 2026 – The Ituri Civil Society Coordination has confirmed the assassination of Désiré Malo Dra, president of the Bahema Badjere civil society, and called on justice and security authorities to conduct independent and urgent investigations to clarify the cir
body_en:
Ituri DRC, February 6, 2026 – The Ituri Civil Society Coordination has confirmed the assassination of Désiré Malo Dra, president of the Bahema Badjere civil society, and called on justice and security authorities to conduct independent and urgent investigations to clarify the circumstances of this crime.
According to an obituary read on Thursday, February 5, by Jean-Marie Ezadri Aguekwa of the Ituri Civil Society Coordination, Malo Dra was killed by unknown assailants in Bule Centre.
“It is with great sadness and regret that the provincial coordination of civil society, Force Vive of Ituri, announces and confirms to the international community the tragic death of one of its active members, the president of the civil society of the Bahema Badjere chiefdom, Désiré Malo Dra, who was cowardly gunned down on February 4, 2026, at around 8:00 p.m. by unidentified armed individuals,” Ezadri stated.
The announcement also noted the abduction of the president of FEC Bule by unidentified assailants, with no communication yet made to his family or professional network.
The civil society coordination urged the security and justice authorities to conduct an independent investigation and called on the international community, including MONUSCO, to assist the Congolese government to ensure a thorough and transparent inquiry.
“The provincial coordination informs the public that funeral arrangements will be announced later. May the soul of our dear colleague rest in peace,” added Ezadri.
Despite the presence of MONUSCO, FARDC, and the UPDF, the security situation in Bule remains fragile, as CRP rebels continue attacks, even though the area is nominally under FARDC control.

title: Rwanda’s Foreign Minister Says UN Has Failed to Learn from Past Genocides
excerpt: Kigali, January 27, 2026 — Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Amb. Olivier Nduhungirehe, has accused the international community, particularly the United Nations, of failing to draw meaningful lessons from past genocides, citing the continued targeting of vulne
title_en: Rwanda’s Foreign Minister Says UN Has Failed to Learn from Past Genocides
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 27, 2026 — Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Amb. Olivier Nduhungirehe, has accused the international community, particularly the United Nations, of failing to draw meaningful lessons from past genocides, citing the continued targeting of vulne
body_en:
Kigali, January 27, 2026 — Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs and Cooperation, Amb. Olivier Nduhungirehe, has accused the international community, particularly the United Nations, of failing to draw meaningful lessons from past genocides, citing the continued targeting of vulnerable communities decades after the Holocaust and the Genocide against the Tutsi.
Speaking at the 81st commemoration of the Genocide against Jews at the Kigali Genocide Memorial, Nduhungirehe said that despite global vows of “never again,” mass atrocities have continued. “In 1945, the whole world said it would never happen again, but it happened again 49 years later in Rwanda,” he said, referring to the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi. “Even today, 32 years later, Tutsi and Mulenge communities in eastern DRC are still being targeted because of their identity.”
He questioned whether the UN has truly learned from the genocides in Europe and Rwanda, arguing that hate speech and violence continue to be ignored in parts of the region.
The ceremony brought together international organizations, members of the Jewish community in Rwanda, diplomats, and senior Rwandan officials. It marked the annual remembrance of the Holocaust, in which more than six million Jews were killed under Nazi rule.
Israel’s Ambassador to Rwanda, Einat Weiss, reflected on the shared histories of Israel and Rwanda, describing humanity as a mix of great good and profound evil. He acknowledged the persistence of Holocaust denial and distortion but praised Rwanda for its approach to remembrance, justice, reconciliation, and reconstruction.
The UN Resident Coordinator in Rwanda, Ozonnia Ojielo, called for stronger international cooperation to combat hate speech and punish those who trivialize genocide, stressing that the principle of ntibizongere (“never again”) must be implemented, not merely repeated.
German Ambassador Heike Uta Dettmann noted that while Jews rebuilt their lives in Germany after the Holocaust, antisemitism continues to surface worldwide, calling it shameful and urging stronger action against hatred.

title_en: President Kiir Appoints Deceased Candidate to Election Team
excerpt_en: Juba South Sudan , 4 February 2026 – President Salva Kiir of South Sudan has caused a political stir by appointing a presidential election team member who had been dead for five years. On 30 January 2026, a decree named Steward Soroba Budia, a former member of the opposition Unit
body_en:
Juba South Sudan , 4 February 2026 – President Salva Kiir of South Sudan has caused a political stir by appointing a presidential election team member who had been dead for five years.
On 30 January 2026, a decree named Steward Soroba Budia, a former member of the opposition United Democratic Party (UDP), to oversee preparations for the December 2026 presidential election. However, it was later revealed that Budia had passed away five years ago.
The announcement triggered widespread social media ridicule. Following the revelation, Kiir fired David Amour Major, former presidential press secretary, and Chief of Staff Valentino Dhel Maluet, citing errors in relying on collaborators for appointments.
A statement from President Kiir’s office expressed gratitude for their work while confirming their dismissal.
Budia had been a key figure in the 2018 peace agreement, which aimed to end the post-independence fighting in South Sudan that began in 2011.

title: Rwanda Launches First Coffee Exhibition in Pakistan

title_en: Rwanda Launches First Coffee Exhibition in Pakistan

body_en:
Islamabad, January 29-30, 2026 — The Rwandan Embassy in Pakistan, in collaboration with the National Agriculture Export Board (NAEB), launched Rwanda’s first coffee exhibition in Pakistan, showcasing the country’s high-quality coffee.
Minister of Industry and Trade Prudence Sebahizi highlighted Rwanda’s strategic position in Africa, emphasizing the country’s potential to help investors access the African market of over 1.2 billion people through the African Continental Free Trade Area (AfCFTA).
Pakistan’s Commerce Minister Jam Kamal Khan expressed willingness to collaborate with Rwanda in agro-manufacturing, leather, and agricultural production, and pledged to facilitate the entry of Rwandan coffee into the Pakistani market.
The exhibition featured Rwandan Ambassador Harerimana Fatou, NAEB Director General Claude Bizimana, and business leaders from both countries.
Coffee remains a major economic crop for Rwanda, with exports generating over 216 billion Rwf in 2025, up from 129 billion Rwf in 2024, totaling 23,860 tons, an increase from 17,142 tons in 2024.

title_en: US Lawyer Expelled Over Opposition Ties
excerpt_en: Kampala Uganda, 4 February 2026 – Ugandan security forces have expelled US lawyer Robert Amsterdam, who represented opposition leader Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu (Bobi Wine). Human rights activist Jeffrey Smith was also expelled. Both were accused of acting against Uganda’s intere
body_en:
Kampala Uganda, 4 February 2026 – Ugandan security forces have expelled US lawyer Robert Amsterdam, who represented opposition leader Robert Kyagulanyi Ssentamu (Bobi Wine). Human rights activist Jeffrey Smith was also expelled. Both were accused of acting against Uganda’s interests and supporting groups opposed to President Yoweri Museveni.
Amsterdam’s expulsion followed comments he made on 2 February, accusing Chief of Defence Staff Gen Muhoozi Kainerugaba of instilling fear among Ugandans and using his family’s wealth to consolidate power.
The lawyer had previously announced plans to seek Uganda’s suspension from the Commonwealth, citing what he called “intimidation” and “internal colonialism” by the Museveni family.
On 3 February, Jeffrey Smith also called for international sanctions against the Ugandan government, highlighting Gen Muhoozi’s recent attacks on the US Embassy in Kampala.

title: Rubavu Honors Heroes, Praises Resistance Against FDLR
excerpt: Rubavu, February 1, 2026 — The courage and resilience of the people of Rubavu District were celebrated during the Heroes of Rwanda ceremony, honoring their decades-long resistance against the FDLR armed group. Speaking at the event, Rubavu Mayor Mulindwa Prosper said the values o

excerpt_en: Rubavu, February 1, 2026 — The courage and resilience of the people of Rubavu District were celebrated during the Heroes of Rwanda ceremony, honoring their decades-long resistance against the FDLR armed group. Speaking at the event, Rubavu Mayor Mulindwa Prosper said the values o
body_en:
Rubavu, February 1, 2026 — The courage and resilience of the people of Rubavu District were celebrated during the Heroes of Rwanda ceremony, honoring their decades-long resistance against the FDLR armed group.
Speaking at the event, Rubavu Mayor Mulindwa Prosper said the values of courage that define Rwandans prevented the district from being defeated, despite its proximity to hostile forces.“These values made Rwanda endure and resist those who carried out repeated attacks,” he said.
He recalled that hostile forces crossed from neighboring countries between 1994 and early 2025, settling in the area but ultimately being defeated. He praised local heroes and criticized those who joined the FDLR instead of contributing to national development.
Western Province Governor Ntibitura Jean Bosco echoed this message, expressing regret that some residents were deceived into joining the group, which he described as cowardly.
He warned that any attempt to undermine Rwanda’s security would fail, urging citizens to encourage those still in armed groups to return home, stressing that the country is now safe and liberated.
Governor Ntibitura also highlighted that Heroes’ Day serves as a reminder of the sacrifices made for Rwanda’s survival and development, while emphasizing the country’s current focus on fighting poverty.
In support of reintegration efforts, the Rwanda Demobilization and Reintegration Commission (RDRC) announced in October 2025 that it has rehabilitated 12,602 former combatants from armed groups operating in eastern DRC since 2001.

body_en:
Mulolya, North Kivu, February 3, 2026 — Four civilians were killed and six motorcycles burned in an ambush by ADF rebels on the Oicha–Mulolya–Mamove road, about 10 km west of Oicha, the main town of Beni territory.
The attack occurred around 8:00 a.m., with rebels coming from west of Mamove, which was itself attacked two days earlier. This brings the death toll in the area to nine civilians in three days.
Another ambush was reported in Malibo the same day, though targeted farmers escaped to Oicha. Traffic remains suspended, and victims’ bodies were taken to the Oicha General Hospital morgue.
The FARDC Deputy Chief of Staff is currently assessing the security situation in Beni.
By Jeff Buleli
& Teammates

title_en: MONUSCO Boosts Ceasefire Monitoring Support Between DRC and AFC/M23
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, February 4, 2026 — The UN Stabilization Mission in the DRC (MONUSCO) announced it has strengthened its preparedness to support the ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism between the Congolese government and the AFC/M23, following talks facilitated in Doha by Qa
body_en:
Kinshasa, February 4, 2026 — The UN Stabilization Mission in the DRC (MONUSCO) announced it has strengthened its preparedness to support the ceasefire monitoring and verification mechanism between the Congolese government and the AFC/M23, following talks facilitated in Doha by Qatar.
MONUSCO confirmed it is authorized under UN Security Council Resolution 2808 (2025) to assist in implementing a permanent ceasefire, and will provide technical and logistical support through the ICGLR-backed mechanism (EJVM+).
The Mission is expected to deploy an initial team to Uvira in the coming days to monitor compliance, as parties reaffirmed their commitment to the Doha Peace Framework signed on November 15, 2025.

body_en:
Kinshasa, February 4, 2026 — The International Monetary Fund (IMF) says security spending is the main cause of budget deviations in the Democratic Republic of Congo, following its second program review.
The IMF reports that prolonged fighting in eastern DRC led to an increase in security expenditures of about 1.2% of GDP, forcing repeated adjustments to fiscal targets and reducing funds for social and investment programs.
Two key targets were missed: limits on emergency spending and minimum levels of social spending. While the IMF approved a higher deficit ceiling due to security pressures, it warned that continued reliance on emergency procedures threatens fiscal discipline and remains the program’s primary vulnerability.

body_en:
Niamey, January 29, 2026 — Two Tuareg marabouts were summarily executed by Nigerien security forces following their arrest in the Niamey 2000 neighborhood. The victims, including Ahmad Ag Almouner Ag Madda, a respected elder from Tessit, Gao, were taken by military personnel in the morning and found dead by late afternoon.
No official charges were filed, and the fate of a third man arrested with them remains unknown. Their burial is scheduled for January 30 at Yantala cemetery.
Calls are growing for an independent investigation into these extrajudicial killings amid rising communal tensions.

title: Kamikaze Drone Attack on Kisangani Airport Thwarted
excerpt: Kisangani DR Congo, February 2, 2026 — The civilian Bangboka International Airport in Kisangani, northern Democratic Republic of Congo, was targeted by kamikaze drones overnight between Saturday and Sunday, according to the Tshopo provincial government. Local authorities confirme
title_en: Kamikaze Drone Attack on Kisangani Airport Thwarted
excerpt_en: Kisangani DR Congo, February 2, 2026 — The civilian Bangboka International Airport in Kisangani, northern Democratic Republic of Congo, was targeted by kamikaze drones overnight between Saturday and Sunday, according to the Tshopo provincial government. Local authorities confirme
body_en:
Kisangani DR Congo, February 2, 2026 — The civilian Bangboka International Airport in Kisangani, northern Democratic Republic of Congo, was targeted by kamikaze drones overnight between Saturday and Sunday, according to the Tshopo provincial government.
Local authorities confirmed that eight enemy drones were intercepted and neutralized before reaching their target. The runway, which is also used by FARDC attack drones and fighter jets conducting strikes against AFC/M23 positions more than 400 kilometers away, was not damaged.
In a televised address, provincial officials stated that the drones were “equipped with unconventional munitions and submunitions” and failed to reach their objectives. No group has claimed responsibility, but authorities have accused the AFC/M23 and Rwanda of orchestrating the attack, alleging it was intended to undermine the Washington peace agreement.
The provincial government has called for calm and urged residents to resume normal activities, insisting there is “no reason to travel” at this time.

body_en:
Bamako/Dakar, January 12–22, 2026 — Friction is emerging between the Senegalese Minister of Transport and his Malian counterpart over Malian containers and equipment abandoned at the Port of Dakar for over two months.
According to Senegalese authorities, the port is operating at full capacity, prompting pressure on Mali to urgently recover its goods. The situation is linked to the de facto closure of the Senegal-Mali border, controlled by armed terrorist groups, which has prevented safe transport.
Mali’s request for Senegalese military escorts to move goods through high-risk areas was reportedly refused, leaving containers stuck and creating growing congestion.
Sources from the Malian Ministry of Transport say discussions are ongoing, with authorities seeking alternative solutions to clear the backlog. Updates are expected as the situation evolves.

title_en: Commander of AES Unified Force Receives Audience with President Assimi Goïta

body_en:
Koulouba, January 29, 2026 – The President of the Transition and Head of State, General Assimi Goïta, received Brigadier General Daouda Traoré, Commander of the AES Unified Force (FU-AES), in an official audience on Thursday, January 29, 2026.
During the meeting, Brigadier General Traoré expressed gratitude to the President for the trust placed in him and presented a detailed report on the preparations for the Unified Force, which comprises 6,000 personnel. He also highlighted efforts to establish this new unit, aimed at strengthening security and stability in the Sahel.
The President of the Transition commended the progress made in the formation of the force and provided guidance to ensure the successful achievement of its objectives.
Conclusion
The period from January 18 to February 1, 2026, underscores a Mali navigating a complex duality of proactive diplomacy and intensifying internal security threats. While the Malian government has successfully strengthened strategic international partnerships—notably with China to advance infrastructure and energy projects, and with the WTO to advocate for the national cotton sector—the domestic landscape remains highly volatile.
The security situation is marked by a significant escalation in insurgent activity and mounting human rights concerns:
Insurgent Expansion: The Group for the Support of Islam and Muslims (JNIM) and Islamic State in the Sahel (IS-Sahel) have demonstrated increased operational capacity, seizing military posts near key hubs such as Sikasso and Koulikoro. A recent ambush on the Diboli-Kayes axis resulted in the destruction of approximately 50 fuel tankers, exacerbating the national energy crisis.
Military Response: The Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) are increasingly pivoting toward air power and AI-powered weaponry to counter these threats, supported by the operationalization of the 6,000-person AES Unified Force, aimed at stabilizing the broader Sahel region.
Civilian Impact: Amidst ongoing fighting, troubling reports have surfaced of civilian abuses by joint patrols of the army and Russian Africa Corps in Kidal and Mopti. Concurrently, political tensions persist, exemplified by the detention of figures like Moussa Mara and Choguel Maïga.
Ultimately, Mali stands at a critical juncture. The successful realization of the “Mali 2063” strategic vision and the tangible benefits of its new diplomatic alliances hinge on the government’s ability to restore security along vital trade routes and foster national reconciliation, all while confronting persistent extremist violence and growing domestic opposition.
By Maïga Sidi Bonkana
(Boukari Zankey Sidi)
Jeff Buleli

body_en:
Bamako, January 23, 2026 – As part of the operational monitoring of bilateral cooperation, His Excellency Mr. Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, held a working meeting on Friday, January 23, 2026, with His Excellency Mr. Li Xiang, Ambassador of the People’s Republic of China to the Republic of Mali.
Reviewing the strategic areas of cooperation, the two officials emphasized the need for the rigorous implementation of priority projects arising from economic and technical cooperation agreements. These include solar energy projects, infrastructure and transportation development, agricultural mechanization, and the construction of healthcare facilities.
Highlighting the importance attached by the highest authorities to economic development, Minister Diop underscored the significant initiatives undertaken by the Government to ensure the secure execution of development projects, in a spirit of pragmatism and mutual interest. Both sides praised the strategic level of the Mali–China partnership and reaffirmed their commitment to the regular and rigorous monitoring of ongoing projects, with a view to the swift realization of shared ambitions of the Malian and Chinese Heads of State.
