title_en: Close Associate of Matata Ponyo Transferred to Ndolo Prison After Four Months of Detention
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC, January 11, 2026 – After four months of detention, a close associate of Augustin Matata Ponyo has been transferred to Ndolo Military Prison. The LGD and Allies political coalition announced on Friday the transfer of Professor Pascal Isumbisho Mwapu, political advis
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC, January 11, 2026 – After four months of detention, a close associate of Augustin Matata Ponyo has been transferred to Ndolo Military Prison.
The LGD and Allies political coalition announced on Friday the transfer of Professor Pascal Isumbisho Mwapu, political advisor to opposition leader Matata Ponyo, to Ndolo Prison in Kinshasa, after several months of detention at the National Cyber Defense Council (CNC).
In a statement dated January 9, the coalition said the transfer took place on Thursday, January 8, following what it described as “four months of arbitrary and illegal detention” at the CNC. Professor Isumbisho was arrested on September 9, 2025.
LGD and its allies maintain that their founding member is being wrongfully accused of collaborating with the AFC/M23 rebels, accusations they describe as “unfounded and politically motivated.” The coalition denounced what it called “political harassment,” “manipulation of the judicial system,” and the “repression of critical voices.”
The coalition is demanding respect for the rights of the defense, an end to arbitrary detentions, and the “immediate and unconditional release” of Professor Isumbisho, arguing that no legal charges justify his continued detention. It also called on the national and international community and human rights organizations to closely monitor the case.
This development comes amid a realignment of the Congolese opposition. A faction has launched a new political platform, “Save the Democratic Republic of Congo,” led by former President Joseph Kabila.
The platform brings together several opposition figures, including Augustin Matata Ponyo, Franck Diongo, Seth Kikuni, and André Claudel Lubaya, as well as civil society actors. body_en:
Masisi, January 12, 2026 – The villages of Humura and Rutoboko, in the Nyamaboko 1 group (Osso Banyungu sector) of Masisi territory, North Kivu, have been abandoned by residents following clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and the Wazalendo.
Residents began fleeing on Sunday, January 11, after fighting erupted near Kazinga. Fearing for their safety, families moved toward the Waloa Yungu group in Walikale territory.
Several displaced families arrived in Langira and Chumba on Sunday evening and Monday. Many are being sheltered by host families, while others have taken refuge in schools and churches.
According to information from the ground, the humanitarian situation is critical, as most people fled without their belongings. The displaced are urgently appealing for food assistance and temporary shelter to protect them from the elements.

title: In Lubumbashi, Jacquemain Shabani Calls for Constant Vigilance to Contain Security Threats Between the DRC and Zambia
excerpt: Lubumbashi Haut-Katanga, January 16, 2026 — The 14th session of the Joint Defense and Security Commission between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the Republic of Zambia concluded on Thursday, January 15, in Lubumbashi, the capital of Haut-Katanga province. This high-le
title_en: In Lubumbashi, Jacquemain Shabani Calls for Constant Vigilance to Contain Security Threats Between the DRC and Zambia
excerpt_en: Lubumbashi Haut-Katanga, January 16, 2026 — The 14th session of the Joint Defense and Security Commission between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the Republic of Zambia concluded on Thursday, January 15, in Lubumbashi, the capital of Haut-Katanga province. This high-le
body_en:
Lubumbashi Haut-Katanga, January 16, 2026 — The 14th session of the Joint Defense and Security Commission between the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the Republic of Zambia concluded on Thursday, January 15, in Lubumbashi, the capital of Haut-Katanga province. This high-level bilateral meeting brought together delegations from both countries over three days to examine shared security challenges in a regional context marked by a resurgence of cross-border threats.
The DRC–Zambia Joint Defense and Security Commission serves as a permanent framework for consultation between the two neighboring states, which share a long border. Its mandate is to strengthen security cooperation, prevent conflicts, combat cross-border crime, and ensure the stability of border areas.
This 14th session took place against a backdrop of persistent security challenges, including armed banditry, transnational crime, terrorism, and border incursions, all of which require close coordination and a concerted response between Kinshasa and Lusaka.
At the close of the session, the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior, Security, Decentralization, and Customary Affairs of the DRC, Jacquemain Shabani, emphasized the gravity and complexity of these shared threats.
“The discussions highlighted terrorism, transnational crime, banditry, and border violations. It is imperative to maintain constant vigilance and continuously adapt to address them,” Mr. Shabani stated.
He stressed the need to move beyond commitments in principle and called for the effective implementation of the decisions taken.
“I recommend rigorous follow-up to the adopted resolutions so that defense and security issues between our two countries produce the results expected by our respective governments,” he added.
For his part, Jacob Mwimbu, Minister of Home Affairs and Security of Zambia, welcomed the progress made by the Joint Commission and reaffirmed his country’s commitment to strengthening security cooperation with the DRC.
“In the area of defense and security, our Commission has successfully implemented concrete strategies to combat cross-border crime and other offenses that threaten defense and security,” he stated.
He also underscored the close link between security and economic development.
“We recognize that without peace and security, the economic growth objectives of our Commission will be difficult to achieve.”
Emphasizing the importance of collaboration between the security services of both countries, the Zambian minister added:
“Our security services have a duty to maintain their cooperation in defense and security matters. It is therefore crucial for us to strengthen our collaboration and conduct joint security and defense operations.”
He concluded with a clear commitment:
“I reaffirm Zambia’s commitment to ensuring the success of the Commission’s mandate. Zambia remains committed to maintaining peace at the regional, national, and international levels.”
The closing of this 14th session marks a new stage in strengthening security relations between the DRC and Zambia, with both countries reaffirming their commitment to translating adopted resolutions into concrete actions to guarantee the security of their populations and the stability of their shared border areas.

title: FARDC Regains Control of Uvira, Denounces Looting Before AFC/M23 Withdrawal
excerpt: Uvira, DRC January 19, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) announced that they have regained control of the city of Uvira, in South Kivu, following the withdrawal of the Rwandan army and its AFC/M23 allies. According to the army, the city was retak
title_en: FARDC Regains Control of Uvira, Denounces Looting Before AFC/M23 Withdrawal
excerpt_en: Uvira, DRC January 19, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) announced that they have regained control of the city of Uvira, in South Kivu, following the withdrawal of the Rwandan army and its AFC/M23 allies. According to the army, the city was retak
body_en:
Uvira, DRC January 19, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) announced that they have regained control of the city of Uvira, in South Kivu, following the withdrawal of the Rwandan army and its AFC/M23 allies. According to the army, the city was retaken on Sunday, January 18, 2026.
In a statement, the FARDC condemned the systematic looting carried out in the city by AFC/M23-RDF forces prior to their evacuation. The army said that around twenty civilians involved in the looting were arrested and will be brought to justice.
“The FARDC are continuing their deployment in and around Uvira to consolidate positions and ensure the safety of people and property,” the statement said.
This development follows a letter sent on January 15, 2026, by the political coordinator of the AFC/M23, Corneille Nangaa, to the United Nations Secretary-General, announcing that the group was placing Uvira under the responsibility of the international community. The movement said this was part of its withdrawal decision, initially announced on December 15, 2025, and reaffirmed as part of its ceasefire commitment.
The rebellion also announced the immediate withdrawal of its “observation and surveillance unit,” declining any further responsibility for the security of Uvira.
However, Congolese authorities have expressed skepticism over this withdrawal, viewing it as an attempt to divert attention and reduce international pressure, particularly on Kigali, which Kinshasa considers the main supporter of the rebellion. On the ground, the AFC/M23 continues territorial advances and is establishing a parallel administration outside government control.
Uvira, a strategic city in South Kivu, had fallen under rebel control, strengthening the group’s hold over North and South Kivu. The city is considered a key security hub, whose control could facilitate further advances toward the Greater Katanga region, the economic heartland of the Democratic Republic of Congo.

title: FARDC Drones Strike AFC/M23 Position in Kikuku
excerpt: Rutshuru, North Kivu, January 23, 2026 – Military pressure on AFC/M23 rebels is intensifying in North Kivu. Following airstrikes in Buleusa, the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) targeted another rebel position in Kikuku, located in the Bwito chiefdom, Ruts
title_en: FARDC Drones Strike AFC/M23 Position in Kikuku
excerpt_en: Rutshuru, North Kivu, January 23, 2026 – Military pressure on AFC/M23 rebels is intensifying in North Kivu. Following airstrikes in Buleusa, the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) targeted another rebel position in Kikuku, located in the Bwito chiefdom, Ruts
body_en:
Rutshuru, North Kivu, January 23, 2026 – Military pressure on AFC/M23 rebels is intensifying in North Kivu. Following airstrikes in Buleusa, the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) targeted another rebel position in Kikuku, located in the Bwito chiefdom, Rutshuru territory.
Shortly after 2 p.m., a FARDC drone carried out a precision strike near the administrative office of the Bwito chiefdom, destroying the rebel position completely, according to local sources. Residents reported loud explosions, thick black smoke, and widespread panic.
No official figures have been released regarding casualties. However, the attack reportedly caused significant material damage, including the total destruction of the rebel camp.
Observers note that the FARDC’s increased use of drones marks a new stage in operations, aimed at weakening rebel capacities and reducing their ability to carry out attacks in the region.
Despite this military pressure, tension remains high in Kikuku, with civilians continuing to bear the brunt of the ongoing insecurity in eastern DRC.
Conclusion
The reporting period from January 12 to 24, 2026, depicts a Democratic Republic of Congo at a critical crossroads, defined by a complex interplay of persistent conflict, intensive diplomacy, and strategic economic shifts. While high-level mediation through the Washington and Doha processes continues, the security situation in the east remains volatile, marked by shifting rebel positions, humanitarian distress for hundreds of thousands of displaced persons, and a growing reliance on drone technology in military operations. Concurrently, the government is asserting greater economic sovereignty, particularly in the mining sector, and pursuing ambitious internal infrastructure projects despite facing significant domestic political opposition and international legal challenges. Ultimately, the path toward lasting stability appears to hinge on the successful operationalization of regional monitoring mechanisms and the realization of a truly inclusive national dialogue
Overviews :
1. Diplomatic & Political Overview: A Region at a Crossroads
The DRC is currently navigating a period of intense but stalled diplomacy. While multiple peace frameworks exist—specifically the Washington and Doha processes—there is a palpable lack of trust between Kinshasa and Kigali.
The "Lomé Momentum": Togo has emerged as a key African mediator, hosting high-level sessions to harmonize these disparate peace initiatives.
Domestic Political Tension: Internally, the government faces a fractured landscape. The exile of figures like Seth Kikuni and the arrest of others like Aubin Minaku signal a deepening rift between the current administration and the opposition.
The Call for Dialogue: International partners, including Belgium’s King Philippe, are increasingly pushing for an "inclusive national dialogue" to address the root causes of instability.
2. Security Overview: Technological Shifts and Precarious Ceasefires
The security landscape in eastern DRC remains volatile, characterized by a "frozen conflict" that frequently thaws into violence.
Drone Warfare: A notable shift in FARDC tactics is the increased use of precision drone strikes to target AFC/M23 positions, as seen in Buleusa and Kikuku.
The Uvira Vacuum: The AFC/M23’s tactical withdrawal from Uvira has created a complex security environment, with the rebels officially placing the city under "international responsibility" while the government views the move as a strategy to deflect international pressure.
Reinforcements vs. Retreats: While rebels withdrew from some areas, they simultaneously reinforced positions in others, such as Masisi, indicating they are preparing for potential counter-offensives.
3. Economic & Technical Overview: Asserting Sovereignty
Kinshasa is actively seeking to reclaim control over its national resources and public systems, though this has led to significant legal and logistical friction.
Resource Nationalism: Gécamines’ decision to directly purchase 100,000 tons of copper from the Tenke Fungurume Mine for the US market is a landmark move to assert state sovereignty over metal pricing and marketing.
Infrastructure Struggles: Efforts to rehabilitate vital infrastructure, such as the Bandundu and Kikwit airports, have been plagued by technical failures and contract terminations, highlighting the challenges of internal development.
Legal Battles: The $4 billion lawsuit by PayServices underscores the risks and complexities the DRC faces as it attempts to modernize and digitize its state payment systems.
4. Humanitarian Overview: A Growing Regional Crisis
The human cost of the conflict has reached a "devastating human tragedy," as described by government officials.
Mass Displacement: Over 200,000 Congolese refugees are now in Burundi alone, with transit centers operating at 200% capacity.
Medical System Collapse: Frontline health facilities in zones like Fizi and Walikale are overwhelmed by gunshot victims and suffering from acute shortages of medicine and nutritional products.
Conservation at Risk: Even conservation efforts are caught in the crossfire; while Virunga National Park recorded a rare mountain gorilla birth, the park remains under threat from the ongoing presence of armed groups.

title: Ndayishimiye Denies Burundi’s Role in DRC War
excerpt: January 17, 2026 — Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye has denied his country’s involvement in the war in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), presenting himself as a key actor in efforts to restore peace and reconciliation in the region. Since 2022, the Burundian go
title_en: Ndayishimiye Denies Burundi’s Role in DRC War
excerpt_en: January 17, 2026 — Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye has denied his country’s involvement in the war in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), presenting himself as a key actor in efforts to restore peace and reconciliation in the region. Since 2022, the Burundian go
body_en:
January 17, 2026 — Burundian President Évariste Ndayishimiye has denied his country’s involvement in the war in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC), presenting himself as a key actor in efforts to restore peace and reconciliation in the region.
Since 2022, the Burundian government has deployed troops to eastern DRC under a bilateral agreement aimed at combating armed groups, including RED Tabara and M23. Burundian forces reportedly suffered heavy losses in North Kivu Province before withdrawing toward South Kivu, where M23 later seized key cities, including Bukavu and Uvira.
Speaking to diplomats in Burundi, Ndayishimiye said he played a major role last year in resolving the conflict, despite widespread perceptions that his country was directly involved in the fighting.
“No, Burundi is not at war. Burundi went to help the DRC to protect the security of its people. We did not go to war. That is why we continue to do our best to play a role in reconciliation, so that the region can find peace,” he said.
He further claimed that the arrival of the Burundian army in South Kivu helped unite previously divided communities, including the Banyamulenge, Bembe, and Fulero.
“You have seen that when the Burundian army arrived in South Kivu, the Banyamulenge, the Bembe, and the Fulero who were fighting immediately united... In South Kivu, we united everyone, and now I am happy that everyone is sending me messages of gratitude,” he said.
However, despite these claims, reports indicate that in 2025, the Burundian army launched major attacks on the Banyamulenge in Minembwe, in collaboration with the DRC government, Wazalendo groups — including Ababembe and Abafulero — and the FDLR terrorist group.
In October 2025, Burundian forces reportedly blocked all roads connecting Minembwe commune to other parts of South Kivu Province, restricting access to markets and health services, citing the presence of the MRDP-Twirwaneho group.
After the AFC/M23 captured Uvira on December 9, Burundian military operations in the DRC were temporarily disrupted. However, attacks have since resumed on Minembwe and surrounding areas where Banyamulenge communities have sought refuge, in coordination with DRC and Wazalendo forces.

title: Rwanda Launches Private Sector Procurement Platform ‘e-Bid’
excerpt: Kigali, January 19, 2026 – A new private sector procurement platform has been launched in Rwanda, aiming to modernize how companies manage tenders and submit bids. The platform, called e-Bid, was developed by Orion Systems & Design, a Rwandan technology company known for building
title_en: Rwanda Launches Private Sector Procurement Platform ‘e-Bid’
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 19, 2026 – A new private sector procurement platform has been launched in Rwanda, aiming to modernize how companies manage tenders and submit bids. The platform, called e-Bid, was developed by Orion Systems & Design, a Rwandan technology company known for building
body_en:
Kigali, January 19, 2026 – A new private sector procurement platform has been launched in Rwanda, aiming to modernize how companies manage tenders and submit bids.
The platform, called e-Bid, was developed by Orion Systems & Design, a Rwandan technology company known for building mobile banking applications used across Rwanda and other African countries. It was unveiled at a private sector software conference held in Kigali on January 16, 2026.
Software engineer Muhire Victor, the project’s lead developer, said the idea was inspired by the government’s procurement platform, Umucyo, after observing how it addressed long-standing challenges in public procurement.
“In the past, tenders were submitted manually, and documents were sometimes lost, causing bidders to lose opportunities,” Muhire explained. “We realized there was an electronic solution, but it was only available to government tenders. The private sector had no such platform.”
As a result, e-Bid was created to serve private companies, and more than 50 private tenders have already been submitted through the platform.
Muhire said the system allows tender announcements, online submission of bid documents, and selection of winners without requiring physical meetings. “The tender issuer can choose to receive bids electronically and select the winning contractor directly through the platform,” he said.
He added that bidder information remains confidential between the bidder and the tender issuer, with platform administrators having no access to the content of submissions.
On the government platform umucyo.gov.rw, contractors can already find tender notices, submit bid documents, and have winners selected without public opening sessions — a model e-Bid aims to replicate for the private sector.
Founded in 2013, Orion Systems & Design operates in Rwanda and four other African countries. The company is among the few Rwandan firms to have received the Digital Trust Seal, a certification awarded by the Software Testing Qualifications Board, with only 16 Rwandan software companies holding the distinction so far.
Rwanda is one of 73 countries worldwide offering the Digital Trust Seal, reflecting its growing technological capacity and international credibility.
Muhire said investment in software development in Rwanda is both demanding and profitable, citing government programs that support the sector. Since its founding, Orion Systems & Design has developed multiple software solutions used by banks and financial institutions across the region.
He encouraged young innovators to pursue technology development, noting that Rwanda offers strong opportunities for those with the skills to create digital solutions.

title: RIB Arrests University Professor Suspected of Child Sexual Abuse
excerpt: Kigali, January 19, 2026 – The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has arrested a university professor suspected of sexually abusing minors and deceiving them with promises of money. In a statement released on January 19, 2026, RIB said preliminary investigations indicate that the
title_en: RIB Arrests University Professor Suspected of Child Sexual Abuse
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 19, 2026 – The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has arrested a university professor suspected of sexually abusing minors and deceiving them with promises of money. In a statement released on January 19, 2026, RIB said preliminary investigations indicate that the
body_en:
Kigali, January 19, 2026 – The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has arrested a university professor suspected of sexually abusing minors and deceiving them with promises of money.
In a statement released on January 19, 2026, RIB said preliminary investigations indicate that the suspect abused several secondary school girls in Bugesera District on different occasions.
The professor, who holds a PhD, is currently being held at the RIB Rwezamenyo Station in Nyarugenge District, and his case has been forwarded to the Prosecution Service.
In its statement, RIB emphasized that rape of a child constitutes a grave violation that destroys the victim’s future, affects families, and harms society as a whole.
The agency warned that sexual abuse of children will not be tolerated and urged minors to avoid individuals who lure them with money or gifts for sexual exploitation.
The issue of child sexual violence remains a serious concern in Rwanda. In February 2025, the Minister of Gender and Family Development, Uwimana Consolée, reported that 22,454 adolescents were raped and impregnated in 2024.
Official statistics indicate that 19,701 adolescents were impregnated in 2020, rising to 23,111 in 2021, 24,472 in 2022, before declining slightly to 22,055 in 2023.
Under Article 14 of Law No. 059/2023 of December 4, 2023, amending Law No. 68/2018, the crime of child rape carries a prison sentence of 20 to 25 years upon conviction.

title: Twirwaneho Captures Point-Zéro from DRC Government Forces
excerpt: On January 16, 2026, MRDP-Twirwaneho announced that it had captured Point-Zéro from the DRC government forces, marking a significant development in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The armed group, which is fighting the DRC government, seized Point-Zéro, a st
title_en: Twirwaneho Captures Point-Zéro from DRC Government Forces
excerpt_en: On January 16, 2026, MRDP-Twirwaneho announced that it had captured Point-Zéro from the DRC government forces, marking a significant development in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo. The armed group, which is fighting the DRC government, seized Point-Zéro, a st
body_en:
On January 16, 2026, MRDP-Twirwaneho announced that it had captured Point-Zéro from the DRC government forces, marking a significant development in the conflict in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo.
The armed group, which is fighting the DRC government, seized Point-Zéro, a strategic area for the coalition of DRC forces, Burundian troops, Wazalendo groups, and the FDLR terrorist group. The capture came on the morning of January 16, a day after Twirwaneho had taken other key positions in Fizi territory, including Mount Baruta, and shot down a drone belonging to the DRC government forces.
The Twirwaneho leadership said that after losing Point-Zéro, Mount Baruta, and Isumo, coalition forces fled toward the Mulima and Mutambala areas.
Point-Zéro had served as a key base for the DRC government forces, blocking the road connecting Minembwe commune with other parts of Fizi and Uvira territories. The base was also used to plan and launch major attacks on Minembwe areas inhabited by the Banyamulenge, as well as other locations where they had sought refuge, including Mikenke.
Analyst Dr. Alex Mvuka, who closely monitors the situation in the DRC, said that Point-Zéro was one of three key locations for government forces.
“They used Point-Zéro as a base to launch indiscriminate attacks on the Banyamulenge villages in the highlands in general and in the Minembwe area in particular,” Dr. Mvuka said.
Supporters of the DRC government have expressed concern that following the fall of Point-Zéro, Twirwaneho fighters could advance further into Fizi, including Mulima, Fizi center, and the town of Baraka.

title: King Philippe Urges Tshisekedi to Launch Inclusive Dialogue, Pledges European Support on DRC Humanitarian Crisis
excerpt: Davos, January 21, 2026 – Belgium’s King Philippe has encouraged President Félix Tshisekedi to organize an inclusive national dialogue in the Democratic Republic of Congo, while pledging to mobilize European partners around the country’s worsening humanitarian situation. The meet
title_en: King Philippe Urges Tshisekedi to Launch Inclusive Dialogue, Pledges European Support on DRC Humanitarian Crisis
excerpt_en: Davos, January 21, 2026 – Belgium’s King Philippe has encouraged President Félix Tshisekedi to organize an inclusive national dialogue in the Democratic Republic of Congo, while pledging to mobilize European partners around the country’s worsening humanitarian situation. The meet
body_en:
Davos, January 21, 2026 – Belgium’s King Philippe has encouraged President Félix Tshisekedi to organize an inclusive national dialogue in the Democratic Republic of Congo, while pledging to mobilize European partners around the country’s worsening humanitarian situation.
The meeting took place on the sidelines of the 56th World Economic Forum Annual Meeting in Davos, where the two leaders discussed the security crisis in eastern DRC and the broader political situation.
Belgian Foreign Minister Maxime Prévot confirmed that Brussels reiterated its support for a national dialogue, long demanded by the opposition and seen as a key step toward addressing the root causes of the country’s multifaceted crisis.
Belgium reaffirmed its commitment to a peaceful resolution of the conflict in eastern DRC and respect for the country’s territorial integrity. King Philippe also pledged to ensure that European governments are fully informed of the dramatic humanitarian conditions facing civilians in areas affected by the M23 rebellion.
“Belgium remains a strategic partner of the DRC, determined to support peace,” Prévot said.
As discussions around a dialogue framework advance, the “Save the DRC” political and social platform, backed by former President Joseph Kabila, has been consulted twice by Angolan President João Lourenço. The platform has indicated it would support abandoning the Doha process with the AFC/M23 only if the proposed dialogue is genuinely inclusive and focused on restoring peace in the east.
Meanwhile, the Catholic bishops (CENCO) and Protestant leaders (ECC) who initiated the dialogue effort were also received by President Lourenço, days after his second meeting in a month with President Tshisekedi in Luanda.
Several opposition figures have likewise met with the current Chairperson of the African Union, as political consultations intensify ahead of a dialogue long awaited by the opposition and civil society.

title: Four Patients Die in Fire at Masisi General Referral Hospital

title_en: Four Patients Die in Fire at Masisi General Referral Hospital
excerpt_en: Masisi, North Kivu, January 20, 2026 – A tragic fire at Masisi General Referral Hospital on the evening of January 19 claimed the lives of four patients, including three children, local medical sources confirmed. According to authorities, the blaze was caused by an electrical mal
body_en:
Masisi, North Kivu, January 20, 2026 – A tragic fire at Masisi General Referral Hospital on the evening of January 19 claimed the lives of four patients, including three children, local medical sources confirmed.
According to authorities, the blaze was caused by an electrical malfunction. Hospital staff evacuated patients during the night as the fire spread. By the following morning, the hospital had reopened, allowing surviving patients to return to their wards.
The fire caused significant material damage, destroying the hospital’s garage and electrical system. Officials emphasized that the flames were contained before reaching inpatient wards, preventing further casualties.
An official investigation has been launched to determine the exact cause of the incident.

body_en:
Sake, January 12, 2026 – Residents of Sake, in the Kamuronza group (Masisi territory) of North Kivu, are alarmed by a sharp rise in insecurity in this town located about 27 km west of Goma.
Between Monday, January 5, and Thursday, January 8, at least four people were killed. The latest incident occurred on Wednesday evening when armed attackers shot dead two people during a raid in Kimoka, near Sake. A man and his child were reportedly killed by assailants suspected of belonging to the AFC/M23 rebels, who control the area.
According to local accounts, the attackers stormed the family home, shot the victims, looted valuables, and fled while firing into the air.
This attack came just two days after another deadly incident in the same town that left three victims—two dead and one wounded—bringing the total death toll to four in four days. Residents continue to attribute these killings to AFC/M23 fighters.
Faced with this alarming security situation, the population of Sake is calling for urgent reinforcement of security measures in the rebel-held area.

title: AFC/M23 Appeals to the UN and Places the City of Uvira Under the “Full and Complete” Responsibility of the International Community
excerpt: Uvira DRC, January 16, 2026 —The AFC/M23 rebellion, which controls large areas of North Kivu and South Kivu, announced that it has placed the strategic city of Uvira under the responsibility of the international community. In a letter dated Thursday, January 15, 2026, to UN Secre
title_en: AFC/M23 Appeals to the UN and Places the City of Uvira Under the “Full and Complete” Responsibility of the International Community
excerpt_en: Uvira DRC, January 16, 2026 —The AFC/M23 rebellion, which controls large areas of North Kivu and South Kivu, announced that it has placed the strategic city of Uvira under the responsibility of the international community. In a letter dated Thursday, January 15, 2026, to UN Secre
body_en:
Uvira DRC, January 16, 2026 —The AFC/M23 rebellion, which controls large areas of North Kivu and South Kivu, announced that it has placed the strategic city of Uvira under the responsibility of the international community. In a letter dated Thursday, January 15, 2026, to UN Secretary-General António Guterres, the group’s political coordinator, Corneille Nangaa, said the move follows the rebels’ withdrawal decision announced on December 15, 2025, recently reaffirmed, and their stated commitment to the ceasefire.
The Rwandan-backed movement said it is immediately withdrawing its “observation and monitoring unit” and declining all responsibility for security in the city.
“With immediate effect, our organization is withdrawing its observation and monitoring unit, which was preparing the transfer of the city to the neutral force, and is declining all responsibility for the security of this important city in South Kivu province. It is now incumbent upon the international community, within the framework of its responsibilities and commitments, to ensure the protection of civilian populations, the maintenance of peace, and the security of all the inhabitants of Uvira, without discrimination,” wrote Corneille Nangaa.
In the same letter, he warned against threats posed by actors not party to the peace agreements, including the Burundian army, the FDLR, the Wazalendo militias, and mercenaries supporting the FARDC, saying their presence could plunge Uvira into chaos and undermine regional peace efforts led by the African Union, Qatar, the United States, and other partners.
“We solemnly draw the international community’s attention to the fact that the Burundian army, the FDLR, the so-called Wazalendo armed groups, and the mercenaries supporting the FARDC pose a clear threat to the city of Uvira. These armed actors are not party to any commitments arising from a peace process. Therefore, their presence and activities represent a direct and immediate threat not only to the civilian population, but also to the ongoing peace process and to regional stability as a whole,” he stated.
He added:
“In this worrying context, it is essential that the international community fully assume its responsibilities and ensure the rapid deployment of a truly neutral force in the city of Uvira, in order to prevent it from descending once again into chaos, devastation, and violence. This initiative demonstrates our firm commitment to protecting civilians, consolidating the ceasefire, and creating the conditions for a lasting peace based on dialogue, respect for international commitments, and the principles of international humanitarian law.”
This initiative comes at a time when, despite the involvement of US President Donald Trump and the apparent acceleration of the Washington process, illustrated by the ratification of agreements by Presidents Félix Tshisekedi and Paul Kagame, the situation on the ground remains fragile. Kinshasa and Kigali continue to struggle to align positions, amid persistent tensions and mutual accusations of failing to uphold commitments made within ongoing diplomatic initiatives.
The same challenges affect the Doha talks, conducted under the auspices of the Emir of Qatar between Kinshasa and the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23, which have yet to yield tangible results on the ground. These negotiations, intended to complement the Washington agreements by addressing root causes such as the restoration of state authority and the reintegration of armed groups, remain stalled. Several agreed measures — including the joint communiqué, the ceasefire mechanism, the declaration of principles, and the framework agreement — have yet to be implemented.
This diplomatic inertia has fueled the continuation of violent clashes between the AFC/M23 and government forces. In addition, the national dialogue called for by several socio-political actors to support these initiatives has not yet been convened.
After announcing its withdrawal from mediation in March 2025, Angola is gradually and discreetly reintegrating into the process. Luanda has relaunched broad consultations, increasing contacts with nearly all stakeholders. Meanwhile, Togo plans to host a high-level meeting on Saturday, January 17, 2026, aimed at strengthening the coherence and consolidation of peace initiatives in the DRC and the Great Lakes region.
It is in this context that João Lourenço, President of Angola and current Chairperson of the African Union, received representatives of the National Episcopal Conference of Congo (CENCO) and the Church of Christ in Congo (ECC) in Luanda. Discussions focused on the need to establish an inclusive national dialogue, bringing together all Congolese stakeholders to achieve lasting peace in the Democratic Republic of Congo. Participants agreed that this process should be launched without delay.
These consultations form part of broader diplomatic efforts to end the armed conflict in eastern DRC, marked by continued fighting between government forces and the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23, according to the United Nations.

excerpt: Burutsi, Walikale January 19, 2026 — The village chief of Burutsi, Mungo Barutsi, was brutally assassinated by unidentified armed men on Sunday, January 18, 2026, in his village located in the Luberike region, in Walikale territory, an area currently controlled by the AFC/M23 reb
title_en: Village Chief Assassinated by Armed Men
excerpt_en: Burutsi, Walikale January 19, 2026 — The village chief of Burutsi, Mungo Barutsi, was brutally assassinated by unidentified armed men on Sunday, January 18, 2026, in his village located in the Luberike region, in Walikale territory, an area currently controlled by the AFC/M23 reb
body_en:
Burutsi, Walikale January 19, 2026 — The village chief of Burutsi, Mungo Barutsi, was brutally assassinated by unidentified armed men on Sunday, January 18, 2026, in his village located in the Luberike region, in Walikale territory, an area currently controlled by the AFC/M23 rebels since April 2025.
The circumstances of the killing remain unclear, but the assailants fled immediately after the attack.
“An investigation is underway to identify the perpetrators and establish responsibility,” local authorities stated, while calling on the population to remain calm and vigilant.
This assassination further worsens an already fragile security situation in this part of Walikale, marked by the presence of AFC/M23 rebels. Since their takeover, residents have lived in a climate of fear, with reports of abuses, movement restrictions, and attacks on traditional authorities.
Residents are denouncing a resurgence of targeted violence against community leaders, viewed as symbols of social cohesion and local resistance.
The killing comes just one week after a deadly landslide in Burutsi that claimed 28 lives, plunging the community into a severe humanitarian crisis.
“We hadn’t even finished mourning our dead from the landslide, and now we’ve lost our village chief. It’s too much for one community,” said a resident.
The death of Mungo Barutsi has sparked strong emotions, with calls for urgent civilian protection, security for customary authorities, and independent investigations to ensure that justice is served.

title: Rwanda Confirms Security Coordination with AFC/M23 in Eastern DRC
excerpt: Kinshasa/Washington, January 23, 2026 – For the first time, Rwanda has officially acknowledged coordinating with the AFC/M23 rebel group operating in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Kigali frames this collaboration as a defensive measure, aimed at protecting Tutsi pop
title_en: Rwanda Confirms Security Coordination with AFC/M23 in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa/Washington, January 23, 2026 – For the first time, Rwanda has officially acknowledged coordinating with the AFC/M23 rebel group operating in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Kigali frames this collaboration as a defensive measure, aimed at protecting Tutsi pop
body_en:
Kinshasa/Washington, January 23, 2026 – For the first time, Rwanda has officially acknowledged coordinating with the AFC/M23 rebel group operating in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC). Kigali frames this collaboration as a defensive measure, aimed at protecting Tutsi populations in the region and preventing any resurgence of genocidal violence.
In a statement addressed to the U.S. Congress on January 22, Rwandan Ambassador to the United States Mathilde Mukantabana said the partnership also facilitated the unilateral withdrawal of AFC/M23 forces from the city of Uvira, signaling the rebel group’s commitment to de-escalation.
“Following the escalation, the AFC/M23, with the support of my government, recently carried out a unilateral withdrawal from Uvira, demonstrating its commitment to reducing tensions,” the ambassador said.
Mukantabana outlined the framework of the collaboration, emphasizing that while Rwanda and AFC/M23 share a common interest in protecting Tutsi communities from the FDLR and other armed groups, Rwanda’s involvement is strictly defensive, conditional, and temporary. She stressed that Rwanda does not seek to influence the internal politics of the DRC.
The statement also recalled the historical context of insecurity in the region, including the legacy of the Abacengezi insurgency and the FDLR, responsible for massacres since 1994. “The memory of genocide survivors, the graves of a million victims, and the documented history of the Abacengezi insurgency compel us to maintain defensive capabilities until credible security guarantees are established,” the ambassador noted.
Kigali further assured that cooperation with AFC/M23 will gradually end once security conditions improve and the FDLR are neutralized, in line with agreements brokered through the Washington peace process.

title: Ambassador Gen. Maj. Nzabamwita Presents Credentials to President Putin
excerpt: Rwanda’s Ambassador to the Russian Federation, Gen. Maj. Joseph Nzabamwita, has formally presented his credentials to President Vladimir Putin, conveying a message from President Paul Kagame. The ceremony took place at the Kremlin Presidential Palace on January 15, 2026, alongsid
title_en: Ambassador Gen. Maj. Nzabamwita Presents Credentials to President Putin
excerpt_en: Rwanda’s Ambassador to the Russian Federation, Gen. Maj. Joseph Nzabamwita, has formally presented his credentials to President Vladimir Putin, conveying a message from President Paul Kagame. The ceremony took place at the Kremlin Presidential Palace on January 15, 2026, alongsid
body_en:
Rwanda’s Ambassador to the Russian Federation, Gen. Maj. Joseph Nzabamwita, has formally presented his credentials to President Vladimir Putin, conveying a message from President Paul Kagame.
The ceremony took place at the Kremlin Presidential Palace on January 15, 2026, alongside 31 other ambassadors accredited to Russia. Senior Russian officials in attendance included Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Head of the Presidential Administration Yuri Ushakov.
Ambassador Nzabamwita officially assumed his duties on April 22, 2025, after presenting copies of his credentials to Deputy Foreign Minister Mikhail Bogdanov. He succeeds Lt. Gen. (Rtd) Frank Mushyo Kamanzi, who concluded his mission on February 4, 2024.
In his address, President Putin underscored that Russia’s foreign policy is grounded in mutual respect, adherence to international law, and the promotion of inclusive governance. He reaffirmed the importance of Russia’s relations with Africa, describing them as based on mutually beneficial cooperation.
“A large number of ambassadors from friendly African countries are present today, including representatives from Rwanda, Somalia, Gabon, Senegal, Mauritania, Algeria, Ghana, and Namibia,” President Putin said. “Russia maintains constructive relations with all African countries through cooperation, assistance, and partnership. We are committed to expanding political, economic, and humanitarian ties.”
He recalled Russia’s historical role in supporting African countries’ paths to independence and development, and noted ongoing commitments made during the Russia–Africa Summits in Sochi and Saint Petersburg, as well as the Africa–Russia Foreign Ministers’ Summit held in Cairo in 2025, with another summit planned for this year.
Following the ceremony, Ambassador Nzabamwita delivered President Kagame’s message to President Putin and held separate discussions with Foreign Minister Sergey Lavrov and Yuri Ushakov, reaffirming their commitment to sustained dialogue.
The talks focused on strengthening the longstanding relations between Rwanda and Russia, which date back to 1963 and have steadily expanded over the years. Presidents Kagame and Putin previously held bilateral discussions during the Russia–Africa Summits in 2018 and 2019.
Bilateral cooperation continues to grow in several sectors, including nuclear technology, where Russia is supporting Rwanda’s efforts to develop nuclear energy, and education, with hundreds of Rwandan students currently studying at Russian universities.
The Rwandan Embassy in Russia reiterated its commitment to deepening these ties and expanding cooperation across the political, economic, social, cultural, commercial, and tourism sectors.

title: RDB Raises Alarm Over Surge in Poaching at Volcanoes National Park
excerpt: Kigali, January 18, 2026 — The Rwanda Development Board (RDB) has expressed serious concern over the sharp increase in poaching at Volcanoes National Park, warning that the trend threatens both wildlife conservation and national development. According to RDB figures, the number o
title_en: RDB Raises Alarm Over Surge in Poaching at Volcanoes National Park
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 18, 2026 — The Rwanda Development Board (RDB) has expressed serious concern over the sharp increase in poaching at Volcanoes National Park, warning that the trend threatens both wildlife conservation and national development. According to RDB figures, the number o
body_en:
Kigali, January 18, 2026 — The Rwanda Development Board (RDB) has expressed serious concern over the sharp increase in poaching at Volcanoes National Park, warning that the trend threatens both wildlife conservation and national development.
According to RDB figures, the number of animal traps has risen steadily in recent years. In 2023, about 2,200 traps were recorded, increasing to over 2,300 in 2024, and reaching 2,336 by October 2025, compared to just 446 in 2019.
The Commander of the 505th Brigade operating in Musanze, Gakenke, and Burera Districts, Col. Steven Kayigumire, said poaching has become widespread and costly for the country.
“There is a serious problem of poaching, and it is causing significant losses. If we are not vigilant, we could lose more than 500 million Rwf,” he warned.
The Director of Conservation at Rwanda Parks, Ngoga Télesphore, also expressed concern, noting that poaching is increasing despite ongoing efforts to support communities around the park.
“It is worrying that people who benefit from the park are involved in its destruction. The rate of poaching in the last 10 months is higher than in the previous year,” he said.
While the causes of the increase are still under investigation, authorities have called on the public to actively participate in conservation efforts.
“Those who understand the benefits of the park should help sensitize others to respect and protect it. Everyone should be an eye for their neighbor,” Télesphore added.
The Governor of the Northern Province, Mugabowagahunde Maurice, said the issue is being addressed by multiple institutions, describing the situation as alarming.
Authorities revealed that in 2025, six gorillas were caught in poachers’ traps. The most affected sectors include Kinigi with over 800 traps, Bugeshi with more than 500, Kabatwa with over 300, and Gataraga with 287.
So far, 38 poachers have been arrested and imprisoned for activities that endanger wildlife. Local leaders and residents say the exact causes of the surge remain unclear but confirm that measures are being taken to address the problem.

excerpt: Ruhango, Rwanda – January 19, 2026 – The Rwanda National Police (RNP) have arrested a 60-year-old woman and her 26-year-old son on suspicion of killing her husband and the young man’s father, Birasamasha Donath, aged 70. The incident occurred on January 19, 2026, in Kivomo Villag
title_en: Mother and Son Arrested on Suspicion of Killing Family Patriarch
excerpt_en: Ruhango, Rwanda – January 19, 2026 – The Rwanda National Police (RNP) have arrested a 60-year-old woman and her 26-year-old son on suspicion of killing her husband and the young man’s father, Birasamasha Donath, aged 70. The incident occurred on January 19, 2026, in Kivomo Villag
body_en:
Ruhango, Rwanda – January 19, 2026 – The Rwanda National Police (RNP) have arrested a 60-year-old woman and her 26-year-old son on suspicion of killing her husband and the young man’s father, Birasamasha Donath, aged 70.
The incident occurred on January 19, 2026, in Kivomo Village, Murama Cell, Bweramana Sector, Ruhango District.
According to preliminary information, the woman allegedly asked her son to help her kill the victim following a family dispute, reportedly over property. Responders found Birasamasha’s body covered in blood at the scene.
The RNP Southern Province spokesperson, Chief Inspector of Police (CIP) Kamanzi Hassan, said that local authorities confirmed the family had an ongoing property conflict.
“It is true, it is suspected that this 70-year-old man was killed by his wife and child. The two were immediately arrested and detained at the Kabagari Police Station while investigations continue,” he said.
CIP Kamanzi urged residents to avoid domestic conflicts, promote a culture of dialogue, and seek support from family members, mediators, and local authorities when disputes arise.
The victim’s body was taken to Gitwe Hospital for an autopsy.
Under Rwandan law, intentional homicide is a criminal offense punishable by life imprisonment if convicted.

title: AFC/M23 Hands Over Uvira to International Forces
excerpt: The AFC/M23 coalition fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has announced that it has handed over the city of Uvira to the international community, calling on it to ensure the safety of residents. On December 16, 2025, AFC/M23 said it would withdraw its fighters from th
title_en: AFC/M23 Hands Over Uvira to International Forces
excerpt_en: The AFC/M23 coalition fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has announced that it has handed over the city of Uvira to the international community, calling on it to ensure the safety of residents. On December 16, 2025, AFC/M23 said it would withdraw its fighters from th
body_en:
The AFC/M23 coalition fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has announced that it has handed over the city of Uvira to the international community, calling on it to ensure the safety of residents.
On December 16, 2025, AFC/M23 said it would withdraw its fighters from the city. Two days later, the group claimed it had withdrawn, though the DRC government denied this.
In a letter to the United Nations Secretary-General dated January 15, 2026, AFC/M23 stated that it had requested three days earlier that the UN Mission in the DRC (MONUSCO) protect the city’s population. The request was addressed to the Special Representative of the UN Secretary-General for the DRC and Acting Head of MONUSCO, Vivian Van de Perre.
“Our community, AFC/M23, has decided today to place the city of Uvira under the full responsibility of the international community,” said AFC/M23 leader Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo.
Nangaa explained that the city had been temporarily occupied by a group of AFC/M23 fighters tasked with monitoring the area while awaiting the arrival of an impartial military force, but that they too had withdrawn on January 15.
AFC/M23 informed the United Nations that the Burundian army, the FDLR terrorist group, Wazalendo groups, and the Cancuru are threatening the security of Uvira’s residents.
“Their presence and activities are not only a threat to the security of civilians, but also to the ongoing peace process and the security of the region,” the group said.
The coalition urged the international community to urgently deploy neutral forces to Uvira to prevent a repeat of the suffering experienced when the city was under DRC government control.
AFC/M23 captured Uvira on December 9, 2025, after a week-long battle in parts of the Ruzizi Valley in South Kivu Province. It said the withdrawal was made at the request of the United States to allow peace talks to continue. According to the group, the U.S. asked it to return to its former positions, within 75 kilometers of Uvira, assuring that only then could the international community ensure the protection of civilians.
When the UN Security Council voted to extend MONUSCO’s mandate for another year, it assigned the mission new responsibilities, including monitoring the peace process in South Kivu Province, suggesting that troops may soon be deployed to Uvira.
Twirwaneho Shoots Down DRC Army Drone
The MRDP-Twirwaneho armed group fighting the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has announced that it has shot down one of the DRC army drones, which it accuses of targeting Banyamulenge civilians in South Kivu Province.
Twirwaneho’s spokesman, Col. Kamasa Ndakize Welcome, said that on January 15, 2026, forces from the DRC, Burundi, the FDLR, and Wazalendo groups carried out attacks in the Point-Zéro area, located about 10 kilometers from Minembwe commune.
“This operation included ground and drone attacks, which deliberately targeted residents of the Rwitsankuku center and surrounding areas, destroying civilian infrastructure, forcing residents to flee, and putting the lives of innocent civilians in grave danger,” Col. Kamasa said.
He added that these attacks prompted Twirwaneho fighters to intervene, shoot down the coalition’s drone, and capture key areas, including Mount Baruta, which he said had long been used by opposing forces.
“In response to these actions, MRDP-Twirwaneho fighters immediately moved to defend civilians, shot down the enemy drone that was firing on civilian areas, repelled the ground attack, destroyed enemy positions, and captured key areas, including Mount Baruta, which had long been used to fire at civilians,” he said.
Twirwaneho declared that it would not tolerate the atrocities committed by the coalition of DRC government forces and said it would continue to fulfill its duty to protect civilians and their property.

excerpt_en: Uvira, DRC – January 21, 2026 – More than 1,000 Congolese Tutsi fled Uvira town after the AFC/M23 coalition withdrew its fighters. A local civil society member reported that between January 19 and 20, FDLR, DRC, and Wazalendo forces abducted residents and took them to unknown loc
body_en:
Uvira, DRC – January 21, 2026 – More than 1,000 Congolese Tutsi fled Uvira town after the AFC/M23 coalition withdrew its fighters.
A local civil society member reported that between January 19 and 20, FDLR, DRC, and Wazalendo forces abducted residents and took them to unknown locations.
Over 300 Tutsi families sought refuge in the Kamanyola Center in Walungu Territory, under AFC/M23 control. Spokesperson Lawrence Kanyuka added that more than 200 Banyamulenge families relocated from Kamanyola Town.
Attempts by some residents to reach the highlands connecting Uvira, Fizi, and Mwenga Territories were blocked by Wazalendo fighters. While those in Kamanyola are reportedly safe, many remain worried for relatives still in Uvira.

title: Qatar Backs Togo’s Initiative to Consolidate Peace Process in Eastern DRC
excerpt: Lomé, January 18, 2026 – The State of Qatar, a key mediator in the crisis between the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the AFC/M23 rebellion, has reaffirmed its commitment to the peace process, viewing Togo’s diplomatic initiative as proof of sustained mom
title_en: Qatar Backs Togo’s Initiative to Consolidate Peace Process in Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: Lomé, January 18, 2026 – The State of Qatar, a key mediator in the crisis between the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the AFC/M23 rebellion, has reaffirmed its commitment to the peace process, viewing Togo’s diplomatic initiative as proof of sustained mom
body_en:
Lomé, January 18, 2026 – The State of Qatar, a key mediator in the crisis between the government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) and the AFC/M23 rebellion, has reaffirmed its commitment to the peace process, viewing Togo’s diplomatic initiative as proof of sustained momentum toward stability in the Great Lakes region.
Qatar took part in a high-level meeting on the coherence and consolidation of peace efforts in the DRC and the wider region, held in Lomé, the capital of Togo. The country was represented by Ahmed Essa Al Sulaiti, advisor to the Minister of State at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs.
Discussions focused on the humanitarian crisis, regional security coordination, de-escalation mechanisms, support for humanitarian operations, and the promotion of economic integration. The meeting followed the signing of the Doha Peace Framework between the Congolese government and the Congo River Alliance (M23 Movement), underscoring continued diplomatic engagement despite the lack of immediate breakthroughs.
Although no new peace initiatives were announced, participants agreed to strengthen African mediation in 2026, relying on five former African heads of state as co-facilitators. Diplomatic missions are planned in the coming days to Kinshasa, Kigali, Kampala, and Gitega to accelerate the implementation of commitments made by the parties.
The final communiqué urged all sides to implement their commitments in good faith, prioritize peaceful conflict resolution, and reaffirmed full support for the Doha process. It also called for the rapid resumption of negotiations on the six remaining protocols and emphasized the need for structured African monitoring of the peace agreements.
With the 39th African Union Summit scheduled for February 11–15, 2026, in Addis Ababa, the Togolese mediator for eastern DRC, Faure Essozimna Gnassingbé, is expected to present a report on the evolving security situation and mediation progress, in line with recent African Union Peace and Security Council decisions.
This diplomatic push comes as the Doha talks, led by the Emir of Qatar, continue to face challenges in translating negotiations into concrete results on the ground. The talks aim to complement the Washington agreements by addressing the root causes of the conflict, including the restoration of state authority and the reintegration of armed groups, but progress remains slow despite the signing of five key instruments.

title: Walikale Faces Severe Shortage of Medicines and Nutritional Products Amid Ongoing Conflict
excerpt: Walikale, North Kivu, January 20, 2026 – Health authorities in Walikale territory are grappling with a critical shortage of medicines and nutritional products, affecting approximately 197,420 residents across Pinga and surrounding health zones. The crisis, exacerbated by the ongo
title_en: Walikale Faces Severe Shortage of Medicines and Nutritional Products Amid Ongoing Conflict
excerpt_en: Walikale, North Kivu, January 20, 2026 – Health authorities in Walikale territory are grappling with a critical shortage of medicines and nutritional products, affecting approximately 197,420 residents across Pinga and surrounding health zones. The crisis, exacerbated by the ongo
body_en:
Walikale, North Kivu, January 20, 2026 – Health authorities in Walikale territory are grappling with a critical shortage of medicines and nutritional products, affecting approximately 197,420 residents across Pinga and surrounding health zones. The crisis, exacerbated by the ongoing conflict between Congolese government forces and the AFC/M23 rebellion, as well as other armed groups, has left local health facilities struggling to provide basic care.
According to a December 2025 UN OCHA report, clashes along the Kalembe-Mpeti-Pinga axis have displaced thousands. On December 6, fighting in Chanjikiro (Kisimba group) triggered mass population movements, while on December 12, residents of Kateku—more than 6,300 people—were forced to flee, seeking refuge in nearby villages such as Kimaka, Miriki, Buleusa, Kayna, and Kanyabayonga.
“This part of the Pinga health zone remains isolated due to physical and security access constraints, limiting the presence and mobility of humanitarian actors,” the report noted. The Pinga General Referral Hospital (HGR) and other local health facilities face acute shortages of essential medicines and nutritional supplies, severely impacting patient care.
OCHA highlighted that the departure of humanitarian partner MEDAIR in April 2025, combined with geographic isolation, has compounded the delivery challenges, leaving residents without consistent medical assistance.
The escalation of violence in North and South Kivu since early 2025 has displaced hundreds of thousands, killed hundreds, and injured thousands, worsening an already dire humanitarian situation. Blocked roads and insecurity continue to hinder aid delivery, despite ongoing efforts by humanitarian organizations to negotiate safe access and provide emergency support.
“The population urgently needs rapid, unimpeded, and safe humanitarian access. All obstacles to aid delivery must be removed,” OCHA emphasized.
Despite high-level mediation initiatives, including the US-led Washington process and Qatar’s role in negotiations with the AFC/M23, on-the-ground conditions remain precarious. Humanitarian and political observers are calling on all parties to uphold their commitments under peace agreements to silence the guns and allow nearly three decades of conflict to end.

title: Haut-Lomami: Suspected Bakata Katanga Attack Leaves at Least Eight Dead in Bukama
excerpt: Bukama, January 12, 2026 – An attack attributed to suspected Bakata Katanga militiamen left at least eight people dead on Sunday, January 11, in the territory of Bukama, Haut-Lomami province. According to local authorities, six militiamen and two civilians were killed, while seve
title_en: Haut-Lomami: Suspected Bakata Katanga Attack Leaves at Least Eight Dead in Bukama
excerpt_en: Bukama, January 12, 2026 – An attack attributed to suspected Bakata Katanga militiamen left at least eight people dead on Sunday, January 11, in the territory of Bukama, Haut-Lomami province. According to local authorities, six militiamen and two civilians were killed, while seve
body_en:
Bukama, January 12, 2026 – An attack attributed to suspected Bakata Katanga militiamen left at least eight people dead on Sunday, January 11, in the territory of Bukama, Haut-Lomami province.
According to local authorities, six militiamen and two civilians were killed, while several others were wounded during clashes that erupted as FARDC reinforcements were passing through a public area near a market. Civilians were reportedly struck by stray bullets during the exchange of fire.
The clashes lasted for about one hour, involving soldiers who had just arrived from the Kamina military base and armed elements linked to the Bakata Katanga movement. Another FARDC reinforcement unit, composed of around 60 soldiers, was also targeted.
Authorities indicated that military reinforcements were deployed not only in Bukama but also in other territories of Haut-Lomami, including Kabongo, following rising insecurity. Information about the troop movements is believed to have circulated in advance, contributing to the ambush.
The army later confirmed the attack on one of its units, identifying the assailants as members of a group calling itself Mai-Mai Zulu, and reported four militiamen killed and one soldier wounded.

title: AFC/M23 Reaches Lemera, Symbolic Village in the Uvira Highlands
excerpt: Lemera DRC, January 16, 2026 —Despite calls for a ceasefire between government forces and the AFC/M23 rebellion in North and South Kivu, military operations continue on the ground. In this context, AFC/M23 rebels entered Lemera, in the Bafuliro chiefdom, Uvira territory highlands
title_en: AFC/M23 Reaches Lemera, Symbolic Village in the Uvira Highlands
excerpt_en: Lemera DRC, January 16, 2026 —Despite calls for a ceasefire between government forces and the AFC/M23 rebellion in North and South Kivu, military operations continue on the ground. In this context, AFC/M23 rebels entered Lemera, in the Bafuliro chiefdom, Uvira territory highlands
body_en:
Lemera DRC, January 16, 2026 —Despite calls for a ceasefire between government forces and the AFC/M23 rebellion in North and South Kivu, military operations continue on the ground. In this context, AFC/M23 rebels entered Lemera, in the Bafuliro chiefdom, Uvira territory highlands, South Kivu, on Thursday, January 15.
Rebel columns were observed early in the morning, following violent clashes with the Wazalendo (local inhabitants) in this strategic village.
According to local sources, the rebels advanced through several villages, including Kaziba, Langala, and Rubanga, to reach Lemera. “The rebels crossed Langala and Rubanga before splitting into two groups. One headed towards Kidote and the other towards Nakandongo,” a civil society source reported. This account is corroborated by multiple sources in the region.
Lemera, located about 30 kilometers from Bwegera, just beyond Luvungi off National Route 5 (RN5), lies along a corridor that passes through Kiringye, Namutiri, Rubanga, Bwesho, and Kidote.
The village holds strong symbolic importance in Uvira territory, as it once hosted the AFDL rebellion’s military training center. For many observers, the capture of Lemera could open the way toward Mulenge and Katala, in the Uvira highlands.
Lemera is also significant for having hosted the original site of Panzi Hospital, where Dr. Denis Mukwege, 2018 Nobel Peace Prize laureate, served as medical director in 1996.

The village holds strong symbolic importance in Uvira territory, as it once hosted the AFDL rebellion’s military training center. For many observers, the capture of Lemera could open the way toward Mulenge and Katala, in the Uvira highlands.
Lemera is also significant for having hosted the original site of Panzi Hospital, where Dr. Denis Mukwege, 2018 Nobel Peace Prize laureate, served as medical director in 1996.

excerpt_en: Nyiragongo, Goma and Karisimbi, North Kivu January 19, 2026 — In December alone, more than 3,380 cases of gender-based violence were recorded in the health zones of Nyiragongo, Goma, and Karisimbi, worsening the critical shortage of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) kits. A humanit
body_en:
Nyiragongo, Goma and Karisimbi, North Kivu January 19, 2026 — In December alone, more than 3,380 cases of gender-based violence were recorded in the health zones of Nyiragongo, Goma, and Karisimbi, worsening the critical shortage of post-exposure prophylaxis (PEP) kits.
A humanitarian report on North Kivu, particularly in the Nyiragongo territory and the city of Goma, indicates that the security situation remained generally calm, despite brief clashes reported between December 9 and 14 in the villages of Ngangi and Kiziba.
The report highlights that women and girls remain particularly vulnerable to sexual violence, especially when traveling to Virunga National Park to collect food and firewood.
In December, humanitarian partners documented more than 3,380 cases of gender-based violence, a situation aggravated by a critical shortage of PEP kits, the main gap in care for survivors of sexual violence in North Kivu.
For the period from December 2025 to February 2026, the unmet need amounts to 20,484 kits. While support enabled the resupply of 23 out of 34 health zones, 11 zones remain completely without kits.
Since the beginning of 2025, the escalation of the conflict and intensified attacks by the Rwandan-backed AFC/M23 in North and South Kivu have displaced hundreds of thousands of people, worsening an already critical humanitarian crisis. The violence has left hundreds dead and thousands wounded, while blocked roads and insecurity continue to hinder humanitarian access.
Despite these conditions, humanitarian actors continue providing emergency medical care, food assistance, and other life-saving aid, while negotiating access to affected areas. Many voices are now calling on all stakeholders to respect their commitments and take concrete steps to silence the guns and restore peace after nearly three decades of conflict.

title: DRC – U.S. Africa Command Explores Security Cooperation with FARDC
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 23, 2026 – U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM) visited the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) on January 22 to explore opportunities for enhanced security cooperation, reflecting a growing strategic rapprochement between Kinshasa and Washington.
title_en: DRC – U.S. Africa Command Explores Security Cooperation with FARDC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 23, 2026 – U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM) visited the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) on January 22 to explore opportunities for enhanced security cooperation, reflecting a growing strategic rapprochement between Kinshasa and Washington.
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 23, 2026 – U.S. Africa Command (AFRICOM) visited the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) on January 22 to explore opportunities for enhanced security cooperation, reflecting a growing strategic rapprochement between Kinshasa and Washington.
Colonel Michael Gacheru, head of the AFRICOM delegation, praised the FARDC’s willingness to collaborate, stating, “This visit demonstrates our unwavering support for the FARDC and the DRC government,” and underscoring efforts to promote peace through strengthened military cooperation. The discussions also included Congolese Generals Jules Banza Mwilambwe and Marcel Lukwikila.
The visit coincides with recent peace agreements between the DRC and Rwanda and bilateral economic accords with the United States. As part of this evolving framework, a memorandum of understanding on defense and security was signed to deepen cooperation, particularly in training, equipping forces, and protecting critical infrastructure.
To date, the U.S. Embassy has supported professional training programs for the FARDC, as well as initiatives to train and equip police officers and construct police stations. Officials note that a similar military cooperation protocol was signed in 2020, though its implementation had been limited, signaling that current efforts aim to build on and expand past agreements.

title: 15 January 2026; Rwanda and Luxembourg Discuss Financial Cooperation

body_en:
Rwandan Ambassador to Luxembourg, Munyangaju Aurore Mimosa, has held discussions with Luxembourg’s Minister of Finance, Gilles Roth, on strengthening financial cooperation between the two countries.
In a statement, Ambassador Munyangaju said the talks focused on deepening bilateral financial ties and reinforcing the strong partnership between Rwanda and Luxembourg.
Ambassador Munyangaju arrived in Luxembourg on February 25, 2025, and officially presented her credentials on March 20, 2025.
The two countries already maintain strong cooperation. In 2024, the governments of Rwanda and Luxembourg signed a €12 million funding agreement to address the impacts of climate change.
In October 2021, both countries also signed a cooperation agreement aimed at promoting the development of the Kigali International Financial Centre, particularly in human resource development, operational capacity building, and positioning the center at an international level.
Rwanda and Luxembourg further cooperate through agreements targeting anti-smuggling efforts and tax evasion prevention.

title: Rwanda Introduces Demerit Point System for Drivers; Cross-Border Drivers Exempt
excerpt: Kigali, January 14, 2026 — Rwanda is set to implement a new electronic demerit point system to monitor drivers’ behavior on the roads, but drivers of cross-border vehicles will not be affected. According to Alfred Byiringiro, Senior Technical Advisor in charge of transport at the
title_en: Rwanda Introduces Demerit Point System for Drivers; Cross-Border Drivers Exempt
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 14, 2026 — Rwanda is set to implement a new electronic demerit point system to monitor drivers’ behavior on the roads, but drivers of cross-border vehicles will not be affected. According to Alfred Byiringiro, Senior Technical Advisor in charge of transport at the
body_en:
Kigali, January 14, 2026 — Rwanda is set to implement a new electronic demerit point system to monitor drivers’ behavior on the roads, but drivers of cross-border vehicles will not be affected.
According to Alfred Byiringiro, Senior Technical Advisor in charge of transport at the Ministry of Infrastructure, the system will apply only to driving licenses issued in Rwanda and those issued abroad but held by permanent residents. Drivers temporarily transiting through Rwanda, such as those transporting goods across borders, will not be registered in the system.
“We have drivers who transit Rwanda temporarily, making multiple trips with cross-border vehicles. It is not possible to register these people. However, if someone chooses to stay in Rwanda, their license is registered and the points system is applied,” Byiringiro explained.
The new law, pending presidential approval, will be accompanied by a ministerial decree defining traffic offenses, penalties, and the number of points deducted for each violation.
Key provisions of the system include:
Every licensed driver starts with 15 points, which are deducted depending on the severity of offenses.
Minor offenses may result in 2 to 6 points being deducted, while serious offenses such as hit-and-run may incur an additional six-point penalty.
Points are reset annually, with deductions applied for offenses committed during the year.
If a driver cannot be immediately identified, points will be assigned to the vehicle number and applied to the driver once identified.
Drivers with suspended or revoked licenses are prohibited from driving in Rwanda, even with a foreign-issued license. Suspended licenses are reinstated after the period expires, while revocations are carried out by a court upon request from road safety authorities.
Byiringiro noted that the government hopes neighboring countries will adopt similar systems to harmonize cross-border road safety regulations.

title: Kabila’s Party Vice President Aubin Minaku Arrested in Kinshasa
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 18, 2026 — Security forces in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have arrested Aubin Minaku, the Vice President of former President Joseph Kabila’s PPRD party, during a late-night operation at his home in Kinshasa. The authorities have not disclosed the reas
title_en: Kabila’s Party Vice President Aubin Minaku Arrested in Kinshasa
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 18, 2026 — Security forces in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have arrested Aubin Minaku, the Vice President of former President Joseph Kabila’s PPRD party, during a late-night operation at his home in Kinshasa. The authorities have not disclosed the reas
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 18, 2026 — Security forces in the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have arrested Aubin Minaku, the Vice President of former President Joseph Kabila’s PPRD party, during a late-night operation at his home in Kinshasa.
The authorities have not disclosed the reason for his arrest, but it comes amid ongoing accusations by the Tshisekedi administration against former figures of the Kabila regime, who are suspected of supporting the AFC/M23 coalition.
On March 7, 2025, the DRC government announced that senior leaders of the PPRD were suspected of working with AFC/M23, which is fighting the DRC government. Following these accusations, several PPRD leaders were arrested after President Félix Tshisekedi accused Joseph Kabila of backing the group — claims the PPRD has denied.
Those implicated include the PPRD Permanent Secretary, Emmanuel Ramazani Shadary, the Vice President, Aubin Minaku, and the Deputy Permanent Secretary, Ferdinand Kambere.
The location of Minaku’s detention remains unknown. Sources said his residence was surrounded by FARDC special forces at the time of his arrest.
The PPRD has not yet issued a statement regarding the arrest.
The development follows the recent arrest and detention of Emmanuel Ramazani Shadary, who is being held at an undisclosed location.
This comes as part of broader legal actions against senior PPRD leaders, after the Military Court tried Joseph Kabila in absentia, accusing him of treason and collaboration with AFC/M23, and sentenced him to death.
