title: Why Soldiers and Youth Are Fleeing Burundi in Large Numbers
excerpt: Bujumbura, January 19, 2026 – Burundi, one of the world’s poorest countries, appears to have reached a breaking point, as growing numbers of soldiers and young people flee the country amid worsening economic hardship and political disillusionment. Although President Évariste Nday
title_en: Why Soldiers and Youth Are Fleeing Burundi in Large Numbers
excerpt_en: Bujumbura, January 19, 2026 – Burundi, one of the world’s poorest countries, appears to have reached a breaking point, as growing numbers of soldiers and young people flee the country amid worsening economic hardship and political disillusionment. Although President Évariste Nday
body_en:
Bujumbura, January 19, 2026 – Burundi, one of the world’s poorest countries, appears to have reached a breaking point, as growing numbers of soldiers and young people flee the country amid worsening economic hardship and political disillusionment.
Although President Évariste Ndayishimiye took office in June 2020 promising economic recovery, his administration has overseen a sharp deterioration in living conditions, with poverty levels now worse than during the last period of relative stability.
At the center of the crisis is an agreement with President Félix Tshisekedi to deploy Burundian troops to fight the AFC/M23 coalition in the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC). The deployment has resulted in soldier casualties, prolonged salary delays, and widespread demoralization within the armed forces.
As a result, many soldiers have deserted, fleeing to countries such as Zambia, Mozambique, and even parts of Asia. The government has responded with tightened border controls and has imprisoned immigration officials accused of issuing passports to deserters.
Meanwhile, Burundian youth are leaving the country in growing numbers, citing lack of employment opportunities, which many say are reserved for members of the ruling CNDD-FDD party. Numerous students have dropped out of school, believing that education offers little value without political affiliation.
In early 2025, school dropout rates reportedly reached 70% in some regions. In the former Kayanza province, more than 4,500 students left school in just three months during the 2024–2025 academic year.
According to the United Nations High Commissioner for Refugees (UNHCR), the number of Burundian refugees in Rwanda increased by 1,721 between 2024 and 2025. As of December 31, 2025, Rwanda was hosting 52,961 Burundian refugees, representing 38.5% of the total refugee population in the country.
Across cities such as Kigali, Kampala, and Nairobi, Burundian youth are now working as street vendors and small traders, sending remittances home that often exceed the salaries of government employees in Burundi.
One young Burundian vendor in Nairobi said he earns about 3,000 Kenyan shillings per month, equivalent to more than 150,000 Burundian francs (Fbu), which he sends to his family. “It is small, but it helps them survive,” he said.
Despite the exodus of soldiers and youth, President Ndayishimiye continues to publicly claim that no country is as rich or blessed as Burundi — a statement many critics see as evidence of the regime’s disconnect from the daily struggles of its citizens.
The growing flight of human capital, observers warn, threatens to further undermine Burundi’s social stability and economic future.

title: ICGLR Defense Ministers’ Meeting: DRC Presses for Peace and Tests Regional Credibility
excerpt: Livingstone, January 12, 2026 – The Defense Ministers of ICGLR member states met in an extraordinary session on January 10 in Livingstone, Zambia, to address the humanitarian and security crisis in eastern DRC and across the Great Lakes region, amid ongoing fighting between gover
title_en: ICGLR Defense Ministers’ Meeting: DRC Presses for Peace and Tests Regional Credibility
excerpt_en: Livingstone, January 12, 2026 – The Defense Ministers of ICGLR member states met in an extraordinary session on January 10 in Livingstone, Zambia, to address the humanitarian and security crisis in eastern DRC and across the Great Lakes region, amid ongoing fighting between gover
body_en:
Livingstone, January 12, 2026 – The Defense Ministers of ICGLR member states met in an extraordinary session on January 10 in Livingstone, Zambia, to address the humanitarian and security crisis in eastern DRC and across the Great Lakes region, amid ongoing fighting between government forces and the AFC/M23 rebellion.
The meeting followed earlier sessions of the ICGLR Specialized Committee of Defense Experts and the Chiefs of Staff, the body responsible for overseeing the Non-Aggression Protocol.
A central focus was the performance of the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism (EJVM), tasked with monitoring and investigating security incidents in the region. The mechanism has faced challenges, including irregular meetings and limited reporting, prompting chiefs of staff to draft recommendations for defense ministers.
The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, stressed that peace cannot be delayed or subordinated to political calculations, calling for regional mechanisms to become credible, operational, and deterrent to protect civilians and end cycles of violence.
He placed particular emphasis on the effective operationalization of the Expanded Joint Verification Mechanism Plus (EJVM+), describing it as a test of credibility for both the ICGLR and the region as a whole.
During the session, ministers officially installed the new commander and deputy commander of the EJVM, based in Goma, reinforcing the regional security framework.
The new roadmap prioritizes the implementation of the Washington and Doha processes, especially the ceasefire mechanism signed on October 14, 2025, between the Congolese government and the AFC/M23 under Qatari mediation. However, implementation on the ground remains difficult, largely because the verification and monitoring mechanism is not yet fully operational.
Revitalizing the EJVM is therefore seen as essential to ensuring effective ceasefire monitoring and restoring the credibility of ongoing peace efforts.

title: Artisanal Copper and Cobalt Mining Resumes After Tensions

title_en: Artisanal Copper and Cobalt Mining Resumes After Tensions
excerpt_en: Lualaba, DRC January 15, 2026 – Artisanal mining activities in Lualaba province have resumed following recent clashes between miners and security forces, signaling a return to calm at several mining sites. According to local sources, the entire artisanal mining chain is now opera
body_en:
Lualaba, DRC January 15, 2026 – Artisanal mining activities in Lualaba province have resumed following recent clashes between miners and security forces, signaling a return to calm at several mining sites.
According to local sources, the entire artisanal mining chain is now operational. Chinese partners, mining cooperatives, and around fifteen processing companies have resumed activities, effectively ending the previous shutdown.
This resumption comes while the commission established by Minister of Mines Louis Watum Kabamba has yet to submit its final report. The commission, headed by Franck Fwamba, is tasked with verifying the legality of companies processing mineral substances from artisanal copper and cobalt mining.
Several institutional actors and stakeholders in Lualaba participated in the commission’s work, including Georges Nyembo Kitungwa, provincial director of SAEMAPE, the provincial director of the Mines Division, Petit Ngombe, and the president of the association of mining cooperatives, alongside representatives of civil society, the provincial government, security services, and other relevant organizations.
Following its visit to Lualaba, the commission is currently meeting in Haut-Katanga province to address similar issues related to artisanal mining there.
While mining activities have resumed, sector stakeholders are awaiting the official conclusions of the mission, which could shape future regulation of artisanal mining in the provinces concerned.

title: Three Police Officers Sentenced for Inciting Theft in Viral Song Case
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 22, 2026 – Three police officers, Sindani, Kabamba, and Kiadi, authors of the controversial song “Zua ye tshombo tika ye akende” (“Take his phone and let him go”), have been sentenced to three years of hard labor by the Kinshasa/Ndjili Garrison Military Court. T
title_en: Three Police Officers Sentenced for Inciting Theft in Viral Song Case
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 22, 2026 – Three police officers, Sindani, Kabamba, and Kiadi, authors of the controversial song “Zua ye tshombo tika ye akende” (“Take his phone and let him go”), have been sentenced to three years of hard labor by the Kinshasa/Ndjili Garrison Military Court. T
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 22, 2026 – Three police officers, Sindani, Kabamba, and Kiadi, authors of the controversial song “Zua ye tshombo tika ye akende” (“Take his phone and let him go”), have been sentenced to three years of hard labor by the Kinshasa/Ndjili Garrison Military Court. The officers were also ordered to pay court costs of 200,000 Congolese francs.
The sentencing follows a summary hearing on Tuesday, January 20, 2026, in which the court examined the conduct of five officers from the Congolese National Police (PNC) implicated in the case.
The court found Sindani, Kabamba, and Kiadi guilty of insubordination, citing the viral video as evidence. In the footage, several visibly intoxicated officers performed the song in unison outside a Kinshasa police station, prompting national outrage.
One officer, Kasongo, was acquitted of failing to report a crime due to insufficient evidence, while another, Tuzolana, received a suspended sentence of twelve months of hard labor for the same offense.
According to observers on social media, the song highlighted what many perceive as lax recruitment and discipline practices within the police force, raising concerns over officers who are entrusted with public protection but sometimes act as perpetrators of abuse.
The ruling serves as a rare instance of accountability for police misconduct in the DRC, sending a signal that public incitement to criminal acts by law enforcement personnel will not be tolerated.

excerpt_en: Masisi, January 14, 2026 --A relative calm returned Wednesday morning, January 14, 2026, in Kalembe, located in the Bashali Mokoto group of Masisi territory, North Kivu, following overnight clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and the Wazalendo. Reports indicate that the Wazalendo laun
body_en:
Masisi, January 14, 2026 --A relative calm returned Wednesday morning, January 14, 2026, in Kalembe, located in the Bashali Mokoto group of Masisi territory, North Kivu, following overnight clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and the Wazalendo.
Reports indicate that the Wazalendo launched simultaneous attacks around 8:00 p.m., aiming to dislodge the rebels from the town they have occupied for over a year. Loud explosions from heavy weapons were heard, forcing many to remain indoors. The human toll from these clashes is currently unknown.
The town continues to host several displaced families fleeing insecurity in surrounding areas. Recent weeks in the Kalembe region have seen repeated clashes, causing mass displacement and looting of residents’ property, with the most recent major incident reported on December 24, 2025.

title: AFC/M23 Completes Withdrawal from Uvira, Places City Under International Responsibility
excerpt: Uvira, DRC, January 17, 2026 — The AFC/M23 armed group announced on Saturday, January 17, 2026, that it has completed its withdrawal from the city of Uvira in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, where elements of its military and administrative presence had remained. The moveme
title_en: AFC/M23 Completes Withdrawal from Uvira, Places City Under International Responsibility
excerpt_en: Uvira, DRC, January 17, 2026 — The AFC/M23 armed group announced on Saturday, January 17, 2026, that it has completed its withdrawal from the city of Uvira in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, where elements of its military and administrative presence had remained. The moveme
body_en:
Uvira, DRC, January 17, 2026 — The AFC/M23 armed group announced on Saturday, January 17, 2026, that it has completed its withdrawal from the city of Uvira in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, where elements of its military and administrative presence had remained.
The movement had previously announced the withdrawal on January 15, following its seizure of the city in early December, the second largest city in South Kivu province. While most fighters and equipment had already left, reports indicated a residual presence in the city.
On Saturday, a column of fighters in military fatigues, with weapons slung over their shoulders and helmets on, exited the city. Some were on foot, while others traveled aboard trucks. Weapons, including rocket launchers, were visible. Observers counted at least 200 fighters, believed to be the group’s “observation and surveillance unit.”
The AFC/M23 officially declared that it now places Uvira under the full responsibility of the international community, declining all responsibility for the security of the city and its approximately 500,000 residents.
Despite the withdrawal, gunfire, including rocket fire, was reported in the vicinity of Uvira on Saturday morning, leaving local residents with heightened anxiety as the day ended.
This development occurs amid ongoing efforts by the international community, including the African Union, the United States, and regional partners, to stabilize eastern DRC and ensure the protection of civilians following months of armed conflict and territorial disputes.

title: MSF Responds to Surge in Wounded Amid Escalating Violence
excerpt: Nyanzale, Rutshuru January 23, 2026 - Doctors Without Borders (MSF) has raised the alarm over an influx of wounded in Nyanzale, following intensified clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo militias, part of the Collective of Movements for Change (CMC), in Rutshuru territory
title_en: MSF Responds to Surge in Wounded Amid Escalating Violence
excerpt_en: Nyanzale, Rutshuru January 23, 2026 - Doctors Without Borders (MSF) has raised the alarm over an influx of wounded in Nyanzale, following intensified clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo militias, part of the Collective of Movements for Change (CMC), in Rutshuru territory
body_en:
Nyanzale, Rutshuru January 23, 2026 - Doctors Without Borders (MSF) has raised the alarm over an influx of wounded in Nyanzale, following intensified clashes between AFC/M23 rebels and Wazalendo militias, part of the Collective of Movements for Change (CMC), in Rutshuru territory, North Kivu.
Since January 20, MSF teams have been supporting the Nyanzale health center, providing medical and logistical assistance to 32 people injured by bullets and shrapnel, most of them civilians.
According to patient testimonies, the wounded began arriving on January 19 after an attack by Wazalendo militiamen. Civilians performing community work, locally called “salogo,” were caught in the crossfire. Several homes were reported burned during the violence.
MSF is also carrying out humanitarian support, including the construction of toilets, distribution of drinking water, and health promotion in vulnerable areas. The organization warns that the affected population is living in precarious conditions, with limited access to hygiene, adequate shelter, food, and basic necessities.
The security situation in Nyanzale remains tense. Fighting resumed Sunday afternoon, January 19, after a brief lull, with intense crossfire reported throughout the area. Civilians who had recently returned from displacement barricaded themselves in their homes for safety.
The Wazalendo faction of the CMC denounced a bomb attack on January 18 that struck several localities, including Nyarubande, Burambo, Muhanga, the center of Kihondo, and Kiyeye, and vowed swift retaliation. Further clashes were reported near Katsiru.
The provisional toll from the violence includes two civilians killed in Kihondo—a man and a woman—and ten houses burned in Nyarubande, Bwito chiefdom.
The situation underscores the persistent vulnerability of civilians in North Kivu amid ongoing armed clashes, highlighting the urgent need for humanitarian assistance and protection.

title: Rwanda and Oman Sign Four Strategic Cooperation Agreements
excerpt: Kigali/Muscat, January 12, 2026 — Rwanda and the Sultanate of Oman on Monday signed four cooperation agreements aimed at strengthening bilateral ties across key sectors, including transport, technology, and innovation, the Omani government announced. The agreements were concluded
title_en: Rwanda and Oman Sign Four Strategic Cooperation Agreements
excerpt_en: Kigali/Muscat, January 12, 2026 — Rwanda and the Sultanate of Oman on Monday signed four cooperation agreements aimed at strengthening bilateral ties across key sectors, including transport, technology, and innovation, the Omani government announced. The agreements were concluded
body_en:
Kigali/Muscat, January 12, 2026 — Rwanda and the Sultanate of Oman on Monday signed four cooperation agreements aimed at strengthening bilateral ties across key sectors, including transport, technology, and innovation, the Omani government announced.
The agreements were concluded following an official visit by a high-level Rwandan delegation to Oman, led by the Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Amb. Olivier Nduhungirehe. The delegation also included the Minister of Technology and Innovation, Paula Ingabire, the Minister of Finance and Economic Planning, Yusuf Murangwa, and the State Minister for Infrastructure at the Ministry of Infrastructure, Eng. Jean de Dieu Uwihanganye.
According to Omani authorities, the accords focus on enhancing cooperation in land ports and freight transport, with both countries set to benefit from joint initiatives aimed at developing logistics and trade infrastructure.
Additional agreements cover the establishment of a large data warehouse, the development of IT infrastructure, and collaboration on projects related to artificial intelligence. Under these frameworks, Rwanda and Oman will jointly build capacity, share expertise, and develop strategies and regulatory frameworks to advance technological innovation.
A separate agreement on air transport will see Oman Air launch direct flights to Kigali starting in June 2026. The airline will operate two non-stop flights per week, marking a significant step in improving connectivity between the two countries.
The fourth agreement, signed between the Rwanda Development Board (RDB) and Oman Airports Company, focuses on air transport development through joint investments, infrastructure development, and the exchange of technical expertise.
Speaking after the signing ceremony, Amb. Nduhungirehe described the agreements as a major milestone in Rwanda–Oman relations, emphasizing their tangible benefits for citizens of both nations.
“Rwanda and Oman share geographical and strategic links through the Indian Ocean, particularly as Rwanda is a member of the East African Community,” he said. “We are committed to implementing these agreements and to signing more in the coming days, all with the goal of delivering real benefits to our people.”
Oman’s Minister of Transport, Communications and Information Technology, Eng. Saeed bin Hamoud Al Maawali, said the agreements align with Oman’s broader strategy to expand cooperation with East Africa.
He added that the accords not only reinforce the strong bilateral relations between Rwanda and Oman but also contribute to shaping a wider framework for cooperation between the Middle East and Africa.

The delegation also included the Minister of Technology and Innovation, Paula Ingabire, the Minister of Finance and Economic Planning, Yusuf Murangwa, and the State Minister for Infrastructure at the Ministry of Infrastructure, Eng. Jean de Dieu Uwihanganye.
According to Omani authorities, the accords focus on enhancing cooperation in land ports and freight transport, with both countries set to benefit from joint initiatives aimed at developing logistics and trade infrastructure.
Additional agreements cover the establishment of a large data warehouse, the development of IT infrastructure, and collaboration on projects related to artificial intelligence. Under these frameworks, Rwanda and Oman will jointly build capacity, share expertise, and develop strategies and regulatory frameworks to advance technological innovation.
A separate agreement on air transport will see Oman Air launch direct flights to Kigali starting in June 2026. The airline will operate two non-stop flights per week, marking a significant step in improving connectivity between the two countries.
The fourth agreement, signed between the Rwanda Development Board (RDB) and Oman Airports Company, focuses on air transport development through joint investments, infrastructure development, and the exchange of technical expertise.

title: Minister Nduhungirehe Calls for Africa-Europe Cooperation Based on Mutual Respect
excerpt: Davos, January 22, 2026 – Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Olivier Nduhungirehe, stressed the need for Africa and Europe to base their partnership on mutual respect rather than the legacy of colonialism, during a Leaders Forum held as part of the World Economic Forum in Davo
title_en: Minister Nduhungirehe Calls for Africa-Europe Cooperation Based on Mutual Respect
excerpt_en: Davos, January 22, 2026 – Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Olivier Nduhungirehe, stressed the need for Africa and Europe to base their partnership on mutual respect rather than the legacy of colonialism, during a Leaders Forum held as part of the World Economic Forum in Davo
body_en:
Davos, January 22, 2026 – Rwanda’s Minister of Foreign Affairs, Olivier Nduhungirehe, stressed the need for Africa and Europe to base their partnership on mutual respect rather than the legacy of colonialism, during a Leaders Forum held as part of the World Economic Forum in Davos, Switzerland.
Nduhungirehe highlighted Europe’s continuing economic strength and importance as a development partner while emphasizing that African nations should move beyond aid-driven relationships toward trade-based cooperation and investment partnerships. He cited Rwanda’s ongoing engagement with the European Union, including a €95 million grant in October 2025 to support vaccine production.
Europe and the Legacy of the Genocide
Addressing Europe’s historical role, Minister Nduhungirehe recalled the continent’s involvement in the 1994 Genocide against the Tutsi, which claimed over a million lives. He pointed to the actions of several European countries:
Belgium for fostering divisions during the colonial era.
France for abandoning Tutsi victims and facilitating the escape of perpetrators.
Other countries that served as refuges for genocide perpetrators.
“Some causes of the genocide stem from the colonial era. Racial discrimination by colonialists left deep scars. Today, Rwanda pursues unity and reconciliation, justice has been served, and we live together in one country,” Nduhungirehe said.
He also highlighted Rwanda’s economic recovery and development, with a focus on trade, investment, and human capital.
Africa’s Growing Role in Global Affairs
On Africa’s role in world governance, Nduhungirehe noted that since the UN’s establishment post-World War II, the continent had little influence. But today, Africa’s population of 1.4 billion, dominated by youth, positions it as a key player on the global stage. He emphasized collaboration with the US, EU, Russia, and China, particularly in modern technologies such as artificial intelligence.
“Africa has natural resources and a young population. With cooperation, finance, and knowledge sharing, we can build a skilled workforce for the future,” he said.
Rwanda-Poland Cooperation as a Model
Nduhungirehe also highlighted Rwanda’s strong partnership with Poland, noting agreements on trade, green technology, education, and security. Both countries have opened embassies in each other’s capitals, and over 1,500 Rwandans currently study in Poland, the largest foreign student group from a single country.
He cited the LuNa Smelter, a Rwandan tin processing plant supported by Polish investment, as an example of effective industrial cooperation.
Looking Forward
Minister Nduhungirehe concluded that Africa-Europe relations must evolve into mutually respectful partnerships, leveraging Africa’s investment potential while addressing internal challenges such as corruption, governance gaps, and youth inclusion.
“Africa has much to offer, but Africans must also take responsibility for their own development,” he said.

title: Karongi District Launches Census of Unemployed Youth
excerpt: Karongi, January 13, 2026 — Authorities in Karongi District have begun a comprehensive census of unemployed youth in a bid to reduce joblessness and improve access to employment opportunities. The announcement was made by the Deputy Mayor in charge of Social Affairs, Pascasie Umu
title_en: Karongi District Launches Census of Unemployed Youth
excerpt_en: Karongi, January 13, 2026 — Authorities in Karongi District have begun a comprehensive census of unemployed youth in a bid to reduce joblessness and improve access to employment opportunities. The announcement was made by the Deputy Mayor in charge of Social Affairs, Pascasie Umu
body_en:
Karongi, January 13, 2026 — Authorities in Karongi District have begun a comprehensive census of unemployed youth in a bid to reduce joblessness and improve access to employment opportunities.
The announcement was made by the Deputy Mayor in charge of Social Affairs, Pascasie Umuhoza, during a ceremony marking the graduation of 20 young people who completed a six-month training program in cooking and meal preparation.
The training, conducted at Bethel Hotel in Rubengera Sector, forms part of the Rwandan government’s broader initiative to equip unemployed youth with practical skills for the labor market.
According to Vice Mayor Umuhoza, the census will record each unemployed person’s educational background to ensure that job opportunities can be matched more effectively to suitable candidates.
“We are enumerating unemployed youth, and this process is ongoing and will be completed soon,” she said. “In about two weeks, we will have a comprehensive list of all unemployed youth in the district.”
The census is being conducted across all 13 sectors of Karongi District.
Sister Marie Louise Niyonsenga, a leader in the Presbyterian Church in Rwanda (EPR), also known as the Servants of Christ, said the training initiative specifically targets youth because of their central role in national development.
“The skills they learned in cooking and meal preparation will help them secure employment or become self-reliant,” she said. “When young people are unemployed, they lose hope and may turn to drugs or prostitution.”
One of the graduates, Liliane Ukwishana from Nyaruguru District, said she enrolled in the program after spending five years studying history, economics, and social sciences without finding employment.
“I have been saving the money they gave us, and I plan to start a restaurant that will create jobs for other young people,” she said. “I will also share the knowledge I have gained here.”
District leaders emphasized that vocational training remains a key strategy for reducing unemployment among school leavers and recent graduates.

title: AFC/M23 Confirms Joseph Kabila Is in the DRC
excerpt: Goma, January 13, 2026 — The leader of the AFC/M23 coalition, Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, has confirmed that former Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) President Joseph Kabila Kabange is currently in the country. Speaking on January 12, 2026, during a meeting between AFC/M23 leaders
title_en: AFC/M23 Confirms Joseph Kabila Is in the DRC
excerpt_en: Goma, January 13, 2026 — The leader of the AFC/M23 coalition, Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, has confirmed that former Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) President Joseph Kabila Kabange is currently in the country. Speaking on January 12, 2026, during a meeting between AFC/M23 leaders
body_en:
Goma, January 13, 2026 — The leader of the AFC/M23 coalition, Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo, has confirmed that former Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) President Joseph Kabila Kabange is currently in the country.
Speaking on January 12, 2026, during a meeting between AFC/M23 leaders and community peace representatives from North Kivu Province, Nangaa announced that Kabila would eventually meet them.
“We have a guest here, the former President of the Republic, Joseph Kabila. Do you know he is here? One day we will bring him to meet you,” Nangaa said. He added that although Kabila holds the constitutional status of senator for life, he was removed from the Senate.
Kabila was last seen publicly in June 2025 in areas under AFC/M23 control, where he reportedly held discussions with citizens from various backgrounds on pathways to restoring peace in the country. During that period, he established a temporary office at his residence in the Kinyogote area, west of Goma.
Following those activities, Kabila was prosecuted in Kinshasa’s High Military Court and sentenced to death in absentia, after being convicted of crimes including treason and membership in an illegal armed group.
After June 2025, Kabila traveled to several African countries, including Kenya, where he founded a political coalition known as “Sauvons le DRC”, aimed at addressing the country’s ongoing political and security challenges.

title: Banyamulenge Flee Uvira for Kamanyola After AFC/M23 Withdrawal

title_en: Banyamulenge Flee Uvira for Kamanyola After AFC/M23 Withdrawal
excerpt_en: Kamanyola, DRC – January 19, 2026 – Members of the Banyamulenge community living in Uvira, South Kivu Province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, have fled to Kamanyola Center in Walungu Territory following the withdrawal of AFC/M23 fighters from the town. The leader of the
body_en:
Kamanyola, DRC – January 19, 2026 – Members of the Banyamulenge community living in Uvira, South Kivu Province in the Democratic Republic of the Congo, have fled to Kamanyola Center in Walungu Territory following the withdrawal of AFC/M23 fighters from the town.
The leader of the Banyamulenge community in Uvira, Muyoboke Ndatabaye, announced on January 18 via the YouTube channel “Agasaro Kaburaga” that the decision was taken due to fears of reprisals from DRC government forces and Wazalendo groups.
According to Ndatabaye, after AFC/M23 announced it would evacuate its remaining fighters from Uvira, members of the Wazalendo militias began sending messages to Banyamulenge residents, threatening to kill them and accusing them of being Rwandans who did not belong in the country.
“On Friday, gangs began to form. You could see people scattered, appearing to organize to harm others. Then yesterday we held a meeting with the population, and I informed them that AFC/M23 had decided to leave the city,” he said.
He added, “After that, people said, ‘We can’t wait any longer for the Wazalendo to attack us,’ so we decided to flee.”
Ndatabaye reported that from the morning of January 18, Banyamulenge homes and their churches were attacked by Wazalendo fighters, with properties destroyed and looted. He confirmed that many families have already fled.
“We are now in Kamanyola. No one has crossed the border. Women, children, and men are sheltering at a school. Those who wish can come and see us. Here we feel safe, even though conditions are difficult. If the Wazalendo remain there, we will continue moving until we reach the border,” he said.
Ndatabaye stated that when AFC/M23 controlled Uvira, the Banyamulenge lived peacefully, noting that prior to that, their security had been threatened by Wazalendo groups. He added that they no longer feel able to coexist with militias they say are supported by the DRC government.

title: Mali | Celebration of the Day of Regained Sovereignty in Kati: A Call for Student Responsibility and Commitment
excerpt: Kati, January 12, 2026 – As part of efforts to strengthen cooperation and the sharing of experiences among the National Committees and Commissions of the AES Confederation, His Excellency Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, held a working se
title_en: Mali | Celebration of the Day of Regained Sovereignty in Kati: A Call for Student Responsibility and Commitment
excerpt_en: Kati, January 12, 2026 – As part of efforts to strengthen cooperation and the sharing of experiences among the National Committees and Commissions of the AES Confederation, His Excellency Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, held a working se
body_en:
Kati, January 12, 2026 – As part of efforts to strengthen cooperation and the sharing of experiences among the National Committees and Commissions of the AES Confederation, His Excellency Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, held a working session on Monday, January 12, 2026, with a delegation from the National Commission of the Confederation of Sahel States of Burkina Faso, led by its President, Bassolma Bazie, during a courtesy and working visit to Mali.
This visit followed the appointment of Captain Ibrahim Traoré, President of Burkina Faso, as head of the AES Confederation, after the inaugural term entrusted to General Assimi Goïta, President of the Transition in Mali.
During fraternal and fruitful discussions, Minister Diop highlighted the challenges encountered in implementing the Confederation, the joint results achieved in applying the roadmap during its first year, the lessons learned from coordinating confederal activities, and the prospects for meeting the aspirations of the people, in line with the shared vision of the three Heads of State.
Given the confederal and ultimately federal nature of the vision, both sides emphasized the priority of meeting the population’s essential needs through concrete actions with a direct impact on living conditions. These include strengthening the free movement of people and promoting socio-economic integration, within a spirit of fraternity, solidarity, pragmatism, shared commitment, and continuity of action.
While acknowledging the significant progress achieved during the first term, the President of the AES Confederation Commission of Burkina Faso requested Mali’s support and assistance to continue the Confederation’s missions under Burkina Faso’s presidency.
Minister Diop stated: “The AES Confederation train has simply changed drivers, but Mali remains on board to reach the agreed destination together.” He concluded by reaffirming the unwavering availability and commitment of the Malian authorities and people to support the shared vision, particularly regarding the security of the Confederation’s territory, the promotion of sustainable development and shared prosperity, within a framework of integration and strengthened diplomacy.
body_fr:
Kati, January 12, 2026 – As part of efforts to strengthen cooperation and the sharing of experiences among the National Committees and Commissions of the AES Confederation, His Excellency Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, held a working session on Monday, January 12, 2026, with a delegation from the National Commission of the Confederation of Sahel States of Burkina Faso, led by its President, Bassolma Bazie, during a courtesy and working visit to Mali.
This visit followed the appointment of Captain Ibrahim Traoré, President of Burkina Faso, as head of the AES Confederation, after the inaugural term entrusted to General Assimi Goïta, President of the Transition in Mali.
During fraternal and fruitful discussions, Minister Diop highlighted the challenges encountered in implementing the Confederation, the joint results achieved in applying the roadmap during its first year, the lessons learned from coordinating confederal activities, and the prospects for meeting the aspirations of the people, in line with the shared vision of the three Heads of State.
Given the confederal and ultimately federal nature of the vision, both sides emphasized the priority of meeting the population’s essential needs through concrete actions with a direct impact on living conditions. These include strengthening the free movement of people and promoting socio-economic integration, within a spirit of fraternity, solidarity, pragmatism, shared commitment, and continuity of action.
While acknowledging the significant progress achieved during the first term, the President of the AES Confederation Commission of Burkina Faso requested Mali’s support and assistance to continue the Confederation’s missions under Burkina Faso’s presidency.
Minister Diop stated: “The AES Confederation train has simply changed drivers, but Mali remains on board to reach the agreed destination together.” He concluded by reaffirming the unwavering availability and commitment of the Malian authorities and people to support the shared vision, particularly regarding the security of the Confederation’s territory, the promotion of sustainable development and shared prosperity, within a framework of integration and strengthened diplomacy.

excerpt: Bamako, January 6, 2026 – Sky Mali, the national airline, has announced the cancellation of multiple flights and schedule changes over the coming days due to severe fuel shortages in the capital. According to airline management, the situation is beyond their control, stemming fro
title_en: Mali | Sky Mali Cancels Flights Amid Fuel Shortages and Rising Insecurity
excerpt_en: Bamako, January 6, 2026 – Sky Mali, the national airline, has announced the cancellation of multiple flights and schedule changes over the coming days due to severe fuel shortages in the capital. According to airline management, the situation is beyond their control, stemming fro
body_en:
Bamako, January 6, 2026 – Sky Mali, the national airline, has announced the cancellation of multiple flights and schedule changes over the coming days due to severe fuel shortages in the capital.
According to airline management, the situation is beyond their control, stemming from logistical constraints in the fuel supply chain. Fuel scarcity in Bamako has been described as a critical issue, with panic buying, black market surges, and prolonged shortages affecting residents and businesses alike.
The crisis has been aggravated by the resurgence of attacks by JNIM jihadists, who control key access points to the capital and had previously disrupted fuel deliveries between September and October 2025. Although a temporary lull occurred following a military council agreement in November 2025, the end of the truce on December 5, 2025, led to renewed attacks on fuel convoys and public transportation.
The capital is currently facing power outages lasting from hours to over a day, limited fuel availability, and widespread insecurity in surrounding areas, including Fana, Kassela, Zantiguila, Kita, and Bougouni.
Sky Mali has pledged to reschedule affected flights and keep passengers informed, emphasizing its commitment to safety, service quality, and transparency. Residents, meanwhile, are struggling with daily disruptions, describing their situation as forced resilience amid energy shortages and rising insecurity.

excerpt_en: Conakry, January 17, 2026 – General Assimi Goïta, President of the Transition in Mali, traveled to Conakry on January 17, 2026, to attend the inauguration ceremony of Guinean President Mamadi Doumbouya, alongside other African heads of state. He was accompanied by a delegation in
body_en:
Conakry, January 17, 2026 – General Assimi Goïta, President of the Transition in Mali, traveled to Conakry on January 17, 2026, to attend the inauguration ceremony of Guinean President Mamadi Doumbouya, alongside other African heads of state.
He was accompanied by a delegation including members of his presidential cabinet and several ministers, notably those of Defense and Veterans Affairs, Economy and Finance, Transport and Infrastructure, and Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation. Mr. Goïta departed Bamako in the morning to attend the event.
The inauguration ceremony of Mamadi Doumbouya, who was elected on December 28, 2025, took place at the 50,000-seat General Lansana Conté Stadium in Nongo, marking the end of the transitional period that began after the 2021 coup.
Among the leaders present were Brice Clotaire Oligui Nguema (Gabon), Bassirou Diomaye Faye (Senegal), Joseph Nyuma Boakai (Liberia), Adama Barrow (Gambia), Julius Maada Bio (Sierra Leone), Mohamed Ould Cheikh El Ghazouani (Mauritania), and Paul Kagame (Rwanda), demonstrating regional support for the inauguration.
According to Guinean authorities, about ten heads of state and international delegations were expected, amid a flurry of diplomatic activity.

body_en:
Nioro du Sahel, Southwestern Mali – For nearly five months, the town of Nioro du Sahel, located on the Mauritanian border, has been under a blockade imposed by JNIM jihadists. The town is effectively cut off from the world, with roads controlled, movement virtually impossible, and kidnappings threatening anyone who attempts to circumvent the encirclement.
Testimonies from residents report a rapid deterioration in living conditions. Basic necessities are becoming scarce, leading to soaring prices in the markets. The price of some food products has nearly doubled, while livestock farming has become unaffordable for many families. Locals say they are barely surviving and are urging the authorities to strengthen security.
Despite the administrative presence of the state and occasional military operations, the blockade persists. Jihadists accuse the population of supporting Malian authorities, further fueling tensions. In Nioro du Sahel, the wait for improvement continues, while isolation and insecurity weigh increasingly on civilians.

title_en: Mali | Record Mining Revenues Exceed 1,000 Billion CFA Francs
excerpt_en: Bamako, January 12, 2026 – Mali has recorded mining revenues of 1,022 billion CFA francs paid to the State, far exceeding initial projections of 400 billion CFA francs. The announcement was made by the President of the Transition, General Assimi Goïta, during the New Year’s greet
body_en:
Bamako, January 12, 2026 – Mali has recorded mining revenues of 1,022 billion CFA francs paid to the State, far exceeding initial projections of 400 billion CFA francs. The announcement was made by the President of the Transition, General Assimi Goïta, during the New Year’s greetings ceremony addressed to Malian civil society.
The results reflect negotiations that led to the recovery of 761 billion CFA francs in arrears from mining companies, an increase of approximately 580 billion CFA francs compared to previous years. These funds were disbursed following a sector audit launched in 2023 and the adoption of a new Mining Code.
The reforms include indexing revenues to world gold prices, replacing fixed payments, and depositing revenues from gold sales in local banks, generating an estimated annual flow of 6 trillion CFA francs for the Malian banking system.

excerpt_en: The Confederation of Sahel States (AES) has condemned the US military intervention in Venezuela, which reportedly led to the capture of President Nicolás Maduro and his wife. In a statement, the AES — comprising Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger — expressed deep concern, describing t
body_en:
The Confederation of Sahel States (AES) has condemned the US military intervention in Venezuela, which reportedly led to the capture of President Nicolás Maduro and his wife.
In a statement, the AES — comprising Burkina Faso, Mali, and Niger — expressed deep concern, describing the operation as the use of armed force against a sovereign state. The organization denounced the action as unacceptable interference and a violation of sovereignty, territorial integrity, and political independence, as enshrined in the Charter of the United Nations.
The Confederation called on the UN Security Council to condemn the US action and to work toward the restoration of international law. It reaffirmed its commitment to multilateralism, sovereign equality of states, and expressed solidarity with the Venezuelan people, whose sovereignty it said had been violated.
This position comes amid mixed international reactions following the operation and the reported capture of Nicolás Maduro in early January, an event criticized by several states as a violation of international law.

excerpt: Bamako, January 11, 2026 – A mission from the Office of the Auditor General is currently examining the management of Moumouni Guindo, former president of the Central Office for Combating Illicit Enrichment (OCLEI), for the period 2021–2025, marking a first for an independent admi
title_en: Mali | Former OCLEI President Moumouni Guindo Under Investigation
excerpt_en: Bamako, January 11, 2026 – A mission from the Office of the Auditor General is currently examining the management of Moumouni Guindo, former president of the Central Office for Combating Illicit Enrichment (OCLEI), for the period 2021–2025, marking a first for an independent admi
body_en:
Bamako, January 11, 2026 – A mission from the Office of the Auditor General is currently examining the management of Moumouni Guindo, former president of the Central Office for Combating Illicit Enrichment (OCLEI), for the period 2021–2025, marking a first for an independent administrative authority.
The allegations concern the creation of an unauthorized office, unexplained travel, telephone expenses included in salary allowances, the funding of private studies, and an attempt to acquire an armored vehicle, which was rejected by the budget department.
Mr. Guindo is accused of failing to fulfill his duties of raising awareness, conducting investigations, and referring cases to the courts, while OCLEI reportedly spent billions of CFA francs without any significant impact on public finances.
His commitment is described as being more focused on individual harassment than on the public interest, with a final annual report compiling previous data highlighting shortcomings.
His mandate ended on May 31, 2025, after eight years, and a request for a nine-month extension was rejected by the Prime Minister.
This audit is presented as a step toward improving the ethical standards of public officials in the fight against illicit enrichment.

title_en: Mali | Over Accusations of Subversion and Glorifying Terrorism
excerpt_en: Bamako, January 16, 2026 – Mali has taken a radical decision. On January 16, 2026, the Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralization, Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, signed a decree banning the dissemination, distribution, and sale of the Jeune Afrique newspaper thro

Bamako, January 16, 2026 – Mali has taken a radical decision. On January 16, 2026, the Minister of Territorial Administration and Decentralization, Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, signed a decree banning the dissemination, distribution, and sale of the Jeune Afrique newspaper throughout the country.
The drastic measure, effective immediately, cites serious grounds, including accusations of subversion and the glorification of terrorism following articles concerning hydrocarbon supplies. Malian authorities also allege the outlet made “unfounded” accusations, displayed a blatant lack of journalistic objectivity, deliberate bias, and incitement to hatred in its coverage of sensitive topics.
The decision specifically mentions allegations of abuses committed against the authorities and armed forces of member countries of the Confederation of Sahel States. Anyone violating the provisions of the decree is subject to the penalties stipulated by Malian law.

Conclusion
The situation in Mali is characterized by a deepening divide between official state rhetoric of "recovered sovereignty" and a deteriorating reality of economic paralysis and widespread insecurity. While the transitional government celebrates diplomatic milestones and record mining revenues, the civilian population faces a critical energy crisis and escalating violence from multiple armed factions.
1. Geopolitical and Diplomatic Shift
The government has intensified its "paradigm shift" toward absolute national sovereignty, focusing on the defense of Malian interests and the strategic choice of partners like China. This period was marked by:

title: Mali | Kal Akal 2025 Annual Report Highlights Worsening Human Rights Situation in Azawad
excerpt: Kidal, January 13, 2026 – The Kal Akal Association’s 2025 annual report paints an extremely worrying picture of the human rights situation in the Azawad region. Based on corroborated and verified information, the report highlights widespread and systematic violence perpetrated ag
title_en: Mali | Kal Akal 2025 Annual Report Highlights Worsening Human Rights Situation in Azawad
excerpt_en: Kidal, January 13, 2026 – The Kal Akal Association’s 2025 annual report paints an extremely worrying picture of the human rights situation in the Azawad region. Based on corroborated and verified information, the report highlights widespread and systematic violence perpetrated ag
body_en:
Kidal, January 13, 2026 – The Kal Akal Association’s 2025 annual report paints an extremely worrying picture of the human rights situation in the Azawad region. Based on corroborated and verified information, the report highlights widespread and systematic violence perpetrated against civilian populations.
A total of 573 cases of summary executions and airstrikes were recorded, indiscriminately targeting women, children, and the elderly, particularly in markets and during community gatherings. Additionally, there were 276 cases of abduction, enforced disappearance, and torture, particularly affecting community leaders, which has severely undermined social cohesion and local governance.
The humanitarian consequences are considerable: more than 210 mass displacements, destruction of livelihoods and vital infrastructure, as well as 117 cases of looting and destruction of civilian property. Environmental degradation and restricted access to essential resources further exacerbate the population’s vulnerability. Despite their limited number, the documented cases of sexual violence have lasting consequences for victims and their communities.
Kal Akal concludes that 2025 will be among the darkest years in Azawad’s recent history, marked by the collapse of the social fabric, chronic insecurity, and profound collective trauma. In response, the organization reaffirms its commitment to documenting violations, strengthening the protection of vulnerable populations, and intensifying its actions in 2026 to promote resilience and provide support for victims.

body_en:
Mali, January 11, 2026 – The General Staff of the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) reported the results of operations conducted nationwide on January 11, 2026.
As part of a territorial surveillance mission, FAMa air assets carried out strikes against three armed terrorist groups:
The first strike, west of Bebelin and south of the Kekoro forest in the Dioïla region, neutralized approximately ten terrorists and destroyed several motorcycles.
The second strike, southeast of Tinkeleni in Dioïla, successfully neutralized several terrorists and destroyed dozens of motorcycles.
The third strike, east of Kidal, targeted a vehicle belonging to armed terrorist groups containing explosives.
Additionally, the Malian Armed Forces thwarted an ambush set by an armed terrorist group in Léré, Timbuktu region, resulting in the neutralization of several terrorists and the recovery of a significant quantity of weapons, ammunition, and motorcycles.

title_en: President Assimi Goïta Gives Instructions to Mali’s New Ambassador to Geneva(Koulouba, Bamako, January 5, 2026)
excerpt_en: The President of the Transition, General Assimi Goïta, received the new Malian Ambassador to Geneva, Sékou dit Gaoussou Cissé, on Monday, January 5, 2026, at the Koulouba Palace. The meeting aimed to provide the diplomat with strategic instructions for the effective defense of Ma
body_en:
The President of the Transition, General Assimi Goïta, received the new Malian Ambassador to Geneva, Sékou dit Gaoussou Cissé, on Monday, January 5, 2026, at the Koulouba Palace. The meeting aimed to provide the diplomat with strategic instructions for the effective defense of Mali’s interests in Switzerland.
Previously Director for Europe at the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, Mr. Cissé will now represent Mali in Geneva.
After the audience, he stated that the Head of State had delivered clear directives, emphasizing that Malian diplomacy is grounded in three constitutional principles: sovereignty, choice of partners, and defense of the interests of the Malian people.
Mr. Cissé also highlighted the cultural and identity dimension of the country’s ongoing restructuring, noting that the President called for promoting the Year of Culture so that every Malian feels fully integrated and enriched by diversity.
The President further reaffirmed the importance of protecting Malians’ interests across all institutions and urged full engagement in the Confederation of Sahel States (CSA), described as a framework forging its own path, free from external influence and aligned with the aspirations of its people.
Addressing upcoming challenges, the ambassador cited international communication as a priority, stressing the need to inform bilateral and multilateral partners accurately, counter disinformation, and clearly explain Mali’s choices.
He concluded by affirming that Mali’s decisions are not directed against anyone, but taken in the interest of the Malian people, and pledged to defend Mali’s interests firmly, loyally, and clearly in a shifting geopolitical landscape.

excerpt: Bamako, January 2026 Minister of Communication, Digital Economy, and Administrative Modernization, Alhamdou Ag Ilyène, held a press conference to officially launch the third edition of Digital Week, now scheduled for January 29–31, 2026 due to a busy institutional agenda. This ed
title_en: Launch of the Third Edition of Digital Week in Mali
excerpt_en: Bamako, January 2026 Minister of Communication, Digital Economy, and Administrative Modernization, Alhamdou Ag Ilyène, held a press conference to officially launch the third edition of Digital Week, now scheduled for January 29–31, 2026 due to a busy institutional agenda. This ed
body_en:
Bamako, January 2026
Minister of Communication, Digital Economy, and Administrative Modernization, Alhamdou Ag Ilyène, held a press conference to officially launch the third edition of Digital Week, now scheduled for January 29–31, 2026 due to a busy institutional agenda.
This edition focuses on the theme: “E-Government in the Age of Artificial Intelligence: Opportunities and Challenges for Culture”, highlighting the Malian authorities’ commitment to digital technology as a strategic lever for sovereignty, administrative modernization, and resilience.
The minister emphasized that artificial intelligence is crucial for transforming public services and cultural industries, and that digital technology is now an essential pillar of public performance and citizen inclusion.
Burkina Faso and Niger will participate as guest countries of honor, under the framework of the Confederation of Sahel States, promoting harmonization of digital policies, e-government strategies, and exchange on AI, cybersecurity, and digital identity.
The program includes a ministerial roundtable, thematic discussions on AI, digital public services, artistic creation, ICT financing, and digital identity, and a national digital innovation competition showcasing startups, project leaders, and public services.
The minister called on youth, innovators, and the private sector to make this edition a moment of collective mobilization to build a sovereign, inclusive, and forward-looking digital Mali.

body_en:
Malian lawmaker Mahamadou Hawa Gassama has reportedly been sentenced to five years in prison in Ivory Coast.
A member of Mali’s National Transitional Council (CNT), Gassama was brought before the criminal court of the Abidjan-Plateau Court of First Instance following proceedings initiated by the investigating judge. He was scheduled to appear before the court on Friday, January 9, 2026.
Gassama was arrested in Ivory Coast on July 2, 2025, after previously making remarks deemed insulting toward the Ivorian state and President Alassane Ouattara. He was detained after traveling to the country following those statements.

body_en:
Bamako, January 5, 2026
On Monday, January 5, 2026, the Ministry of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation held its official New Year’s greetings ceremony for staff, addressed to His Excellency Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation.
The ceremony included speeches by the President of the Association of Women in Foreign Affairs, the Secretary General of the Free Union of Foreign Affairs, and the Secretary General of the Ministry, followed by remarks and greetings from Minister Abdoulaye Diop.
The event provided an opportunity to review the achievements of 2025 and to hold frank and constructive discussions on staff working conditions, paving the way for renewed commitment to strengthening Malian diplomacy in 2026.
Minister Diop welcomed the results achieved through teamwork and paid tribute to diplomatic and consular staff, the women of the department, and retirees for their dedication, commitment, and patriotism, which have enhanced Mali’s international influence.
He also addressed the improvement of working conditions and the effectiveness of diplomatic action, particularly through the updating of outdated documents to better respond to the country’s current challenges.
In conclusion, Abdoulaye Diop urged staff to redouble their efforts with honor, dignity, and professionalism to meet the challenges of 2026 and further strengthen Malian diplomacy, extending his wishes for peace, happiness, and prosperity to all employees, their families, and the nation.

title: Cooperation within the ESA | Mali Reaffirms Support for Burkina Faso’s Presidency of the Confederation
excerpt: Bamako, January 12, 2026 – As part of efforts to strengthen cooperation and share experiences among the ESA National Committees and Commissions of the Confederation’s member states, His Excellency Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, held a w
title_en: Cooperation within the ESA | Mali Reaffirms Support for Burkina Faso’s Presidency of the Confederation
excerpt_en: Bamako, January 12, 2026 – As part of efforts to strengthen cooperation and share experiences among the ESA National Committees and Commissions of the Confederation’s member states, His Excellency Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, held a w
body_en:
Bamako, January 12, 2026 – As part of efforts to strengthen cooperation and share experiences among the ESA National Committees and Commissions of the Confederation’s member states, His Excellency Abdoulaye Diop, Minister of Foreign Affairs and International Cooperation, held a working meeting on Monday, January 12, 2026, with a delegation from the National Commission of the Confederation of Sahel States of Burkina Faso, led by its President, Bassolma Bazie, during a courtesy and working visit to Mali.
This visit followed the appointment of Captain Ibrahim Traoré, President of Burkina Faso, as head of the ESA Confederation, after the inaugural term entrusted to General Assimi Goïta, President of the Transition in Mali.
During fraternal and fruitful discussions, Minister Diop highlighted the challenges encountered in implementing the Confederation, the joint results achieved in applying the roadmap during its first year, the lessons learned from coordinating confederal activities, and the prospects for meeting the aspirations of the people, in line with the shared vision of the three Heads of State.
Given the confederal and ultimately federal nature of the vision, both sides emphasized the priority of meeting the population’s essential needs through concrete actions with a direct impact on living conditions. These include strengthening the free movement of people and promoting socio-economic integration, within a spirit of fraternity, solidarity, pragmatism, shared commitment, and continuity of action.
While acknowledging the significant progress achieved during the first term, the President of the ESA Confederation Commission of Burkina Faso requested Mali’s support and assistance to continue the Confederation’s missions under Burkina Faso’s presidency.
Minister Diop stated: “The ESA Confederation train has simply changed drivers, but Mali remains on board to reach the agreed destination together.” He concluded by reaffirming the unwavering availability and commitment of the Malian authorities and people to support the shared vision, particularly regarding the security of the Confederation’s territory, the promotion of sustainable development and shared prosperity, within a framework of integration and strengthened diplomacy.

title: Mali | 4th National Day of Restored Sovereignty Celebrated Across the Country and Abroad
excerpt: Bamako, January 14, 2026 – Mali marked the 4th National Day of Restored Sovereignty on Wednesday, January 14, 2026, a historic occasion celebrating the mobilization of the Malian people to assert their sovereignty and reject sanctions deemed illegitimate. The commemoration featur
title_en: Mali | 4th National Day of Restored Sovereignty Celebrated Across the Country and Abroad
excerpt_en: Bamako, January 14, 2026 – Mali marked the 4th National Day of Restored Sovereignty on Wednesday, January 14, 2026, a historic occasion celebrating the mobilization of the Malian people to assert their sovereignty and reject sanctions deemed illegitimate. The commemoration featur
body_en:
Bamako, January 14, 2026 – Mali marked the 4th National Day of Restored Sovereignty on Wednesday, January 14, 2026, a historic occasion celebrating the mobilization of the Malian people to assert their sovereignty and reject sanctions deemed illegitimate. The commemoration featured a series of official, social, and educational activities nationwide and within the diaspora.
In Bamako, the Minister of Health and Social Development, Colonel-Major Assa Badiallo Touré, presented a significant donation of medicines to the Kalaban-Coro Reference Health Center (CSRéf). The equipment included birthing kits, feminine hygiene kits, modern stretchers, and essential injections and tablets, aimed at improving the quality of care and access to healthcare services.
In Nioro du Sahel, the Minister of Livestock and Fisheries, Youba Ba, joined local authorities, school officials, and students in the celebrations, highlighting the government’s emphasis on civic education and patriotism among youth. The day began with a flag-raising ceremony at Kaïmé School, followed by the singing of the national anthem in Bambara and a history lecture for ninth-grade students on the recovery of sovereignty.
The minister and his delegation later visited Maison Rose, where a large crowd continued the celebrations in an atmosphere of patriotic unity and social cohesion.
In Dakar, Senegal, the Minister for Malians Abroad and African Integration, Mossa Ag Attaher, celebrated the day with the Malian community and nationals from other African and Southern African countries, presiding over a flag-raising ceremony and leading a conference on the origin and significance of the historic day.
In Bamako, the Prime Minister, Major General Abdoulaye Maïga, delivered the official commemorative address, calling for national unity and highlighting progress since 2022, particularly the strengthening of state sovereignty and trust between the people and their leaders.
In Timbuktu, the Minister of National Entrepreneurship, Employment, and Training, Oumou Sall Seck, participated in festivities that began on January 13, involving children in educational workshops on sovereignty, and presenting them with symbolic gifts.
The 4th edition of the National Day of Reclaimed Sovereignty was marked by a spirit of patriotism, solidarity, and collective responsibility, reflecting the commitment of the Malian authorities and people to build a sovereign, stable, and prosperous Mali.

title_en: Mali | MSF Reports on Malian Army Strikes in Dogofry

body_en:
Dogofry, Ségou region, January 6, 2026 – Following an airstrike that hit the market in Dogofry, in the Sokolo district, teams from MSF and the Ministry of Health treated 54 wounded people. Of these, 24 were transferred to the hospital in Niono and 30 to the Dogofry community health center.
The majority of the wounded were children and women, including a pregnant woman who lost her child in the attack. Patients presented with fractures, cervical wounds, and signs of pneumothorax, requiring intensive care in the surgical ward in Niono.
Attacks against civilians have been frequent in the region, notably on December 29 and January 3, particularly in the K2 area, where about ten people were wounded.

title: Over 20 Houses Destroyed in Kazumba Following Ethnic Conflict
excerpt: Kazumba, Kasai-Central | December 29, 2025 More than twenty homes were set ablaze overnight from Sunday to Monday in the village of Bena-Bilala, Kazumba Territory, according to local sources. The incident is linked to an ethnic conflict triggered by the death of a local resident.
title_en: Over 20 Houses Destroyed in Kazumba Following Ethnic Conflict
excerpt_en: Kazumba, Kasai-Central | December 29, 2025 More than twenty homes were set ablaze overnight from Sunday to Monday in the village of Bena-Bilala, Kazumba Territory, according to local sources. The incident is linked to an ethnic conflict triggered by the death of a local resident.
body_en:
Kazumba, Kasai-Central | December 29, 2025
More than twenty homes were set ablaze overnight from Sunday to Monday in the village of Bena-Bilala, Kazumba Territory, according to local sources. The incident is linked to an ethnic conflict triggered by the death of a local resident.
The victim, Muyaya Mbombo, a man in his forties, died on Saturday after reportedly consuming excessive alcohol. His family, believing he had been murdered, retaliated by setting fire to surrounding homes, destroying more than twenty thatched houses and two corrugated iron structures, according to Jean-Carré Muyaya, coordinator of the New Congolese Society in Kazumba.
“This tragedy began with Muyaya Mbombo’s celebrations on December 25. Two days later, he drank excessively and died behind the houses of the villagers. His family assumed foul play and set fire to more than twenty houses,” explained Jean-Carré Muyaya.
Calm has been temporarily restored thanks to the intervention of the National Police, but many residents have fled to the bush, fearing further reprisals.
Local authorities are being urged to strengthen security in the area, and calls have been made for the perpetrators to be brought to justice. The incident highlights a resurgence of insecurity in the region, fueled by misunderstandings and ethnic tensions.

title: Two Police Officers Convicted for the Murder of Dr. Emmanuel Nawej in Kolwezi
excerpt: Kolwezi, Lualaba Province, January 5, 2026 — Two officers of the Congolese National Police (PNC) have been convicted for the murder of Dr. Emmanuel Dibu Nawej, who died in police custody in Kolwezi, the capital of Lualaba province. The verdict was delivered last weekend following
title_en: Two Police Officers Convicted for the Murder of Dr. Emmanuel Nawej in Kolwezi
excerpt_en: Kolwezi, Lualaba Province, January 5, 2026 — Two officers of the Congolese National Police (PNC) have been convicted for the murder of Dr. Emmanuel Dibu Nawej, who died in police custody in Kolwezi, the capital of Lualaba province. The verdict was delivered last weekend following
body_en:
Kolwezi, Lualaba Province, January 5, 2026 — Two officers of the Congolese National Police (PNC) have been convicted for the murder of Dr. Emmanuel Dibu Nawej, who died in police custody in Kolwezi, the capital of Lualaba province. The verdict was delivered last weekend following several public hearings.
In total, five defendants—including four police officers and one civilian—were prosecuted on charges of violations of individual rights and freedoms and acts of torture. At the end of the trial, two police officers were found guilty.
Benathar Christian Mwisange was sentenced to 24 months of forced labor, while Virginie Mujinga Kadima received a 12-month sentence. The court also ordered the two convicts to pay the civil party damages equivalent to 25,000 US dollars, in Congolese francs.
The three remaining defendants, including two police officers and one civilian, were acquitted due to insufficient evidence.
In addition, the court ordered the burial of Dr. Emmanuel Nawej, nearly two months after his death, and the release of his remains to his family.
Background
Dr. Emmanuel Dibu Nawej died during the night of November 9–10, 2025, while being held in a cell at the Kolwezi Operations Coordination Center. He had been arrested following a minor traffic incident, in which his vehicle reportedly grazed that of a police officer near a supermarket.
His death sparked public outrage, with witnesses and the provincial coordinator of the National Human Rights Commission (CNDH), Arthur Kabulo, describing the circumstances as highly suspicious and calling for a thorough and transparent investigation.
On November 11, dozens of doctors took to the streets of Kolwezi to protest Dr. Nawej’s death, demanding justice and the prosecution of those responsible.

title: Burundi: Congolese Refugees in Dire Conditions Following Uvira-Fizi Clashes
excerpt: Bujumbura, Burundi – January 2, 2026 A recent report highlights the extreme living conditions of Congolese refugees who fled the ongoing conflict between AFC/M23 rebels in the Uvira and Fizi territories of the DRC. Since arriving in Burundi on December 10, 2025, these refugees ha
title_en: Burundi: Congolese Refugees in Dire Conditions Following Uvira-Fizi Clashes
excerpt_en: Bujumbura, Burundi – January 2, 2026 A recent report highlights the extreme living conditions of Congolese refugees who fled the ongoing conflict between AFC/M23 rebels in the Uvira and Fizi territories of the DRC. Since arriving in Burundi on December 10, 2025, these refugees ha
body_en:
Bujumbura, Burundi – January 2, 2026
A recent report highlights the extreme living conditions of Congolese refugees who fled the ongoing conflict between AFC/M23 rebels in the Uvira and Fizi territories of the DRC.
Since arriving in Burundi on December 10, 2025, these refugees have been hosted in transit camps at Rugombo, Rumonge, and Gatumba, where they are enduring severe poverty and lack of basic necessities.
Mapenzi Manyebwa, a representative of the refugees, described the situation:
“In Gatumba, Congolese refugees spent the New Year in anguish, as most could not afford clothes or gifts for their children. We live in unsanitary conditions, and many lack food. It was in this suffering and stress that the majority of Congolese refugees spent the holidays.”
Despite the dire circumstances, Manyebwa expressed gratitude for the opportunity to begin a new year, even amidst hardship.
Aid has been minimal, limited to isolated individual interventions, leaving the majority of refugees without adequate support.
The UNHCR in Burundi is currently resettling refugees in Ruhigi province, approximately 60 km north of Bujumbura, in an effort to improve their living conditions.

excerpt: Irumu, Ituri, January 7, 2026 — Approximately 70% of residents who fled ADF (Allied Democratic Forces) attacks in recent months have returned to their villages along National Route 4, on the Komanda–Luna axis in the Irumu territory of Ituri province. The latest wave of returnees,
title_en: Joint FARDC–UPDF Operations Enable Return of Displaced Persons to Irumu
excerpt_en: Irumu, Ituri, January 7, 2026 — Approximately 70% of residents who fled ADF (Allied Democratic Forces) attacks in recent months have returned to their villages along National Route 4, on the Komanda–Luna axis in the Irumu territory of Ituri province. The latest wave of returnees,
body_en:
Irumu, Ituri, January 7, 2026 — Approximately 70% of residents who fled ADF (Allied Democratic Forces) attacks in recent months have returned to their villages along National Route 4, on the Komanda–Luna axis in the Irumu territory of Ituri province.
The latest wave of returnees, primarily from Eringeti, Oicha, Beni, and Butembo in North Kivu, arrived on Tuesday, January 6, in Ndalya and Otmaber, in the Walese Vonkutu chiefdom.
Local human rights activists credit the improved security situation, resulting from joint operations by the FARDC and the UPDF, for enabling this return. The rehabilitation of National Route 4 and increased military patrols have made movement safer. Christophe Munyanderu, an activist monitoring the situation, said:“People are returning by motorcycle or car. The reopening of the RN4 national highway and the easing of violence are facilitating their return, thanks to strengthened security measures.”
The return of displaced populations will allow residents to resume agricultural activities and strengthen their resilience following past crises. Joint security efforts are being praised for their role in stabilizing the area and enabling communities to rebuild their livelihoods.
body_fr:

title: Angolan and Qatari Foreign Ministers Discuss Rwanda-DRC Peace Efforts

title_en: Angolan and Qatari Foreign Ministers Discuss Rwanda-DRC Peace Efforts
excerpt_en: Doha/Luanda – 10 January 2026: The Foreign Ministers of Angola and Qatar held talks on resolving ongoing issues between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) through peaceful means. According to a statement from the Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Sheikh Mohammed
body_en:
Doha/Luanda – 10 January 2026: The Foreign Ministers of Angola and Qatar held talks on resolving ongoing issues between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) through peaceful means.
According to a statement from the Qatari Ministry of Foreign Affairs, Sheikh Mohammed bin Abdulrahman bin Jassim Al Thani, Qatar’s Prime Minister and Foreign Minister, spoke by phone with Angolan Foreign Minister Tete Antonio. The discussions focused on peaceful conflict resolution and strengthening international cooperation between the two nations.
The statement emphasized that Qatar supports resolving disputes through dialogue and in accordance with international law to restore peace and security.
Since the deterioration of Rwanda-DRC relations, Qatar has played an active role in mediation. It was first mentioned in reconciliation talks in January 2023, and in March 2025, it helped facilitate meetings between President Paul Kagame of Rwanda and President Félix Tshisekedi of the DRC.
The Qatari-led peace process contributed to the signing of a bilateral peace agreement in Washington, D.C., in December 2025, and Qatar continues to maintain communication between the DRC government and the AFC/M23 rebel movement, which remains in active conflict with the DRC army.

body_en:
Kigali, January 1, 2026
The Rwanda Investigation Bureau (RIB) has confirmed the arrest of journalist Ndahiro Emmanuel, also known as ‘Taikun’, following an incident at a New Year concert organized by the City of Kigali at the Kigali Convention Centre.
According to RIB, Ndahiro allegedly assaulted a security guard, causing injury, property damage, and using threatening language. He is currently being held at the RIB Kimihurura Station while investigations continue.
Dr. Murangira B. Thierry, spokesperson for RIB, emphasized that under Rwandan law, anyone who intentionally injures or assaults another person may face imprisonment and fines. Penalties vary depending on the severity of the injury:
Minor injuries: 6 months to 1 year in prison, with fines between 100,000 and 300,000 Rwf.
Serious injuries causing incapacity: 3 to 5 years in prison, with fines between 500,000 and 1,000,000 Rwf.
Permanent disability or terminal illness caused: Higher penalties apply.
RIB reminded the public to exercise restraint during holidays and celebrations, warning that excessive drinking and reckless behavior can lead to criminal charges and imprisonment. Authorities called for tolerance and adherence to the law to ensure public safety.

excerpt_en: Goma, 8 January 2026: The AFC/M23 rebel coalition has issued a direct threat against President Félix Tshisekedi Tshilombo, announcing intentions to arrest him and bring him to court. The statement came from Lt Col Willy Ngoma, spokesman for AFC/M23, during a farewell ceremony for
body_en:
Goma, 8 January 2026: The AFC/M23 rebel coalition has issued a direct threat against President Félix Tshisekedi Tshilombo, announcing intentions to arrest him and bring him to court.
The statement came from Lt Col Willy Ngoma, spokesman for AFC/M23, during a farewell ceremony for 22 civilians from the Masisi Center, North Kivu, who were reportedly killed by a DRC Army drone strike on 2 January 2026.
Lt Col Ngoma said: "He will definitely pay for this. It will not be long, you will see. He will go to court for these things. We will arrest him, he will go to court."
The General Director of AFC/M23, Corneille Nangaa, condemned the DRC government for killing civilians, accusing it of failing to distinguish between combatants and non-combatants. He stated: "The false political power that the Kinshasa government has given itself does not give it the right to kill civilians. No elections, no international recognition, no patriotic struggle can justify the killing of civilians."
Nangaa assured residents in AFC/M23-controlled areas that their security remains a priority, promising that the fighters will continue to protect civilians with the same dedication.
This latest declaration underscores the rising tensions between the DRC government and the AFC/M23, with threats now extending directly to the national leadership.
