title: Bunia Media Observe Three Days of Radio Silence After Murder of RTNC Journalist
excerpt: Bunia, Ituri Province | December 30, 2025 More than twenty radio stations and online media outlets operating in Bunia, in the eastern province of Ituri, began a three-day suspension of broadcasting and news programs on Tuesday to protest what they describe as repeated attacks aga
title_en: Bunia Media Observe Three Days of Radio Silence After Murder of RTNC Journalist
excerpt_en: Bunia, Ituri Province | December 30, 2025 More than twenty radio stations and online media outlets operating in Bunia, in the eastern province of Ituri, began a three-day suspension of broadcasting and news programs on Tuesday to protest what they describe as repeated attacks aga
body_en:
Bunia, Ituri Province | December 30, 2025
More than twenty radio stations and online media outlets operating in Bunia, in the eastern province of Ituri, began a three-day suspension of broadcasting and news programs on Tuesday to protest what they describe as repeated attacks against journalists and growing threats to press freedom.
The action follows the brutal killing of RTNC journalist Thierry Lole, who was murdered at his home on Sunday night by unidentified armed men, according to local media organizations.
Residents of Bunia woke up on Tuesday to an unusual silence on the airwaves. Several radio stations halted their regular programming entirely, while others suspended news bulletins, airing only music in tribute to their slain colleague.
According to journalists’ rights organizations, the killing highlights ongoing efforts by unknown actors to intimidate and silence the press in a region affected by chronic insecurity since 2017. The coordinated media blackout is intended to pressure authorities to take responsibility for ensuring the effective protection of civilians, including media professionals, in Ituri.
“These three days of radio silence are a strong message to the authorities,” said Constant Same Bagalwa, editor-in-chief of Radio Les Rebâtisseurs and director of the online outlet Bunia News. “They reflect the media’s refusal to continue working under constant threat.”
Ituri Province is home to approximately forty radio stations, several of which operate outside Bunia. A number of these outlets have also announced their intention to join the protest, extending the media blackout across parts of the province.

title: Court of Cassation Seeks Authorization to Prosecute Tshopo Governor
excerpt: Kisangani, January 5, 2026 — The Court of Cassation has formally requested authorization from the Tshopo Provincial Assembly to initiate legal proceedings against Governor Paulin Lendongolia, who faces allegations of embezzlement of public funds. The request, submitted to the Ass
title_en: Court of Cassation Seeks Authorization to Prosecute Tshopo Governor
excerpt_en: Kisangani, January 5, 2026 — The Court of Cassation has formally requested authorization from the Tshopo Provincial Assembly to initiate legal proceedings against Governor Paulin Lendongolia, who faces allegations of embezzlement of public funds. The request, submitted to the Ass
body_en:
Kisangani, January 5, 2026 — The Court of Cassation has formally requested authorization from the Tshopo Provincial Assembly to initiate legal proceedings against Governor Paulin Lendongolia, who faces allegations of embezzlement of public funds.
The request, submitted to the Assembly’s bureau, seeks permission to bring the governor to trial. The bureau committed to examining the petition in accordance with its internal regulations, a decision adopted during a meeting held on Saturday, January 3, 2026.
During the same meeting, the bureau also discussed the unjustified absence of several provincial deputies from plenary sessions in September 2025, as well as the governor’s recent reinstatement following a ruling by the Constitutional Court.
Speaking after the meeting, Paul Lokesa, rapporteur of the Provincial Assembly, expressed regret over the handling of the case. He noted that, unlike the opposing party, which appeared to have been properly informed, the Assembly was only officially notified of the case’s inclusion on the court docket after the governor’s reinstatement.
An examination of the Attorney General’s indictment revealed a procedural irregularity during the vote to remove the governor: 10 deputies voted in favor of impeachment instead of the required 18. However, according to the bureau, this flaw does not affect the substance of the allegations against Paulin Lendongolia.
“This error does not alter the facts of the case,” Paul Lokesa said. “In accordance with the internal regulations, the bureau will hear from the Attorney General or his representative, as well as from Paulin Lendongolia himself, in order to assess the merits of the allegations and decide whether or not to authorize a judicial investigation.”
Governor Reinstated
Governor Paulin Lendongolia returned to Kisangani on Sunday, January 4, after nearly two months in Kinshasa, and officially resumed his duties following the Constitutional Court’s ruling of November 26. He had been removed from office on October 27 through a vote of no confidence linked to allegations of misappropriation of public funds.
Upon his arrival at Bangoka International Airport, the governor called on all political actors to work together for the development of Tshopo province, amid a political climate still marked by legal and institutional tensions.

title: North Kivu: Deadly Attacks and Cattle Theft in Rutshuru Over Two Weeks
excerpt: Rutshuru, North Kivu, DRC – January 2, 2026 At least seven people have been killed and four others injured, including two children, in a series of violent incidents attributed to armed groups in Rutshuru territory over the past two weeks, according to local sources. In addition t
title_en: North Kivu: Deadly Attacks and Cattle Theft in Rutshuru Over Two Weeks
excerpt_en: Rutshuru, North Kivu, DRC – January 2, 2026 At least seven people have been killed and four others injured, including two children, in a series of violent incidents attributed to armed groups in Rutshuru territory over the past two weeks, according to local sources. In addition t
body_en:
Rutshuru, North Kivu, DRC – January 2, 2026
At least seven people have been killed and four others injured, including two children, in a series of violent incidents attributed to armed groups in Rutshuru territory over the past two weeks, according to local sources.
In addition to the human toll, over 100 cows were stolen during this period, highlighting the combined impact of violence and economic losses on local communities.
The attacks have been reported in at least seven localities north of the Bwito chiefdom, including the Lusoha-Mirangi road (Kanyabayonga group), Kibirizi-Kibingu road, and Kibirizi-Rwindi road (Mutanda group).
According to the program manager of SOCOLUT-DRC (Community Solidarity Against Tribalism in the DRC), the incidents include:
Kidnappings: three in Lusogha, three in Kyaghala.
Murders and gunshot injuries: in Birundule and along the Kibirizi-Rwindi road.
Cattle theft: 80 cows in Kilombo, 25 cows in Byanderema (Mirangi, Mutanda group).
Looting: two cases in Lusogha (Friday and Saturday nights), two cases on the Kibirizi-Rwindi road, and one on the Kibirizi-Kibingu road.
SOCOLUT-DRC calls for increased protection of civilians, who are routinely targeted during these atrocities, and urges humanitarian partners and peace actors to strengthen security and provide support to victims.
The affected areas, Kanyabayonga and Mutanda, are currently hosting over 20,000 displaced families, many of whom are directly impacted by these recent attacks.

The attacks have been reported in at least seven localities north of the Bwito chiefdom, including the Lusoha-Mirangi road (Kanyabayonga group), Kibirizi-Kibingu road, and Kibirizi-Rwindi road (Mutanda group).
According to the program manager of SOCOLUT-DRC (Community Solidarity Against Tribalism in the DRC), the incidents include:
Kidnappings: three in Lusogha, three in Kyaghala.
Murders and gunshot injuries: in Birundule and along the Kibirizi-Rwindi road.
Cattle theft: 80 cows in Kilombo, 25 cows in Byanderema (Mirangi, Mutanda group).
Looting: two cases in Lusogha (Friday and Saturday nights), two cases on the Kibirizi-Rwindi road, and one on the Kibirizi-Kibingu road.
SOCOLUT-DRC calls for increased protection of civilians, who are routinely targeted during these atrocities, and urges humanitarian partners and peace actors to strengthen security and provide support to victims.
The affected areas, Kanyabayonga and Mutanda, are currently hosting over 20,000 displaced families, many of whom are directly impacted by these recent attacks.

excerpt_en: Mambasa, Ituri, January 5, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC), in cooperation with the Ugandan People’s Defence Force (UPDF), dismantled an ADF rebel stronghold last week in Matolo-Kaseni, near the Ituri River. The joint operation was announced on Monday, January 5, durin
body_en:
Mambasa, Ituri, January 5, 2026 — The Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC), in cooperation with the Ugandan People’s Defence Force (UPDF), dismantled an ADF rebel stronghold last week in Matolo-Kaseni, near the Ituri River. The joint operation was announced on Monday, January 5, during an evaluation meeting in the Babila Bakwanza chiefdom, Mambasa territory. Both forces pledged to continue and intensify operations against the ADF in other villages where the rebels are attempting to regroup and attack local communities.
According to military sources, the nighttime operation, conducted from December 29 to 30, targeted a major ADF stronghold on the border between the Mambasa and Irumu territories.
Provincial deputies and civil society representatives, who accompanied the military delegation to Elake to assess progress, welcomed the efforts but called for the establishment of military positions in Elake, Leta, and Sita Rudi to ensure that local populations can safely access their fields.
Officials in Mambasa also urged that the joint operations be extended westward to Lolwa and Menzimenzi, where ADF fighters are reportedly regrouping in preparation for new attacks.
These measures form part of a months-long collaboration between the FARDC and UPDF aimed at neutralizing ADF activity and protecting civilians in the region.

title_en: Police Officer and Child Shot in Mbuji-Mayi by Armed Men
excerpt_en: Mbuji-Mayi, January 10, 2026 — A Congolese National Police officer (PNC) and his child under 10 years old were seriously wounded by gunfire from armed men wearing police uniforms on the night of Friday, January 10, in Bipemba, a commune in Mbuji-Mayi, Kasai-Oriental province. The
body_en:
Mbuji-Mayi, January 10, 2026 — A Congolese National Police officer (PNC) and his child under 10 years old were seriously wounded by gunfire from armed men wearing police uniforms on the night of Friday, January 10, in Bipemba, a commune in Mbuji-Mayi, Kasai-Oriental province. The motive for the attack remains unknown.
One of the assailants was apprehended by local police who arrived on the scene. Residents report that this incident is part of a series of criminal acts terrorizing the commune over several days.
The mayor of Bipemba has called for an increase in police personnel to ensure the safety of the population.
Residents expressed deep concern over the insecurity. Monique Mujinga, a local housewife, said:"At home, we haven't slept since the holidays. We spend the nights outside so we can shout. As soon as the bandits enter a house, they beat the owners, kill them, and steal all their belongings. It's terrible."
Conclusion: A Nation at a Strategic and Security Crossroads
The period between late December 2025 and early January 2026 has been defined by a complex interplay of strategic diplomatic maneuvers, persistent security volatility, and ambitious domestic reforms. As the DRC enters 2026, it faces a critical "refoundation" phase aimed at balancing international partnerships with the urgent need for internal stability.
1. Strategic Diplomacy and Sovereignty A central theme of this period was the government’s defense of the Washington Agreement, a strategic partnership with the United States. Despite domestic criticism alleging a "sell-off" of national resources, the executive branch maintained that the agreement is a technical framework for long-term development in sectors like energy (Grand Inga) and infrastructure (Lobito Corridor) without compromising sovereignty. Simultaneously, the DRC’s entry into the UN Security Council as a non-permanent member on January 1, 2026, signals its intent to internationalize the eastern crisis and demand greater respect for international law.
2. Persistent Security and Humanitarian Challenges The security situation in the eastern provinces remains the nation's most pressing concern. The government continues to condemn what it describes as a "war imposed" by Rwandan forces and the expansion of territory held by AFC/M23. While joint FARDC-UPDF operations have enabled the return of some displaced persons in Irumu, other regions like Masisi and Ituri face ongoing violence, resulting in the displacement of thousands and the paralysis of essential services like education.
3. Internal Governance and Social Unrest Domestically, the government is grappling with issues of governance and human rights. The suspension of military spokesman Major General Sylvain Ekenge over discriminatory remarks highlights the sensitive nature of ethnic tensions and hate speech within the country. Furthermore, a series of criminal acts—including the assassination of a journalist in Bunia and a professor in Kinshasa—has fueled public outcry and demands for better protection of civilians.
4. Economic Modernization and Health Trends On a positive note, the DRC has made strides in digital reform, launching electronic systems to modernize foreign trade and secure vehicle registration to combat fraud and increase state revenue. In public health, there is an encouraging decline in monkeypox cases, though new outbreaks of measles in Kasai-Oriental present a fresh challenge to the health system.
Final Outlook The start of 2026 finds the DRC caught between the hope of economic transformation and the reality of chronic conflict. The success of the "year of refoundation" will likely depend on the government's ability to translate its new international diplomatic standing into tangible security gains on the ground and to foster national unity through inclusive dialogue and transparent governance.
By Glad MUSEMA
Jeff Buleli

title: Rwandan Defense Minister Marizamunda Attends ICGLR Special Security Meeting on Eastern DRC
excerpt: Livingstone, Zambia – 10 January 2026: Rwanda’s Minister of Defense, Juvenal Marizamunda, participated in a special meeting of the ICGLR (International Conference on the Great Lakes Region) Defense Ministers to discuss security challenges in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (
title_en: Rwandan Defense Minister Marizamunda Attends ICGLR Special Security Meeting on Eastern DRC
excerpt_en: Livingstone, Zambia – 10 January 2026: Rwanda’s Minister of Defense, Juvenal Marizamunda, participated in a special meeting of the ICGLR (International Conference on the Great Lakes Region) Defense Ministers to discuss security challenges in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (
body_en:
Livingstone, Zambia – 10 January 2026: Rwanda’s Minister of Defense, Juvenal Marizamunda, participated in a special meeting of the ICGLR (International Conference on the Great Lakes Region) Defense Ministers to discuss security challenges in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC).
According to a statement from the Rwandan Ministry of Defense, the meeting focused on ensuring security and facilitating humanitarian operations in the eastern DRC, a region long affected by armed conflict.
The ministerial meeting followed sessions held on 8 January 2026 by the ICGLR Security Expert Group and the Chiefs of Defense of ICGLR member states.
The eastern DRC has experienced decades of conflict, intensified over the past 32 years by former Ex-FAR members and Interahamwe militias, and more recently by clashes between government forces and the AFC/M23 coalition. The region is also threatened by over 260 armed groups, which continue to attack communities, kill civilians, and loot property.
The ICGLR ministers emphasized the need for regional cooperation to stabilize the area and protect civilians while supporting humanitarian operations.

title: Rwanda Launches Home-Based Cervical Cancer Screening Program
excerpt: Kigali, January 4, 2026 — Rwanda has officially launched a home-based cervical cancer screening program, enabling women to self-test at home without visiting a health facility. The initiative, announced by the Rwanda National Cancer Institute (RNCI), aims to expand access to scre
title_en: Rwanda Launches Home-Based Cervical Cancer Screening Program
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 4, 2026 — Rwanda has officially launched a home-based cervical cancer screening program, enabling women to self-test at home without visiting a health facility. The initiative, announced by the Rwanda National Cancer Institute (RNCI), aims to expand access to scre
body_en:
Kigali, January 4, 2026 — Rwanda has officially launched a home-based cervical cancer screening program, enabling women to self-test at home without visiting a health facility. The initiative, announced by the Rwanda National Cancer Institute (RNCI), aims to expand access to screening and remove barriers that have long limited early detection.
Under the program, women use a self-sampling device at home. The sample is then collected and analyzed at a specialized laboratory to detect human papillomavirus (HPV), the leading cause of cervical cancer. Once results are available, women are informed by a health professional, and those who test positive for HPV are referred for further medical evaluation or treatment.
The screening is free of charge and targets women aged 30 and above, including those without symptoms. Health officials stress that cervical cancer often develops silently, making early screening essential for prevention and survival.
Although the program was piloted six months ago, initial uptake was limited. Authorities say the home-based approach is designed to overcome challenges such as shame, embarrassment, fear of examinations, and limited access to doctors, while remaining as reliable as conventional clinical screening.
Participating private health facilities include Legacy Clinic, DMC Carrefour, Good Life, Bien Naitre, Bwiza Medical, MBC Hospital, Polyclinic Medico-Social, and Saint Jean Polyclinique in Nyarugenge.
According to national cancer data, between 600 and 800 new cervical cancer cases are diagnosed each year in Rwanda, with around 600 deaths annually, highlighting the urgency of prevention efforts.
Rwanda aims to eliminate cervical cancer by 2027, in line with the WHO 90-70-90 strategy, which targets:
90% HPV vaccination coverage among girls aged 13–15,
70% screening of women aged 29–49, and
90% treatment for women diagnosed with early-stage disease.
Health authorities emphasize that early detection saves lives and that the new program empowers women to take control of their health while accelerating progress toward national elimination goals.

title: Conflict Erupts Between Wazalendo and FARDC Leadership
excerpt: On January 7, 2026, tensions surfaced between the Wazalendo coalition, aligned with the Congolese government, and the Democratic Republic of Congo’s military leadership. According to Wazalendo spokesperson Habyarimana Mbitsemunda, also known as Jules Mulumba, a serious conspiracy
title_en: Conflict Erupts Between Wazalendo and FARDC Leadership
excerpt_en: On January 7, 2026, tensions surfaced between the Wazalendo coalition, aligned with the Congolese government, and the Democratic Republic of Congo’s military leadership. According to Wazalendo spokesperson Habyarimana Mbitsemunda, also known as Jules Mulumba, a serious conspiracy
body_en:
On January 7, 2026, tensions surfaced between the Wazalendo coalition, aligned with the Congolese government, and the Democratic Republic of Congo’s military leadership. According to Wazalendo spokesperson Habyarimana Mbitsemunda, also known as Jules Mulumba, a serious conspiracy within the FARDC affected battlefield operations and internal coordination.
Mulumba stated that the arrest of Gen. Maj. Janvier Mayanga wa Gishuba, Deputy Commander of the DRC’s Rescue Forces, was the result of a conspiracy orchestrated by Lt. Gen. Padiri Bulenda, the FARDC Commander-in-Chief. He explained that Gen. Mayanga opposed the transfer of $8 million intended for Wazalendo from the Ministry of Defense and Finance.
The Wazalendo leadership also criticized Lt. Gen. Padiri Bulenda for sending messages attacking their coalition, which Mulumba described as a smear campaign against these armed groups. Mulumba further accused Gen. Fall Sikabwe of contributing to the capture of Goma by AFC/M23 forces on January 27, 2025, alleging that he facilitated joint operations between South African, Burundian, and Wazalendo forces.
Other FARDC officers were also blamed for military failures. Mulumba cited Lt. Gen. Masunzu Pacifique and Brig. Gen. Olivier Gasita, both from South Kivu, as responsible for operational missteps, questioning why they remain in active positions.
In Kinshasa, several senior officers were arrested over alleged plots against President Félix Tshisekedi, including Gen. Dieudonné Mutupeke Kiamata, Gen. Marcel Mbangu Mashita, Gen. Franck Ntumba (formerly in charge of military operations at the presidential palace), and Gen. Christian Tshiwewe Songesha, Chief of Army Staff. Wazalendo claims that Gen. Ntumba and Gen. Tshiwewe were involved in planning a coup, while Mutupeke and Mbangu face accusations of crimes they did not commit.
This dispute highlights deep fractures within the Congolese military and its allied forces, revealing mistrust and infighting that continue to undermine security operations in eastern DRC.

title: DRC Launches New Secure Vehicle License Plate System
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 6, 2026 — The General Directorate of Taxes (DGI) is set to officially launch a new secure vehicle license plate this Tuesday, January 6, 2026, in Kinshasa, marking a major step in the modernization of vehicle registration in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
title_en: DRC Launches New Secure Vehicle License Plate System
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 6, 2026 — The General Directorate of Taxes (DGI) is set to officially launch a new secure vehicle license plate this Tuesday, January 6, 2026, in Kinshasa, marking a major step in the modernization of vehicle registration in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 6, 2026 — The General Directorate of Taxes (DGI) is set to officially launch a new secure vehicle license plate this Tuesday, January 6, 2026, in Kinshasa, marking a major step in the modernization of vehicle registration in the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
According to a statement from the DGI, the new license plate—designed in line with international standards—will replace the old system with the aim of improving road safety, harmonizing the national vehicle registration framework, and facilitating traffic controls across the country.
The tax authority informed the general public, particularly vehicle owners and road users, of this government measure, emphasizing its importance for regulatory compliance and better traffic management.
The DGI is urging all concerned parties to promptly obtain the new license plates, noting that widespread adoption is essential to ensure the full harmonization of the registration system.
This initiative, the DGI added, is part of the government’s broader commitment to modernizing public services, strengthening road safety, and enhancing the efficiency and security of vehicle identification in the DRC.

title: RTNC Suspends Journalist Who Hosted Controversial Interview With Gen. Maj. Ekenge
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC — December 29, 2025 The Radio-Télévision Nationale Congolaise (RTNC) has suspended journalist Joseph Oscar Mbal Kahij following the broadcast of remarks deemed discriminatory toward the Tutsi ethnic group during a live program on the state-run television channel. In
title_en: RTNC Suspends Journalist Who Hosted Controversial Interview With Gen. Maj. Ekenge
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC — December 29, 2025 The Radio-Télévision Nationale Congolaise (RTNC) has suspended journalist Joseph Oscar Mbal Kahij following the broadcast of remarks deemed discriminatory toward the Tutsi ethnic group during a live program on the state-run television channel. In
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC — December 29, 2025
The Radio-Télévision Nationale Congolaise (RTNC) has suspended journalist Joseph Oscar Mbal Kahij following the broadcast of remarks deemed discriminatory toward the Tutsi ethnic group during a live program on the state-run television channel.
In a statement released on December 29, 2025, the RTNC executive board announced that “the head of broadcasting on the television, Oscar Mbal Kahij, has been suspended from his duties for allowing the airing of statements targeting the Tutsi ethnic group by the FARDC Spokesperson, Gen. Sylvain Ekenge Efomi.”
Mbal Kahij hosted Gen. Maj. Sylvain Ekenge on December 27 during the program “Plateau Spécial”, which was initially intended to address the security situation in eastern Democratic Republic of Congo, particularly in areas affected by fighting in South Kivu Province.
However, according to RTNC’s internal assessment, the discussion deviated from its stated purpose. Instead of focusing on military developments, the exchange included repeated remarks targeting Rwandans and Congolese Tutsis.
During the broadcast, Gen. Maj. Ekenge made controversial statements, including comments suggesting that marrying a Tutsi woman (Umutsikazi) requires caution, alleging that they refuse to have children with people from other ethnic groups. These remarks sparked widespread criticism both nationally and internationally.
On December 28, the Chief of the General Staff of the FARDC, Lt. Gen. Jules Banza Mwilambwe, announced the temporary suspension of Gen. Maj. Ekenge, citing that his statements were incompatible with military ethics and national policy, following intense public pressure.
Observers and human rights advocates argue that the incident reflects the growing level of ethnic hatred directed at Congolese Tutsis, despite the DRC government’s longstanding position that all citizens are equal before the law.
The suspensions of both the military spokesman and the journalist mark a rare acknowledgment by state institutions of responsibility in the handling of hate speech on public media, though critics continue to question the depth and sincerity of these measures.

title: North Kivu: M23 Rebels Launch Offensive to Retake Katoyi
excerpt: Masisi, North Kivu, DRC – January 2, 2026 AFC/M23 rebels launched an offensive early Friday morning in an attempt to regain control of the town of Katoyi, the main town of the sector of the same name in Masisi territory. Local sources confirm that the rebels are seeking to reclai
title_en: North Kivu: M23 Rebels Launch Offensive to Retake Katoyi
excerpt_en: Masisi, North Kivu, DRC – January 2, 2026 AFC/M23 rebels launched an offensive early Friday morning in an attempt to regain control of the town of Katoyi, the main town of the sector of the same name in Masisi territory. Local sources confirm that the rebels are seeking to reclai
body_en:
Masisi, North Kivu, DRC – January 2, 2026
AFC/M23 rebels launched an offensive early Friday morning in an attempt to regain control of the town of Katoyi, the main town of the sector of the same name in Masisi territory. Local sources confirm that the rebels are seeking to reclaim territory they lost at the end of December 2025.
According to reports, the attack targets four positions held by fighters from the Congolese Patriotic Resistance Group (PARECO), an ally of the FARDC. Fighting is concentrated in the village of Kasheke (Nyamaboko 1 group, Osso Banyungu sector), located approximately 7 km from Katoyi town center.
Gunfire was also reported in surrounding villages, including Busurirwa (Ufamandu 1 group), Myole (Mufunyi Kibabi group, Bahunde chiefdom), and Muhairwa (Kibabi 2 group, Katoyi sector).
This marks the second attempt by M23 to retake Katoyi, following an earlier assault last Tuesday. On December 29, 2025, Wazalendo fighters from PARECO/Strike Force recaptured Katoyi and neighboring villages—including Mitimingi, Kahundu, Kasheke, and Kakoka—after intense clashes that left several dead on both sides and resulted in the capture of 28 M23 fighters and 12 weapons, according to military sources.
The town of Katoyi has switched hands multiple times since mid-November 2025, reflecting the ongoing volatility in the Masisi sector and the persistence of M23’s attempts to regain strategic control.

body_en:
Walungu, South Kivu, January 5, 2026 — At least four civilians were killed and several others wounded during clashes between Wazalendo fighters and AFC-M23 rebels in the Walungu territory of South Kivu.
The fighting, which began on Sunday and continued into Monday, January 5, 2026, affected the villages of Bumbalali, Mwendo, and Cirhavanyi.
Residents reported that several houses were damaged by bombs reportedly dropped by M23 forces, exacerbating the humanitarian impact. One local resident described experiencing extremely difficult conditions over the past 48 hours, highlighting the heavy toll on civilians in the area.

title: Eve Bazaïba Travels to Bujumbura to Assess Humanitarian Crisis Affecting 250,000 Congolese Refugees
excerpt: Bujumbura, January 9, 2026 — Minister of State for Humanitarian Affairs, Eve Bazaïba, visited Bujumbura, Burundi, on Friday, January 9, to strengthen aid coordination and evaluate the humanitarian situation of at least 250,000 Congolese refugees who fled Uvira, South Kivu, after
title_en: Eve Bazaïba Travels to Bujumbura to Assess Humanitarian Crisis Affecting 250,000 Congolese Refugees
excerpt_en: Bujumbura, January 9, 2026 — Minister of State for Humanitarian Affairs, Eve Bazaïba, visited Bujumbura, Burundi, on Friday, January 9, to strengthen aid coordination and evaluate the humanitarian situation of at least 250,000 Congolese refugees who fled Uvira, South Kivu, after
body_en:
Bujumbura, January 9, 2026 — Minister of State for Humanitarian Affairs, Eve Bazaïba, visited Bujumbura, Burundi, on Friday, January 9, to strengthen aid coordination and evaluate the humanitarian situation of at least 250,000 Congolese refugees who fled Uvira, South Kivu, after its fall to AFC-M23 rebels in November 2025.
Humanitarian data indicates that over 101,000 displaced Congolese crossed into Burundi following Uvira’s capture, bringing the total number of Congolese refugees in the country to more than 250,000. Many of these refugees are from North and South Kivu provinces and live in precarious conditions, with approximately 30,000 children out of school, further exacerbating family vulnerabilities.
During her visit, Eve Bazaïba met with Burundian authorities and UNHCR officials to improve the coordination of humanitarian assistance. Priority needs include food, clean water, medical care, and emergency shelter.
The UNHCR has highlighted an alarming health situation, reporting 53 deaths, including 25 from cholera, and estimates that over US$33 million is required to respond adequately to the emergency.
Minister Bazaïba reaffirmed the Congolese government’s commitment, including the systematic registration of refugees to prevent infiltration and ensure proper assistance.

title: DRC: President Tshisekedi Seeks New Kinshasa Peace Talks with AFC/M23
excerpt: Kinshasa/Luanda – 8 January 2026: President Félix Tshisekedi Tshilombo of the Democratic Republic of Congo has requested that new peace talks between his government and the AFC/M23 coalition take place in Kinshasa, signaling a shift from the ongoing Doha mediation led by Qatar. T
title_en: DRC: President Tshisekedi Seeks New Kinshasa Peace Talks with AFC/M23
excerpt_en: Kinshasa/Luanda – 8 January 2026: President Félix Tshisekedi Tshilombo of the Democratic Republic of Congo has requested that new peace talks between his government and the AFC/M23 coalition take place in Kinshasa, signaling a shift from the ongoing Doha mediation led by Qatar. T
body_en:
Kinshasa/Luanda – 8 January 2026: President Félix Tshisekedi Tshilombo of the Democratic Republic of Congo has requested that new peace talks between his government and the AFC/M23 coalition take place in Kinshasa, signaling a shift from the ongoing Doha mediation led by Qatar.
Tshisekedi traveled to Luanda, Angola, on 14 December 2025 and returned on 5 January 2026. On 8 January, he again met Angolan President João Gonçalves Lourenço to discuss strategies for restoring peace and security in eastern DRC. During these discussions, Tshisekedi asked Lourenço to initiate new inclusive talks involving all Congolese affected by the war.
The proposed talks are expected to include:
Government supporters and political opposition
Armed groups, including AFC/M23
Civil society representatives
Religious figures and churches
The Angolan government has reportedly begun contacting several opposition figures who may participate in the new negotiations. Tshisekedi has also agreed, in principle, to the release of some AFC/M23 prisoners, with individual cases reviewed to verify the justification of previous convictions.
Sources in Kinshasa confirm that the President wants the AFC/M23 to declare a ceasefire, with the DRC government taking responsibility for monitoring its implementation.
Tshisekedi continues to reject Doha-based talks despite AFC/M23 leader Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo stating on 31 December 2025 that the DRC government refused to send representatives to two Qatar-led meetings intended to monitor the ceasefire.
The DRC government maintains that AFC/M23 fighters captured the town of Uvira in South Kivu, though the group claims to have withdrawn from the town to resume peace talks under the Doha framework.
These developments indicate that Tshisekedi is pursuing a new, domestically anchored negotiation strategy, potentially sidelining previous international mediation efforts.

Tshisekedi continues to reject Doha-based talks despite AFC/M23 leader Corneille Nangaa Yobeluo stating on 31 December 2025 that the DRC government refused to send representatives to two Qatar-led meetings intended to monitor the ceasefire.
The DRC government maintains that AFC/M23 fighters captured the town of Uvira in South Kivu, though the group claims to have withdrawn from the town to resume peace talks under the Doha framework.
These developments indicate that Tshisekedi is pursuing a new, domestically anchored negotiation strategy, potentially sidelining previous international mediation efforts.

body_en:
Kigali, January 2, 2026
Rwanda National Police (RNP) reported eight serious accidents over the Christmas and New Year period, spanning December 24, 2025, to January 2, 2026. Police Spokesperson ACP Boniface Rutikanga noted that these incidents occurred despite the generally smooth and secure conduct of festivities across the country.
“It was a week filled with travel, concerts, and entertainment. Security was good, and residents were able to enjoy the celebrations safely,” ACP Rutikanga said, emphasizing that minor incidents linked to drunkenness did not disrupt the overall festivities.
The accidents were evenly split between the holiday periods: four serious accidents occurred on December 24-25, 2025, and four more between December 31, 2025, and January 1, 2026. While exact casualty figures were not disclosed, these accidents contributed to the holiday’s tragic toll.
In addition to accidents, the police arrested 95 people nationwide for driving under the influence of alcohol, with 75% of offenders operating motorcycles or bicycles. Bunani recorded the highest number of arrests, with 47 individuals detained.
RNP reminded the public that Rwanda’s traffic laws impose fines of 150,000 Rwf, vehicle impoundment up to seven days, and possible imprisonment from seven days to two months for driving under the influence.
ACP Rutikanga also highlighted that road safety remains a significant concern in Rwanda, citing that 41,164 accidents occurred between 2022 and October 2025, resulting in 2,907 deaths, often caused by speeding, distracted driving, and driving under the influence.
“We urge residents to comply with traffic safety programs to prevent accidents and ensure public safety,” he concluded.

title: More Than 1,000 Burundian Soldiers Missing Over the Past Month
excerpt: More than 1,000 Burundian soldiers deployed in the Rusizi/Ruzizi Valley in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have gone missing over the past month. Between December 2 and 9, 2025, intense fighting erupted in several areas, including Luvungi, Sange, Luberizi, and Kili
title_en: More Than 1,000 Burundian Soldiers Missing Over the Past Month
excerpt_en: More than 1,000 Burundian soldiers deployed in the Rusizi/Ruzizi Valley in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have gone missing over the past month. Between December 2 and 9, 2025, intense fighting erupted in several areas, including Luvungi, Sange, Luberizi, and Kili
body_en:
More than 1,000 Burundian soldiers deployed in the Rusizi/Ruzizi Valley in the eastern Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) have gone missing over the past month. Between December 2 and 9, 2025, intense fighting erupted in several areas, including Luvungi, Sange, Luberizi, and Kiliba, pitting M23 fighters against DRC forces, supported by Burundian troops, the Wazalendo movement, and the FDLR.
The clashes began with the deployment of approximately 20,000 Burundian soldiers in South Kivu province. During the fighting, Burundian forces reportedly suffered heavy losses, including soldiers killed, wounded, or captured. The injured were evacuated to medical facilities such as Kamenge Military Hospital, Tanganyika Care Polyclinic, and Kira Hospital.
The M23 movement has confirmed that it captured numerous Burundian soldiers during the fighting in the Rusizi Valley, stating that it is respecting their rights while in custody and expressing its intention to facilitate their return home. Although M23 has not disclosed exact figures, sources in South Kivu indicate that the number of captured soldiers runs into the hundreds.
On January 4, 2026, the FOCODE organization, which advocates for the rights of Burundians, particularly those who have disappeared, announced that more than 1,000 Burundian soldiers are unaccounted for in the Rusizi Valley. Their status remains unclear, with uncertainty over whether they are alive, captured, killed, or wandering in the forests.
According to testimonies from soldiers who participated in the fighting in Kamanyola–Lubarika–Luvungi, the Burundian army has no information on the whereabouts of over 1,000 soldiers. It is reportedly unknown whether they died in combat, deserted, were captured, or remain missing in the bush.
Another reliable source in Burundi claims that 1,794 Burundian soldiers lost their lives in the Rusizi Valley, adding that these soldiers are considered to have deserted the army, with their whereabouts still unknown.

title: Mukoko Samba Calls for Regulation of Local Product Supply Chains
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 2, 2026 — The Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the National Economy, Daniel Mukoko Samba, has reiterated the government’s determination to standardize and regulate the local value chain, from production areas to consumer markets, in order to strengthen the sup
title_en: Mukoko Samba Calls for Regulation of Local Product Supply Chains
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 2, 2026 — The Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the National Economy, Daniel Mukoko Samba, has reiterated the government’s determination to standardize and regulate the local value chain, from production areas to consumer markets, in order to strengthen the sup
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 2, 2026 — The Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the National Economy, Daniel Mukoko Samba, has reiterated the government’s determination to standardize and regulate the local value chain, from production areas to consumer markets, in order to strengthen the supply of locally produced goods.
He made these remarks following a field visit to the public port of Kinkole in the N’sele commune, as well as the ports of Baramoto and CDI Bwamanda in the Gombe commune of Kinshasa.
The visit began at the fishing port of Kinkole, where the Deputy Prime Minister observed the arrival of sacks of grain from the provinces of Kwilu, Maï-Ndombe, and Kasaï. He also toured the area where cassava chips, unloaded from fishing boats, were being displayed for sale.
The ministerial delegation then proceeded to the port of Baramoto to assess ongoing supply challenges, before concluding the tour at the port of CDI Bwamanda.
At CDI Bwamanda, Daniel Mukoko Samba visited the production plant, which has a combined capacity of 50 tons per day for both the old and new units, bringing the total capacity to 100 tons per day. This output represents more than 10,000 bags of 10 kilograms per day, or approximately 2,500 bags of 25 kilograms, all destined for the Kinshasa market.
CDI Bwamanda, a Partner of the State
On this occasion, Édouard Sangina Toko, Deputy Managing Director of CDI Bwamanda, welcomed the Deputy Prime Minister’s visit, describing it as “very encouraging.”
He recalled that the Bwamanda International Development Center (CDI Bwamanda) has long played a key role in feeding the city of Kinshasa, particularly during the 1980s, 1990s, 2000s, and 2010s. However, as a non-profit organization, the institution has faced a decline in subsidies, which largely explains its current difficulties.
According to him, the main challenges facing the organization include:
access to quality seeds,
insufficient support for farmers, and
the poor state of road infrastructure, which complicates the transport of agricultural produce, even when production levels are adequate.
Despite these constraints, Édouard Sangina Toko stressed that CDI Bwamanda retains significant potential to revive its activities, provided it receives substantial financial support from the government, particularly to strengthen rural development services and build storage silos.
“To date, CDI Bwamanda has adequate infrastructure, with more than seven depots of 2,000 square meters each in Kinshasa, large warehouses in the interior of the country, as well as facilities dedicated to the storage and processing of maize. It is therefore positioned as a reliable partner that the State can support to contribute sustainably to the national food supply,” he affirmed.

title: Djihad and Co-Defendants Appeal for Provisional Release Before Nyarugenge High Court
excerpt: Kigali, Rwanda — December 29, 2025 The Nyarugenge High Court on Monday heard an appeal filed by Uzabakiriho Cyprien, known as Djihad, and his co-defendants, who are seeking provisional release after being placed in pretrial detention by the Kicukiro Primary Court. The appeal foll
title_en: Djihad and Co-Defendants Appeal for Provisional Release Before Nyarugenge High Court
excerpt_en: Kigali, Rwanda — December 29, 2025 The Nyarugenge High Court on Monday heard an appeal filed by Uzabakiriho Cyprien, known as Djihad, and his co-defendants, who are seeking provisional release after being placed in pretrial detention by the Kicukiro Primary Court. The appeal foll
body_en:
Kigali, Rwanda — December 29, 2025
The Nyarugenge High Court on Monday heard an appeal filed by Uzabakiriho Cyprien, known as Djihad, and his co-defendants, who are seeking provisional release after being placed in pretrial detention by the Kicukiro Primary Court.
The appeal follows the defendants’ dissatisfaction with a decision ordering the temporary detention of Uzabakiriho Cyprien (Djihad), Ishimwe Patrick (Pazzo Man), Ishimwe François Xavier, and Kwizera Nestor (Pappy Nesta).
The four men are charged with distributing explicit videos allegedly showing Yampano engaged in sexual activity with his girlfriend.
During the hearing, all defendants argued that the Kicukiro Primary Court failed to properly consider their defense arguments. Djihad told the court he was dissatisfied that his explanations were dismissed, insisting that no video had ever been shared by him.
He specifically rejected the prosecution’s claim that he posted the videos on his WhatsApp status, arguing that the screenshots presented did not clearly demonstrate that the content originated from his phone number. He further suggested that the prosecution may have confused him with another individual using the same name.
Djihad’s lawyer emphasized that the lower court ignored elements favorable to his client, including the possibility of release on bail, and formally requested the High Court to grant provisional freedom.
Ishimwe François Xavier, who represented himself, also criticized the pretrial detention order, stating that he had demonstrated he was not responsible for distributing the videos. Similar arguments were presented by Ishimwe Patrick (Pazzo Man), who said his detention resulted from the court’s failure to adequately assess his defense.
All defendants, including Kwizera Nestor (Pappy Nesta), requested to be released and prosecuted without detention, stressing that the 30-day detention ordered by the lower court was unjustified.
The prosecution, present at the hearing, defended the decision of the Kicukiro Primary Court, describing it as transparent and lawful, and asked the Nyarugenge High Court to uphold the detention while investigations continue. Prosecutors added that other suspects linked to the alleged distribution of the videos have also been arrested.
After hearing both sides, the presiding judge announced that the court’s ruling on the appeal will be delivered on January 5, 2026.

title: Tragedy in Ango: Two Killed by Police Officer on New Year’s Day
excerpt: Ango, Tshopo Province, DRC – January 1, 2026 A police officer shot and killed two people in the Ango territory on New Year’s Day, plunging the community into shock and grief. Ango is located approximately 500 km north of Kisangani. According to local sources, the victims were cel
title_en: Tragedy in Ango: Two Killed by Police Officer on New Year’s Day
excerpt_en: Ango, Tshopo Province, DRC – January 1, 2026 A police officer shot and killed two people in the Ango territory on New Year’s Day, plunging the community into shock and grief. Ango is located approximately 500 km north of Kisangani. According to local sources, the victims were cel
body_en:
Ango, Tshopo Province, DRC – January 1, 2026
A police officer shot and killed two people in the Ango territory on New Year’s Day, plunging the community into shock and grief. Ango is located approximately 500 km north of Kisangani.
According to local sources, the victims were celebrating the arrival of the new year at a bar in the Ango shopping center when an altercation broke out. Around 8:00 PM, a police jeep arrived at high speed, and two officers disembarked, ordering the crowd to disperse. Moments later, one officer fired point-blank, killing two individuals.
The incident has sparked outrage among residents and local authorities. The interim administrator of Ango territory condemned the use of live ammunition against civilians, urging the police hierarchy to take swift action.
“What I deplore is that the police officers fired live ammunition at the population. I hope, through my report to the governor, that their superiors will authorize their arrest. This would be a good thing, because it is the very wish of the population: that peace reign here above all else,” the administrator stated.
The Vice-President of the Tshopo Provincial Assembly, Antoine Gambolipay, who represents Ango, echoed this call, demanding that both officers be apprehended and brought to justice.
Authorities report that one officer remains at large, while the other is in custody at his camp. Investigations are ongoing as the community awaits accountability.

Bunia, Ituri, January 4, 2026 — On the occasion of National Independence Martyrs’ Day, observed annually on January 4 in honor of the independence heroes who fell in 1959, the 32nd Military Region of the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC) in Bunia issued a call for popular support to help end the ongoing conflicts in North Kivu and Ituri.
Military authorities emphasized that the current violence has claimed many lives, now recognized as martyrs, and urged citizens to contribute to the restoration of peace in the region.
Colonel Emmanuel Libandi, coordinator of the Armed Reserve for Defense and president of the organizing committee, highlighted security improvements over the past six months, particularly in the Djugu territory. He attributed this progress to a combination of military operations and dialogue with local communities, despite continuing threats from Thomas Lubanga’s CRP militia and the widespread proliferation of illegal weapons.
The FARDC reaffirmed its commitment to ongoing operations aimed at achieving lasting peace and called on all citizens to follow the example set by the martyrs in supporting peacebuilding efforts.
The commemoration brought together religious leaders, state representatives, and civil society actors, with plans underway to extend similar events to other territories within Ituri province.

title_en: FARDC and UPDF Intensify Operations Against ADF in Mambasa
excerpt_en: Mambasa, January 9, 2026 — Joint FARDC-UPDF forces continued their offensive against ADF rebels on Friday, January 9, in the Kolo-Kolo and Banju-Banju localities, deep in the forests of Mambasa territory. The operations follow a recent ADF attack on an army position, which report
body_en:
Mambasa, January 9, 2026 — Joint FARDC-UPDF forces continued their offensive against ADF rebels on Friday, January 9, in the Kolo-Kolo and Banju-Banju localities, deep in the forests of Mambasa territory. The operations follow a recent ADF attack on an army position, which reportedly killed around ten FARDC soldiers.
The month-long offensive aims to dismantle ADF strongholds in the Babila Bakwanza chiefdom, allowing civilians to safely access their fields and move freely. For several months, the ADF rebels have established fortified positions in the heart of the chiefdom, approximately 100 kilometers southwest of Bunia, from which they plan attacks on civilians and security forces along National Route 4 on the Komanda–Mambasa axis.
Local sources report that the rebels also impose illegal taxes on farmers, exacerbating the hardships faced by the population.
Security forces have faced heavy casualties, including the loss of about ten soldiers, and some army camps have been burned during ambushes. Reinforcements have since been deployed to continue the dismantling of ADF positions.
Civil society actors in Mambasa have welcomed the interventions, noting that ADF violence has significantly decreased in the region as a result of the joint operations.

title: Kinshasa, DRC – 8 January 2026: Finance Minister Muzito Says Kabila Is Not an Enemy of the State
excerpt: The Minister of Finance of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Adolphe Muzito, stated on 8 January that former President Joseph Kabila Kabange should not be considered an enemy of the state, despite a death sentence handed down by the DRC’s High Military Court. Kabila, who led
title_en: Kinshasa, DRC – 8 January 2026: Finance Minister Muzito Says Kabila Is Not an Enemy of the State
excerpt_en: The Minister of Finance of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Adolphe Muzito, stated on 8 January that former President Joseph Kabila Kabange should not be considered an enemy of the state, despite a death sentence handed down by the DRC’s High Military Court. Kabila, who led
body_en:
The Minister of Finance of the Democratic Republic of the Congo, Adolphe Muzito, stated on 8 January that former President Joseph Kabila Kabange should not be considered an enemy of the state, despite a death sentence handed down by the DRC’s High Military Court.
Kabila, who led the country from 2001 to 2019, has had a strained relationship with current President Félix Tshisekedi. Following accusations that he collaborated with the AFC/M23 rebel group controlling large parts of eastern DRC, Kabila fled to South Africa at the end of 2023.
In September 2025, the High Military Court confirmed Kabila as the leader of AFC/M23, found him guilty of treason, war crimes, crimes against humanity, and membership in an illegal armed group, and sentenced him to death.
During an interview with France 24, Muzito, who has been Finance Minister under Tshisekedi since August 2025, clarified his position:
“He is not an enemy of the DRC. I am not commenting on the court’s decision. We are a country at war, it is a military court that has made a decision. I am not commenting.”
When asked if he believed Tshisekedi would carry out the death sentence if Kabila were arrested, Muzito responded that, to his knowledge, the President would not do so.
Muzito’s remarks come amid ongoing political tensions in the DRC over Kabila’s alleged role with rebel forces and reflect a cautious approach to a highly sensitive issue.

title: Kigali – First Day of 2026 Sees Quiet Streets and Limited Activities
excerpt: Kigali, January 1, 2026 The first day of 2026 in Kigali was marked by unusually low activity and sparse crowds, as many residents chose to spend the day quietly following New Year celebrations. Unlike the chaotic closing and opening nights of the previous year, streets and commer
title_en: Kigali – First Day of 2026 Sees Quiet Streets and Limited Activities
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 1, 2026 The first day of 2026 in Kigali was marked by unusually low activity and sparse crowds, as many residents chose to spend the day quietly following New Year celebrations. Unlike the chaotic closing and opening nights of the previous year, streets and commer
body_en:
Kigali, January 1, 2026
The first day of 2026 in Kigali was marked by unusually low activity and sparse crowds, as many residents chose to spend the day quietly following New Year celebrations. Unlike the chaotic closing and opening nights of the previous year, streets and commercial areas were largely empty, with few people and vehicles moving around the city.
In neighborhoods such as Nyamirambo and the city center, residents explained that the first day of the year is often dedicated to visiting family and friends, or resting after late-night festivities. Church attendance was modest, as many had already spent the night in prayer and returned home in the morning.
Eric Twizerimana, who spent New Year’s Eve in church, said he planned to spend the day socializing with friends and family while keeping his faith central: “Everyone celebrates holidays in general. I started the last year in church and will start this year in the same spirit. This new year, I have many resolutions, but the Lord will enable us.”
Business owners also noted the quiet day. Jean Pierre Maniraghuha, a household appliance seller in Nyamirambo, said customers were slowly returning, but he went to work regardless: “We started the year in church at night, but our daily lives are sustained by work. Even one customer is worth attending to, and this year I am planning to innovate and expand my business.”
Typically busy areas, such as Downtown Station, were almost empty, with many shops remaining closed. Some churches, particularly Catholic parishes, held services to start the new year, with families participating in baptisms and masses that emphasized love, faith, and community.
Evening gatherings also brought some activity, as certain churches combined worship with entertainment, attracting small crowds, but overall the first day of 2026 in Kigali was calm, reflecting a mix of religious devotion, family visits, and rest after the New Year celebrations.

title: AFC/M23 Claims Discovery of Belgian-Supplied Weapons Near Uvira
excerpt: January 3, 2026 — The AFC/M23 movement claims that its fighters discovered a cache of weapons allegedly supplied to the Democratic Republic of Congo by Belgium during their advance toward Uvira, according to statements by Dr. Balinda Oscar, Deputy Spokesperson of the AFC/M23. Dr.
title_en: AFC/M23 Claims Discovery of Belgian-Supplied Weapons Near Uvira
excerpt_en: January 3, 2026 — The AFC/M23 movement claims that its fighters discovered a cache of weapons allegedly supplied to the Democratic Republic of Congo by Belgium during their advance toward Uvira, according to statements by Dr. Balinda Oscar, Deputy Spokesperson of the AFC/M23. Dr.
body_en:
January 3, 2026 — The AFC/M23 movement claims that its fighters discovered a cache of weapons allegedly supplied to the Democratic Republic of Congo by Belgium during their advance toward Uvira, according to statements by Dr. Balinda Oscar, Deputy Spokesperson of the AFC/M23.
Dr. Balinda asserted that, as fighters reached the Luvungi area, less than 10 kilometers from Uvira, they came across military equipment still packed in boxes, allegedly stored in a school and not yet deployed. He claimed the weapons had been provided by Belgium to the DRC.
According to the AFC/M23 official, the capture of Uvira followed what he described as provocations by Congolese forces, including airstrikes in Kamanyola that reportedly caused civilian casualties and property destruction. He alleged that Burundian elements had joined the fighting, prompting the movement to resume hostilities after a period he described as ten months of calm in parts of Kamanyola and Katogota.
Dr. Balinda further claimed that the coalition opposing the AFC/M23 lacked combat experience, alleging that some Wazalendo fighters were civilians without adequate training, and accusing Burundian Imbonerakure of operating in military uniforms.
He also alleged that a significant portion of the AFC/M23’s equipment is obtained from the battlefield, claiming that some FARDC officers abandoned or sold weapons—an assertion he linked to ongoing judicial proceedings against senior officers.
Addressing Belgium’s role, Dr. Balinda accused Brussels of maintaining political and military support for Kinshasa, citing historical ties and what he described as a close relationship with President Félix Tshisekedi. He used strong language to claim that Congolese sovereignty had been compromised, framing the conflict as a renewed struggle for independence.
Despite these accusations, Dr. Balinda stated that the AFC/M23 supports peace talks with the Congolese government and insisted that the movement does not seek to seize power, but claims to be fighting for the rights of the Congolese people.

title: DRC Launches Digital Reform to Modernize Foreign Trade Management
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC | December 29, 2025 The Democratic Republic of Congo has taken a major step in modernizing foreign trade with the launch of electronic transmission of documentation packages from the S-ONE system of the Integrated Single Window Operating Company (SEGUCE) to SYDONIA
title_en: DRC Launches Digital Reform to Modernize Foreign Trade Management
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC | December 29, 2025 The Democratic Republic of Congo has taken a major step in modernizing foreign trade with the launch of electronic transmission of documentation packages from the S-ONE system of the Integrated Single Window Operating Company (SEGUCE) to SYDONIA
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC | December 29, 2025
The Democratic Republic of Congo has taken a major step in modernizing foreign trade with the launch of electronic transmission of documentation packages from the S-ONE system of the Integrated Single Window Operating Company (SEGUCE) to SYDONIA World, the automated system of the General Directorate of Customs and Excise (DGDA). The launch was presided over by Prime Minister Judith Suminwa on Monday, December 29.
This historic reform is designed to facilitate import and export operations, improve information flow between stakeholders, and strengthen resource mobilization for the state coffers.
According to Minister of Foreign Trade Julien Paluku, the reform will reduce costs and delays for import, export, and transit operations, ensure complete transparency, guarantee traceability, and enforce standards.
"I want to reassure economic operators that this reform will not hinder trade operations. On the contrary, it will reduce costs and delays, strengthen transparency, and protect agents from harassment," Paluku emphasized.
Prime Minister Suminwa described the initiative as a historic revolution for the DRC, further consolidating its integration into international trade.
“The implementation of electronic transmission marks a decisive step in digital development, in line with the Sustainable Development Goals,” she stated.
Finance Minister Doudou Fwamba highlighted that the reform will simplify procedures and increase public revenue by combating customs fraud.
Beyond technical modernization, the reform also represents a shift in administrative culture, promising reduced processing times, enhanced traceability, increased transparency, and a direct fight against fraud. Mandatory for all users, the new system is seen as a critical lever for improving the business climate, securing public revenue, and integrating the DRC into international trade standards.

Mandatory for all users, the new system is seen as a critical lever for improving the business climate, securing public revenue, and integrating the DRC into international trade standards.

title: DRC Government Confirms Suspension of Military Spokesman Over Discriminatory Remarks
excerpt: Kinshasa, DRC — December 28, 2025 The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has confirmed the temporary suspension of the national military spokesman, Major General Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa, following remarks deemed discriminatory against Congolese Tutsi. According to
title_en: DRC Government Confirms Suspension of Military Spokesman Over Discriminatory Remarks
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, DRC — December 28, 2025 The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has confirmed the temporary suspension of the national military spokesman, Major General Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa, following remarks deemed discriminatory against Congolese Tutsi. According to
body_en:
Kinshasa, DRC — December 28, 2025
The government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has confirmed the temporary suspension of the national military spokesman, Major General Sylvain Ekenge Bomusa, following remarks deemed discriminatory against Congolese Tutsi.
According to official sources, the suspension order was signed on December 28, 2025, by the Chief of Staff of the Armed Forces of the DRC (FARDC), Lieutenant General Jules Banza Mwilambwe.
The decision follows comments made by Maj Gen Ekenge on December 27 during a broadcast on state television (RTNC), in which he stated that marrying a Tutsi woman required caution, alleging that interethnic marriages would not result in children. The remarks sparked strong reactions within the country and beyond.
The incident occurred amid accusations that the DRC authorities tolerate or support hate speech targeting Tutsi communities, particularly in the eastern provinces, where atrocities have been reported.
In announcing the suspension, Lt Gen Mwilambwe stated that the comments were not aligned with the values of the national army or state policy. However, critics have questioned the sincerity of this position.
Fanny Kaj Kayemb, a senior finance official within the AFC/M23 alliance, argued that the punishment was symbolic and that the remarks reflected a broader command policy.“The military spokesman does not speak on his own,” Kayemb said. “He follows the line approved by the high command. In the DRC, the Commander-in-Chief is President Félix Tshisekedi.”
Kayemb further described the suspension as an attempt to mislead public opinion and the international community, asserting that the remarks were consistent with what he called a discriminatory political orientation.
Observers also point to past cases, notably statements by MP Justin Bitakwira, who publicly targeted Tutsi, especially Banyamulenge, without facing domestic sanctions, despite being sanctioned by the European Union in 2022.
Additionally, on December 22, 2025, President Félix Tshisekedi received two Congolese nationals living in the United States, including Jean-Claude Mubenga, who has previously made violent statements against Tutsi. The meeting reportedly focused on national unity, drawing further criticism from human rights observers.
According to several sources, verbal attacks against Congolese Tutsi have coincided with airstrikes and drone attacks targeting areas inhabited by Banyamulenge communities since early 2025, raising concerns about ethnic targeting and escalating tensions.

title: FARDC Honors Colonel Mamadou Ndala, 12 Years After His Assassination
excerpt: Kinshasa/North Kivu, DRC – January 2, 2026 The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) paid tribute on January 2 to Colonel Mamadou Ndala, twelve years after he was assassinated in an ambush while traveling to Eringeti in North Kivu. On this solemn day of remembr
title_en: FARDC Honors Colonel Mamadou Ndala, 12 Years After His Assassination
excerpt_en: Kinshasa/North Kivu, DRC – January 2, 2026 The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) paid tribute on January 2 to Colonel Mamadou Ndala, twelve years after he was assassinated in an ambush while traveling to Eringeti in North Kivu. On this solemn day of remembr
body_en:
Kinshasa/North Kivu, DRC – January 2, 2026
The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) paid tribute on January 2 to Colonel Mamadou Ndala, twelve years after he was assassinated in an ambush while traveling to Eringeti in North Kivu.
On this solemn day of remembrance, the FARDC reaffirmed its determination to continue the fight for which Colonel Ndala sacrificed his life: building a united, sovereign, and peaceful Democratic Republic of Congo.
“Honor and glory to General Mamadou Ndala. The grateful nation will never forget you. Long live the FARDC, long live the Democratic Republic of Congo!” the FARDC wrote on its official account.
At the time of his death, Colonel Ndala was leading military operations against the Ugandan Allied Democratic Forces (ADF) and other armed groups active in the Beni region. His courage, loyalty, and strategic leadership earned him the status of a national hero and an emblematic figure of supreme sacrifice in defense of the homeland.
The FARDC highlighted his enduring legacy:
Leadership on the ground, closely engaging with troops.
Unwavering commitment to peace, security, and territorial integrity.
Determination in the face of the enemy, inspiring generations of Congolese soldiers.
“His legacy remains alive in the hearts of Congolese soldiers and the entire nation,” the army concluded, paying homage to a commander whose life exemplified heroism and dedication.
This 12th anniversary commemoration comes as the Congolese army continues to face ongoing clashes with AFC/M23 rebels, who are reportedly supported by the Rwandan army in eastern DRC.

title_en: Burundi Transfers Congolese Refugees to Ruhigi Camp
excerpt_en: Bujumbura, January 5, 2026 — The Burundian government has begun transferring thousands of Congolese refugees from the Rumonge and Gatumba camps to the Ruhigi refugee camp, located about 60 kilometers north of Bujumbura, according to humanitarian sources. The displaced Congolese,
body_en:
Bujumbura, January 5, 2026 — The Burundian government has begun transferring thousands of Congolese refugees from the Rumonge and Gatumba camps to the Ruhigi refugee camp, located about 60 kilometers north of Bujumbura, according to humanitarian sources.
The displaced Congolese, who fled fighting involving the AFC/M23 in South Kivu, had been living in extremely precarious conditions in the Rumonge and Gatumba camps, where they reportedly survived without sufficient humanitarian assistance.
Authorities said the relocation aims to move the refugees away from the Congolese border, citing security and logistical considerations.
However, conditions at the Ruhigi camp have also drawn concern. Refugees report facing harsh weather conditions and ongoing hardships, raising fears that the humanitarian situation may remain critical despite the transfer.
One refugee described the situation as difficult, underscoring the continued vulnerability of displaced Congolese populations seeking safety in neighboring Burundi.

title: Central Bank of Congo Maintains Easing of Monetary Policy
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 8, 2026 — The Central Bank of Congo (BCC) announced the continuation of its monetary policy easing during its ordinary session on Thursday, January 8, in Kinshasa. This marks the second decision in three months to maintain the policy initiated in the last quarte
title_en: Central Bank of Congo Maintains Easing of Monetary Policy
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 8, 2026 — The Central Bank of Congo (BCC) announced the continuation of its monetary policy easing during its ordinary session on Thursday, January 8, in Kinshasa. This marks the second decision in three months to maintain the policy initiated in the last quarte
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 8, 2026 — The Central Bank of Congo (BCC) announced the continuation of its monetary policy easing during its ordinary session on Thursday, January 8, in Kinshasa. This marks the second decision in three months to maintain the policy initiated in the last quarter of 2025.
The Monetary Policy Committee, chaired by Governor André Wameso Nkualoloki, explained that the measure aims to create favorable financing conditions for the national economy while preserving macroeconomic stability. In practice, this means gradually lowering borrowing costs to facilitate credit for businesses and households without jeopardizing the financial system.
Governor Nkualoloki stated:“For 2026, the Monetary Policy Committee forecasts controlled price increases, in a context of exchange rate stabilization and sustained economic growth.”
He added that the national economy is expected to benefit from favorable developments in metal prices, particularly copper and cobalt, while remaining influenced by global geopolitical tensions and tariffs. At the domestic level, easing monetary policy is also linked to hopes for reduced conflicts in the eastern regions.
The committee reaffirmed its commitment to closely monitoring economic developments and liquidity, emphasizing that businesses will enjoy better borrowing conditions, encouraging productive investment, and households will have improved access to financing for housing or business activities.

title: Central African Republic, 8 January 2026: Rwandan Peacekeepers Honored for Service
excerpt: Rwandan soldiers serving with the MINUSCA peacekeeping mission in the Bria region of the Central African Republic have been awarded United Nations medals in recognition of their professionalism and contributions to restoring peace. The awards were presented to soldiers from the R
title_en: Central African Republic, 8 January 2026: Rwandan Peacekeepers Honored for Service
excerpt_en: Rwandan soldiers serving with the MINUSCA peacekeeping mission in the Bria region of the Central African Republic have been awarded United Nations medals in recognition of their professionalism and contributions to restoring peace. The awards were presented to soldiers from the R
body_en:
Rwandan soldiers serving with the MINUSCA peacekeeping mission in the Bria region of the Central African Republic have been awarded United Nations medals in recognition of their professionalism and contributions to restoring peace.
The awards were presented to soldiers from the RWABG VII battalion and the RWAMED X medical team during a ceremony at the RWABG VII battalion camp in Haute-Kotto prefecture.
The ceremony was attended by Maj Gen Maychel Asmi, Deputy Commander of MINUSCA, and Olivier Kayumba, Rwandan Ambassador to the Central African Republic. Maj Gen Asmi praised the Rwandan troops for their conduct, discipline, and productive work, highlighting their role in the smooth conduct of recent presidential elections won by Faustin Archange Touadéra.
The RWABG VII battalion was recognized for maintaining security in Bria, Ouadda, and Sam-Ouandja, while RWAMED X was commended for providing medical support to both fellow peacekeepers and the local population.
Lt Col Willy Ntagara, Commander of RWABG VII, and Col Dr. Simon R. Nyagasaza, Commander of RWAMED X, noted that the medals would strengthen their commitment to their duties, which include protecting civilians, senior officials, UN personnel, infrastructure, and key installations such as M’Poko International Airport.
Rwandan troops first deployed to the Central African Republic in 2014, and in 2020, special forces were sent as part of the CAR-Rwanda partnership to quell unrest linked to armed groups allegedly supported by former president François Bozizé. Their ongoing mission remains focused on maintaining security and supporting peace in the region.

title: Rwanda – Rubavu District Distributes Over 12,000 Cows to Fight Poverty
excerpt: Rubavu, December 31, 2025 The Rubavu District Administration has announced that more than 12,000 cows have been distributed to local residents under the Girinka program since 2006, as part of ongoing efforts to combat poverty and promote self-sufficiency. During a program visit i
title_en: Rwanda – Rubavu District Distributes Over 12,000 Cows to Fight Poverty
excerpt_en: Rubavu, December 31, 2025 The Rubavu District Administration has announced that more than 12,000 cows have been distributed to local residents under the Girinka program since 2006, as part of ongoing efforts to combat poverty and promote self-sufficiency. During a program visit i
body_en:
Rubavu, December 31, 2025
The Rubavu District Administration has announced that more than 12,000 cows have been distributed to local residents under the Girinka program since 2006, as part of ongoing efforts to combat poverty and promote self-sufficiency.
During a program visit in Kanzenze Sector, Kirerema Cell, 30 cows were handed over to beneficiaries, highlighting the district’s commitment to improving livelihoods.
Mayor Mulindwa Prosper described a cow as a “factory” for households, explaining that it provides fertilizer, milk for nutrition, income from sales, and contributes to overall economic growth. “We ask those who have cows to feed them well, clean them, and insure them so they provide a good yield,” he said.
The Mayor also emphasized the broader economic potential of the program, urging residents not to focus solely on raising cows but to exploit business opportunities, including the foreign market, to maximize benefits.
According to the Ministry of Local Government, Rubavu District has helped 49.7% of residents escape poverty in the last three years, compared to the national average of 62.4%.
Since the launch of the Girinka program in Rwanda in 2006, 12,647 cows have been distributed in Rubavu, with 5,986 received as donations, bringing the total number of cows in the district to 32,645.

title_en: AFC/M23 Accuses DRC Government of Genocide Amid Ongoing Violence
excerpt_en: January 2, 2026 – Eastern DRC The AFC/M23 Alliance has accused the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government of committing acts of genocide, condemning what it describes as systematic attacks against civilians in the eastern regions of the country. The statement, released on
body_en:
January 2, 2026 – Eastern DRC
The AFC/M23 Alliance has accused the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government of committing acts of genocide, condemning what it describes as systematic attacks against civilians in the eastern regions of the country. The statement, released on January 2, 2026, cites widespread human rights violations, targeting women, and looting by Congolese government forces in areas including Uvira, Makobola, Kamanyola, Luvungi, and Sange.
According to the group, Kamanyola alone saw eight people killed and 55 others injured, while civilians in Uvira faced violent suppression during a peaceful demonstration on December 22, 2025, where heavy weaponry was reportedly used against protesters.
The statement criticized the DRC government under President Félix Tshisekedi, accusing it of prioritizing military expenditures, such as drones, over the protection of civilians in the eastern provinces. AFC/M23 further condemned:
Deliberate violations of the ceasefire agreement
Hate crimes and ethnically motivated torture
Systematic attacks on populated areas and AFC/M23 positions by land, sea, and air
Hate speech propagated by former FARDC Military Spokesperson, Gen Maj Sylvain Ekenge, in an interview aired on RTNC on December 27, 2025
The group emphasized that these actions contravene international principles against genocide, including those adopted in 1948, and constitute a campaign of persecution, exclusion, and oppression against Tutsi communities in the DRC.
AFC/M23 reiterated its commitment to defending those affected, protecting their security, dignity, and fundamental rights, stating:
“We are on the side of those who continue to be oppressed and will continue to make efforts to protect them against this murderous regime.”
The alliance called on the international community to recognize these violations and take notice of the ongoing humanitarian crisis in eastern DRC.
