title: DRC’s Size Used as a Pretext for Tshisekedi’s Failure to Protect Citizens
excerpt: January 4, 2026- The sheer size of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is increasingly being used as a pretext to justify President Félix Tshisekedi’s persistent inability to guarantee security for the Congolese people. As insecurity continues to worsen in eastern DRC, par
title_en: DRC’s Size Used as a Pretext for Tshisekedi’s Failure to Protect Citizens
excerpt_en: January 4, 2026- The sheer size of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is increasingly being used as a pretext to justify President Félix Tshisekedi’s persistent inability to guarantee security for the Congolese people. As insecurity continues to worsen in eastern DRC, par
body_en:
January 4, 2026- The sheer size of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) is increasingly being used as a pretext to justify President Félix Tshisekedi’s persistent inability to guarantee security for the Congolese people. As insecurity continues to worsen in eastern DRC, particularly in the Kivu region, senior officials have repeatedly argued that the country’s vast territory is responsible for decades of instability.
A recurring narrative among DRC leaders is that the Congo is simply too large to govern effectively. This argument has been frequently invoked by President Tshisekedi to explain the ongoing violence. In 2022, he publicly claimed that the country’s security challenges stem from its size, insisting that the national army could not be deployed everywhere to fight armed groups such as the ADF, an Islamic State–linked Ugandan militia, and other insurgents operating on Congolese soil.
Despite numbering around 130,000 troops, the FARDC is plagued by low morale, inadequate training, weak command structures, ethnic discrimination, corruption, and the integration of the FDLR, a Rwandan militia responsible for the 1994 genocide against the Tutsis, incorporated under Tshisekedi’s authority.
Tshisekedi’s reliance on Burundian troops, the Wazalendo militia, European mercenaries, and SADC forces has steadily declined, particularly after South Africa, Malawi, and Tanzania withdrew their contingents following military setbacks against the AFC/M23.
Some analysts now question whether Tshisekedi fully understood the vastness of the Congolese territory before assuming office, when he promised to restore security nationwide, or whether this reality only became apparent to him after taking power. Others openly question his true intentions regarding the country’s territorial integrity, wondering whether a reduction in size might better serve his political interests.
As the saying goes, a leader is one who knows the way, walks the way, and shows the way. The conduct of Tshisekedi and his inner circle suggests that the crisis in eastern DRC is of little concern, as long as Kinshasa remains untouched.
In a statement issued on November 26, government spokesperson Patrick Muyaya claimed that the Kivu regions affected by insecurity represent only a small portion of the DRC.
“What does 2,345,000 square kilometers really mean?” he asked, adding that foreigners often exaggerate the conflict by saying, “There is war in the DRC,” while visitors to Kinshasa are surprised to find calm in the capital.
Such remarks have reinforced the perception that the Tshisekedi administration has never prioritized the well-being of populations in eastern DRC.
In 2025, Brigadier General Eddy Kapend, commander of the 22nd Military Region, openly stated that the country was not concerned by the occupation of parts of eastern DRC by AFC/M23 fighters, stressing instead that the real issue would be their presence in Katanga province. He further noted that there were no major concerns as long as Katanga remained untouched.
That same year, Anthony Nkinzo Kamole, Chief of Staff to the Presidency, declared during an interview that the conflict in eastern DRC was happening 2,000 kilometers away, describing the eastern regions as “foreign zones”, while Kinshasa was considered their country.
These statements echo similar remarks made by Tshisekedi, Muyaya, General Kapend, Nkinzo, and others, including Jules Alingete, the Auditor General, who once said that the war was 2,000 kilometers from Kinshasa and that “we only see it on television”. Such views underscore a deep disconnect from the realities faced by eastern populations.
Beyond the argument of territorial size, another frequent strategy has been to blame Rwanda for all problems, allowing the Congolese government to avoid acknowledging its own failures.
Eastern DRC has become a battleground for more than 260 armed groups, resulting in thousands of civilian deaths, mass rapes, forced recruitment of children, and the displacement of millions, both internally and abroad.
Tshisekedi has further exacerbated the crisis by arming groups accused of serious human rights violations to support the FARDC against the AFC/M23, a movement that claims to be fighting against the genocide of Congolese Tutsis allegedly perpetrated by the Kinshasa government.
The FDLR, which invaded Rwanda in 1994, continues to be deeply entrenched within the Congolese army and is actively involved in arming the predominantly civilian Wazalendo movement.
To date, Tshisekedi has shown no clear political will to end the war or restore peace. He appears largely indifferent to the fate of Congolese refugees and civilians who continue to risk their lives daily amid the conflict.
Sheltered more than 2,000 kilometers away from the frontlines, the president has repeatedly minimized the crisis by arguing that the affected areas are too small to matter. Critics argue that he is now using the war in eastern DRC as a political tool, exploiting the ongoing instability to justify extending his hold on power.

The FDLR, which invaded Rwanda in 1994, continues to be deeply entrenched within the Congolese army and is actively involved in arming the predominantly civilian Wazalendo movement.
To date, Tshisekedi has shown no clear political will to end the war or restore peace. He appears largely indifferent to the fate of Congolese refugees and civilians who continue to risk their lives daily amid the conflict.
Sheltered more than 2,000 kilometers away from the frontlines, the president has repeatedly minimized the crisis by arguing that the affected areas are too small to matter. Critics argue that he is now using the war in eastern DRC as a political tool, exploiting the ongoing instability to justify extending his hold on power.

title: Funding Secured for Major Expansion of Karenge Waterworks in Rwanda
excerpt: Rwamagana, January 3, 2026 The Rwamagana District Administration has announced that funding has been fully secured for the expansion and distribution project of the Karenge Waterworks, with the first phase of construction already reaching a satisfactory level of completion. The K
title_en: Funding Secured for Major Expansion of Karenge Waterworks in Rwanda
excerpt_en: Rwamagana, January 3, 2026 The Rwamagana District Administration has announced that funding has been fully secured for the expansion and distribution project of the Karenge Waterworks, with the first phase of construction already reaching a satisfactory level of completion. The K
body_en:
Rwamagana, January 3, 2026
The Rwamagana District Administration has announced that funding has been fully secured for the expansion and distribution project of the Karenge Waterworks, with the first phase of construction already reaching a satisfactory level of completion.
The Karenge Waterworks is a strategic infrastructure project expected to significantly increase water supply to Rwamagana town, the district’s industrial zone, and parts of Kigali City. Under the expansion plan, the plant’s production capacity will rise from 12,000 cubic meters per day to 48,000 cubic meters, a fourfold increase.
The initial agreement for the expansion was signed between Rwanda and Hungary. More recently, on November 28, 2025, the Cabinet approved the final ratification of a financing agreement between the Government of Rwanda and the Abu Dhabi Fund for Economic Development, which is providing a loan of 34.7 billion Rwandan francs to support the expansion of the water transportation and distribution system linked to the Karenge plant.
Rwamagana District Mayor Mbonyumuvunyi Radjab confirmed that construction works are underway and progressing well. He explained that once operational, water from the Karenge plant will be shared between Kigali City and Rwamagana District, with part directed to the industrial area and the remainder distributed to households.
The Abu Dhabi-funded component of the project will focus on the construction of water reservoirs and the installation of large transmission pipelines, covering more than 40 kilometers, to ensure water reaches different sectors of the district. These pipelines will connect to secondary distribution networks serving residential areas.
According to the mayor, the project is planned over three years, with the first year nearing completion. Trial distribution of water to the population is expected to begin within the coming months.
Currently, 93% of Rwamagana District’s population has access to clean water. Local authorities say the ultimate goal of the Karenge Waterworks expansion is to achieve universal access to safe drinking water across the district.

title: Kinshasa-DRC: Senior Military Officers Transferred to Ndolo Prison Amid Treason Investigations
excerpt: On January 7, 2026, Gen. Franck Ntumba Buamunda, former head of the military office at the presidential palace, and Gen. Maj Christian Ndaywel Okura, former head of the military intelligence service, were transferred to Ndolo military prison in Kinshasa. Gen. Ntumba had been arre
title_en: Kinshasa-DRC: Senior Military Officers Transferred to Ndolo Prison Amid Treason Investigations
excerpt_en: On January 7, 2026, Gen. Franck Ntumba Buamunda, former head of the military office at the presidential palace, and Gen. Maj Christian Ndaywel Okura, former head of the military intelligence service, were transferred to Ndolo military prison in Kinshasa. Gen. Ntumba had been arre
body_en:
On January 7, 2026, Gen. Franck Ntumba Buamunda, former head of the military office at the presidential palace, and Gen. Maj Christian Ndaywel Okura, former head of the military intelligence service, were transferred to Ndolo military prison in Kinshasa.
Gen. Ntumba had been arrested in July 2025, while Ndaywel was detained in August 2025, shortly after leaving the intelligence service. Both were initially held in the National Security Council cell during ongoing investigations. Their transfer to Ndolo marks the continuation of their cases at the High Military Court.
Other senior officers reported to have spent the night at Ndolo include Brig Gen Benjamin Katende Batubadila, Brig Gen Antoine Longondjo Lobandi, Col Jules Boele Bagolome, and Maj Jean-Lambert Embole Ngondili. The detainees face charges including conspiracy against the Head of State, treason, attempted murder, spreading rumors, and disobeying orders.
Meanwhile, Gen. Christian Tshiwewe Songesha, former Chief of Staff of the FARDC and military advisor to President Félix Tshisekedi, remains in the High Security Council cell. He has been accused of plotting to assassinate the president, and the Secretary General of the ruling UDPS party, Augustin Kabuya, stated that Tshiwewe confessed to the alleged plot.
Military expert Jean-Jacques Wondo has raised concerns that several of these detentions may be unjust or politically motivated, aimed at removing senior officers from military decision-making. Officers cited by Wondo include Gen. Freddy Kalume, Gen. Maj Frank Ngama Lebe, and Gen. Dieudonné Mutupeke Kiamata, all accused in connection with alleged plots against President Tshisekedi.

title: DRC Condemns Continued Rwandan Occupation and Expansion in the East
excerpt: Kinshasa — The Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has strongly denounced the continued occupation of parts of its national territory by Rwandan forces, accusing Kigali of progressively expanding its presence in the eastern regions of the country, particularly around U
title_en: DRC Condemns Continued Rwandan Occupation and Expansion in the East
excerpt_en: Kinshasa — The Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has strongly denounced the continued occupation of parts of its national territory by Rwandan forces, accusing Kigali of progressively expanding its presence in the eastern regions of the country, particularly around U
body_en:
Kinshasa — The Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo has strongly denounced the continued occupation of parts of its national territory by Rwandan forces, accusing Kigali of progressively expanding its presence in the eastern regions of the country, particularly around Uvira and its surrounding areas, with a southward advance.
The condemnation was made public on Wednesday, December 31, in a press release issued by the Ministry of Communication and Media. In the statement, Congolese authorities described the situation as a flagrant violation of the country’s sovereignty, a serious and repeated breach of international law, and a clear disregard for regional and international commitments.
The government further warned that the ongoing occupation is exacerbating an already fragile security and humanitarian situation, leaving civilian populations increasingly exposed to widespread violence and instability in the affected areas.
No immediate response was issued by Rwandan authorities at the time of publication.

title: Displaced Families Spend New Year in Fear and Hunger in Ituri’s Savo Plain
excerpt: Djugu Territory, Ituri | January 1, 2026 — More than a thousand residents from Bulé and neighboring villages in the Djugu territory of Ituri Province spent New Year’s Day in dire conditions after fleeing renewed clashes between the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo
title_en: Displaced Families Spend New Year in Fear and Hunger in Ituri’s Savo Plain
excerpt_en: Djugu Territory, Ituri | January 1, 2026 — More than a thousand residents from Bulé and neighboring villages in the Djugu territory of Ituri Province spent New Year’s Day in dire conditions after fleeing renewed clashes between the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo
body_en:
Djugu Territory, Ituri | January 1, 2026 — More than a thousand residents from Bulé and neighboring villages in the Djugu territory of Ituri Province spent New Year’s Day in dire conditions after fleeing renewed clashes between the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) and militias of the Convention for the Popular Revolution (CRP) led by Thomas Lubanga.
The displaced families have sought refuge in the Savo Plain, located about four kilometers north of Bulé, where they are living in extreme precarity. According to local sources, the most recent group of displaced persons arrived on Wednesday, following intensified fighting in the area.
“For more than a week now, these vulnerable people—mostly women and children—have been sleeping in the open air without food or basic necessities,” said Floribert Dezunga, one of the displaced residents.
Traditional local authorities warn that the continued armed violence in the Bulé region could trigger a major humanitarian catastrophe if urgent assistance is not provided. They are calling on national authorities and humanitarian organizations to open a humanitarian corridor to facilitate aid delivery and prevent further loss of life among the displaced population.

title: FARDC Announces Recapture of Lwanga and Kigongo in South Kivu’s Uvira Territory
excerpt: Uvira, South Kivu | December 30, 2025 The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) announced on Tuesday that they have regained control of the localities of Lwanga and Kigongo in Uvira Territory, South Kivu Province, amid ongoing fighting in the region. According
title_en: FARDC Announces Recapture of Lwanga and Kigongo in South Kivu’s Uvira Territory
excerpt_en: Uvira, South Kivu | December 30, 2025 The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) announced on Tuesday that they have regained control of the localities of Lwanga and Kigongo in Uvira Territory, South Kivu Province, amid ongoing fighting in the region. According
body_en:
Uvira, South Kivu | December 30, 2025
The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) announced on Tuesday that they have regained control of the localities of Lwanga and Kigongo in Uvira Territory, South Kivu Province, amid ongoing fighting in the region.
According to Second Lieutenant Reagan Kalonji, spokesperson for Operation Sokola 2 South in South Kivu, the latest gains follow the recapture of Makobola 1 and Makobola 2 villages earlier this week.
He further stated that at least five armed M23 fighters surrendered to FARDC forces during the operations.
Despite the army’s announcement, local sources in Uvira reported the arrival of M23 reinforcements in the area beginning Tuesday, December 29, raising concerns about a possible escalation of clashes.
On Sunday, December 28, the national military spokesperson, Major General Sylvain Ekenge, confirmed that FARDC had retaken Makobola 1 and Makobola 2 in Fizi Territory, adding that fighting was still ongoing approximately seven kilometers from the town of Uvira.
The security situation in southern South Kivu remains volatile as FARDC continues operations against the M23 rebellion, with control over several strategic localities changing hands in recent days.

title: M23 Launches Offensive to Retake Katoyi in Masisi
excerpt: North Kivu, January 2, 2026 — AFC/M23 rebels launched a new offensive early Friday morning to regain control of the town of Katoyi, the main locality of the Katoyi sector, in Masisi territory, North Kivu, according to local sources. The attack comes after the AFC/M23 lost Katoyi
title_en: M23 Launches Offensive to Retake Katoyi in Masisi
excerpt_en: North Kivu, January 2, 2026 — AFC/M23 rebels launched a new offensive early Friday morning to regain control of the town of Katoyi, the main locality of the Katoyi sector, in Masisi territory, North Kivu, according to local sources. The attack comes after the AFC/M23 lost Katoyi
body_en:
North Kivu, January 2, 2026 — AFC/M23 rebels launched a new offensive early Friday morning to regain control of the town of Katoyi, the main locality of the Katoyi sector, in Masisi territory, North Kivu, according to local sources.
The attack comes after the AFC/M23 lost Katoyi in late December 2025. Multiple sources indicate that the rebels are attempting to recapture the town, targeting four positions held by fighters of the Congolese Patriotic Resistance Group (PARECO), an ally of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (FARDC).
The fighting is mainly concentrated in the village of Kasheke, within the Nyamaboko 1 group, Osso Banyungu sector, located about seven kilometers from Katoyi’s town center.
However, gunfire was also reported in several surrounding localities, including Busurirwa (Ufamandu 1 group), Myole (Mufunyi Kibabi group, Bahunde chiefdom), and Muhairwa (Kibabi 2 group, Katoyi sector), highlighting the spread of clashes across the area.
On December 29, Wazalendo fighters from the PARECO/Strike Force regained control of Katoyi and neighboring villages—Mitimingi, Kahundu, Kasheke, and Kakoka—following intense fighting. According to military sources, the clashes resulted in several deaths on both sides, as well as the capture of 28 M23 fighters and 12 weapons.
The AFC/M23 had maintained control of the area since mid-November 2025. This latest assault marks the second attempt by the group to retake Katoyi, following an earlier, unsuccessful effort earlier in the week.

title: Late Burial of Civilian Victims Following AFC/M23 Clashes in Walungu
excerpt: Walungu, South Kivu, January 7, 2026 — The bodies of civilians killed during clashes between the AFC-M23 rebels and the Wazalendo militia in the Ikoma region of Walungu territory last Sunday were finally buried two days later. The delay came as residents of Bumbalali fled the vio
title_en: Late Burial of Civilian Victims Following AFC/M23 Clashes in Walungu
excerpt_en: Walungu, South Kivu, January 7, 2026 — The bodies of civilians killed during clashes between the AFC-M23 rebels and the Wazalendo militia in the Ikoma region of Walungu territory last Sunday were finally buried two days later. The delay came as residents of Bumbalali fled the vio
body_en:
Walungu, South Kivu, January 7, 2026 — The bodies of civilians killed during clashes between the AFC-M23 rebels and the Wazalendo militia in the Ikoma region of Walungu territory last Sunday were finally buried two days later.
The delay came as residents of Bumbalali fled the violence, leaving behind the bodies of their neighbors who had been killed by bombs. Upon returning on Tuesday, villagers discovered the corpses still lying on the ground. In total, four civilians lost their lives: three in Bumbalali and one in Mwendo. Residents reported that the bodies were already decomposing.

title: Sudan Seeks Rwanda’s Expertise in Peacebuilding and Regional Cooperation

title_en: Sudan Seeks Rwanda’s Expertise in Peacebuilding and Regional Cooperation
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 2, 2026 Sudan is looking to Rwanda as a model for peacebuilding and national reconstruction, according to Sudanese Ambassador to Rwanda, Khalid Musa Dafalla. Speaking at the Rwanda Broadcasting Agency (RBA), Ambassador Musa highlighted Sudan’s interest in learning
body_en:
Kigali, January 2, 2026
Sudan is looking to Rwanda as a model for peacebuilding and national reconstruction, according to Sudanese Ambassador to Rwanda, Khalid Musa Dafalla. Speaking at the Rwanda Broadcasting Agency (RBA), Ambassador Musa highlighted Sudan’s interest in learning from Rwanda’s experience in achieving peace, unity, and rapid development.
“Sudan needs Rwanda not only as a development partner, but also as a peacebuilding partner. Rwanda provides peace and has a strong voice in understanding Africanness,” he said.
Ambassador Musa emphasized that Sudan is eager to strengthen regional cooperation and draw on Rwanda’s expertise in managing post-conflict reconstruction, reconciliation, and governance. He praised Rwanda’s leadership under President Paul Kagame, noting its influence in Africa and its ability to guide other nations in conflict resolution.
Sudan also values Rwanda’s hospitality toward Sudanese nationals, including 4,000 individuals who fled the ongoing conflict in Sudan since 2023, and the relocation of the Sudanese University of Medical Sciences and Technology (UMST) to Rwanda. Sudanese investments in Rwanda currently exceed $20 million, spanning agriculture, healthcare, construction, and education.
In sports, Sudanese football teams displaced by the war have also been allowed to compete in the Rwandan First Division Championship, reflecting Rwanda’s commitment to regional solidarity and support.
Ambassador Musa concluded that Rwanda serves as a model of development, unity, and reconciliation, and Sudan is keen to continue building on this partnership for the benefit of both nations and the region.

title: Rwanda Launches One Stop Center Website to Streamline Investment Services
excerpt: Kigali, January 2, 2026 The Rwanda Development Board (RDB) announced that its One Stop Center (OSC) website will officially launch on January 5, 2026, consolidating a wide range of investment and trade services online to improve accessibility, speed, and transparency. The OSC web
title_en: Rwanda Launches One Stop Center Website to Streamline Investment Services
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 2, 2026 The Rwanda Development Board (RDB) announced that its One Stop Center (OSC) website will officially launch on January 5, 2026, consolidating a wide range of investment and trade services online to improve accessibility, speed, and transparency. The OSC web
body_en:
Kigali, January 2, 2026
The Rwanda Development Board (RDB) announced that its One Stop Center (OSC) website will officially launch on January 5, 2026, consolidating a wide range of investment and trade services online to improve accessibility, speed, and transparency.
The OSC website, accessible at http://onestopcentre.rdb.rw, will allow users to apply for permits, track applications, and access services previously scattered across multiple institutions.
RDB Director General Jean-Guy Afrika said the initiative will integrate over 460 services from 24 institutions, covering areas such as construction permits and agricultural processing licenses, with more services expected to be added in the coming months.
“RDB is on a journey to modernize the way it provides services through the One Stop Center. The goal is to simplify service delivery, reduce application processing times, and increase transparency,” Afrika said.
The move builds on a 2023 revamp of the One Stop Center, which aimed to centralize service provision, and reflects Rwanda’s continued commitment to fostering a favorable business environment for investors.
According to RDB, Rwanda recorded $3.2 billion (over Rwf 4,528 billion) in new investments in 2024, up from $2.4 billion in 2023, reinforcing the country’s position as a leading investment destination in the region.
By consolidating services digitally, the OSC website is expected to facilitate investor engagement, reduce bureaucracy, and accelerate project implementation across the country.

title: Rwanda Police Shoot Dead Suspect in Murder and Robbery Case
excerpt: On January 7, 2026, the Rwanda National Police in the Eastern Province reported that Dukuzumuremyi Eric, a suspect wanted for the robbery and murder of a motorcyclist in Kirehe District, was shot dead after attempting to flee from law enforcement. According to Eastern Province Po
title_en: Rwanda Police Shoot Dead Suspect in Murder and Robbery Case
excerpt_en: On January 7, 2026, the Rwanda National Police in the Eastern Province reported that Dukuzumuremyi Eric, a suspect wanted for the robbery and murder of a motorcyclist in Kirehe District, was shot dead after attempting to flee from law enforcement. According to Eastern Province Po
body_en:
On January 7, 2026, the Rwanda National Police in the Eastern Province reported that Dukuzumuremyi Eric, a suspect wanted for the robbery and murder of a motorcyclist in Kirehe District, was shot dead after attempting to flee from law enforcement.
According to Eastern Province Police Spokesperson SP Hamdun Twizeyimana, Dukuzumuremyi had previously ambushed a motorcyclist on January 2, 2026, killing him and stealing his motorcycle. Following the attack, the police launched a search with help from local residents, eventually locating the suspect in Nyagatare District.
On the morning of January 7, Dukuzumuremyi was being escorted by officers to reveal the locations where he had hidden stolen items. During the process, he attempted to escape, prompting the police to open fire, resulting in his death.
SP Twizeyimana urged the public to refrain from theft, reminding citizens that security forces remain vigilant and that stealing is a serious crime with legal consequences.

title_en: Renewed Clashes in Masisi: AFC/M23 and Wazalendo Battle Amid Civilian Casualties
excerpt_en: Masisi, North Kivu – 11 January 2026: Fighting has resumed in Masisi Territory between the AFC/M23 rebels and the Wazalendo coalition, aligned with the DRC government. According to local reports, clashes began at midnight in the Kazinga area, with residents hearing heavy and ligh
body_en:
Masisi, North Kivu – 11 January 2026: Fighting has resumed in Masisi Territory between the AFC/M23 rebels and the Wazalendo coalition, aligned with the DRC government. According to local reports, clashes began at midnight in the Kazinga area, with residents hearing heavy and light weapons being fired.
Sources say the Wazalendo forces are attempting to prevent AFC/M23 from expanding control over additional areas, including the first and second Nyamaboko groups.
This flare-up follows a FARDC attack on 2 January 2026, during which six civilians were killed and 41 others injured in a populated area of Masisi. Both AFC/M23 and the United Nations peacekeeping mission (MONUSCO) condemned the January 2 attack.
The renewed clashes highlight the ongoing instability in North Kivu, where armed confrontations continue to threaten civilians and hamper peace efforts in the region.
Conclusion
Between late 2025 and early 2026, Rwanda and the surrounding region are characterized by a dual focus on internal development and complex regional diplomacy. Internally, Rwanda is experiencing significant growth in private investment and infrastructure, exemplified by the inauguration of the 7 billion Frw GLADS Apartment and the expansion of the Karenge Waterworks to meet increasing demand for clean water. The government is also modernizing economic services through initiatives like the Rwanda Development Board’s One Stop Center website to further streamline investment.
On the diplomatic and security front, the period is marked by several key developments:
Regional Influence and Cooperation: Rwanda continues to be viewed as a model for peacebuilding, with nations like Sudan actively seeking its expertise for national reconstruction. Furthermore, Rwandan peacekeepers continue to receive international recognition for their professionalism in missions like MINUSCA in the Central African Republic.
Ongoing DRC Tensions: Relations between Rwanda and the Democratic Republic of the Congo remain strained. The DRC government faces internal and external criticism for its handling of security in the East, with ongoing conflicts involving the AFC/M23 coalition. While there are shifting efforts to restart mediation—moving between Qatari-led and Angolan-led frameworks—the path to a lasting peace remains uncertain due to deep-seated mistrust and conflicting negotiation strategies.
Strategic Resource Management: Rwanda is proactively addressing future challenges, such as the need to expand its national fuel reserves to accommodate rising consumption driven by industrial growth and increased vehicle use.
In summary, while Rwanda is successfully advancing its domestic economic and developmental agenda, it remains deeply involved in—and affected by—the persistent security challenges and diplomatic maneuvering in the broader Great Lakes Region.
By Jeff Buleli

title: Corneille Nangaa Delivers End-of-Year Message, Calls for Unity and Justice in DRC
excerpt: Kinshasa / RDC – December 31, 2025 Corneille Nangaa, coordinator of the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) and M23, addressed the Congolese people in a formal end-of-year message, posted on social media, reflecting on 2025 and outlining priorities for 2026. Speaking from a formal office
title_en: Corneille Nangaa Delivers End-of-Year Message, Calls for Unity and Justice in DRC
excerpt_en: Kinshasa / RDC – December 31, 2025 Corneille Nangaa, coordinator of the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) and M23, addressed the Congolese people in a formal end-of-year message, posted on social media, reflecting on 2025 and outlining priorities for 2026. Speaking from a formal office
body_en:
Kinshasa / RDC – December 31, 2025
Corneille Nangaa, coordinator of the Alliance Fleuve Congo (AFC) and M23, addressed the Congolese people in a formal end-of-year message, posted on social media, reflecting on 2025 and outlining priorities for 2026.
Speaking from a formal office setting with AFC and DRC flags in the background, Nangaa began by paying tribute to fallen fighters and the Congolese Revolutionary Army for their sacrifices in the struggle for freedom. He also thanked AFC political personnel and called for the voluntary return of Congolese refugees, including those recently expelled to Burundi.
He highlighted progress in areas “liberated” under AFC/M23 control, emphasizing:
Restoration of peace and security
Establishment of functional administration
Operational justice system
Resilient local economy and emerging financial institutions
Infrastructure development
Mass return of internally displaced persons
Resumption of agriculture, schools, and hospitals
Nangaa positioned the AFC/M23 as a credible alternative to the current government.
He sharply criticized the Kinshasa government, accusing it of betraying 2025 peace agreements, including joint communiqués, prisoner release mechanisms, and ceasefire monitoring. Key allegations included:
No political prisoners released
Repeated ceasefire violations, including bombardments of civilians
Official promotion of ethnic hate speech, particularly against Kinyarwanda-speaking Tutsis and Swahili speakers
Tribal purges within the army
Massacres, arbitrary arrests, endemic corruption, and looting of natural resources
Nangaa also highlighted mass popular protests across multiple cities and called for national unity, an end to impunity, and sustainable peace based on truth.
Looking ahead to 2026, he pledged continued struggle for freedom, justice, peace, and the reconstruction of the Congolese state. He concluded with New Year wishes, envisioning a united, peaceful, and prosperous Congo.
The message was delivered in a solemn, structured, and presidential tone, underscoring the AFC/M23’s political narrative and priorities for the upcoming year.

title_en: DRC – Monkeypox Cases Declining: Around 300 Weekly Reports
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 1, 2026 The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is currently reporting approximately 300 cases of monkeypox per week, a significant decrease compared to previous months, according to Christian Ngandu, coordinator of the Public Health Emergency Operations Center (
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 1, 2026
The Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) is currently reporting approximately 300 cases of monkeypox per week, a significant decrease compared to previous months, according to Christian Ngandu, coordinator of the Public Health Emergency Operations Center (PHOOC) at the National Institute of Public Health (INSP).
During a press briefing in Kinshasa on December 31, 2025, Ngandu explained that 19 health zones reported cases in December, down from initial expectations of 401 zones between 2024 and November 2025.
“Initially, we were receiving about 2,000 notifications per week, but currently, we have between 250 and 300,” he said, highlighting the encouraging trend in the reduction of new cases.
Most of the reported cases are concentrated in North Kivu and South Kivu, areas affected by insecurity, as well as in Sankuru.
Health authorities continue to monitor the situation closely and urge communities to remain vigilant and follow recommended public health measures to prevent further spread.

title: FARDC Accuses Close Associates of President Tshisekedi of Leading Mobondo Armed Group
excerpt: Kinshasa / Kwilu, DRC — December 28, 2025 The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have accused individuals close to President Félix Tshisekedi of leading the Mobondo armed group, which has destabilized western parts of the country for nearly three years. The
title_en: FARDC Accuses Close Associates of President Tshisekedi of Leading Mobondo Armed Group
excerpt_en: Kinshasa / Kwilu, DRC — December 28, 2025 The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have accused individuals close to President Félix Tshisekedi of leading the Mobondo armed group, which has destabilized western parts of the country for nearly three years. The
body_en:
Kinshasa / Kwilu, DRC — December 28, 2025
The Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) have accused individuals close to President Félix Tshisekedi of leading the Mobondo armed group, which has destabilized western parts of the country for nearly three years.
The allegations were made by Captain Anthony Mwalushay, spokesman for military operations in provinces including Kwilu, during a press briefing on December 28, 2025, following weekend clashes in which five FARDC soldiers were killed.
According to Capt. Mwalushay, some individuals who publicly claim allegiance to President Tshisekedi are allegedly involved in commanding Mobondo fighters, while others are said to be collaborating with armed groups operating in eastern DRC.
“We have information about some who are working with armed groups in the east,” Mwalushay said. “For Mobondo, the problem is that many of those who support it are often seen behind the President of the Republic. During the day they appear harmless, but at night they lead Mobondo.”
The FARDC spokesperson stated that during the recent fighting, 15 Mobondo fighters were killed, and several others were arrested. He added that some detainees allegedly identified political and institutional figures as being linked to the group.
“Our institutions are investigating before releasing names,” Mwalushay said. “If Kinshasa supports those who are secretly behind Mobondo for political reasons, we soldiers will continue to do our job with weapons.”
The Mobondo movement, largely composed of members of the Yaka ethnic group, emerged in June 2022, initially targeting the FARDC and the Teke community, primarily over land disputes.
Since then, Mobondo attacks have severely affected security in rural areas surrounding Kinshasa and in neighboring provinces, including Mai-Ndombe, Kwilu, Kongo Central, and Kwango, resulting in thousands of deaths and widespread displacement.
In recent months, Mobondo fighters have reportedly attempted to expand their operations into peri-urban areas of Kinshasa, including Maluku and Kingakati. The government, however, says it has taken strong preventive measures to prevent further deterioration of security in the national capital.

title: DRC Defense Minister Sets Reconquest of Occupied Territories as Top Priority for 2026
excerpt: Kinshasa | January 1, 2026 — The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, has declared the restoration of state authority across the national territory and the reconquest of currently occupied areas as his top priorities for 2026. In a New
title_en: DRC Defense Minister Sets Reconquest of Occupied Territories as Top Priority for 2026
excerpt_en: Kinshasa | January 1, 2026 — The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, has declared the restoration of state authority across the national territory and the reconquest of currently occupied areas as his top priorities for 2026. In a New
body_en:
Kinshasa | January 1, 2026 — The Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of National Defense, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita, has declared the restoration of state authority across the national territory and the reconquest of currently occupied areas as his top priorities for 2026.
In a New Year message addressed to the nation, Kabombo underscored the determination of the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC) to defend national sovereignty and ensure the protection of civilians throughout the country.
He paid tribute to soldiers who have fallen in the line of duty, praising the FARDC’s continued commitment and loyalty to the national flag. “Darkness will not reign forever,” he said, expressing optimism that 2026 will be a year of hope and renewal for the Congolese people.
The Defense Minister reaffirmed his commitment to peace, security, and development, while calling on citizens to show solidarity, courage, and confidence in the future.
On December 31, a day earlier, Guy Kabombo Muadiamvita carried out a working visit to Kalemie, in Tanganyika Province, where he assessed the operational capacity of the FARDC, with particular attention to military infrastructure.
During the visit, he chaired a closed-door strategic meeting at the headquarters of the 22nd Naval Force Group, in the presence of the Deputy Chief of Staff in charge of Operations and Intelligence. Discussions focused on security challenges and operational issues facing the unit.
The visit concluded with an inspection of logistical and technical facilities, including maintenance and operational support structures, aimed at evaluating working conditions for military personnel and identifying priority needs to strengthen defense capabilities in the region.

Kinshasa, January 7, 2026 — Lieutenant Colonel Mak Hazukay Mongba has been appointed interim spokesperson for the Armed Forces of the Democratic Republic of Congo (FARDC), according to a service note signed by the FARDC Chief of Staff.

title: DRC Conflict: AFC/M23 Criticizes Tshisekedi’s Government for Blaming International Community
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 2, 2026 The AFC/M23 Alliance has sharply criticized President Félix Tshisekedi’s government for attributing the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s ongoing insecurity to foreign actors, calling it a tactic to hide domestic failures. Political Coordinator Corneill
title_en: DRC Conflict: AFC/M23 Criticizes Tshisekedi’s Government for Blaming International Community
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 2, 2026 The AFC/M23 Alliance has sharply criticized President Félix Tshisekedi’s government for attributing the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s ongoing insecurity to foreign actors, calling it a tactic to hide domestic failures. Political Coordinator Corneill
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 2, 2026
The AFC/M23 Alliance has sharply criticized President Félix Tshisekedi’s government for attributing the Democratic Republic of the Congo’s ongoing insecurity to foreign actors, calling it a tactic to hide domestic failures.
Political Coordinator Corneille Nangaa said the Kinshasa administration is attempting to shift responsibility for killings, massacres, corruption, ethnic conflicts, urban crime, poverty, and other systemic issues onto the international community instead of addressing the root causes.
“The problems that exist are the Congolese themselves. Trying to blame them on the international community is to focus on the symptoms of the disease without addressing the root of the problem. It is a hypocritical plan by the Kinshasa regime to hide the failure of its government,” Nangaa stated.
He added that efforts to petition other countries will not solve the country’s structural problems, and that the AFC/M23’s approach emphasizes transparency, truth, accountability, and justice.
Nangaa underscored that the movement’s goal is not revenge, but a lasting solution for the Congolese people, based on reconciliation, unity, non-discrimination, and law enforcement.
“The time for deception, lies, and false promises is over. From now on, the Congolese stand firm, determined and with great will. The year 2026 will be the year to strengthen our struggle for liberation, justice, peace, and the reconstruction of the State,” he said.
He also confirmed that Doha-facilitated talks between the DRC government and AFC/M23 have failed to yield a viable solution, and noted that the Tshisekedi administration has refused further negotiations, whether in person or virtually.
This statement highlights the deepening mistrust between the Congolese government and the AFC/M23 Alliance, raising concerns over the prospects for peace and stability in eastern DRC.

title: Rwanda – GLADS Apartment Inaugurated in Gasabo District at 7 Billion Frw Investment
excerpt: Gasabo, December 30, 2025 Entrepreneur Gafurama Wilson celebrated the inauguration of his 7 billion Frw GLADS Apartment, financed by the Bank of Kigali, in Ndera Sector, Gasabo District. The multi-use building marks a major milestone in private investment and urban development in
title_en: Rwanda – GLADS Apartment Inaugurated in Gasabo District at 7 Billion Frw Investment
excerpt_en: Gasabo, December 30, 2025 Entrepreneur Gafurama Wilson celebrated the inauguration of his 7 billion Frw GLADS Apartment, financed by the Bank of Kigali, in Ndera Sector, Gasabo District. The multi-use building marks a major milestone in private investment and urban development in
body_en:
Gasabo, December 30, 2025
Entrepreneur Gafurama Wilson celebrated the inauguration of his 7 billion Frw GLADS Apartment, financed by the Bank of Kigali, in Ndera Sector, Gasabo District. The multi-use building marks a major milestone in private investment and urban development in Rwanda.
The GLADS Apartment features 15 commercial services, including:
A hall with a 1,500-person capacity
A sauna and massage room
Private swimming pool
Multiple bedrooms
A market, gym, hair salon, restaurant, and bar
Gafurama Wilson highlighted the importance of ideas, mentorship, and perseverance in realizing ambitious projects. “Many people prioritize money, but action starts with an idea. When you have a good idea, it helps you find money,” he said, urging other Rwandan investors to seize opportunities and have the courage to develop large-scale projects locally.
Bank of Kigali, represented by Mukunzi Darius, Head of Small Business and Microfinance, emphasized the bank’s commitment to supporting Rwandan entrepreneurs. “Everyone can find themselves at Bank of Kigali, where at every branch there is a project expert ready to help,” he stated.
Safari Alphonse, in charge of Quality Assurance in Hotels and Tourism at the Rwanda Development Board (RDB), praised the project, noting it strengthens national development and creates numerous jobs. “It brings development to the country directly and indirectly,” he said.
This inauguration underscores Rwanda’s growing entrepreneurial spirit, public-private collaboration, and efforts to foster local investment in large-scale infrastructure.

The court ruled that the grounds for appeal presented by Djihad were unfounded and upheld the earlier decision ordering his continued detention.
Regarding Ishimwe Patrick, also known as Pazzo Man, the court found that the reasons cited by the Kicukiro Primary Court to place him in provisional detention were justified, and therefore rejected his request for immediate release on bail.
For Ishimwe François Xavier, the judges concluded that there were serious grounds to suspect his involvement in the sale of pornographic videos. As a result, the court upheld the decision to keep him in temporary detention.
The court also dismissed the arguments raised by Kwizera Nestor (Pappy Nesta), finding them without merit.
However, Kalisa John, widely known as K. John, who is also implicated in the same case, was released on bail and will stand trial while out of custody.
The four detainees are accused of distributing explicit videos involving Yampano and his girlfriend. All had previously expressed dissatisfaction with the ruling of the Kicukiro Primary Court, arguing that it failed to take into account certain elements presented during earlier proceedings.

title: Angolan President Lourenço Urges DRC Government and AFC/M23 to End Hostilities
excerpt: Luanda, Angola – 8 January 2026: Angolan President and African Union Chairperson, João Lourenço, has called on the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government and the AFC/M23 coalition to immediately cease hostilities and focus on a peaceful resolution to the ongoing conflict i
title_en: Angolan President Lourenço Urges DRC Government and AFC/M23 to End Hostilities
excerpt_en: Luanda, Angola – 8 January 2026: Angolan President and African Union Chairperson, João Lourenço, has called on the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government and the AFC/M23 coalition to immediately cease hostilities and focus on a peaceful resolution to the ongoing conflict i
body_en:
Luanda, Angola – 8 January 2026: Angolan President and African Union Chairperson, João Lourenço, has called on the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) government and the AFC/M23 coalition to immediately cease hostilities and focus on a peaceful resolution to the ongoing conflict in eastern DRC.
President Lourenço made the statement following a meeting with DRC President Félix Tshisekedi, who traveled to Luanda to discuss strategies to restore peace and security in the region.
Expressing concern over the continued instability and displacement in eastern DRC, Lourenço warned that ongoing fighting is undermining international peace initiatives, including talks previously held in Washington and Doha.
He urged all parties to:
Cease hostilities immediately
Respect existing agreements
Prioritize the interests of the Congolese people Lourenço also called on the international community to support efforts aimed at stabilizing eastern DRC.
Tshisekedi has requested that new peace talks bring together representatives from all Congolese groups, including the AFC/M23, with discussions to be held in Kinshasa under the facilitation of the Angolan government.
According to reports, Lourenço has accepted Tshisekedi’s request, engaging with opposition figures in the DRC to prepare for the talks. Tshisekedi emphasized that the AFC/M23 must first observe a ceasefire, while the DRC government will verify compliance before formal negotiations begin.
This development signals renewed efforts to restart dialogue in the eastern DRC conflict, with Angola taking a central mediation role.

title: DRC–U.S. Strategic Partnership: Government Rejects Claims of “Selling Off” National Interests
excerpt: Kinshasa | December 31, 2025 The Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has strongly denied allegations that the strategic partnership agreement signed with the United States constitutes a sell-off of the country’s economic or mineral interests. Speaking during a jo
title_en: DRC–U.S. Strategic Partnership: Government Rejects Claims of “Selling Off” National Interests
excerpt_en: Kinshasa | December 31, 2025 The Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has strongly denied allegations that the strategic partnership agreement signed with the United States constitutes a sell-off of the country’s economic or mineral interests. Speaking during a jo
body_en:
Kinshasa | December 31, 2025
The Government of the Democratic Republic of Congo (DRC) has strongly denied allegations that the strategic partnership agreement signed with the United States constitutes a sell-off of the country’s economic or mineral interests.
Speaking during a joint press briefing on Tuesday, December 30, Deputy Prime Minister in charge of the National Economy, Daniel Mukoko Samba, alongside the Minister of Communication and Media, Patrick Muyaya, sought to clarify the economic component of the Washington Agreement, signed on December 4, 2025, under the auspices of U.S. President Donald Trump.
“This is neither a deal, nor a contract, nor a document intended to sell out the interests of the DRC,” Mukoko Samba stated, responding to widespread criticism circulating in political circles, civil society, and online media.
A Framework Agreement, Not a Transaction
According to the government, the agreement should be understood as a strategic and legal framework for cooperation, rather than a transactional document involving the transfer of assets or concessions.
“This is a technical framework agreement defining areas of cooperation—economy and trade, security, governance, education, science, and technology—without ceding a single mine, designating a single investor, or awarding any contract,” Mukoko emphasized.
He categorically rejected claims of a “fire sale” of Congolese mineral resources, stating that no mining concessions, no preferential pricing, and no derogation from Congolese laws are mentioned in the agreement.
Major Development Projects Highlighted
Mukoko Samba underlined that the partnership aims to support peace, security, and economic development, with the prospect of large-scale job creation. He cited flagship projects included in the cooperation framework, notably:
The Grand Inga hydropower project
The Lobito Corridor
Key national road infrastructure projects
Government officials stressed that the agreement goes beyond the mining sector, encompassing defense, security, and governance reforms, positioning it as a long-term development partnership.
Monitoring and Governance Mechanisms
To ensure transparency and implementation, the Washington Agreement provides for the establishment of a joint steering committee, composed of five representatives from each country. The committee is expected to convene within 90 days of the agreement’s signing, with evaluations scheduled every three years.
In the event of disputes, Mukoko Samba noted that Prime Minister Judith Suminwa would serve as the arbitration authority, providing an institutional mechanism for dialogue and resolution.
Government Pushback Against “Misinformation”
Minister Patrick Muyaya echoed these clarifications, accusing critics of spreading misinformation based on emotional or partial readings of a public and technical document. The executive branch insists that the agreement in no way compromises Congolese sovereignty.
As debates continue within political and civil society circles, the government says it remains committed to transparency and to defending national interests while pursuing strategic international partnerships.

title: Journalists in Bunia Protest the Murder of Colleague Thierry Lole

title_en: Journalists in Bunia Protest the Murder of Colleague Thierry Lole
excerpt_en: Bunia, Ituri, DRC | December 29, 2025 Journalists in Bunia held a march on Monday morning, ending at the Ituri provincial governor's office, to protest the murder of Thierry Lole, a colleague at the Congolese National Radio and Television (RTNC). Lole was killed at his home by as
body_en:
Bunia, Ituri, DRC | December 29, 2025
Journalists in Bunia held a march on Monday morning, ending at the Ituri provincial governor's office, to protest the murder of Thierry Lole, a colleague at the Congolese National Radio and Television (RTNC). Lole was killed at his home by assailants armed with machetes during the night of Sunday to Monday, according to local sources.
Dozens of media professionals demanded a swift investigation during the demonstration.
According to protesters, criminals armed with machetes broke into Lole’s home around 2:00 a.m., striking him severely on the head before fleeing without stealing anything. Lole later died from his injuries at Salama Hospital on Monday morning.
During a meeting with the provincial governor, journalists called for an investigation to identify and bring to justice the perpetrators, requested that funeral expenses be covered, and advocated for a media blackout to highlight the danger facing journalists.
Protesters also cited increasing attacks against journalists in Ituri, referencing a recent kidnapping of a journalist, who was held hostage for four days, followed by the murder of his child by unknown assailants.
Provincial authorities stated that an investigation is underway to apprehend those responsible and promised to cover funeral expenses.

title: APUKIN Suspends Classes Following Assassination of Professor Abata
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 9, 2026 — The Association of Professors of the University of Kinshasa (APUKIN) has suspended all academic activities until Wednesday, January 14, following the assassination of Professor Matthieu Abata. The decision was made during an extraordinary general assem
title_en: APUKIN Suspends Classes Following Assassination of Professor Abata
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 9, 2026 — The Association of Professors of the University of Kinshasa (APUKIN) has suspended all academic activities until Wednesday, January 14, following the assassination of Professor Matthieu Abata. The decision was made during an extraordinary general assem
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 9, 2026 — The Association of Professors of the University of Kinshasa (APUKIN) has suspended all academic activities until Wednesday, January 14, following the assassination of Professor Matthieu Abata. The decision was made during an extraordinary general assembly held on Friday, January 9, at APUKIN headquarters.
The association also announced plans for a sit-in on Monday, January 12, in front of the Ministry of the Interior and Security to demand enhanced protection for faculty and researchers.
David Lubo, President of APUKIN, declared: “No activities will take place on university campuses. We will meet again on Wednesday to assess the situation. APUKIN and allied institutions have decided to organize a sit-in this Monday, January 12, 2026, in front of the offices of the Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior.”
Professor Matthieu Abata was shot dead by armed bandits on Thursday, January 8, during a nighttime raid on his home in the Plateau des Professeurs neighborhood of Lemba, Kinshasa.
APUKIN is calling on the government to cover funeral expenses and ensure the well-being of his widow and children, highlighting the urgent need for better security measures for university staff.

title: DRC – Kinshasa: Over 460 Suspected Urban Gang Members Arrested During Operation Ndobo
excerpt: Kinshasa, January 1, 2026 Authorities in Kinshasa reported the arrest of approximately 464 suspected members of urban gangs, locally known as “kulunas”, during end-of-year festivities as part of Operation Ndobo. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior and Security, Jac
title_en: DRC – Kinshasa: Over 460 Suspected Urban Gang Members Arrested During Operation Ndobo
excerpt_en: Kinshasa, January 1, 2026 Authorities in Kinshasa reported the arrest of approximately 464 suspected members of urban gangs, locally known as “kulunas”, during end-of-year festivities as part of Operation Ndobo. Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior and Security, Jac
body_en:
Kinshasa, January 1, 2026
Authorities in Kinshasa reported the arrest of approximately 464 suspected members of urban gangs, locally known as “kulunas”, during end-of-year festivities as part of Operation Ndobo.
Deputy Prime Minister and Minister of the Interior and Security, Jacquemain Shabani Lukoo, announced the figures following inspections of several police stations in the capital.
The breakdown of arrests across Kinshasa districts is as follows:
Masina (Tshangu): 242 arrests
Limete: 56 arrests
Kalamu: 51 arrests
Mont-Ngafula: 45 arrests
Gombe (Camp Lufungula): ~40 arrests
Kintambo: 30 arrests
Total: 464 individuals apprehended
Masina district recorded the highest number of arrests, nearly half of the total, highlighting the scale of gang-related activity in the area.
Operation Ndobo, currently active in 10 of the DRC’s 26 provinces, is part of ongoing efforts by the government to combat urban crime, protect citizens, and safeguard property across the country.
Authorities have emphasized that the operation will continue nationwide to maintain security and public order.

title_en: Boat Shipwreck in Bolomba: At Least 6 Dead, Several Missing
excerpt_en: Bolomba, Équateur Province, January 6, 2026 — A tragic boat accident occurred on the night of January 5–6 on the Congo River, between the Dianga chiefdom and the village of Bokuma in Bolomba territory, leaving at least six dead, several missing, and 73 survivors. A significant ca
body_en:
Bolomba, Équateur Province, January 6, 2026 — A tragic boat accident occurred on the night of January 5–6 on the Congo River, between the Dianga chiefdom and the village of Bokuma in Bolomba territory, leaving at least six dead, several missing, and 73 survivors. A significant cargo was also lost, and the number of casualties could rise.
According to reports, the disaster was caused by a collision between a motorized pirogue carrying passengers and a whaleboat (registered H/B Zulu). Survivors who reached Mbandaka are facing difficulties returning to Bolomba.
This incident is part of a series of recurring accidents on the Congo River, often caused by overloaded boats, nighttime navigation, and lack of safety equipment.
Tragic Precedents

title: Ambassador Bazivamo Conveys President Kagame’s Message to Rwandans in Brazzaville
excerpt: Brazzaville, Republic of Congo — Sunday, December 28, 2025 The Secretary General of the RPF Inkotanyi, Ambassador Christophe Bazivamo, met with Rwandans living in Brazzaville during a working visit to the Republic of Congo, where he conveyed a message from President Paul Kagame.
title_en: Ambassador Bazivamo Conveys President Kagame’s Message to Rwandans in Brazzaville
excerpt_en: Brazzaville, Republic of Congo — Sunday, December 28, 2025 The Secretary General of the RPF Inkotanyi, Ambassador Christophe Bazivamo, met with Rwandans living in Brazzaville during a working visit to the Republic of Congo, where he conveyed a message from President Paul Kagame.
body_en:
Brazzaville, Republic of Congo — Sunday, December 28, 2025
The Secretary General of the RPF Inkotanyi, Ambassador Christophe Bazivamo, met with Rwandans living in Brazzaville during a working visit to the Republic of Congo, where he conveyed a message from President Paul Kagame.
According to a statement released by the RPF Inkotanyi, Amb. Bazivamo delivered the greetings of President Kagame, wishing the Rwandan diaspora good health and continued progress, while outlining the development programs Rwanda has committed to. He emphasized that Rwandans abroad are expected to play a direct role in contributing to the country’s national development.
The ambassador reaffirmed that Rwanda continues to support its citizens abroad in their development initiatives and remains ready to assist them whenever possible. He encouraged the diaspora to uphold Rwandan values, particularly teamwork and honesty.
Amb. Bazivamo concluded the meeting by extending New Year 2026 wishes to the Rwandan community.
During his stay in Brazzaville, the ambassador also participated in the sixth ordinary congress of the ruling Parti Congolais du Travail (PCT), to which he was officially invited. He highlighted the strong people-centered leadership shared by the PCT and the RPF Inkotanyi, expressing willingness to further strengthen relations between the two political parties and enhance bilateral cooperation between Rwanda and Congo-Brazzaville.
The two countries maintain longstanding diplomatic and political relations, reinforced by Rwanda’s opening of its embassy in Brazzaville in 2016. In 2011, both nations signed several cooperation agreements covering sectors such as air transport, tourism, energy, security, justice, environment, and fisheries.
Bilateral ties deepened further in 2023, when President Denis Sassou Nguesso paid an official visit to Rwanda, shortly after Congo-Brazzaville introduced visa-free entry for Rwandan citizens, allowing visas to be obtained upon arrival and free of charge. During that visit, eight new cooperation agreements were signed, adding to the 25 agreements concluded in April 2022 during President Kagame’s visit to Brazzaville.

title: DRC Cabinet Issues Warning on Government Communication After Minister Criticizes Army
excerpt: Kinshasa – 8 January 2026: Following critical remarks about the DRC army and intelligence by Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Muhindo Nzangi Butondo, President Félix Tshisekedi and Prime Minister Judith Suminwa have issued strict instructions to government officials rega
title_en: DRC Cabinet Issues Warning on Government Communication After Minister Criticizes Army
excerpt_en: Kinshasa – 8 January 2026: Following critical remarks about the DRC army and intelligence by Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Muhindo Nzangi Butondo, President Félix Tshisekedi and Prime Minister Judith Suminwa have issued strict instructions to government officials rega
body_en:
Kinshasa – 8 January 2026: Following critical remarks about the DRC army and intelligence by Minister of Agriculture and Food Security Muhindo Nzangi Butondo, President Félix Tshisekedi and Prime Minister Judith Suminwa have issued strict instructions to government officials regarding public communication.
At a Cabinet meeting on 8 January, Prime Minister Suminwa emphasized that all government statements must be reliable, properly supervised, and aligned with official policy, particularly on sensitive topics such as military operations, security, public unity, and foreign affairs. She warned that violations of this communication protocol would not be tolerated.
Suminwa stressed that any statements or media appearances by ministers should first be reviewed in coordination with the Minister of Information and relevant offices of the Presidency and Prime Minister to avoid insecurity or diplomatic issues.
The Cabinet meeting followed remarks by Minister Butondo on 5 January 2026, in an interview on the Bosolo na Politik YouTube channel, in which he criticized the FARDC (Armed Forces of the DRC) for fleeing before AFC/M23 forces took Uvira. He stated:
"Give me an example of the capture of Uvira. They announced the capture of Uvira but M23 was still in Luvungi. They tweeted, everyone heard that Uvira had been captured, they left Uvira while the enemy was still 30 kilometers away."
President Tshisekedi and Prime Minister Suminwa indicated that government officials must exercise caution in public comments and ensure all statements reflect a positive image of the country and align with their responsibilities.

excerpt: Kigali, January 2026 The High Council of the Judiciary has taken decisive action against corruption within Rwanda’s courts, permanently dismissing two judges and two court clerks and suspending another judge for six months without pay. These measures, aimed at reinforcing integri
title_en: Rwanda: Judiciary Shake-Up – Two Judges and Court Clerks Permanently Dismissed Over Corruption
excerpt_en: Kigali, January 2026 The High Council of the Judiciary has taken decisive action against corruption within Rwanda’s courts, permanently dismissing two judges and two court clerks and suspending another judge for six months without pay. These measures, aimed at reinforcing integri
body_en:
Kigali, January 2026
The High Council of the Judiciary has taken decisive action against corruption within Rwanda’s courts, permanently dismissing two judges and two court clerks and suspending another judge for six months without pay. These measures, aimed at reinforcing integrity in the judicial system, were announced following a meeting chaired by Chief Justice Mukantaganzwa Domitilla, President of the Supreme Court.
Key Dismissals and Suspensions
Kamanzi Dalaus – former High Court judge
Hategekimana Zozime – former Mukamira Primary Court judge
Murenzi Prosper – former Chief Registrar, Nyakabuye Primary Court
Masengesho Céline – Registrar, Nyarugenge High Court (dismissed for leaving post without cause)
Hamenyimana Télesphore – Judge, Karongi High Court (suspended 6 months without pay for delaying cases and judgments)
All dismissed personnel were accused of corruption-related offences or misconduct affecting judicial integrity.
New Appointments and Reassignments
The council also appointed 15 individuals to key judicial roles to strengthen the system:
Nsengiyumva Jean Claude – President of the High Court, Rusizi Chamber
Giraneza Clémentine – President, Rusizi Intermediate Court
Umubeyeyi Francine – Vice President, Gicumbi Intermediate Court
Byukusenge Marie Claire – Advisor, Office of the Vice President of the Supreme Court
Bandora Jean Baptiste & Murererehe Saouda – Court Inspectors
Several judges and registrars were assigned to high and lower courts across the country, including Nyagatare and Muhoza Primary Courts.
The council also approved the resignation of Mukaburega Marie Claire, formerly a judge at Nyarugenge Primary Court.
These moves underscore Rwanda’s commitment to transparency, accountability, and restoring public trust in its judicial institutions, sending a clear message that corruption and dereliction of duty will not be tolerated.

title: Burundi Sends Troops Back to Fizi Amid Alleged Threats to Banyamulenge Civilians
excerpt: Fizi, DRC – 8 January 2026: Burundi has redeployed troops to areas inhabited by the Banyamulenge in the Democratic Republic of Congo, prompting condemnation from the armed group MRDP-Twirwaneho, which opposes the DRC government. According to Col Kamasa Ndakize Welcome, spokesman
title_en: Burundi Sends Troops Back to Fizi Amid Alleged Threats to Banyamulenge Civilians
excerpt_en: Fizi, DRC – 8 January 2026: Burundi has redeployed troops to areas inhabited by the Banyamulenge in the Democratic Republic of Congo, prompting condemnation from the armed group MRDP-Twirwaneho, which opposes the DRC government. According to Col Kamasa Ndakize Welcome, spokesman
body_en:
Fizi, DRC – 8 January 2026: Burundi has redeployed troops to areas inhabited by the Banyamulenge in the Democratic Republic of Congo, prompting condemnation from the armed group MRDP-Twirwaneho, which opposes the DRC government.
According to Col Kamasa Ndakize Welcome, spokesman for Twirwaneho, Burundian forces, led by officers including one named Nshimirimana, returned to the Bibokoboko and Point-Zéro areas with intentions to control the mountainous region.
He said: "MRDP-Twirwaneho strongly condemns this evil plan of foreign forces, which only aims to attack Banyamulenge civilians in Bibokoboko and Minembwe and block their access, which will make their situation worse."
MRDP-Twirwaneho claimed that since March 2025, Burundian troops, collaborating with the DRC government, Wazalendo groups, and FDLR forces, have reportedly killed and tortured civilians, abducted individuals, committed sexual violence, and looted property.
Since October 2025, the Banyamulenge in Minembwe have faced worsening conditions, with blocked roads to markets and health centers, causing shortages of basic goods and a spike in deaths, particularly among children under five due to lack of medical care.
After the AFC/M23 coalition captured Uvira and much of the Ruzizi Valley in December 2025, many Burundian troops temporarily returned home. Recent reports indicate that they have now redeployed to Fizi, including the town of Baraka, to resume joint operations with DRC forces.
MRDP-Twirwaneho warned that it will not tolerate the presence of these troops while civilian security and property remain at risk.
This development highlights the ongoing regional complexities in eastern DRC, with foreign forces and local militias continuing to impact the safety and livelihood of vulnerable communities.

title: Media | Confederation of Sahel States Launches AES Television in Bamako
excerpt: Bamako, December 23, 2025 The Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) officially inaugurated AES Television on Tuesday, December 23, 2025, in Bamako, marking a major step in the development of a sovereign confederal media platform serving the Sahel region. The c
title_en: Media | Confederation of Sahel States Launches AES Television in Bamako
excerpt_en: Bamako, December 23, 2025 The Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) officially inaugurated AES Television on Tuesday, December 23, 2025, in Bamako, marking a major step in the development of a sovereign confederal media platform serving the Sahel region. The c
body_en:
Bamako, December 23, 2025
The Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES) officially inaugurated AES Television on Tuesday, December 23, 2025, in Bamako, marking a major step in the development of a sovereign confederal media platform serving the Sahel region.
The ceremony was led by Captain Ibrahim Traoré, President of Burkina Faso; General Assimi Goïta, President of the Transition of Mali and President of the Confederation of Sahel States (AES); and General Abdourahamane Tiani, President of the Republic of Niger. It was attended by the Prime Minister of Mali, the President of the National Transitional Council, members of the government, and administrative and municipal authorities of the Bamako District.
During the event, the Heads of State cut the ribbon, officially launching the pilot phase of AES Television, followed by a guided tour of the channel’s technical and administrative facilities.
The Minister of Communication, Digital Economy, and Administrative Modernization of Mali, Alhamdou Ag Ilyène, took part in the ceremony alongside his counterparts from Burkina Faso and Niger, reflecting the joint nature of the project.
The creation of AES Television, initiated by the Ministry of Communication, Digital Economy, and Administrative Modernization of Mali in close coordination with the communication ministries of Burkina Faso and Niger, underscores the collective commitment of the three member states. The project benefited from high-level political support from the President of the Confederation, General Assimi Goïta, whose leadership helped bring this strategic initiative to fruition.
Positioned as a key instrument for institutional communication and regional integration, AES Television aims to serve the peoples of the Sahel and Africa, as well as broader audiences committed to freedom, equality, and progress. The channel seeks to promote the values of solidarity, sovereignty, and resilience, provide reliable and balanced information, support confederal public policies, and strengthen cohesion among the peoples of the Sahel and Southern Africa.
The inauguration, held on the sidelines of the 2nd College of Heads of State of the Confederation of Sahel States, illustrates the determination of AES leaders to advance political, economic, and security integration through the establishment of sovereign media serving the interests and aspirations of the region’s populations.

title: 4th Rapid Intervention Battalion Class Trains in Tactical Mobility
excerpt: Koulikoro — December 31, 2025 ; Amid ongoing security challenges, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) are placing renewed emphasis on the Rapid Intervention Battalions (BIR) to enhance their operational capacity against terrorist threats. In Koulikoro, the 4th graduating class of this
title_en: 4th Rapid Intervention Battalion Class Trains in Tactical Mobility
excerpt_en: Koulikoro — December 31, 2025 ; Amid ongoing security challenges, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) are placing renewed emphasis on the Rapid Intervention Battalions (BIR) to enhance their operational capacity against terrorist threats. In Koulikoro, the 4th graduating class of this
body_en:
Koulikoro — December 31, 2025 ; Amid ongoing security challenges, the Malian Armed Forces (FAMa) are placing renewed emphasis on the Rapid Intervention Battalions (BIR) to enhance their operational capacity against terrorist threats. In Koulikoro, the 4th graduating class of this elite unit is undergoing intensive training to prepare for deployment in complex operational environments.
The creation of the BIR was part of a strategic initiative by Malian authorities to respond swiftly to the resurgence of terrorist attacks, intercommunal violence, and the pressures these pose on civilian populations. These units are designed for rapid deployment across the country, equipped and trained to operate under the diverse conditions encountered in Mali.
Currently stationed at the Boubacar Sada Sy Training Center in Koulikoro, the 4th BIR class is specializing in mobility-focused tactics. Under the supervision of instructors from the National Gendarmerie, trainees are refining skills critical for operational effectiveness, including:
Motorcycle riding in challenging terrains
Obstacle crossing and alignment techniques
Two-wheeled vehicle control
Navigation through chicanes
Emergency braking procedures
While the precise operational deployment of these units has not yet been disclosed, their missions are guided by three core principles: mobility, specialization, and proximity. The BIRs are expected to strengthen national security and pursue armed terrorist groups relentlessly, even into their last strongholds.
Colonel-Major Boubacar Serme, director of the training center, commended the professionalism of the recruits, noting that the BIR program represents a strategic modernization of FAMa in response to an asymmetric and evolving conflict environment. “This fourth graduating class embodies the political will to modernize our army,” he stated.
The training concluded with a demonstration of the operational capabilities acquired by the recruits, highlighting the growing effectiveness and responsiveness of Mali’s elite forces in maintaining national security.
